title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
intro_en: A restless young Englishman defies his father and runs off to sea. Storms, capture, and slavery follow — until a shipwreck leaves him the sole survivor on a deserted island. With only what he can salvage, he learns to grow food, raise goats, build a home, and keep his faith across long years of solitude. Then a single footprint in the sand changes everything.
intro_zh: 一个不安分的英国青年不听父亲劝告,偷偷出海。风暴、被俘、沦为奴隶接踵而来——直到一次海难,让他成了荒凉小岛上唯一的幸存者。只靠从破船上抢救下来的东西,他学着种粮、养羊、盖房子,在漫长孤独的岁月里守住信念。直到有一天,沙滩上的一枚脚印改变了一切。
copyright_note: 公版书 · Daniel Defoe, 1719 · 英文正文取自 Project Gutenberg (#521) · 中译由本平台生成。

paragraphs.en: I was born in the year 1632, in the city of York, of a good family, though not of that country, my father being a foreigner of Bremen, who settled first at Hull.
paragraphs.cn: 我于1632年出生在约克城,家境不错,不过并非本地人家——我父亲是不来梅的外乡人,最初落脚在赫尔。

paragraphs.en: He got a good estate by merchandise, and leaving off his trade, lived afterwards at York, from whence he had married my mother, whose relations were named Robinson, a very good family in that country, and from whom I was called Robinson Kreutznaer; but, by the usual corruption of words in England, we are now called—nay, we call ourselves and write our name—Crusoe; and so my companions always called me.
paragraphs.cn: 他靠做生意挣下一份可观的家业,后来歇了买卖,搬到约克住下,还在那里娶了我母亲;母亲娘家姓鲁滨逊,是当地一户很体面的人家,我便随母姓取名鲁滨逊·克鲁茨纳。可是照英国人念字走音的老习惯,如今大家把我们叫作——不,是我们自己也这样称呼、这样写自己的姓——克鲁索;我的同伴们也一直这么叫我。

paragraphs.en: I had two elder brothers, one of whom was lieutenant-colonel to an English regiment of foot in Flanders, formerly commanded by the famous Colonel Lockhart, and was killed at the battle near Dunkirk against the Spaniards.
paragraphs.cn: 我有两个哥哥,大哥是驻佛兰德斯的一支英国步兵团的中校,那个团先前由赫赫有名的洛卡特上校统领,大哥后来在敦刻尔克附近同西班牙人作战时阵亡了。

paragraphs.en: What became of my second brother I never knew, any more than my father or mother knew what became of me.
paragraphs.cn: 至于二哥的下落，我从来不知道，就像我父母也从来不知道我后来的下落一样。

paragraphs.en: Being the third son of the family and not bred to any trade, my head began to be filled very early with rambling thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 我是家里的第三个儿子，没让我去学什么手艺，于是我脑子里很早就装满了四处漂荡的念头。

paragraphs.en: My father, who was very ancient, had given me a competent share of learning, as far as house-education and a country free school generally go, and designed me for the law; but I would be satisfied with nothing but going to sea; and my inclination to this led me so strongly against the will, nay, the commands of my father, and against all the entreaties and persuasions of my mother and other friends, that there seemed to be something fatal in that propensity of nature, tending directly to the life of misery which was to befall me.
paragraphs.cn: 我父亲年事已高，尽力供我读了些书，凡是家塾和乡下义学一般能教的都让我学了，本打算让我去做律师；可我除了出海什么都不甘心。这份心思如此强烈，竟违逆了父亲的意愿，甚至违抗了他的命令，也不顾母亲和别的亲友再三的央求和劝说，仿佛我这天性里有种注定的东西，径直把我引向日后要临到我头上的悲惨生涯。

paragraphs.en: My father, a wise and grave man, gave me serious and excellent counsel against what he foresaw was my design.
paragraphs.cn: 我父亲是个明智稳重的人，早看出了我的心思，便郑重其事地给了我一番极好的劝告，要我打消这念头。

paragraphs.en: He called me one morning into his chamber, where he was confined by the gout, and expostulated very warmly with me upon this subject.
paragraphs.cn: 一天早晨，他把我叫进他的卧室——他正因痛风卧床——为这件事很动感情地同我恳谈了一番。

paragraphs.en: He asked me what reasons, more than a mere wandering inclination, I had for leaving father’s house and my native country, where I might be well introduced, and had a prospect of raising my fortune by application and industry, with a life of ease and pleasure.
paragraphs.cn: 他问我：除了想要四处漂荡这一点，我究竟有什么理由要离开父亲的家、离开自己的祖国？在这里我本可以有人引荐，凭勤勉努力便有望挣下家业，过上安逸快活的日子。

paragraphs.en: He told me it was men of desperate fortunes on one hand, or of aspiring, superior fortunes on the other, who went abroad upon adventures, to rise by enterprise, and make themselves famous in undertakings of a nature out of the common road; that these things were all either too far above me or too far below me; that mine was the middle state, or what might be called the upper station of low life, which he had found, by long experience, was the best state in the world, the most suited to human happiness, not exposed to the miseries and hardships, the labour and sufferings of the mechanic part of mankind, and not embarrassed with the pride, luxury, ambition, and envy of the upper part of mankind.
paragraphs.cn: 他对我说：出洋去冒险、想靠闯荡出人头地、在寻常人不走的路子上闯出名堂的，无非是两种人——一种是穷途末路的，一种是野心勃勃、想更上一层楼的；而这两样对我来说，要么高不可攀，要么低不足取；我所处的正是中间的境地，也可说是平民里的上等地位。他凭多年的阅历早已明白，这是世上最好的境地，最合乎人的幸福，既不必受下层劳作之人那种困苦艰辛、辛劳与磨难，也不必沾染上层人那种骄奢、放纵、野心与妒忌。

paragraphs.en: He told me I might judge of the happiness of this state by this one thing—viz. that this was the state of life which all other people envied; that kings have frequently lamented the miserable consequence of being born to great things, and wished they had been placed in the middle of the two extremes, between the mean and the great; that the wise man gave his testimony to this, as the standard of felicity, when he prayed to have neither poverty nor riches.
paragraphs.cn: 他说，我只凭这一件事便可以掂量出这种境地有多幸福——就是说，这正是别人个个羡慕的境地；帝王们常常悲叹自己生来担着大事业的苦命，恨不能生在两个极端之间、居于卑贱与显赫之间；就连那位智者也为此作证，把它当作幸福的标尺，因为他祈求既不要贫穷，也不要富贵。

paragraphs.en: He bade me observe it, and I should always find that the calamities of life were shared among the upper and lower part of mankind, but that the middle station had the fewest disasters, and was not exposed to so many vicissitudes as the higher or lower part of mankind; nay, they were not subjected to so many distempers and uneasinesses, either of body or mind, as those were who, by vicious living, luxury, and extravagances on the one hand, or by hard labour, want of necessaries, and mean or insufficient diet on the other hand, bring distemper upon themselves by the natural consequences of their way of living; that the middle station of life was calculated for all kind of virtue and all kind of enjoyments; that peace and plenty were the handmaids of a middle fortune; that temperance, moderation, quietness, health, society, all agreeable diversions, and all desirable pleasures, were the blessings attending the middle station of life; that this way men went silently and smoothly through the world, and comfortably out of it, not embarrassed with the labours of the hands or of the head, not sold to a life of slavery for daily bread, nor harassed with perplexed circumstances, which rob the soul of peace and the body of rest, nor enraged with the passion of envy, or the secret burning lust of ambition for great things; but, in easy circumstances, sliding gently through the world, and sensibly tasting the sweets of living, without the bitter; feeling that they are happy, and learning by every day’s experience to know it more sensibly.
paragraphs.cn: 他嘱咐我留意，我便会明白：人生的种种灾祸，多半落在上层和下层人身上，唯独中间境地的人遭的祸患最少，不像上层或下层的人那样饱经无常的起落；不仅如此，他们也不像那些人——一边是靠着放荡、奢侈、挥霍而自招疾患，一边是靠着苦役、缺衣少食、粗劣或不足的饮食而自损身体，两头都因各自的活法自然而然地招来病痛——不像他们那样，身心都受着那么多疾病和烦恼的折磨；中间境地正是为一切美德和一切享乐而设的；平安与丰足是中等家境的侍女；节制、有度、安宁、康健、亲朋往来、一切惬意的消遣、一切称心的乐趣，都是伴着中间境地而来的福分；走这条路的人，静悄悄、平顺顺地走过这一世，又安安稳稳地离世，既不必为手上或脑力的劳作所累，也不必为糊口而卖身为奴，更不必被纷乱的境遇搅得心神不宁、身不得歇，也不会被妒火烧灼、被那暗自灼烧的功名之欲折磨；而是在从容的境况里，轻轻地滑过人世，实实在在地尝着生活的甜，尝不到那份苦；只觉自己是幸福的，还一天天从亲身体验里越发真切地懂得这份幸福。

paragraphs.en: After this he pressed me earnestly, and in the most affectionate manner, not to play the young man, nor to precipitate myself into miseries which nature, and the station of life I was born in, seemed to have provided against; that I was under no necessity of seeking my bread; that he would do well for me, and endeavour to enter me fairly into the station of life which he had just been recommending to me; and that if I was not very easy and happy in the world, it must be my mere fate or fault that must hinder it; and that he should have nothing to answer for, having thus discharged his duty in warning me against measures which he knew would be to my hurt; in a word, that as he would do very kind things for me if I would stay and settle at home as he directed, so he would not have so much hand in my misfortunes as to give me any encouragement to go away; and to close all, he told me I had my elder brother for an example, to whom he had used the same earnest persuasions to keep him from going into the Low Country wars, but could not prevail, his young desires prompting him to run into the army, where he was killed; and though he said he would not cease to pray for me, yet he would venture to say to me, that if I did take this foolish step, God would not bless me, and I should have leisure hereafter to reflect upon having neglected his counsel when there might be none to assist in my recovery.
paragraphs.cn: 说完这些，他又极其恳切、极其慈爱地劝我，不要充那愣头青，不要一头栽进那些苦难里去——天性也好、我生来所处的境地也好，本都像是替我防着这些的；他说我根本不愁没饭吃；他会好好待我，尽力把我妥妥地安顿进他方才向我推荐的那种境地；倘若我在世上过得不安稳、不快活，那也只能怪我自己的命或自己的错在从中作梗；他自己则问心无愧，既已尽了本分，警告过我提防这些他明知会害我的举动；一句话，只要我肯听他的话留在家里安顿下来，他自会为我多多操办；反过来，他也决不肯在我的不幸里插手，去给我半点出走的怂恿。最后，他对我说：我有大哥的前车之鉴——他当年也是这样苦劝大哥，不让他去低地国家打仗，可拗不过，大哥年少气盛，非要去从军，结果送了命；他说他固然不会停下为我祷告，可他还是要放话给我：倘若我真走了这愚蠢的一步，上帝不会保佑我，往后我有的是工夫追悔当初没听他的劝告，而那时只怕再没人能拉我一把了。

paragraphs.en: I observed in this last part of his discourse, which was truly prophetic, though I suppose my father did not know it to be so himself—I say, I observed the tears run down his face very plentifully, especially when he spoke of my brother who was killed: and that when he spoke of my having leisure to repent, and none to assist me, he was so moved that he broke off the discourse, and told me his heart was so full he could say no more to me.
paragraphs.cn: 他这番话的末了一段，实在像预言一般应验了，尽管我想我父亲自己当时并不知道会这般灵验——我是说，我看见泪水扑簌簌地淌下他的脸，尤其是他讲到阵亡的大哥时；而当他讲到我日后将有工夫追悔、却再没人来搭救时，他动了真情，竟说不下去了，只对我说他心里塞得满满的，再没别的话对我讲了。

paragraphs.en: I was sincerely affected with this discourse, and, indeed, who could be otherwise? and I resolved not to think of going abroad any more, but to settle at home according to my father’s desire.
paragraphs.cn: 这番话教我由衷地感动——说真的，谁听了能不感动呢？我下定决心，再不去想什么出洋的事，照父亲的心愿在家安顿下来。

paragraphs.en: But alas! a few days wore it all off; and, in short, to prevent any of my father’s further importunities, in a few weeks after I resolved to run quite away from him.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，唉！没几天工夫，这决心便烟消云散了；简单说，为了免得父亲再来啰唆，几个礼拜之后我便打定主意，索性从他身边一走了之。

paragraphs.en: However, I did not act quite so hastily as the first heat of my resolution prompted; but I took my mother at a time when I thought her a little more pleasant than ordinary, and told her that my thoughts were so entirely bent upon seeing the world that I should never settle to anything with resolution enough to go through with it, and my father had better give me his consent than force me to go without it; that I was now eighteen years old, which was too late to go apprentice to a trade or clerk to an attorney; that I was sure if I did I should never serve out my time, but I should certainly run away from my master before my time was out, and go to sea; and if she would speak to my father to let me go one voyage abroad, if I came home again, and did not like it, I would go no more; and I would promise, by a double diligence, to recover the time that I had lost.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我并没有全凭那股一时冲动就贸然行事；我挑了个自觉母亲心情比平日略好的时候，对她说：我一心一意只想去见识见识这世界，无论如何也没法安下心来把哪桩事有始有终地做完；父亲与其硬逼我不告而别，倒不如爽快应了我；我已经十八岁了，这年纪去学手艺当学徒、或去律师那儿当文书都太迟了；我敢说，就算去了，也断然熬不满师期，准会在期满之前从东家那儿逃走出海去；求她替我向父亲说说情，让我出洋走一趟，倘若回来后我不喜欢，就再不去了；我愿加倍勤奋，把耽误的时光补回来。

paragraphs.en: This put my mother into a great passion; she told me she knew it would be to no purpose to speak to my father upon any such subject; that he knew too well what was my interest to give his consent to anything so much for my hurt; and that she wondered how I could think of any such thing after the discourse I had had with my father, and such kind and tender expressions as she knew my father had used to me; and that, in short, if I would ruin myself, there was no help for me; but I might depend I should never have their consent to it; that for her part she would not have so much hand in my destruction; and I should never have it to say that my mother was willing when my father was not.
paragraphs.cn: 这话把我母亲惹得大为光火；她对我说，她知道拿这种事去跟我父亲讲全无用处；父亲太清楚什么才是对我好，断不会应允这样明摆着害我的事；她还纳闷，我怎么在同父亲那番长谈之后、在明知父亲对我说了那么多慈爱恳切的话之后，还能起这样的念头；一句话，倘若我执意要自毁前程，那也没法救我了；可我尽管放心，他们二老是决不会答应的；就她而言，她可不愿在我的自毁里沾半点手；也决不能让我日后有话说，说母亲肯了、只是父亲不肯。

paragraphs.en: Though my mother refused to move it to my father, yet I heard afterwards that she reported all the discourse to him, and that my father, after showing a great concern at it, said to her, with a sigh, “That boy might be happy if he would stay at home; but if he goes abroad, he will be the most miserable wretch that ever was born: I can give no consent to it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我母亲虽不肯替我向父亲开口，可后来我听说，她把这番话原原本本都学给了父亲；父亲听了大为忧心，叹着气对她说：“那孩子若肯留在家里，本可以过得幸福；可他一旦出洋，就会成为天底下最苦命的可怜虫：这事我断断不能答应。”

paragraphs.en: It was not till almost a year after this that I broke loose, though, in the meantime, I continued obstinately deaf to all proposals of settling to business, and frequently expostulated with my father and mother about their being so positively determined against what they knew my inclinations prompted me to.
paragraphs.cn: 又过了差不多一年，我才终于挣脱了；不过这期间，我对一切安分做事的劝说始终执拗地充耳不闻，还三番五次同父母顶嘴，怪他们明知我心之所向，却偏要死死拦着。

paragraphs.en: But being one day at Hull, where I went casually, and without any purpose of making an elopement at that time; but, I say, being there, and one of my companions being about to sail to London in his father’s ship, and prompting me to go with them with the common allurement of seafaring men, that it should cost me nothing for my passage, I consulted neither father nor mother any more, nor so much as sent them word of it; but leaving them to hear of it as they might, without asking God’s blessing or my father’s, without any consideration of circumstances or consequences, and in an ill hour, God knows, on the 1st of September 1651, I went on board a ship bound for London.
paragraphs.cn: 可有一天，我偶然来到赫尔，本没打算就此私逃；可我说，人既在那里，恰好有个同伴要搭他父亲的船去伦敦，又拿海上人惯用的那套引诱来撺掇我一同去，说搭船一文钱不用花——于是我再没去请示父母，连个信儿也没捎给他们；由他们日后自己去听说吧，既没求上帝的祝福，也没求父亲的祝福，全不顾前因后果，就在——天知道，那是个多不吉利的时辰——1651年9月1日，我登上了一艘开往伦敦的船。

paragraphs.en: Never any young adventurer’s misfortunes, I believe, began sooner, or continued longer than mine.
paragraphs.cn: 我想，从没有哪个年轻冒险家的厄运，开头比我更早，延续得比我更久。

paragraphs.en: The ship was no sooner out of the Humber than the wind began to blow and the sea to rise in a most frightful manner; and, as I had never been at sea before, I was most inexpressibly sick in body and terrified in mind.
paragraphs.cn: 船刚驶出亨伯河口，风就刮了起来，海面也以最骇人的架势翻涌上来；我从没出过海，浑身难受得说不出，心里更是怕得要命。

paragraphs.en: I began now seriously to reflect upon what I had done, and how justly I was overtaken by the judgment of Heaven for my wicked leaving my father’s house, and abandoning my duty.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我才当真开始反省自己都做了些什么，反省自己那样不肖地离开父亲的家、抛下本分，如今遭天谴，实在是罪有应得。

paragraphs.en: All the good counsels of my parents, my father’s tears and my mother’s entreaties, came now fresh into my mind; and my conscience, which was not yet come to the pitch of hardness to which it has since, reproached me with the contempt of advice, and the breach of my duty to God and my father.
paragraphs.cn: 父母的种种忠告、父亲的眼泪、母亲的央求，此刻都新鲜鲜地涌回我心头；而我那还没磨到日后那般硬的良心，也责备我不该轻蔑劝告，不该违背对上帝和对父亲应尽的本分。

paragraphs.en: All this while the storm increased, and the sea went very high, though nothing like what I have seen many times since; no, nor what I saw a few days after; but it was enough to affect me then, who was but a young sailor, and had never known anything of the matter.
paragraphs.cn: 这工夫风暴愈发大了，海涛涌得极高——虽说比起我日后多次见过的风浪算不得什么，甚至比不上我几天后所见的；可对当时的我这么个初出茅庐、全然不懂海事的年轻水手来说，已经够受的了。

paragraphs.en: I expected every wave would have swallowed us up, and that every time the ship fell down, as I thought it did, in the trough or hollow of the sea, we should never rise more; in this agony of mind, I made many vows and resolutions that if it would please God to spare my life in this one voyage, if ever I got once my foot upon dry land again, I would go directly home to my father, and never set it into a ship again while I lived; that I would take his advice, and never run myself into such miseries as these any more.
paragraphs.cn: 我只当每一个浪头都要把我们吞没，每一回船身往下栽——我总觉得它是往海的浪谷或空洞里栽下去——我们就再也起不来了；在这般心焦如焚里，我许下许多誓愿、下了许多决心：只要上帝开恩，肯在这一趟里保住我的命，只要我这脚一旦重新踏上干爽的陆地，我就一直回父亲家去，这辈子再不踏上船一步；我要听他的话，再不把自己往这样的苦难里推了。

paragraphs.en: Now I saw plainly the goodness of his observations about the middle station of life, how easy, how comfortably he had lived all his days, and never had been exposed to tempests at sea or troubles on shore; and I resolved that I would, like a true repenting prodigal, go home to my father.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我算是看清了，父亲讲的那番关于中间境地的道理是多么在理——他这一生过得多安逸、多舒坦，从没在海上遭过风暴，也没在岸上受过烦扰；于是我下定决心，要像个真心悔悟的浪子那样，回到父亲身边去。

paragraphs.en: These wise and sober thoughts continued all the while the storm lasted, and indeed some time after; but the next day the wind was abated, and the sea calmer, and I began to be a little inured to it; however, I was very grave for all that day, being also a little sea-sick still; but towards night the weather cleared up, the wind was quite over, and a charming fine evening followed; the sun went down perfectly clear, and rose so the next morning; and having little or no wind, and a smooth sea, the sun shining upon it, the sight was, as I thought, the most delightful that ever I saw.
paragraphs.cn: 这些明智清醒的念头，在风暴持续的整段时间里都不曾断过，暴风过后也着实延续了一阵子；可到第二天，风势缓了，海面也平静了些，我也开始略略习惯了；不过那一整天我仍旧神色凝重，人也还有点晕船；可临近夜里，天却放晴了，风完全歇了，接着来了个迷人的好傍晚；夕阳清清朗朗地落下，第二天早晨又那样清清朗朗地升起；风又小得几乎没有，海面平滑如镜，阳光洒在上面——在我看来，这景象是我平生所见最赏心悦目的了。

paragraphs.en: I had slept well in the night, and was now no more sea-sick, but very cheerful, looking with wonder upon the sea that was so rough and terrible the day before, and could be so calm and so pleasant in so little a time after.
paragraphs.cn: 夜里我睡得香甜，这会儿也不再晕船，反倒兴致勃勃，惊奇地望着这片海：昨天还那样凶险可怖，隔了这么一小会儿工夫，竟能变得这般平静、这般宜人。

paragraphs.en: And now, lest my good resolutions should continue, my companion, who had enticed me away, comes to me; “Well, Bob,” says he, clapping me upon the shoulder, “how do you do after it?
paragraphs.cn: 就在这当口，唯恐我那些良善的决心当真持续下去似的，那个把我勾引出来的同伴走到我跟前；“喂，鲍勃，”他一边说，一边拍拍我的肩膀，“这一场过后，你觉得怎么样啊？

paragraphs.en: I warrant you were frighted, wer’n’t you, last night, when it blew but a capful of wind?”
paragraphs.cn: 我担保你昨晚吓坏了吧，是不是？可那才刮了那么一丁点儿风呀。”

paragraphs.en: “A capful d’you call it?” said I; “’twas a terrible storm.”
paragraphs.cn: “你管那叫一丁点儿风？”我说，“那可是一场吓人的大风暴。”

paragraphs.en: “A storm, you fool you,” replies he; “do you call that a storm? why, it was nothing at all; give us but a good ship and sea-room, and we think nothing of such a squall of wind as that; but you’re but a fresh-water sailor, Bob.
paragraphs.cn: “大风暴，你这傻瓜，”他回道，“你管那也叫风暴？咳，那压根算不了什么；只要给我们一条好船、一片开阔水面，这么一阵飑风我们根本不当回事；你不过是个没见过世面的旱鸭子水手罢了，鲍勃。

paragraphs.en: Come, let us make a bowl of punch, and we’ll forget all that; d’ye see what charming weather ’tis now?”
paragraphs.cn: 来吧，咱们调一钵潘趣酒，把那些统统忘掉；你瞧瞧，眼下这天气多迷人？”

paragraphs.en: To make short this sad part of my story, we went the way of all sailors; the punch was made and I was made half drunk with it: and in that one night’s wickedness I drowned all my repentance, all my reflections upon my past conduct, all my resolutions for the future.
paragraphs.cn: 长话短说，把我这段伤心的故事说短些吧——我们走上了所有水手都走的老路：潘趣酒调好了，我被灌得半醉；就在那一夜的荒唐里，我把满腔的悔恨、把对过往行径的一切反省、把对将来的一切决心，全都淹了个干净。

paragraphs.en: In a word, as the sea was returned to its smoothness of surface and settled calmness by the abatement of that storm, so the hurry of my thoughts being over, my fears and apprehensions of being swallowed up by the sea being forgotten, and the current of my former desires returned, I entirely forgot the vows and promises that I made in my distress.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话，正如那场风暴平息、海面重归平滑安宁一样，我心头的慌乱也过去了，被海吞没的种种惊惧担忧被抛到脑后，从前那些欲念又卷土重来，我便把患难中许下的誓愿和承诺忘得一干二净。

paragraphs.en: I found, indeed, some intervals of reflection; and the serious thoughts did, as it were, endeavour to return again sometimes; but I shook them off, and roused myself from them as it were from a distemper, and applying myself to drinking and company, soon mastered the return of those fits—for so I called them; and I had in five or six days got as complete a victory over conscience as any young fellow that resolved not to be troubled with it could desire.
paragraphs.cn: 说真的，我也曾有过几次反省的间隙；那些郑重的念头有时也仿佛竭力要回来；可我一把甩开它们，像抖落一场病似的从中挣脱，一头扎进酒和玩伴里，很快就把那些“发作”——我是这么叫它们的——重新压了下去；不出五六天，我就把良心制得服服帖帖，凡是打定主意不愿被它搅扰的年轻小伙子，谁能求得比这更彻底的胜利呢。

paragraphs.en: But I was to have another trial for it still; and Providence, as in such cases generally it does, resolved to leave me entirely without excuse; for if I would not take this for a deliverance, the next was to be such a one as the worst and most hardened wretch among us would confess both the danger and the mercy of.
paragraphs.cn: 但这事我还得再受一次考验；而天意——遇上这种情形它一向如此——存心要叫我彻底无可推诿：因为倘若我不肯把上一回当作一次搭救，那下一回便要来得叫我们中间最恶劣、最顽固的坏蛋都不得不承认其中既有凶险、也有慈悲。

paragraphs.en: The sixth day of our being at sea we came into Yarmouth Roads; the wind having been contrary and the weather calm, we had made but little way since the storm.
paragraphs.cn: 出海的第六天，我们驶进了雅茅斯锚地；因为一路顶风、天气又平静无风，风暴过后我们没走出多远。

paragraphs.en: Here we were obliged to come to an anchor, and here we lay, the wind continuing contrary—viz. at south-west—for seven or eight days, during which time a great many ships from Newcastle came into the same Roads, as the common harbour where the ships might wait for a wind for the river.
paragraphs.cn: 在这里我们只得下锚停泊，就这么停着，风仍旧是逆的——就是西南风——一连刮了七八天；这期间，许多从纽卡斯尔来的船也驶进了这同一片锚地，把它当作寻常的避风港，好在这儿等一阵顺风驶进河去。

paragraphs.en: We had not, however, rid here so long but we should have tided it up the river, but that the wind blew too fresh, and after we had lain four or five days, blew very hard.
paragraphs.cn: 其实我们停在这儿的工夫，本也够趁潮把船驶上河去了，无奈风刮得太急；我们停了四五天之后，风更是刮得极凶。

paragraphs.en: However, the Roads being reckoned as good as a harbour, the anchorage good, and our ground-tackle very strong, our men were unconcerned, and not in the least apprehensive of danger, but spent the time in rest and mirth, after the manner of the sea; but the eighth day, in the morning, the wind increased, and we had all hands at work to strike our topmasts, and make everything snug and close, that the ship might ride as easy as possible.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，这片锚地一向被看作跟港口一样稳妥，抛锚的底子好，我们的锚具又极结实，因此我们船上的人都满不在乎，一点儿也不担心有什么危险，只照海上人的老规矩，在歇息和玩乐里打发日子；可到了第八天早晨，风大了起来，我们全体动手放倒中桅，把一切都收拾得妥妥帖帖、绑绑扎扎，好让船尽量停得平稳些。

paragraphs.en: By noon the sea went very high indeed, and our ship rode forecastle in, shipped several seas, and we thought once or twice our anchor had come home; upon which our master ordered out the sheet-anchor, so that we rode with two anchors ahead, and the cables veered out to the bitter end.
paragraphs.cn: 到晌午，海涛当真涌得极高了，我们的船连船头楼都埋进浪里，好几回给海浪扫上了甲板；我们有一两次只当锚已经走了位；船长便下令抛出备用大锚，于是我们船头拉着两只锚，锚缆一直放到了尽头。

paragraphs.en: By this time it blew a terrible storm indeed; and now I began to see terror and amazement in the faces even of the seamen themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 到这时，天上刮的当真是一场骇人的大风暴了；如今我开始看见，连那些水手自己脸上，也露出了惊恐和骇然。

paragraphs.en: The master, though vigilant in the business of preserving the ship, yet as he went in and out of his cabin by me, I could hear him softly to himself say, several times, “Lord be merciful to us! we shall be all lost! we shall be all undone!” and the like.
paragraphs.cn: 船长虽说一心扑在保船的差事上，可他打我身边进进出出舱房时，我好几次听见他低声自语：“主啊，可怜可怜我们吧！我们要全完了！我们要全毁了！”诸如此类的话。

paragraphs.en: During these first hurries I was stupid, lying still in my cabin, which was in the steerage, and cannot describe my temper: I could ill resume the first penitence which I had so apparently trampled upon and hardened myself against: I thought the bitterness of death had been past, and that this would be nothing like the first; but when the master himself came by me, as I said just now, and said we should be all lost, I was dreadfully frighted.
paragraphs.cn: 在这最初的一阵慌乱里，我木呆呆的，一动不动地躺在我那间设在舵舱的小舱里，那份心境实在没法描摹：我早已明摆着把当初那点悔悟践踏了、又硬着心肠抵挡它，如今再难拾起；我原以为死亡的苦楚已经过去，这一回不会像头一回那样厉害；可当船长本人打我身边经过、像我方才说的那样，说我们要全完了，我便怕得魂飞魄散。

paragraphs.en: I got up out of my cabin and looked out; but such a dismal sight I never saw: the sea ran mountains high, and broke upon us every three or four minutes; when I could look about, I could see nothing but distress round us; two ships that rode near us, we found, had cut their masts by the board, being deep laden; and our men cried out that a ship which rode about a mile ahead of us was foundered.
paragraphs.cn: 我从小舱里爬起来往外望；可那样一幅凄惨景象，我平生从没见过：海浪高如山岭，每隔三四分钟就朝我们劈头砸下；我勉强能四下张望时，只见我们周遭尽是灾殃；停在我们近旁的两条船，我们发现因为吃水太深，都已经把桅杆齐着船帮砍掉了；我们的人还嚷道，停在我们前头约莫一海里处的一条船已经沉了。

paragraphs.en: Two more ships, being driven from their anchors, were run out of the Roads to sea, at all adventures, and that with not a mast standing.
paragraphs.cn: 另有两条船因为脱了锚，被逼出锚地、冲进大海，听天由命地任其漂去，连一根桅杆都没剩下。

paragraphs.en: The light ships fared the best, as not so much labouring in the sea; but two or three of them drove, and came close by us, running away with only their spritsail out before the wind.
paragraphs.cn: 空载的轻船境况最好，因为在海里颠簸得不那么厉害；可其中也有两三条脱锚漂了过来，紧擦着我们身边，只挂着一张斜桁帆顺风飞逃而去。

paragraphs.en: Towards evening the mate and boatswain begged the master of our ship to let them cut away the fore-mast, which he was very unwilling to do; but the boatswain protesting to him that if he did not the ship would founder, he consented; and when they had cut away the fore-mast, the main-mast stood so loose, and shook the ship so much, they were obliged to cut that away also, and make a clear deck.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚时分，大副和水手长恳求船长准许他们砍掉前桅，船长很不情愿；可水手长向他力陈，若不砍船就要沉，船长这才应了；等他们砍掉前桅，主桅便晃荡得松脱脱的，把船摇得那么厉害，他们只得连它也一并砍掉，弄出一片光溜溜的甲板。

paragraphs.en: Any one may judge what a condition I must be in at all this, who was but a young sailor, and who had been in such a fright before at but a little.
paragraphs.cn: 谁都想得出，眼见这一切，我这么个刚出海、先前才为那么一点风浪就吓成那样的年轻水手，此刻会是什么光景。

paragraphs.en: But if I can express at this distance the thoughts I had about me at that time, I was in tenfold more horror of mind upon account of my former convictions, and the having returned from them to the resolutions I had wickedly taken at first, than I was at death itself; and these, added to the terror of the storm, put me into such a condition that I can by no words describe it.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，倘若我如今还说得出当时我心里那些念头，我要说：比起对死亡本身的恐惧，我更是因念及从前那番省悟、又从中折回去、重拾起初那昧着良心下的决心，而心里生出十倍的惊怖；这份惊怖再添上风暴的骇人，把我逼到一种我无论用什么话都描摹不出的境地。

paragraphs.en: But the worst was not come yet; the storm continued with such fury that the seamen themselves acknowledged they had never seen a worse.
paragraphs.cn: 可最糟的还没到呢；风暴仍旧那样狂暴，连水手们自己都承认从没见过更凶的。

paragraphs.en: We had a good ship, but she was deep laden, and wallowed in the sea, so that the seamen every now and then cried out she would founder.
paragraphs.cn: 我们的船是条好船，可吃水太深，在海里直打滚，弄得水手们隔一阵就嚷嚷说它要沉了。

paragraphs.en: It was my advantage in one respect, that I did not know what they meant by _founder_ till I inquired.
paragraphs.cn: 有一点倒算我走运：直到我开口去问，我才知道他们所说的“沉船”是什么意思。

paragraphs.en: However, the storm was so violent that I saw, what is not often seen, the master, the boatswain, and some others more sensible than the rest, at their prayers, and expecting every moment when the ship would go to the bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 然而风暴那样猛烈，我竟看见了一幕平日难得一见的景象：船长、水手长，还有另外几个比其余人更明白事理的，都在祷告，只等着船随时沉到海底去。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of the night, and under all the rest of our distresses, one of the men that had been down to see cried out we had sprung a leak; another said there was four feet water in the hold.
paragraphs.cn: 半夜里，在我们所有这些患难之上，一个下去查看的人又嚷道：我们漏水了；另一个说，舱底积水已有四英尺深。

paragraphs.en: Then all hands were called to the pump.
paragraphs.cn: 于是全体被唤去抽水。

paragraphs.en: At that word, my heart, as I thought, died within me: and I fell backwards upon the side of my bed where I sat, into the cabin.
paragraphs.cn: 听到这句话，我只觉得自己的心仿佛在胸口死了过去：我一屁股往后瘫倒在我坐着的床沿上，跌进了小舱里。

paragraphs.en: However, the men roused me, and told me that I, that was able to do nothing before, was as well able to pump as another; at which I stirred up and went to the pump, and worked very heartily.
paragraphs.cn: 可众人把我拽了起来，对我说：我这先前什么都干不了的人，抽起水来跟别人一样使得；我这才振作起来，去到水泵旁，卖力地干了起来。

paragraphs.en: While this was doing, the master, seeing some light colliers, who, not able to ride out the storm were obliged to slip and run away to sea, and would come near us, ordered to fire a gun as a signal of distress.
paragraphs.cn: 正干着，船长瞧见几条运煤的轻船——它们经不住这场风暴，只得砍缆放漂、逃往大海，眼看要漂近我们——便下令放一炮，作为求救的信号。

paragraphs.en: I, who knew nothing what they meant, thought the ship had broken, or some dreadful thing happened.
paragraphs.cn: 我全然不懂他们是什么意思，只当船撞破了，或是出了什么可怕的事。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I was so surprised that I fell down in a swoon.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话，我惊骇得晕了过去，一头栽倒在地。

paragraphs.en: As this was a time when everybody had his own life to think of, nobody minded me, or what was become of me; but another man stepped up to the pump, and thrusting me aside with his foot, let me lie, thinking I had been dead; and it was a great while before I came to myself.
paragraphs.cn: 眼下正是人人都只顾自己活命的时候，谁也没心思理会我、理会我出了什么事；另一个人跨上前去接替抽水，一脚把我踢到一边，由我躺着，只当我已经死了；过了好大一会儿我才苏醒过来。

paragraphs.en: We worked on; but the water increasing in the hold, it was apparent that the ship would founder; and though the storm began to abate a little, yet it was not possible she could swim till we might run into any port; so the master continued firing guns for help; and a light ship, who had rid it out just ahead of us, ventured a boat out to help us.
paragraphs.cn: 我们接着干；可舱里的水越积越多，眼看船是要沉了；虽说风暴开始略略缓了些，可要撑到我们驶进哪个港口，是断然不成的了；于是船长不停地放炮求救；恰好有一条轻船，方才顶着风暴稳稳停在我们正前头，这时冒险放下一只小艇来救我们。

paragraphs.en: It was with the utmost hazard the boat came near us; but it was impossible for us to get on board, or for the boat to lie near the ship’s side, till at last the men rowing very heartily, and venturing their lives to save ours, our men cast them a rope over the stern with a buoy to it, and then veered it out a great length, which they, after much labour and hazard, took hold of, and we hauled them close under our stern, and got all into their boat.
paragraphs.cn: 那小艇冒着天大的凶险才靠近我们；可我们要上艇、或要那小艇贴着船帮停住，都是不可能的；直到最后，艇上的人拼命划桨、豁出性命来救我们的命，我们的人从船尾抛给他们一根系着浮筒的绳子，又放出老长一截，他们费了好大力气、冒了好大险才抓住，我们便把他们拽到船尾底下，人人都上了他们的艇。

paragraphs.en: It was to no purpose for them or us, after we were in the boat, to think of reaching their own ship; so all agreed to let her drive, and only to pull her in towards shore as much as we could; and our master promised them, that if the boat was staved upon shore, he would make it good to their master: so partly rowing and partly driving, our boat went away to the northward, sloping towards the shore almost as far as Winterton Ness.
paragraphs.cn: 上了艇之后，无论对他们还是对我们，再想着回他们自己的船都是白搭；于是大家一致商定，索性任那船漂去，只尽力把小艇往岸边划；我们船长向他们许诺：若小艇在岸上撞坏了，他会照价赔给他们船主；就这样，一半靠划、一半靠漂，我们的小艇朝北去了，斜斜地贴着海岸，差不多划到了温特顿岬。

paragraphs.en: We were not much more than a quarter of an hour out of our ship till we saw her sink, and then I understood for the first time what was meant by a ship foundering in the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我们离开自己那条船不过一刻钟出头，就眼看着它沉了下去；我这才头一回明白，“船沉进海里”是怎么一回事。

paragraphs.en: I must acknowledge I had hardly eyes to look up when the seamen told me she was sinking; for from the moment that they rather put me into the boat than that I might be said to go in, my heart was, as it were, dead within me, partly with fright, partly with horror of mind, and the thoughts of what was yet before me.
paragraphs.cn: 我得承认，当水手们告诉我船正在下沉时，我几乎没胆量抬眼去看；因为打从他们与其说让我上艇、不如说把我塞进艇里的那一刻起，我这颗心便仿佛在胸口死了过去，一半是吓的，一半是心里骇然，还有想到自己前头还等着什么的那份恐惧。

paragraphs.en: While we were in this condition—the men yet labouring at the oar to bring the boat near the shore—we could see (when, our boat mounting the waves, we were able to see the shore) a great many people running along the strand to assist us when we should come near; but we made but slow way towards the shore; nor were we able to reach the shore till, being past the lighthouse at Winterton, the shore falls off to the westward towards Cromer, and so the land broke off a little the violence of the wind.
paragraphs.cn: 我们正是这般处境——众人还在使劲划桨，想把小艇划近岸边——每当小艇被浪托起、我们能望见岸时，就看见岸上有许许多多人沿着沙滩奔跑，要在我们靠近时来搭救我们；可我们朝岸边划得极慢；直到过了温特顿的灯塔，海岸朝西转向克罗默那一带凹了进去，陆地略略挡去了些风势，我们才总算靠了岸。

paragraphs.en: Here we got in, and though not without much difficulty, got all safe on shore, and walked afterwards on foot to Yarmouth, where, as unfortunate men, we were used with great humanity, as well by the magistrates of the town, who assigned us good quarters, as by particular merchants and owners of ships, and had money given us sufficient to carry us either to London or back to Hull as we thought fit.
paragraphs.cn: 我们在这里驶了进去，虽说费了好大的劲，总算人人都安然上了岸，随后步行走到雅茅斯；在那儿，人们把我们当作遭难的人，待我们极为仁厚——镇上的官长给我们安排了好住处，几位商人和船主也特别照应，还给了我们够用的钱，好让我们或去伦敦、或回赫尔，随我们自己的意思。

paragraphs.en: Had I now had the sense to have gone back to Hull, and have gone home, I had been happy, and my father, as in our blessed Saviour’s parable, had even killed the fatted calf for me; for hearing the ship I went away in was cast away in Yarmouth Roads, it was a great while before he had any assurances that I was not drowned.
paragraphs.cn: 我这时若还有点见识，肯回赫尔去、回家去，本可以过得幸福，我父亲也会像我们那位可颂的救主所讲的比喻里那样，为我宰了那头肥牛犊；因为他听说我搭乘的那条船在雅茅斯锚地失了事，过了好久才总算确信我没有淹死。

paragraphs.en: But my ill fate pushed me on now with an obstinacy that nothing could resist; and though I had several times loud calls from my reason and my more composed judgment to go home, yet I had no power to do it.
paragraphs.cn: 可我的厄运此刻却推着我往前，那股拗劲什么都挡不住；虽说好几次，我的理智、我那更冷静的判断都高声呼唤我回家去，我却半点也没那力气去照做。

paragraphs.en: I know not what to call this, nor will I urge that it is a secret overruling decree, that hurries us on to be the instruments of our own destruction, even though it be before us, and that we rush upon it with our eyes open.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道该把这叫作什么，也不想硬说这是某种冥冥中主宰一切的定数，硬把我们推去做那毁灭自己的器具，哪怕那毁灭就摆在眼前，我们还睁着眼睛往上撞。

paragraphs.en: Certainly, nothing but some such decreed unavoidable misery, which it was impossible for me to escape, could have pushed me forward against the calm reasonings and persuasions of my most retired thoughts, and against two such visible instructions as I had met with in my first attempt.
paragraphs.cn: 可以肯定，若不是有这么一种命中注定、我万难逃脱的苦厄，是断不能推着我一意孤行，去违逆我最静僻的心思里那些冷静的推理和劝告，去违逆我头一趟出海就遭遇的那样两桩明明白白的警示的。

paragraphs.en: My comrade, who had helped to harden me before, and who was the master’s son, was now less forward than I.
paragraphs.cn: 我那位同伴——先前正是他帮着把我的心磨硬的，他又是船长的儿子——这会儿却比我还退缩了。

paragraphs.en: The first time he spoke to me after we were at Yarmouth, which was not till two or three days, for we were separated in the town to several quarters; I say, the first time he saw me, it appeared his tone was altered; and, looking very melancholy, and shaking his head, he asked me how I did, and telling his father who I was, and how I had come this voyage only for a trial, in order to go further abroad, his father, turning to me with a very grave and concerned tone “Young man,” says he, “you ought never to go to sea any more; you ought to take this for a plain and visible token that you are not to be a seafaring man.”
paragraphs.cn: 到了雅茅斯之后，他头一回同我说话，已是两三天以后了，因为我们在镇上给分开安置到了不同的住处；我是说，他头一回见我，那口气显然变了；他一脸忧郁、直摇着头，问我可好，又把我是谁、我这趟出海只为一试、原是打算日后走得更远的事，都告诉了他父亲；他父亲便转过身来，神色极其凝重、极其关切地对我说：“年轻人，”他说，“你这辈子再不该出海了；你该把这事当作一个明明白白的凭据，晓得你天生就不该做个吃海上饭的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, sir,” said I, “will you go to sea no more?”
paragraphs.cn: “可是，先生，”我说，“您自己不也还要出海吗？”

paragraphs.en: “That is another case,” said he; “it is my calling, and therefore my duty; but as you made this voyage on trial, you see what a taste Heaven has given you of what you are to expect if you persist.
paragraphs.cn: “那是另一码事，”他说，“出海是我的行当，因而是我的本分；可你这趟出海是来试一试的，你也瞧见了，上天已叫你尝到点滋味，晓得你若一意坚持，往后要有什么等着你。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps this has all befallen us on your account, like Jonah in the ship of Tarshish.
paragraphs.cn: 说不定我们这一场，全是为了你才招来的，就像约拿在那条开往他施的船上一样。

paragraphs.en: Pray,” continues he, “what are you; and on what account did you go to sea?”
paragraphs.cn: 请问，”他接着说，“你到底是什么人？你又为着什么去出海？”

paragraphs.en: Upon that I told him some of my story; at the end of which he burst out into a strange kind of passion: “What had I done,” says he, “that such an unhappy wretch should come into my ship?
paragraphs.cn: 于是我把自己的经历讲了些给他听；讲到末了，他勃然大怒，发作起一种古怪的性子来：“我造了什么孽，”他说，“竟叫这么个晦气的可怜虫上了我的船？

paragraphs.en: I would not set my foot in the same ship with thee again for a thousand pounds.”
paragraphs.cn: 就是给我一千镑，我也再不肯同你踏进同一条船了。”

paragraphs.en: This indeed was, as I said, an excursion of his spirits, which were yet agitated by the sense of his loss, and was farther than he could have authority to go.
paragraphs.cn: 这话，我方才说过，其实是他一时的意气发作，他的心绪还被丧船之痛搅动着，这番话也说得过了头，超出了他本该有的分寸。

paragraphs.en: However, he afterwards talked very gravely to me, exhorting me to go back to my father, and not tempt Providence to my ruin, telling me I might see a visible hand of Heaven against me.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他后来倒是很郑重地同我谈了一番，劝我回到父亲身边去，别再拿天意来试自己的败亡，还对我说，我可以看出有一只上天的手明明白白地在跟我作对。

paragraphs.en: “And, young man,” said he, “depend upon it, if you do not go back, wherever you go, you will meet with nothing but disasters and disappointments, till your father’s words are fulfilled upon you.”
paragraphs.cn: “还有，年轻人，”他说，“你听好了，你若不回去，那么无论你走到哪里，除了灾祸和失望你什么都遇不着，直到你父亲的话在你身上应验为止。”

paragraphs.en: We parted soon after; for I made him little answer, and I saw him no more; which way he went I knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 不久我们便分了手；因为我没怎么答理他，从此再没见过他，他往哪个方向去了我也不知道。

paragraphs.en: As for me, having some money in my pocket, I travelled to London by land; and there, as well as on the road, had many struggles with myself what course of life I should take, and whether I should go home or to sea.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我，口袋里既有几个钱，便从陆路去了伦敦；一路上，还有到了伦敦以后，我心里反复挣扎，拿不定该走哪条人生的路，该回家去还是该出海去。

paragraphs.en: As to going home, shame opposed the best motions that offered to my thoughts, and it immediately occurred to me how I should be laughed at among the neighbours, and should be ashamed to see, not my father and mother only, but even everybody else; from whence I have since often observed, how incongruous and irrational the common temper of mankind is, especially of youth, to that reason which ought to guide them in such cases—viz. that they are not ashamed to sin, and yet are ashamed to repent; not ashamed of the action for which they ought justly to be esteemed fools, but are ashamed of the returning, which only can make them be esteemed wise men.
paragraphs.cn: 说到回家，羞耻压住了我脑子里冒出来的一切好念头；我立时想到街坊邻里会怎样笑话我，我会羞于去见——不单是父亲母亲，连别的什么人都羞于去见；由此我后来常常留意到，人的常情、尤其是年轻人的常情，同那本该在这种事上引导他们的理性，是多么地不合、多么地悖理——就是说，他们不以作恶为耻，却以悔改为耻；不以那本该被人正正当当地骂作蠢事的行径为耻，却以那唯一能叫人被称作明智之人的回头为耻。

paragraphs.en: In this state of life, however, I remained some time, uncertain what measures to take, and what course of life to lead.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，我就这样在这种人生状态里待了些时候，拿不定该采取什么办法、该过怎样的日子。

paragraphs.en: An irresistible reluctance continued to going home; and as I stayed away a while, the remembrance of the distress I had been in wore off, and as that abated, the little motion I had in my desires to return wore off with it, till at last I quite laid aside the thoughts of it, and looked out for a voyage.
paragraphs.cn: 我心里那股回家的抗拒始终按捺不下；随着我在外头耽搁久了，先前那番患难的记忆渐渐淡去，随着它一淡，我那点想回家的微弱心思也跟着淡了，直到最后，我索性把回家的念头彻底抛开，去张罗着找一趟航船了。

paragraphs.en: That evil influence which carried me first away from my father’s house—which hurried me into the wild and indigested notion of raising my fortune, and that impressed those conceits so forcibly upon me as to make me deaf to all good advice, and to the entreaties and even the commands of my father—I say, the same influence, whatever it was, presented the most unfortunate of all enterprises to my view; and I went on board a vessel bound to the coast of Africa; or, as our sailors vulgarly called it, a voyage to Guinea.
paragraphs.cn: 那股邪恶的力量,当初把我从父亲的家里带走,催着我生出发财致富这种荒唐、盲目的念头,又把这些空想深深地烙进我心里,使我对一切良言忠告都充耳不闻,连父亲的恳求乃至命令也听不进去——我要说,还是这同一股力量,不管它究竟是什么,把一切事业中最不幸的那一桩摆到了我面前;于是我登上了一艘开往非洲海岸的船;用我们水手粗俗的说法,就是去几内亚航行一趟。

paragraphs.en: It was my great misfortune that in all these adventures I did not ship myself as a sailor; when, though I might indeed have worked a little harder than ordinary, yet at the same time I should have learnt the duty and office of a fore-mast man, and in time might have qualified myself for a mate or lieutenant, if not for a master.
paragraphs.cn: 在这些冒险里,我最大的不幸就是没有以水手的身份上船;其实我只要比平常多出些力气,同时便能学会一名普通水手的职责与本领,日久天长,就算当不上船长,也能有资格做大副或二副。

paragraphs.en: But as it was always my fate to choose for the worse, so I did here; for having money in my pocket and good clothes upon my back, I would always go on board in the habit of a gentleman; and so I neither had any business in the ship, nor learned to do any.
paragraphs.cn: 可我的命运总是偏偏挑最坏的走,这一回也不例外;因为口袋里有钱、身上又穿着体面衣裳,我上船时总摆出一副绅士派头;结果船上的事我一样都不用干,也一样都没学会。

paragraphs.en: It was my lot first of all to fall into pretty good company in London, which does not always happen to such loose and misguided young fellows as I then was; the devil generally not omitting to lay some snare for them very early; but it was not so with me.
paragraphs.cn: 我起初在伦敦有幸结交了一帮相当不错的朋友,这在我当时那样放荡、迷途的年轻人身上可不常有;魔鬼一般总不忘早早给这种人设下圈套,可我却没落进去。

paragraphs.en: I first got acquainted with the master of a ship who had been on the coast of Guinea; and who, having had very good success there, was resolved to go again.
paragraphs.cn: 我先认识了一位船长,他去过几内亚海岸,而且在那里收获颇丰,便打定主意要再去一趟。

paragraphs.en: This captain taking a fancy to my conversation, which was not at all disagreeable at that time, hearing me say I had a mind to see the world, told me if I would go the voyage with him I should be at no expense; I should be his messmate and his companion; and if I could carry anything with me, I should have all the advantage of it that the trade would admit; and perhaps I might meet with some encouragement.
paragraphs.cn: 这位船长看中了我的谈吐——那时我说起话来倒也不讨人厌——听我说想去见见世面,便对我说,如果我愿意随他航行,一路上不用花一文钱;我可以和他同桌吃饭、做他的伙伴;若是我能带些货物,凡贸易许可的好处都归我;说不定还能有些赚头。

paragraphs.en: I embraced the offer; and entering into a strict friendship with this captain, who was an honest, plain-dealing man, I went the voyage with him, and carried a small adventure with me, which, by the disinterested honesty of my friend the captain, I increased very considerably; for I carried about £40 in such toys and trifles as the captain directed me to buy.
paragraphs.cn: 我欣然接受了这个提议;和这位船长结成了亲密的友谊——他是个诚实、正直的人——就随他出了海,还带了一小笔本钱做买卖,靠着这位船长朋友的一片无私诚意,这本钱增值了许多;因为我照船长的吩咐,买了约合四十英镑的小玩意儿和零碎货。

paragraphs.en: These £40 I had mustered together by the assistance of some of my relations whom I corresponded with; and who, I believe, got my father, or at least my mother, to contribute so much as that to my first adventure.
paragraphs.cn: 这四十英镑,是我靠几位有书信往来的亲戚帮忙凑起来的;我想,是他们说动了我父亲,或至少是我母亲,给我这第一趟冒险出了这么一笔钱。

paragraphs.en: This was the only voyage which I may say was successful in all my adventures, which I owe to the integrity and honesty of my friend the captain; under whom also I got a competent knowledge of the mathematics and the rules of navigation, learned how to keep an account of the ship’s course, take an observation, and, in short, to understand some things that were needful to be understood by a sailor; for, as he took delight to instruct me, I took delight to learn; and, in a word, this voyage made me both a sailor and a merchant; for I brought home five pounds nine ounces of gold-dust for my adventure, which yielded me in London, at my return, almost £300; and this filled me with those aspiring thoughts which have since so completed my ruin.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我所有冒险中唯一可算成功的一趟,全靠我那位船长朋友的正直和诚实;在他手下,我还学到了不少数学和航海规则的知识,学会了记录航程、观测方位,总之,懂得了一名水手该懂的一些事;因为他乐于教我,我也乐于学;一句话,这趟航行使我既成了水手,又成了商人;因为我这趟冒险带回了五磅九盎司金砂,回到伦敦一变卖,几乎值三百英镑;这便让我满脑子都是雄心壮志,而正是这些心思,后来彻底毁了我。

paragraphs.en: Yet even in this voyage I had my misfortunes too; particularly, that I was continually sick, being thrown into a violent calenture by the excessive heat of the climate; our principal trading being upon the coast, from latitude of 15 degrees north even to the line itself.
paragraphs.cn: 然而即便这趟航行,我也有我的不幸;尤其是我一路上不停地病,酷热的气候把我抛进了一场剧烈的热病;我们主要的贸易都在海岸一带进行,从北纬十五度一直到赤道线。

paragraphs.en: I was now set up for a Guinea trader; and my friend, to my great misfortune, dying soon after his arrival, I resolved to go the same voyage again, and I embarked in the same vessel with one who was his mate in the former voyage, and had now got the command of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我算是做上了几内亚的商人;而我那位朋友,不幸得很,刚回来不久就去世了,于是我决定再走一趟同样的航路,便登上了同一艘船,而带船的正是上一趟给他当大副、如今接了船长之职的人。

paragraphs.en: This was the unhappiest voyage that ever man made; for though I did not carry quite £100 of my new-gained wealth, so that I had £200 left, which I had lodged with my friend’s widow, who was very just to me, yet I fell into terrible misfortunes.
paragraphs.cn: 这是人所曾有过的最倒霉的一趟航行;虽说我这回并没带上新赚来财产的一百英镑,还剩下两百英镑存在我那位朋友的遗孀那里——她待我很公道——可我还是落进了可怕的灾难。

paragraphs.en: The first was this: our ship making her course towards the Canary Islands, or rather between those islands and the African shore, was surprised in the grey of the morning by a Turkish rover of Sallee, who gave chase to us with all the sail she could make.
paragraphs.cn: 头一桩是这样的:我们的船朝加那利群岛驶去,或者不如说,是在这些岛屿和非洲海岸之间行驶,拂晓灰蒙蒙的时候,冷不防遭一艘萨累的土耳其海盗船袭击,它张满了帆,拼命向我们追来。

paragraphs.en: We crowded also as much canvas as our yards would spread, or our masts carry, to get clear; but finding the pirate gained upon us, and would certainly come up with us in a few hours, we prepared to fight; our ship having twelve guns, and the rogue eighteen.
paragraphs.cn: 我们也把船帆尽量张满,能挂多少挂多少,想要甩开;可眼看海盗船越追越近,再过几个钟头必定赶上,我们便准备迎战;我们的船有十二门炮,那恶棍有十八门。

paragraphs.en: About three in the afternoon he came up with us, and bringing to, by mistake, just athwart our quarter, instead of athwart our stern, as he intended, we brought eight of our guns to bear on that side, and poured in a broadside upon him, which made him sheer off again, after returning our fire, and pouring in also his small shot from near two hundred men which he had on board.
paragraphs.cn: 下午三点光景,他赶上了我们,由于失误,他没像原打算那样横到我们船尾,却横到了我们船舷,于是我们把那一边的八门炮对准他,给了他一记舷炮齐射,把他打得又退了开去,不过他也还了火,还用船上将近两百人的火枪向我们猛烈扫射。

paragraphs.en: However, we had not a man touched, all our men keeping close.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我们无一人挂彩,大家都紧紧地隐蔽着。

paragraphs.en: He prepared to attack us again, and we to defend ourselves.
paragraphs.cn: 他准备再次进攻,我们则准备自卫。

paragraphs.en: But laying us on board the next time upon our other quarter, he entered sixty men upon our decks, who immediately fell to cutting and hacking the sails and rigging.
paragraphs.cn: 可他这一回从我们另一侧船舷靠了上来,派了六十个人登上我们的甲板,那些人立刻动手砍杀我们的船帆和索具。

paragraphs.en: We plied them with small shot, half-pikes, powder-chests, and such like, and cleared our deck of them twice.
paragraphs.cn: 我们用火枪、半长矛、火药箱一类的东西招呼他们,两度把甲板上的敌人清干净。

paragraphs.en: However, to cut short this melancholy part of our story, our ship being disabled, and three of our men killed, and eight wounded, we were obliged to yield, and were carried all prisoners into Sallee, a port belonging to the Moors.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,长话短说,把我们这段惨痛的经历说完吧:我们的船已丧失战力,死了三人,伤了八人,只得投降,全被押作俘虏带进萨累——那是摩尔人的一个港口。

paragraphs.en: The usage I had there was not so dreadful as at first I apprehended; nor was I carried up the country to the emperor’s court, as the rest of our men were, but was kept by the captain of the rover as his proper prize, and made his slave, being young and nimble, and fit for his business.
paragraphs.cn: 我在那里受到的对待,并不像我起初担心的那么可怕;我也没像其余船员那样被押送到内地去见皇帝的宫廷,而是被那海盗船长留下,当作他理所当然的战利品,做了他的奴隶,因为我年轻敏捷,正合他使唤。

paragraphs.en: At this surprising change of my circumstances, from a merchant to a miserable slave, I was perfectly overwhelmed; and now I looked back upon my father’s prophetic discourse to me, that I should be miserable and have none to relieve me, which I thought was now so effectually brought to pass that I could not be worse; for now the hand of Heaven had overtaken me, and I was undone without redemption; but, alas! this was but a taste of the misery I was to go through, as will appear in the sequel of this story.
paragraphs.cn: 境遇如此惊人地一变,从一个商人沦为可怜的奴隶,我彻底崩溃了;这时我回想起父亲当初预言般的那番话,说我终将落得悲惨、无人搭救的下场,如今看来是应验得这样彻底,我觉得再糟也糟不到哪里去了;因为上天之手已经把我逮住,我万劫不复;可是,唉!这不过是我将要历经的苦难的一点尝头罢了,后文自会分晓。

paragraphs.en: As my new patron, or master, had taken me home to his house, so I was in hopes that he would take me with him when he went to sea again, believing that it would some time or other be his fate to be taken by a Spanish or Portugal man-of-war; and that then I should be set at liberty.
paragraphs.cn: 既然我这位新主人把我带回了他家,我便盼着他再出海时能带上我,心想说不定哪一天他会被西班牙或葡萄牙的军舰俘获,到那时我就能重获自由了。

paragraphs.en: But this hope of mine was soon taken away; for when he went to sea, he left me on shore to look after his little garden, and do the common drudgery of slaves about his house; and when he came home again from his cruise, he ordered me to lie in the cabin to look after the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 可我这个指望很快就落了空;因为他出海时,把我留在岸上照看他的小花园,干些奴隶在他家里干的粗活;等他巡航回来,又吩咐我睡在船舱里看船。

paragraphs.en: Here I meditated nothing but my escape, and what method I might take to effect it, but found no way that had the least probability in it; nothing presented to make the supposition of it rational; for I had nobody to communicate it to that would embark with me—no fellow-slave, no Englishman, Irishman, or Scotchman there but myself; so that for two years, though I often pleased myself with the imagination, yet I never had the least encouraging prospect of putting it in practice.
paragraphs.cn: 在这里,我一心只想着逃走,琢磨着该用什么法子才能得手,却始终找不到一条哪怕有一丝把握的路;没有任何条件能让这个念头显得靠谱;因为我没有人可以商量,没有人愿意跟我一起走——那里除了我自己,再没有别的奴隶,也没有英格兰人、爱尔兰人或苏格兰人;所以这两年里,尽管我常拿这个念头自娱,却从没有过一丝把它付诸实行的指望。

paragraphs.en: After about two years, an odd circumstance presented itself, which put the old thought of making some attempt for my liberty again in my head.
paragraphs.cn: 大约过了两年,一件古怪的事情出现了,又把设法争取自由的老念头勾回了我的脑子里。

paragraphs.en: My patron lying at home longer than usual without fitting out his ship, which, as I heard, was for want of money, he used constantly, once or twice a week, sometimes oftener if the weather was fair, to take the ship’s pinnace and go out into the road a-fishing; and as he always took me and young Maresco with him to row the boat, we made him very merry, and I proved very dexterous in catching fish; insomuch that sometimes he would send me with a Moor, one of his kinsmen, and the youth—the Maresco, as they called him—to catch a dish of fish for him.
paragraphs.cn: 我主人在家待的时间比往常都长,却迟迟不给船装备出海,据我听说是缺钱的缘故;他一向每周一两次、天气好时更勤些,乘船上的舢板出海到锚地去钓鱼;每回他都带上我和小马雷斯科替他划船,我们把他逗得挺开心,而我抓鱼又很在行;因此有时他会打发我,带上一个摩尔人——他的一个亲戚——和那个少年,也就是他们所称的马雷斯科,替他钓一盘鱼回来。

paragraphs.en: It happened one time, that going a-fishing in a calm morning, a fog rose so thick that, though we were not half a league from the shore, we lost sight of it; and rowing we knew not whither or which way, we laboured all day, and all the next night; and when the morning came we found we had pulled off to sea instead of pulling in for the shore; and that we were at least two leagues from the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 有一回,我们在一个风平浪静的早晨出海钓鱼,升起一场浓雾,浓得虽然离岸还不到半里格,却看不见岸了;我们划着船,不知划向何处、朝哪个方向,苦干了一整天和第二个通宵;等天亮时才发现,我们不是划向岸边,反倒划到海上去了,离岸至少有两里格远。

paragraphs.en: However, we got well in again, though with a great deal of labour and some danger; for the wind began to blow pretty fresh in the morning; but we were all very hungry.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我们费了好大的劲、冒了些险,总算又平安划了回来;因为清晨起了相当猛的风;而我们全都饿坏了。

paragraphs.en: But our patron, warned by this disaster, resolved to take more care of himself for the future; and having lying by him the longboat of our English ship that he had taken, he resolved he would not go a-fishing any more without a compass and some provision; so he ordered the carpenter of his ship, who also was an English slave, to build a little state-room, or cabin, in the middle of the long-boat, like that of a barge, with a place to stand behind it to steer, and haul home the main-sheet; the room before for a hand or two to stand and work the sails.
paragraphs.cn: 可我们的主人被这场祸事惊动,决意日后要多加小心;他手头正好有一艘他掳来的英国船的大艇,便打定主意,以后钓鱼没有罗盘和些许干粮就绝不出海;于是他吩咐船上的木匠——也是个英国奴隶——在大艇当中造一间小舱室,像驳船上那样,后面留出一块地方可以站着掌舵、收放主帆索;舱室前面则可以站一两个人操纵船帆。

paragraphs.en: She sailed with what we call a shoulder-of-mutton sail; and the boom jibed over the top of the cabin, which lay very snug and low, and had in it room for him to lie, with a slave or two, and a table to eat on, with some small lockers to put in some bottles of such liquor as he thought fit to drink; and his bread, rice, and coffee.
paragraphs.cn: 这船挂的是我们所说的那种羊肩帆;帆的下桁越过舱顶转来转去,那舱又稳当又低矮,里面容得下他躺卧,带上一两个奴隶,还有一张吃饭的桌子,几只小柜子用来放几瓶他爱喝的酒;还有他的面包、大米和咖啡。

paragraphs.en: We went frequently out with this boat a-fishing; and as I was most dexterous to catch fish for him, he never went without me.
paragraphs.cn: 我们常乘这条船出海钓鱼;而由于我替他抓鱼最在行,他出海从不落下我。

paragraphs.en: It happened that he had appointed to go out in this boat, either for pleasure or for fish, with two or three Moors of some distinction in that place, and for whom he had provided extraordinarily, and had, therefore, sent on board the boat overnight a larger store of provisions than ordinary; and had ordered me to get ready three fusees with powder and shot, which were on board his ship, for that they designed some sport of fowling as well as fishing.
paragraphs.cn: 有一回,他约好要乘这条船出去,或是游玩,或是钓鱼,同行的还有当地两三位有身份的摩尔人,他为此格外备了些东西,便在头天晚上就往船上送了比平常更多的粮食;还吩咐我把船上的三支火枪连同火药、铁砂都备好,因为他们打算既钓鱼,也打打野禽取乐。

paragraphs.en: I got all things ready as he had directed, and waited the next morning with the boat washed clean, her ancient and pendants out, and everything to accommodate his guests; when by-and-by my patron came on board alone, and told me his guests had put off going from some business that fell out, and ordered me, with the man and boy, as usual, to go out with the boat and catch them some fish, for that his friends were to sup at his house, and commanded that as soon as I got some fish I should bring it home to his house; all which I prepared to do.
paragraphs.cn: 我照他吩咐把一切都备齐了,第二天早晨等着,船已洗得干干净净,船旗和飘带都挂了出来,一切都张罗妥当,好招待他的客人;不多会儿,我主人独自上了船,告诉我他的客人因临时有事推掉了这趟出行,便吩咐我照旧带上那男人和男孩,驾船出去替他钓些鱼,因为他的朋友要到他家来吃晚饭,又命我一钓到鱼就赶紧送回他家去;这一切我都张罗着去办。

paragraphs.en: This moment my former notions of deliverance darted into my thoughts, for now I found I was likely to have a little ship at my command; and my master being gone, I prepared to furnish myself, not for fishing business, but for a voyage; though I knew not, neither did I so much as consider, whither I should steer—anywhere to get out of that place was my desire.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这一刻,我先前那些出逃的念头猛地闪进了脑海,因为我发现自己眼看就要有一条小船听我调遣了;主人一走,我便动手替自己作准备,不是为钓鱼,而是为一场航行;虽说我不知道、甚至也压根没去想该往哪里驶——只要能离开那地方,去哪儿都行,这就是我的心愿。

paragraphs.en: My first contrivance was to make a pretence to speak to this Moor, to get something for our subsistence on board; for I told him we must not presume to eat of our patron’s bread.
paragraphs.cn: 我头一个花招,是找借口去跟那摩尔人搭话,好弄些吃的上船;因为我对他说,我们可不能擅自吃主人的面包。

paragraphs.en: He said that was true; so he brought a large basket of rusk or biscuit, and three jars of fresh water, into the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 他说这话不错;于是他往船上搬来一大篮硬面包或饼干,还有三罐淡水。

paragraphs.en: I knew where my patron’s case of bottles stood, which it was evident, by the make, were taken out of some English prize, and I conveyed them into the boat while the Moor was on shore, as if they had been there before for our master.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道我主人那箱酒放在哪里,从样式看,分明是从某艘英国战利品船上取来的,趁那摩尔人上岸时,我把它们搬进了船,仿佛它们原本就是为主人放在那里的。

paragraphs.en: I conveyed also a great lump of beeswax into the boat, which weighed about half a hundred-weight, with a parcel of twine or thread, a hatchet, a saw, and a hammer, all of which were of great use to us afterwards, especially the wax, to make candles.
paragraphs.cn: 我还往船上搬了一大块蜂蜡,约莫有半英担重,连同一捆麻线或棉线、一把短柄斧、一把锯子和一把锤子,这些日后都对我们大有用处,尤其是那蜡,可以用来做蜡烛。

paragraphs.en: Another trick I tried upon him, which he innocently came into also: his name was Ismael, which they call Muley, or Moely; so I called to him—“Moely,” said I, “our patron’s guns are on board the boat; can you not get a little powder and shot?
paragraphs.cn: 我还对他耍了另一个花招,他也一样天真地上了钩:他名叫伊斯梅尔,他们管这名字叫穆莱或莫里;于是我招呼他——“莫里,”我说,“主人的枪都在船上了;你能不能弄点火药和铁砂来?

paragraphs.en: It may be we may kill some alcamies (a fowl like our curlews) for ourselves, for I know he keeps the gunner’s stores in the ship.”
paragraphs.cn: 说不定我们能替自己打几只阿尔卡米(一种像我们这里麻鹬的鸟),我知道他把火枪手的军需都存在船上呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” says he, “I’ll bring some;” and accordingly he brought a great leather pouch, which held a pound and a half of powder, or rather more; and another with shot, that had five or six pounds, with some bullets, and put all into the boat.
paragraphs.cn: “行,”他说,“我去拿点来;”于是他果真拿来一只大皮袋,装着一磅半火药,或许还多些;又拿来一只装铁砂的,足有五六磅,还带了些子弹,统统放进了船里。

paragraphs.en: At the same time I had found some powder of my master’s in the great cabin, with which I filled one of the large bottles in the case, which was almost empty, pouring what was in it into another; and thus furnished with everything needful, we sailed out of the port to fish.
paragraphs.cn: 与此同时,我在大舱里找到了些主人的火药,便用它把箱子里一只几乎空了的大瓶灌满,原先瓶里那点残酒则倒进了另一只瓶;这样一来,一切必需之物都齐备了,我们便驶出港口去钓鱼。

paragraphs.en: The castle, which is at the entrance of the port, knew who we were, and took no notice of us; and we were not above a mile out of the port before we hauled in our sail and set us down to fish.
paragraphs.cn: 港口入口处的那座城堡认得我们,并没在意;我们出港还不到一英里,就收起帆坐下来钓鱼。

paragraphs.en: The wind blew from the N.
paragraphs.cn: 风从北方吹来

paragraphs.en: N.
paragraphs.cn: 偏

paragraphs.en: E.
paragraphs.cn: 东

paragraphs.en: , which was contrary to my desire, for had it blown southerly I had been sure to have made the coast of Spain, and at least reached to the bay of Cadiz; but my resolutions were, blow which way it would, I would be gone from that horrid place where I was, and leave the rest to fate.
paragraphs.cn: ,这跟我的心愿恰恰相反,因为若是刮南风,我准能抵达西班牙海岸,至少能到加的斯湾;可我打定的主意是,不管风往哪儿刮,我都要离开我所在的那个可怕地方,其余的听天由命。

paragraphs.en: After we had fished some time and caught nothing—for when I had fish on my hook I would not pull them up, that he might not see them—I said to the Moor, “This will not do; our master will not be thus served; we must stand farther off.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们钓了一阵子,什么也没钓着——因为我钩上有鱼时,故意不把它们拉上来,免得让他看见——我便对那摩尔人说:“这样不行;主人可不能就这么打发;我们得再往远处去。”

paragraphs.en: He, thinking no harm, agreed, and being in the head of the boat, set the sails; and, as I had the helm, I ran the boat out near a league farther, and then brought her to, as if I would fish; when, giving the boy the helm, I stepped forward to where the Moor was, and making as if I stooped for something behind him, I took him by surprise with my arm under his waist, and tossed him clear overboard into the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 他没起疑,答应了,他在船头,便去张帆;而我掌着舵,把船又开出将近一里格远,然后叫它停住,装作要钓鱼的样子;这时我把舵交给那男孩,自己朝摩尔人所在的船头走去,假装弯腰去拾他身后的什么东西,趁其不备,一条胳膊搂住他的腰,把他直接掀出了船,抛进了海里。

paragraphs.en: He rose immediately, for he swam like a cork, and called to me, begged to be taken in, told me he would go all over the world with me.
paragraphs.cn: 他立刻浮了上来,因为他游泳像个软木塞一样,他向我喊话,央求我把他拉上来,说他愿意跟我走遍天涯海角。

paragraphs.en: He swam so strong after the boat that he would have reached me very quickly, there being but little wind; upon which I stepped into the cabin, and fetching one of the fowling-pieces, I presented it at him, and told him I had done him no hurt, and if he would be quiet I would do him none.
paragraphs.cn: 他在船后游得那样有力,眼看很快就要够到我了,那时风又小;于是我跨进舱里,取出一支猎枪,对准他,告诉他我并没伤他,只要他安分,我也不会伤他。

paragraphs.en: “But,” said I, “you swim well enough to reach to the shore, and the sea is calm; make the best of your way to shore, and I will do you no harm; but if you come near the boat I’ll shoot you through the head, for I am resolved to have my liberty;” so he turned himself about, and swam for the shore, and I make no doubt but he reached it with ease, for he was an excellent swimmer.
paragraphs.cn: “不过,”我说,“你游得够好,能游回岸边,海面又平静;赶紧往岸上去,我不会加害于你;可你要是靠近这船,我就一枪打穿你的脑袋,因为我决意要争取自由;”于是他掉转身,朝岸边游去,我毫不怀疑他轻而易举就游到了,因为他是个出色的游泳好手。

paragraphs.en: I could have been content to have taken this Moor with me, and have drowned the boy, but there was no venturing to trust him.
paragraphs.cn: 我本可以乐得把这摩尔人一起带走,而把那男孩淹死,可是这摩尔人万万信不得。

paragraphs.en: When he was gone, I turned to the boy, whom they called Xury, and said to him, “Xury, if you will be faithful to me, I’ll make you a great man; but if you will not stroke your face to be true to me”—that is, swear by Mahomet and his father’s beard—“I must throw you into the sea too.”
paragraphs.cn: 他一走,我便转向那男孩——他们管他叫佐立——对他说:“佐立,你要是肯对我忠心,我就让你出人头地;可你要是不肯抚面起誓对我忠诚”——就是指着穆罕默德和他父亲的胡须发誓——“我就只好把你也扔进海里。”

paragraphs.en: The boy smiled in my face, and spoke so innocently that I could not distrust him, and swore to be faithful to me, and go all over the world with me.
paragraphs.cn: 那男孩冲着我的脸微微一笑,说得那样天真,叫我无法不信他,他起誓要对我忠心,愿跟我走遍天下。

paragraphs.en: While I was in view of the Moor that was swimming, I stood out directly to sea with the boat, rather stretching to windward, that they might think me gone towards the Straits’ mouth (as indeed any one that had been in their wits must have been supposed to do): for who would have supposed we were sailed on to the southward, to the truly Barbarian coast, where whole nations of negroes were sure to surround us with their canoes and destroy us; where we could not go on shore but we should be devoured by savage beasts, or more merciless savages of human kind.
paragraphs.cn: 趁那游水的摩尔人还望得见我时,我径直把船朝海上开去,略微抢向上风,好让他们以为我是往直布罗陀海峡口去了(其实,凡是有点头脑的人,都会料想我这么走):因为谁会想到我们竟一路往南开去,驶向那真正的野蛮海岸,那里成群结队的黑人必定驾着独木舟把我们团团围住,将我们杀害;在那里我们一上岸,不是被野兽吞掉,便是被比野兽更狠心的野人吞掉。

paragraphs.en: But as soon as it grew dusk in the evening, I changed my course, and steered directly south and by east, bending my course a little towards the east, that I might keep in with the shore; and having a fair, fresh gale of wind, and a smooth, quiet sea, I made such sail that I believe by the next day, at three o’clock in the afternoon, when I first made the land, I could not be less than one hundred and fifty miles south of Sallee; quite beyond the Emperor of Morocco’s dominions, or indeed of any other king thereabouts, for we saw no people.
paragraphs.cn: 可是傍晚天色一暗下来,我便改了航向,径直朝南偏东驶去,把航向稍稍偏东,好让自己贴着海岸走;仗着一阵顺畅的清风和一片平静的海面,我把帆张得那么足,我相信到第二天下午三点,我头一回望见陆地时,离萨累已不下一百五十英里的南方了;早已越出摩洛哥皇帝的疆域,其实也越出了那一带任何别的国王的地界,因为我们看不见一个人。

paragraphs.en: Yet such was the fright I had taken of the Moors, and the dreadful apprehensions I had of falling into their hands, that I would not stop, or go on shore, or come to an anchor; the wind continuing fair till I had sailed in that manner five days; and then the wind shifting to the southward, I concluded also that if any of our vessels were in chase of me, they also would now give over; so I ventured to make to the coast, and came to an anchor in the mouth of a little river, I knew not what, nor where, neither what latitude, what country, what nation, or what river.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我对摩尔人怕到了那般地步,一想到落进他们手里就万分惊惧,以致我不肯停下,不肯上岸,也不肯抛锚;顺风一直吹到我这样航行了五天;这时风转向了南方,我便断定,即便我们有哪艘船在追我,如今大概也放弃了;于是我壮起胆子驶向海岸,在一条小河的河口抛了锚,可我不知道那是什么河,不知在何处,也不知是什么纬度、什么国土、什么民族、什么河流。

paragraphs.en: I neither saw, nor desired to see any people; the principal thing I wanted was fresh water.
paragraphs.cn: 我既没看见,也不指望看见什么人;我最想要的东西就是淡水。

paragraphs.en: We came into this creek in the evening, resolving to swim on shore as soon as it was dark, and discover the country; but as soon as it was quite dark, we heard such dreadful noises of the barking, roaring, and howling of wild creatures, of we knew not what kinds, that the poor boy was ready to die with fear, and begged of me not to go on shore till day.
paragraphs.cn: 我们傍晚驶进这条小河汊,打算天一黑就游上岸去探探这片地方;可天刚一黑透,我们就听见那样可怕的声音——种种叫不出名目的野兽的吠叫、咆哮和嗥叫——吓得那可怜的男孩魂飞魄散,央求我天亮前别上岸。

paragraphs.en: “Well, Xury,” said I, “then I won’t; but it may be that we may see men by day, who will be as bad to us as those lions.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧,佐立,”我说,“那我就不上;不过说不定白天我们会碰见人,他们对我们兴许跟那些狮子一样凶呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Then we give them the shoot gun,” says Xury, laughing, “make them run wey.”
paragraphs.cn: “那我们就给他们一枪,”佐立笑着说,“叫他们跑掉。”

paragraphs.en: Such English Xury spoke by conversing among us slaves.
paragraphs.cn: 佐立会说这样的英语,是在我们这些奴隶中间交谈学来的。

paragraphs.en: However, I was glad to see the boy so cheerful, and I gave him a dram (out of our patron’s case of bottles) to cheer him up.
paragraphs.cn: 不管怎样,看到这男孩这么高兴,我心里也欢喜,便给了他一口酒(从我们主人那箱瓶酒里倒的),给他提提神。

paragraphs.en: After all, Xury’s advice was good, and I took it; we dropped our little anchor, and lay still all night; I say still, for we slept none; for in two or three hours we saw vast great creatures (we knew not what to call them) of many sorts, come down to the sea-shore and run into the water, wallowing and washing themselves for the pleasure of cooling themselves; and they made such hideous howlings and yellings, that I never indeed heard the like.
paragraphs.cn: 说到底,佐立的主意是好的,我采纳了;我们抛下小锚,整夜都停着不动;我说停着不动,其实我们一点没睡;因为两三个钟头里,我们看见许多种庞然大物(我们不知该叫它们什么)从海边下来,跑进水里,为了图个凉快而翻滚洗浴;它们发出那样吓人的嗥叫和号鸣,我当真从没听见过那样的声音。

paragraphs.en: Xury was dreadfully frighted, and indeed so was I too; but we were both more frighted when we heard one of these mighty creatures come swimming towards our boat; we could not see him, but we might hear him by his blowing to be a monstrous huge and furious beast.
paragraphs.cn: 佐立吓坏了,说实话我也是;可当我们听见其中一头巨兽朝我们的船游来时,两人都更害怕了;我们看不见它,却能凭它喷水的声音听出那是一头庞大凶猛的野兽。

paragraphs.en: Xury said it was a lion, and it might be so for aught I know; but poor Xury cried to me to weigh the anchor and row away; “No,” says I, “Xury; we can slip our cable, with the buoy to it, and go off to sea; they cannot follow us far.”
paragraphs.cn: 佐立说那是头狮子,也许当真是,反正我也不知道;可怜的佐立哭着求我起锚划走;“不,”我说,“佐立;我们可以松掉锚缆,连着浮标一起丢下,开到海上去;它们追不了我们多远。”

paragraphs.en: I had no sooner said so, but I perceived the creature (whatever it was) within two oars’ length, which something surprised me; however, I immediately stepped to the cabin door, and taking up my gun, fired at him; upon which he immediately turned about and swam towards the shore again.
paragraphs.cn: 话刚出口,我就发觉那头动物(不管它是什么)已到了两支桨那么远的地方,这多少叫我一惊;不过我立刻跨到舱门口,举起枪来朝它开了一火;它当即掉头,又朝岸边游了回去。

paragraphs.en: But it is impossible to describe the horrid noises, and hideous cries and howlings that were raised, as well upon the edge of the shore as higher within the country, upon the noise or report of the gun, a thing I have some reason to believe those creatures had never heard before: this convinced me that there was no going on shore for us in the night on that coast, and how to venture on shore in the day was another question too; for to have fallen into the hands of any of the savages had been as bad as to have fallen into the hands of the lions and tigers; at least we were equally apprehensive of the danger of it.
paragraphs.cn: 可枪声一响,岸边乃至内陆更远处,顿时掀起了那样可怕的声浪、那样凄厉的号叫和嗥鸣——那是我有理由相信那些野兽从前从没听过的声音;真是笔墨难以形容:这使我确信,在那海岸,夜里我们是绝不能上岸的,而白天怎么冒险上岸,又是另一个难题;因为落进任何野人手里,和落进狮子、老虎口中同样糟糕;至少我们对这两种危险同样心惊胆战。

paragraphs.en: Be that as it would, we were obliged to go on shore somewhere or other for water, for we had not a pint left in the boat; when and where to get to it was the point.
paragraphs.cn: 无论如何,我们总得找个地方上岸取水,因为船里连一品脱水也不剩了;问题是何时、何地才取得到。

paragraphs.en: Xury said, if I would let him go on shore with one of the jars, he would find if there was any water, and bring some to me.
paragraphs.cn: 佐立说,只要我肯让他带上一只罐子上岸,他就去看看有没有水,给我打些来。

paragraphs.en: I asked him why he would go? why I should not go, and he stay in the boat?
paragraphs.cn: 我问他为什么要他去?为什么不是我去,由他留在船上?

paragraphs.en: The boy answered with so much affection as made me love him ever after.
paragraphs.cn: 那男孩答得那样深情,叫我从此一辈子疼爱他。

paragraphs.en: Says he, “If wild mans come, they eat me, you go wey.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“要是野人来了,他们吃我,你就开走。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, Xury,” said I, “we will both go and if the wild mans come, we will kill them, they shall eat neither of us.”
paragraphs.cn: “好,佐立,”我说,“我们俩一块儿去,野人要是来了,我们就宰了他们,谁也别想吃掉我们。”

paragraphs.en: So I gave Xury a piece of rusk bread to eat, and a dram out of our patron’s case of bottles which I mentioned before; and we hauled the boat in as near the shore as we thought was proper, and so waded on shore, carrying nothing but our arms and two jars for water.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我给了佐立一块硬面包吃,又从前面提过的主人那箱瓶酒里倒了一口给他;我们把船尽量往岸边靠拢到觉得合适的地方,便涉水上了岸,除了武器和两只取水的罐子,别的什么都没带。

paragraphs.en: I did not care to go out of sight of the boat, fearing the coming of canoes with savages down the river; but the boy seeing a low place about a mile up the country, rambled to it, and by-and-by I saw him come running towards me.
paragraphs.cn: 我不敢走出望不见船的地方,生怕有野人驾着独木舟顺河而下;可那男孩看见约莫一英里外的内陆有块低洼地,便溜达过去了,不多会儿,我看见他朝我跑来。

paragraphs.en: I thought he was pursued by some savage, or frighted with some wild beast, and I ran forward towards him to help him; but when I came nearer to him I saw something hanging over his shoulders, which was a creature that he had shot, like a hare, but different in colour, and longer legs; however, we were very glad of it, and it was very good meat; but the great joy that poor Xury came with, was to tell me he had found good water and seen no wild mans.
paragraphs.cn: 我以为他被什么野人追着,或是被什么野兽吓着了,便迎上前去帮他;可等我走近了,才看见他肩上搭着个什么东西,原来是他打死的一只动物,像野兔,却颜色不同、腿更长;不管怎样,我们都很高兴,那肉也很好吃;可这可怜的佐立带来的天大喜讯,是告诉我他找到了好水,又没见着一个野人。

paragraphs.en: But we found afterwards that we need not take such pains for water, for a little higher up the creek where we were we found the water fresh when the tide was out, which flowed but a little way up; so we filled our jars, and feasted on the hare he had killed, and prepared to go on our way, having seen no footsteps of any human creature in that part of the country.
paragraphs.cn: 可我们后来才发现,取水根本用不着费这么大劲,因为在我们所在的小河汊往上一点,潮退时水就是淡的,而潮水也只上涨一小段;于是我们灌满了罐子,饱餐了他打死的那只野兔,又准备上路,一路上在那片地方没见着一个人的脚印。

paragraphs.en: As I had been one voyage to this coast before, I knew very well that the islands of the Canaries, and the Cape de Verde Islands also, lay not far off from the coast.
paragraphs.cn: 由于我从前来过这海岸一趟,我很清楚加那利群岛,还有佛得角群岛,离这海岸都不算远。

paragraphs.en: But as I had no instruments to take an observation to know what latitude we were in, and not exactly knowing, or at least remembering, what latitude they were in, I knew not where to look for them, or when to stand off to sea towards them; otherwise I might now easily have found some of these islands.
paragraphs.cn: 可是我没有仪器观测方位,弄不清我们身处什么纬度,又不确切知道、或至少记不清那些岛屿在什么纬度,所以我不知该往哪里找它们,也不知该何时驶向海面去靠近它们;不然,我这会儿本可以轻易找到其中某个岛的。

paragraphs.en: But my hope was, that if I stood along this coast till I came to that part where the English traded, I should find some of their vessels upon their usual design of trade, that would relieve and take us in.
paragraphs.cn: 但我的指望是,只要我沿着这海岸走,走到英国人做买卖的那一带,就能碰上他们的船照例来做贸易,好搭救我们、把我们接上去。

paragraphs.en: By the best of my calculation, that place where I now was must be that country which, lying between the Emperor of Morocco’s dominions and the negroes, lies waste and uninhabited, except by wild beasts; the negroes having abandoned it and gone farther south for fear of the Moors, and the Moors not thinking it worth inhabiting by reason of its barrenness; and indeed, both forsaking it because of the prodigious number of tigers, lions, leopards, and other furious creatures which harbour there; so that the Moors use it for their hunting only, where they go like an army, two or three thousand men at a time; and indeed for near a hundred miles together upon this coast we saw nothing but a waste, uninhabited country by day, and heard nothing but howlings and roaring of wild beasts by night.
paragraphs.cn: 照我最靠谱的推算,我此刻所在的这地方,准是那片夹在摩洛哥皇帝疆域和黑人地界之间、荒废无人烟、只有野兽出没的国土;黑人因怕摩尔人而弃了它、往更南边去了,摩尔人又嫌它贫瘠、不值得居住;其实,两下都因这里出没着数不清的老虎、狮子、豹子和别的凶猛野兽而将它舍弃;所以摩尔人只拿它当猎场,一去就像一支军队,一次两三千人;而这海岸沿线将近一百英里,我们白天所见,无非是一片荒废无人烟的国土,夜里所闻,无非是野兽的嗥叫和咆哮。

paragraphs.en: Once or twice in the daytime I thought I saw the Pico of Teneriffe, being the high top of the Mountain Teneriffe in the Canaries, and had a great mind to venture out, in hopes of reaching thither; but having tried twice, I was forced in again by contrary winds, the sea also going too high for my little vessel; so, I resolved to pursue my first design, and keep along the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 白天里有一两回,我以为望见了特纳里夫峰,就是加那利群岛特纳里夫山那高高的顶峰,便很想冒险出海,盼着能到那儿去;可试了两回,都叫逆风逼了回来,海浪对我这条小船来说也太高;于是我决意还是照最初的打算,沿着海岸走。

paragraphs.en: Several times I was obliged to land for fresh water, after we had left this place; and once in particular, being early in morning, we came to an anchor under a little point of land, which was pretty high; and the tide beginning to flow, we lay still to go farther in.
paragraphs.cn: 离开那地方之后,我好几回不得不上岸取淡水;有一回尤其记得,那是清晨,我们在一块相当高的小岬角下抛了锚;潮水开始上涨,我们便停着不动,好再往里驶。

paragraphs.en: Xury, whose eyes were more about him than it seems mine were, calls softly to me, and tells me that we had best go farther off the shore; “For,” says he, “look, yonder lies a dreadful monster on the side of that hillock, fast asleep.”
paragraphs.cn: 佐立的眼睛比我的似乎要尖,他轻轻招呼我,说我们最好离岸远些;“因为,”他说,“瞧,那边小丘坡上躺着一头可怕的怪物,睡得正香。”

paragraphs.en: I looked where he pointed, and saw a dreadful monster indeed, for it was a terrible, great lion that lay on the side of the shore, under the shade of a piece of the hill that hung as it were a little over him.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝他指的地方望去,果然看见一头可怕的怪物,原来是一头吓人的大狮子,躺在岸边坡上,借着一块仿佛微微探出、罩在它头顶的山石的阴影。

paragraphs.en: “Xury,” says I, “you shall go on shore and kill him.”
paragraphs.cn: “佐立,”我说,“你上岸去把它打死。”

paragraphs.en: Xury, looked frighted, and said, “Me kill! he eat me at one mouth!”
paragraphs.cn: 佐立露出害怕的样子,说:“我打死它!它一口就把我吃掉!”

paragraphs.en: —one mouthful he meant.
paragraphs.cn: ——他是说一口吞掉。

paragraphs.en: However, I said no more to the boy, but bade him lie still, and I took our biggest gun, which was almost musket-bore, and loaded it with a good charge of powder, and with two slugs, and laid it down; then I loaded another gun with two bullets; and the third (for we had three pieces) I loaded with five smaller bullets.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我没再对这男孩多说什么,只叫他躺着别动,自己拿起我们最大的那支枪,口径几乎有火枪那么大,装上足量的火药和两颗大铅弹,把它搁下;接着又给另一支枪装上两颗子弹;第三支(因为我们有三支枪)则装上五颗小些的子弹。

paragraphs.en: I took the best aim I could with the first piece to have shot him in the head, but he lay so with his leg raised a little above his nose, that the slugs hit his leg about the knee and broke the bone.
paragraphs.cn: 我用头一支枪尽量瞄准,想打它的脑袋,可它躺的姿势,一条腿略略抬到鼻子上头,结果那两颗大铅弹打中了它膝盖附近的腿,把骨头打断了。

paragraphs.en: He started up, growling at first, but finding his leg broken, fell down again; and then got upon three legs, and gave the most hideous roar that ever I heard.
paragraphs.cn: 它一跃而起,起先咆哮着,可发觉腿断了,又倒了下去;随后靠三条腿撑起身,发出我平生听过的最吓人的一声吼。

paragraphs.en: I was a little surprised that I had not hit him on the head; however, I took up the second piece immediately, and though he began to move off, fired again, and shot him in the head, and had the pleasure to see him drop and make but little noise, but lie struggling for life.
paragraphs.cn: 我有点意外,竟没打中它的脑袋;不过我立刻抄起第二支枪,尽管它已开始挪走,我还是又开了一火,打中了它的脑袋,痛快地看着它倒下,几乎没出多大声响,只是挣扎着求生。

paragraphs.en: Then Xury took heart, and would have me let him go on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 这下佐立胆壮了,非要我让他上岸不可。

paragraphs.en: “Well, go,” said I: so the boy jumped into the water and taking a little gun in one hand, swam to shore with the other hand, and coming close to the creature, put the muzzle of the piece to his ear, and shot him in the head again, which despatched him quite.
paragraphs.cn: “好,去吧,”我说:那男孩便跳进水里,一手拿着一支小枪,另一只手划水游到岸边,凑近那头野兽,把枪口抵在它耳朵上,又朝它脑袋开了一火,这一下便把它彻底结果了。

paragraphs.en: This was game indeed to us, but this was no food; and I was very sorry to lose three charges of powder and shot upon a creature that was good for nothing to us.
paragraphs.cn: 这对我们来说倒真是场好猎,可这算不上食物;我很懊丧,白白在一头对我们毫无用处的野兽身上耗掉了三份火药和铁砂。

paragraphs.en: However, Xury said he would have some of him; so he comes on board, and asked me to give him the hatchet.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,佐立说他要弄它身上的点什么;于是他上了船,向我讨那把短柄斧。

paragraphs.en: “For what, Xury?” said I.
paragraphs.cn: “要它干什么,佐立?”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Me cut off his head,” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “我砍下它的头,”他说。

paragraphs.en: However, Xury could not cut off his head, but he cut off a foot, and brought it with him, and it was a monstrous great one.
paragraphs.cn: 然而佐立砍不下它的头,却砍下了一只脚,带了回来,那脚大得吓人。

paragraphs.en: I bethought myself, however, that, perhaps the skin of him might, one way or other, be of some value to us; and I resolved to take off his skin if I could.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我转念一想,或许它的皮多少对我们有点用处;便决意能剥就把它的皮剥下来。

paragraphs.en: So Xury and I went to work with him; but Xury was much the better workman at it, for I knew very ill how to do it.
paragraphs.cn: 于是佐立和我便动手对付它;可佐立干这活儿比我在行得多,因为我实在不大会剥。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, it took us both up the whole day, but at last we got off the hide of him, and spreading it on the top of our cabin, the sun effectually dried it in two days’ time, and it afterwards served me to lie upon.
paragraphs.cn: 说实话,这活儿把我们俩整整耗了一天,不过末了我们总算把它的皮剥了下来,摊在舱顶上,太阳花了两天工夫把它彻底晒干,后来它便成了我躺卧的垫子。

paragraphs.en: After this stop, we made on to the southward continually for ten or twelve days, living very sparingly on our provisions, which began to abate very much, and going no oftener to the shore than we were obliged to for fresh water.
paragraphs.cn: 这次停泊之后,我们一连往南航行了十来天,粮食吃得非常省,因为存粮开始大大减少;除非为了取淡水不得不上岸,我们尽量不靠岸。

paragraphs.en: My design in this was to make the river Gambia or Senegal, that is to say anywhere about the Cape de Verde, where I was in hopes to meet with some European ship; and if I did not, I knew not what course I had to take, but to seek for the islands, or perish there among the negroes.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样做的打算,是想到达冈比亚河或塞内加尔河,也就是佛得角一带的某个地方,指望能在那儿遇上一艘欧洲船;万一遇不上,我就不知道该怎么办了,只能去找那些岛屿,不然就死在黑人中间。

paragraphs.en: I knew that all the ships from Europe, which sailed either to the coast of Guinea or to Brazil, or to the East Indies, made this cape, or those islands; and, in a word, I put the whole of my fortune upon this single point, either that I must meet with some ship or must perish.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道,凡是从欧洲开往几内亚海岸、或巴西、或东印度群岛的船,都要经过这个海角或那些岛屿;总之,我把自己全部的命运都押在这一点上——要么遇上一条船,要么就此丧命。

paragraphs.en: When I had pursued this resolution about ten days longer, as I have said, I began to see that the land was inhabited; and in two or three places, as we sailed by, we saw people stand upon the shore to look at us; we could also perceive they were quite black and naked.
paragraphs.cn: 照我说的,又这样坚持航行了十来天以后,我开始看出这一带是有人居住的;有两三处地方,我们驶过时看见有人站在岸上望着我们;还能看清他们浑身乌黑,一丝不挂。

paragraphs.en: I was once inclined to have gone on shore to them; but Xury was my better counsellor, and said to me, “No go, no go.”
paragraphs.cn: 我一度想上岸去找他们;可是佐立比我有见识,他对我说:“别去,别去。”

paragraphs.en: However, I hauled in nearer the shore that I might talk to them, and I found they ran along the shore by me a good way.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我还是把船靠近了些岸,好跟他们说说话,我发现他们沿着岸边跟着我跑了好长一段路。

paragraphs.en: I observed they had no weapons in their hand, except one, who had a long slender stick, which Xury said was a lance, and that they could throw them a great way with good aim; so I kept at a distance, but talked with them by signs as well as I could; and particularly made signs for something to eat: they beckoned to me to stop my boat, and they would fetch me some meat.
paragraphs.cn: 我注意到他们手里没有武器,只有一个人拿着一根又长又细的棍子,佐立说那是标枪,说他们能把它掷得很远,而且掷得很准;所以我保持着距离,只尽量用手势跟他们交谈;我特别打手势要点吃的:他们招手要我把船停下,说要给我拿些肉来。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I lowered the top of my sail and lay by, and two of them ran up into the country, and in less than half-an-hour came back, and brought with them two pieces of dried flesh and some corn, such as is the produce of their country; but we neither knew what the one or the other was; however, we were willing to accept it, but how to come at it was our next dispute, for I would not venture on shore to them, and they were as much afraid of us; but they took a safe way for us all, for they brought it to the shore and laid it down, and went and stood a great way off till we fetched it on board, and then came close to us again.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我降下船帆停了下来,他们中有两个人往内陆跑去,不到半个钟头就回来了,带来两块干肉和一些谷子,是他们那地方出产的东西;可这两样我们都不认得;不过我们还是愿意收下,可怎么拿到手又成了难题,因为我不敢上岸去找他们,他们也一样怕我们;但他们想出了一个对大家都稳妥的办法:他们把东西送到岸边放下,然后走开,远远地站着,等我们取上了船,才又走近我们。
