paragraphs.en: We made signs of thanks to them, for we had nothing to make them amends; but an opportunity offered that very instant to oblige them wonderfully; for while we were lying by the shore came two mighty creatures, one pursuing the other (as we took it) with great fury from the mountains towards the sea; whether it was the male pursuing the female, or whether they were in sport or in rage, we could not tell, any more than we could tell whether it was usual or strange, but I believe it was the latter; because, in the first place, those ravenous creatures seldom appear but in the night; and, in the second place, we found the people terribly frighted, especially the women.
paragraphs.cn: 我们向他们打手势道谢,因为我们没什么东西可回报他们;可就在这时,恰好有个机会让我们大大地帮了他们一把;原来我们停在岸边时,来了两只巨兽,像是一只在拼命追赶另一只,气势汹汹地从山里往海边冲来;到底是公的追母的,还是它们在嬉戏,或是在发怒,我们说不上来,正如我们也说不清这是常见还是稀罕的事,不过我相信是稀罕的;因为,第一,那种凶猛的野兽很少在夜晚以外出现;第二,我们看见那些人吓得要命,尤其是女人。

paragraphs.en: The man that had the lance or dart did not fly from them, but the rest did; however, as the two creatures ran directly into the water, they did not offer to fall upon any of the negroes, but plunged themselves into the sea, and swam about, as if they had come for their diversion; at last one of them began to come nearer our boat than at first I expected; but I lay ready for him, for I had loaded my gun with all possible expedition, and bade Xury load both the others.
paragraphs.cn: 拿着标枪或投枪的那个人没有逃走,其余的人都逃了;不过那两只野兽一直冲进了水里,并没有去扑那些黑人,而是纵身跳进海中,游来游去,好像是来玩耍似的;末了,其中一只开始比我起初料想的更靠近我们的船;可我早有准备,因为我已经飞快地把枪装好了弹药,还叫佐立把另外两支也装上。

paragraphs.en: As soon as he came fairly within my reach, I fired, and shot him directly in the head; immediately he sank down into the water, but rose instantly, and plunged up and down, as if he were struggling for life, and so indeed he was; he immediately made to the shore; but between the wound, which was his mortal hurt, and the strangling of the water, he died just before he reached the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 等它一进入我的射程之内,我就开了枪,正打中它的脑袋;它立刻沉入水中,却又马上浮起来,上下扑腾,像是在挣扎求生,它确实是在挣命;它随即朝岸边游去;可是既受了那致命的伤,又被水呛着,它没游到岸边就死了。

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to express the astonishment of these poor creatures at the noise and fire of my gun: some of them were even ready to die for fear, and fell down as dead with the very terror; but when they saw the creature dead, and sunk in the water, and that I made signs to them to come to the shore, they took heart and came, and began to search for the creature.
paragraphs.cn: 我这枪的响声和火光叫那些可怜的人惊骇得无法形容:有几个人甚至吓得半死,只因这一惊便像死了一样倒了下去;可当他们看见那野兽死了、沉进了水里,又见我打手势叫他们到岸边来,他们才壮起胆子走过来,开始寻找那只野兽。

paragraphs.en: I found him by his blood staining the water; and by the help of a rope, which I slung round him, and gave the negroes to haul, they dragged him on shore, and found that it was a most curious leopard, spotted, and fine to an admirable degree; and the negroes held up their hands with admiration, to think what it was I had killed him with.
paragraphs.cn: 我凭着它的血把水染红找到了它;我用一根绳子套在它身上,把绳子递给黑人们去拉,他们便把它拖上了岸,发现那是一头极其罕见的豹子,身上有斑点,漂亮得叫人赞叹;黑人们举起双手连声惊叹,想不出我是用什么东西把它打死的。

paragraphs.en: The other creature, frighted with the flash of fire and the noise of the gun, swam on shore, and ran up directly to the mountains from whence they came; nor could I, at that distance, know what it was.
paragraphs.cn: 另一只野兽被枪的火光和响声吓着了,游上岸去,一直朝它们来的那些山里跑去;隔着那么远,我也认不出它是什么。

paragraphs.en: I found quickly the negroes wished to eat the flesh of this creature, so I was willing to have them take it as a favour from me; which, when I made signs to them that they might take him, they were very thankful for.
paragraphs.cn: 我很快发现黑人们想吃这只野兽的肉,于是我愿意让他们把它当作我送的一份人情收下;当我打手势告诉他们可以把它拿去时,他们非常感激。

paragraphs.en: Immediately they fell to work with him; and though they had no knife, yet, with a sharpened piece of wood, they took off his skin as readily, and much more readily, than we could have done with a knife.
paragraphs.cn: 他们立刻动手收拾它;虽然没有刀,他们却用一块削尖的木头,把它的皮剥了下来,又快又利落,比我们用刀还要利索得多。

paragraphs.en: They offered me some of the flesh, which I declined, pointing out that I would give it them; but made signs for the skin, which they gave me very freely, and brought me a great deal more of their provisions, which, though I did not understand, yet I accepted.
paragraphs.cn: 他们分了些肉给我,我谢绝了,示意说把肉都送给他们;可我打手势要那张皮,他们很爽快地给了我,还给我拿来了许多他们的食物,虽然我不认得那是什么,却也收下了。

paragraphs.en: I then made signs to them for some water, and held out one of my jars to them, turning it bottom upward, to show that it was empty, and that I wanted to have it filled.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我向他们打手势要点水,把我的一只罐子递过去,罐口朝下,表明它是空的,我想把它装满。

paragraphs.en: They called immediately to some of their friends, and there came two women, and brought a great vessel made of earth, and burnt, as I supposed, in the sun, this they set down to me, as before, and I sent Xury on shore with my jars, and filled them all three.
paragraphs.cn: 他们立刻招呼几个同伴,来了两个女人,抬来一只大瓦罐,我想那是在太阳底下晒烧成的,她们像先前那样把罐子放在我面前,我便叫佐立带着我的罐子上岸,把三只罐子全都装满了。

paragraphs.en: The women were as naked as the men.
paragraphs.cn: 那些女人跟男人一样,浑身赤裸。

paragraphs.en: I was now furnished with roots and corn, such as it was, and water; and leaving my friendly negroes, I made forward for about eleven days more, without offering to go near the shore, till I saw the land run out a great length into the sea, at about the distance of four or five leagues before me; and the sea being very calm, I kept a large offing to make this point.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我备足了根茎、谷子——不管是什么样的,还有水;别过了那些友好的黑人,我又往前航行了大约十一天,不敢靠近岸边,直到看见前方约四五里格远的地方,陆地长长地伸进海里;海面很平静,我便离岸远远地绕过这个海角。

paragraphs.en: At length, doubling the point, at about two leagues from the land, I saw plainly land on the other side, to seaward; then I concluded, as it was most certain indeed, that this was the Cape de Verde, and those the islands called, from thence, Cape de Verde Islands.
paragraphs.cn: 终于,在离陆地约两里格的地方绕过海角以后,我清清楚楚地看见另一边、朝海那一侧也有陆地;于是我断定——这确实千真万确——这就是佛得角,那些便是因此得名的佛得角群岛。

paragraphs.en: However, they were at a great distance, and I could not well tell what I had best to do; for if I should be taken with a fresh of wind, I might neither reach one or other.
paragraphs.cn: 不过它们离得很远,我一时拿不定主意该怎么办才好;因为万一刮起一阵大风,我可能哪一处都到不了。

paragraphs.en: In this dilemma, as I was very pensive, I stepped into the cabin and sat down, Xury having the helm; when, on a sudden, the boy cried out, “Master, master, a ship with a sail!” and the foolish boy was frighted out of his wits, thinking it must needs be some of his master’s ships sent to pursue us, but I knew we were far enough out of their reach.
paragraphs.cn: 正在这进退两难、心事重重的时候,我走进船舱坐了下来,让佐立掌舵;忽然,那孩子喊了起来:“主人,主人,一条挂帆的船!”这傻孩子吓得魂飞魄散,以为那准是他主人派来追我们的船;可我知道我们早已远远地出了他们所能追及的范围。

paragraphs.en: I jumped out of the cabin, and immediately saw, not only the ship, but that it was a Portuguese ship; and, as I thought, was bound to the coast of Guinea, for negroes.
paragraphs.cn: 我从舱里跳出来,一眼就看见那不但是条船,而且是条葡萄牙船;照我看,是开往几内亚海岸去贩黑人的。

paragraphs.en: But, when I observed the course she steered, I was soon convinced they were bound some other way, and did not design to come any nearer to the shore; upon which I stretched out to sea as much as I could, resolving to speak with them if possible.
paragraphs.cn: 可是,当我看清它所走的航向时,我很快就断定他们是往别处去的,并不打算再靠近海岸;于是我尽力朝海里驶去,下决心只要有可能就跟他们搭上话。

paragraphs.en: With all the sail I could make, I found I should not be able to come in their way, but that they would be gone by before I could make any signal to them: but after I had crowded to the utmost, and began to despair, they, it seems, saw by the help of their glasses that it was some European boat, which they supposed must belong to some ship that was lost; so they shortened sail to let me come up.
paragraphs.cn: 我把所有的帆都张满了,却发现自己赶不到他们的航路上去,他们会在我来得及向他们发出任何信号之前就驶过去;可是我拼尽全力赶上去、正开始绝望的时候,看来他们借着望远镜看出那是一条欧洲小船,以为准是属于某艘失事的大船;于是他们收帆减速,好让我赶上来。

paragraphs.en: I was encouraged with this, and as I had my patron’s ancient on board, I made a waft of it to them, for a signal of distress, and fired a gun, both which they saw; for they told me they saw the smoke, though they did not hear the gun.
paragraphs.cn: 这叫我大受鼓舞,由于船上带着我主人的一面旧旗,我便挥动它向他们发出遇险的信号,又放了一枪,这两样他们都看见了;因为他们后来告诉我,他们看见了硝烟,只是没听见枪声。

paragraphs.en: Upon these signals they very kindly brought to, and lay by for me; and in about three hours’ time I came up with them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们见了这些信号,便很和善地停了下来,等着我;大约过了三个钟头,我赶上了他们。

paragraphs.en: They asked me what I was, in Portuguese, and in Spanish, and in French, but I understood none of them; but at last a Scotch sailor, who was on board, called to me: and I answered him, and told him I was an Englishman, that I had made my escape out of slavery from the Moors, at Sallee; they then bade me come on board, and very kindly took me in, and all my goods.
paragraphs.cn: 他们用葡萄牙语、西班牙语、法语问我是什么人,可这几种话我一句都听不懂;末了,船上一个苏格兰水手朝我喊话:我答了他,告诉他我是英国人,是从萨累的摩尔人那里逃出来的奴隶;他们于是叫我上船,很和善地接纳了我,连同我所有的货物。

paragraphs.en: It was an inexpressible joy to me, which any one will believe, that I was thus delivered, as I esteemed it, from such a miserable and almost hopeless condition as I was in; and I immediately offered all I had to the captain of the ship, as a return for my deliverance; but he generously told me he would take nothing from me, but that all I had should be delivered safe to me when I came to the Brazils.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样得救,脱离了我先前那种悲惨得几乎毫无指望的境地,这份喜悦是任谁都能想见、难以言表的;我立刻把自己所有的一切都献给船长,当作对救命之恩的报答;可他慷慨地对我说,他什么都不要,等我到了巴西,我的东西会原封不动地全数交还给我。

paragraphs.en: “For,” says he, “I have saved your life on no other terms than I would be glad to be saved myself: and it may, one time or other, be my lot to be taken up in the same condition.
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“我救你的命,并不图别的,只求换我自己遇难时也有人肯救;说不定哪一天,我也会落到同样的境地被人搭救。

paragraphs.en: Besides,” said he, “when I carry you to the Brazils, so great a way from your own country, if I should take from you what you have, you will be starved there, and then I only take away that life I have given.
paragraphs.cn: 再说,”他说,“我把你带到巴西,离你的家乡那么远,倘若我拿走你的东西,你到了那儿就会饿死,那我岂不等于把我给你的这条命又夺了回去。

paragraphs.en: No, no,” says he: “Seignior Inglese” (Mr. Englishman), “I will carry you thither in charity, and those things will help to buy your subsistence there, and your passage home again.”
paragraphs.cn: 不,不,”他说,“英国先生”（意思是英格兰绅士）,“我出于善心把你送到那儿,这些东西会帮你在那里维持生计,还够你买回家的船钱。”

paragraphs.en: As he was charitable in this proposal, so he was just in the performance to a tittle; for he ordered the seamen that none should touch anything that I had: then he took everything into his own possession, and gave me back an exact inventory of them, that I might have them, even to my three earthen jars.
paragraphs.cn: 他这番提议既慷慨,做起来也丝毫不差、分文不苟;他吩咐水手们谁也不许动我的东西,然后把一切都收进他自己保管,又给了我一份一丝不差的清单,好让我样样都能拿回来,连我那三只瓦罐也不例外。

paragraphs.en: As to my boat, it was a very good one; and that he saw, and told me he would buy it of me for his ship’s use; and asked me what I would have for it?
paragraphs.cn: 至于我那条小船,是条很好的船;这他看得出来,便对我说他想买下来给他的船用;还问我要多少钱?

paragraphs.en: I told him he had been so generous to me in everything that I could not offer to make any price of the boat, but left it entirely to him: upon which he told me he would give me a note of hand to pay me eighty pieces of eight for it at Brazil; and when it came there, if any one offered to give more, he would make it up.
paragraphs.cn: 我对他说,他待我样样都那么慷慨,我实在不好意思为这船开价,全由他做主;于是他说他会给我立一张字据,到了巴西付我八十枚八字银元;等船运到那儿,要是有人肯出更高的价，他还会给我补足。

paragraphs.en: He offered me also sixty pieces of eight more for my boy Xury, which I was loth to take; not that I was unwilling to let the captain have him, but I was very loth to sell the poor boy’s liberty, who had assisted me so faithfully in procuring my own.
paragraphs.cn: 他还愿意再出六十枚八字银元买我那小佐立,这我却舍不得答应;倒不是我不愿把他给船长,而是我实在不忍心卖掉这可怜孩子的自由,他曾那样忠心地帮我换来了我自己的自由。

paragraphs.en: However, when I let him know my reason, he owned it to be just, and offered me this medium, that he would give the boy an obligation to set him free in ten years, if he turned Christian: upon this, and Xury saying he was willing to go to him, I let the captain have him.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,当我把缘由说给他听后,他也承认我说得在理,便向我提了个折中的办法:他愿意给这孩子立个字据,只要他改信基督教,十年之后就放他自由;既然这样,加上佐立自己说愿意跟他去,我便把他给了船长。

paragraphs.en: We had a very good voyage to the Brazils, and I arrived in the Bay de Todos los Santos, or All Saints’ Bay, in about twenty-two days after.
paragraphs.cn: 我们一路顺风,平安到了巴西,大约二十二天后驶进了万圣湾,也就是“全体圣徒湾”。

paragraphs.en: And now I was once more delivered from the most miserable of all conditions of life; and what to do next with myself I was to consider.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我再一次脱离了人生中最悲惨的境地;下一步该怎么安排自己,我得好好盘算盘算了。

paragraphs.en: The generous treatment the captain gave me I can never enough remember: he would take nothing of me for my passage, gave me twenty ducats for the leopard’s skin, and forty for the lion’s skin, which I had in my boat, and caused everything I had in the ship to be punctually delivered to me; and what I was willing to sell he bought of me, such as the case of bottles, two of my guns, and a piece of the lump of beeswax—for I had made candles of the rest: in a word, I made about two hundred and twenty pieces of eight of all my cargo; and with this stock I went on shore in the Brazils.
paragraphs.cn: 船长待我的那份慷慨,我永远铭记不忘:他不收我一文船钱,给了我二十枚达克特金币买那张豹皮,又给了四十枚买我船上那张狮皮,还叫人把我在船上的东西一样不差地交还给我;我愿意卖的他都买下,比如那箱瓶子、我的两支枪、和一块蜂蜡——其余的蜂蜡我做成了蜡烛;总之,我把全部货物卖了大约二百二十枚八字银元;带着这笔本钱,我在巴西上了岸。

paragraphs.en: I had not been long here before I was recommended to the house of a good honest man like himself, who had an _ingenio_, as they call it (that is, a plantation and a sugar-house).
paragraphs.cn: 我到这儿没多久,就有人把我推荐给一位跟船长一样正直厚道的好人家,那人有一座他们所谓的“engenio”（也就是一片种植园加一间制糖坊）。

paragraphs.en: I lived with him some time, and acquainted myself by that means with the manner of planting and making of sugar; and seeing how well the planters lived, and how they got rich suddenly, I resolved, if I could get a licence to settle there, I would turn planter among them: resolving in the meantime to find out some way to get my money, which I had left in London, remitted to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我在他家住了一阵子,借此熟悉了种甘蔗和制糖的门道;眼看那些种植园主日子过得多好、发家致富多么迅速,我便下决心,只要能弄到一份准许在那里落户的执照,就也去当个种植园主,和他们一样;同时打算想个办法,把我留在伦敦的那笔钱汇到手。

paragraphs.en: To this purpose, getting a kind of letter of naturalisation, I purchased as much land that was uncured as my money would reach, and formed a plan for my plantation and settlement; such a one as might be suitable to the stock which I proposed to myself to receive from England.
paragraphs.cn: 为此,我弄到了一种入籍文书,用手头的钱尽量多地买下了未开垦的荒地,又为我的种植园和产业订了个计划,好跟我打算从英国收到的那笔本钱相称。

paragraphs.en: I had a neighbour, a Portuguese, of Lisbon, but born of English parents, whose name was Wells, and in much such circumstances as I was.
paragraphs.cn: 我有个邻居,是里斯本的葡萄牙人,却是英国父母所生,名叫威尔斯,境况和我差不多。

paragraphs.en: I call him my neighbour, because his plantation lay next to mine, and we went on very sociably together.
paragraphs.cn: 我管他叫邻居,是因为他的种植园紧挨着我的,我们相处得很和睦。

paragraphs.en: My stock was but low, as well as his; and we rather planted for food than anything else, for about two years.
paragraphs.cn: 我的本钱不多,他也一样;头两年左右,我们种地主要是为了糊口,别的顾不上。

paragraphs.en: However, we began to increase, and our land began to come into order; so that the third year we planted some tobacco, and made each of us a large piece of ground ready for planting canes in the year to come.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我们渐渐有了起色,地也开始上了正轨;到第三年,我们种了些烟草,还各自整出一大块地,预备着来年种甘蔗。

paragraphs.en: But we both wanted help; and now I found, more than before, I had done wrong in parting with my boy Xury.
paragraphs.cn: 可我们俩都缺人手;这时我比先前更觉得,当初把小佐立卖掉是做错了。

paragraphs.en: But, alas! for me to do wrong that never did right, was no great wonder.
paragraphs.cn: 唉,可是像我这样从没做对过一件事的人,做错事又有什么稀奇。

paragraphs.en: I had no remedy but to go on: I had got into an employment quite remote to my genius, and directly contrary to the life I delighted in, and for which I forsook my father’s house, and broke through all his good advice.
paragraphs.cn: 我别无办法,只得硬着头皮干下去:我干上了一门与我天性极不相投的营生,恰恰跟我所向往的生活背道而驰——为了那种生活,我离弃了父亲的家,把他一切良言都置之不顾。

paragraphs.en: Nay, I was coming into the very middle station, or upper degree of low life, which my father advised me to before, and which, if I resolved to go on with, I might as well have stayed at home, and never have fatigued myself in the world as I had done; and I used often to say to myself, I could have done this as well in England, among my friends, as have gone five thousand miles off to do it among strangers and savages, in a wilderness, and at such a distance as never to hear from any part of the world that had the least knowledge of me.
paragraphs.cn: 如今,我倒偏偏走进了我父亲从前劝我安守的那种“中间地位”、也就是底层生活的上等一档;若我下决心就这样干下去,那我当初还不如待在家里,何必像先前那样跑到世上来白白折腾自己;我常常对自己说,这种事我在英国、在朋友们中间照样能做,何苦跑五千英里到陌生人和野蛮人中间、到荒野里、到这么个偏远的地方来做,连一点认得我的人的消息也听不到。

paragraphs.en: In this manner I used to look upon my condition with the utmost regret.
paragraphs.cn: 我就这样怀着无限的懊悔看待自己的处境。

paragraphs.en: I had nobody to converse with, but now and then this neighbour; no work to be done, but by the labour of my hands; and I used to say, I lived just like a man cast away upon some desolate island, that had nobody there but himself.
paragraphs.cn: 除了偶尔跟这位邻居聊聊,我没有别人可以交谈;除了亲手劳作,没有别的活计可做;我常说,我活得就像一个被抛弃在某座荒岛上的人,岛上除了他自己再没有别人。

paragraphs.en: But how just has it been—and how should all men reflect, that when they compare their present conditions with others that are worse, Heaven may oblige them to make the exchange, and be convinced of their former felicity by their experience—I say, how just has it been, that the truly solitary life I reflected on, in an island of mere desolation, should be my lot, who had so often unjustly compared it with the life which I then led, in which, had I continued, I had in all probability been exceeding prosperous and rich.
paragraphs.cn: 可这是何等的公道啊——所有人都该好好想想:当他们拿眼下的境况和更糟的境况相比时,老天也许会逼他们真去过一过那更糟的日子,好让他们亲身尝到、才明白从前是何等有福——我要说,这是何等的公道:我曾在一座荒无人烟的岛上臆想过的那种真正孤独的生活,后来竟真落到了我头上,而我先前还常常不公平地拿它去比我当时所过的日子;那种日子若我一直过下去,十有八九早就发达富足了。

paragraphs.en: I was in some degree settled in my measures for carrying on the plantation before my kind friend, the captain of the ship that took me up at sea, went back—for the ship remained there, in providing his lading and preparing for his voyage, nearly three months—when telling him what little stock I had left behind me in London, he gave me this friendly and sincere advice:—“Seignior Inglese,” says he (for so he always called me), “if you will give me letters, and a procuration in form to me, with orders to the person who has your money in London to send your effects to Lisbon, to such persons as I shall direct, and in such goods as are proper for this country, I will bring you the produce of them, God willing, at my return; but, since human affairs are all subject to changes and disasters, I would have you give orders but for one hundred pounds sterling, which, you say, is half your stock, and let the hazard be run for the first; so that, if it come safe, you may order the rest the same way, and, if it miscarry, you may have the other half to have recourse to for your supply.”
paragraphs.cn: 在那位好心的朋友——就是在海上搭救我的那条船的船长——动身回去之前,我经营种植园的种种打算已多少有了着落;那条船在当地停留了近三个月,备货并为航行做准备;这时,我把留在伦敦的那点本钱的事讲给他听,他给了我这番友好而诚恳的忠告:“英国先生,”他说（他一向这样称呼我）,“你若肯给我写几封信,再正式立个委托书交给我,叫那个在伦敦替你管钱的人把你的财物送到里斯本、交给我指定的人,并且换成适合这个国家的货物,那么承蒙上帝保佑,我回来时就把这些货的收益带给你;不过,既然人世间的事都免不了变故和灾祸,我劝你头一回只吩咐拨出一百英镑,你说那是你本钱的一半;先拿这一半去冒这个险,倘若平安到了,你再照样把其余的也调过来,万一有个闪失,你还留着另一半可以指靠、补上供给。”

paragraphs.en: This was so wholesome advice, and looked so friendly, that I could not but be convinced it was the best course I could take; so I accordingly prepared letters to the gentlewoman with whom I had left my money, and a procuration to the Portuguese captain, as he desired.
paragraphs.cn: 这忠告既这么妥当、又显得这么诚挚,我不能不信这是我所能采取的上策;于是我便照办,给那位替我保管钱财的女士写了信,又照他所要求的,给这位葡萄牙船长立了一份委托书。

paragraphs.en: I wrote the English captain’s widow a full account of all my adventures—my slavery, escape, and how I had met with the Portuguese captain at sea, the humanity of his behaviour, and what condition I was now in, with all other necessary directions for my supply; and when this honest captain came to Lisbon, he found means, by some of the English merchants there, to send over, not the order only, but a full account of my story to a merchant in London, who represented it effectually to her; whereupon she not only delivered the money, but out of her own pocket sent the Portugal captain a very handsome present for his humanity and charity to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我给那位英国船长的遗孀写了一封信,把我的种种经历——沦为奴隶、逃脱、如何在海上遇见这位葡萄牙船长、他待人的仁厚、以及我如今的处境,还有一切必要的取款指示,统统详细写明;等这位老实的船长到了里斯本,便设法托当地几个英国商人,不但把委托书、连同我全部的故事,一并寄给伦敦的一位商人,那商人又切切实实地转告了那位遗孀;于是她不但如数交出了钱款,还自掏腰包给这葡萄牙船长送了一份很体面的礼物,酬谢他对我的仁义与善心。

paragraphs.en: The merchant in London, vesting this hundred pounds in English goods, such as the captain had written for, sent them directly to him at Lisbon, and he brought them all safe to me to the Brazils; among which, without my direction (for I was too young in my business to think of them), he had taken care to have all sorts of tools, ironwork, and utensils necessary for my plantation, and which were of great use to me.
paragraphs.cn: 伦敦那位商人拿这一百英镑照船长开列的清单置办成英国货物,直接运到里斯本交给他,他又把这些货全数平安地带给了我、送到巴西;其中,他还不待我吩咐（因为我经营生意还太嫩,想不到这些）,就细心地替我配齐了各样工具、铁器和种植园所需的用具,这些东西对我大有用处。

paragraphs.en: When this cargo arrived I thought my fortune made, for I was surprised with the joy of it; and my good steward, the captain, had laid out the five pounds, which my friend had sent him for a present for himself, to purchase and bring me over a servant, under bond for six years’ service, and would not accept of any consideration, except a little tobacco, which I would have him accept, being of my own produce.
paragraphs.cn: 这批货运到时,我只道自己发迹在望了,喜出望外;我那位好管家——就是船长,把我朋友托他自用的那五英镑礼金也花了出去,替我买来并带回一个佣人,立了六年服役的契约,而且除了一点烟草,他别的酬谢一概不肯收,那点烟草还是我硬要他收下的,是我自己地里出产的。

paragraphs.en: Neither was this all; for my goods being all English manufacture, such as cloths, stuffs, baize, and things particularly valuable and desirable in the country, I found means to sell them to a very great advantage; so that I might say I had more than four times the value of my first cargo, and was now infinitely beyond my poor neighbour—I mean in the advancement of my plantation; for the first thing I did, I bought me a negro slave, and an European servant also—I mean another besides that which the captain brought me from Lisbon.
paragraphs.cn: 还不止这些呢;因为我的货全是英国货,像呢绒、料子、粗呢这类在当地格外值钱、格外抢手的东西,我便设法把它们卖了个大价钱;所以可以说,我如今赚得的价值比头一批货高出四倍还多,已远远超过我那可怜的邻居——我是说在种植园的经营上;因为我头一件事就是给自己买了一个黑奴,还添了一个欧洲佣人——我是说除了船长从里斯本给我带来的那个之外,又添的一个。

paragraphs.en: But as abused prosperity is oftentimes made the very means of our greatest adversity, so it was with me.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,被滥用的顺境往往正是我们招致最大厄运的祸根,我的情形正是如此。

paragraphs.en: I went on the next year with great success in my plantation: I raised fifty great rolls of tobacco on my own ground, more than I had disposed of for necessaries among my neighbours; and these fifty rolls, being each of above a hundredweight, were well cured, and laid by against the return of the fleet from Lisbon: and now increasing in business and wealth, my head began to be full of projects and undertakings beyond my reach; such as are, indeed, often the ruin of the best heads in business.
paragraphs.cn: 第二年我的种植园大获成功:我在自己的地里种出了五十大卷烟草,除去在邻居间换取必需品用掉的以外还有富余;这五十卷,每卷都在一英担以上,都精心熏制好了,存放起来等里斯本的船队回来;这时生意兴隆、财富渐增,我脑子里开始装满了种种超出我能力的规划和企图;这类东西,说实在的,往往正是生意场上最精明的头脑的祸根。

paragraphs.en: Had I continued in the station I was now in, I had room for all the happy things to have yet befallen me for which my father so earnestly recommended a quiet, retired life, and of which he had so sensibly described the middle station of life to be full of; but other things attended me, and I was still to be the wilful agent of all my own miseries; and particularly, to increase my fault, and double the reflections upon myself, which in my future sorrows I should have leisure to make, all these miscarriages were procured by my apparent obstinate adhering to my foolish inclination of wandering abroad, and pursuing that inclination, in contradiction to the clearest views of doing myself good in a fair and plain pursuit of those prospects, and those measures of life, which nature and Providence concurred to present me with, and to make my duty.
paragraphs.cn: 假如我一直安守在眼下的境地里,那么我父亲当年苦口婆心劝我去过那种安静、隐退生活时所指望的一切美满之事,都还有到来的余地;那种“中间地位”,他曾那么中肯地描述过、说它满是这类好处;可偏偏另有一些事缠上了我,我注定还要亲手酿成自己一切的苦难;尤其叫我罪加一等、叫我日后在苦难中有的是工夫去反躬自省、悔恨倍增的是:所有这些祸事,都是因我分明顽固地迁就自己那愚蠢的四海漂泊的癖性、一味听凭这癖性作祟而招来的,全然违背了最清楚不过的道理——本可以踏踏实实、平平正正地去追求那些前景和那种生活方式,那是天性与天意一齐摆在我面前、要我尽的本分。

paragraphs.en: As I had once done thus in my breaking away from my parents, so I could not be content now, but I must go and leave the happy view I had of being a rich and thriving man in my new plantation, only to pursue a rash and immoderate desire of rising faster than the nature of the thing admitted; and thus I cast myself down again into the deepest gulf of human misery that ever man fell into, or perhaps could be consistent with life and a state of health in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我当年就是这样挣脱了父母;如今我又不能安分,偏要抛下眼看就要在新种植园里成为富足兴旺之人的美好前景,只为去追逐那不顾一切、超乎常理的野心——妄想比事物本身所容许的更快地发迹;就这样,我又一次把自己扔进了人所能陷入的最深的苦难深渊，那深渊之深，恐怕已到了人在世上还能保住性命与健康的极限。

paragraphs.en: To come, then, by the just degrees to the particulars of this part of my story.
paragraphs.cn: 那么,就让我按部就班地讲到我这段故事的详情吧。

paragraphs.en: You may suppose, that having now lived almost four years in the Brazils, and beginning to thrive and prosper very well upon my plantation, I had not only learned the language, but had contracted acquaintance and friendship among my fellow-planters, as well as among the merchants at St. Salvador, which was our port; and that, in my discourses among them, I had frequently given them an account of my two voyages to the coast of Guinea: the manner of trading with the negroes there, and how easy it was to purchase upon the coast for trifles—such as beads, toys, knives, scissors, hatchets, bits of glass, and the like—not only gold-dust, Guinea grains, elephants’ teeth, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 你可以设想:我如今在巴西差不多住了四年,种植园开始蒸蒸日上、大有起色,我不但学会了当地的语言,还在同行的种植园主中间、以及在圣萨尔瓦多——那是我们的港口——的商人中间结交了熟人和朋友;而在跟他们的闲谈中,我常常向他们讲起我两次去几内亚海岸的航行:在那里跟黑人做买卖的情形,以及在那海岸上用些不值钱的小玩意儿——比如珠子、玩具、小刀、剪子、斧头、玻璃片之类——买东西是多么容易,不但能换到金砂、几内亚谷、象牙等等,

paragraphs.en: , but negroes, for the service of the Brazils, in great numbers.
paragraphs.cn: 还能换到大批黑人,供巴西役使。

paragraphs.en: They listened always very attentively to my discourses on these heads, but especially to that part which related to the buying of negroes, which was a trade at that time, not only not far entered into, but, as far as it was, had been carried on by assientos, or permission of the kings of Spain and Portugal, and engrossed in the public stock: so that few negroes were bought, and these excessively dear.
paragraphs.cn: 他们听我讲这些的时候总是听得格外专心,尤其是讲到买卖黑人那一段;当时贩卖黑人这门生意不但还没怎么开展开来,而且就它已开展的部分而言,一向是靠“专卖执照”、也就是西班牙和葡萄牙两国国王的特许来经营,由国家垄断的;所以买到的黑人很少,而且贵得离谱。

paragraphs.en: It happened, being in company with some merchants and planters of my acquaintance, and talking of those things very earnestly, three of them came to me next morning, and told me they had been musing very much upon what I had discoursed with them of the last night, and they came to make a secret proposal to me; and, after enjoining me to secrecy, they told me that they had a mind to fit out a ship to go to Guinea; that they had all plantations as well as I, and were straitened for nothing so much as servants; that as it was a trade that could not be carried on, because they could not publicly sell the negroes when they came home, so they desired to make but one voyage, to bring the negroes on shore privately, and divide them among their own plantations; and, in a word, the question was whether I would go their supercargo in the ship, to manage the trading part upon the coast of Guinea; and they offered me that I should have my equal share of the negroes, without providing any part of the stock.
paragraphs.cn: 有一回,我正跟几个相熟的商人和种植园主聚在一起、热切地谈论这些事;第二天早上,他们中有三个人来找我,说昨夜我跟他们讲的那些话叫他们琢磨了半宿,于是前来向我提一个秘密的建议;他们先叮嘱我保密,然后告诉我:他们有意装备一条船去几内亚;他们跟我一样都有种植园,别的都不缺,唯独最缺的就是劳力;因为这买卖没法公开做——他们把黑人运回来后不能公开出售——所以他们只想做一趟,把黑人偷偷弄上岸,分到各自的种植园里;一句话,问题就是:我肯不肯当这条船的押货员,去几内亚海岸上打理贸易那一摊;他们提出,我可以平分一份黑人,而不必出任何本钱。

paragraphs.en: This was a fair proposal, it must be confessed, had it been made to any one that had not had a settlement and a plantation of his own to look after, which was in a fair way of coming to be very considerable, and with a good stock upon it; but for me, that was thus entered and established, and had nothing to do but to go on as I had begun, for three or four years more, and to have sent for the other hundred pounds from England; and who in that time, and with that little addition, could scarce have failed of being worth three or four thousand pounds sterling, and that increasing too—for me to think of such a voyage was the most preposterous thing that ever man in such circumstances could be guilty of.
paragraphs.cn: 平心而论,这是个公道的提议——倘若是向一个没有自己产业、没有种植园要照看的人提的话;可我这产业正一步步走向可观、地上还有一笔不错的家底;而我这样一个已经安顿下来、根基已立的人,本来什么都不必做,只消照着已经起步的样子再干上三四年,再从英国把另外那一百英镑调过来;凭这点时间加上那么一点添头,几乎稳稳就能挣到三四千英镑,而且还在往上涨——像我这样的人竟去动这样一趟航行的念头,真是处在这种境地的人所能犯下的最荒唐的糊涂事了。

paragraphs.en: But I, that was born to be my own destroyer, could no more resist the offer than I could restrain my first rambling designs when my father’s good counsel was lost upon me.
paragraphs.cn: 可我这个天生要毁自己的人,竟没法抵挡这提议,正如当年父亲的良言在我身上白费、我按捺不住头一回四处漂泊的念头一样。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I told them I would go with all my heart, if they would undertake to look after my plantation in my absence, and would dispose of it to such as I should direct, if I miscarried.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话,我告诉他们,只要他们肯在我离开期间照看我的种植园,并且万一我遭遇不测,就按我的吩咐把它处置了,我就满心情愿跟他们去。

paragraphs.en: This they all engaged to do, and entered into writings or covenants to do so; and I made a formal will, disposing of my plantation and effects in case of my death, making the captain of the ship that had saved my life, as before, my universal heir, but obliging him to dispose of my effects as I had directed in my will; one half of the produce being to himself, and the other to be shipped to England.
paragraphs.cn: 这些他们全都答应了,还立下字据契约保证照办;我又正式立了一份遗嘱,把我的种植园和财产在我万一身故时的处置一一交代清楚,依旧指定那位救过我命的船长为我的全部财产继承人,但要求他按我遗嘱里的吩咐处置我的财产:所得的一半归他自己,另一半运往英国。

paragraphs.en: In short, I took all possible caution to preserve my effects and to keep up my plantation.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,凡是能想到的防范我都做足了,以保全我的财产、维系我的种植园。

paragraphs.en: Had I used half as much prudence to have looked into my own interest, and have made a judgment of what I ought to have done and not to have done, I had certainly never gone away from so prosperous an undertaking, leaving all the probable views of a thriving circumstance, and gone upon a voyage to sea, attended with all its common hazards, to say nothing of the reasons I had to expect particular misfortunes to myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我若肯拿出这份谨慎的一半来审度自己的利害、掂量掂量什么该做什么不该做,那我断然不会撇下这么一桩兴旺的事业、抛开种种发家在望的前景,而跑去做一趟海上航行,去承受它一切寻常的凶险——更不用说我本有种种理由预料自己会遭到特别的不幸了。

paragraphs.en: But I was hurried on, and obeyed blindly the dictates of my fancy rather than my reason; and, accordingly, the ship being fitted out, and the cargo furnished, and all things done, as by agreement, by my partners in the voyage, I went on board in an evil hour, the 1st September 1659, being the same day eight years that I went from my father and mother at Hull, in order to act the rebel to their authority, and the fool to my own interests.
paragraphs.cn: 可我就这样被冲昏了头,一味盲从的是我的臆想而不是我的理智;于是,船装备好了,货也备齐了,一切都照约定由我那几个航行的合伙人办妥了,我便在一个不祥的时辰上了船,那是一六五九年九月一日,恰好正是八年前我在赫尔离开父母的同一天——当年我离家去做违抗他们权威的叛子、坑害自己利益的傻瓜。

paragraphs.en: Our ship was about one hundred and twenty tons burden, carried six guns and fourteen men, besides the master, his boy, and myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我们的船约莫一百二十吨的载重,配了六门炮、十四个人,此外还有船长、他的小听差和我自己。

paragraphs.en: We had on board no large cargo of goods, except of such toys as were fit for our trade with the negroes, such as beads, bits of glass, shells, and other trifles, especially little looking-glasses, knives, scissors, hatchets, and the like.
paragraphs.cn: 船上没装什么大宗货物,只有些适合跟黑人做交易的小玩意儿,比如珠子、玻璃片、贝壳和别的零碎东西,尤其是小镜子、小刀、剪子、斧头之类。

paragraphs.en: The same day I went on board we set sail, standing away to the northward upon our own coast, with design to stretch over for the African coast when we came about ten or twelve degrees of northern latitude, which, it seems, was the manner of course in those days.
paragraphs.cn: 我上船的当天,我们就起了锚,沿着我们自己的海岸往北驶去,打算等到了北纬约十来度的地方再横渡过去、驶往非洲海岸;看来当时的航法就是这样。

paragraphs.en: We had very good weather, only excessively hot, all the way upon our own coast, till we came to the height of Cape St. Augustino; from whence, keeping further off at sea, we lost sight of land, and steered as if we were bound for the isle Fernando de Noronha, holding our course N.
paragraphs.cn: 沿着我们自己的海岸一路天气都很好,只是热得厉害,直到我们来到圣奥古斯丁角那一带;从那儿起,我们离岸更远地驶入外海,看不见陆地了,航向仿佛是奔着费尔南多·迪诺罗尼亚岛去,取的是北偏东、

paragraphs.en: E. by N.
paragraphs.cn: 北东偏北的方向,

paragraphs.en: , and leaving those isles on the east.
paragraphs.cn: 把那些岛屿留在东边。

paragraphs.en: In this course we passed the line in about twelve days’ time, and were, by our last observation, in seven degrees twenty-two minutes northern latitude, when a violent tornado, or hurricane, took us quite out of our knowledge.
paragraphs.cn: 照这航向,我们约莫十二天就越过了赤道线,按我们最后一次的观测,已到北纬七度二十二分;这时,一阵猛烈的龙卷风、或者说飓风,把我们卷得晕头转向、莫名所以。

paragraphs.en: It began from the south-east, came about to the north-west, and then settled in the north-east; from whence it blew in such a terrible manner, that for twelve days together we could do nothing but drive, and, scudding away before it, let it carry us whither fate and the fury of the winds directed; and, during these twelve days, I need not say that I expected every day to be swallowed up; nor, indeed, did any in the ship expect to save their lives.
paragraphs.cn: 它先从东南方刮起,转到西北,随后又稳定在东北;从那个方向刮来,来势凶得吓人,一连十二天我们什么也做不了,只能任它推着走,顺风逃遁,听凭它把我们刮到命运和狂风所指引的地方去;这十二天里,我不必说我天天都以为自己要被大海吞没了;说实在的,船上没一个人指望还能保住性命。

paragraphs.en: In this distress we had, besides the terror of the storm, one of our men die of the calenture, and one man and the boy washed overboard.
paragraphs.cn: 在这场患难中,除了风暴的恐怖之外,我们还有一个人死于热病,另有一个人和那小听差被浪卷下了海。

paragraphs.en: About the twelfth day, the weather abating a little, the master made an observation as well as he could, and found that he was in about eleven degrees north latitude, but that he was twenty-two degrees of longitude difference west from Cape St. Augustino; so that he found he was upon the coast of Guiana, or the north part of Brazil, beyond the river Amazon, toward that of the river Orinoco, commonly called the Great River; and began to consult with me what course he should take, for the ship was leaky, and very much disabled, and he was going directly back to the coast of Brazil.
paragraphs.cn: 到第十二天前后,天气稍稍缓和了些,船长尽力做了一次观测,发现自己大约在北纬十一度,可是经度上却比圣奥古斯丁角偏西了二十二度;这么一来,他发觉自己已到了圭亚那海岸、也就是巴西的北部、亚马孙河以外、靠近奥里诺科河——通常人称“大河”——的一带;他便开始跟我商量该走哪条航路,因为船已漏水,损坏得很厉害,他打算径直折回巴西海岸去。

paragraphs.en: I was positively against that; and looking over the charts of the sea-coast of America with him, we concluded there was no inhabited country for us to have recourse to till we came within the circle of the Caribbee Islands, and therefore resolved to stand away for Barbadoes; which, by keeping off at sea, to avoid the indraft of the Bay or Gulf of Mexico, we might easily perform, as we hoped, in about fifteen days’ sail; whereas we could not possibly make our voyage to the coast of Africa without some assistance both to our ship and to ourselves.
paragraphs.cn: 我坚决反对那么做;我跟他一起翻看了美洲海岸的海图,断定在到达加勒比群岛那一圈之前,沿途没有有人居住的国土可供我们投奔,因此下决心朝巴巴多斯驶去;我们指望着,只要离岸远些、避开墨西哥湾那股向内的涌流,大约十五天就能顺利到达;反正若不给我们的船、给我们自己弄到些接济,我们无论如何也没法完成到非洲海岸去的航程。

paragraphs.en: With this design we changed our course, and steered away N.
paragraphs.cn: 抱定这个打算,我们改了航向,朝着北西偏西、

paragraphs.en: W. by W.
paragraphs.cn: 西北偏西的方向驶去,

paragraphs.en: , in order to reach some of our English islands, where I hoped for relief.
paragraphs.cn: 指望到达我们某个英属岛屿,我盼着能在那儿得到救援。

paragraphs.en: But our voyage was otherwise determined; for, being in the latitude of twelve degrees eighteen minutes, a second storm came upon us, which carried us away with the same impetuosity westward, and drove us so out of the way of all human commerce, that, had all our lives been saved as to the sea, we were rather in danger of being devoured by savages than ever returning to our own country.
paragraphs.cn: 可我们这趟航行另有安排;因为在北纬十二度十八分的地方,第二场风暴向我们袭来,以同样的猛势把我们往西边卷去,把我们刮得远离了一切人类往来之地,以至于就算我们全都逃过大海这一劫、保住性命,也多半会被野人吞吃,再回不了自己的国家了。

paragraphs.en: In this distress, the wind still blowing very hard, one of our men early in the morning cried out, “Land!” and we had no sooner run out of the cabin to look out, in hopes of seeing whereabouts in the world we were, than the ship struck upon a sand, and in a moment her motion being so stopped, the sea broke over her in such a manner that we expected we should all have perished immediately; and we were immediately driven into our close quarters, to shelter us from the very foam and spray of the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 在这场患难中,风依旧刮得极猛;清早,我们中有个人喊了起来:“陆地!”我们刚跑出舱来张望、指望看清自己身在天涯何处,船就一头撞上了一片沙滩,顷刻间船身猛地停住,海浪劈头盖脸地打过来,来势之凶,叫我们只道立时就要全都送命了;我们连忙被赶进船上的隔舱躲避,好挡一挡那扑面的泡沫和飞溅的浪花。

paragraphs.en: It is not easy for any one who has not been in the like condition to describe or conceive the consternation of men in such circumstances.
paragraphs.cn: 凡是没有身临其境的人,都不容易描述或想象出人处在这种境地时那份惊惶。

paragraphs.en: We knew nothing where we were, or upon what land it was we were driven—whether an island or the main, whether inhabited or not inhabited.
paragraphs.cn: 我们全然不知自己身在何处,也不知被冲上的是什么地方——是海岛还是大陆,有人烟还是没人烟。

paragraphs.en: As the rage of the wind was still great, though rather less than at first, we could not so much as hope to have the ship hold many minutes without breaking into pieces, unless the winds, by a kind of miracle, should turn immediately about.
paragraphs.cn: 风势虽比起初稍减,却依旧很猛;我们连指望这船能在破碎之前多撑几分钟都不敢,除非风向凭着某种奇迹立刻转过来。

paragraphs.en: In a word, we sat looking upon one another, and expecting death every moment, and every man, accordingly, preparing for another world; for there was little or nothing more for us to do in this.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话,我们坐在那儿面面相觑,时刻等着死亡降临,人人都在为往另一个世界去做准备;因为在这个世界上,我们已几乎无事可做了。

paragraphs.en: That which was our present comfort, and all the comfort we had, was that, contrary to our expectation, the ship did not break yet, and that the master said the wind began to abate.
paragraphs.cn: 眼下唯一让我们宽慰、也是我们仅有的宽慰,就是出乎意料，这船到底还没有散架,而且船长说风势开始减弱了。

paragraphs.en: Now, though we thought that the wind did a little abate, yet the ship having thus struck upon the sand, and sticking too fast for us to expect her getting off, we were in a dreadful condition indeed, and had nothing to do but to think of saving our lives as well as we could.
paragraphs.cn: 可是,虽然我们觉得风稍稍小了些,船却这样撞在了沙滩上,搁得太死,别指望它还能脱身,我们的处境实在可怕极了,除了尽力设法保住性命,再没别的可做。

paragraphs.en: We had a boat at our stern just before the storm, but she was first staved by dashing against the ship’s rudder, and in the next place she broke away, and either sunk or was driven off to sea; so there was no hope from her.
paragraphs.cn: 风暴来临之前,我们船尾本来系着一只小船,可它先是撞在船舵上给撞坏了,接着又脱缆漂走,不是沉了就是被卷到海里去了;所以指望不上它。

paragraphs.en: We had another boat on board, but how to get her off into the sea was a doubtful thing.
paragraphs.cn: 船上还有另一只小船,可怎么把它放下海去,却是件没把握的事。

paragraphs.en: However, there was no time to debate, for we fancied that the ship would break in pieces every minute, and some told us she was actually broken already.
paragraphs.cn: 然而已经没工夫争论了,因为我们只当那大船随时都会散成碎片,还有人告诉我们它其实已经裂开了。

paragraphs.en: In this distress the mate of our vessel laid hold of the boat, and with the help of the rest of the men got her slung over the ship’s side; and getting all into her, let go, and committed ourselves, being eleven in number, to God’s mercy and the wild sea; for though the storm was abated considerably, yet the sea ran dreadfully high upon the shore, and might be well called _den wild zee_, as the Dutch call the sea in a storm.
paragraphs.cn: 在这危难关头,我们船上的大副抓住了那只小船,靠其余人手的帮忙,把它从船舷吊放下去;大家全都爬进船里,松了缆绳,我们一共十一个人,便把自己交给了上帝的慈悲和这狂野的大海;因为风暴虽已大为减弱,岸边的海浪却依然汹涌骇人,真可以称它作“den wild zee”——荷兰人管风暴中的大海就这么叫。

paragraphs.en: And now our case was very dismal indeed; for we all saw plainly that the sea went so high that the boat could not live, and that we should be inevitably drowned.
paragraphs.cn: 这一下我们的处境真是凄惨到了极点;因为我们都清清楚楚地看见,海浪高得那只小船根本浮不住,我们必定难逃淹死的命运。

paragraphs.en: As to making sail, we had none, nor if we had could we have done anything with it; so we worked at the oar towards the land, though with heavy hearts, like men going to execution; for we all knew that when the boat came near the shore she would be dashed in a thousand pieces by the breach of the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 要说张帆,我们没有帆,就算有也使不上;所以我们只得摇桨朝陆地划去,尽管人人心情沉重,像赴刑场的人一样;因为我们都知道,小船一靠近岸边,就会被拍岸的巨浪撞得粉身碎骨。

paragraphs.en: However, we committed our souls to God in the most earnest manner; and the wind driving us towards the shore, we hastened our destruction with our own hands, pulling as well as we could towards land.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此,我们还是极其恳切地把灵魂托付给了上帝;风把我们往岸边推,我们便亲手加速自己的毁灭,竭尽全力朝陆地划去。

paragraphs.en: What the shore was, whether rock or sand, whether steep or shoal, we knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 那岸边究竟是什么样,是礁石还是沙滩,是陡峭还是浅平,我们全然不知。

paragraphs.en: The only hope that could rationally give us the least shadow of expectation was, if we might find some bay or gulf, or the mouth of some river, where by great chance we might have run our boat in, or got under the lee of the land, and perhaps made smooth water.
paragraphs.cn: 凭理智还能给我们哪怕一丝一毫指望的,唯一的希望就是:或许能找到什么海湾、港汊,或某条河的入海口,凭着天大的运气把小船划进去,或者绕到陆地的背风一侧,兴许能有一片平静的水面。

paragraphs.en: But there was nothing like this appeared; but as we made nearer and nearer the shore, the land looked more frightful than the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 可这样的东西一点也没出现;相反,我们越靠近岸边,那陆地看上去比大海还要可怕。

paragraphs.en: After we had rowed, or rather driven about a league and a half, as we reckoned it, a raging wave, mountain-like, came rolling astern of us, and plainly bade us expect the _coup de grâce_.
paragraphs.cn: 我们划着——或者不如说被冲着——走了约莫一里格半，照我们的估算,一个像小山般的滔天巨浪从我们船尾滚滚压来,分明是叫我们等着领那“致命的一击”。

paragraphs.en: It took us with such a fury, that it overset the boat at once; and separating us as well from the boat as from one another, gave us no time to say, “O God!” for we were all swallowed up in a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 它来势之凶,一下子就把小船掀翻了;它把我们跟小船、也把我们彼此都冲散开,连让我们喊一声“天哪!”的工夫都没有,顷刻之间我们就全被吞没了。

paragraphs.en: Nothing can describe the confusion of thought which I felt when I sank into the water; for though I swam very well, yet I could not deliver myself from the waves so as to draw breath, till that wave having driven me, or rather carried me, a vast way on towards the shore, and having spent itself, went back, and left me upon the land almost dry, but half dead with the water I took in.
paragraphs.cn: 我沉入水里时心中那份慌乱,真是无法形容;因为我虽水性很好,却没法从浪里挣脱出来喘上一口气,直到那个浪把我推着、或者说卷着往岸边送了老远一段,浪势耗尽退了回去,把我几乎撂在了近乎干爽的陆地上,只是我灌了一肚子水,已半死不活。

paragraphs.en: I had so much presence of mind, as well as breath left, that seeing myself nearer the mainland than I expected, I got upon my feet, and endeavoured to make on towards the land as fast as I could before another wave should return and take me up again; but I soon found it was impossible to avoid it; for I saw the sea come after me as high as a great hill, and as furious as an enemy, which I had no means or strength to contend with: my business was to hold my breath, and raise myself upon the water if I could; and so, by swimming, to preserve my breathing, and pilot myself towards the shore, if possible, my greatest concern now being that the sea, as it would carry me a great way towards the shore when it came on, might not carry me back again with it when it gave back towards the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我还剩下几分镇定,气也还没喘尽;一看自己离大陆比预想的近,便一骨碌爬起身来,拼命想在下一个浪回头把我卷走之前尽快往陆地上奔;可我很快发现,这是躲不掉的;因为我看见海水在我身后追上来,高得像座大山,凶得像个仇敌,我既没办法、也没气力去跟它抗争:我能做的,就是屏住呼吸,尽量把身子托到水面上,借着游水保住呼吸,尽可能把自己引向岸边;我这时最担心的是,那海水既能在扑来时把我送出老远、往岸边送去,可别在退回大海时又把我一同卷回去。

paragraphs.en: The wave that came upon me again buried me at once twenty or thirty feet deep in its own body, and I could feel myself carried with a mighty force and swiftness towards the shore—a very great way; but I held my breath, and assisted myself to swim still forward with all my might.
paragraphs.cn: 又扑到我身上的那个浪，一下子就把我埋进它自己的浪body里、深达二三十英尺,我能感到自己被一股巨大的力量飞快地朝岸边卷去——卷了很远很远;可我屏住呼吸,竭尽全力帮着自己继续往前游。

paragraphs.en: I was ready to burst with holding my breath, when, as I felt myself rising up, so, to my immediate relief, I found my head and hands shoot out above the surface of the water; and though it was not two seconds of time that I could keep myself so, yet it relieved me greatly, gave me breath, and new courage.
paragraphs.cn: 我憋着气,快要憋炸了;正在这时,我觉出自己在往上升,于是立时得了解脱——我发现自己的头和手都窜出了水面;虽然我这样撑不到两秒钟,却也叫我大大松了口气,让我喘上了气,添了新的勇气。

paragraphs.en: I was covered again with water a good while, but not so long but I held it out; and finding the water had spent itself, and began to return, I struck forward against the return of the waves, and felt ground again with my feet.
paragraphs.cn: 我又被水没顶了好一阵,不过没到我撑不住的地步;等我发觉浪势耗尽、开始回退,便趁浪回头之际奋力向前一冲,脚下又踩到了地。

paragraphs.en: I stood still a few moments to recover breath, and till the waters went from me, and then took to my heels and ran with what strength I had further towards the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 我站住脚喘了几口气,等水从我身边退去,随后拔腿就跑,使出全身的力气再往岸边奔。

paragraphs.en: But neither would this deliver me from the fury of the sea, which came pouring in after me again; and twice more I was lifted up by the waves and carried forward as before, the shore being very flat.
paragraphs.cn: 可这一回还是没能让我逃脱大海的凶威,它又跟在我身后汹涌扑来;我又两次被浪卷起、像先前那样往前带去,只因那岸边非常平坦。

paragraphs.en: The last time of these two had well-nigh been fatal to me, for the sea having hurried me along as before, landed me, or rather dashed me, against a piece of rock, and that with such force, that it left me senseless, and indeed helpless, as to my own deliverance; for the blow taking my side and breast, beat the breath as it were quite out of my body; and had it returned again immediately, I must have been strangled in the water; but I recovered a little before the return of the waves, and seeing I should be covered again with the water, I resolved to hold fast by a piece of the rock, and so to hold my breath, if possible, till the wave went back.
paragraphs.cn: 这两次里的后一次,险些要了我的命;因为那海水像先前一样把我一路裹挟,把我抛上——或者不如说狠狠摔到——一块岩石上,来势之猛,把我摔得昏死过去,当真是无力自救了;因为这一下打在我的肋边和胸口,几乎把我一身的气都打了出来;倘若浪立刻回头,我准得憋死在水里;可我在浪回头之前稍稍缓过来一点,一见自己又要被水没顶,便下决心紧紧抱住那块岩石,尽量屏住呼吸,直到浪退回去。

paragraphs.en: Now, as the waves were not so high as at first, being nearer land, I held my hold till the wave abated, and then fetched another run, which brought me so near the shore that the next wave, though it went over me, yet did not so swallow me up as to carry me away; and the next run I took, I got to the mainland, where, to my great comfort, I clambered up the cliffs of the shore and sat me down upon the grass, free from danger and quite out of the reach of the water.
paragraphs.cn: 这时,浪已不像起初那么高了,因为离岸更近了些,我便死死抱住,等浪一低下去,又拔腿冲了一程,这一冲把我送到离岸很近的地方,以至下一个浪虽从我头上盖过,却没能把我卷走;我再冲的这一程,便到了大陆上;叫我大为宽慰的是,我攀上了岸边的峭壁,一屁股坐在草地上,脱离了危险,完全到了海水够不着的地方。

paragraphs.en: I was now landed and safe on shore, and began to look up and thank God that my life was saved, in a case wherein there was some minutes before scarce any room to hope.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我总算登上了岸、平安无事;我开始抬头感谢上帝救了我的命,而就在几分钟前,这几乎是毫无指望的事。

paragraphs.en: I believe it is impossible to express, to the life, what the ecstasies and transports of the soul are, when it is so saved, as I may say, out of the very grave: and I do not wonder now at the custom, when a malefactor, who has the halter about his neck, is tied up, and just going to be turned off, and has a reprieve brought to him—I say, I do not wonder that they bring a surgeon with it, to let him blood that very moment they tell him of it, that the surprise may not drive the animal spirits from the heart and overwhelm him.
paragraphs.cn: 我相信,一个人这样从坟墓边上、可以说是从鬼门关里被救回来时,灵魂那份狂喜与激荡,是无论如何也无法活灵活现地形容出来的;如今我也不再奇怪那种风俗了——当一个脖子上套着绞索的死囚被吊起、就要被推下去处决,忽然有人给他送来缓刑令时——我是说,我不再奇怪人们会同时带一位外科医生来,在告诉他消息的那一刹那就给他放血,免得这突如其来的惊喜把他的精气从心口逼散、把他压垮。

paragraphs.en: “For sudden joys, like griefs, confound at first.”
paragraphs.cn: “因为突如其来的狂喜,和悲痛一样,乍一临头总叫人不知所措。”

paragraphs.en: I walked about on the shore lifting up my hands, and my whole being, as I may say, wrapped up in a contemplation of my deliverance; making a thousand gestures and motions, which I cannot describe; reflecting upon all my comrades that were drowned, and that there should not be one soul saved but myself; for, as for them, I never saw them afterwards, or any sign of them, except three of their hats, one cap, and two shoes that were not fellows.
paragraphs.cn: 我在岸上走来走去,举起双手,整个身心可以说都沉浸在对自己获救的默想里;做出千百种我说不清的手势和动作;想起我那些淹死的同伴,想到除了我竟没有一个人的性命得救;因为至于他们,我此后再没见过他们,也没见过他们的一点踪影,只见到他们的三顶帽子、一顶便帽,和两只不成对的鞋子。

paragraphs.en: I cast my eye to the stranded vessel, when, the breach and froth of the sea being so big, I could hardly see it, it lay so far off; and considered, Lord! how was it possible I could get on shore?
paragraphs.cn: 我把目光投向那搁浅的船,由于海上碎浪和泡沫太大,我几乎看不见它,它躺在那么远的地方;我不禁寻思——主啊！我究竟怎么才能上得了岸呢?

paragraphs.en: After I had solaced my mind with the comfortable part of my condition, I began to look round me, to see what kind of place I was in, and what was next to be done; and I soon found my comforts abate, and that, in a word, I had a dreadful deliverance; for I was wet, had no clothes to shift me, nor anything either to eat or drink to comfort me; neither did I see any prospect before me but that of perishing with hunger or being devoured by wild beasts; and that which was particularly afflicting to me was, that I had no weapon, either to hunt and kill any creature for my sustenance, or to defend myself against any other creature that might desire to kill me for theirs.
paragraphs.cn: 等我用自己境况中值得庆幸的那一面聊以自慰之后,我开始环顾四周,看看自己身在什么样的地方、下一步该做什么;可我很快发现,这份宽慰渐渐消退了——一句话,我这场获救实在可怕:因为我浑身湿透,没有衣服替换,也没有任何可吃可喝的东西聊以慰藉;我眼前望不见别的前景,只有饿死或被野兽吞吃;尤其叫我难受的是,我手边没有一件武器,既不能去猎杀什么野物来充饥,也无法防身、抵御任何想拿我当口粮的野兽。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I had nothing about me but a knife, a tobacco-pipe, and a little tobacco in a box.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话,我身上除了一把刀、一支烟斗和一盒里的一点烟草,别的什么也没有。

paragraphs.en: This was all my provisions; and this threw me into such terrible agonies of mind, that for a while I ran about like a madman.
paragraphs.cn: 这就是我全部的家当了;这叫我陷入极其可怕的精神苦痛,有好一阵子我像个疯子似的四处乱跑。

paragraphs.en: Night coming upon me, I began with a heavy heart to consider what would be my lot if there were any ravenous beasts in that country, as at night they always come abroad for their prey.
paragraphs.cn: 夜幕向我压来,我开始怀着沉重的心情盘算:万一这地方有什么凶猛的野兽,我该有怎样的下场,因为一到夜里,它们总要出来觅食。

paragraphs.en: All the remedy that offered to my thoughts at that time was to get up into a thick bushy tree like a fir, but thorny, which grew near me, and where I resolved to sit all night, and consider the next day what death I should die, for as yet I saw no prospect of life.
paragraphs.cn: 那时我所能想到的唯一办法,就是爬到我近旁一棵长得像枞树、却生满棘刺的茂密大树上去,我打定主意在那上头坐一整夜,等第二天再琢磨我该死于哪种死法,因为眼下我还看不到一线生的指望。

paragraphs.en: I walked about a furlong from the shore, to see if I could find any fresh water to drink, which I did, to my great joy; and having drank, and put a little tobacco into my mouth to prevent hunger, I went to the tree, and getting up into it, endeavoured to place myself so that if I should sleep I might not fall.
paragraphs.cn: 我从岸边走出约莫一浪远,想看看能不能找到点淡水喝,还真找到了,叫我喜出望外;喝过水,又往嘴里塞了一点烟草压压饥,我便走到那棵树跟前,爬了上去,想法子把自己安顿好,免得万一睡着了会摔下来。

paragraphs.en: And having cut me a short stick, like a truncheon, for my defence, I took up my lodging; and having been excessively fatigued, I fell fast asleep, and slept as comfortably as, I believe, few could have done in my condition, and found myself more refreshed with it than, I think, I ever was on such an occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 我又砍了一根短棍、像根短棒似的用来防身,便这样安下了身;因为累得实在不行,我一下子就睡熟了,睡得那么香甜——我相信,处在我这般境地里,能睡这么好的人没有几个;这一觉给我的恢复,我想是我在这类情形下从未有过的。

paragraphs.en: When I waked it was broad day, the weather clear, and the storm abated, so that the sea did not rage and swell as before.
paragraphs.cn: 我醒来时天已大亮,天气晴朗,风暴也平息了,海面不再像先前那样怒吼翻腾。

paragraphs.en: But that which surprised me most was, that the ship was lifted off in the night from the sand where she lay by the swelling of the tide, and was driven up almost as far as the rock which I at first mentioned, where I had been so bruised by the wave dashing me against it.
paragraphs.cn: 但最让我吃惊的是,那条船在夜里被上涨的潮水从它搁浅的沙地上托了起来,几乎被推到了我最初提到的那块礁石附近——就是我被海浪撞得遍体鳞伤的地方。

paragraphs.en: This being within about a mile from the shore where I was, and the ship seeming to stand upright still, I wished myself on board, that at least I might save some necessary things for my use.
paragraphs.cn: 这里离我所在的岸边约莫一英里,船看上去还直立着,我真希望自己能上船去,好歹能抢救些对我有用的必需品。

paragraphs.en: When I came down from my apartment in the tree, I looked about me again, and the first thing I found was the boat, which lay, as the wind and the sea had tossed her up, upon the land, about two miles on my right hand.
paragraphs.cn: 我从树上的住处爬下来,又四下张望,首先看到的就是那只小艇,它被风浪抛上了岸,躺在我右手边约两英里处。

paragraphs.en: I walked as far as I could upon the shore to have got to her; but found a neck or inlet of water between me and the boat which was about half a mile broad; so I came back for the present, being more intent upon getting at the ship, where I hoped to find something for my present subsistence.
paragraphs.cn: 我沿着岸边尽力朝它走去,却发现我和小艇之间隔着一条约莫半英里宽的水湾或水道;于是我暂且回来,心里更急着要上大船,盼着能在那里找到点眼下活命的东西。

paragraphs.en: A little after noon I found the sea very calm, and the tide ebbed so far out that I could come within a quarter of a mile of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 过了正午不久,我发现海面十分平静,潮水退得很远,我可以走到离船不到四分之一英里的地方。

paragraphs.en: And here I found a fresh renewing of my grief; for I saw evidently that if we had kept on board we had been all safe—that is to say, we had all got safe on shore, and I had not been so miserable as to be left entirely destitute of all comfort and company as I now was.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这里,我的悲伤又重新涌上心头;因为我清楚地看到,要是我们当初都留在船上,本来都能平安无事——也就是说,我们本可以全都安全上岸,我也不至于像现在这样孤苦伶仃,失去一切慰藉和同伴。

paragraphs.en: This forced tears to my eyes again; but as there was little relief in that, I resolved, if possible, to get to the ship; so I pulled off my clothes—for the weather was hot to extremity—and took the water.
paragraphs.cn: 这又逼得我热泪盈眶;但哭也无济于事,我便下定决心,只要可能,就要设法上船;于是我脱掉衣服——因为天气热得厉害——下了水。

paragraphs.en: But when I came to the ship my difficulty was still greater to know how to get on board; for, as she lay aground, and high out of the water, there was nothing within my reach to lay hold of.
paragraphs.cn: 可等我游到船边,难题更大了:我不知道该怎么上去;因为船搁在浅滩上,高高露出水面,我伸手够不着任何可以攀住的东西。

paragraphs.en: I swam round her twice, and the second time I spied a small piece of rope, which I wondered I did not see at first, hung down by the fore-chains so low, as that with great difficulty I got hold of it, and by the help of that rope I got up into the forecastle of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我绕着船游了两圈,第二圈时发现一小段绳子,我很纳闷自己头一回竟没看见,它从船头的锚链处垂下来,很低,我费了好大劲才抓住它,借着这根绳子爬上了船的前甲板。

paragraphs.en: Here I found that the ship was bulged, and had a great deal of water in her hold, but that she lay so on the side of a bank of hard sand, or, rather earth, that her stern lay lifted up upon the bank, and her head low, almost to the water.
paragraphs.cn: 上船后我发现船身已经裂开,舱底进了不少水,但它斜靠在一片坚硬的沙岸或者说泥岸的边上,船尾被托高在岸上,船头低垂,几乎贴近水面。

paragraphs.en: By this means all her quarter was free, and all that was in that part was dry; for you may be sure my first work was to search, and to see what was spoiled and what was free.
paragraphs.cn: 这样一来,整个船后半部都露在外面,那部分的东西都是干的;你可以想见,我头一件事就是四处查看,弄清什么坏了、什么还完好。

paragraphs.en: And, first, I found that all the ship’s provisions were dry and untouched by the water, and being very well disposed to eat, I went to the bread room and filled my pockets with biscuit, and ate it as I went about other things, for I had no time to lose.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我发现船上所有的食物都干燥无损,没被水浸;我正饿得慌,便走进面包舱,把口袋塞满饼干,一边做别的事一边吃,因为我一刻也不能耽搁。

paragraphs.en: I also found some rum in the great cabin, of which I took a large dram, and which I had, indeed, need enough of to spirit me for what was before me.
paragraphs.cn: 我还在大舱里找到一些朗姆酒,喝了一大口;说真的,我也确实需要它来给自己壮壮胆,好应付眼前的事。

paragraphs.en: Now I wanted nothing but a boat to furnish myself with many things which I foresaw would be very necessary to me.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我什么都不缺,只缺一只船,好让我把预见到将来非常需要的许多东西运走。

paragraphs.en: It was in vain to sit still and wish for what was not to be had; and this extremity roused my application.
paragraphs.cn: 呆坐着空想那些得不到的东西是没用的;这困境反倒激起了我的干劲。

paragraphs.en: We had several spare yards, and two or three large spars of wood, and a spare topmast or two in the ship; I resolved to fall to work with these, and I flung as many of them overboard as I could manage for their weight, tying every one with a rope, that they might not drive away.
paragraphs.cn: 船上有几根备用的桁材,还有两三根大木杆,以及一两根备用的中桅;我决定就用这些动手,把我力气能对付的都尽量抛下水去,每根都系上绳子,免得漂走。

paragraphs.en: When this was done I went down the ship’s side, and pulling them to me, I tied four of them together at both ends as well as I could, in the form of a raft, and laying two or three short pieces of plank upon them crossways, I found I could walk upon it very well, but that it was not able to bear any great weight, the pieces being too light.
paragraphs.cn: 弄好之后,我顺着船舷下去,把它们拉到跟前,尽力把四根的两端捆在一起,做成木筏的样子,再在上面横放两三块短木板,发现我能在上面站得很稳,只是它载不了太重的东西,因为那些木料太轻了。

paragraphs.en: So I went to work, and with a carpenter’s saw I cut a spare topmast into three lengths, and added them to my raft, with a great deal of labour and pains.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我又动手,用木匠的锯子把一根备用中桅锯成三段,费了九牛二虎之力,把它们加到我的木筏上。

paragraphs.en: But the hope of furnishing myself with necessaries encouraged me to go beyond what I should have been able to have done upon another occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 但一想到能给自己置办些必需品,我就来了劲,做出了平时根本做不到的事。

paragraphs.en: My raft was now strong enough to bear any reasonable weight.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我的木筏已经结实,能承受相当的重量了。

paragraphs.en: My next care was what to load it with, and how to preserve what I laid upon it from the surf of the sea; but I was not long considering this.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来我操心的是往上面装什么,以及怎样才能不让装的东西被海浪冲走;不过这我没多费思量。

paragraphs.en: I first laid all the planks or boards upon it that I could get, and having considered well what I most wanted, I got three of the seamen’s chests, which I had broken open, and emptied, and lowered them down upon my raft; the first of these I filled with provisions—viz. bread, rice, three Dutch cheeses, five pieces of dried goat’s flesh (which we lived much upon), and a little remainder of European corn, which had been laid by for some fowls which we brought to sea with us, but the fowls were killed.
paragraphs.cn: 我先把能找到的木板都铺在筏上,又仔细想了想自己最需要什么,便找来三只水手的箱子,把它们撬开、倒空,吊到筏上;头一只我装满了食物——即面包、大米、三块荷兰奶酪、五块干羊肉(这是我们平日的主食),还有一点剩下的欧洲谷子,那本是留给我们随船带的家禽吃的,可惜家禽都死了。

paragraphs.en: There had been some barley and wheat together; but, to my great disappointment, I found afterwards that the rats had eaten or spoiled it all.
paragraphs.cn: 原本还有些大麦和小麦掺在一起;但让我大为失望的是,后来我发现全被老鼠吃光或糟蹋了。

paragraphs.en: As for liquors, I found several, cases of bottles belonging to our skipper, in which were some cordial waters; and, in all, about five or six gallons of rack.
paragraphs.cn: 至于酒类,我找到好几箱瓶装的,是属于船长的,里面有些甜露酒;总共还有大约五六加仑的甘蔗烧酒。

paragraphs.en: These I stowed by themselves, there being no need to put them into the chest, nor any room for them.
paragraphs.cn: 这些我另外放好,不必装进箱子,箱里也没地方放它们。

paragraphs.en: While I was doing this, I found the tide begin to flow, though very calm; and I had the mortification to see my coat, shirt, and waistcoat, which I had left on the shore, upon the sand, swim away.
paragraphs.cn: 我正忙着这些时,发现潮水开始上涨,虽然很平静;我懊恼地看着自己留在岸上沙滩上的外衣、衬衫和背心都漂走了。

paragraphs.en: As for my breeches, which were only linen, and open-kneed, I swam on board in them and my stockings.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我的短裤,不过是亚麻的,膝盖处敞着口,我就是穿着它和长袜游上船的。

paragraphs.en: However, this set me on rummaging for clothes, of which I found enough, but took no more than I wanted for present use, for I had other things which my eye was more upon—as, first, tools to work with on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,这倒促使我去翻找衣服,我找到不少,但只拿了眼下够用的,因为我更看重别的东西——首先就是上岸干活用的工具。

paragraphs.en: And it was after long searching that I found out the carpenter’s chest, which was, indeed, a very useful prize to me, and much more valuable than a shipload of gold would have been at that time.
paragraphs.cn: 找了好久,我才找出那只木匠的工具箱,它对我来说实在是一份极宝贵的战利品,在那时候比一船黄金还值钱得多。

paragraphs.en: I got it down to my raft, whole as it was, without losing time to look into it, for I knew in general what it contained.
paragraphs.cn: 我把它整个吊到筏上,没花时间去细看里面,因为我大致知道它装着些什么。

paragraphs.en: My next care was for some ammunition and arms.
paragraphs.cn: 我接下来操心的是弹药和武器。

paragraphs.en: There were two very good fowling-pieces in the great cabin, and two pistols.
paragraphs.cn: 大舱里有两支很好的鸟枪和两把手枪。

paragraphs.en: These I secured first, with some powder-horns and a small bag of shot, and two old rusty swords.
paragraphs.cn: 我先把这些拿好,还有几个火药筒、一小袋铅弹和两把生了锈的旧刀剑。

paragraphs.en: I knew there were three barrels of powder in the ship, but knew not where our gunner had stowed them; but with much search I found them, two of them dry and good, the third had taken water.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道船上有三桶火药,却不知道炮手把它们藏在哪儿;费了好大劲我才找到,其中两桶是干的、好的,第三桶进了水。

paragraphs.en: Those two I got to my raft with the arms.
paragraphs.cn: 那两桶我连同武器一起搬到了筏上。

paragraphs.en: And now I thought myself pretty well freighted, and began to think how I should get to shore with them, having neither sail, oar, nor rudder; and the least capful of wind would have overset all my navigation.
paragraphs.cn: 这下我觉得自己装得差不多了,便开始琢磨怎样把这些东西运上岸,可我既没有帆,也没有桨和舵;哪怕一丁点风,都能把我这套航行的家当掀翻。

paragraphs.en: I had three encouragements—1st, a smooth, calm sea; 2ndly, the tide rising, and setting in to the shore; 3rdly, what little wind there was blew me towards the land.
paragraphs.cn: 我有三样有利条件——第一,海面平静无波;第二,潮水正涨,朝岸边涌来;第三,那点微风也把我吹向陆地。

paragraphs.en: And thus, having found two or three broken oars belonging to the boat—and, besides the tools which were in the chest, I found two saws, an axe, and a hammer; with this cargo I put to sea.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我又找到属于那只小艇的两三支断桨——除了箱子里的工具,我还找到两把锯子、一把斧头和一把锤子;带着这些货物,我出发下海了。

paragraphs.en: For a mile or thereabouts my raft went very well, only that I found it drive a little distant from the place where I had landed before; by which I perceived that there was some indraft of the water, and consequently I hoped to find some creek or river there, which I might make use of as a port to get to land with my cargo.
paragraphs.cn: 大约一英里的路程,我的筏子走得很顺当,只是我发现它渐渐偏离了我先前登陆的地方;由此我看出这里有一股向内的水流,便盼着能在那儿找到一条小河或水湾,可以当作港口,把货物运上岸。

paragraphs.en: As I imagined, so it was.
paragraphs.cn: 果然不出我所料。

paragraphs.en: There appeared before me a little opening of the land, and I found a strong current of the tide set into it; so I guided my raft as well as I could, to keep in the middle of the stream.
paragraphs.cn: 我面前出现了一道陆地间的小口子,我发觉一股很强的潮流正涌进去;于是我尽力驾着筏子,让它保持在水流中央。

paragraphs.en: But here I had like to have suffered a second shipwreck, which, if I had, I think verily would have broken my heart; for, knowing nothing of the coast, my raft ran aground at one end of it upon a shoal, and not being aground at the other end, it wanted but a little that all my cargo had slipped off towards the end that was afloat, and so fallen into the water.
paragraphs.cn: 可就在这里,我险些遭到第二次翻船之祸;若真如此,我想我这颗心一定会碎;因为我对这一带全然陌生,筏子一头搁在了浅滩上,另一头却没搁住,差一点我所有的货物都要朝还浮着的那头滑去,掉进水里。

paragraphs.en: I did my utmost, by setting my back against the chests, to keep them in their places, but could not thrust off the raft with all my strength; neither durst I stir from the posture I was in; but holding up the chests with all my might, I stood in that manner near half-an-hour, in which time the rising of the water brought me a little more upon a level; and a little after, the water still-rising, my raft floated again, and I thrust her off with the oar I had into the channel, and then driving up higher, I at length found myself in the mouth of a little river, with land on both sides, and a strong current of tide running up.
paragraphs.cn: 我用尽全力,用后背抵住箱子,想把它们稳在原处,可拼了命也推不动筏子;我又不敢挪动身子;只好用尽气力撑着那些箱子,就这么站了近半个钟头,这期间水位上涨,把我托得平了一些;又过了一会儿,水还在涨,筏子重新浮了起来,我用手里那支桨把它撑进水道,再往上驶去,最后发现自己进了一条小河的河口,两岸都是陆地,一股强劲的潮流正往上涌。

paragraphs.en: I looked on both sides for a proper place to get to shore, for I was not willing to be driven too high up the river: hoping in time to see some ships at sea, and therefore resolved to place myself as near the coast as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝两边张望,想找个合适的地方上岸,因为我不愿被冲得离河口太远:我盼着日后能看见海上有船经过,所以决意尽量靠海岸安顿自己。

paragraphs.en: At length I spied a little cove on the right shore of the creek, to which with great pain and difficulty I guided my raft, and at last got so near that, reaching ground with my oar, I could thrust her directly in.
paragraphs.cn: 最后,我在水湾右岸发现一个小小的港汊,费了极大的力气和周折才把筏子引过去,终于靠得够近,用桨探到了河底,得以把它直直地撑了进去。

paragraphs.en: But here I had like to have dipped all my cargo into the sea again; for that shore lying pretty steep—that is to say sloping—there was no place to land, but where one end of my float, if it ran on shore, would lie so high, and the other sink lower, as before, that it would endanger my cargo again.
paragraphs.cn: 可就在这里,我又险些让全部货物再次沉入海里;因为那岸边相当陡峭——也就是说是斜坡——没有可以停靠的地方,只有让我筏子的一头搁上岸时高高翘起、另一头像先前那样往下沉,又要危及我的货物。

paragraphs.en: All that I could do was to wait till the tide was at the highest, keeping the raft with my oar like an anchor, to hold the side of it fast to the shore, near a flat piece of ground, which I expected the water would flow over; and so it did.
paragraphs.cn: 我所能做的,只是等潮水涨到最高,用桨像锚一样撑住筏子,把它的一侧牢牢抵在岸边一块平地附近,我料想潮水会漫过那块地;后来果然如此。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I found water enough—for my raft drew about a foot of water—I thrust her upon that flat piece of ground, and there fastened or moored her, by sticking my two broken oars into the ground, one on one side near one end, and one on the other side near the other end; and thus I lay till the water ebbed away, and left my raft and all my cargo safe on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 等水一涨够——我的筏子吃水约一英尺——我就把它推上那块平地,再用两支断桨插进地里把它系住或者说泊住,一支在一端的一侧,一支在另一端的另一侧;我就这样等着,直到潮水退去,把我的筏子连同全部货物安然留在了岸上。

paragraphs.en: My next work was to view the country, and seek a proper place for my habitation, and where to stow my goods to secure them from whatever might happen.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来我要做的是查看这一带地方,寻个合适的地点安家,并找地方存放我的货物,好保护它们免遭任何不测。

paragraphs.en: Where I was, I yet knew not; whether on the continent or on an island; whether inhabited or not inhabited; whether in danger of wild beasts or not.
paragraphs.cn: 我此刻身在何处,还一无所知;不知是在大陆还是海岛;有没有人住;会不会有野兽出没。

paragraphs.en: There was a hill not above a mile from me, which rose up very steep and high, and which seemed to overtop some other hills, which lay as in a ridge from it northward.
paragraphs.cn: 离我不到一英里有一座小山,又陡又高地拔起,似乎高过它北面像山脊一样排列的其他几座山。

paragraphs.en: I took out one of the fowling-pieces, and one of the pistols, and a horn of powder; and thus armed, I travelled for discovery up to the top of that hill, where, after I had with great labour and difficulty got to the top, I saw my fate, to my great affliction—viz. that I was in an island environed every way with the sea: no land to be seen except some rocks, which lay a great way off; and two small islands, less than this, which lay about three leagues to the west.
paragraphs.cn: 我取出一支鸟枪、一把手枪和一筒火药;就这样武装起来,我为探路爬上那座山顶;费了极大的力气登顶之后,我看清了自己的命运,大为痛心——原来我身处一座四面环海的孤岛:除了远处几块礁石,别无陆地可见;还有两座比这更小的岛屿,在西面约三里格处。

paragraphs.en: I found also that the island I was in was barren, and, as I saw good reason to believe, uninhabited except by wild beasts, of whom, however, I saw none.
paragraphs.cn: 我还发现自己所在的这座岛荒芜贫瘠,而且我有充分理由相信,除了野兽之外没有人烟,不过野兽我也一头都没见着。

paragraphs.en: Yet I saw abundance of fowls, but knew not their kinds; neither when I killed them could I tell what was fit for food, and what not.
paragraphs.cn: 倒是禽鸟见了不少,却认不出是什么种类;而且即便我打下来,也说不清哪些能吃、哪些不能。

paragraphs.en: At my coming back, I shot at a great bird which I saw sitting upon a tree on the side of a great wood.
paragraphs.cn: 回来的路上,我朝一只大鸟开了枪,那鸟正停在一片大树林边的一棵树上。

paragraphs.en: I believe it was the first gun that had been fired there since the creation of the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我相信那是自开天辟地以来,这里响起的第一声枪响。

paragraphs.en: I had no sooner fired, than from all parts of the wood there arose an innumerable number of fowls, of many sorts, making a confused screaming and crying, and every one according to his usual note, but not one of them of any kind that I knew.
paragraphs.cn: 我这一枪刚放,林子的四面八方就腾起数不清的各种飞鸟,乱哄哄地尖叫哀鸣,各自按它惯常的叫声叫着,可没有一只是我认得的。

paragraphs.en: As for the creature I killed, I took it to be a kind of hawk, its colour and beak resembling it, but it had no talons or claws more than common.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我打死的那只鸟,我看它是一种鹰,毛色和喙都像,只是爪子跟普通的鸟没什么两样。

paragraphs.en: Its flesh was carrion, and fit for nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 它的肉像腐肉,什么用也没有。

paragraphs.en: Contented with this discovery, I came back to my raft, and fell to work to bring my cargo on shore, which took me up the rest of that day.
paragraphs.cn: 这番发现让我心满意足,我回到筏子边,动手把货物搬上岸,这花去了我那天剩下的时间。

paragraphs.en: What to do with myself at night I knew not, nor indeed where to rest, for I was afraid to lie down on the ground, not knowing but some wild beast might devour me, though, as I afterwards found, there was really no need for those fears.
paragraphs.cn: 夜里我该怎么办、该在哪儿歇息,我都不知道,因为我怕睡在地上,担心会有野兽把我吃掉,尽管我后来发现,这些担忧其实全无必要。

paragraphs.en: However, as well as I could, I barricaded myself round with the chest and boards that I had brought on shore, and made a kind of hut for that night’s lodging.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我还是尽力用搬上岸的箱子和木板把自己围了起来,搭了个类似小棚屋的东西,好过这一夜。

paragraphs.en: As for food, I yet saw not which way to supply myself, except that I had seen two or three creatures like hares run out of the wood where I shot the fowl.
paragraphs.cn: 至于食物,我还没想出怎么解决,只是曾看见两三只像野兔的动物,从我打鸟的那片林子里跑了出来。

paragraphs.en: I now began to consider that I might yet get a great many things out of the ship which would be useful to me, and particularly some of the rigging and sails, and such other things as might come to land; and I resolved to make another voyage on board the vessel, if possible.
paragraphs.cn: 我这时开始盘算,或许还能从船上弄下许多对我有用的东西,尤其是一些索具和帆,以及别的能运上岸的物件;我便决心,只要可能,就再上那条船去一趟。

paragraphs.en: And as I knew that the first storm that blew must necessarily break her all in pieces, I resolved to set all other things apart till I had got everything out of the ship that I could get.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道头一场刮起的风暴必定会把它整个撞得粉碎,便决意把其他一切都搁在一边,先把船上我能弄下来的东西全弄下来。

paragraphs.en: Then I called a council—that is to say in my thoughts—whether I should take back the raft; but this appeared impracticable: so I resolved to go as before, when the tide was down; and I did so, only that I stripped before I went from my hut, having nothing on but my chequered shirt, a pair of linen drawers, and a pair of pumps on my feet.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我开了个会——也就是在自己心里合计——要不要把筏子撑回去;但这显然行不通:所以我决定像先前一样,趁退潮的时候去;我照办了,只是这回临出棚屋前我先脱了衣服,身上只穿着一件格子衬衫、一条亚麻内裤,脚上蹬一双薄底鞋。

paragraphs.en: I got on board the ship as before, and prepared a second raft; and, having had experience of the first, I neither made this so unwieldy, nor loaded it so hard, but yet I brought away several things very useful to me; as first, in the carpenters stores I found two or three bags full of nails and spikes, a great screw-jack, a dozen or two of hatchets, and, above all, that most useful thing called a grindstone.
paragraphs.cn: 我像上次那样登上船,备好第二只筏子;有了头一回的经验,我这次没把它做得那么笨重,也没装那么满,可还是运走了好几样对我很有用的东西;首先,在木匠的储物处,我找到两三袋钉子和道钉、一个大螺旋千斤顶、一两打短柄小斧,尤其还有那件最有用的东西——磨刀石。

paragraphs.en: All these I secured, together with several things belonging to the gunner, particularly two or three iron crows, and two barrels of musket bullets, seven muskets, another fowling-piece, with some small quantity of powder more; a large bagful of small shot, and a great roll of sheet-lead; but this last was so heavy, I could not hoist it up to get it over the ship’s side.
paragraphs.cn: 这些我都拿稳了,连同一些属于炮手的东西,特别是两三根铁撬棍、两桶滑膛枪子弹、七支滑膛枪、另一支鸟枪,还有少量火药;一大袋小铅弹和一大卷铅皮;可这最后一样太重,我没法把它吊起来越过船舷。

paragraphs.en: Besides these things, I took all the men’s clothes that I could find, and a spare fore-topsail, a hammock, and some bedding; and with this I loaded my second raft, and brought them all safe on shore, to my very great comfort.
paragraphs.cn: 除了这些,我还把能找到的水手衣物全带走了,又拿了一张备用的前中桅帆、一张吊床和一些铺盖;我把第二只筏子装上这些,全都安然运上了岸,叫我大为宽慰。

paragraphs.en: I was under some apprehension, during my absence from the land, that at least my provisions might be devoured on shore: but when I came back I found no sign of any visitor; only there sat a creature like a wild cat upon one of the chests, which, when I came towards it, ran away a little distance, and then stood still.
paragraphs.cn: 我离开陆地那阵子,一直有些担心岸上的食物至少会被吃掉:可回来时却没见任何来客的痕迹;只有一只像野猫的动物蹲在一只箱子上,我朝它走去时,它跑开一小段距离,又停住不动了。

paragraphs.en: She sat very composed and unconcerned, and looked full in my face, as if she had a mind to be acquainted with me.
paragraphs.cn: 它坐得十分安详自若,直勾勾地盯着我的脸,仿佛有心想跟我结识。

paragraphs.en: I presented my gun at her, but, as she did not understand it, she was perfectly unconcerned at it, nor did she offer to stir away; upon which I tossed her a bit of biscuit, though by the way, I was not very free of it, for my store was not great: however, I spared her a bit, I say, and she went to it, smelled at it, and ate it, and looked (as if pleased) for more; but I thanked her, and could spare no more: so she marched off.
paragraphs.cn: 我举枪对准它,可它不懂这是什么,便毫不在意,也不打算走开;于是我扔给它一小块饼干,尽管说实话我并不舍得,因为我的存粮不多:不过我还是省下一小块给了它,它走过去,闻了闻,吃掉了,又(像很满意似的)望着我想再要;可我谢谢它,再匀不出来了:它便扬长而去。

paragraphs.en: Having got my second cargo on shore—though I was fain to open the barrels of powder, and bring them by parcels, for they were too heavy, being large casks—I went to work to make me a little tent with the sail and some poles which I cut for that purpose: and into this tent I brought everything that I knew would spoil either with rain or sun; and I piled all the empty chests and casks up in a circle round the tent, to fortify it from any sudden attempt, either from man or beast.
paragraphs.cn: 把第二批货物弄上岸后——虽然我不得不把火药桶打开,一份一份地搬,因为整桶太重,都是大桶——我便动手用那张帆和几根为此砍来的木杆给自己搭个小帐篷:凡是我知道会被雨淋或日晒糟蹋的东西,我都搬进这帐篷里;又把所有空箱空桶围成一圈堆在帐篷四周,好防备无论人还是野兽的突然来袭。

paragraphs.en: When I had done this, I blocked up the door of the tent with some boards within, and an empty chest set up on end without; and spreading one of the beds upon the ground, laying my two pistols just at my head, and my gun at length by me, I went to bed for the first time, and slept very quietly all night, for I was very weary and heavy; for the night before I had slept little, and had laboured very hard all day to fetch all those things from the ship, and to get them on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 做好这些后,我在帐篷里侧用几块木板堵住门口,外面竖起一只空箱子;又在地上铺开一张床铺,把两把手枪就放在头边,长枪横放在身旁,我第一次躺下睡觉,整夜睡得十分安稳,因为我实在又累又困;头一天晚上我几乎没睡,一整天又拼命干活,从船上搬那些东西再运上岸。

paragraphs.en: I had the biggest magazine of all kinds now that ever was laid up, I believe, for one man: but I was not satisfied still, for while the ship sat upright in that posture, I thought I ought to get everything out of her that I could; so every day at low water I went on board, and brought away something or other; but particularly the third time I went I brought away as much of the rigging as I could, as also all the small ropes and rope-twine I could get, with a piece of spare canvas, which was to mend the sails upon occasion, and the barrel of wet gunpowder.
paragraphs.cn: 我如今拥有的各类物资,恐怕是有史以来一个人所积攒的最大一批了;可我仍不满足,因为只要船还那样直立着,我就觉得该把能弄的东西都弄下来;于是每天退潮时我都上船,总带回点这样那样的东西;尤其是第三回去时,我尽量多地带回了索具,还有能弄到的所有细绳和绳线,以及一块备用的帆布(那是用来临时补帆的),还有那桶湿了的火药。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I brought away all the sails, first and last; only that I was fain to cut them in pieces, and bring as much at a time as I could, for they were no more useful to be sails, but as mere canvas only.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,前前后后我把所有的帆都带走了;只是我不得不把它们剪成一块块,每次尽量多带些,因为它们再也当不成帆,只能当普通帆布用了。

paragraphs.en: But that which comforted me more still, was, that last of all, after I had made five or six such voyages as these, and thought I had nothing more to expect from the ship that was worth my meddling with—I say, after all this, I found a great hogshead of bread, three large runlets of rum, or spirits, a box of sugar, and a barrel of fine flour; this was surprising to me, because I had given over expecting any more provisions, except what was spoiled by the water.
paragraphs.cn: 但更让我欣慰的是,最后——在我这样跑了五六趟、以为船上再没有什么值得我费心去弄的东西之后——我说,在这一切之后,我竟发现了一大桶面包、三大桶朗姆酒或烈酒、一箱糖和一桶上等面粉;这叫我又惊又喜,因为我早已不指望还能找到别的食物,只当剩下的都被水糟蹋了。

paragraphs.en: I soon emptied the hogshead of the bread, and wrapped it up, parcel by parcel, in pieces of the sails, which I cut out; and, in a word, I got all this safe on shore also.
paragraphs.cn: 我很快把那大桶面包倒空,一份一份地用剪下来的帆布片包好;总之,这些我也全都安然弄上了岸。

paragraphs.en: The next day I made another voyage, and now, having plundered the ship of what was portable and fit to hand out, I began with the cables.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天我又跑了一趟,如今船上能搬动、能拿出来的东西我都掠走了,便开始动那些缆索。

paragraphs.en: Cutting the great cable into pieces, such as I could move, I got two cables and a hawser on shore, with all the ironwork I could get; and having cut down the spritsail-yard, and the mizzen-yard, and everything I could, to make a large raft, I loaded it with all these heavy goods, and came away.
paragraphs.cn: 我把粗大的缆绳割成我搬得动的段,弄了两根缆绳和一根系索上岸,还有我能弄到的全部铁器;又砍下了斜桁帆桁和后桅桁,以及一切能做成大筏子的东西,把这些沉重的货物统统装上,便撑离了船。

paragraphs.en: But my good luck began now to leave me; for this raft was so unwieldy, and so overladen, that, after I had entered the little cove where I had landed the rest of my goods, not being able to guide it so handily as I did the other, it overset, and threw me and all my cargo into the water.
paragraphs.cn: 可我的好运气这会儿开始离我而去了;因为这筏子太笨重、装得太满,我进了先前卸下其余货物的那个小港汊后,没法像驾另一只那样得心应手,它翻了,把我和全部货物都掀进了水里。

paragraphs.en: As for myself, it was no great harm, for I was near the shore; but as to my cargo, it was a great part of it lost, especially the iron, which I expected would have been of great use to me; however, when the tide was out, I got most of the pieces of the cable ashore, and some of the iron, though with infinite labour; for I was fain to dip for it into the water, a work which fatigued me very much.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我自己,倒没多大伤害,因为离岸很近;可我的货物却损失了一大部分,尤其是那些铁器,我本指望它们对我大有用处;不过等退潮后,我费尽无穷气力,把大部分缆绳段和一些铁器捞上了岸;因为我不得不潜到水里去摸,这活儿把我累得够呛。

paragraphs.en: After this, I went every day on board, and brought away what I could get.
paragraphs.cn: 这之后,我每天都上船,尽量把能弄到的都带回来。

paragraphs.en: I had been now thirteen days on shore, and had been eleven times on board the ship, in which time I had brought away all that one pair of hands could well be supposed capable to bring; though I believe verily, had the calm weather held, I should have brought away the whole ship, piece by piece.
paragraphs.cn: 我如今已上岸十三天,上船十一回,这期间凡是一双手所能搬来的,我都搬来了;不过我确信,若这平静的天气能一直保持下去,我准会把整条船一块块地全搬光。

paragraphs.en: But preparing the twelfth time to go on board, I found the wind began to rise: however, at low water I went on board, and though I thought I had rummaged the cabin so effectually that nothing more could be found, yet I discovered a locker with drawers in it, in one of which I found two or three razors, and one pair of large scissors, with some ten or a dozen of good knives and forks: in another I found about thirty-six pounds value in money—some European coin, some Brazil, some pieces of eight, some gold, and some silver.
paragraphs.cn: 可正当我准备第十二次上船时,发现风开始刮起来了:不过趁退潮我还是上了船,虽然我以为舱里已被我翻遍、再找不出什么,却发现了一个带抽屉的柜子,在一只抽屉里找到两三把剃刀、一把大剪刀,还有约莫十来把上好的刀叉:另一只抽屉里我找到约值三十六镑的钱——有些欧洲硬币,有些巴西的,有些八字银元,有些金币,有些银币。

paragraphs.en: I smiled to myself at the sight of this money: “O drug!” said I, aloud, “what art thou good for?
paragraphs.cn: 看着这些钱,我暗自苦笑:“唉,废物!”我出声说道,“你有什么用?
