paragraphs.en: Thou art not worth to me—no, not the taking off the ground; one of those knives is worth all this heap; I have no manner of use for thee—e’en remain where thou art, and go to the bottom as a creature whose life is not worth saving.”
paragraphs.cn: 你对我一文不值——不,连从地上捡起你都不值;那些刀子里随便一把都抵得上这一整堆;我压根用不着你——就待在原处吧,像个不值得救的东西一样沉到海底去。”

paragraphs.en: However, upon second thoughts I took it away; and wrapping all this in a piece of canvas, I began to think of making another raft; but while I was preparing this, I found the sky overcast, and the wind began to rise, and in a quarter of an hour it blew a fresh gale from the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 不过转念一想,我还是把它拿走了;我把这些全用一块帆布包好,开始琢磨再做一只筏子;可正当我准备时,发现天色阴沉下来,风又开始刮起,一刻钟工夫就从岸上刮来一阵强劲的大风。

paragraphs.en: It presently occurred to me that it was in vain to pretend to make a raft with the wind offshore; and that it was my business to be gone before the tide of flood began, otherwise I might not be able to reach the shore at all.
paragraphs.cn: 我随即想到,想在离岸风里做筏子是白费力气;我该做的是趁涨潮之前离开,否则怕是根本回不到岸上了。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, I let myself down into the water, and swam across the channel, which lay between the ship and the sands, and even that with difficulty enough, partly with the weight of the things I had about me, and partly the roughness of the water; for the wind rose very hastily, and before it was quite high water it blew a storm.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我下到水里,游过横在船与沙滩之间的那条水道,而且游得相当吃力,一半是因为我身上带的东西重,一半是因为水面波涛汹涌;因为风来得极猛,还没等到满潮就刮成了一场风暴。

paragraphs.en: But I had got home to my little tent, where I lay, with all my wealth about me, very secure.
paragraphs.cn: 但我已经回到我的小帐篷里,连同我所有的财物躺在里面,十分安稳。

paragraphs.en: It blew very hard all night, and in the morning, when I looked out, behold, no more ship was to be seen!
paragraphs.cn: 整夜风刮得很凶,早晨我朝外一看,瞧啊,那条船再也不见了!

paragraphs.en: I was a little surprised, but recovered myself with the satisfactory reflection that I had lost no time, nor abated any diligence, to get everything out of her that could be useful to me; and that, indeed, there was little left in her that I was able to bring away, if I had had more time.
paragraphs.cn: 我略微吃了一惊,但转念一想便释然了,颇感欣慰:我没有浪费一点时间,也没有松懈丝毫努力,凡是对我有用的东西都从船上弄了下来;而且说实在的,即便再多给我些时间,船上也没剩下多少我搬得走的了。

paragraphs.en: I now gave over any more thoughts of the ship, or of anything out of her, except what might drive on shore from her wreck; as, indeed, divers pieces of her afterwards did; but those things were of small use to me.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我不再去多想那条船,或船上的任何东西了,除了那些也许会从残骸漂上岸来的——后来果然有各种碎片漂来;可那些东西对我用处不大。

paragraphs.en: My thoughts were now wholly employed about securing myself against either savages, if any should appear, or wild beasts, if any were in the island; and I had many thoughts of the method how to do this, and what kind of dwelling to make—whether I should make me a cave in the earth, or a tent upon the earth; and, in short, I resolved upon both; the manner and description of which, it may not be improper to give an account of.
paragraphs.cn: 我此刻的心思全用在防备自己了——防备野人(万一有的话)和野兽(万一岛上有的话);我反复思量该用什么办法,以及该造什么样的住处——是在土里挖个洞穴,还是在地面搭个帐篷;简而言之,我决定两样都要;至于其式样和情形,不妨在此交代一番。

paragraphs.en: I soon found the place I was in was not fit for my settlement, because it was upon a low, moorish ground, near the sea, and I believed it would not be wholesome, and more particularly because there was no fresh water near it; so I resolved to find a more healthy and more convenient spot of ground.
paragraphs.cn: 我很快发现自己所在的地方不适合安家,因为它地处海边一片低洼的沼泽地,我料想那儿不利健康,尤其是附近没有淡水;于是我决意去找一处更利于健康、更方便的地方。

paragraphs.en: I consulted several things in my situation, which I found would be proper for me: 1st, health and fresh water, I just now mentioned; 2ndly, shelter from the heat of the sun; 3rdly, security from ravenous creatures, whether man or beast; 4thly, a view to the sea, that if God sent any ship in sight, I might not lose any advantage for my deliverance, of which I was not willing to banish all my expectation yet.
paragraphs.cn: 我考虑了自身处境中的几项条件,觉得它们对我很要紧:第一,健康和淡水,我刚提过;第二,能遮挡烈日的暑热;第三,能防范凶猛的生灵,无论是人还是兽;第四,能望见大海,这样若上帝差来什么船只映入眼帘,我便不至于错过任何获救的机会,而对于获救,我此时还不愿彻底放弃指望。

paragraphs.en: In search of a place proper for this, I found a little plain on the side of a rising hill, whose front towards this little plain was steep as a house-side, so that nothing could come down upon me from the top.
paragraphs.cn: 为寻这样一处地方,我在一座隆起的小山坡上找到一小片平地,它朝着这小平地的正面陡得像房子的一堵墙,这样就没有什么东西能从山顶上冲下来砸到我。

paragraphs.en: On the one side of the rock there was a hollow place, worn a little way in, like the entrance or door of a cave but there was not really any cave or way into the rock at all.
paragraphs.cn: 这岩壁的一侧有个凹进去的地方,朝里凹进一小段,像洞穴的入口或门户,可实际上岩石里根本没有什么洞穴,也没有通路。

paragraphs.en: On the flat of the green, just before this hollow place, I resolved to pitch my tent.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这凹处正前方那片绿茵的平地上,我决意支起我的帐篷。

paragraphs.en: This plain was not above a hundred yards broad, and about twice as long, and lay like a green before my door; and, at the end of it, descended irregularly every way down into the low ground by the seaside.
paragraphs.cn: 这片平地宽不过一百码,长约莫是它的两倍,像一块草坪一样铺在我门前;它的尽头则参差不齐地向四面下坡,直落到海边的低地。

paragraphs.en: It was on the N.
paragraphs.cn: 它在山的北

paragraphs.en: N.
paragraphs.cn: 北

paragraphs.en: W. side of the hill; so that it was sheltered from the heat every day, till it came to a W. and by S. sun, or thereabouts, which, in those countries, is near the setting.
paragraphs.cn: 偏西那一面;所以每天都能遮挡暑热,直到太阳偏到西南方向前后——在那些地方,那时候已近日落。

paragraphs.en: Before I set up my tent I drew a half-circle before the hollow place, which took in about ten yards in its semi-diameter from the rock, and twenty yards in its diameter from its beginning and ending.
paragraphs.cn: 在支帐篷之前,我在那凹处前面画了个半圆,半径从岩壁量起约十码,直径从首尾量起约二十码。

paragraphs.en: In this half-circle I pitched two rows of strong stakes, driving them into the ground till they stood very firm like piles, the biggest end being out of the ground above five feet and a half, and sharpened on the top.
paragraphs.cn: 在这半圆里,我打下两排结实的木桩,把它们钉进土里,直到它们像桩柱一样立得十分牢固,粗的一头露出地面五英尺半以上,顶端削尖。

paragraphs.en: The two rows did not stand above six inches from one another.
paragraphs.cn: 这两排桩子相距不到六英寸。

paragraphs.en: Then I took the pieces of cable which I had cut in the ship, and laid them in rows, one upon another, within the circle, between these two rows of stakes, up to the top, placing other stakes in the inside, leaning against them, about two feet and a half high, like a spur to a post; and this fence was so strong, that neither man nor beast could get into it or over it.
paragraphs.cn: 然后我取来在船上割下的那些缆绳段,一根压一根地成排铺在圆圈之内、这两排桩子之间,一直堆到顶;又在里侧另立一些桩子斜靠着它们,约两英尺半高,像给柱子支上的斜撑;这道栅栏结实得无论人还是兽都进不来、翻不过去。

paragraphs.en: This cost me a great deal of time and labour, especially to cut the piles in the woods, bring them to the place, and drive them into the earth.
paragraphs.cn: 这花了我大量的时间和力气,尤其是到林子里砍那些桩子、把它们运到这地方、再钉进土里。

paragraphs.en: The entrance into this place I made to be, not by a door, but by a short ladder to go over the top; which ladder, when I was in, I lifted over after me; and so I was completely fenced in and fortified, as I thought, from all the world, and consequently slept secure in the night, which otherwise I could not have done; though, as it appeared afterwards, there was no need of all this caution from the enemies that I apprehended danger from.
paragraphs.cn: 进这地方的入口,我没做成门,而是用一架短梯翻越顶端;等我进去后就把梯子提过来收在里面;这样我就自以为完完全全被围了起来、防得固若金汤,可以与世隔绝,因而夜里睡得安稳,否则我是断然睡不着的;不过后来才知道,对于我所担心的那些敌人,这一切戒备其实全无必要。

paragraphs.en: Into this fence or fortress, with infinite labour, I carried all my riches, all my provisions, ammunition, and stores, of which you have the account above; and I made a large tent, which to preserve me from the rains that in one part of the year are very violent there, I made double—one smaller tent within, and one larger tent above it; and covered the uppermost with a large tarpaulin, which I had saved among the sails.
paragraphs.cn: 我费尽无穷气力,把我全部的财富、全部的食物、弹药和物资都搬进这道围栏或者说堡垒里,清单前面已经列过;我还搭了个大帐篷,为了挡住那里一年中某个时节极其凶猛的雨水,我把它做成双层——里面一顶较小的帐篷,外面罩一顶较大的;最外层盖上一大块防水帆布,那是我从帆里省下来的。

paragraphs.en: And now I lay no more for a while in the bed which I had brought on shore, but in a hammock, which was indeed a very good one, and belonged to the mate of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 这下我暂时不再睡在搬上岸的那张床上,而是睡吊床,那吊床确实很好,原是船上大副的。

paragraphs.en: Into this tent I brought all my provisions, and everything that would spoil by the wet; and having thus enclosed all my goods, I made up the entrance, which till now I had left open, and so passed and repassed, as I said, by a short ladder.
paragraphs.cn: 我把全部食物和一切会被潮湿糟蹋的东西都搬进这帐篷;把所有货物这样围起来之后,我便封上入口——那入口我至今一直敞着,如前所说靠一架短梯进进出出。

paragraphs.en: When I had done this, I began to work my way into the rock, and bringing all the earth and stones that I dug down out through my tent, I laid them up within my fence, in the nature of a terrace, so that it raised the ground within about a foot and a half; and thus I made me a cave, just behind my tent, which served me like a cellar to my house.
paragraphs.cn: 做完这些,我开始动手往岩石里掏,把挖下来的泥土石块全从帐篷里运出去,堆在围栏之内,做成一道台地似的,把里面的地面垫高了约一英尺半;我就这样在帐篷正后方给自己掏了个洞穴,它对我的住所来说就像一间地窖。

paragraphs.en: It cost me much labour and many days before all these things were brought to perfection; and therefore I must go back to some other things which took up some of my thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切弄得完美无缺之前,花了我许多力气、许多天工夫;因此我得往回说说别的一些占了我心思的事。

paragraphs.en: At the same time it happened, after I had laid my scheme for the setting up my tent, and making the cave, that a storm of rain falling from a thick, dark cloud, a sudden flash of lightning happened, and after that a great clap of thunder, as is naturally the effect of it.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时候,我为支帐篷、掏洞穴筹划停当之后,恰好从一片浓黑的乌云里降下一阵暴雨,突然闪过一道电光,接着是一声炸雷,这自然是电光的结果。

paragraphs.en: I was not so much surprised with the lightning as I was with the thought which darted into my mind as swift as the lightning itself—Oh, my powder!
paragraphs.cn: 叫我吃惊的与其说是那道闪电,不如说是随之像闪电一样迅疾射进我脑海的念头——哦,我的火药!

paragraphs.en: My very heart sank within me when I thought that, at one blast, all my powder might be destroyed; on which, not my defence only, but the providing my food, as I thought, entirely depended.
paragraphs.cn: 一想到只需一下轰击,我全部的火药或许就会被毁,我的心便直往下沉;因为在我看来,不光我的防卫,连我谋取食物,全都指着它。

paragraphs.en: I was nothing near so anxious about my own danger, though, had the powder took fire, I should never have known who had hurt me.
paragraphs.cn: 我对自己的安危倒并不那么在意,尽管万一火药着了火,我恐怕永远也弄不清是谁伤了我。

paragraphs.en: Such impression did this make upon me, that after the storm was over I laid aside all my works, my building and fortifying, and applied myself to make bags and boxes, to separate the powder, and to keep it a little and a little in a parcel, in the hope that, whatever might come, it might not all take fire at once; and to keep it so apart that it should not be possible to make one part fire another.
paragraphs.cn: 这事给我的印象如此之深,以至暴风雨过后,我把一切活计——盖房子、筑防御——都撂下,专心去做袋子和箱子,好把火药分开,一小份一小份地分装,指望着无论出什么事,它都不至于一下子全部着火;而且要分得那样开,使得一份绝不可能引燃另一份。

paragraphs.en: I finished this work in about a fortnight; and I think my powder, which in all was about two hundred and forty pounds weight, was divided in not less than a hundred parcels.
paragraphs.cn: 这活儿我干了约莫两个星期才完;我的火药总共约两百四十磅重,我想是分成了不下一百份。

paragraphs.en: As to the barrel that had been wet, I did not apprehend any danger from that; so I placed it in my new cave, which, in my fancy, I called my kitchen; and the rest I hid up and down in holes among the rocks, so that no wet might come to it, marking very carefully where I laid it.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那桶湿了的火药,我料想它不会有什么危险;所以把它安置在我的新洞穴里,那洞穴我异想天开地称作我的厨房;其余的则东一处西一处藏在岩石间的窟窿里,免得受潮,并很仔细地记下我把它们放在哪儿。

paragraphs.en: In the interval of time while this was doing, I went out once at least every day with my gun, as well to divert myself as to see if I could kill anything fit for food; and, as near as I could, to acquaint myself with what the island produced.
paragraphs.cn: 在做这事的间隙,我每天至少带枪出去一趟,既是散心,也是看看能不能打到什么可吃的东西;并尽我所能,弄清这岛上出产些什么。

paragraphs.en: The first time I went out, I presently discovered that there were goats in the island, which was a great satisfaction to me; but then it was attended with this misfortune to me—viz. that they were so shy, so subtle, and so swift of foot, that it was the most difficult thing in the world to come at them; but I was not discouraged at this, not doubting but I might now and then shoot one, as it soon happened; for after I had found their haunts a little, I laid wait in this manner for them: I observed if they saw me in the valleys, though they were upon the rocks, they would run away, as in a terrible fright; but if they were feeding in the valleys, and I was upon the rocks, they took no notice of me; from whence I concluded that, by the position of their optics, their sight was so directed downward that they did not readily see objects that were above them; so afterwards I took this method—I always climbed the rocks first, to get above them, and then had frequently a fair mark.
paragraphs.cn: 头一回出去,我立刻发现岛上有山羊,这叫我大为满意;可随之而来的却是一桩不幸——那就是它们太机警、太狡猾、脚力又太快,要接近它们真是天下第一难事;但我并不因此气馁,深信自己总能不时打到一只,后来果然如此;因为我把它们出没的地方摸熟了一点后,便这样守候它们:我发现,如果它们在山岩上,而我在谷中被它们看见,它们就会像受了极大惊吓似的逃走;可如果它们在谷里吃草,我在山岩上,它们却毫不理会我;由此我断定,由于它们眼睛长的位置,它们的视线朝下,不大容易看见高处的东西;所以后来我用了这个法子——总是先爬上山岩,占到它们上方,这样常常能有个好靶子。

paragraphs.en: The first shot I made among these creatures, I killed a she-goat, which had a little kid by her, which she gave suck to, which grieved me heartily; for when the old one fell, the kid stood stock still by her, till I came and took her up; and not only so, but when I carried the old one with me, upon my shoulders, the kid followed me quite to my enclosure; upon which I laid down the dam, and took the kid in my arms, and carried it over my pale, in hopes to have bred it up tame; but it would not eat; so I was forced to kill it and eat it myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我头一枪打进这群牲口里,打死了一只母山羊,它身边有只正吃奶的小羊羔,这叫我打心里难过;因为老羊倒下时,小羊一动不动地站在它身旁,直到我走过去把老羊抱起来;不仅如此,我把老羊扛在肩上带走时,小羊一路跟着我,直跟到我的围栏;于是我放下母羊,把小羊抱在怀里,抱过我的栅栏,指望把它养驯;可它就是不肯吃食;我只好把它杀了自己吃掉。

paragraphs.en: These two supplied me with flesh a great while, for I ate sparingly, and saved my provisions, my bread especially, as much as possibly I could.
paragraphs.cn: 这两只羊供了我好一阵子的肉食,因为我省着吃,并尽可能地节省我的存粮,尤其是面包。

paragraphs.en: Having now fixed my habitation, I found it absolutely necessary to provide a place to make a fire in, and fuel to burn: and what I did for that, and also how I enlarged my cave, and what conveniences I made, I shall give a full account of in its place; but I must now give some little account of myself, and of my thoughts about living, which, it may well be supposed, were not a few.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我住所已经定下,我发现绝对有必要备一个生火的地方和可烧的燃料:至于我为此做了些什么,以及我如何扩大我的洞穴、又添了些什么方便设施,我将在适当的地方详加交代;但我现在得说说自己的一些情形,以及我对生活的种种思绪,可以想见,这些思绪着实不少。

paragraphs.en: I had a dismal prospect of my condition; for as I was not cast away upon that island without being driven, as is said, by a violent storm, quite out of the course of our intended voyage, and a great way, viz. some hundreds of leagues, out of the ordinary course of the trade of mankind, I had great reason to consider it as a determination of Heaven, that in this desolate place, and in this desolate manner, I should end my life.
paragraphs.cn: 我对自己的处境有着悲凉的预感;因为我之所以落难此岛,如前所述,是被一场狂暴的风暴驱赶着,完全偏离了我们预定的航线,离人类通商的寻常航道足有好几百里格之远,我有充分的理由认为,这是上天的裁定——我注定要在这荒凉之地、以这荒凉的方式了结此生。

paragraphs.en: The tears would run plentifully down my face when I made these reflections; and sometimes I would expostulate with myself why Providence should thus completely ruin His creatures, and render them so absolutely miserable; so without help, abandoned, so entirely depressed, that it could hardly be rational to be thankful for such a life.
paragraphs.cn: 每当我这样反省时,泪水便顺着脸颊扑簌簌流下;有时我会同自己争辩,为什么上天要这样彻底毁掉他的造物,叫他们如此绝对地悲惨;这般孤立无援、被抛弃、被彻底压垮,以至对这样的生命心存感激简直算不上有理智。

paragraphs.en: But something always returned swift upon me to check these thoughts, and to reprove me; and particularly one day, walking with my gun in my hand by the seaside, I was very pensive upon the subject of my present condition, when reason, as it were, expostulated with me the other way, thus: “Well, you are in a desolate condition, it is true; but, pray remember, where are the rest of you?
paragraphs.cn: 但总有个什么念头飞快地回来制止我这些想法、责备我;尤其有一天,我手握枪在海边散步,正对自己眼下的处境闷闷不乐,理智仿佛从另一面同我争辩起来,是这样说的:“好吧,你处境荒凉,这不假;可请记着,你其余的人都在哪儿呢?

paragraphs.en: Did not you come, eleven of you in the boat?
paragraphs.cn: 你们上小艇时不是十一个人吗?

paragraphs.en: Where are the ten?
paragraphs.cn: 那十个在哪儿?

paragraphs.en: Why were they not saved, and you lost?
paragraphs.cn: 为什么他们没得救,倒是你活了下来?

paragraphs.en: Why were you singled out?
paragraphs.cn: 为什么单单挑中了你?

paragraphs.en: Is it better to be here or there?”
paragraphs.cn: 是在这儿好,还是在那儿好呢?”

paragraphs.en: And then I pointed to the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 说着,我指了指大海。

paragraphs.en: All evils are to be considered with the good that is in them, and with what worse attends them.
paragraphs.cn: 一切祸患,都该连同其中所含的好处、以及可能伴随而来的更坏情形一并考量。

paragraphs.en: Then it occurred to me again, how well I was furnished for my subsistence, and what would have been my case if it had not happened (which was a hundred thousand to one) that the ship floated from the place where she first struck, and was driven so near to the shore that I had time to get all these things out of her; what would have been my case, if I had been forced to have lived in the condition in which I at first came on shore, without necessaries of life, or necessaries to supply and procure them?
paragraphs.cn: 于是我又想到,我为求生所置办的东西何其齐备,而若不是碰巧(那机会是十万分之一)那船从最初触礁的地方浮起、被推到离岸那么近,叫我有时间把这一切都从船上弄下来,我又会落到什么地步;倘若我被迫按最初上岸时那副光景过活,没有生活必需品,也没有添置和获取它们的手段,我又会是什么景况?

paragraphs.en: “Particularly,” said I, aloud (though to myself), “what should I have done without a gun, without ammunition, without any tools to make anything, or to work with, without clothes, bedding, a tent, or any manner of covering?” and that now I had all these to sufficient quantity, and was in a fair way to provide myself in such a manner as to live without my gun, when my ammunition was spent: so that I had a tolerable view of subsisting, without any want, as long as I lived; for I considered from the beginning how I would provide for the accidents that might happen, and for the time that was to come, even not only after my ammunition should be spent, but even after my health and strength should decay.
paragraphs.cn: “尤其是,”我出声说道(虽说是对自己说),“要是没有枪,没有弹药,没有任何做东西或干活的工具,没有衣服、铺盖、帐篷或任何遮身之物,我可怎么办?”而如今我这些全都有了,而且数量充足,还大有希望安排得妥妥当当,好在弹药用尽后不靠枪也能过活:这样一来,只要我活着,就有指望不愁温饱地维持下去;因为我从一开始就盘算好,该如何应对可能发生的意外,以及为将来做准备,不光是弹药用完之后,甚至是我的健康和体力衰退之后。

paragraphs.en: I confess I had not entertained any notion of my ammunition being destroyed at one blast—I mean my powder being blown up by lightning; and this made the thoughts of it so surprising to me, when it lightened and thundered, as I observed just now.
paragraphs.cn: 我承认,我从没想过我的弹药会被一下子炸毁——我是说我的火药会被雷电引爆;正因如此,如我方才所说,当电闪雷鸣时,这个念头才叫我那样吃惊。

paragraphs.en: And now being about to enter into a melancholy relation of a scene of silent life, such, perhaps, as was never heard of in the world before, I shall take it from its beginning, and continue it in its order.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我即将展开一段凄凉的记述,讲一幕寂静的生活,这样的生活或许是世上前所未闻的,我将从它的开端说起,并按其次序讲下去。

paragraphs.en: It was by my account the 30th of September, when, in the manner as above said, I first set foot upon this horrid island; when the sun, being to us in its autumnal equinox, was almost over my head; for I reckoned myself, by observation, to be in the latitude of nine degrees twenty-two minutes north of the line.
paragraphs.cn: 照我的记算,那是九月三十日,如前所述,我头一次踏上这可怕的荒岛;那时太阳对我们来说正处在秋分,几乎当头照着;因为我据观测推算,自己身处赤道以北北纬九度二十二分。

paragraphs.en: After I had been there about ten or twelve days, it came into my thoughts that I should lose my reckoning of time for want of books, and pen and ink, and should even forget the Sabbath days; but to prevent this, I cut with my knife upon a large post, in capital letters—and making it into a great cross, I set it up on the shore where I first landed—“I came on shore here on the 30th September 1659.”
paragraphs.cn: 我在那儿待了约莫十天或十二天后,忽然想到,由于没有书籍、没有纸笔,我会算不清日子,甚至会忘了安息日;为防止这事,我用刀在一根大柱子上刻下大写字母——并把它做成一个大十字架,竖在我最初登陆的岸边——“我于一六五九年九月三十日在此上岸。”

paragraphs.en: Upon the sides of this square post I cut every day a notch with my knife, and every seventh notch was as long again as the rest, and every first day of the month as long again as that long one; and thus I kept my calendar, or weekly, monthly, and yearly reckoning of time.
paragraphs.cn: 在这根方柱的各面上,我每天用刀刻一道凹痕,每逢第七道就刻得比其余的长一倍,每月的头一天又比那长的再长一倍;我就这样记着我的日历,或者说按周、按月、按年记算时间。

paragraphs.en: In the next place, we are to observe that among the many things which I brought out of the ship, in the several voyages which, as above mentioned, I made to it, I got several things of less value, but not at all less useful to me, which I omitted setting down before; as, in particular, pens, ink, and paper, several parcels in the captain’s, mate’s, gunner’s and carpenter’s keeping; three or four compasses, some mathematical instruments, dials, perspectives, charts, and books of navigation, all which I huddled together, whether I might want them or no; also, I found three very good Bibles, which came to me in my cargo from England, and which I had packed up among my things; some Portuguese books also; and among them two or three Popish prayer-books, and several other books, all which I carefully secured.
paragraphs.cn: 其次,该提一提的是,在我如前所述几次上船、从船里带出来的许多东西当中,我还弄到几样价值较小、但对我一点也不逊于有用的物件,先前忘了记下;比方说,笔、墨和纸,几包分别存放在船长、大副、炮手和木匠处;三四个罗盘、一些数学仪器、日晷、望远镜、海图和航海书,这些我不管用得着用不着,都一股脑儿归拢到一起;我还找到三部很好的《圣经》,那是随我的货物从英格兰运来的,我把它们打包在我的东西里;还有一些葡萄牙文的书;其中有两三本天主教祈祷书,以及别的几本书,这些我都小心收好了。

paragraphs.en: And I must not forget that we had in the ship a dog and two cats, of whose eminent history I may have occasion to say something in its place; for I carried both the cats with me; and as for the dog, he jumped out of the ship of himself, and swam on shore to me the day after I went on shore with my first cargo, and was a trusty servant to me many years; I wanted nothing that he could fetch me, nor any company that he could make up to me; I only wanted to have him talk to me, but that would not do.
paragraphs.cn: 我可不能忘了,船上还有一条狗和两只猫,关于它们值得一提的事迹,我或许会在适当的地方说上几句;因为那两只猫我都带上了;至于那条狗,它自己从船上跳下来,在我带头一批货物上岸后的第二天泅水游到我这儿,做了我许多年忠实的仆从;凡是它能替我取来的,我都不缺;凡是它能给我做的伴,我也都有;我只盼它能同我说话,可那是办不到的。

paragraphs.en: As I observed before, I found pens, ink, and paper, and I husbanded them to the utmost; and I shall show that while my ink lasted, I kept things very exact, but after that was gone I could not, for I could not make any ink by any means that I could devise.
paragraphs.cn: 如前所述,我找到了笔、墨和纸,便尽量省着用;我要说明,墨水还有的时候,我把事情记得很确切,可墨水用完之后就不行了,因为我想尽办法也调不出墨水来。

paragraphs.en: And this put me in mind that I wanted many things notwithstanding all that I had amassed together; and of these, ink was one; as also a spade, pickaxe, and shovel, to dig or remove the earth; needles, pins, and thread; as for linen, I soon learned to want that without much difficulty.
paragraphs.cn: 这也提醒了我,尽管我攒了那么多东西,可我仍缺许多物件;其中之一便是墨水;还有一把铁锹、一把镐和一把铲子,好挖土或移土;针、别针和线;至于亚麻布,我很快就学会了没有它也能凑合过,没多大困难。

paragraphs.en: This want of tools made every work I did go on heavily; and it was near a whole year before I had entirely finished my little pale, or surrounded my habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 这缺工具使我做的每一样活计都进展艰难;差不多花了整整一年,我才彻底完工我那道小栅栏,或者说把我的住所围了起来。

paragraphs.en: The piles, or stakes, which were as heavy as I could well lift, were a long time in cutting and preparing in the woods, and more, by far, in bringing home; so that I spent sometimes two days in cutting and bringing home one of those posts, and a third day in driving it into the ground; for which purpose I got a heavy piece of wood at first, but at last bethought myself of one of the iron crows; which, however, though I found it, made driving those posts or piles very laborious and tedious work.
paragraphs.cn: 那些桩子或者说木桩,重得我勉强才提得动,在林子里砍伐、备料就花了很长时间,运回家更是远远地耗时;所以我有时要花两天砍伐、运回一根这样的柱子,再花第三天把它钉进土里;为此我起初弄了根沉重的木棒,后来才想到那几根铁撬棍中的一根;不过话虽如此,即便有了它,把那些柱子或木桩钉进土里仍是极费力、极烦人的活儿。

paragraphs.en: But what need I have been concerned at the tediousness of anything I had to do, seeing I had time enough to do it in? nor had I any other employment, if that had been over, at least that I could foresee, except the ranging the island to seek for food, which I did, more or less, every day.
paragraphs.cn: 可我又何必为自己要做的任何事的烦人而烦心呢,既然我有的是时间去做?何况即便这些活干完了,我也没有别的差事,至少是我预见得到的,除了跑遍全岛去觅食,而这我或多或少每天都在做。

paragraphs.en: I now began to consider seriously my condition, and the circumstances I was reduced to; and I drew up the state of my affairs in writing, not so much to leave them to any that were to come after me—for I was likely to have but few heirs—as to deliver my thoughts from daily poring over them, and afflicting my mind; and as my reason began now to master my despondency, I began to comfort myself as well as I could, and to set the good against the evil, that I might have something to distinguish my case from worse; and I stated very impartially, like debtor and creditor, the comforts I enjoyed against the miseries I suffered, thus:—
paragraphs.cn: 我这时开始认真思量我的处境,以及我被逼到的这般境地;我把我的事务状况写下来,与其说是为了留给日后可能来到我身后的人——因为我大概不会有几个后人——不如说是为了让我的思绪从每天对它们的苦苦思量中解脱出来,免得折磨我的心;而当我的理智开始压服我的沮丧时,我便尽力宽慰自己,把好处同坏处相权,好让我的处境有点什么能与更糟的情形区别开来;我很公允地、像记债主与债户账目那样,把我所享的安慰同我所受的苦难两相对照,如下:——

paragraphs.en: _Evil_.
paragraphs.cn: 祸。

paragraphs.en: _Good_.
paragraphs.cn: 福。

paragraphs.en: I am cast upon a horrible, desolate island, void of all hope of recovery.
paragraphs.cn: 我被抛到一座可怕、荒凉的孤岛上,毫无获救的指望。

paragraphs.en: But I am alive; and not drowned, as all my ship’s company were.
paragraphs.cn: 可我还活着;没有像我同船的人那样统统淹死。

paragraphs.en: I am singled out and separated, as it were, from all the world, to be miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 我被单单挑出、仿佛与全世界隔绝,注定悲惨。

paragraphs.en: But I am singled out, too, from all the ship’s crew, to be spared from death; and He that miraculously saved me from death can deliver me from this condition.
paragraphs.cn: 可我也是从全船水手中被单单挑出、得以幸免于死的那个;那位奇迹般把我从死亡中救出的主,也能把我从这处境中解救出来。

paragraphs.en: I am divided from mankind—a solitaire; one banished from human society.
paragraphs.cn: 我与人类隔绝——一个孤独者;一个被逐出人类社会的人。

paragraphs.en: But I am not starved, and perishing on a barren place, affording no sustenance.
paragraphs.cn: 可我并没有饿死、没有在一片不产任何食物的贫瘠之地上等死。

paragraphs.en: I have no clothes to cover me.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有衣服蔽体。

paragraphs.en: But I am in a hot climate, where, if I had clothes, I could hardly wear them.
paragraphs.cn: 可我身处炎热的气候里,就算有衣服,恐怕也难以穿得住。

paragraphs.en: I am without any defence, or means to resist any violence of man or beast.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有任何防卫,也没有抵御人或兽任何暴力的手段。

paragraphs.en: But I am cast on an island where I see no wild beasts to hurt me, as I saw on the coast of Africa; and what if I had been shipwrecked there?
paragraphs.cn: 可我被抛到一座我没见到任何伤人野兽的岛上,不像我在非洲海岸所见的那样;倘若我当初是在那里遇难,又会怎样呢?

paragraphs.en: I have no soul to speak to or relieve me.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有一个人可以倾诉、可以宽慰我。

paragraphs.en: But God wonderfully sent the ship in near enough to the shore, that I have got out as many necessary things as will either supply my wants or enable me to supply myself, even as long as I live.
paragraphs.cn: 可上帝奇妙地把那船送到离岸够近的地方,叫我得以取出足够多的必需品,或供我所需,或使我能自给自足,哪怕活到老。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, here was an undoubted testimony that there was scarce any condition in the world so miserable but there was something negative or something positive to be thankful for in it; and let this stand as a direction from the experience of the most miserable of all conditions in this world: that we may always find in it something to comfort ourselves from, and to set, in the description of good and evil, on the credit side of the account.
paragraphs.cn: 总的说来,这里有个确凿的明证:世上几乎没有哪种处境悲惨到没有什么可消极或积极地感恩的;愿这作为一条来自世间最悲惨处境之经验的指引:我们总能在其中找到点什么来宽慰自己,并在权衡祸福时,把它记在账目的贷方一栏。

paragraphs.en: Having now brought my mind a little to relish my condition, and given over looking out to sea, to see if I could spy a ship—I say, giving over these things, I began to apply myself to arrange my way of living, and to make things as easy to me as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我已让自己的心稍稍能安于处境,并放下了朝海上张望、看能不能瞥见一条船的念头——我是说,放下这些事之后,我便开始着手安排我的生活方式,尽量把日子过得舒坦些。

paragraphs.en: I have already described my habitation, which was a tent under the side of a rock, surrounded with a strong pale of posts and cables: but I might now rather call it a wall, for I raised a kind of wall up against it of turfs, about two feet thick on the outside; and after some time (I think it was a year and a half) I raised rafters from it, leaning to the rock, and thatched or covered it with boughs of trees, and such things as I could get, to keep out the rain; which I found at some times of the year very violent.
paragraphs.cn: 我已经描述过我的住所,那是一座搭在岩壁下的帐篷,四周围着一道由木柱和缆绳构成的坚固栅栏:不过如今我倒不如称它为一堵墙,因为我顺着它筑起了一道草皮墙,外侧约两英尺厚;过了一段时间(我想是一年半)我又从它那里架起椽子,斜靠在岩壁上,盖上或者说苫上树枝和我能弄到的东西,好挡住雨水;那雨水我发现一年中某些时节很是凶猛。

paragraphs.en: I have already observed how I brought all my goods into this pale, and into the cave which I had made behind me.
paragraphs.cn: 我已经讲过,我如何把全部货物搬进这道栅栏、搬进我在身后掏出的那个洞穴。

paragraphs.en: But I must observe, too, that at first this was a confused heap of goods, which, as they lay in no order, so they took up all my place; I had no room to turn myself: so I set myself to enlarge my cave, and work farther into the earth; for it was a loose sandy rock, which yielded easily to the labour I bestowed on it: and so when I found I was pretty safe as to beasts of prey, I worked sideways, to the right hand, into the rock; and then, turning to the right again, worked quite out, and made me a door to come out on the outside of my pale or fortification.
paragraphs.cn: 但我也得说明,起初这是一堆乱糟糟的货物,它们既不成条理,便占满了我全部的地方;我连转个身的空当都没有:于是我着手扩大我的洞穴,往地里更深处掏;因为那是一块松软的沙岩,我下的力气一使,它很容易就让开了:等我发现自己对猛兽已相当安全之后,我便朝右手一侧横着掏,然后再向右一转,一直掏了出去,给自己做了一道门,好从我的栅栏或者说防御工事外面出来。

paragraphs.en: This gave me not only egress and regress, as it was a back way to my tent and to my storehouse, but gave me room to store my goods.
paragraphs.cn: 这不仅给了我进出之路,作为通到帐篷和库房的一条后道,还给了我存放货物的地方。

paragraphs.en: And now I began to apply myself to make such necessary things as I found I most wanted, particularly a chair and a table; for without these I was not able to enjoy the few comforts I had in the world; I could not write or eat, or do several things, with so much pleasure without a table: so I went to work.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我开始着手制作我发觉自己最缺的一些必需品,尤其是一把椅子和一张桌子;因为没有这些,我就没法享受我在这世上仅有的那几样安乐;没有桌子,我写字、吃饭,或做别的好几样事,都不能那么惬意:于是我动手干了起来。

paragraphs.en: And here I must needs observe, that as reason is the substance and origin of the mathematics, so by stating and squaring everything by reason, and by making the most rational judgment of things, every man may be, in time, master of every mechanic art.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里不得不指出,正如理性是数学的本体与本源一样,只要按理性去审度、去规范一切事物,并对事物做出最合乎理性的判断,任何人假以时日,都能精通每一门手艺。

paragraphs.en: I had never handled a tool in my life; and yet, in time, by labour, application, and contrivance, I found at last that I wanted nothing but I could have made it, especially if I had had tools.
paragraphs.cn: 我这辈子从没摆弄过工具;可是渐渐地,凭着劳作、用心和巧思,我最后发现,没有什么东西是我造不出来的,尤其是假如我有工具的话。

paragraphs.en: However, I made abundance of things, even without tools; and some with no more tools than an adze and a hatchet, which perhaps were never made that way before, and that with infinite labour.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,即便没有工具,我也造出了大量的东西;有些除了一把锛子和一把短柄斧再没别的工具,那些东西也许从来没人那样造过,而且是费了无穷的气力造成的。

paragraphs.en: For example, if I wanted a board, I had no other way but to cut down a tree, set it on an edge before me, and hew it flat on either side with my axe, till I brought it to be thin as a plank, and then dub it smooth with my adze.
paragraphs.cn: 比方说,若我要一块木板,除了砍倒一棵树、把它立在面前、用斧头把两面都劈平,直劈到薄得像块板子,再用锛子把它削光滑,我别无他法。

paragraphs.en: It is true, by this method I could make but one board out of a whole tree; but this I had no remedy for but patience, any more than I had for the prodigious deal of time and labour which it took me up to make a plank or board: but my time or labour was little worth, and so it was as well employed one way as another.
paragraphs.cn: 不错,用这法子我一整棵树只能做出一块板子;可这我没别的办法,只有靠耐心,正如我对做成一块板子所耗去的那大得惊人的时间和劳力也别无他法一样:但我的时间或劳力值不了几个钱,所以这样用和那样用也没什么两样。

paragraphs.en: However, I made me a table and a chair, as I observed above, in the first place; and this I did out of the short pieces of boards that I brought on my raft from the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 不管怎样,我如上所述,首先给自己做了一张桌子和一把椅子;这是我用从船上筏子运来的那些短木板做成的。

paragraphs.en: But when I had wrought out some boards as above, I made large shelves, of the breadth of a foot and a half, one over another all along one side of my cave, to lay all my tools, nails and ironwork on; and, in a word, to separate everything at large into their places, that I might come easily at them.
paragraphs.cn: 可等我如上所述做出了一些木板后,我又做了几层大搁板,一英尺半宽,一层叠一层地沿着我洞穴的一整面排开,用来放我所有的工具、钉子和铁器;总之,把所有东西分门别类、宽宽敞敞地各归其位,好让我随手就能取到。

paragraphs.en: I knocked pieces into the wall of the rock to hang my guns and all things that would hang up; so that, had my cave been to be seen, it looked like a general magazine of all necessary things; and had everything so ready at my hand, that it was a great pleasure to me to see all my goods in such order, and especially to find my stock of all necessaries so great.
paragraphs.cn: 我把一些木块凿进岩壁里,好挂我的枪和一切挂得起来的东西;这样一来,我的洞穴倘若给人看见,就活像一个百物齐备的总仓库了;而且一切都这样触手可及,看着我全部的货物如此井然有序,尤其是发觉我各项必需品的存货如此充足,真叫我大为快慰。

paragraphs.en: And now it was that I began to keep a journal of every day’s employment; for, indeed, at first I was in too much hurry, and not only hurry as to labour, but in too much discomposure of mind; and my journal would have been full of many dull things; for example, I must have said thus: “30_th_.
paragraphs.cn: 也正是这时候,我开始记起每日营生的日记来;因为说实在的,起初我太忙乱,不光是活计上忙乱,心境也太不平静;我的日记本会写满许多枯燥的事;比方说,我大概会这样写:“三十日。

paragraphs.en: —After I had got to shore, and escaped drowning, instead of being thankful to God for my deliverance, having first vomited, with the great quantity of salt water which had got into my stomach, and recovering myself a little, I ran about the shore wringing my hands and beating my head and face, exclaiming at my misery, and crying out, ‘I was undone, undone!’ till, tired and faint, I was forced to lie down on the ground to repose, but durst not sleep for fear of being devoured.”
paragraphs.cn: ——我上岸、逃过淹死之后,没有为自己的获救感谢上帝,反倒先是呕吐了一番,因为大量海水灌进了我的肚子,略微缓过来一点后,便在岸上跑来跑去,绞着双手、捶着脑袋和脸,痛斥自己的悲惨,大喊大叫:‘我完了,我完了!’直到又累又乏,不得不躺在地上歇息,却又不敢睡,生怕被吞掉。”

paragraphs.en: Some days after this, and after I had been on board the ship, and got all that I could out of her, yet I could not forbear getting up to the top of a little mountain and looking out to sea, in hopes of seeing a ship; then fancy at a vast distance I spied a sail, please myself with the hopes of it, and then after looking steadily, till I was almost blind, lose it quite, and sit down and weep like a child, and thus increase my misery by my folly.
paragraphs.cn: 这之后过了几天,在我上过船、把能弄的都从船里弄出来之后,我还是忍不住爬上一座小山顶,朝海上张望,盼着能看见一条船;接着又幻想在极远处瞥见一片帆,拿这指望自娱一番,然后目不转睛地盯着看,直到眼睛几乎发花,又把它彻底看丢,便坐下来像孩子一样哭泣,就这样以自己的愚蠢添增自己的悲苦。

paragraphs.en: But having gotten over these things in some measure, and having settled my household staff and habitation, made me a table and a chair, and all as handsome about me as I could, I began to keep my journal; of which I shall here give you the copy (though in it will be told all these particulars over again) as long as it lasted; for having no more ink, I was forced to leave it off.
paragraphs.cn: 但把这些事在某种程度上熬过来之后,我安顿好了家什和住所,给自己做了一张桌子和一把椅子,并尽我所能把周遭一切都收拾得像样些,我便开始记我的日记;我这就把它的抄本在此奉上(尽管里面会把这一切细节重新讲上一遍),直到它记完为止;因为再没有墨水了,我只好把它搁下不写了。

paragraphs.en: September 30, 1659.

—I, poor miserable Robinson Crusoe, being shipwrecked during a dreadful storm in the offing, came on shore on this dismal, unfortunate island, which I called “The Island of Despair”; all the rest of the ship’s company being drowned, and myself almost dead.
paragraphs.cn: ——我,可怜又不幸的鲁滨逊·克鲁索,在一场可怕的海上风暴中遭遇船难,漂到了这座凄凉而不祥的岛上,我把它叫作“绝望岛”;船上其余的人全都淹死了,我自己也几乎丧了命。

paragraphs.en: All the rest of the day I spent in afflicting myself at the dismal circumstances I was brought to—viz.
paragraphs.cn: 这一整天余下的时间,我都在为自己落到的悲惨处境而痛苦——也就是说,

paragraphs.en: I had neither food, house, clothes, weapon, nor place to fly to; and in despair of any relief, saw nothing but death before me—either that I should be devoured by wild beasts, murdered by savages, or starved to death for want of food.
paragraphs.cn: 我既没有食物、房屋、衣服、武器,也没有可以逃往的地方;绝望之中看不到一丝救援,眼前只有死亡——要么被野兽吞掉,要么被野人杀死,要么因缺粮而饿死。

paragraphs.en: At the approach of night I slept in a tree, for fear of wild creatures; but slept soundly, though it rained all night.
paragraphs.cn: 夜幕降临时,我怕野兽,便睡在一棵树上;虽然下了一整夜的雨,我却睡得很沉。

paragraphs.en: _October_ 1.

—In the morning I saw, to my great surprise, the ship had floated with the high tide, and was driven on shore again much nearer the island; which, as it was some comfort, on one hand—for, seeing her set upright, and not broken to pieces, I hoped, if the wind abated, I might get on board, and get some food and necessaries out of her for my relief—so, on the other hand, it renewed my grief at the loss of my comrades, who, I imagined, if we had all stayed on board, might have saved the ship, or, at least, that they would not have been all drowned as they were; and that, had the men been saved, we might perhaps have built us a boat out of the ruins of the ship to have carried us to some other part of the world.
paragraphs.cn: ——早晨,我惊讶万分地发现,那条船随涨潮浮了起来,又被冲到更靠近小岛的岸边;这一方面让我稍感安慰——看到它直立着,没有散架,我便盼着若风势减弱,或许能爬上船,弄些食物和必需品来救急——可另一方面,又勾起我丧失同伴的悲痛,我想,要是当初大家都留在船上,也许能保住这条船,至少不至于像现在这样全都淹死;而若那些人得以生还,我们或许还能用船的残骸造一条小船,把我们带到世界别的地方去。

paragraphs.en: I spent great part of this day in perplexing myself on these things; but at length, seeing the ship almost dry, I went upon the sand as near as I could, and then swam on board.
paragraphs.cn: 这一天我大部分时间都在为这些事困扰;但最后,见船已几乎露出水面,我便沿沙滩尽量走近,然后游上了船。

paragraphs.en: This day also it continued raining, though with no wind at all.
paragraphs.cn: 这一天也一直下着雨,不过一点风也没有。

paragraphs.en: _From the 1st of October to the 24th_.
paragraphs.cn: 从10月1日到24日。

paragraphs.en: —All these days entirely spent in many several voyages to get all I could out of the ship, which I brought on shore every tide of flood upon rafts.
paragraphs.cn: ——这些天全都花在了一次次往返船上、尽量把能取的东西都取出来,每逢涨潮我就用木筏把它们运上岸。

paragraphs.en: Much rain also in the days, though with some intervals of fair weather; but it seems this was the rainy season.
paragraphs.cn: 这些日子里雨也下得很多,偶尔才放晴;看来这正是雨季。

paragraphs.en: _Oct.
—I overset my raft, and all the goods I had got upon it; but, being in shoal water, and the things being chiefly heavy, I recovered many of them when the tide was out.
paragraphs.cn: ——我把木筏连同上面装的所有货物都弄翻了;好在那是浅水,东西又大多沉重,退潮时我把许多都捞了回来。

paragraphs.en: _Oct.

—It rained all night and all day, with some gusts of wind; during which time the ship broke in pieces, the wind blowing a little harder than before, and was no more to be seen, except the wreck of her, and that only at low water.
paragraphs.cn: ——整夜整日都下着雨,还夹着阵阵狂风;这期间那条船碎裂了,风比先前刮得猛了些,船便再也看不见了,只剩残骸,而且只有落潮时才露得出来。

paragraphs.en: I spent this day in covering and securing the goods which I had saved, that the rain might not spoil them.
paragraphs.cn: 这一天我用来遮盖并收好抢救下来的货物,免得被雨淋坏。

paragraphs.en: _Oct.
—I walked about the shore almost all day, to find out a place to fix my habitation, greatly concerned to secure myself from any attack in the night, either from wild beasts or men.
paragraphs.cn: ——我几乎走了一整天海岸,想找个地方安家,一心想着夜里如何防备野兽或人来袭。

paragraphs.en: Towards night, I fixed upon a proper place, under a rock, and marked out a semicircle for my encampment; which I resolved to strengthen with a work, wall, or fortification, made of double piles, lined within with cables, and without with turf.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚时分,我在一块岩石下选定了合适的地点,并划出一个半圆作为我的营地;我决意用一道工事、围墙或防御来加固它,用双排木桩筑成,里面衬以缆索,外面覆以草皮。

paragraphs.en: From the 26th to the 30th I worked very hard in carrying all my goods to my new habitation, though some part of the time it rained exceedingly hard.
paragraphs.cn: 从26日到30日,我拼命地把所有货物搬到新住处,尽管有些时候雨下得极大。

paragraphs.en: The 31st, in the morning, I went out into the island with my gun, to seek for some food, and discover the country; when I killed a she-goat, and her kid followed me home, which I afterwards killed also, because it would not feed.
paragraphs.cn: 31日早晨,我带着枪走进岛里,想找些食物,并探查一下这地方;我打死了一只母山羊,它的小羊跟着我回了家,后来我把小羊也杀了,因为它不肯吃食。

paragraphs.en: _November_ 1.
—I set up my tent under a rock, and lay there for the first night; making it as large as I could, with stakes driven in to swing my hammock upon.
paragraphs.cn: ——我在一块岩石下支起帐篷,头一夜就睡在那里;我把帐篷做得尽量大,打下木桩来挂我的吊床。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—I set up all my chests and boards, and the pieces of timber which made my rafts, and with them formed a fence round me, a little within the place I had marked out for my fortification.
paragraphs.cn: ——我把所有箱子、木板,还有做木筏用的木料都竖起来,用它们在自己四周围了一道栅栏,位置就在我划出的防御线略往里一点。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—I went out with my gun, and killed two fowls like ducks, which were very good food.
paragraphs.cn: ——我带枪出去,打死两只像鸭子的水禽,肉很好吃。

paragraphs.en: In the afternoon went to work to make me a table.
paragraphs.cn: 下午动手做了一张桌子。

paragraphs.en: _Nov_.

—This morning I began to order my times of work, of going out with my gun, time of sleep, and time of diversion—viz. every morning I walked out with my gun for two or three hours, if it did not rain; then employed myself to work till about eleven o’clock; then eat what I had to live on; and from twelve to two I lay down to sleep, the weather being excessively hot; and then, in the evening, to work again.
paragraphs.cn: ——这天早晨,我开始安排作息:干活的时间、带枪外出的时间、睡觉和消遣的时间——也就是说,每天早晨若不下雨,我就带枪出去走两三个钟头;然后干活到十一点左右;接着吃些赖以维生的东西;从十二点到两点躺下睡觉,因为天热得厉害;傍晚再干活。

paragraphs.en: The working part of this day and of the next were wholly employed in making my table, for I was yet but a very sorry workman, though time and necessity made me a complete natural mechanic soon after, as I believe they would do any one else.
paragraphs.cn: 这一天和第二天用来干活的时间,全都花在做桌子上,因为我那时还是个很蹩脚的工匠,不过时间和需要不久就把我练成了一个地道的能工巧匠,我相信换了别人也会一样。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—This day went abroad with my gun and my dog, and killed a wild cat; her skin pretty soft, but her flesh good for nothing; every creature that I killed I took of the skins and preserved them.
paragraphs.cn: ——这天我带着枪和狗出门,打死一只野猫;它的皮相当柔软,肉却毫无用处;每只被我打死的动物,我都剥下皮保存起来。

paragraphs.en: Coming back by the sea-shore, I saw many sorts of sea-fowls, which I did not understand; but was surprised, and almost frightened, with two or three seals, which, while I was gazing at, not well knowing what they were, got into the sea, and escaped me for that time.
paragraphs.cn: 沿海岸回来时,我看见许多种叫不出名字的海鸟;还有两三头海豹,把我吓了一跳,几乎叫我害怕,我正盯着它们、弄不清是什么东西时,它们钻进海里,这回逃脱了。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—After my morning walk I went to work with my table again, and finished it, though not to my liking; nor was it long before I learned to mend it.
paragraphs.cn: ——晨间散步之后,我又去做那张桌子,把它做完了,虽然不合我意;不过没多久我就学会了把它修好。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—Now it began to be settled fair weather.
paragraphs.cn: ——如今天气开始转为稳定的晴朗。

paragraphs.en: The 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and part of the 12th (for the 11th was Sunday) I took wholly up to make me a chair, and with much ado brought it to a tolerable shape, but never to please me; and even in the making I pulled it in pieces several times.
paragraphs.cn: 7日、8日、9日、10日,还有12日的一部分（因为11日是星期日），我全都用来给自己做一把椅子,好不容易才做成个勉强像样的形状,可我总不满意;甚至在做的过程中,我几次把它拆散重来。

paragraphs.en: _Note_.
paragraphs.cn: 附注。

paragraphs.en: —I soon neglected my keeping Sundays; for, omitting my mark for them on my post, I forgot which was which.
paragraphs.cn: ——我很快就不再记着过星期日了;因为我忘了在木柱上刻下标记,便分不清哪天是哪天了。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—This day it rained, which refreshed me exceedingly, and cooled the earth; but it was accompanied with terrible thunder and lightning, which frightened me dreadfully, for fear of my powder.
paragraphs.cn: ——这天下雨,让我格外清爽,也给大地降了温;但雨中伴着可怕的雷电,把我吓得要命,生怕我的火药出事。

paragraphs.en: As soon as it was over, I resolved to separate my stock of powder into as many little parcels as possible, that it might not be in danger.
paragraphs.cn: 雨一停,我便决意把火药尽量分成许多小包,免得它遭遇危险。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.

—These three days I spent in making little square chests, or boxes, which might hold about a pound, or two pounds at most, of powder; and so, putting the powder in, I stowed it in places as secure and remote from one another as possible.
paragraphs.cn: ——这三天我用来做一些小方箱或小盒子,每个约莫能装一磅、最多两磅火药;装好火药后,我把它们尽量安放在彼此安全又隔得远的地方。

paragraphs.en: On one of these three days I killed a large bird that was good to eat, but I knew not what to call it.
paragraphs.cn: 这三天里的某一天,我打死一只大鸟,肉很好吃,可我不知道该叫它什么。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—This day I began to dig behind my tent into the rock, to make room for my further conveniency.
paragraphs.cn: ——这天我开始在帐篷后面往岩石里挖,好给自己腾出更多方便的空间。

paragraphs.en: _Note_.
paragraphs.cn: 附注。

paragraphs.en: —Three things I wanted exceedingly for this work—viz. a pickaxe, a shovel, and a wheelbarrow or basket; so I desisted from my work, and began to consider how to supply that want, and make me some tools.
paragraphs.cn: ——干这活我极其需要三样东西——也就是一把镐、一把铲,还有一辆手推车或一只筐;于是我停下手来,琢磨怎么弥补这缺口,给自己做几件工具。

paragraphs.en: As for the pickaxe, I made use of the iron crows, which were proper enough, though heavy; but the next thing was a shovel or spade; this was so absolutely necessary, that, indeed, I could do nothing effectually without it; but what kind of one to make I knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 至于镐,我就用那几根铁撬,虽然沉重,倒也够用;可接下来是铲子或锹;这东西实在太不可少,没有它我什么正经事都干不成;只是该做个什么样的,我却毫无头绪。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.
—The next day, in searching the woods, I found a tree of that wood, or like it, which in the Brazils they call the iron-tree, for its exceeding hardness.
paragraphs.cn: ——第二天,我在林子里搜寻时,找到一棵那种木头做的树,或是类似的树,巴西人因它异常坚硬,把它叫作铁树。

paragraphs.en: Of this, with great labour, and almost spoiling my axe, I cut a piece, and brought it home, too, with difficulty enough, for it was exceeding heavy.
paragraphs.cn: 我费了好大的劲,几乎把斧子都毁了,才从上面砍下一段,又好不容易把它扛回了家,因为它沉得出奇。

paragraphs.en: The excessive hardness of the wood, and my having no other way, made me a long while upon this machine, for I worked it effectually by little and little into the form of a shovel or spade; the handle exactly shaped like ours in England, only that the board part having no iron shod upon it at bottom, it would not last me so long; however, it served well enough for the uses which I had occasion to put it to; but never was a shovel, I believe, made after that fashion, or so long in making.
paragraphs.cn: 这木头硬得离谱,我又别无他法,便在这件家伙上耗了很久,因为我是一点一点、切实地把它做成铲子或锹的样子;把手完全照我们英格兰的式样做,只是铲板底下没包铁皮,不能用得太久;不过对我要派它去干的活儿,倒也够用了;可我相信,从没有一把铲子是照那样做出来的,也没有一把做得那么费时。

paragraphs.en: I was still deficient, for I wanted a basket or a wheelbarrow.
paragraphs.cn: 我仍缺一样东西,因为我还想要个筐或手推车。

paragraphs.en: A basket I could not make by any means, having no such things as twigs that would bend to make wicker-ware—at least, none yet found out; and as to a wheelbarrow, I fancied I could make all but the wheel; but that I had no notion of; neither did I know how to go about it; besides, I had no possible way to make the iron gudgeons for the spindle or axis of the wheel to run in; so I gave it over, and so, for carrying away the earth which I dug out of the cave, I made me a thing like a hod which the labourers carry mortar in when they serve the bricklayers.
paragraphs.cn: 筐我怎么也做不成,因为没有能弯折来编柳器的枝条——至少眼下还没找到;至于手推车,我觉得除了轮子,别的都能做;可轮子我毫无概念,也不知从何下手;再说,我根本没法做出让轮轴或转轴转动所需的铁轴承;于是我作罢了,便为搬运从洞里挖出来的泥土,给自己做了个类似泥兜的东西,就是工人给泥瓦匠打下手时用来盛灰浆的那种。

paragraphs.en: This was not so difficult to me as the making the shovel; and yet this and the shovel, and the attempt which I made in vain to make a wheelbarrow, took me up no less than four days—I mean always excepting my morning walk with my gun, which I seldom failed, and very seldom failed also bringing home something fit to eat.
paragraphs.cn: 这对我不像做铲子那么难;可这个连同铲子,再加上我白费力气想做手推车的那番折腾,竟花了我整整四天——我是说,这里头始终不算我每天早晨带枪的散步,那我很少落下,也很少空着手回来、不带点能吃的东西。

paragraphs.en: _Nov.

—My other work having now stood still, because of my making these tools, when they were finished I went on, and working every day, as my strength and time allowed, I spent eighteen days entirely in widening and deepening my cave, that it might hold my goods commodiously.
paragraphs.cn: ——我别的活儿因做这些工具都停了下来,工具做好后我又接着干,每天在体力和时间许可下干活,整整花了十八天来加宽加深我的洞穴,好让它宽敞地容下我的货物。

paragraphs.en: _Note_.
paragraphs.cn: 附注。

paragraphs.en: —During all this time I worked to make this room or cave spacious enough to accommodate me as a warehouse or magazine, a kitchen, a dining-room, and a cellar.
paragraphs.cn: ——这段时间里,我一直在把这个屋子或洞穴弄得够宽敞,好当我的仓库或货栈、厨房、饭厅兼地窖。

paragraphs.en: As for my lodging, I kept to the tent; except that sometimes, in the wet season of the year, it rained so hard that I could not keep myself dry, which caused me afterwards to cover all my place within my pale with long poles, in the form of rafters, leaning against the rock, and load them with flags and large leaves of trees, like a thatch.
paragraphs.cn: 至于睡觉,我仍住在帐篷里;只是有时候,在一年中多雨的季节,雨下得太大,我没法保持干爽,这使我后来在围栏里的整块地方上都盖起长杆,做成椽子的样子,斜靠在岩石上,再压上菖蒲和大树叶,像铺茅草一样。

paragraphs.en: _December_ 10.

—I began now to think my cave or vault finished, when on a sudden (it seems I had made it too large) a great quantity of earth fell down from the top on one side; so much that, in short, it frighted me, and not without reason, too, for if I had been under it, I had never wanted a gravedigger.
paragraphs.cn: ——我正开始觉得我的洞穴或地窖大功告成,不料一下子（看来是我把它挖得太大了）,顶上一侧塌下大量泥土;塌得如此之多,总之把我吓坏了,而且不无道理,因为我若当时正在下面,就永远用不着掘墓人了。

paragraphs.en: I had now a great deal of work to do over again, for I had the loose earth to carry out; and, which was of more importance, I had the ceiling to prop up, so that I might be sure no more would come down.
paragraphs.cn: 这下我又有一大堆活要重做,因为松土得清出去;更要紧的是,我得把顶棚撑住,好确保不会再有东西塌下来。

paragraphs.en: _Dec_.

—This day I went to work with it accordingly, and got two shores or posts pitched upright to the top, with two pieces of boards across over each post; this I finished the next day; and setting more posts up with boards, in about a week more I had the roof secured, and the posts, standing in rows, served me for partitions to part off the house.
paragraphs.cn: ——这天我照此动手,弄了两根撑木或立柱直顶到顶上,每根柱子上横搭两块木板;第二天我把这活做完;又立起更多带木板的柱子,再过约莫一个星期,我便把顶固定住了,那些成排立着的柱子,还给我当了隔断,把屋子分了开来。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—From this day to the 20th I placed shelves, and knocked up nails on the posts, to hang everything up that could be hung up; and now I began to be in some order within doors.
paragraphs.cn: ——从这天到20日,我装了搁板,在柱子上钉起钉子,好把能挂的东西都挂起来;这下屋里总算有了些条理。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.

—Now I carried everything into the cave, and began to furnish my house, and set up some pieces of boards like a dresser, to order my victuals upon; but boards began to be very scarce with me; also, I made me another table.
paragraphs.cn: ——如今我把一切都搬进了洞里,开始布置我的家,还立起几块木板像个碗柜似的,好把食物摆放整齐;可木板对我来说开始变得很紧缺了;我还给自己做了另一张桌子。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—Much rain all night and all day.
paragraphs.cn: ——整夜整日都下大雨。

paragraphs.en: No stirring out.
paragraphs.cn: 没法出门。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—Rain all day.
paragraphs.cn: ——下了一整天雨。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—No rain, and the earth much cooler than before, and pleasanter.
paragraphs.cn: ——没下雨,地面比先前凉爽多了,也惬意多了。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—Killed a young goat, and lamed another, so that I caught it and led it home in a string; when I had it at home, I bound and splintered up its leg, which was broke.
paragraphs.cn: ——打死一只小山羊,又打伤了另一只,我便逮住它,用绳子牵回了家;到家后,我把它折断的腿绑好、上了夹板。
特别

paragraphs.en: B.
paragraphs.cn: 注意。

paragraphs.en: _—I took such care of it that it lived, and the leg grew well and as strong as ever; but, by my nursing it so long, it grew tame, and fed upon the little green at my door, and would not go away.
paragraphs.cn: ——我这般精心照料它,它竟活了下来,那条腿也长好了,和从前一样有力;可我照看它这么久,它变得温驯了,吃着我门口那点青草,再也不肯走开。

paragraphs.en: This was the first time that I entertained a thought of breeding up some tame creatures, that I might have food when my powder and shot was all spent.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我头一回起了饲养些温驯牲畜的念头,好在火药和铅弹用光后仍有食物可吃。

paragraphs.en: _Dec.
—Great heats and no breeze, so that there was no stirring abroad except in the evening for food; this time I spent in putting all my things in order within doors.
paragraphs.cn: ——酷热难当,又无一丝微风,除了傍晚出去找食,外面根本待不住;这段时间我用来把屋里所有东西都收拾停当。

paragraphs.en: _January_ 1.
paragraphs.cn: 1月1日。

paragraphs.en: —Very hot still: but I went abroad early and late with my gun, and lay still in the middle of the day.
paragraphs.cn: ——天仍很热:但我一早一晚都带枪出门,正午则静静地躺着。

paragraphs.en: This evening, going farther into the valleys which lay towards the centre of the island, I found there were plenty of goats, though exceedingly shy, and hard to come at; however, I resolved to try if I could not bring my dog to hunt them down.
paragraphs.cn: 这天傍晚,我往岛中央那些山谷更深处走去,发现那里山羊很多,只是它们极其胆怯,难以接近;不过我决意试试,看能不能训练我的狗把它们追捕下来。

paragraphs.en: _Jan.
paragraphs.cn: 1月

paragraphs.en: —Accordingly, the next day I went out with my dog, and set him upon the goats, but I was mistaken, for they all faced about upon the dog, and he knew his danger too well, for he would not come near them.
paragraphs.cn: ——于是第二天我带狗出去,放它去追山羊,可我错了,因为它们全都掉头面对着狗,而狗深知自己的危险,不肯靠近它们。

paragraphs.en: _Jan.
paragraphs.cn: 1月

paragraphs.en: —I began my fence or wall; which, being still jealous of my being attacked by somebody, I resolved to make very thick and strong.
paragraphs.cn: ——我开始筑我的栅栏或围墙;因为始终提防着有人来袭,我决意把它筑得又厚又结实。
特别

paragraphs.en: B.
paragraphs.cn: 注意。

paragraphs.en: _—This wall being described before, I purposely omit what was said in the journal; it is sufficient to observe, that I was no less time than from the 2nd of January to the 14th of April working, finishing, and perfecting this wall, though it was no more than about twenty-four yards in length, being a half-circle from one place in the rock to another place, about eight yards from it, the door of the cave being in the centre behind it.
paragraphs.cn: ——这道墙前面已经描述过,我便有意略去日记里说过的话;只需交代一句:我从1月2日一直干到4月14日,才把这道墙修筑、完成并做得完善,尽管它不过约二十四码长,是从岩石上一处到另一处、相距约八码的一个半圆,洞门就在它后面的正中央。

paragraphs.en: All this time I worked very hard, the rains hindering me many days, nay, sometimes weeks together; but I thought I should never be perfectly secure till this wall was finished; and it is scarce credible what inexpressible labour everything was done with, especially the bringing piles out of the woods and driving them into the ground; for I made them much bigger than I needed to have done.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间我干得非常辛苦,雨水耽误了我许多天,不,有时接连几个星期;可我觉得,不把这道墙筑好,我就永远不会有十足的安全感;而且几乎叫人难以置信,每件事都费了多少说不出的力气,尤其是从林子里弄来木桩、把它们打进地里;因为我把它们做得比实际需要的粗大多了。

paragraphs.en: When this wall was finished, and the outside double fenced, with a turf wall raised up close to it, I perceived myself that if any people were to come on shore there, they would not perceive anything like a habitation; and it was very well I did so, as may be observed hereafter, upon a very remarkable occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 这道墙筑好、外侧又用一道紧贴着它的草皮墙双重加固之后,我发觉,倘若有人上岸到这里来,是丝毫看不出这里像个住处的;我这样做很对,日后在一桩很值得一提的事情上便可看出来。

paragraphs.en: During this time I made my rounds in the woods for game every day when the rain permitted me, and made frequent discoveries in these walks of something or other to my advantage; particularly, I found a kind of wild pigeons, which build, not as wood-pigeons in a tree, but rather as house-pigeons, in the holes of the rocks; and taking some young ones, I endeavoured to breed them up tame, and did so; but when they grew older they flew away, which perhaps was at first for want of feeding them, for I had nothing to give them; however, I frequently found their nests, and got their young ones, which were very good meat.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间里,只要雨停,我每天都到林子里巡猎,在这些行走中常有种种发现对我有利;特别是,我找到一种野鸽,它们不像林鸽那样在树上筑巢,倒像家鸽那样在岩石的洞窟里做窝;我捉了些雏鸽,想把它们养驯,也确实养驯了;可它们长大些便飞走了,起初或许是因为我没喂它们,因为我没什么可给它们吃的;不过我常常找到它们的窝,取来它们的雏鸟,那肉很好吃。

paragraphs.en: And now, in the managing my household affairs, I found myself wanting in many things, which I thought at first it was impossible for me to make; as, indeed, with some of them it was: for instance, I could never make a cask to be hooped.
paragraphs.cn: 如今,在料理家务之际,我发觉自己缺许多东西,起初我以为这些是我根本做不出来的;其中有些确实如此:比方说,我怎么也做不出一只能箍起来的木桶。

paragraphs.en: I had a small runlet or two, as I observed before; but I could never arrive at the capacity of making one by them, though I spent many weeks about it; I could neither put in the heads, or join the staves so true to one another as to make them hold water; so I gave that also over.
paragraphs.cn: 我有一两只小桶,前面提到过;可我怎么也达不到照着它们做一只的本领,尽管为此花了好几个星期;我既装不上桶底,也没法把桶板拼接得严丝合缝到能盛水;于是这事我也放弃了。

paragraphs.en: In the next place, I was at a great loss for candles; so that as soon as ever it was dark, which was generally by seven o’clock, I was obliged to go to bed.
paragraphs.cn: 其次,我极缺蜡烛;所以天一黑,一般到七点钟,我就不得不上床睡觉。

paragraphs.en: I remembered the lump of beeswax with which I made candles in my African adventure; but I had none of that now; the only remedy I had was, that when I had killed a goat I saved the tallow, and with a little dish made of clay, which I baked in the sun, to which I added a wick of some oakum, I made me a lamp; and this gave me light, though not a clear, steady light, like a candle.
paragraphs.cn: 我记得当年在非洲历险时,曾用一块蜂蜡做蜡烛;可现在我一点也没有了;我唯一的办法是,打死山羊后把油脂留下,再用一只我在太阳下晒硬的小陶碟,加上一根麻絮做的灯芯,给自己做了盏灯;这灯给了我亮光,虽不像蜡烛那样明亮而稳定。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of all my labours it happened that, rummaging my things, I found a little bag which, as I hinted before, had been filled with corn for the feeding of poultry—not for this voyage, but before, as I suppose, when the ship came from Lisbon.
paragraphs.cn: 忙碌之中,我偶然在翻检自己的东西时,找到一个小袋子,前面暗示过,里面曾装着喂家禽的谷子——不是这趟航行装的,我猜是更早以前、船从里斯本开来时装的。

paragraphs.en: The little remainder of corn that had been in the bag was all devoured by the rats, and I saw nothing in the bag but husks and dust; and being willing to have the bag for some other use (I think it was to put powder in, when I divided it for fear of the lightning, or some such use), I shook the husks of corn out of it on one side of my fortification, under the rock.
paragraphs.cn: 袋里剩下的那点谷子早被老鼠啃光了,我在袋里只见到些谷壳和尘土;我想把袋子挪作他用（我想是分火药以防雷电时用来装火药,或是诸如此类的用途）,便把里面的谷壳往我防御工事一侧、岩石下面抖了出来。

paragraphs.en: It was a little before the great rains just now mentioned that I threw this stuff away, taking no notice, and not so much as remembering that I had thrown anything there, when, about a month after, or thereabouts, I saw some few stalks of something green shooting out of the ground, which I fancied might be some plant I had not seen; but I was surprised, and perfectly astonished, when, after a little longer time, I saw about ten or twelve ears come out, which were perfect green barley, of the same kind as our European—nay, as our English barley.
paragraphs.cn: 我把这堆东西倒掉,正是在刚才提到的那场大雨之前,当时并没在意,甚至根本不记得往那儿倒过什么东西;不料约莫一个月后,我看见地里冒出几根绿茎,我以为大概是某种我没见过的植物;可又过了些时候,我看到抽出约莫十来穗,竟是十足的青大麦,和我们欧洲的——不,和我们英格兰的大麦一模一样,我又惊又骇,简直目瞪口呆。

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to express the astonishment and confusion of my thoughts on this occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 我此刻心里的惊愕与纷乱,实在无法用言语表达。

paragraphs.en: I had hitherto acted upon no religious foundation at all; indeed, I had very few notions of religion in my head, nor had entertained any sense of anything that had befallen me otherwise than as chance, or, as we lightly say, what pleases God, without so much as inquiring into the end of Providence in these things, or His order in governing events for the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这以前根本没有任何宗教信仰;说实在的,我脑子里几乎没有宗教观念,对降临到我身上的一切,也只当作偶然,或者像我们随口说的“上帝高兴罢了”,压根儿没去探究天意在这些事上的用意,也没想过祂治理世间万事的安排。

paragraphs.en: But after I saw barley grow there, in a climate which I knew was not proper for corn, and especially that I knew not how it came there, it startled me strangely, and I began to suggest that God had miraculously caused His grain to grow without any help of seed sown, and that it was so directed purely for my sustenance on that wild, miserable place.
paragraphs.cn: 可自从我看见大麦长在这里——一个我知道并不适合种谷物的气候里,尤其是我不知道它是怎么来的——这就叫我大为惊异,我开始揣想是上帝奇迹般地让祂的谷物没经播种就长了出来,而这样安排纯是为了在这荒凉悲惨之地供养我。

paragraphs.en: This touched my heart a little, and brought tears out of my eyes, and I began to bless myself that such a prodigy of nature should happen upon my account; and this was the more strange to me, because I saw near it still, all along by the side of the rock, some other straggling stalks, which proved to be stalks of rice, and which I knew, because I had seen it grow in Africa when I was ashore there.
paragraphs.cn: 这稍稍触动了我的心,叫我流下泪来,我开始庆幸,这样一桩自然界的奇迹竟为我而发生;这对我更显奇异,因为我看见近旁、沿着岩石一侧,还有些零散的茎秆,后来证明是稻茎,我认得,因为我当年在非洲上岸时曾见它生长。

paragraphs.en: I not only thought these the pure productions of Providence for my support, but not doubting that there was more in the place, I went all over that part of the island, where I had been before, peering in every corner, and under every rock, to see for more of it, but I could not find any.
paragraphs.cn: 我不但把这些当作天意为供养我而生的纯粹造物,而且深信这地方还有更多,便走遍我先前到过的那一带岛地,在每个角落、每块岩石下张望,想找到更多,却一无所获。

paragraphs.en: At last it occurred to my thoughts that I shook a bag of chickens’ meat out in that place; and then the wonder began to cease; and I must confess my religious thankfulness to God’s providence began to abate, too, upon the discovering that all this was nothing but what was common; though I ought to have been as thankful for so strange and unforeseen a providence as if it had been miraculous; for it was really the work of Providence to me, that should order or appoint that ten or twelve grains of corn should remain unspoiled, when the rats had destroyed all the rest, as if it had been dropped from heaven; as also, that I should throw it out in that particular place, where, it being in the shade of a high rock, it sprang up immediately; whereas, if I had thrown it anywhere else at that time, it had been burnt up and destroyed.
paragraphs.cn: 最后我想起,我曾在那地方抖出过一袋喂鸡的饲料;于是这惊奇便开始消退;我得承认,一发现这一切不过是寻常之事,我对上帝天意那份虔敬的感激也随之淡了下去;其实我本该像它真是奇迹一样心怀感激,因为它对我实在是天意的安排:老鼠毁掉了其余全部,偏偏这十来粒谷子未遭损坏,仿佛是从天上落下来的;况且我又偏偏把它抖在那个地方,那里正处在一块高岩的荫下,谷子立刻就发了芽;而我若当时把它抖在别处,早就被晒枯毁掉了。

paragraphs.en: I carefully saved the ears of this corn, you may be sure, in their season, which was about the end of June; and, laying up every corn, I resolved to sow them all again, hoping in time to have some quantity sufficient to supply me with bread.
paragraphs.cn: 你尽可放心,到了收成时节——约莫六月底——我小心地把这谷穗都留了下来;把每一粒谷子都收好,我决意全都重新播下,盼着日久能积攒足够的量来供我做面包。

paragraphs.en: But it was not till the fourth year that I could allow myself the least grain of this corn to eat, and even then but sparingly, as I shall say afterwards, in its order; for I lost all that I sowed the first season by not observing the proper time; for I sowed it just before the dry season, so that it never came up at all, at least not as it would have done; of which in its place.
paragraphs.cn: 可直到第四年,我才舍得吃这谷子中最小的一粒,即便那时也很省着吃,后面我会按次序细说;因为头一季播下的我全都糟蹋了,只因没留意适当的时节;我恰恰在旱季前播了种,结果它根本没出苗,至少没能像该有的那样长起来;这事到时候再讲。

paragraphs.en: Besides this barley, there were, as above, twenty or thirty stalks of rice, which I preserved with the same care and for the same use, or to the same purpose—to make me bread, or rather food; for I found ways to cook it without baking, though I did that also after some time.
paragraphs.cn: 除了这大麦,如上所说,还有二三十根稻茎,我以同样的小心保存下来,作同样的用途,或说为同一个目的——给我做面包,或者不如说做食物;因为我找到了不经烘烤就能煮它的法子,不过过了一阵我也学会了烘烤。

paragraphs.en: But to return to my Journal.
paragraphs.cn: 但还是回到我的日记吧。

paragraphs.en: I worked excessive hard these three or four months to get my wall done; and the 14th of April I closed it up, contriving to go into it, not by a door but over the wall, by a ladder, that there might be no sign on the outside of my habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 这三四个月里,我拼命地干活好把墙筑完;4月14日,我把它封闭起来,想法子不从门、而是借一架梯子翻墙进去,好让我的住处外面看不出任何痕迹。

paragraphs.en: _April_ 16.
—I finished the ladder; so I went up the ladder to the top, and then pulled it up after me, and let it down in the inside.
paragraphs.cn: ——我做好了梯子;于是我顺着梯子爬到墙顶,再把它拉上来,放到里面去。

paragraphs.en: This was a complete enclosure to me; for within I had room enough, and nothing could come at me from without, unless it could first mount my wall.
paragraphs.cn: 这对我便是一处完备的围栏;因为里面我有足够的地方,外面的东西也别想到得了我跟前,除非它能先翻过我的墙。

paragraphs.en: The very next day after this wall was finished I had almost had all my labour overthrown at once, and myself killed.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这道墙筑好后的第二天,我几乎一下子把全部劳作都毁掉,连自己也险些送了命。

paragraphs.en: The case was thus: As I was busy in the inside, behind my tent, just at the entrance into my cave, I was terribly frighted with a most dreadful, surprising thing indeed; for all on a sudden I found the earth come crumbling down from the roof of my cave, and from the edge of the hill over my head, and two of the posts I had set up in the cave cracked in a frightful manner.
paragraphs.cn: 情形是这样:我正在里面、帐篷后头、洞口那儿忙活,冷不防被一件极其可怕、惊人的事吓得魂飞魄散;因为突然间,我发觉泥土从洞顶、从我头顶那山坡的边缘直往下崩落,我在洞里立起的两根柱子也吓人地咔嚓裂开。

paragraphs.en: I was heartily scared; but thought nothing of what was really the cause, only thinking that the top of my cave was fallen in, as some of it had done before: and for fear I should be buried in it I ran forward to my ladder, and not thinking myself safe there neither, I got over my wall for fear of the pieces of the hill, which I expected might roll down upon me.
paragraphs.cn: 我着实吓坏了;却没往真正的起因上想,只当是洞顶塌了下来,像先前塌过的那样:我生怕被埋在里头,便朝梯子奔去,可觉得在那儿也不安全,又翻过墙去,唯恐山上的碎块会滚下来砸到我。

paragraphs.en: I had no sooner stepped down upon the firm ground, than I plainly saw it was a terrible earthquake, for the ground I stood on shook three times at about eight minutes’ distance, with three such shocks as would have overturned the strongest building that could be supposed to have stood on the earth; and a great piece of the top of a rock which stood about half a mile from me next the sea fell down with such a terrible noise as I never heard in all my life.
paragraphs.cn: 我刚踏上坚实的地面,就分明看出这是一场可怕的地震,因为我脚下的地在约莫八分钟的间隔里晃了三次,那三下震动足以掀翻地上所能设想的最坚固的建筑;离我约半英里、靠海那边一块岩顶的一大块塌落下来,发出的可怕巨响是我这辈子从未听过的。

paragraphs.en: I perceived also the very sea was put into violent motion by it; and I believe the shocks were stronger under the water than on the island.
paragraphs.cn: 我还发觉,连大海也被它搅得剧烈动荡起来;我相信水下的震动比岛上还要猛烈。

paragraphs.en: I was so much amazed with the thing itself, having never felt the like, nor discoursed with any one that had, that I was like one dead or stupefied; and the motion of the earth made my stomach sick, like one that was tossed at sea; but the noise of the falling of the rock awakened me, as it were, and rousing me from the stupefied condition I was in, filled me with horror; and I thought of nothing then but the hill falling upon my tent and all my household goods, and burying all at once; and this sunk my very soul within me a second time.
paragraphs.cn: 这事本身让我惊骇不已,我从没经历过这样的事,也没跟经历过的人谈起过,以致我像个死人或呆子;地面的晃动叫我胃里翻腾,像在海上被颠簸的人一样;可岩石塌落的巨响仿佛把我唤醒,把我从呆滞中激了起来,满心恐惧;那时我别的都不想,只想着那山坡会塌到我帐篷和全部家当上,把一切一下子埋掉;这第二次又叫我的心直往下沉。

paragraphs.en: After the third shock was over, and I felt no more for some time, I began to take courage; and yet I had not heart enough to go over my wall again, for fear of being buried alive, but sat still upon the ground greatly cast down and disconsolate, not knowing what to do.
paragraphs.cn: 第三下震动过去、我有一阵子再没感到什么之后,我开始鼓起勇气;可我仍没胆量再翻过墙去,唯恐被活埋,只是颓丧沮丧地坐在地上,不知如何是好。

paragraphs.en: All this while I had not the least serious religious thought; nothing but the common “Lord have mercy upon me!” and when it was over that went away too.
paragraphs.cn: 这整段时间里,我心里没有半点认真的宗教念头;只有那句寻常的“主啊,可怜可怜我吧！”;等震过去了,连这也抛到脑后了。

paragraphs.en: While I sat thus, I found the air overcast and grow cloudy, as if it would rain.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样坐着时,发觉天色转阴、云层密布,像是要下雨。

paragraphs.en: Soon after that the wind arose by little and little, so that in less than half-an-hour it blew a most dreadful hurricane; the sea was all on a sudden covered over with foam and froth; the shore was covered with the breach of the water, the trees were torn up by the roots, and a terrible storm it was.
paragraphs.cn: 不久风就一点点刮了起来,不到半个钟头竟刮成了一场极其可怕的飓风;海面转眼间盖满了泡沫和浪花;岸上白浪滔天,树木被连根拔起,真是一场骇人的风暴。

paragraphs.en: This held about three hours, and then began to abate; and in two hours more it was quite calm, and began to rain very hard.
paragraphs.cn: 这大约持续了三个钟头,然后开始减弱;又过两个钟头便完全平息,接着下起了大雨。

paragraphs.en: All this while I sat upon the ground very much terrified and dejected; when on a sudden it came into my thoughts, that these winds and rain being the consequences of the earthquake, the earthquake itself was spent and over, and I might venture into my cave again.
paragraphs.cn: 这整段时间里,我都坐在地上,惊恐而沮丧;忽然我心里想到,这些风雨既是地震的后果,那地震本身想必已经消停过去,我或许可以冒险再进我的洞里去。

paragraphs.en: With this thought my spirits began to revive; and the rain also helping to persuade me, I went in and sat down in my tent.
paragraphs.cn: 这么一想,我的精神开始振作起来;雨也帮着劝我,我便走进去、在帐篷里坐下。

paragraphs.en: But the rain was so violent that my tent was ready to be beaten down with it; and I was forced to go into my cave, though very much afraid and uneasy, for fear it should fall on my head.
paragraphs.cn: 可雨太猛了,我的帐篷眼看要被打塌;我只得进到洞里去,虽然十分害怕不安,生怕它会塌到我头上。

paragraphs.en: This violent rain forced me to a new work—viz. to cut a hole through my new fortification, like a sink, to let the water go out, which would else have flooded my cave.
paragraphs.cn: 这场猛雨逼得我又添了一桩新活——就是在我新筑的工事上凿一个孔,像个排水口,好让水流出去,否则它会淹了我的洞。

paragraphs.en: After I had been in my cave for some time, and found still no more shocks of the earthquake follow, I began to be more composed.
paragraphs.cn: 我在洞里待了一阵,发现地震再没有余震跟来,便渐渐镇定下来。

paragraphs.en: And now, to support my spirits, which indeed wanted it very much, I went to my little store, and took a small sup of rum; which, however, I did then and always very sparingly, knowing I could have no more when that was gone.
paragraphs.cn: 这会儿,为了给自己确实很需要振作的精神打气,我走到我那小小的贮藏处,喝了一小口朗姆酒;不过那时和往后我都喝得很省,因为我知道这酒喝完就再没有了。

paragraphs.en: It continued raining all that night and great part of the next day, so that I could not stir abroad; but my mind being more composed, I began to think of what I had best do; concluding that if the island was subject to these earthquakes, there would be no living for me in a cave, but I must consider of building a little hut in an open place which I might surround with a wall, as I had done here, and so make myself secure from wild beasts or men; for I concluded, if I stayed where I was, I should certainly one time or other be buried alive.
paragraphs.cn: 那一整夜和第二天大半天都下着雨,弄得我没法出门;可我心境较为平静了,便开始盘算最好该怎么办;我断定,若这岛常闹这种地震,住在洞里就没法活命了,我得考虑在一处开阔地方盖间小屋,像我这里一样用墙把它围起来,好防备野兽或人;因为我料定,若一直待在原处,我迟早总有一天会被活埋。

paragraphs.en: With these thoughts, I resolved to remove my tent from the place where it stood, which was just under the hanging precipice of the hill; and which, if it should be shaken again, would certainly fall upon my tent; and I spent the two next days, being the 19th and 20th of April, in contriving where and how to remove my habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 抱着这些念头,我决意把帐篷从原地挪走,那地方正好在山坡那悬空的绝壁底下;万一它再被震动,准会塌到我帐篷上;接下来的两天,也就是4月19日和20日,我都用来筹划把住处挪到何处、怎样挪。

paragraphs.en: The fear of being swallowed up alive made me that I never slept in quiet; and yet the apprehension of lying abroad without any fence was almost equal to it; but still, when I looked about, and saw how everything was put in order, how pleasantly concealed I was, and how safe from danger, it made me very loath to remove.
paragraphs.cn: 生怕被活活吞掉的恐惧,使我从没睡过一个安稳觉;可露天躺着、毫无围栏的担忧,又几乎与之不相上下;然而每当我环顾四周,看到一切都收拾得井井有条、我藏得多么惬意、离危险多么安全,便叫我很不情愿搬走。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, it occurred to me that it would require a vast deal of time for me to do this, and that I must be contented to venture where I was, till I had formed a camp for myself, and had secured it so as to remove to it.
paragraphs.cn: 与此同时,我想到,做这事要花去我极多的时间,我只得甘心在原处冒险待着,直到给自己搭起一处营地、并把它弄得足够牢靠、可以搬过去为止。

paragraphs.en: So with this resolution I composed myself for a time, and resolved that I would go to work with all speed to build me a wall with piles and cables, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 于是抱着这个决心,我暂且让自己安下心来,决意要全力以赴,给自己筑一道用木桩、缆索等等围成的墙,

paragraphs.en: , in a circle, as before, and set my tent up in it when it was finished; but that I would venture to stay where I was till it was finished, and fit to remove.
paragraphs.cn: 就像先前那样,围成一圈,等它建成后再把帐篷支到里面;不过在它建成、可以搬入之前,我甘愿冒险留在原地。

paragraphs.en: This was the 21st.
paragraphs.cn: 这是21日。

paragraphs.en: _April_ 22.
—The next morning I begin to consider of means to put this resolve into execution; but I was at a great loss about my tools.
paragraphs.cn: ——第二天早晨,我开始琢磨把这决心付诸实行的办法;可我为工具犯了大难。

paragraphs.en: I had three large axes, and abundance of hatchets (for we carried the hatchets for traffic with the Indians); but with much chopping and cutting knotty hard wood, they were all full of notches, and dull; and though I had a grindstone, I could not turn it and grind my tools too.
paragraphs.cn: 我有三把大斧,还有许多小斧（那些小斧是我们带来跟印第安人交易用的）;可砍削多节的硬木砍多了,它们全都缺了口、钝了;虽然我有一块磨石,却没法一边转它、一边磨我的工具。

paragraphs.en: This cost me as much thought as a statesman would have bestowed upon a grand point of politics, or a judge upon the life and death of a man.
paragraphs.cn: 这事花去我的心思,不亚于一个政治家用在一件国家大事上,或一个法官用在一个人的生死上。

paragraphs.en: At length I contrived a wheel with a string, to turn it with my foot, that I might have both my hands at liberty.
paragraphs.cn: 最后我设计出一个带绳子的轮子,用脚来转它,好让我腾出两只手来。

paragraphs.en: _Note_.
paragraphs.cn: 附注。

paragraphs.en: —I had never seen any such thing in England, or at least, not to take notice how it was done, though since I have observed, it is very common there; besides that, my grindstone was very large and heavy.
paragraphs.cn: ——这样的东西我在英格兰从没见过,至少没留意过它是怎么弄的,不过后来我倒注意到,那玩意儿在那儿很常见;再说,我这块磨石又大又重。

paragraphs.en: This machine cost me a full week’s work to bring it to perfection.
paragraphs.cn: 这机械花了我整整一星期的工夫才做到完善。

paragraphs.en: —These two whole days I took up in grinding my tools, my machine for turning my grindstone performing very well.
paragraphs.cn: ——这整整两天我都用来磨我的工具,我那转磨石的机械运转得很好。

paragraphs.en: _April_ 30.
—Having perceived my bread had been low a great while, now I took a survey of it, and reduced myself to one biscuit cake a day, which made my heart very heavy.
paragraphs.cn: ——发觉我的面包早已所剩无几,如今我清点了一下,把自己限定为每天一块饼干,这叫我心里很是沉重。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 1.
paragraphs.cn: 5月1日。

paragraphs.en: —In the morning, looking towards the sea side, the tide being low, I saw something lie on the shore bigger than ordinary, and it looked like a cask; when I came to it, I found a small barrel, and two or three pieces of the wreck of the ship, which were driven on shore by the late hurricane; and looking towards the wreck itself, I thought it seemed to lie higher out of the water than it used to do.
paragraphs.cn: ——早晨,朝海边望去,正值落潮,我看见岸上躺着个比寻常大些的东西,看着像只桶;走近一看,原来是个小木桶,还有两三块船的残骸,是被前些天那场飓风冲上岸的;再朝那残骸本身望去,我觉得它似乎比往常露出水面更高了。

paragraphs.en: I examined the barrel which was driven on shore, and soon found it was a barrel of gunpowder; but it had taken water, and the powder was caked as hard as a stone; however, I rolled it farther on shore for the present, and went on upon the sands, as near as I could to the wreck of the ship, to look for more.
paragraphs.cn: 我查看那只被冲上岸的桶,很快发现它是一桶火药;不过它已经进了水,火药结成了石头一样硬的块;然而我暂且把它往岸上再滚远些,又走到沙滩上,尽量靠近那船的残骸,去寻找更多东西。

paragraphs.en: When I came down to the ship I found it strangely removed.
paragraphs.cn: 我下到船那里时,发现它离奇地移了位。

paragraphs.en: The forecastle, which lay before buried in sand, was heaved up at least six feet, and the stern, which was broke in pieces and parted from the rest by the force of the sea, soon after I had left rummaging her, was tossed as it were up, and cast on one side; and the sand was thrown so high on that side next her stern, that whereas there was a great place of water before, so that I could not come within a quarter of a mile of the wreck without swimming I could now walk quite up to her when the tide was out.
paragraphs.cn: 从前埋在沙里的船头楼,如今至少被顶高了六英尺;而船尾在我离开搜查它之后不久,已被海浪的力量撞得粉碎、脱离了船身,像被抛起来一样甩到了一边;靠近船尾那一侧的沙堆得极高,原先那儿本是一大片水,我不游泳就到不了离残骸四分之一英里以内,如今退潮时我竟能一直走到船跟前。

paragraphs.en: I was surprised with this at first, but soon concluded it must be done by the earthquake; and as by this violence the ship was more broke open than formerly, so many things came daily on shore, which the sea had loosened, and which the winds and water rolled by degrees to the land.
paragraphs.cn: 起初我很惊讶,但很快断定这必是地震所致;由于这场剧烈的震动,船比先前裂得更开,于是每天都有许多东西冲上岸来,都是海水松动了的,又被风和水一点点卷到陆地上来。

paragraphs.en: This wholly diverted my thoughts from the design of removing my habitation, and I busied myself mightily, that day especially, in searching whether I could make any way into the ship; but I found nothing was to be expected of that kind, for all the inside of the ship was choked up with sand.
paragraphs.cn: 这件事把我的心思完全从搬家的打算上引开了,那天我尤其卖力地忙着,想看看能不能设法钻进船里去;可我发现这方面没什么指望,因为船的内部全被沙塞满了。

paragraphs.en: However, as I had learned not to despair of anything, I resolved to pull everything to pieces that I could of the ship, concluding that everything I could get from her would be of some use or other to me.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我既已学会对任何事都不绝望,便决意把船上凡是能拆的都拆下来,心想从船上弄到的每样东西,对我总会有这样那样的用处。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 3.
paragraphs.cn: 5月3日。

paragraphs.en: —I began with my saw, and cut a piece of a beam through, which I thought held some of the upper part or quarter-deck together, and when I had cut it through, I cleared away the sand as well as I could from the side which lay highest; but the tide coming in, I was obliged to give over for that time.
paragraphs.cn: 我先动用锯子,锯断了一根横梁,我想它撑着上层甲板或后甲板的一部分;锯断以后,我尽量把那高出来的一侧的沙清掉;可潮水涨了上来,我只得暂且作罢。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 4.
paragraphs.cn: 5月4日。

paragraphs.en: —I went a-fishing, but caught not one fish that I durst eat of, till I was weary of my sport; when, just going to leave off, I caught a young dolphin.
paragraphs.cn: 我去钓鱼,却没钓到一条敢吃的,直钓得我厌倦了这消遣;正要收手时,钓到一条小海豚。

paragraphs.en: I had made me a long line of some rope-yarn, but I had no hooks; yet I frequently caught fish enough, as much as I cared to eat; all which I dried in the sun, and ate them dry.
paragraphs.cn: 我用些绳纱给自己做了一根长钓线,却没有鱼钩;可我还是常能钓到足够多的鱼,想吃多少有多少;这些鱼我都放在太阳下晒干,晒干了吃。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 5.
paragraphs.cn: 5月5日。

paragraphs.en: —Worked on the wreck; cut another beam asunder, and brought three great fir planks off from the decks, which I tied together, and made to float on shore when the tide of flood came on.
paragraphs.cn: 在残骸上干活;又锯断一根横梁,从甲板上弄下三块大冷杉木板,把它们捆在一起,趁涨潮时让它们漂上岸来。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 6.
paragraphs.cn: 5月6日。

paragraphs.en: —Worked on the wreck; got several iron bolts out of her and other pieces of ironwork.
paragraphs.cn: 在残骸上干活;从船上取下几根铁螺栓和别的铁件。

paragraphs.en: Worked very hard, and came home very much tired, and had thoughts of giving it over.
paragraphs.cn: 干得很辛苦,回到家累得够呛,一度想撂开手不干了。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 7.
paragraphs.cn: 5月7日。

paragraphs.en: —Went to the wreck again, not with an intent to work, but found the weight of the wreck had broke itself down, the beams being cut; that several pieces of the ship seemed to lie loose, and the inside of the hold lay so open that I could see into it; but it was almost full of water and sand.
paragraphs.cn: 又去了残骸那里,本没打算干活,却发现由于横梁被锯断,残骸靠自身的重量塌了下去;船的好几块部件像是松动了,舱内也敞开得能让我看进去;可里面几乎全是水和沙。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 8.
paragraphs.cn: 5月8日。

paragraphs.en: —Went to the wreck, and carried an iron crow to wrench up the deck, which lay now quite clear of the water or sand.
paragraphs.cn: 去了残骸,带上一根铁撬棍,好撬起如今已完全露出水和沙的甲板。

paragraphs.en: I wrenched open two planks, and brought them on shore also with the tide.
paragraphs.cn: 我撬开两块木板,也趁潮水把它们带上了岸。

paragraphs.en: I left the iron crow in the wreck for next day.
paragraphs.cn: 我把铁撬棍留在残骸里,留着第二天用。

paragraphs.en: _May_ 9.
paragraphs.cn: 5月9日。

paragraphs.en: —Went to the wreck, and with the crow made way into the body of the wreck, and felt several casks, and loosened them with the crow, but could not break them up.
paragraphs.cn: 去了残骸,用撬棍钻进了残骸的舱身,摸到几只大桶,用撬棍把它们撬松了,却撬不开。

paragraphs.en: I felt also a roll of English lead, and could stir it, but it was too heavy to remove.
paragraphs.cn: 我还摸到一卷英国铅,推得动它,可它太重,搬不走。
5月10日至14日。
