paragraphs.en: —Went every day to the wreck; and got a great many pieces of timber, and boards, or plank, and two or three hundredweight of iron.
paragraphs.cn: 每天都去残骸;弄到许多木料、木板或板材,还有两三百磅重的铁。

paragraphs.en: —I carried two hatchets, to try if I could not cut a piece off the roll of lead by placing the edge of one hatchet and driving it with the other; but as it lay about a foot and a half in the water, I could not make any blow to drive the hatchet.
paragraphs.cn: 我带了两把短斧,想试试能不能从那卷铅上砍下一块来:把一把斧刃搁上去,用另一把去砸;可那卷铅躺在约一英尺半深的水里,我使不上劲把斧头砸下去。

paragraphs.en: —It had blown hard in the night, and the wreck appeared more broken by the force of the water; but I stayed so long in the woods, to get pigeons for food, that the tide prevented my going to the wreck that day.
paragraphs.cn: 夜里刮了大风,残骸被水的力量冲得更破了;可我在林子里待得太久,忙着打鸽子当食物,潮水一涨,那天就没能去成残骸。

paragraphs.en: —I saw some pieces of the wreck blown on shore, at a great distance, near two miles off me, but resolved to see what they were, and found it was a piece of the head, but too heavy for me to bring away.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见残骸的几块碎片被吹到很远的岸上,离我近两英里,可我决意去看看那是什么,发现是船头的一块,只是太重,我搬不走。

paragraphs.en: —Every day, to this day, I worked on the wreck; and with hard labour I loosened some things so much with the crow, that the first flowing tide several casks floated out, and two of the seamen’s chests; but the wind blowing from the shore, nothing came to land that day but pieces of timber, and a hogshead, which had some Brazil pork in it; but the salt water and the sand had spoiled it.
paragraphs.cn: 直到这一天,我每天都在残骸上干活;凭着苦力,我用撬棍把一些东西撬得松动了,头一次涨潮时便有几只桶漂了出来,还有两只水手的箱子;可风从岸上吹来,那天什么也没漂到陆地,只有些木料,和一只装着巴西猪肉的大桶,不过咸水和沙把肉糟蹋了。

paragraphs.en: I continued this work every day to the 15th of June, except the time necessary to get food, which I always appointed, during this part of my employment, to be when the tide was up, that I might be ready when it was ebbed out; and by this time I had got timber and plank and ironwork enough to have built a good boat, if I had known how; and also I got, at several times and in several pieces, near one hundredweight of the sheet lead.
paragraphs.cn: 我天天干这活,一直干到6月15日,只留出弄食物必需的时间;干这段活期间,我总把弄食物的时间定在涨潮时,好在退潮时能腾出手来;到这时,我弄到的木料、木板和铁件已足够造一条好船——只要我懂得怎么造;我还分几次、一块块地弄到近一百磅重的铅皮。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 16.
—Going down to the seaside, I found a large tortoise or turtle.
paragraphs.cn: 走到海边时,我发现一只大陆龟或海龟。

paragraphs.en: This was the first I had seen, which, it seems, was only my misfortune, not any defect of the place, or scarcity; for had I happened to be on the other side of the island, I might have had hundreds of them every day, as I found afterwards; but perhaps had paid dear enough for them.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我见到的头一只,看来这只是我运气不好,并非这地方有什么缺陷或稀罕;因为若我碰巧在岛的另一边,每天本可弄到成百只,这是我后来才知道的;不过也许我为它们付的代价够大了。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 17.
—I spent in cooking the turtle.
paragraphs.cn: 这一天我花在煮那只海龟上。

paragraphs.en: I found in her three-score eggs; and her flesh was to me, at that time, the most savoury and pleasant that ever I tasted in my life, having had no flesh, but of goats and fowls, since I landed in this horrid place.
paragraphs.cn: 我在它体内发现六十只蛋;它的肉在那时于我是这辈子尝过的最鲜美可口的,因为自从我落到这可怕的地方,除了山羊和禽类的肉,就没吃过别的肉。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 18.
—Rained all day, and I stayed within.
paragraphs.cn: 下了一整天雨,我待在屋里。

paragraphs.en: I thought at this time the rain felt cold, and I was something chilly; which I knew was not usual in that latitude.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我觉得雨是凉的,身上有点发冷;我知道这在那个纬度是不寻常的。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 19.
—Very ill, and shivering, as if the weather had been cold.
paragraphs.cn: 病得很重,浑身打颤,仿佛天气很冷似的。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 20.
—No rest all night; violent pains in my head, and feverish.
paragraphs.cn: 整夜不得安宁;头痛剧烈,还发着烧。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 21.
—Very ill; frighted almost to death with the apprehensions of my sad condition—to be sick, and no help.
paragraphs.cn: 病得很重;一想到自己处境凄凉——病倒了又无人相助——几乎吓得要死。

paragraphs.en: Prayed to God, for the first time since the storm off Hull, but scarce knew what I said, or why, my thoughts being all confused.
paragraphs.cn: 自赫尔外海那场风暴以来,我头一次向上帝祷告,却几乎不知自己在说什么、为何而说,思绪一片混乱。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 22.
—A little better; but under dreadful apprehensions of sickness.
paragraphs.cn: 好了一点;却仍对生病怀着可怕的忧惧。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 23.
—Very bad again; cold and shivering, and then a violent headache.
paragraphs.cn: 又很糟;发冷打颤,接着是剧烈的头痛。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 24.
—Much better.
paragraphs.cn: 好多了。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 25.
—An ague very violent; the fit held me seven hours; cold fit and hot, with faint sweats after it.
paragraphs.cn: 疟疾发得很凶;这一阵折磨了我七个钟头;先是发冷,接着发热,过后又出了些虚汗。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 26.
—Better; and having no victuals to eat, took my gun, but found myself very weak.
paragraphs.cn: 好些了;因为没有吃的,便拿起枪,却觉得自己十分虚弱。

paragraphs.en: However, I killed a she-goat, and with much difficulty got it home, and broiled some of it, and ate, I would fain have stewed it, and made some broth, but had no pot.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我打死了一只母山羊,费了好大劲才把它弄回家,烤了一些吃了;我本想把它炖了,熬点肉汤,可没有锅。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 27.
—The ague again so violent that I lay a-bed all day, and neither ate nor drank.
paragraphs.cn: 疟疾又发得那么凶,我整天躺在床上,不吃也不喝。

paragraphs.en: I was ready to perish for thirst; but so weak, I had not strength to stand up, or to get myself any water to drink.
paragraphs.cn: 我渴得快要死了;可身子太弱,连站起来、给自己弄点水喝的力气都没有。

paragraphs.en: Prayed to God again, but was light-headed; and when I was not, I was so ignorant that I knew not what to say; only I lay and cried, “Lord, look upon me!
paragraphs.cn: 我又向上帝祷告,却头晕脑胀;等不晕的时候,我又愚昧得不知该说什么;只是躺着哭喊:“主啊,看顾我吧！

paragraphs.en: Lord, pity me!
paragraphs.cn: 主啊,可怜我吧！

paragraphs.en: Lord, have mercy upon me!”
paragraphs.cn: 主啊,怜悯我吧！”

paragraphs.en: I suppose I did nothing else for two or three hours; till, the fit wearing off, I fell asleep, and did not wake till far in the night.
paragraphs.cn: 我想我这样喊了两三个钟头,别的什么也没做;后来那阵子渐渐过去,我睡着了,直到深夜才醒。

paragraphs.en: When I awoke, I found myself much refreshed, but weak, and exceeding thirsty.
paragraphs.cn: 醒来时,我觉得精神好了许多,只是虚弱,而且渴得厉害。

paragraphs.en: However, as I had no water in my habitation, I was forced to lie till morning, and went to sleep again.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我屋里没有水,只得躺着等到天亮,又睡了过去。

paragraphs.en: In this second sleep I had this terrible dream: I thought that I was sitting on the ground, on the outside of my wall, where I sat when the storm blew after the earthquake, and that I saw a man descend from a great black cloud, in a bright flame of fire, and light upon the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 在这第二觉里,我做了这样一个可怕的梦:我梦见自己坐在地上,坐在我墙外——就是地震后刮风暴时我坐的地方——看见一个人从一大团乌黑的云里、在一片明亮的火焰中降下来,落到地上。

paragraphs.en: He was all over as bright as a flame, so that I could but just bear to look towards him; his countenance was most inexpressibly dreadful, impossible for words to describe.
paragraphs.cn: 他浑身像火焰一样明亮,我几乎不敢正眼看他;他的面容可怕得无以言表,言语根本无法形容。

paragraphs.en: When he stepped upon the ground with his feet, I thought the earth trembled, just as it had done before in the earthquake, and all the air looked, to my apprehension, as if it had been filled with flashes of fire.
paragraphs.cn: 当他双脚踏上地面时,我觉得大地在颤抖,正如先前地震时一样;在我看来,四周的空气仿佛都充满了火光的闪动。

paragraphs.en: He was no sooner landed upon the earth, but he moved forward towards me, with a long spear or weapon in his hand, to kill me; and when he came to a rising ground, at some distance, he spoke to me—or I heard a voice so terrible that it is impossible to express the terror of it.
paragraphs.cn: 他一落到地上,就手持一支长矛似的武器,朝我走来,要杀我;当他走到不远处一块高地上时,便对我说话——或者说,我听见一个声音,可怕得无法形容那种恐怖。

paragraphs.en: All that I can say I understood was this: “Seeing all these things have not brought thee to repentance, now thou shalt die;” at which words, I thought he lifted up the spear that was in his hand to kill me.
paragraphs.cn: 我所能听懂的只有这句话:“既然这一切都没能使你悔改,如今你就得死。”说这话时,我觉得他举起手中的长矛要杀我。

paragraphs.en: No one that shall ever read this account will expect that I should be able to describe the horrors of my soul at this terrible vision.
paragraphs.cn: 凡是读到这段记述的人,都别指望我能描述出这可怕幻象在我灵魂里激起的恐怖。

paragraphs.en: I mean, that even while it was a dream, I even dreamed of those horrors.
paragraphs.cn: 我是说,即便在梦中,我也梦见了那些恐怖。

paragraphs.en: Nor is it any more possible to describe the impression that remained upon my mind when I awaked, and found it was but a dream.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我醒来、发现这不过是一场梦时留在心头的那种印象,同样无法描述。

paragraphs.en: I had, alas! no divine knowledge.
paragraphs.cn: 唉,我那时没有半点关于神的知识。

paragraphs.en: What I had received by the good instruction of my father was then worn out by an uninterrupted series, for eight years, of seafaring wickedness, and a constant conversation with none but such as were, like myself, wicked and profane to the last degree.
paragraphs.cn: 我从父亲的谆谆教诲中所领受的,那时已被八年间接连不断的航海恶行磨得一干二净,朝夕相处的又无一不是像我一样恶劣、亵渎到极点的人。

paragraphs.en: I do not remember that I had, in all that time, one thought that so much as tended either to looking upwards towards God, or inwards towards a reflection upon my own ways; but a certain stupidity of soul, without desire of good, or conscience of evil, had entirely overwhelmed me; and I was all that the most hardened, unthinking, wicked creature among our common sailors can be supposed to be; not having the least sense, either of the fear of God in danger, or of thankfulness to God in deliverance.
paragraphs.cn: 我不记得在那整段时间里,我曾有过哪怕一个念头,是稍稍向上仰望上帝、或向内反省自己行径的;有的只是一种灵魂的麻木,既无向善之心,也无为恶之愧,把我整个吞没了;我们普通水手中最冥顽不化、浑噩不思、恶劣透顶的人是什么样,我便是什么样;无论身处危难时对上帝的敬畏,还是获救时对上帝的感恩,我丝毫没有。

paragraphs.en: In the relating what is already past of my story, this will be the more easily believed when I shall add, that through all the variety of miseries that had to this day befallen me, I never had so much as one thought of it being the hand of God, or that it was a just punishment for my sin—my rebellious behaviour against my father—or my present sins, which were great—or so much as a punishment for the general course of my wicked life.
paragraphs.cn: 在讲述我这已经过去的故事时,若我再补上一句,这话就更容易叫人相信了:纵使直到这一天种种苦难都已降临我身,我却从未有过哪怕一个念头,想到这是上帝之手,或是对我罪孽的公正惩罚——不论是我悖逆父亲的行为,还是我眼下那些不小的罪,乃至对我整个恶劣生涯的惩罚。

paragraphs.en: When I was on the desperate expedition on the desert shores of Africa, I never had so much as one thought of what would become of me, or one wish to God to direct me whither I should go, or to keep me from the danger which apparently surrounded me, as well from voracious creatures as cruel savages.
paragraphs.cn: 当我在非洲那荒凉海岸上亡命奔波时,我从未有过哪怕一个念头去想自己会有什么下场,也从未有过一个祈望,求上帝指引我该往哪里去、或护我脱离那分明四面环伺的凶险——无论是贪婪的野兽还是残忍的野人。

paragraphs.en: But I was merely thoughtless of a God or a Providence, acted like a mere brute, from the principles of nature, and by the dictates of common sense only, and, indeed, hardly that.
paragraphs.cn: 我压根就没想到有上帝或天意,活像一头畜生,只凭天性行事,只听凭常识的指使——其实连常识也谈不上。

paragraphs.en: When I was delivered and taken up at sea by the Portugal captain, well used, and dealt justly and honourably with, as well as charitably, I had not the least thankfulness in my thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 当我在海上获救、被那位葡萄牙船长搭救,受到善待,得到公正、体面又仁慈的对待时,我心里连一丝感恩都没有。

paragraphs.en: When, again, I was shipwrecked, ruined, and in danger of drowning on this island, I was as far from remorse, or looking on it as a judgment.
paragraphs.cn: 后来我再度遭遇船难、倾家荡产、险些淹死在这岛上时,我离悔恨、离把它看作一种惩罚,依旧那么远。

paragraphs.en: I only said to myself often, that I was an unfortunate dog, and born to be always miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 我只是常对自己说,我是条倒霉的狗,生来就注定要永远受苦。

paragraphs.en: It is true, when I got on shore first here, and found all my ship’s crew drowned and myself spared, I was surprised with a kind of ecstasy, and some transports of soul, which, had the grace of God assisted, might have come up to true thankfulness; but it ended where it began, in a mere common flight of joy, or, as I may say, being glad I was alive, without the least reflection upon the distinguished goodness of the hand which had preserved me, and had singled me out to be preserved when all the rest were destroyed, or an inquiry why Providence had been thus merciful unto me.
paragraphs.cn: 诚然,我头一回上到这岸上、发现全船水手都淹死了唯独我幸免时,曾涌起一阵狂喜,灵魂里有过几分激荡,若有上帝的恩典相助,本可升华为真正的感恩;可它从哪儿起就在哪儿止,不过是一阵寻常的欢喜勃发,或者说,只是庆幸自己还活着,丝毫没有反思那只保全了我、在众人尽毁时独独拣选我存活的手是何等奇异的恩慈,也不曾追问天意为何这般怜悯我。

paragraphs.en: Even just the same common sort of joy which seamen generally have, after they are got safe ashore from a shipwreck, which they drown all in the next bowl of punch, and forget almost as soon as it is over; and all the rest of my life was like it.
paragraphs.cn: 那不过是水手们从船难中平安上岸后通常有的那种寻常欢喜,他们把它全泡在下一碗潘趣酒里,几乎一过就忘;我此后的一生也都是如此。

paragraphs.en: Even when I was afterwards, on due consideration, made sensible of my condition, how I was cast on this dreadful place, out of the reach of human kind, out of all hope of relief, or prospect of redemption, as soon as I saw but a prospect of living and that I should not starve and perish for hunger, all the sense of my affliction wore off; and I began to be very easy, applied myself to the works proper for my preservation and supply, and was far enough from being afflicted at my condition, as a judgment from heaven, or as the hand of God against me: these were thoughts which very seldom entered my head.
paragraphs.cn: 即便后来我经过一番思量,明白了自己的处境——如何被抛到这可怕的地方,远离人烟,断了一切获救的指望、赎脱的前景——可我一看到有活下去的指望、不至于挨饿丧命,对苦难的全部感受便消散了;我开始过得十分安逸,一心扑在维持生计的活计上,压根谈不上因自己的处境而痛苦,更没把它当成上天的惩罚或与我作对的上帝之手:这些念头极少钻进我脑子里。

paragraphs.en: The growing up of the corn, as is hinted in my Journal, had at first some little influence upon me, and began to affect me with seriousness, as long as I thought it had something miraculous in it; but as soon as ever that part of the thought was removed, all the impression that was raised from it wore off also, as I have noted already.
paragraphs.cn: 那庄稼的长起——正如我日记里提过的——起初对我略有些影响,只要我还以为其中有几分神迹,便开始叫我心生郑重;可一旦这份想头里那部分被打消,由它激起的一切印象也随之消散,这我先前已经说过了。

paragraphs.en: Even the earthquake, though nothing could be more terrible in its nature, or more immediately directing to the invisible Power which alone directs such things, yet no sooner was the first fright over, but the impression it had made went off also.
paragraphs.cn: 就连那场地震——其本身再没有比它更可怕的了,也再没有什么比它更直接地指向那唯一主宰万事的无形力量——可头一阵惊恐一过,它留下的印象也就消退了。

paragraphs.en: I had no more sense of God or His judgments—much less of the present affliction of my circumstances being from His hand—than if I had been in the most prosperous condition of life.
paragraphs.cn: 我对上帝或他的审判——更别说眼下的苦境是出自他手——毫无感受,仿佛我正处在一生最顺遂的境地一般。

paragraphs.en: But now, when I began to be sick, and a leisurely view of the miseries of death came to place itself before me; when my spirits began to sink under the burden of a strong distemper, and nature was exhausted with the violence of the fever; conscience, that had slept so long, began to awake, and I began to reproach myself with my past life, in which I had so evidently, by uncommon wickedness, provoked the justice of God to lay me under uncommon strokes, and to deal with me in so vindictive a manner.
paragraphs.cn: 可如今,我开始病倒,死亡的种种凄惨从容地展现在我眼前;我的精神在重病的压迫下开始下沉,体力也被高烧的猛烈耗尽;那沉睡已久的良心开始苏醒,我开始责备自己过往的一生——我分明以罕见的恶行,惹得上帝的公义降下罕见的重击,如此报复般地对待我。

paragraphs.en: These reflections oppressed me for the second or third day of my distemper; and in the violence, as well of the fever as of the dreadful reproaches of my conscience, extorted some words from me like praying to God, though I cannot say they were either a prayer attended with desires or with hopes: it was rather the voice of mere fright and distress.
paragraphs.cn: 这些反省在我发病的第二三天里压得我喘不过气;在高烧和良心可怕责备的双重猛烈之下,逼出我几句像是向上帝祷告的话,虽说我不敢讲那算得上带着渴望或指望的祷告:那更像是纯粹出于惊惧和困苦的呼喊。

paragraphs.en: My thoughts were confused, the convictions great upon my mind, and the horror of dying in such a miserable condition raised vapours into my head with the mere apprehensions; and in these hurries of my soul I knew not what my tongue might express.
paragraphs.cn: 我思绪混乱,心里的悔悟极深,一想到要在这般凄惨的境况里死去,那恐怖只凭这份忧惧就在我脑中升起一团昏乱;在这灵魂的慌乱中,我不知自己舌头会吐出什么话来。

paragraphs.en: But it was rather exclamation, such as, “Lord, what a miserable creature am I!
paragraphs.cn: 那更像是惊呼,诸如:“主啊,我是何等凄惨的一个人！

paragraphs.en: If I should be sick, I shall certainly die for want of help; and what will become of me!”
paragraphs.cn: 我若病了,必定因无人相助而死;那我可怎么办！”

paragraphs.en: Then the tears burst out of my eyes, and I could say no more for a good while.
paragraphs.cn: 于是眼泪从我眼里夺眶而出,好一阵子我再说不出话来。

paragraphs.en: In this interval the good advice of my father came to my mind, and presently his prediction, which I mentioned at the beginning of this story—viz. that if I did take this foolish step, God would not bless me, and I would have leisure hereafter to reflect upon having neglected his counsel when there might be none to assist in my recovery.
paragraphs.cn: 在这当口,父亲的良言浮上我心头,紧接着是他的预言——我在这故事开头提过的——就是说,我若真走这愚蠢的一步,上帝不会赐福于我,日后我便有的是闲工夫去反省自己怎样忽视了他的忠告,而那时或许无人能助我康复。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” said I, aloud, “my dear father’s words are come to pass; God’s justice has overtaken me, and I have none to help or hear me.
paragraphs.cn: “如今,”我高声说道,“我亲爱的父亲的话应验了;上帝的公义追上了我,却没有人来帮我或听我诉说。

paragraphs.en: I rejected the voice of Providence, which had mercifully put me in a posture or station of life wherein I might have been happy and easy; but I would neither see it myself nor learn to know the blessing of it from my parents.
paragraphs.cn: 我拒绝了天意的呼声,它本仁慈地把我安置在一种境地或身份里,我原可在那里过得幸福安逸;可我既不肯自己去看清,也不肯从父母那里学着认识这份福气。

paragraphs.en: I left them to mourn over my folly, and now I am left to mourn under the consequences of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我撇下他们为我的愚行伤悲,如今轮到我独自为这愚行的后果伤悲了。

paragraphs.en: I abused their help and assistance, who would have lifted me in the world, and would have made everything easy to me; and now I have difficulties to struggle with, too great for even nature itself to support, and no assistance, no help, no comfort, no advice.”
paragraphs.cn: 我辜负了他们的帮助和扶持,他们本想把我扶上社会、让我事事顺遂;如今我却有种种难关要苦苦挣扎,大到连天性本身都撑不住,而且没有援手,没有帮助,没有安慰,没有指点。”

paragraphs.en: Then I cried out, “Lord, be my help, for I am in great distress.”
paragraphs.cn: 于是我喊道:“主啊,求你帮助我,因为我陷在极大的苦难里。”

paragraphs.en: This was the first prayer, if I may call it so, that I had made for many years.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我许多年来所做的头一个祷告,如果这也算得上祷告的话。

paragraphs.en: But to return to my Journal.
paragraphs.cn: 不过还是回到我的日记吧。

paragraphs.en: _June_ 28.

—Having been somewhat refreshed with the sleep I had had, and the fit being entirely off, I got up; and though the fright and terror of my dream was very great, yet I considered that the fit of the ague would return again the next day, and now was my time to get something to refresh and support myself when I should be ill; and the first thing I did, I filled a large square case-bottle with water, and set it upon my table, in reach of my bed; and to take off the chill or aguish disposition of the water, I put about a quarter of a pint of rum into it, and mixed them together.
paragraphs.cn: 睡了那一觉,精神稍稍恢复,那阵病也完全过去了,我便起了身;虽说梦里的惊恐还很厉害,可我想到疟疾第二天还会再发,眼下正是趁机弄点东西、好在犯病时提神支撑身子的时候;我做的头一件事,就是把一只大方形箱瓶灌满水,放在桌上、伸手就够得着床边的地方;为了去掉水里那股冰凉、发疟似的性子,我往里倒了约四分之一品脱朗姆酒,把它们兑到一起。

paragraphs.en: Then I got me a piece of the goat’s flesh and broiled it on the coals, but could eat very little.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我取了一块山羊肉,搁在炭火上烤,却只吃得下一点点。

paragraphs.en: I walked about, but was very weak, and withal very sad and heavy-hearted under a sense of my miserable condition, dreading, the return of my distemper the next day.
paragraphs.cn: 我走动了一阵,却十分虚弱,加上一想到自己凄惨的处境便忧愁沉重,满心恐惧第二天病又会发。

paragraphs.en: At night I made my supper of three of the turtle’s eggs, which I roasted in the ashes, and ate, as we call it, in the shell, and this was the first bit of meat I had ever asked God’s blessing to, that I could remember, in my whole life.
paragraphs.cn: 夜里我拿三只海龟蛋当晚饭,埋在灰里烤了,照我们的说法,连壳一起吃;这是我这辈子记忆所及、头一回为一口肉食求过上帝赐福。

paragraphs.en: After I had eaten I tried to walk, but found myself so weak that I could hardly carry a gun, for I never went out without that; so I went but a little way, and sat down upon the ground, looking out upon the sea, which was just before me, and very calm and smooth.
paragraphs.cn: 吃完后我想走走,却发现自己虚弱得几乎连枪都拿不动——我从不空手出门;于是只走了一小段路,便坐在地上,眺望着眼前那片海,海面平静又光滑。

paragraphs.en: As I sat here some such thoughts as these occurred to me: What is this earth and sea, of which I have seen so much?
paragraphs.cn: 我坐在这里时,脑中生出些这样的念头:这我见了这么多的大地和海洋,究竟是什么？

paragraphs.en: Whence is it produced?
paragraphs.cn: 它是从哪里来的？

paragraphs.en: And what am I, and all the other creatures wild and tame, human and brutal?
paragraphs.cn: 我又是什么,还有其他一切生灵——野的驯的、人的兽的——又都是什么？

paragraphs.en: Whence are we?
paragraphs.cn: 我们又是从哪里来的？

paragraphs.en: Sure we are all made by some secret Power, who formed the earth and sea, the air and sky.
paragraphs.cn: 我们必定都是某种隐秘的力量造的,是它造了大地和海洋、空气和天空。

paragraphs.en: And who is that?
paragraphs.cn: 那又是谁呢？

paragraphs.en: Then it followed most naturally, it is God that has made all.
paragraphs.cn: 于是极自然地接下去:是上帝造了这一切。

paragraphs.en: Well, but then it came on strangely, if God has made all these things, He guides and governs them all, and all things that concern them; for the Power that could make all things must certainly have power to guide and direct them.
paragraphs.cn: 好吧,可接着又奇异地想到:上帝若造了这一切,他便掌管统辖着这一切,以及一切与它们相关的事;因为那能造万物的力量,必定也有力量引导指挥它们。

paragraphs.en: If so, nothing can happen in the great circuit of His works, either without His knowledge or appointment.
paragraphs.cn: 若是这样,在他运作的大范围之内,凡事都不会脱离他的知晓或安排而发生。

paragraphs.en: And if nothing happens without His knowledge, He knows that I am here, and am in this dreadful condition; and if nothing happens without His appointment, He has appointed all this to befall me.
paragraphs.cn: 既然万事都不脱离他的知晓而发生,他便知道我在这里,身陷这可怕的境地;既然万事都不脱离他的安排而发生,那这一切降在我身上,便都是他安排的。

paragraphs.en: Nothing occurred to my thought to contradict any of these conclusions, and therefore it rested upon me with the greater force, that it must needs be that God had appointed all this to befall me; that I was brought into this miserable circumstance by His direction, He having the sole power, not of me only, but of everything that happened in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我脑中想不出任何能驳倒这些结论的东西,于是它便更有力地压在我心上:这一切降到我身上,必定是上帝安排的;是他的指引把我带进这凄惨的境况,因为他独掌大权,不单掌管我,也掌管世上发生的每一件事。

paragraphs.en: Immediately it followed: Why has God done this to me?
paragraphs.cn: 紧接着便想到:上帝为什么这样对待我？

paragraphs.en: What have I done to be thus used?
paragraphs.cn: 我做了什么,竟落得这般对待？

paragraphs.en: My conscience presently checked me in that inquiry, as if I had blasphemed, and methought it spoke to me like a voice: “Wretch! dost _thou_ ask what thou hast done?
paragraphs.cn: 我的良心立刻在这一追问上喝止了我,仿佛我亵渎了神明,我觉得它像一个声音似的对我说:“孽障！你也配问自己做了什么？

paragraphs.en: Look back upon a dreadful misspent life, and ask thyself what thou hast _not_ done?
paragraphs.cn: 回头看看你那可怕虚度的一生,问问自己有什么坏事没做过？

paragraphs.en: Ask, why is it that thou wert not long ago destroyed?
paragraphs.cn: 问问,你为什么早没被毁掉？

paragraphs.en: Why wert thou not drowned in Yarmouth Roads; killed in the fight when the ship was taken by the Sallee man-of-war; devoured by the wild beasts on the coast of Africa; or drowned _here_, when all the crew perished but thyself?
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么没淹死在雅茅斯锚地;没在萨累海盗船夺船那一仗里被杀;没在非洲海岸被野兽吞食;或没在这里、在全船除你之外都丧命时淹死？

paragraphs.en: Dost _thou_ ask, what have I done?”
paragraphs.cn: 你也配问,我做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: I was struck dumb with these reflections, as one astonished, and had not a word to say—no, not to answer to myself, but rose up pensive and sad, walked back to my retreat, and went up over my wall, as if I had been going to bed; but my thoughts were sadly disturbed, and I had no inclination to sleep; so I sat down in my chair, and lighted my lamp, for it began to be dark.
paragraphs.cn: 这些反省叫我哑口无言,像人惊呆了一般,一个字也说不出——不,连回答自己也答不上,只是满怀愁思悲哀地站起身,走回我的藏身处,翻过我的墙头,仿佛要去睡觉;可我思绪扰乱得厉害,一点睡意也没有;于是我在椅子上坐下,点起灯,因为天开始黑了。

paragraphs.en: Now, as the apprehension of the return of my distemper terrified me very much, it occurred to my thought that the Brazilians take no physic but their tobacco for almost all distempers, and I had a piece of a roll of tobacco in one of the chests, which was quite cured, and some also that was green, and not quite cured.
paragraphs.cn: 这时,由于害怕病再发作把我吓得不轻,我脑中忽然想起,巴西人几乎治什么病都不吃别的药,只用他们的烟草,而我有一只箱子里就有一卷烟草的残段,已经完全烤制好了,还有些是生的、没完全制好的。

paragraphs.en: I went, directed by Heaven no doubt; for in this chest I found a cure both for soul and body.
paragraphs.cn: 我走过去,无疑是上天指引的;因为在这只箱子里,我找到了医治灵魂与身体的两样良药。

paragraphs.en: I opened the chest, and found what I looked for, the tobacco; and as the few books I had saved lay there too, I took out one of the Bibles which I mentioned before, and which to this time I had not found leisure or inclination to look into.
paragraphs.cn: 我打开箱子,找到了我要找的烟草;因为我救下的那几本书也搁在里头,我便取出先前提过的一本《圣经》——直到这时,我还一直没得空、也没心思去翻它。

paragraphs.en: I say, I took it out, and brought both that and the tobacco with me to the table.
paragraphs.cn: 我是说,我把它取了出来,连同烟草一起带到桌边。

paragraphs.en: What use to make of the tobacco I knew not, in my distemper, or whether it was good for it or no: but I tried several experiments with it, as if I was resolved it should hit one way or other.
paragraphs.cn: 在病中,这烟草该怎么用、对病究竟好不好,我都不知道;可我拿它做了几样试验,像是打定主意,总要让它这样那样地见点效。

paragraphs.en: I first took a piece of leaf, and chewed it in my mouth, which, indeed, at first almost stupefied my brain, the tobacco being green and strong, and that I had not been much used to.
paragraphs.cn: 我先取了一片烟叶,放进嘴里嚼,那烟草又生又烈,起初着实几乎把我的脑子弄麻了,我又不大嚼得惯。

paragraphs.en: Then I took some and steeped it an hour or two in some rum, and resolved to take a dose of it when I lay down; and lastly, I burnt some upon a pan of coals, and held my nose close over the smoke of it as long as I could bear it, as well for the heat as almost for suffocation.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我取了些,在朗姆酒里泡了一两个钟头,打算躺下时服它一剂;最后,我又在一盘炭火上烧了些,把鼻子凑近烟上、能忍多久就熏多久,又是烫又几乎叫人窒息。

paragraphs.en: In the interval of this operation I took up the Bible and began to read; but my head was too much disturbed with the tobacco to bear reading, at least at that time; only, having opened the book casually, the first words that occurred to me were these, “Call on Me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me.”
paragraphs.cn: 在做这番折腾的间隙,我拿起《圣经》读起来;可我脑子被烟草搅得太乱,读不下去,至少那时读不下去;只是我随手翻开书,头一眼撞上的便是这几句话:“你在患难之日求告我,我必搭救你,你也要荣耀我。”

paragraphs.en: These words were very apt to my case, and made some impression upon my thoughts at the time of reading them, though not so much as they did afterwards; for, as for being _delivered_, the word had no sound, as I may say, to me; the thing was so remote, so impossible in my apprehension of things, that I began to say, as the children of Israel did when they were promised flesh to eat, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness?” so I began to say, “Can God Himself deliver me from this place?”
paragraphs.cn: 这几句话很切合我的处境,读的当时对我的心思有些触动,虽不及日后那般深;因为说到“搭救”,这词儿在我听来可以说毫无分量;那事太遥远了,在我对事物的想象里太不可能,以致我开始说——就像以色列人得了应许有肉吃时所说的那样——“上帝岂能在旷野摆设筵席呢？”于是我也开始说:“上帝自己岂能把我从这地方救出去呢？”

paragraphs.en: And as it was not for many years that any hopes appeared, this prevailed very often upon my thoughts; but, however, the words made a great impression upon me, and I mused upon them very often.
paragraphs.cn: 由于此后许多年都不见一丝指望,这想头便常常占据我的心思;可不管怎样,那几句话在我心里留下了很深的印象,我时常反复琢磨它们。

paragraphs.en: It grew now late, and the tobacco had, as I said, dozed my head so much that I inclined to sleep; so I left my lamp burning in the cave, lest I should want anything in the night, and went to bed.
paragraphs.cn: 这时天已很晚,那烟草如我所说把我的头脑弄得昏沉,我直想睡;于是我把灯留在洞里点着,免得夜里需要什么,便上床去了。

paragraphs.en: But before I lay down, I did what I never had done in all my life—I kneeled down, and prayed to God to fulfil the promise to me, that if I called upon Him in the day of trouble, He would deliver me.
paragraphs.cn: 可躺下之前,我做了一件这辈子从没做过的事——我跪了下来,祷告上帝为我成就那应许:我若在患难之日求告他,他必搭救我。

paragraphs.en: After my broken and imperfect prayer was over, I drank the rum in which I had steeped the tobacco, which was so strong and rank of the tobacco that I could scarcely get it down; immediately upon this I went to bed.
paragraphs.cn: 我这断断续续、残缺不全的祷告完了,便把泡过烟草的朗姆酒喝了,那酒烟味又浓又冲,我几乎咽不下去;喝完我立刻上了床。

paragraphs.en: I found presently it flew up into my head violently; but I fell into a sound sleep, and waked no more till, by the sun, it must necessarily be near three o’clock in the afternoon the next day—nay, to this hour I am partly of opinion that I slept all the next day and night, and till almost three the day after; for otherwise I know not how I should lose a day out of my reckoning in the days of the week, as it appeared some years after I had done; for if I had lost it by crossing and recrossing the line, I should have lost more than one day; but certainly I lost a day in my account, and never knew which way.
paragraphs.cn: 我立时觉出酒劲猛地冲上头来;可我随即沉沉睡去,直到再没醒过,依日头看,第二天必已近下午三点才醒——不,直到此刻我还多少认为,我把第二天一整天连夜都睡了过去,一直睡到第三天将近三点;否则我实在不明白,我怎会在一周的日子里丢了一天,这是我记日子好些年后才发觉的;因为倘若是我越过赤道又折回而丢的,那丢的就不止一天了;可我账上确实丢了一天,却始终不知丢在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Be that, however, one way or the other, when I awaked I found myself exceedingly refreshed, and my spirits lively and cheerful; when I got up I was stronger than I was the day before, and my stomach better, for I was hungry; and, in short, I had no fit the next day, but continued much altered for the better.
paragraphs.cn: 且不论究竟是这样还是那样,我醒来时,只觉得自己精神大爽,情绪活泼欢畅;起身时我比头一天有劲了,胃口也好了,因为我饿了;总之,第二天我没有再犯病,而是一直好转了许多。

paragraphs.en: This was the 29th.
paragraphs.cn: 这天是二十九号。

paragraphs.en: The 30th was my well day, of course, and I went abroad with my gun, but did not care to travel too far.
paragraphs.cn: 三十号照例是我的康健日,我便带上枪出了门,却不想走得太远。

paragraphs.en: I killed a sea-fowl or two, something like a brandgoose, and brought them home, but was not very forward to eat them; so I ate some more of the turtle’s eggs, which were very good.
paragraphs.cn: 我打死了一两只海鸟,有点像黑雁,把它们带回了家,却不大想吃;于是又吃了些海龟蛋,那蛋很好吃。

paragraphs.en: This evening I renewed the medicine, which I had supposed did me good the day before—the tobacco steeped in rum; only I did not take so much as before, nor did I chew any of the leaf, or hold my head over the smoke; however, I was not so well the next day, which was the first of July, as I hoped I should have been; for I had a little spice of the cold fit, but it was not much.
paragraphs.cn: 这天晚上我又用了那味自以为头天对我有益的药——泡在朗姆酒里的烟草;只是我没像先前用那么多,也没嚼烟叶,没把头凑在烟上熏;可第二天,也就是七月一号,我却不像盼的那样好;因为我又略有一点发冷的迹象,不过不厉害。

paragraphs.en: _July_ 2.
paragraphs.cn: 7月2日。

paragraphs.en: —I renewed the medicine all the three ways; and dosed myself with it as at first, and doubled the quantity which I drank.
paragraphs.cn: 我把那三种用法的药全都又用了一遍;像头一回那样给自己下了药,还把喝的分量加了一倍。

paragraphs.en: _July_ 3.
paragraphs.cn: 7月3日。

paragraphs.en: —I missed the fit for good and all, though I did not recover my full strength for some weeks after.
paragraphs.cn: 我从此彻底不再发病了,虽说此后好几个星期才完全恢复元气。

paragraphs.en: While I was thus gathering strength, my thoughts ran exceedingly upon this Scripture, “I will deliver thee”; and the impossibility of my deliverance lay much upon my mind, in bar of my ever expecting it; but as I was discouraging myself with such thoughts, it occurred to my mind that I pored so much upon my deliverance from the main affliction, that I disregarded the deliverance I had received, and I was as it were made to ask myself such questions as these—viz.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样渐渐恢复气力时,心思异常执着地萦绕在这句经文上:“我必搭救你”;而获救之无望又沉沉压在我心头,叫我根本不敢指望;可正当我用这类念头灰自己心的时候,我忽然想到:我太一味惦记着从眼前这大苦难中获救,以致把已经得到的搭救全然忽视了;于是我像是不由得问自己这样几个问题——就是说:

paragraphs.en: Have I not been delivered, and wonderfully too, from sickness—from the most distressed condition that could be, and that was so frightful to me? and what notice had I taken of it?
paragraphs.cn: 我岂不是已经获救,而且救得如此奇妙——从疾病里,从那再凄惨不过、叫我那样惊惧的境地里？可我又何曾对此留过一点心？

paragraphs.en: Had I done my part?
paragraphs.cn: 我尽了自己的本分吗？

paragraphs.en: God had delivered me, but I had not glorified Him—that is to say, I had not owned and been thankful for that as a deliverance; and how could I expect greater deliverance?
paragraphs.cn: 上帝搭救了我,我却没有荣耀他——就是说,我没有承认这是一次搭救、也没有为它感恩;那我又怎能指望更大的搭救呢？

paragraphs.en: This touched my heart very much; and immediately I knelt down and gave God thanks aloud for my recovery from my sickness.
paragraphs.cn: 这深深触动了我的心;我当即跪下,高声为自己病愈感谢上帝。

paragraphs.en: _July_ 4.
paragraphs.cn: 7月4日。

paragraphs.en: —In the morning I took the Bible; and beginning at the New Testament, I began seriously to read it, and imposed upon myself to read a while every morning and every night; not tying myself to the number of chapters, but long as my thoughts should engage me.
paragraphs.cn: 早晨我拿起《圣经》;从《新约》起头,认认真真读了起来,并给自己定下规矩,每天早晚都读上一阵;不拘定读几章,只随着心思愿意读多久便读多久。

paragraphs.en: It was not long after I set seriously to this work till I found my heart more deeply and sincerely affected with the wickedness of my past life.
paragraphs.cn: 我认真做起这件事没多久,便觉得自己的心对过往一生的邪恶,受了更深切、更真诚的触动。

paragraphs.en: The impression of my dream revived; and the words, “All these things have not brought thee to repentance,” ran seriously through my thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 那梦的印象又活了过来;“这一切都没能使你悔改”这几句话,郑重地在我思绪里反复回响。

paragraphs.en: I was earnestly begging of God to give me repentance, when it happened providentially, the very day, that, reading the Scripture, I came to these words: “He is exalted a Prince and a Saviour, to give repentance and to give remission.”
paragraphs.cn: 我正恳切地求上帝赐我悔改之心时,恰好在天意的安排下,就在那一天,我读经读到了这几句话:“他被高举,作君王作救主,将悔改的心和赦罪的恩赐给人。”

paragraphs.en: I threw down the book; and with my heart as well as my hands lifted up to heaven, in a kind of ecstasy of joy, I cried out aloud, “Jesus, thou son of David!
paragraphs.cn: 我把书一撂,连心带手都举向天,在一种狂喜里高声喊道:“耶稣啊,你大卫的子孙！

paragraphs.en: Jesus, thou exalted Prince and Saviour! give me repentance!”
paragraphs.cn: 耶稣啊,你被高举的君王和救主！求你赐我悔改之心！”

paragraphs.en: This was the first time I could say, in the true sense of the words, that I prayed in all my life; for now I prayed with a sense of my condition, and a true Scripture view of hope, founded on the encouragement of the Word of God; and from this time, I may say, I began to hope that God would hear me.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我头一回可以真正照这几个字的意思说,我这辈子做了祷告;因为如今我是带着对自己处境的体认、带着以上帝话语的鼓励为根基、合乎圣经的盼望来祷告的;从这时起,我可以说,我开始盼望上帝会垂听我。

paragraphs.en: Now I began to construe the words mentioned above, “Call on Me, and I will deliver thee,” in a different sense from what I had ever done before; for then I had no notion of anything being called _deliverance_, but my being delivered from the captivity I was in; for though I was indeed at large in the place, yet the island was certainly a prison to me, and that in the worse sense in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我开始以一种从前从未有过的意思,去理解上面提过的那句话“你求告我,我必搭救你”;因为先前我心里对所谓“搭救”没有别的概念,只以为是把我从所陷的囚禁里救出去;因为我虽在这地方行动无阻,这岛于我却确实是座牢狱,而且是世上最坏那种意义上的牢狱。

paragraphs.en: But now I learned to take it in another sense: now I looked back upon my past life with such horror, and my sins appeared so dreadful, that my soul sought nothing of God but deliverance from the load of guilt that bore down all my comfort.
paragraphs.cn: 可如今我学会了从另一种意思去领会它:如今我回望过往的一生,满怀恐惧,我的罪显得那样可怕,以致我的灵魂向上帝所求的,不是别的,只是从那压垮我一切安慰的罪疚重担下得着解脱。

paragraphs.en: As for my solitary life, it was nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我这孤寂的生活,那算不得什么。

paragraphs.en: I did not so much as pray to be delivered from it or think of it; it was all of no consideration in comparison to this.
paragraphs.cn: 我甚至都没有祷告求脱离它,连想都没去想它;比起这个来,那全然不值一提。

paragraphs.en: And I add this part here, to hint to whoever shall read it, that whenever they come to a true sense of things, they will find deliverance from sin a much greater blessing than deliverance from affliction.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里加上这一段,是想提醒每一个读到它的人:一旦他们真正认清事物的本相,就会发觉从罪中得解脱,远比从苦难中得解脱是大得多的福分。

paragraphs.en: But, leaving this part, I return to my Journal.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,撇开这一段,还是回到我的日记吧。

paragraphs.en: My condition began now to be, though not less miserable as to my way of living, yet much easier to my mind: and my thoughts being directed, by a constant reading the Scripture and praying to God, to things of a higher nature, I had a great deal of comfort within, which till now I knew nothing of; also, my health and strength returned, I bestirred myself to furnish myself with everything that I wanted, and make my way of living as regular as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我的处境虽说在生活方式上并没少些凄惨,可在心境上却轻松多了:由于不断读经、向上帝祷告,我的心思被引向更崇高的事物,内心得着了极大的安慰——这安慰直到如今我还从不知晓;加上健康和气力都恢复了,我便打起精神,张罗齐自己所需的一切,尽量把生活过得有条有理。

paragraphs.en: From the 4th of July to the 14th I was chiefly employed in walking about with my gun in my hand, a little and a little at a time, as a man that was gathering up his strength after a fit of sickness; for it is hardly to be imagined how low I was, and to what weakness I was reduced.
paragraphs.cn: 从七月四号到十四号,我主要就是手里提着枪四处走动,一点一点地走,像个大病一场后正积攒气力的人;因为我那时虚弱到什么地步、衰弱成什么样子,简直难以想象。

paragraphs.en: The application which I made use of was perfectly new, and perhaps which had never cured an ague before; neither can I recommend it to any to practise, by this experiment: and though it did carry off the fit, yet it rather contributed to weakening me; for I had frequent convulsions in my nerves and limbs for some time.
paragraphs.cn: 我所用的这法子是全新的,也许从来没治好过一次疟疾;我也不能凭这次经验就推荐给任何人去试:虽说它确实把病压了下去,却反倒使我更加虚弱;因为此后有一阵子,我的神经和四肢常常抽搐。

paragraphs.en: I learned from it also this, in particular, that being abroad in the rainy season was the most pernicious thing to my health that could be, especially in those rains which came attended with storms and hurricanes of wind; for as the rain which came in the dry season was almost always accompanied with such storms, so I found that rain was much more dangerous than the rain which fell in September and October.
paragraphs.cn: 我还从中特别懂得了这一点:在雨季里出门在外,对我的健康是再有害不过的了,尤其是那些伴着暴风飓雨而来的雨;因为旱季里下的雨几乎总是伴着这样的风暴,所以我发觉那种雨比九、十月间下的雨危险得多。

paragraphs.en: I had now been in this unhappy island above ten months.
paragraphs.cn: 到这时,我在这座不幸的荒岛上已经住了十个多月。

paragraphs.en: All possibility of deliverance from this condition seemed to be entirely taken from me; and I firmly believe that no human shape had ever set foot upon that place.
paragraphs.cn: 看来一切脱离这种处境的可能都被彻底夺走了;我坚信从没有任何人踏足过这个地方。

paragraphs.en: Having now secured my habitation, as I thought, fully to my mind, I had a great desire to make a more perfect discovery of the island, and to see what other productions I might find, which I yet knew nothing of.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我自认为已把住所安排得完全称心,便非常想把这座岛更彻底地探察一番,看看还能找到些别的什么出产——那些我至今一无所知的东西。

paragraphs.en: It was on the 15th of July that I began to take a more particular survey of the island itself.
paragraphs.cn: 就在七月十五日,我开始对这座岛本身作一番更仔细的勘查。

paragraphs.en: I went up the creek first, where, as I hinted, I brought my rafts on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 我先沿着那条小河湾往上走,就是我先前提到的、把木筏运上岸的地方。

paragraphs.en: I found after I came about two miles up, that the tide did not flow any higher, and that it was no more than a little brook of running water, very fresh and good; but this being the dry season, there was hardly any water in some parts of it—at least not enough to run in any stream, so as it could be perceived.
paragraphs.cn: 往上走了约莫两英里后我发现,潮水到那里就不再往上涨了,那只是一条小溪,溪水潺潺,十分清甜可口;但正值旱季,有些河段几乎没什么水——至少不足以形成看得出来的水流。

paragraphs.en: On the banks of this brook I found many pleasant savannahs or meadows, plain, smooth, and covered with grass; and on the rising parts of them, next to the higher grounds, where the water, as might be supposed, never overflowed, I found a great deal of tobacco, green, and growing to a great and very strong stalk.
paragraphs.cn: 在这条小溪两岸,我看到许多宜人的草原或草地,平坦、光滑,长满青草;在靠近高地的隆起处,想来是水永远淹不到的地方,我发现了大量烟草,青翠茂盛,长成又高又粗壮的茎秆。

paragraphs.en: There were divers other plants, which I had no notion of or understanding about, that might, perhaps, have virtues of their own, which I could not find out.
paragraphs.cn: 还有其他各种植物,我一概不认识、不了解,或许它们各有自己的功用,只是我发现不了罢了。

paragraphs.en: I searched for the cassava root, which the Indians, in all that climate, make their bread of, but I could find none.
paragraphs.cn: 我到处寻找木薯根——那一带的印第安人都用它来做面包——却一株也没找到。

paragraphs.en: I saw large plants of aloes, but did not understand them.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见许多芦荟的大株,可是我不懂得怎么用它。

paragraphs.en: I saw several sugar-canes, but wild, and, for want of cultivation, imperfect.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见几根甘蔗,但都是野生的,因为无人栽培,长得并不好。

paragraphs.en: I contented myself with these discoveries for this time, and came back, musing with myself what course I might take to know the virtue and goodness of any of the fruits or plants which I should discover, but could bring it to no conclusion; for, in short, I had made so little observation while I was in the Brazils, that I knew little of the plants in the field; at least, very little that might serve to any purpose now in my distress.
paragraphs.cn: 这一次我便满足于这些发现,往回走,一路琢磨着有什么办法能弄清所发现的果实或植物哪些有用、哪些好,却怎么也得不出结论;总之,我在巴西时观察得太少,对田里的作物知之甚少——至少对眼下落难时能派上用场的东西,懂得实在不多。

paragraphs.en: The next day, the sixteenth, I went up the same way again; and after going something further than I had gone the day before, I found the brook and the savannahs cease, and the country become more woody than before.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天,十六日,我又沿原路往上走;比前一天走得远了些以后,我发现小溪和草原到了尽头,地势也比先前更多树林了。

paragraphs.en: In this part I found different fruits, and particularly I found melons upon the ground, in great abundance, and grapes upon the trees.
paragraphs.cn: 在这一带我发现了不同的果子,尤其是地上有大量的甜瓜,树上则结着葡萄。

paragraphs.en: The vines had spread, indeed, over the trees, and the clusters of grapes were just now in their prime, very ripe and rich.
paragraphs.cn: 藤蔓确实爬满了树,一串串葡萄正当时令,熟透而饱满。

paragraphs.en: This was a surprising discovery, and I was exceeding glad of them; but I was warned by my experience to eat sparingly of them; remembering that when I was ashore in Barbary, the eating of grapes killed several of our Englishmen, who were slaves there, by throwing them into fluxes and fevers.
paragraphs.cn: 这真是个令人惊喜的发现,我为此高兴极了;但经验告诫我要少吃一些——我记得从前在巴巴里上岸时,吃葡萄害死了我们好几个在那里当奴隶的英国人,叫他们患上痢疾和热病。

paragraphs.en: But I found an excellent use for these grapes; and that was, to cure or dry them in the sun, and keep them as dried grapes or raisins are kept, which I thought would be, as indeed they were, wholesome and agreeable to eat when no grapes could be had.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我给这些葡萄找到了一个极妙的用处,那就是把它们放在太阳下晒干,像人们保存葡萄干那样存起来;我想这样一来,在没有鲜葡萄的时候,它们既有益健康又好吃——后来果然如此。

paragraphs.en: I spent all that evening there, and went not back to my habitation; which, by the way, was the first night, as I might say, I had lain from home.
paragraphs.cn: 那一整晚我都待在那里,没有回住所;顺便说一句,可以说这是我头一回离家过夜。

paragraphs.en: In the night, I took my first contrivance, and got up in a tree, where I slept well; and the next morning proceeded upon my discovery; travelling nearly four miles, as I might judge by the length of the valley, keeping still due north, with a ridge of hills on the south and north side of me.
paragraphs.cn: 夜里,我使出第一招,爬到一棵树上,睡得很好;第二天早晨继续我的探察;照我看那山谷的长度判断,我走了将近四英里,一直朝正北方走,南北两侧都有一道山脊。

paragraphs.en: At the end of this march I came to an opening where the country seemed to descend to the west; and a little spring of fresh water, which issued out of the side of the hill by me, ran the other way, that is, due east; and the country appeared so fresh, so green, so flourishing, everything being in a constant verdure or flourish of spring that it looked like a planted garden.
paragraphs.cn: 这一程走到尽头,我来到一处开阔地,那里地势似乎向西倾斜;一小股清泉从我身旁的山坡里涌出,却朝另一个方向、也就是正东流去;这一带景色如此清新、翠绿、繁茂,处处一派长青、一片春意,看上去就像一座人工栽培的花园。

paragraphs.en: I descended a little on the side of that delicious vale, surveying it with a secret kind of pleasure, though mixed with my other afflicting thoughts, to think that this was all my own; that I was king and lord of all this country indefensibly, and had a right of possession; and if I could convey it, I might have it in inheritance as completely as any lord of a manor in England.
paragraphs.cn: 我顺着那可爱山谷的坡沿往下走了一小段,怀着一种暗自的喜悦打量着它,虽然这喜悦里也夹杂着我别的忧思——想到这一切都归我所有;想到我毫无争议地是这整片土地的君王与主人,拥有占有的权利;假如能够转让,我尽可像英格兰任何一位庄园领主那样把它完完整整地传给子孙。

paragraphs.en: I saw here abundance of cocoa trees, orange, and lemon, and citron trees; but all wild, and very few bearing any fruit, at least not then.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里看到大量可可树、橙树、柠檬树和香橼树;但都是野生的,结果的极少——至少当时如此。

paragraphs.en: However, the green limes that I gathered were not only pleasant to eat, but very wholesome; and I mixed their juice afterwards with water, which made it very wholesome, and very cool and refreshing.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我采到的青柠不仅吃着可口,而且很有益;后来我把它们的汁掺在水里,喝起来非常爽口、清凉解渴,又有益健康。

paragraphs.en: I found now I had business enough to gather and carry home; and I resolved to lay up a store as well of grapes as limes and lemons, to furnish myself for the wet season, which I knew was approaching.
paragraphs.cn: 我这时发现要采要运回家的东西已经够多了;我便决心把葡萄连同青柠、柠檬都储存起来,好应付我知道就要到来的雨季。

paragraphs.en: In order to do this, I gathered a great heap of grapes in one place, a lesser heap in another place, and a great parcel of limes and lemons in another place; and taking a few of each with me, I travelled homewards; resolving to come again, and bring a bag or sack, or what I could make, to carry the rest home.
paragraphs.cn: 为此,我在一处堆了一大堆葡萄,在另一处堆了小一点的一堆,又在别处堆了一大批青柠和柠檬;然后每样带一点,动身回家,打算改天再来,带上口袋或麻袋、或是我能做出来的什么东西,把其余的运回去。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, having spent three days in this journey, I came home (so I must now call my tent and my cave); but before I got thither the grapes were spoiled; the richness of the fruit and the weight of the juice having broken them and bruised them, they were good for little or nothing; as to the limes, they were good, but I could bring but a few.
paragraphs.cn: 于是,这趟走了三天,我回到了家(如今我只能这样称呼我的帐篷和洞穴);可是还没到家,葡萄就坏了——果子太丰润、汁水太重,把它们自己压破挤烂,几乎一点用都没有了;至于青柠,倒还好,只是我带回来的没几个。

paragraphs.en: The next day, being the nineteenth, I went back, having made me two small bags to bring home my harvest; but I was surprised, when coming to my heap of grapes, which were so rich and fine when I gathered them, to find them all spread about, trod to pieces, and dragged about, some here, some there, and abundance eaten and devoured.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天,十九日,我又回去,还给自己做了两个小袋子好把收成带回家;可是当我来到那堆葡萄跟前时,却大吃一惊——采时那么饱满漂亮的葡萄,如今全撒得满地都是,被踩得稀烂,东一堆西一堆地拖来拖去,还有一大批被吃掉了。

paragraphs.en: By this I concluded there were some wild creatures thereabouts, which had done this; but what they were I knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 由此我断定,附近有某种野兽干了这事;但究竟是什么,我不得而知。

paragraphs.en: However, as I found there was no laying them up on heaps, and no carrying them away in a sack, but that one way they would be destroyed, and the other way they would be crushed with their own weight, I took another course; for I gathered a large quantity of the grapes, and hung upon the out-branches of the trees, that they might cure and dry in the sun; and as for the limes and lemons, I carried as many back as I could well stand under.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,既然我发现既不能把葡萄堆着,又不能装进袋子运走——一样是被糟蹋,另一样是被自身的重量压烂——我便改用别的办法;我采了一大批葡萄,挂在树的外侧枝条上,让它们在太阳下风干;至于青柠和柠檬,我能扛多少就往回带多少。

paragraphs.en: When I came home from this journey, I contemplated with great pleasure the fruitfulness of that valley, and the pleasantness of the situation; the security from storms on that side of the water, and the wood: and concluded that I had pitched upon a place to fix my abode which was by far the worst part of the country.
paragraphs.cn: 这趟回到家,我满心欢喜地想着那山谷的丰饶、那地方的宜人,想着它那一侧临水、又有树林,足以挡风避雨;于是我断定,我先前选来安家的这个地方,竟是全岛最糟糕的一处。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, I began to consider of removing my habitation, and looking out for a place equally safe as where now I was situate, if possible, in that pleasant, fruitful part of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 总的说来,我开始考虑搬家,想在那宜人富饶的岛的那一带,找一处若有可能与我现居之地同样安全的地方。

paragraphs.en: This thought ran long in my head, and I was exceeding fond of it for some time, the pleasantness of the place tempting me; but when I came to a nearer view of it, I considered that I was now by the seaside, where it was at least possible that something might happen to my advantage, and, by the same ill fate that brought me hither might bring some other unhappy wretches to the same place; and though it was scarce probable that any such thing should ever happen, yet to enclose myself among the hills and woods in the centre of the island was to anticipate my bondage, and to render such an affair not only improbable, but impossible; and that therefore I ought not by any means to remove.
paragraphs.cn: 这念头在我脑子里盘桓了很久,有一阵子我对它着迷极了,被那地方的宜人所诱惑;但当我更仔细地考量时,我想到自己如今住在海边,这里至少还有可能发生对我有利的事——同样把我抛到这里的厄运,说不定也会把别的落难之人送到这同一个地方;虽然这种事几乎不大可能发生,可要是把自己关进岛中央的山林之间,那就等于是自甘囚禁,叫这样的事不仅不大可能、简直根本不可能了;因此我无论如何都不该搬走。

paragraphs.en: However, I was so enamoured of this place, that I spent much of my time there for the whole of the remaining part of the month of July; and though upon second thoughts, I resolved not to remove, yet I built me a little kind of a bower, and surrounded it at a distance with a strong fence, being a double hedge, as high as I could reach, well staked and filled between with brushwood; and here I lay very secure, sometimes two or three nights together; always going over it with a ladder; so that I fancied now I had my country house and my sea-coast house; and this work took me up to the beginning of August.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我对这地方实在太着迷了,以致七月剩下的整段日子里,我大部分时间都待在那儿;虽然再三思量后我决定不搬家,可我还是给自己搭了个小小的凉棚,并在四周隔开一段距离围上一道结实的篱笆——那是一道双层的树篱,高及我手能够到的地方,牢牢打了桩,中间填满了灌木枝;在这里我睡得很安稳,有时一连两三夜;每次都靠一架梯子翻进翻出;于是我幻想自己如今既有了乡间别墅,又有了海边宅子;这项工程一直做到八月初。

paragraphs.en: I had but newly finished my fence, and began to enjoy my labour, when the rains came on, and made me stick close to my first habitation; for though I had made me a tent like the other, with a piece of a sail, and spread it very well, yet I had not the shelter of a hill to keep me from storms, nor a cave behind me to retreat into when the rains were extraordinary.
paragraphs.cn: 我刚把篱笆做完、开始享受自己的劳动成果,雨季就来了,逼得我紧紧守在最初那个住所;因为我虽然像另一处那样、用一块帆布给自己搭了顶帐篷,也铺得很好,却没有一座山挡着风雨,身后也没有洞穴可以在暴雨异常时躲进去。

paragraphs.en: About the beginning of August, as I said, I had finished my bower, and began to enjoy myself.
paragraphs.cn: 如我所说,大约八月初,我把凉棚做好了,开始过起自在的日子。

paragraphs.en: The 3rd of August, I found the grapes I had hung up perfectly dried, and, indeed, were excellent good raisins of the sun; so I began to take them down from the trees, and it was very happy that I did so, for the rains which followed would have spoiled them, and I had lost the best part of my winter food; for I had above two hundred large bunches of them.
paragraphs.cn: 八月三日,我发现挂起来的葡萄已经晒得干透,确实是极好的太阳晒葡萄干;于是我开始把它们从树上取下来;幸好我这么做了,因为随后的雨水本会把它们毁掉,那样我就损失了过冬粮食里最好的一份——因为我总共有两百多大串呢。

paragraphs.en: No sooner had I taken them all down, and carried the most of them home to my cave, than it began to rain; and from hence, which was the 14th of August, it rained, more or less, every day till the middle of October; and sometimes so violently, that I could not stir out of my cave for several days.
paragraphs.cn: 我刚把它们全取下来、把大部分运回洞里,就下起雨来;从这天、也就是八月十四日起,一直到十月中旬,天天都或多或少地下雨;有时下得那么猛,我一连好几天都出不了洞。

paragraphs.en: In this season I was much surprised with the increase of my family; I had been concerned for the loss of one of my cats, who ran away from me, or, as I thought, had been dead, and I heard no more tidings of her till, to my astonishment, she came home about the end of August with three kittens.
paragraphs.cn: 在这段时节里,我的家庭成员增添了,叫我很是意外;我一直为丢了一只猫而挂心,它从我这儿跑掉了,我还以为它死了呢,此后再没它的音讯,直到八月底,它竟带着三只小猫回了家,叫我惊讶不已。

paragraphs.en: This was the more strange to me because, though I had killed a wild cat, as I called it, with my gun, yet I thought it was quite a different kind from our European cats; but the young cats were the same kind of house-breed as the old one; and both my cats being females, I thought it very strange.
paragraphs.cn: 这事更叫我觉得奇怪,因为我虽然用枪打死过一只被我称作野猫的东西,却认定那和我们欧洲的猫是很不一样的种类;可这几只小猫和老猫一样,都是家养的品种;而我那两只猫又都是母的,我便觉得实在蹊跷。

paragraphs.en: But from these three cats I afterwards came to be so pestered with cats that I was forced to kill them like vermin or wild beasts, and to drive them from my house as much as possible.
paragraphs.cn: 但从这三只猫起,后来我被猫群闹得不胜其烦,不得不像对付害虫或野兽那样把它们打死,并尽量把它们赶出我的住处。

paragraphs.en: From the 14th of August to the 26th, incessant rain, so that I could not stir, and was now very careful not to be much wet.
paragraphs.cn: 从八月十四日到二十六日,大雨不停,我出不了门,这时我很小心,不让自己淋得太湿。

paragraphs.en: In this confinement, I began to be straitened for food: but venturing out twice, I one day killed a goat; and the last day, which was the 26th, found a very large tortoise, which was a treat to me, and my food was regulated thus: I ate a bunch of raisins for my breakfast; a piece of the goat’s flesh, or of the turtle, for my dinner, broiled—for, to my great misfortune, I had no vessel to boil or stew anything; and two or three of the turtle’s eggs for my supper.
paragraphs.cn: 在这被困期间,我的食物开始短缺;但我冒险出去过两次,一天打到一只山羊;最后一天、也就是二十六日,又找到一只很大的陆龟,这对我可是一顿美餐;我的饮食就这样安排:早饭吃一串葡萄干;午饭吃一块羊肉或龟肉,烤着吃——因为很不幸,我没有任何器皿可以煮或炖东西;晚饭吃两三个龟蛋。

paragraphs.en: During this confinement in my cover by the rain, I worked daily two or three hours at enlarging my cave, and by degrees worked it on towards one side, till I came to the outside of the hill, and made a door or way out, which came beyond my fence or wall; and so I came in and out this way.
paragraphs.cn: 在被雨困在藏身处的这段日子里,我每天花两三个小时挖大我的洞穴,一点点朝一侧掏进去,直到掏到山的外侧,开出一道门、一条出路,通到我的篱笆或围墙之外;从此我就走这条路进进出出。

paragraphs.en: But I was not perfectly easy at lying so open; for, as I had managed myself before, I was in a perfect enclosure; whereas now I thought I lay exposed, and open for anything to come in upon me; and yet I could not perceive that there was any living thing to fear, the biggest creature that I had yet seen upon the island being a goat.
paragraphs.cn: 但躺在这么敞开的地方我并不十分安心;因为照我先前的布置,我原是处在一圈严密的围护之中;而现在我却觉得自己暴露在外,任什么东西都能闯进来袭击我;然而我又察觉不出有什么活物值得害怕,毕竟我在岛上见过的最大的动物也不过是一只山羊。

paragraphs.en: _Sept.
paragraphs.cn: 九月
三十日。

paragraphs.en: —I was now come to the unhappy anniversary of my landing.
paragraphs.cn: ——我如今来到了登岛那个不幸日子的周年。

paragraphs.en: I cast up the notches on my post, and found I had been on shore three hundred and sixty-five days.
paragraphs.cn: 我把柱子上刻的痕数了一遍,发现自己已经上岸三百六十五天了。

paragraphs.en: I kept this day as a solemn fast, setting it apart for religious exercise, prostrating myself on the ground with the most serious humiliation, confessing my sins to God, acknowledging His righteous judgments upon me, and praying to Him to have mercy on me through Jesus Christ; and not having tasted the least refreshment for twelve hours, even till the going down of the sun, I then ate a biscuit-cake and a bunch of grapes, and went to bed, finishing the day as I began it.
paragraphs.cn: 我把这一天当作庄严的斋戒日,专门用来做宗教功课,俯伏在地,怀着最深切的谦卑,向上帝忏悔我的罪,承认他对我公义的审判,祈求他借着耶稣基督怜悯我;我整整十二个小时、直到日落都不曾进一点吃食,然后才吃了一块饼干和一串葡萄,便上床睡觉,以开始这一天的方式来结束这一天。

paragraphs.en: I had all this time observed no Sabbath day; for as at first I had no sense of religion upon my mind, I had, after some time, omitted to distinguish the weeks, by making a longer notch than ordinary for the Sabbath day, and so did not really know what any of the days were; but now, having cast up the days as above, I found I had been there a year; so I divided it into weeks, and set apart every seventh day for a Sabbath; though I found at the end of my account I had lost a day or two in my reckoning.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间里我一直没有守安息日;因为起初我心里毫无宗教观念,过了一阵之后,我便懒得再用一道比平常长些的刻痕来标出安息日、以区分星期了,于是实在不知道每天是星期几;但如今照上面所说数过日子,我发现自己在这里已经待了一年;于是我把它划成一个个星期,每逢第七天便定为安息日;尽管算到末了,我发觉自己的计数里漏了一两天。

paragraphs.en: A little after this, my ink began to fail me, and so I contented myself to use it more sparingly, and to write down only the most remarkable events of my life, without continuing a daily memorandum of other things.
paragraphs.cn: 这之后不久,我的墨水开始不够用了,于是我只好省着点用,只把生平最值得记的事写下来,不再逐日记录别的琐事。

paragraphs.en: The rainy season and the dry season began now to appear regular to me, and I learned to divide them so as to provide for them accordingly; but I bought all my experience before I had it, and this I am going to relate was one of the most discouraging experiments that I made.
paragraphs.cn: 雨季和旱季这时在我看来渐渐有了规律,我学会了这样划分它们,以便相应地作准备;可我所有的经验都是先付了代价才得来的,我接下来要讲的,就是我做过的最叫人灰心的一次尝试。

paragraphs.en: I have mentioned that I had saved the few ears of barley and rice, which I had so surprisingly found spring up, as I thought, of themselves, and I believe there were about thirty stalks of rice, and about twenty of barley; and now I thought it a proper time to sow it, after the rains, the sun being in its southern position, going from me.
paragraphs.cn: 我曾提到,我留下了那几穗大麦和稻子——就是我意想不到地发现、自以为是自生自长的那些;我想大约有三十来根稻茎、二十来根麦茎;如今雨后我觉得正是播种的好时候,因为太阳这时正处在南边、离我而去。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, I dug up a piece of ground as well as I could with my wooden spade, and dividing it into two parts, I sowed my grain; but as I was sowing, it casually occurred to my thoughts that I would not sow it all at first, because I did not know when was the proper time for it, so I sowed about two-thirds of the seed, leaving about a handful of each.
paragraphs.cn: 于是,我用木锹尽力挖出一块地,把它分成两半,播下我的谷种;可正撒种时,我偶然想到,不该一下子全撒了,因为我不知道什么时候才是合适的播种季节,于是只撒了约莫三分之二的种子,每样各留了一把光景。

paragraphs.en: It was a great comfort to me afterwards that I did so, for not one grain of what I sowed this time came to anything: for the dry months following, the earth having had no rain after the seed was sown, it had no moisture to assist its growth, and never came up at all till the wet season had come again, and then it grew as if it had been but newly sown.
paragraphs.cn: 后来我很庆幸自己这么做了,因为这一回撒下去的种子没有一粒长出来:随后是干旱的月份,种子撒下后地里再没下过雨,没有水分助它生长,一直到雨季重又来临才冒出苗来,那时它长得就像刚播下去似的。

paragraphs.en: Finding my first seed did not grow, which I easily imagined was by the drought, I sought for a moister piece of ground to make another trial in, and I dug up a piece of ground near my new bower, and sowed the rest of my seed in February, a little before the vernal equinox; and this having the rainy months of March and April to water it, sprung up very pleasantly, and yielded a very good crop; but having part of the seed left only, and not daring to sow all that I had, I had but a small quantity at last, my whole crop not amounting to above half a peck of each kind.
paragraphs.cn: 发现我头一批种子没长出来——我不难想到是干旱所致——我便另找了一块较湿润的地再试一回,在我新凉棚附近挖了一块地,于二月、春分前不久把余下的种子播了下去;这一批赶上了三四月的雨月得到浇灌,长得很喜人,收成很不错;可是因为只剩了一部分种子,我又不敢把手里的全撒了,到头来收成很少,两样加起来还不到半配克。

paragraphs.en: But by this experiment I was made master of my business, and knew exactly when the proper season was to sow, and that I might expect two seed-times and two harvests every year.
paragraphs.cn: 但经过这次试验,我算是把这门营生弄明白了,确切知道了什么时候是播种的合适季节,也知道自己每年可望有两个播种期、两次收获。

paragraphs.en: While this corn was growing I made a little discovery, which was of use to me afterwards.
paragraphs.cn: 这批谷子生长期间,我有了个小小的发现,后来对我很有用。

paragraphs.en: As soon as the rains were over, and the weather began to settle, which was about the month of November, I made a visit up the country to my bower, where, though I had not been some months, yet I found all things just as I left them.
paragraphs.cn: 雨一停、天气开始稳定下来,大约是十一月里,我上乡下去探看我的凉棚;虽然我有几个月没去了,却发现一切都和我离开时一模一样。

paragraphs.en: The circle or double hedge that I had made was not only firm and entire, but the stakes which I had cut out of some trees that grew thereabouts were all shot out and grown with long branches, as much as a willow-tree usually shoots the first year after lopping its head.
paragraphs.cn: 我做的那圈双层树篱不仅牢固完好,而且我从附近长着的几棵树上砍来做桩的那些木条,全都发了芽、抽出了长长的枝条,长势就像柳树被截去树梢后头一年通常抽枝那样茂盛。

paragraphs.en: I could not tell what tree to call it that these stakes were cut from.
paragraphs.cn: 我说不出这些桩子是从什么树上砍下来的。

paragraphs.en: I was surprised, and yet very well pleased, to see the young trees grow; and I pruned them, and led them up to grow as much alike as I could; and it is scarce credible how beautiful a figure they grew into in three years; so that though the hedge made a circle of about twenty-five yards in diameter, yet the trees, for such I might now call them, soon covered it, and it was a complete shade, sufficient to lodge under all the dry season.
paragraphs.cn: 看着这些小树生长,我又惊又喜;我给它们剪枝,引导它们尽量长得整齐一致;它们在三年里长成的模样之美,几乎叫人难以置信;因此,那道篱笆虽然围成一个直径约二十五码的圆圈,可那些树——如今我尽可以这样称呼它们了——很快就把它遮盖住了,成了一片完整的绿荫,足够我在整个旱季藏身其下。

paragraphs.en: This made me resolve to cut some more stakes, and make me a hedge like this, in a semi-circle round my wall (I mean that of my first dwelling), which I did; and placing the trees or stakes in a double row, at about eight yards distance from my first fence, they grew presently, and were at first a fine cover to my habitation, and afterwards served for a defence also, as I shall observe in its order.
paragraphs.cn: 这使我下决心再砍些桩子,照这样给我那道围墙(我是说最初住处的那道)绕出一道半圆形的树篱来;我照办了;我把这些树或桩子排成双行,离我最初那道篱笆约莫八码远,它们很快就长起来,起初给我的住所添了一道漂亮的遮蔽,后来也充当了防御——这我将按次序讲到。

paragraphs.en: I found now that the seasons of the year might generally be divided, not into summer and winter, as in Europe, but into the rainy seasons and the dry seasons, which were generally thus:—The half of February, the whole of March, and the half of April—rainy, the sun being then on or near the equinox.
paragraphs.cn: 我这时发现,这里一年的季节大体上并不像欧洲那样分为夏冬,而是分为雨季和旱季,大致如下:——二月的一半、整个三月、四月的一半——是雨季,太阳这时正处在或接近春分点。

paragraphs.en: The half of April, the whole of May, June, and July, and the half of August—dry, the sun being then to the north of the line.
paragraphs.cn: 四月的一半、整个五月、六月、七月、以及八月的一半——是旱季,太阳这时在赤道线以北。

paragraphs.en: The half of August, the whole of September, and the half of October—rainy, the sun being then come back.
paragraphs.cn: 八月的一半、整个九月、十月的一半——是雨季,太阳这时已经折返。

paragraphs.en: The half of October, the whole of November, December, and January, and the half of February—dry, the sun being then to the south of the line.
paragraphs.cn: 十月的一半、整个十一月、十二月、一月、以及二月的一半——是旱季,太阳这时在赤道线以南。

paragraphs.en: The rainy seasons sometimes held longer or shorter as the winds happened to blow, but this was the general observation I made.
paragraphs.cn: 雨季有时因刮什么风而或长或短,不过这是我作出的大致观察。

paragraphs.en: After I had found by experience the ill consequences of being abroad in the rain, I took care to furnish myself with provisions beforehand, that I might not be obliged to go out, and I sat within doors as much as possible during the wet months.
paragraphs.cn: 在我凭经验尝到了冒雨外出的恶果之后,我便留心事先给自己备好粮食,免得不得不出门;整个雨月里,我尽可能地待在屋内。

paragraphs.en: This time I found much employment, and very suitable also to the time, for I found great occasion for many things which I had no way to furnish myself with but by hard labour and constant application; particularly I tried many ways to make myself a basket, but all the twigs I could get for the purpose proved so brittle that they would do nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间我找到了许多活计,也很合乎时令,因为我发现有很多东西非得靠苦干和持之以恒不可,别无办法给自己置办;我尤其试了许多法子想给自己编个篮子,可我能弄到的枝条都太脆,一点用都派不上。

paragraphs.en: It proved of excellent advantage to me now, that when I was a boy, I used to take great delight in standing at a basket-maker’s, in the town where my father lived, to see them make their wicker-ware; and being, as boys usually are, very officious to help, and a great observer of the manner in which they worked those things, and sometimes lending a hand, I had by these means full knowledge of the methods of it, and I wanted nothing but the materials, when it came into my mind that the twigs of that tree from whence I cut my stakes that grew might possibly be as tough as the sallows, willows, and osiers in England, and I resolved to try.
paragraphs.cn: 如今有一件事对我大有好处:小时候,我住在父亲所在的镇上,常常极爱站在一个编篮匠跟前,看他们编柳条器物;像一般男孩那样,我很热心地帮忙,又爱仔细观察他们编这些东西的手法,有时也搭把手,靠这些我把编法门道摸得一清二楚,如今我什么都不缺,单缺材料——这时我忽然想到,我砍来做那些已发芽的桩子的那种树,它的枝条说不定和英格兰的黄花柳、柳树、白柳一样柔韧,我便决心试一试。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, the next day I went to my country house, as I called it, and cutting some of the smaller twigs, I found them to my purpose as much as I could desire; whereupon I came the next time prepared with a hatchet to cut down a quantity, which I soon found, for there was great plenty of them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是第二天我去了我称作乡间别墅的地方,砍下几根较细的枝条,发现它们完全合乎我的用途,称心如意;于是下一回我便带上短斧有备而去,砍下了一大批——很快就砍够了,因为那种枝条多得很。

paragraphs.en: These I set up to dry within my circle or hedge, and when they were fit for use I carried them to my cave; and here, during the next season, I employed myself in making, as well as I could, a great many baskets, both to carry earth or to carry or lay up anything, as I had occasion; and though I did not finish them very handsomely, yet I made them sufficiently serviceable for my purpose; thus, afterwards, I took care never to be without them; and as my wicker-ware decayed, I made more, especially strong, deep baskets to place my corn in, instead of sacks, when I should come to have any quantity of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我把这些枝条竖在我那圈篱笆里晾干,等它们可以用了,便搬到洞里;在这里,接下来的一季我尽力做了许多篮子,或用来运土,或用来搬运、存放我需要装的种种东西;虽然我做得并不十分漂亮,可对我的用途来说已经够结实好使了;从此我留心让自己从不缺篮子;柳条器物一坏,我就再做新的,尤其是些结实的深篮,好在将来收到粮食时用来装谷子,代替口袋。

paragraphs.en: Having mastered this difficulty, and employed a world of time about it, I bestirred myself to see, if possible, how to supply two wants.
paragraphs.cn: 攻克了这道难关、在上头花了无数工夫之后,我便振作起来,看看有没有可能补上另外两样缺欠。

paragraphs.en: I had no vessels to hold anything that was liquid, except two runlets, which were almost full of rum, and some glass bottles—some of the common size, and others which were case bottles, square, for the holding of water, spirits, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有器皿可以盛装任何液体,只有两个小桶,里头几乎装满了朗姆酒,还有几个玻璃瓶——有些是普通大小的,另一些是方形的匣装瓶,用来盛水、烈酒之类。

paragraphs.en: I had not so much as a pot to boil anything, except a great kettle, which I saved out of the ship, and which was too big for such as I desired it—viz. to make broth, and stew a bit of meat by itself.
paragraphs.cn: 我连一口煮东西的锅都没有,只有一口大水壶是我从船上救下来的,可它对我想要的用途来说太大了——就是说,拿来熬点汤、单煮一小块肉。

paragraphs.en: The second thing I fain would have had was a tobacco-pipe, but it was impossible to me to make one; however, I found a contrivance for that, too, at last.
paragraphs.cn: 我第二样极想要的东西是一根烟斗,可我怎么也做不出来;不过到末了,这件事我也想出了一个巧法子。

paragraphs.en: I employed myself in planting my second rows of stakes or piles, and in this wicker-working all the summer or dry season, when another business took me up more time than it could be imagined I could spare.
paragraphs.cn: 整个夏天或者说旱季,我都忙着栽种我第二排桩子或木桩,并做这些柳条活儿;这时,另一件事占去了我的工夫,多得叫人难以想象我竟还挤得出时间来。

paragraphs.en: I mentioned before that I had a great mind to see the whole island, and that I had travelled up the brook, and so on to where I built my bower, and where I had an opening quite to the sea, on the other side of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 我前面提到过,我很想把整座岛看个遍,也说过我曾沿着那条小溪往上走,一直走到我搭凉棚的地方,在那里有一处开阔地,正对着岛另一侧的大海。

paragraphs.en: I now resolved to travel quite across to the sea-shore on that side; so, taking my gun, a hatchet, and my dog, and a larger quantity of powder and shot than usual, with two biscuit-cakes and a great bunch of raisins in my pouch for my store, I began my journey.
paragraphs.cn: 这一次我下决心一直穿过去,走到那一边的海岸;于是我带上枪、一把小斧和我的狗,又比平常多带了些火药和铅弹,袋子里还装了两块饼干和一大串葡萄干作干粮,便动身上路了。

paragraphs.en: When I had passed the vale where my bower stood, as above, I came within view of the sea to the west, and it being a very clear day, I fairly descried land—whether an island or a continent I could not tell; but it lay very high, extending from the W. to the W.
paragraphs.cn: 我照前面说的那样,越过了凉棚所在的那道山谷,便望见了西边的大海;那天天气极晴朗,我清清楚楚地看见了一片陆地——究竟是岛屿还是大陆,我说不上来;但它地势很高,从西一直延伸到西。

paragraphs.en: S.
paragraphs.cn: 南。

paragraphs.en: W. at a very great distance; by my guess it could not be less than fifteen or twenty leagues off.
paragraphs.cn: 偏西,离得非常远;据我估计,少说也有十五到二十里格。

paragraphs.en: I could not tell what part of the world this might be, otherwise than that I knew it must be part of America, and, as I concluded by all my observations, must be near the Spanish dominions, and perhaps was all inhabited by savages, where, if I had landed, I had been in a worse condition than I was now; and therefore I acquiesced in the dispositions of Providence, which I began now to own and to believe ordered everything for the best; I say I quieted my mind with this, and left off afflicting myself with fruitless wishes of being there.
paragraphs.cn: 我说不清这是世界上的哪个地方,只知道它一定属于美洲的一部分;而且照我种种观察推断,它必定离西班牙人的领地不远,或许全住着野蛮人;倘若我当初在那里登陆,处境只会比现在更糟。因此我顺服了天意的安排——如今我开始承认并相信,天意把一切都安排得最好;我是说,我以此宽慰自己,不再拿“要是能到那边去”这种徒劳的空想来折磨自己了。

paragraphs.en: Besides, after some thought upon this affair, I considered that if this land was the Spanish coast, I should certainly, one time or other, see some vessel pass or repass one way or other; but if not, then it was the savage coast between the Spanish country and Brazils, where are found the worst of savages; for they are cannibals or men-eaters, and fail not to murder and devour all the human bodies that fall into their hands.
paragraphs.cn: 再说,对这件事我又想了想:倘若那片陆地是西班牙人的海岸,我迟早总能看见有船只从这边或那边经过;可若不是,那它便是西班牙属地与巴西之间的野蛮海岸,那里出没着最凶恶的野蛮人;因为他们是食人生番,凡落到他们手里的活人,无不被杀掉吃掉。

paragraphs.en: With these considerations, I walked very leisurely forward.
paragraphs.cn: 抱着这些念头,我不慌不忙地往前走。

paragraphs.en: I found that side of the island where I now was much pleasanter than mine—the open or savannah fields sweet, adorned with flowers and grass, and full of very fine woods.
paragraphs.cn: 我发觉我如今所在的岛这一侧比我住的那边可爱得多——开阔的草原甜美宜人,点缀着花草,还有很多极好的树林。

paragraphs.en: I saw abundance of parrots, and fain I would have caught one, if possible, to have kept it to be tame, and taught it to speak to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见许许多多鹦鹉,很想能捉一只养起来,把它驯服,教它跟我说话。

paragraphs.en: I did, after some painstaking, catch a young parrot, for I knocked it down with a stick, and having recovered it, I brought it home; but it was some years before I could make him speak; however, at last I taught him to call me by name very familiarly.
paragraphs.cn: 费了些工夫后,我果然捉到一只小鹦鹉,是用一根棍子把它打落的;等它缓过来,我便把它带回了家;可过了好几年我才让它开口说话;不过最后我总算教会了它熟熟稔稔地叫我的名字。

paragraphs.en: But the accident that followed, though it be a trifle, will be very diverting in its place.
paragraphs.cn: 而随后发生的一桩意外,虽说是件小事,到时候讲起来却很有意思。

paragraphs.en: I was exceedingly diverted with this journey.
paragraphs.cn: 这趟旅行让我极为快活。

paragraphs.en: I found in the low grounds hares (as I thought them to be) and foxes; but they differed greatly from all the other kinds I had met with, nor could I satisfy myself to eat them, though I killed several.
paragraphs.cn: 我在低地里发现了(我当它们是)野兔和狐狸;但它们跟我从前见过的各种都大不相同,虽然我打死了好几只,却总下不了决心吃它们。

paragraphs.en: But I had no need to be venturous, for I had no want of food, and of that which was very good too, especially these three sorts, viz. goats, pigeons, and turtle, or tortoise, which added to my grapes, Leadenhall market could not have furnished a table better than I, in proportion to the company; and though my case was deplorable enough, yet I had great cause for thankfulness that I was not driven to any extremities for food, but had rather plenty, even to dainties.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我也犯不着冒险,因为我不愁吃的,而且吃的还很好,尤其是这三样:山羊、鸽子和海龟(或叫乌龟),再加上我的葡萄,论供应的人数,伦敦的利登霍尔市场也未必能摆出比我更好的餐桌;虽说我的境况够可怜的,可我也大有理由感恩,因为我并没落到为觅食而走投无路的地步,反倒相当丰足,甚至称得上有美味。

paragraphs.en: I never travelled in this journey above two miles outright in a day, or thereabouts; but I took so many turns and re-turns to see what discoveries I could make, that I came weary enough to the place where I resolved to sit down all night; and then I either reposed myself in a tree, or surrounded myself with a row of stakes set upright in the ground, either from one tree to another, or so as no wild creature could come at me without waking me.
paragraphs.cn: 这趟旅行我每天径直走的路程从不超过两英里,大约就这么点;但我来来回回兜了许多圈子,看看能有什么发现,以至走到我决定过夜的地方时已经够累的了;然后我要么在树上歇息,要么在身边一圈插上直立的木桩,或从这棵树连到那棵树,好让任何野兽不惊醒我就无法近身。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I came to the sea-shore, I was surprised to see that I had taken up my lot on the worst side of the island, for here, indeed, the shore was covered with innumerable turtles, whereas on the other side I had found but three in a year and a half.
paragraphs.cn: 一到海边,我便吃惊地发现自己竟落脚在了岛上最糟的一侧,因为这边海岸上爬满了数不清的海龟,而在我住的那边,一年半里我才碰到过三只。

paragraphs.en: Here was also an infinite number of fowls of many kinds, some which I had seen, and some which I had not seen before, and many of them very good meat, but such as I knew not the names of, except those called penguins.
paragraphs.cn: 这里还有多得数不清的各种飞禽,有些我见过,有些我从前没见过,其中许多肉质极好,但除了那种叫企鹅的,我叫不上它们的名字。

paragraphs.en: I could have shot as many as I pleased, but was very sparing of my powder and shot, and therefore had more mind to kill a she-goat if I could, which I could better feed on; and though there were many goats here, more than on my side the island, yet it was with much more difficulty that I could come near them, the country being flat and even, and they saw me much sooner than when I was on the hills.
paragraphs.cn: 我本可以爱打多少就打多少,但我很珍惜火药和铅弹,所以更想打一只母山羊,那样我更好养活;这里山羊虽多,比我那边的岛上还多,可我要靠近它们却难得多,因为这一带地势平坦开阔,它们老远就看见我,不像我在山上时那样。

paragraphs.en: I confess this side of the country was much pleasanter than mine; but yet I had not the least inclination to remove, for as I was fixed in my habitation it became natural to me, and I seemed all the while I was here to be as it were upon a journey, and from home.
paragraphs.cn: 我承认岛这一侧比我那边可爱得多;可我却丝毫不想搬过来,因为我在自己那住处安顿惯了,已经觉得那才自然,而在这边逗留的整段时间里,我总仿佛是在旅途中、离家在外似的。

paragraphs.en: However, I travelled along the shore of the sea towards the east, I suppose about twelve miles, and then setting up a great pole upon the shore for a mark, I concluded I would go home again, and that the next journey I took should be on the other side of the island east from my dwelling, and so round till I came to my post again.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我还是沿着海岸朝东走去,大约走了十二英里,然后在岸上竖起一根大木杆当记号,便打定主意要回家去,并且我下次出行要走岛的另一侧、从我住处往东,一路绕过来,直到再回到我这根木杆跟前。

paragraphs.en: I took another way to come back than that I went, thinking I could easily keep all the island so much in my view that I could not miss finding my first dwelling by viewing the country; but I found myself mistaken, for being come about two or three miles, I found myself descended into a very large valley, but so surrounded with hills, and those hills covered with wood, that I could not see which was my way by any direction but that of the sun, nor even then, unless I knew very well the position of the sun at that time of the day.
paragraphs.cn: 回去时我另择了一条路,不走来时的路,心想只要把整座岛尽收眼底,靠观望地形准能找回我最初的住处;可结果我错了,因为走了大约两三英里,我发现自己下到了一处极大的山谷,四面全被山围住,山上又都覆着树林,除了看太阳,我无法辨认哪条是我该走的路,而即便看太阳,也得我很清楚那时辰太阳的方位才行。

paragraphs.en: It happened, to my further misfortune, that the weather proved hazy for three or four days while I was in the valley, and not being able to see the sun, I wandered about very uncomfortably, and at last was obliged to find the seaside, look for my post, and come back the same way I went: and then, by easy journeys, I turned homeward, the weather being exceeding hot, and my gun, ammunition, hatchet, and other things very heavy.
paragraphs.cn: 更倒霉的是,我待在山谷里的那三四天偏偏天色阴霾,看不见太阳,我很不自在地四处乱转,最后只得先找到海边,寻着我那根木杆,再照来时的原路返回;然后我一程一程慢慢地折向家去,天热得厉害,而我的枪、弹药、小斧和其他东西又都很沉。

paragraphs.en: In this journey my dog surprised a young kid, and seized upon it; and I, running in to take hold of it, caught it, and saved it alive from the dog.
paragraphs.cn: 这趟路上我的狗惊起一只小山羊,一口咬住;我赶紧跑过去抓,把它抓住了,从狗嘴里救下这条活命。

paragraphs.en: I had a great mind to bring it home if I could, for I had often been musing whether it might not be possible to get a kid or two, and so raise a breed of tame goats, which might supply me when my powder and shot should be all spent.
paragraphs.cn: 我很想能把它带回家,因为我常在琢磨,是不是有可能弄到一两只小羊,好养出一群驯羊,等我火药铅弹全用光时,它们可以接济我。

paragraphs.en: I made a collar for this little creature, and with a string, which I made of some rope-yarn, which I always carried about me, I led him along, though with some difficulty, till I came to my bower, and there I enclosed him and left him, for I was very impatient to be at home, from whence I had been absent above a month.
paragraphs.cn: 我给这小东西做了个项圈,又用我随身常带的一些绳纱搓成一根绳子,费了点劲牵着它,直走到我的凉棚,便把它圈在那里留下,因为我已归心似箭——我离家一个多月了。

paragraphs.en: I cannot express what a satisfaction it was to me to come into my old hutch, and lie down in my hammock-bed.
paragraphs.cn: 回到我那老窝、躺进我的吊床上时,那份满足我简直说不出来。

paragraphs.en: This little wandering journey, without settled place of abode, had been so unpleasant to me, that my own house, as I called it to myself, was a perfect settlement to me compared to that; and it rendered everything about me so comfortable, that I resolved I would never go a great way from it again while it should be my lot to stay on the island.
paragraphs.cn: 这趟没有固定落脚处的漂泊旅行,让我实在难受,相比之下,我心里管它叫“自己家”的那处住所,简直就是个十全十美的安身之地了;这使我周围的一切都显得那么舒适,以至我下定决心:只要我命该留在这岛上,就再也不离它远行了。

paragraphs.en: I reposed myself here a week, to rest and regale myself after my long journey; during which most of the time was taken up in the weighty affair of making a cage for my Poll, who began now to be a mere domestic, and to be well acquainted with me.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里歇了一个礼拜,好在长途跋涉后休整、犒劳自己一番;这期间大半工夫都花在了一桩要紧事上——给我的鹦鹉波尔做个笼子,它这会儿已经俨然成了家养的宠物,跟我很熟了。

paragraphs.en: Then I began to think of the poor kid which I had penned in within my little circle, and resolved to go and fetch it home, or give it some food; accordingly I went, and found it where I left it, for indeed it could not get out, but was almost starved for want of food.
paragraphs.cn: 然后我想起了被我圈在小围栏里的那只可怜小羊,决定去把它牵回家,或者给它点吃的;于是我去了,在原地找到了它,因为它确实出不来,却已因没东西吃而几乎饿死了。

paragraphs.en: I went and cut boughs of trees, and branches of such shrubs as I could find, and threw it over, and having fed it, I tied it as I did before, to lead it away; but it was so tame with being hungry, that I had no need to have tied it, for it followed me like a dog: and as I continually fed it, the creature became so loving, so gentle, and so fond, that it became from that time one of my domestics also, and would never leave me afterwards.
paragraphs.cn: 我去砍了些树枝,还有我能找到的灌木枝条,扔进围栏给它吃;喂过之后,我像先前一样把它拴上牵走;可它饿得这么温顺,其实我用不着拴,因为它像狗一样跟着我:而我又不断喂它,这小东西便变得又亲昵、又温柔、又黏人,从那时起也成了我的一个家养伙伴,此后再也不肯离开我了。

paragraphs.en: The rainy season of the autumnal equinox was now come, and I kept the 30th of September in the same solemn manner as before, being the anniversary of my landing on the island, having now been there two years, and no more prospect of being delivered than the first day I came there, I spent the whole day in humble and thankful acknowledgments of the many wonderful mercies which my solitary condition was attended with, and without which it might have been infinitely more miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 秋分时节的雨季这时到了,我像从前一样庄重地过了九月三十日这个日子——这是我登上此岛的周年纪念,如今我在这里已满两年,获救的指望却和我初来那天一样渺茫;我整整一天都在谦卑而感恩地承认:我这孤独的处境竟蒙受了如此众多奇妙的恩慈,若没有这些恩慈,处境本会悲惨无数倍。

paragraphs.en: I gave humble and hearty thanks that God had been pleased to discover to me that it was possible I might be more happy in this solitary condition than I should have been in the liberty of society, and in all the pleasures of the world; that He could fully make up to me the deficiencies of my solitary state, and the want of human society, by His presence and the communications of His grace to my soul; supporting, comforting, and encouraging me to depend upon His providence here, and hope for His eternal presence hereafter.
paragraphs.cn: 我谦卑而由衷地感恩:上帝乐意让我明白,我在这孤独处境中,或许比我置身社会的自由、置身世上一切欢乐之中还要幸福;上帝能以祂的同在、以祂恩典对我灵魂的交通,来完全弥补我孤独境况的欠缺和缺少人间往来的憾恨;支撑我、安慰我、鼓励我在此处依靠祂的眷顾,并盼望日后祂永恒的同在。

paragraphs.en: It was now that I began sensibly to feel how much more happy this life I now led was, with all its miserable circumstances, than the wicked, cursed, abominable life I led all the past part of my days; and now I changed both my sorrows and my joys; my very desires altered, my affections changed their gusts, and my delights were perfectly new from what they were at my first coming, or, indeed, for the two years past.
paragraphs.cn: 正是从这时起,我开始真切地感到:我如今所过的这种生活,纵有种种悲苦境遇,却比我从前那段邪恶、可诅咒、可憎的日子幸福得多;如今我的忧愁和喜乐都变了样;我的种种欲望改了向,我的情感换了口味,我的乐趣与初到时、甚或与过去这两年相比,都焕然一新。

paragraphs.en: Before, as I walked about, either on my hunting or for viewing the country, the anguish of my soul at my condition would break out upon me on a sudden, and my very heart would die within me, to think of the woods, the mountains, the deserts I was in, and how I was a prisoner, locked up with the eternal bars and bolts of the ocean, in an uninhabited wilderness, without redemption.
paragraphs.cn: 从前,我无论是外出打猎还是察看地势,一想到自己的处境,灵魂的痛楚就会突然向我袭来,我的心几乎在胸中死去——想到我身处的这些树林、山峦、荒野,想到我如何成了囚徒,被大洋那永恒的门闩铁锁锁在一片无人的荒野里,无从解脱。

paragraphs.en: In the midst of the greatest composure of my mind, this would break out upon me like a storm, and make me wring my hands and weep like a child.
