paragraphs.cn: 在我心境最为平静的当口,这痛楚也会像一场风暴般向我袭来,叫我绞着双手、像孩子似的哭泣。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes it would take me in the middle of my work, and I would immediately sit down and sigh, and look upon the ground for an hour or two together; and this was still worse to me, for if I could burst out into tears, or vent myself by words, it would go off, and the grief, having exhausted itself, would abate.
paragraphs.cn: 有时它会在我干活干到一半时攫住我,我便立刻坐下叹气,一连一两个钟头呆望着地面;这对我更糟,因为倘若我能痛哭一场,或用言语发泄出来,它反倒会过去,悲伤耗尽了自己,也就减轻了。

paragraphs.en: But now I began to exercise myself with new thoughts: I daily read the word of God, and applied all the comforts of it to my present state.
paragraphs.cn: 但如今我开始用新的念头来磨砺自己:我每天诵读上帝的话语,把其中一切安慰都应用到我眼下的境况上。

paragraphs.en: One morning, being very sad, I opened the Bible upon these words, “I will never, never leave thee, nor forsake thee.”
paragraphs.cn: 一天早晨,我心里非常忧伤,翻开《圣经》,恰好翻到这句话:“我永不,永不撇下你,也不丢弃你。”

paragraphs.en: Immediately it occurred that these words were to me; why else should they be directed in such a manner, just at the moment when I was mourning over my condition, as one forsaken of God and man?
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻想到,这话是对我说的;不然,为何偏偏在我为自己的处境哀伤、自觉被上帝和世人所弃的那一刻,这话会这样指向我呢?

paragraphs.en: “Well, then,” said I, “if God does not forsake me, of what ill consequence can it be, or what matters it, though the world should all forsake me, seeing on the other hand, if I had all the world, and should lose the favour and blessing of God, there would be no comparison in the loss?”
paragraphs.cn: “那么好吧,”我说,“若上帝不撇弃我,纵使全世界都撇弃我,又能有什么坏处,又打什么紧呢?反过来看,倘若我拥有全世界,却失去了上帝的恩宠与祝福,那损失又岂能相提并论?”

paragraphs.en: From this moment I began to conclude in my mind that it was possible for me to be more happy in this forsaken, solitary condition than it was probable I should ever have been in any other particular state in the world; and with this thought I was going to give thanks to God for bringing me to this place.
paragraphs.cn: 从这一刻起,我心里开始断定:我在这被遗弃的孤独处境中,或许比我置身世上任何别的境地都更可能幸福;想到这里,我正要为上帝把我带到此地而感恩。

paragraphs.en: I know not what it was, but something shocked my mind at that thought, and I durst not speak the words.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知那是什么,但那念头忽然叫我心里一震,我竟不敢把话说出口。

paragraphs.en: “How canst thou become such a hypocrite,” said I, even audibly, “to pretend to be thankful for a condition which, however thou mayest endeavour to be contented with, thou wouldst rather pray heartily to be delivered from?”
paragraphs.cn: “你怎能这般虚伪,”我甚至出声说道,“竟假装为一种境况感恩——尽管你尽力想安于其中,内心却宁愿恳切祈求脱离它?”

paragraphs.en: So I stopped there; but though I could not say I thanked God for being there, yet I sincerely gave thanks to God for opening my eyes, by whatever afflicting providences, to see the former condition of my life, and to mourn for my wickedness, and repent.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我就此打住;可我虽说不上为身在此地而感谢上帝,却真心为上帝借着种种苦难的安排开了我的眼而感恩——让我看清自己前半生的境况,为自己的邪恶哀痛并悔改。

paragraphs.en: I never opened the Bible, or shut it, but my very soul within me blessed God for directing my friend in England, without any order of mine, to pack it up among my goods, and for assisting me afterwards to save it out of the wreck of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我每回翻开《圣经》或合上它,我心底的灵魂都要称颂上帝:是祂在英国指点我那位朋友——并没有我的吩咐——把它收进我的行李,后来又助我把它从沉船中抢救出来。

paragraphs.en: Thus, and in this disposition of mind, I began my third year; and though I have not given the reader the trouble of so particular an account of my works this year as the first, yet in general it may be observed that I was very seldom idle, but having regularly divided my time according to the several daily employments that were before me, such as: first, my duty to God, and the reading the Scriptures, which I constantly set apart some time for thrice every day; secondly, the going abroad with my gun for food, which generally took me up three hours in every morning, when it did not rain; thirdly, the ordering, cutting, preserving, and cooking what I had killed or caught for my supply; these took up great part of the day.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,怀着这样的心境,我开始了我在岛上的第三年;虽说我不像记第一年那样、拿这一年活计的详情来烦扰读者,但大体上可以看出:我很少有闲着的时候,而是把时间按眼前几样每日的营生有规律地分配开来,比如:第一,对上帝的本分,以及诵读《圣经》,我每天固定拨出三段时间来做;第二,带着枪外出觅食,不下雨时,这每天早上一般要占去我三个钟头;第三,把打到或捉到的猎物加以处置、切割、腌藏和烹煮以供食用;这些占去了一天的大部分。

paragraphs.en: Also, it is to be considered, that in the middle of the day, when the sun was in the zenith, the violence of the heat was too great to stir out; so that about four hours in the evening was all the time I could be supposed to work in, with this exception, that sometimes I changed my hours of hunting and working, and went to work in the morning, and abroad with my gun in the afternoon.
paragraphs.cn: 还得想到,正午时分太阳当顶,酷热难当,不宜外出走动;所以我能干活的时间,大约只有傍晚那四个钟头,例外是有时我把打猎和干活的时辰对调,上午干活,下午带枪外出。

paragraphs.en: To this short time allowed for labour I desire may be added the exceeding laboriousness of my work; the many hours which, for want of tools, want of help, and want of skill, everything I did took up out of my time.
paragraphs.cn: 在这点有限的劳作时间之外,还得加上我那活计的格外费力:由于缺工具、缺帮手、缺手艺,我做的每一样都要占去我许多钟头。

paragraphs.en: For example, I was full two and forty days in making a board for a long shelf, which I wanted in my cave; whereas, two sawyers, with their tools and a saw-pit, would have cut six of them out of the same tree in half a day.
paragraphs.cn: 举个例子,我整整花了四十二天才做出一块长搁板,我那洞里正缺它;而两个锯木工带着工具和一个锯坑,半天工夫就能从同一棵树上锯出六块来。

paragraphs.en: My case was this: it was to be a large tree which was to be cut down, because my board was to be a broad one.
paragraphs.cn: 我的情形是这样:得先砍倒一棵大树,因为我的板子要做得宽。

paragraphs.en: This tree I was three days in cutting down, and two more cutting off the boughs, and reducing it to a log or piece of timber.
paragraphs.cn: 砍倒这棵树我花了三天,又花了两天砍去枝桠、把它削成一根圆木或木料。

paragraphs.en: With inexpressible hacking and hewing I reduced both the sides of it into chips till it began to be light enough to move; then I turned it, and made one side of it smooth and flat as a board from end to end; then, turning that side downward, cut the other side til I brought the plank to be about three inches thick, and smooth on both sides.
paragraphs.cn: 我又是砍又是劈,费尽难以言表的力气,把它两侧都削成木片,直到它轻得能挪动为止;然后我把它翻过来,把一面从头到尾削得像木板一样光滑平整;再把这面朝下,削另一面,直到把这块板削到约莫三英寸厚、两面都光滑为止。

paragraphs.en: Any one may judge the labour of my hands in such a piece of work; but labour and patience carried me through that, and many other things.
paragraphs.cn: 谁都能掂量出干这么一件活我这双手要费多大力气;但凭着劳作和耐心,我熬过了这件事,也熬过了别的许多事。

paragraphs.en: I only observe this in particular, to show the reason why so much of my time went away with so little work—viz. that what might be a little to be done with help and tools, was a vast labour and required a prodigious time to do alone, and by hand.
paragraphs.cn: 我特地记下这一件,只为说明为何我耗去那么多时间,干的活却那么少——就是说:有帮手有工具本是小事一桩的活,单靠一双手独力去做,却成了巨大的劳役,要花去大得惊人的时间。

paragraphs.en: But notwithstanding this, with patience and labour I got through everything that my circumstances made necessary to me to do, as will appear by what follows.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此,凭着耐心和劳作,凡是我的处境要我非做不可的事,我都一一做成了,后文自会见分晓。

paragraphs.en: I was now, in the months of November and December, expecting my crop of barley and rice.
paragraphs.cn: 这时正当十一、十二月,我在等着大麦和稻子的收成。

paragraphs.en: The ground I had manured and dug up for them was not great; for, as I observed, my seed of each was not above the quantity of half a peck, for I had lost one whole crop by sowing in the dry season.
paragraphs.cn: 我为它们施肥翻掘的地并不大;因为我说过,我两样种子加起来也不过半配克,只因在旱季播种,我已损失了整整一茬收成。

paragraphs.en: But now my crop promised very well, when on a sudden I found I was in danger of losing it all again by enemies of several sorts, which it was scarcely possible to keep from it; as, first, the goats, and wild creatures which I called hares, who, tasting the sweetness of the blade, lay in it night and day, as soon as it came up, and eat it so close, that it could get no time to shoot up into stalk.
paragraphs.cn: 但如今我这茬庄稼长势喜人,不料我突然发觉,自己又有可能被好几种敌害弄得颗粒无收,而这些敌害几乎没法防住;首先是山羊,还有我称作野兔的野物,它们一尝到嫩苗的甜头,苗一冒出来就日夜卧在里头,啃得那么贴地,叫苗没工夫往上抽秆。

paragraphs.en: This I saw no remedy for but by making an enclosure about it with a hedge; which I did with a great deal of toil, and the more, because it required speed.
paragraphs.cn: 对此我想不出别的法子,只有围着它扎一道篱笆把它圈起来;我费了好大的力气才办成,尤其因为这事必须赶紧。

paragraphs.en: However, as my arable land was but small, suited to my crop, I got it totally well fenced in about three weeks’ time; and shooting some of the creatures in the daytime, I set my dog to guard it in the night, tying him up to a stake at the gate, where he would stand and bark all night long; so in a little time the enemies forsook the place, and the corn grew very strong and well, and began to ripen apace.
paragraphs.cn: 好在我那片耕地不大,和我的收成相称,大约三个礼拜就把它整个围严实了;白天我打死几只野物,夜里则派我的狗守着,把它拴在门口一根桩子上,它便整夜站在那儿吠叫;没多久那些敌害便弃了这地方,禾苗长得又壮又好,开始很快地成熟起来。

paragraphs.en: But as the beasts ruined me before, while my corn was in the blade, so the birds were as likely to ruin me now, when it was in the ear; for, going along by the place to see how it throve, I saw my little crop surrounded with fowls, of I know not how many sorts, who stood, as it were, watching till I should be gone.
paragraphs.cn: 但正如先前禾苗还在叶期时野兽把我毁了一样,如今谷穗抽出时,飞鸟又眼看要毁了我;因为我打那地方路过、去看长势时,只见我那小片庄稼被飞禽团团围住,也不知有多少种,它们仿佛在守着,只等我一走开。

paragraphs.en: I immediately let fly among them, for I always had my gun with me.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻朝它们开火,因为我总是随身带枪。

paragraphs.en: I had no sooner shot, but there rose up a little cloud of fowls, which I had not seen at all, from among the corn itself.
paragraphs.cn: 枪一响,竟从谷子当中腾起一小片我先前压根没看见的飞鸟。

paragraphs.en: This touched me sensibly, for I foresaw that in a few days they would devour all my hopes; that I should be starved, and never be able to raise a crop at all; and what to do I could not tell; however, I resolved not to lose my corn, if possible, though I should watch it night and day.
paragraphs.cn: 这真真切切地触痛了我,因为我预见到,不出几天它们就会把我的全部指望吞个精光;我会挨饿,再也种不出一茬庄稼来;而该怎么办我又拿不定主意;不过我打定主意:只要有可能,哪怕日夜守着,也不能丢了我的谷子。

paragraphs.en: In the first place, I went among it to see what damage was already done, and found they had spoiled a good deal of it; but that as it was yet too green for them, the loss was not so great but that the remainder was likely to be a good crop if it could be saved.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我走进地里查看已经遭了多少损失,发现它们已糟蹋了不少;但因谷子对它们来说还太青,损失倒还不算大,剩下的若能保住,仍有望是个好收成。

paragraphs.en: I stayed by it to load my gun, and then coming away, I could easily see the thieves sitting upon all the trees about me, as if they only waited till I was gone away, and the event proved it to be so; for as I walked off, as if I was gone, I was no sooner out of their sight than they dropped down one by one into the corn again.
paragraphs.cn: 我守在地边给枪装弹,然后一走开,就轻易看见那些贼子停在我周围所有的树上,仿佛只等我离去;结果证明果真如此;因为我一走开、装作已经走了,才一走出它们的视线,它们就一只接一只地又落回谷子里去了。

paragraphs.en: I was so provoked, that I could not have patience to stay till more came on, knowing that every grain that they ate now was, as it might be said, a peck-loaf to me in the consequence; but coming up to the hedge, I fired again, and killed three of them.
paragraphs.cn: 我被激得实在没耐性再等更多的飞来,明知它们此刻每吃一粒,往后于我便如同吃掉了一大块面包;于是我走到篱笆跟前,又开了一枪,打死了它们中的三只。

paragraphs.en: This was what I wished for; so I took them up, and served them as we serve notorious thieves in England—hanged them in chains, for a terror to others.
paragraphs.cn: 这正是我求之不得的;于是我把它们拾起来,照我们在英国处置臭名昭著的贼子那样对付它们——把它们上了铁链吊起来示众,以儆效尤。

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to imagine that this should have such an effect as it had, for the fowls would not only not come at the corn, but, in short, they forsook all that part of the island, and I could never see a bird near the place as long as my scarecrows hung there.
paragraphs.cn: 谁也想不到这法子竟有那么大的效验,因为那些飞禽不但不再飞近谷子,简直索性弃了岛上那整片地方;只要我的稻草人还挂在那儿,我在附近就再也见不到一只鸟。

paragraphs.en: This I was very glad of, you may be sure, and about the latter end of December, which was our second harvest of the year, I reaped my corn.
paragraphs.cn: 这一点你尽可以想见,我是多么高兴;大约到了十二月末,也就是我这一年的第二次收获,我把庄稼收割了。

paragraphs.en: I was sadly put to it for a scythe or sickle to cut it down, and all I could do was to make one, as well as I could, out of one of the broadswords, or cutlasses, which I saved among the arms out of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 为了弄一把镰刀来割它,我实在犯了愁,能做的只是尽力用我从船上武器中抢救下来的一把阔剑或短弯刀,勉强打制出一把来。

paragraphs.en: However, as my first crop was but small, I had no great difficulty to cut it down; in short, I reaped it in my way, for I cut nothing off but the ears, and carried it away in a great basket which I had made, and so rubbed it out with my hands; and at the end of all my harvesting, I found that out of my half-peck of seed I had near two bushels of rice, and about two bushels and a half of barley; that is to say, by my guess, for I had no measure at that time.
paragraphs.cn: 好在我头一茬庄稼不多,割起来没多大难处;总之,我照自己的法子把它收了,因为我只割穗子,把穗子装进我做的一只大篮子里搬走,再用手把谷粒搓出来;收割完毕后我发现,半配克的种子竟长出了将近两蒲式耳稻子和约莫两蒲式耳半大麦;也就是说,凭我估摸,因为那时我没有量器。

paragraphs.en: However, this was a great encouragement to me, and I foresaw that, in time, it would please God to supply me with bread.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这大大鼓舞了我,我预见到,假以时日,上帝会乐意供我以面包。

paragraphs.en: And yet here I was perplexed again, for I neither knew how to grind or make meal of my corn, or indeed how to clean it and part it; nor, if made into meal, how to make bread of it; and if how to make it, yet I knew not how to bake it.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我在这里又犯了难,因为我既不懂怎样把谷子磨碎、做成面粉,其实也不懂怎样把它舂净、簸分;就算磨成了面粉,又不懂怎样把它做成面包;就算懂得怎样做,我也不懂怎样烤它。

paragraphs.en: These things being added to my desire of having a good quantity for store, and to secure a constant supply, I resolved not to taste any of this crop but to preserve it all for seed against the next season; and in the meantime to employ all my study and hours of working to accomplish this great work of providing myself with corn and bread.
paragraphs.cn: 这些难处,再加上我想多备些存粮、以保证接济不断的心愿,使我下决心:这一茬一粒也不尝,全留作下一季的种子;这期间则把我全副心思和干活的时辰都用来完成这桩大事——给自己置办谷子和面包。

paragraphs.en: It might be truly said, that now I worked for my bread.
paragraphs.cn: 可以真真切切地说,如今我是在为自己的面包而劳作了。

paragraphs.en: I believe few people have thought much upon the strange multitude of little things necessary in the providing, producing, curing, dressing, making, and finishing this one article of bread.
paragraphs.cn: 我相信,很少有人认真想过:在供应、生产、加工、料理、制作并最终成就面包这一样东西时,需要多少五花八门的琐碎事。

paragraphs.en: I, that was reduced to a mere state of nature, found this to my daily discouragement; and was made more sensible of it every hour, even after I had got the first handful of seed-corn, which, as I have said, came up unexpectedly, and indeed to a surprise.
paragraphs.cn: 我这个沦落到纯然原始状态的人,天天为此而灰心;而且越发时时刻刻体会到这一点,哪怕在我已经得着那第一把种谷之后——我说过,那谷子出乎意料地冒了出来,着实叫我吃了一惊。

paragraphs.en: First, I had no plough to turn up the earth—no spade or shovel to dig it.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我没有犁来翻土——没有锹或铲来挖它。

paragraphs.en: Well, this I conquered by making me a wooden spade, as I observed before; but this did my work but in a wooden manner; and though it cost me a great many days to make it, yet, for want of iron, it not only wore out soon, but made my work the harder, and made it be performed much worse.
paragraphs.cn: 好吧,这个难处我靠自己做了一把木锹克服了,前面提到过;可这把木锹干起活来也只是“木头把式”;它虽花了我许多天才做成,却因缺铁,不但很快就磨坏了,还使我的活更吃力,干出来也差得多。

paragraphs.en: However, this I bore with, and was content to work it out with patience, and bear with the badness of the performance.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这我也忍了,甘心凭耐心把活做完,将就着那蹩脚的成效。

paragraphs.en: When the corn was sown, I had no harrow, but was forced to go over it myself, and drag a great heavy bough of a tree over it, to scratch it, as it may be called, rather than rake or harrow it.
paragraphs.cn: 谷种撒下后,我没有耙,只得亲自在地里走一遍,拖着一根又大又重的树枝在上头蹚,权当把土抓松——只能叫抓,谈不上耙或耱。

paragraphs.en: When it was growing, and grown, I have observed already how many things I wanted to fence it, secure it, mow or reap it, cure and carry it home, thrash, part it from the chaff, and save it.
paragraphs.cn: 谷子生长、长成之后,我前面已经说过,我缺多少东西来给它围篱、护守、刈割或收获、加工并搬运回家、脱粒、扬去糠秕、把它存起来。

paragraphs.en: Then I wanted a mill to grind it, sieves to dress it, yeast and salt to make it into bread, and an oven to bake it; but all these things I did without, as shall be observed; and yet the corn was an inestimable comfort and advantage to me too.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我又缺一台磨来磨它,缺筛子来簸它,缺酵母和盐来把它做成面包,缺炉子来烤它;可这一切东西我都是将就着没有它们过来的,后文自会说到;然而这谷子于我也仍是一种无价的慰藉和益处。

paragraphs.en: All this, as I said, made everything laborious and tedious to me; but that there was no help for.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切,如我所说,使我样样活计都又费力又乏味;可这也是没办法的事。

paragraphs.en: Neither was my time so much loss to me, because, as I had divided it, a certain part of it was every day appointed to these works; and as I had resolved to use none of the corn for bread till I had a greater quantity by me, I had the next six months to apply myself wholly, by labour and invention, to furnish myself with utensils proper for the performing all the operations necessary for making the corn, when I had it, fit for my use.
paragraphs.cn: 我的时间倒也没白白损失多少,因为如我所分配的,每天都拨出一定的一段专用于这些活计;而既然我已决意在存粮更多之前一粒也不用来做面包,我便有接下来的六个月专心一意地凭劳作和巧思去给自己置办各样合用的器具,以便日后有了谷子时,能完成把它加工到可供我食用所必需的一切工序。

paragraphs.en: But first I was to prepare more land, for I had now seed enough to sow above an acre of ground.
paragraphs.cn: 但我首先得开垦更多土地,因为如今我的种子已够播种一英亩多的地了。

paragraphs.en: Before I did this, I had a week’s work at least to make me a spade, which, when it was done, was but a sorry one indeed, and very heavy, and required double labour to work with it.
paragraphs.cn: 在动手之前,我至少花了一个星期做了一把铲子;做好后,它实在只能算个蹩脚货,又特别沉,用起来得费上加倍的力气。

paragraphs.en: However, I got through that, and sowed my seed in two large flat pieces of ground, as near my house as I could find them to my mind, and fenced them in with a good hedge, the stakes of which were all cut off that wood which I had set before, and knew it would grow; so that, in a year’s time, I knew I should have a quick or living hedge, that would want but little repair.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我还是熬了过去,把种子播在两大块平坦的地里,尽量挑离我住处近、又合我心意的地方,四周用一道结实的篱笆围了起来;篱笆的桩子全是从我先前栽下、知道能活的那种树上砍来的,所以我知道,一年之后我就会有一道很快长成的活篱笆,几乎不用怎么修补。

paragraphs.en: This work did not take me up less than three months, because a great part of that time was the wet season, when I could not go abroad.
paragraphs.cn: 这项活儿花了我不下三个月,因为其中大半时间正逢雨季,我没法出门。

paragraphs.en: Within-doors, that is when it rained and I could not go out, I found employment in the following occupations—always observing, that all the while I was at work I diverted myself with talking to my parrot, and teaching him to speak; and I quickly taught him to know his own name, and at last to speak it out pretty loud, “Poll,” which was the first word I ever heard spoken in the island by any mouth but my own.
paragraphs.cn: 在屋里的时候，也就是下雨出不了门时，我用下面这些事情打发日子——要说明的是，我干活的整个过程中都靠跟我的鹦鹉说话、教它讲话来消遣;我很快就教会了它认得自己的名字,最后还能相当响亮地叫出“波尔”来,这是我在岛上除了自己以外,头一回从别的嘴里听到的话。

paragraphs.en: This, therefore, was not my work, but an assistance to my work; for now, as I said, I had a great employment upon my hands, as follows: I had long studied to make, by some means or other, some earthen vessels, which, indeed, I wanted sorely, but knew not where to come at them.
paragraphs.cn: 所以这并不是我的正经活儿,只是我干活时的一点消遣;因为如今,正如我说过的,我手头有件大事要办,是这样的:我早就琢磨着想法子做几件陶器,我实在太需要它们了,却不知道从哪儿弄来。

paragraphs.en: However, considering the heat of the climate, I did not doubt but if I could find out any clay, I might make some pots that might, being dried in the sun, be hard enough and strong enough to bear handling, and to hold anything that was dry, and required to be kept so; and as this was necessary in the preparing corn, meal, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,考虑到这里气候炎热,我并不怀疑:只要能找到黏土,我就能做出几个罐子来,在太阳下晒干后,应该会够硬够结实,经得起拿放,能盛放任何干燥、需要保持干燥的东西;而这在处理谷物、面粉之类时正是必需的——

paragraphs.en: , which was the thing I was doing, I resolved to make some as large as I could, and fit only to stand like jars, to hold what should be put into them.
paragraphs.cn: 而处理谷物正是我眼下在做的事,所以我决定尽量做几个大的,做成能像坛子一样立着的样子,好盛放要放进去的东西。

paragraphs.en: It would make the reader pity me, or rather laugh at me, to tell how many awkward ways I took to raise this paste; what odd, misshapen, ugly things I made; how many of them fell in and how many fell out, the clay not being stiff enough to bear its own weight; how many cracked by the over-violent heat of the sun, being set out too hastily; and how many fell in pieces with only removing, as well before as after they were dried; and, in a word, how, after having laboured hard to find the clay—to dig it, to temper it, to bring it home, and work it—I could not make above two large earthen ugly things (I cannot call them jars) in about two months’ labour.
paragraphs.cn: 要说我用了多少笨拙的法子来和这团泥;做出多少稀奇古怪、歪歪扭扭、丑陋不堪的东西;有多少塌了进去、又有多少瘫了下来,因为泥不够硬,撑不住自己的分量;有多少因为晒得太急,被烈日烤裂了;又有多少一挪动就散成了碎片,不论晒干前还是晒干后都是如此;总之,在费尽力气找到黏土——把它挖出来、和好、搬回家、加工之后,我花了大约两个月的功夫,却做不出两件以上又大又丑的陶器(我实在不能管它们叫坛子)——这要是说出来,准会让读者可怜我,或者不如说,笑话我。

paragraphs.en: However, as the sun baked these two very dry and hard, I lifted them very gently up, and set them down again in two great wicker baskets, which I had made on purpose for them, that they might not break; and as between the pot and the basket there was a little room to spare, I stuffed it full of the rice and barley straw; and these two pots being to stand always dry I thought would hold my dry corn, and perhaps the meal, when the corn was bruised.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,既然太阳把这两件东西烤得又干又硬,我便非常小心地把它们提起来,重新放进两个我专门为它们编的大柳条筐里,免得碰破;罐子和筐之间还留着一点空隙,我就塞满了稻草和大麦秸;这两个罐子既然要一直干着放,我想应该能盛我的干谷物,或许谷子磨碎后的面粉也能盛。

paragraphs.en: Though I miscarried so much in my design for large pots, yet I made several smaller things with better success; such as little round pots, flat dishes, pitchers, and pipkins, and any things my hand turned to; and the heat of the sun baked them quite hard.
paragraphs.cn: 虽然我做大罐子的打算大多失败了,可我做了几件小些的东西却顺手得多,比如小圆罐、扁盘、水壶、小炖锅,凡是我手头能做的都做了;太阳的热力把它们全烤得很硬。

paragraphs.en: But all this would not answer my end, which was to get an earthen pot to hold what was liquid, and bear the fire, which none of these could do.
paragraphs.cn: 但这一切都达不到我的目的,我要的是一个能盛液体、又经得住火烧的陶罐,而这些东西一个也做不到。

paragraphs.en: It happened after some time, making a pretty large fire for cooking my meat, when I went to put it out after I had done with it, I found a broken piece of one of my earthenware vessels in the fire, burnt as hard as a stone, and red as a tile.
paragraphs.cn: 过了些时候,有一次我生了一大堆火来煮肉,用完后去灭火时,发现火里有一块我打碎的陶器碎片,烧得像石头一样硬,像瓦一样红。

paragraphs.en: I was agreeably surprised to see it, and said to myself, that certainly they might be made to burn whole, if they would burn broken.
paragraphs.cn: 我看了又惊又喜,对自己说:碎的都能烧成这样,那整个的当然也一定能烧成。

paragraphs.en: This set me to study how to order my fire, so as to make it burn some pots.
paragraphs.cn: 这促使我开始琢磨怎样安排火候,好把几个罐子烧成。

paragraphs.en: I had no notion of a kiln, such as the potters burn in, or of glazing them with lead, though I had some lead to do it with; but I placed three large pipkins and two or three pots in a pile, one upon another, and placed my firewood all round it, with a great heap of embers under them.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有陶工烧陶用的那种窑的概念,也不懂怎样用铅给它们上釉——尽管我手头有点铅可以用;但我把三个大炖锅和两三个罐子摞成一堆,一个叠一个,又把柴火全堆在四周,底下垫上一大堆炭火。

paragraphs.en: I plied the fire with fresh fuel round the outside and upon the top, till I saw the pots in the inside red-hot quite through, and observed that they did not crack at all.
paragraphs.cn: 我在外围和顶上不断添新柴,直到看见里面的罐子通红,烧透了,而且发现它们一点也没裂。

paragraphs.en: When I saw them clear red, I let them stand in that heat about five or six hours, till I found one of them, though it did not crack, did melt or run; for the sand which was mixed with the clay melted by the violence of the heat, and would have run into glass if I had gone on; so I slacked my fire gradually till the pots began to abate of the red colour; and watching them all night, that I might not let the fire abate too fast, in the morning I had three very good (I will not say handsome) pipkins, and two other earthen pots, as hard burnt as could be desired, and one of them perfectly glazed with the running of the sand.
paragraphs.cn: 等我看到它们通体红透,便让它们在那样的高温里放了大约五六个钟头,后来发现其中一个虽然没裂,却开始熔化流淌了;原来是和在黏土里的沙子被猛火熔化了,要是我再烧下去,准会熔成玻璃;于是我便慢慢把火减弱,直到罐子的红色渐渐退去;我守了它们一整夜,免得火退得太快,到早晨我便得了三个很好的(我不敢说好看的)小炖锅,还有两个别的陶罐,烧得再硬也不过如此了,其中一个还被熔化的沙子上得满是釉。

paragraphs.en: After this experiment, I need not say that I wanted no sort of earthenware for my use; but I must needs say as to the shapes of them, they were very indifferent, as any one may suppose, when I had no way of making them but as the children make dirt pies, or as a woman would make pies that never learned to raise paste.
paragraphs.cn: 经过这次试验,不必说,我用的各种陶器就再也不缺了;不过我得承认,论它们的样子,那实在很不像话,谁都能想得到,因为我做它们的法子,不过就像小孩子捏泥饼,或是像一个从没学过和面的女人做馅饼罢了。

paragraphs.en: No joy at a thing of so mean a nature was ever equal to mine, when I found I had made an earthen pot that would bear the fire; and I had hardly patience to stay till they were cold before I set one on the fire again with some water in it to boil me some meat, which it did admirably well; and with a piece of a kid I made some very good broth, though I wanted oatmeal, and several other ingredients requisite to make it as good as I would have had it been.
paragraphs.cn: 当我发现自己做成了一个经得住火烧的陶罐时,那份喜悦是别的什么低贱小事都比不上的;我几乎等不及它们凉下来,就又把一个放到火上,里面盛了些水去煮肉,结果煮得妙极了;我用一块小山羊肉熬了一锅很不错的肉汤,虽然我缺燕麦粉和几样别的配料,没能把它熬得像我原想的那么好。

paragraphs.en: My next concern was to get me a stone mortar to stamp or beat some corn in; for as to the mill, there was no thought of arriving at that perfection of art with one pair of hands.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来我操心的是弄一个石臼,好舂捣谷物;至于磨,凭我这一双手,是别想达到那种手艺的完美境界了。

paragraphs.en: To supply this want, I was at a great loss; for, of all the trades in the world, I was as perfectly unqualified for a stone-cutter as for any whatever; neither had I any tools to go about it with.
paragraphs.cn: 为了满足这个需要,我实在犯了大难;因为在世上所有的行当里,要论当石匠,我跟干别的一样,完全是个外行;况且我也没有任何工具可用。

paragraphs.en: I spent many a day to find out a great stone big enough to cut hollow, and make fit for a mortar, and could find none at all, except what was in the solid rock, and which I had no way to dig or cut out; nor indeed were the rocks in the island of hardness sufficient, but were all of a sandy, crumbling stone, which neither would bear the weight of a heavy pestle, nor would break the corn without filling it with sand.
paragraphs.cn: 我花了好多天去找一块够大、能凿空做臼的大石头,却一块也找不到,除了嵌在整块岩石里的以外,而那些我又没法挖出或凿下来;况且这岛上的岩石硬度也不够,全是些沙质、易碎的石头,既经不住沉重的杵捣,又没法把谷子捣碎,反倒会掺进一堆沙子。

paragraphs.en: So, after a great deal of time lost in searching for a stone, I gave it over, and resolved to look out for a great block of hard wood, which I found, indeed, much easier; and getting one as big as I had strength to stir, I rounded it, and formed it on the outside with my axe and hatchet, and then with the help of fire and infinite labour, made a hollow place in it, as the Indians in Brazil make their canoes.
paragraphs.cn: 于是,白白花了许多时间找石头之后,我便放弃了,决定改找一大块硬木头,这果然容易得多;我挑了一块凭我的力气能搬得动的,把它削圆,用斧头和短柄斧修整外形,然后借助火和无数的劳作,在里面挖出一个凹坑,就像巴西的印第安人做独木舟那样。

paragraphs.en: After this, I made a great heavy pestle or beater of the wood called the iron-wood; and this I prepared and laid by against I had my next crop of corn, which I proposed to myself to grind, or rather pound into meal to make bread.
paragraphs.cn: 做完这个,我又用一种叫铁木的木料做了一根又大又重的杵或捣棒;我把它准备好放在一边,留着下一季谷物收成后用来磨碎——不如说舂成面粉去做面包。

paragraphs.en: My next difficulty was to make a sieve or searce, to dress my meal, and to part it from the bran and the husk; without which I did not see it possible I could have any bread.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来的难题是做一个筛子或箩,好筛我的面粉,把它和麸皮、谷壳分开;要是没有它,我看是没法做出面包来的。

paragraphs.en: This was a most difficult thing even to think on, for to be sure I had nothing like the necessary thing to make it—I mean fine thin canvas or stuff to searce the meal through.
paragraphs.cn: 这件事光是想想都极其为难,因为我确实没有一样近似做筛子必需的材料——我是说那种细密轻薄、能筛面粉的帆布或料子。

paragraphs.en: And here I was at a full stop for many months; nor did I really know what to do.
paragraphs.cn: 在这上头我卡了好几个月;我真不知道该怎么办。

paragraphs.en: Linen I had none left but what was mere rags; I had goat’s hair, but neither knew how to weave it or spin it; and had I known how, here were no tools to work it with.
paragraphs.cn: 亚麻布我一点也没剩,除了些破布头;我有山羊毛,却既不会织也不会纺;就算我会,这里也没有工具去加工它。

paragraphs.en: All the remedy that I found for this was, that at last I did remember I had, among the seamen’s clothes which were saved out of the ship, some neckcloths of calico or muslin; and with some pieces of these I made three small sieves proper enough for the work; and thus I made shift for some years: how I did afterwards, I shall show in its place.
paragraphs.cn: 我为这事找到的唯一办法,是我终于想起来:在从船上抢救下来的水手衣物里,有几条印花布或平纹细布的领巾;我用其中几块做了三个小筛子,勉强够用了;就这样我将就着用了几年:后来我是怎么办的,以后到该说的地方再讲。

paragraphs.en: The baking part was the next thing to be considered, and how I should make bread when I came to have corn; for first, I had no yeast.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来要考虑的是烘烤这件事,以及等我有了谷子该怎样做面包;因为首先,我没有酵母。

paragraphs.en: As to that part, there was no supplying the want, so I did not concern myself much about it.
paragraphs.cn: 至于酵母这一样,那是没法补上的,所以我也就不怎么为它操心了。

paragraphs.en: But for an oven I was indeed in great pain.
paragraphs.cn: 但为了一个烤炉,我可真是大伤脑筋。

paragraphs.en: At length I found out an experiment for that also, which was this: I made some earthen-vessels very broad but not deep, that is to say, about two feet diameter, and not above nine inches deep.
paragraphs.cn: 最后我为这事也想出了一个法子,是这样的:我做了几个又扁又浅的陶器,也就是说,直径约两英尺,深不过九英寸。

paragraphs.en: These I burned in the fire, as I had done the other, and laid them by; and when I wanted to bake, I made a great fire upon my hearth, which I had paved with some square tiles of my own baking and burning also; but I should not call them square.
paragraphs.cn: 这些我像烧别的东西一样放在火里烧好,搁在一边;等我要烤面包时,就在我的炉床上生一大堆火,那炉床是我用自己烧制的几块方砖铺成的;不过我不该管它们叫方砖。

paragraphs.en: When the firewood was burned pretty much into embers or live coals, I drew them forward upon this hearth, so as to cover it all over, and there I let them lie till the hearth was very hot.
paragraphs.cn: 等柴火烧得差不多成了炭或红热的煤块,我就把它们扒到这炉床上摊开,盖满整个炉面,让它们放在那儿,直到炉床烧得滚烫。

paragraphs.en: Then sweeping away all the embers, I set down my loaf or loaves, and whelming down the earthen pot upon them, drew the embers all round the outside of the pot, to keep in and add to the heat; and thus as well as in the best oven in the world, I baked my barley-loaves, and became in little time a good pastrycook into the bargain; for I made myself several cakes and puddings of the rice; but I made no pies, neither had I anything to put into them supposing I had, except the flesh either of fowls or goats.
paragraphs.cn: 然后把所有的炭都扫开,放下我的一个或几个面包坯,把那扁陶器倒扣在上面,再把炭火全扒到陶器四周,以保住并增加热气;就这样,我烤出了我的大麦面包,烤得跟世上最好的烤炉一样好,没多久我还顺带成了个不错的糕点师;因为我用米做了好几样蛋糕和布丁;不过我没做馅饼,就算做,我也没什么可放进去的,除了禽肉或羊肉。

paragraphs.en: It need not be wondered at if all these things took me up most part of the third year of my abode here; for it is to be observed that in the intervals of these things I had my new harvest and husbandry to manage; for I reaped my corn in its season, and carried it home as well as I could, and laid it up in the ear, in my large baskets, till I had time to rub it out, for I had no floor to thrash it on, or instrument to thrash it with.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切事情占去了我在此居住第三年的大部分光阴,那也不足为奇;因为要知道,在做这些事的间隙里,我还得料理新的收成和农活;我按时节收割谷子,尽力搬回家,连穗带秆堆在我的大筐里,等有空再把谷粒搓出来,因为我没有打谷的场地,也没有打谷的工具。

paragraphs.en: And now, indeed, my stock of corn increasing, I really wanted to build my barns bigger; I wanted a place to lay it up in, for the increase of the corn now yielded me so much, that I had of the barley about twenty bushels, and of the rice as much or more; insomuch that now I resolved to begin to use it freely; for my bread had been quite gone a great while; also I resolved to see what quantity would be sufficient for me a whole year, and to sow but once a year.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我的存粮确实在增加,我真需要把谷仓造得更大些了;我需要一个存放的地方,因为谷子的收成如今多得很,我收了大麦约二十蒲式耳,稻米也一样多,甚至更多;以至于我如今决定放开来吃了;因为我的面包早就吃光了很久;我还决定看看一整年我需要多少才够,好一年只播种一次。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, I found that the forty bushels of barley and rice were much more than I could consume in a year; so I resolved to sow just the same quantity every year that I sowed the last, in hopes that such a quantity would fully provide me with bread, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 总的算下来,我发现这四十蒲式耳的大麦和稻米,远比我一年能吃掉的要多;于是我决定每年就播种跟上一年一样多的量,指望这个数量能足够供给我面包等所需。

paragraphs.en: All the while these things were doing, you may be sure my thoughts ran many times upon the prospect of land which I had seen from the other side of the island; and I was not without secret wishes that I were on shore there, fancying that, seeing the mainland, and an inhabited country, I might find some way or other to convey myself further, and perhaps at last find some means of escape.
paragraphs.cn: 在做这一切的时候,你可以断定,我的心思常常飞向我从岛那一边望见的那片陆地;我心里未尝没有暗暗盼望自己能上到那边的岸,幻想着既然望得见大陆和有人居住的地方,我或许能想出这样那样的法子把自己送得更远,说不定最终能找到某种逃脱的门路。

paragraphs.en: But all this while I made no allowance for the dangers of such an undertaking, and how I might fall into the hands of savages, and perhaps such as I might have reason to think far worse than the lions and tigers of Africa: that if I once came in their power, I should run a hazard of more than a thousand to one of being killed, and perhaps of being eaten; for I had heard that the people of the Caribbean coast were cannibals or man-eaters, and I knew by the latitude that I could not be far from that shore.
paragraphs.cn: 但这整段时间里,我全然没有考虑这种冒险的种种危险,没想到我可能落入野人之手,而那些野人说不定比非洲的狮子老虎还要凶恶得多:一旦落到他们手里,我被杀掉的凶险简直是千分之一都不止,说不定还会被吃掉;因为我听说加勒比海岸的人是吃人的生番,而我凭纬度知道,自己离那海岸不会太远。

paragraphs.en: Then, supposing they were not cannibals, yet they might kill me, as many Europeans who had fallen into their hands had been served, even when they had been ten or twenty together—much more I, that was but one, and could make little or no defence; all these things, I say, which I ought to have considered well; and did come into my thoughts afterwards, yet gave me no apprehensions at first, and my head ran mightily upon the thought of getting over to the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 再说,就算他们不吃人,他们也可能杀了我,就像许多落到他们手里的欧洲人所遭遇的那样,哪怕那些人是十个二十个结伙的——何况我孤身一人,几乎无从抵抗;这一切事情,我说,本该好好掂量的;后来它们也确实浮上了我的心头,可当初却丝毫没让我心生忌惮,我满脑子念念不忘的只是渡到对岸去。

paragraphs.en: Now I wished for my boy Xury, and the long-boat with shoulder-of-mutton sail, with which I sailed above a thousand miles on the coast of Africa; but this was in vain: then I thought I would go and look at our ship’s boat, which, as I have said, was blown up upon the shore a great way, in the storm, when we were first cast away.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我多想有我的小佐立,还有那条挂着羊腿帆的长舢板,我当年就是驾着它沿非洲海岸航行了一千多英里;可这都是白想:于是我又想,不如去看看我们那条船上的小艇,我说过,当初我们头一回遭难时,那小艇在风暴中被吹到了岸上很远的地方。

paragraphs.en: She lay almost where she did at first, but not quite; and was turned, by the force of the waves and the winds, almost bottom upward, against a high ridge of beachy, rough sand, but no water about her.
paragraphs.cn: 它躺的地方几乎还是当初那处,却不完全一样;它被浪涛和风力掀得几乎底朝天,抵着一道高高的、满是砾石和粗沙的沙脊,周围倒没有水。

paragraphs.en: If I had had hands to have refitted her, and to have launched her into the water, the boat would have done well enough, and I might have gone back into the Brazils with her easily enough; but I might have foreseen that I could no more turn her and set her upright upon her bottom than I could remove the island; however, I went to the woods, and cut levers and rollers, and brought them to the boat resolving to try what I could do; suggesting to myself that if I could but turn her down, I might repair the damage she had received, and she would be a very good boat, and I might go to sea in her very easily.
paragraphs.cn: 要是我有人手把它修好、推下水去,这小艇本会挺管用,我大可轻轻松松驾着它回巴西去;可我本该料到,要我把它翻个身、正正地竖在船底上,跟要我搬走这座岛一样办不到;不过我还是到林子里去砍了些撬杠和滚木,搬到小艇边,决心试试看我能做到什么地步;心里琢磨着,只要能把它翻过来,我就能修好它受的损伤,那它会是条很不错的船,我就能轻轻松松驾它出海了。

paragraphs.en: I spared no pains, indeed, in this piece of fruitless toil, and spent, I think, three or four weeks about it; at last finding it impossible to heave it up with my little strength, I fell to digging away the sand, to undermine it, and so to make it fall down, setting pieces of wood to thrust and guide it right in the fall.
paragraphs.cn: 在这桩徒劳无功的苦差事上,我确实没少下力气,我想前后花了三四个星期;最后发现凭我这点力气根本抬不动它,我便动手挖开沙子,从下面把它掏空,好让它自己塌下来,又摆好几块木头,在它塌落时去顶住、引导它落正。

paragraphs.en: But when I had done this, I was unable to stir it up again, or to get under it, much less to move it forward towards the water; so I was forced to give it over; and yet, though I gave over the hopes of the boat, my desire to venture over for the main increased, rather than decreased, as the means for it seemed impossible.
paragraphs.cn: 可等我这样做完,我却既没法再把它撬起来,也没法钻到它下面去,更别说把它朝水边挪动了;于是我只得作罢;然而,尽管放弃了这条小艇的指望,我渡海去大陆的欲望却不减反增,正因为实现的手段看来已无可能。

paragraphs.en: This at length put me upon thinking whether it was not possible to make myself a canoe, or periagua, such as the natives of those climates make, even without tools, or, as I might say, without hands, of the trunk of a great tree.
paragraphs.cn: 这终于让我开始琢磨:能不能自己造一条独木舟,或者叫独木船,就像那些地方的土人所造的那样,哪怕没有工具,或者可以说没有人手,就用一棵大树的树干来造。

paragraphs.en: This I not only thought possible, but easy, and pleased myself extremely with the thoughts of making it, and with my having much more convenience for it than any of the negroes or Indians; but not at all considering the particular inconveniences which I lay under more than the Indians did—viz. want of hands to move it, when it was made, into the water—a difficulty much harder for me to surmount than all the consequences of want of tools could be to them; for what was it to me, if when I had chosen a vast tree in the woods, and with much trouble cut it down, if I had been able with my tools to hew and dub the outside into the proper shape of a boat, and burn or cut out the inside to make it hollow, so as to make a boat of it—if, after all this, I must leave it just there where I found it, and not be able to launch it into the water?
paragraphs.cn: 这我不但认为可行,而且觉得容易,想到要造它我便得意非常,还想到我比那些黑人或印第安人有着多得多的便利;却全然没考虑到,我所处的种种不便比印第安人多得多——那就是:船造好后没有人手把它挪进水里——这个难关我要克服,比工具短缺给他们造成的一切后果都难得多;因为对我来说,若是在林子里挑中一棵参天大树,费尽千辛万苦把它砍倒,又能用工具把外面削凿成一条船的样子,把里面烧空或挖空好造成船,可若是做完这一切之后,我却只能把它撇在原地,没法把它推下水去,那这一切于我又有什么用呢?

paragraphs.en: One would have thought I could not have had the least reflection upon my mind of my circumstances while I was making this boat, but I should have immediately thought how I should get it into the sea; but my thoughts were so intent upon my voyage over the sea in it, that I never once considered how I should get it off the land: and it was really, in its own nature, more easy for me to guide it over forty-five miles of sea than about forty-five fathoms of land, where it lay, to set it afloat in the water.
paragraphs.cn: 人们或许会以为,我造这条船时,心里对自己的处境总该有那么一丁点儿的省察,总该立刻想到该怎样把它弄下海去;可我的心思全扑在驾它渡海的航行上,竟一次也没考虑过该怎样把它弄离陆地:说实在的,就其本身而言,让我驾它渡过四十五英里的海面,倒比把它从它所躺的、约莫四十五英寻的陆地上弄到水里浮起来还要容易些。

paragraphs.en: I went to work upon this boat the most like a fool that ever man did who had any of his senses awake.
paragraphs.cn: 我着手造这条船,那副蠢样,是任何一个尚有几分清醒神智的人都不曾有过的。

paragraphs.en: I pleased myself with the design, without determining whether I was ever able to undertake it; not but that the difficulty of launching my boat came often into my head; but I put a stop to my inquiries into it by this foolish answer which I gave myself—“Let me first make it; I warrant I will find some way or other to get it along when it is done.”
paragraphs.cn: 我一味沉醉在这个计划里,却没有定夺自己究竟有没有能力把它办成;倒不是说下水的难处不常常涌上我的心头;可我总用这样一个蠢答案来打断自己的深究,搪塞自己说——“先让我把它造出来;我担保等它造好了,我总会想出这样那样的法子把它弄过去。”

paragraphs.en: This was a most preposterous method; but the eagerness of my fancy prevailed, and to work I went.
paragraphs.cn: 这实在是个荒谬透顶的做法;可我那股狂热的空想占了上风,于是我就动手干了起来。

paragraphs.en: I felled a cedar-tree, and I question much whether Solomon ever had such a one for the building of the Temple of Jerusalem; it was five feet ten inches diameter at the lower part next the stump, and four feet eleven inches diameter at the end of twenty-two feet; after which it lessened for a while, and then parted into branches.
paragraphs.cn: 我砍倒了一棵香柏树,我很怀疑当年所罗门造耶路撒冷圣殿时是否有过这样一棵:它靠近树桩的下部直径有五英尺十英寸,到二十二英尺高处直径还有四英尺十一英寸;再往上便渐渐收细了一阵,然后才分出枝杈。

paragraphs.en: It was not without infinite labour that I felled this tree; I was twenty days hacking and hewing at it at the bottom; I was fourteen more getting the branches and limbs and the vast spreading head cut off, which I hacked and hewed through with axe and hatchet, and inexpressible labour; after this, it cost me a month to shape it and dub it to a proportion, and to something like the bottom of a boat, that it might swim upright as it ought to do.
paragraphs.cn: 砍倒这棵树可着实费了我无数的力气;我在树根处砍削了二十天;又花了十四天砍掉那些枝干和硕大蔓展的树冠,那些我都是用斧头和短柄斧一路砍削过去的,费尽了难以言表的力气;此后,把它削凿成一定的比例、修成有点像船底的样子好让它能正正地浮着,又花了我一个月。

paragraphs.en: It cost me near three months more to clear the inside, and work it out so as to make an exact boat of it; this I did, indeed, without fire, by mere mallet and chisel, and by the dint of hard labour, till I had brought it to be a very handsome periagua, and big enough to have carried six-and-twenty men, and consequently big enough to have carried me and all my cargo.
paragraphs.cn: 把里面清空、掏挖成一条名副其实的船,又花了我将近三个月;这我确实没用火,全靠一把木槌和一把凿子,凭着一股苦干的劲头,直到把它做成一条很漂亮的独木船,大得足以载得下二十六个人,因而也就大得足以载下我和我全部的货物了。

paragraphs.en: When I had gone through this work I was extremely delighted with it.
paragraphs.cn: 干完这桩活儿,我对它满意极了。

paragraphs.en: The boat was really much bigger than ever I saw a canoe or periagua, that was made of one tree, in my life.
paragraphs.cn: 这船确实比我这辈子见过的任何用一棵树做成的独木舟或独木船都要大得多。

paragraphs.en: Many a weary stroke it had cost, you may be sure; and had I gotten it into the water, I make no question, but I should have begun the maddest voyage, and the most unlikely to be performed, that ever was undertaken.
paragraphs.cn: 你可以断定,这船着实费了我无数疲惫的斧凿;要是我能把它弄下水,我毫不怀疑,我准会开始一场空前疯狂、也最不可能完成的航行。

paragraphs.en: But all my devices to get it into the water failed me; though they cost me infinite labour too.
paragraphs.cn: 可我为把它弄下水想出的一切法子都落了空;尽管它们也同样耗费了我无数的力气。

paragraphs.en: It lay about one hundred yards from the water, and not more; but the first inconvenience was, it was up hill towards the creek.
paragraphs.cn: 它躺在离水约莫一百码的地方,不算更远;可头一桩不便是,朝那条小河那边是往上坡的。

paragraphs.en: Well, to take away this discouragement, I resolved to dig into the surface of the earth, and so make a declivity: this I began, and it cost me a prodigious deal of pains (but who grudge pains who have their deliverance in view?)
paragraphs.cn: 好吧,为了除掉这个障碍,我决定把地表挖开,好造出一道斜坡:我开始动手了,这可花了我大得惊人的力气(可是眼看着能获得解脱,谁又会舍不得力气呢?)

paragraphs.en: ; but when this was worked through, and this difficulty managed, it was still much the same, for I could no more stir the canoe than I could the other boat.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,等这活儿干通了、这道难关也对付过去了,情形却还是老样子,因为我照样挪不动这独木舟,跟挪不动那另一条小艇一样。

paragraphs.en: Then I measured the distance of ground, and resolved to cut a dock or canal, to bring the water up to the canoe, seeing I could not bring the canoe down to the water.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我量了量那段地面的距离,决定挖一条船坞或运河,把水引到独木舟这边来,既然我没法把独木舟弄下去就水。

paragraphs.en: Well, I began this work; and when I began to enter upon it, and calculate how deep it was to be dug, how broad, how the stuff was to be thrown out, I found that, by the number of hands I had, being none but my own, it must have been ten or twelve years before I could have gone through with it; for the shore lay so high, that at the upper end it must have been at least twenty feet deep; so at length, though with great reluctancy, I gave this attempt over also.
paragraphs.cn: 好吧,我开始干这活儿;可当我着手动工、盘算它得挖多深、多宽、挖出的土该怎么甩出去时,我发现:凭我手头的人手——除了我自己再没别人——那非得花上十年或十二年才能干完;因为那岸势太高,在靠上头的那端,少说也得挖二十英尺深;于是最后,尽管万分不情愿,我把这个尝试也放弃了。

paragraphs.en: This grieved me heartily; and now I saw, though too late, the folly of beginning a work before we count the cost, and before we judge rightly of our own strength to go through with it.
paragraphs.cn: 这让我从心底里难过;如今我看清了——虽然为时已晚——一件事情还没核算清代价、还没正确掂量自己有没有力气把它干完就动手,那是何等的愚蠢。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of this work I finished my fourth year in this place, and kept my anniversary with the same devotion, and with as much comfort as ever before; for, by a constant study and serious application to the Word of God, and by the assistance of His grace, I gained a different knowledge from what I had before.
paragraphs.cn: 在做这活儿的中途,我在这地方满了第四个年头,我又以一如既往的虔诚、和从前一样多的安慰过了我的这个纪念日;因为凭着对上帝圣言坚持不懈的钻研与郑重的践行,又借着祂恩典的扶助,我获得了一种跟从前不同的领悟。

paragraphs.en: I entertained different notions of things.
paragraphs.cn: 我对种种事物有了不同的看法。

paragraphs.en: I looked now upon the world as a thing remote, which I had nothing to do with, no expectations from, and, indeed, no desires about: in a word, I had nothing indeed to do with it, nor was ever likely to have, so I thought it looked, as we may perhaps look upon it hereafter—viz. as a place I had lived in, but was come out of it; and well might I say, as Father Abraham to Dives, “Between me and thee is a great gulf fixed.”
paragraphs.cn: 如今我把这世界看作一样遥远的东西,与我毫不相干,我对它无所指望,说实在的,也无所欲求:总之,我确实跟它再无瓜葛,往后大概也不会有,所以我觉得,我看它的眼光,就仿佛我们来日或许会有的那种眼光——也就是说,把它看作一处我曾住过、如今却已走出来的地方;我大可像亚伯拉罕老祖对财主所说的那样讲:“在我与你之间,有深渊隔定了。”

paragraphs.en: In the first place, I was removed from all the wickedness of the world here; I had neither the lusts of the flesh, the lusts of the eye, nor the pride of life.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我在这里远离了世上一切的邪恶;我既没有肉体的私欲,没有眼目的贪求,也没有今生的骄傲。

paragraphs.en: I had nothing to covet, for I had all that I was now capable of enjoying; I was lord of the whole manor; or, if I pleased, I might call myself king or emperor over the whole country which I had possession of: there were no rivals; I had no competitor, none to dispute sovereignty or command with me: I might have raised ship-loadings of corn, but I had no use for it; so I let as little grow as I thought enough for my occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有什么可贪图的,因为凡是我如今能享用的,我全都有了;我是这整片田庄的主人;或者,只要我高兴,我大可自称是我所占有的这整个国土的国王或皇帝:这里没有对手;我没有竞争者,没有谁来跟我争夺主权或号令权:我本可以种出一船一船的谷子,可我用不着;所以我觉得够我用的了,便只让它长那么一点。

paragraphs.en: I had tortoise or turtle enough, but now and then one was as much as I could put to any use: I had timber enough to have built a fleet of ships; and I had grapes enough to have made wine, or to have cured into raisins, to have loaded that fleet when it had been built.
paragraphs.cn: 我有足够的龟鳖,可我至多也就时不时用得上一只:我有足够的木材,可以造一支船队;我还有足够的葡萄,可以酿酒,或者晒成葡萄干,足够在那船队造好后把它装满。

paragraphs.en: But all I could make use of was all that was valuable: I had enough to eat and supply my wants, and what was all the rest to me?
paragraphs.cn: 但我能用得着的,才是全部有价值的东西:我有足够的吃食来满足需要,其余的一切对我又算得了什么呢?

paragraphs.en: If I killed more flesh than I could eat, the dog must eat it, or vermin; if I sowed more corn than I could eat, it must be spoiled; the trees that I cut down were lying to rot on the ground; I could make no more use of them but for fuel, and that I had no occasion for but to dress my food.
paragraphs.cn: 我要是杀的肉多过我能吃的,那就得让狗去吃,或让虫豸去糟蹋;我要是种的谷子多过我能吃的,那就得任它烂掉;我砍倒的那些树,只能躺在地上朽烂;除了当柴火,我再没别的用处,而柴火我也只在做饭时才用得着。

paragraphs.en: In a word, the nature and experience of things dictated to me, upon just reflection, that all the good things of this world are no farther good to us than they are for our use; and that, whatever we may heap up to give others, we enjoy just as much as we can use, and no more.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,事物的本性和亲身的体验,经过公允的省察,教会了我一个道理:这世上一切好东西,对我们的好处不过就在于我们用得着的那部分;而无论我们积攒下多少留给别人,我们自己享用的,也只是我们用得了的那么多,再多也没有了。

paragraphs.en: The most covetous, griping miser in the world would have been cured of the vice of covetousness if he had been in my case; for I possessed infinitely more than I knew what to do with.
paragraphs.cn: 世上最贪婪、最悭吝的守财奴,若是处在我这境地,他那贪财的恶习也准能治好;因为我拥有的,比我知道该拿它怎么办的要多得无穷无尽。

paragraphs.en: I had no room for desire, except it was of things which I had not, and they were but trifles, though, indeed, of great use to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有可欲求的余地,除非是欲求那些我没有的东西,而它们不过是些琐碎小物,尽管对我实在很有用处。

paragraphs.en: I had, as I hinted before, a parcel of money, as well gold as silver, about thirty-six pounds sterling.
paragraphs.cn: 我先前提过,我有一小笔钱,金子银子都有,约莫三十六英镑。

paragraphs.en: Alas! there the sorry, useless stuff lay; I had no more manner of business for it; and often thought with myself that I would have given a handful of it for a gross of tobacco-pipes; or for a hand-mill to grind my corn; nay, I would have given it all for a sixpenny-worth of turnip and carrot seed out of England, or for a handful of peas and beans, and a bottle of ink.
paragraphs.cn: 唉!这堆可怜、没用的东西就搁在那儿;我对它再没有任何用途;我常常暗自寻思,情愿拿出一把来换一箩烟斗;或者换一台磨谷子的手磨;不,我情愿把它全拿出来,去换从英国来的六便士的萝卜和胡萝卜种子,或者换一把豌豆和蚕豆,再加一瓶墨水。

paragraphs.en: As it was, I had not the least advantage by it or benefit from it; but there it lay in a drawer, and grew mouldy with the damp of the cave in the wet seasons; and if I had had the drawer full of diamonds, it had been the same case—they had been of no manner of value to me, because of no use.
paragraphs.cn: 就它现在的样子,我从它身上得不到丝毫的好处或益处;它只是躺在一个抽屉里,在雨季随着洞里的潮气发霉;就算我那抽屉里装满了钻石,情形也是一样——它们对我毫无价值可言,因为毫无用处。

paragraphs.en: I had now brought my state of life to be much easier in itself than it was at first, and much easier to my mind, as well as to my body.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我已把自己的生活境况调理得比起初本身要安适得多了,不论对我的心还是对我的身体,都轻松了许多。

paragraphs.en: I frequently sat down to meat with thankfulness, and admired the hand of God’s providence, which had thus spread my table in the wilderness.
paragraphs.cn: 我时常怀着感恩之心坐下来用饭,赞叹上帝眷顾的手,它就这样在这荒野里为我摆设了筵席。

paragraphs.en: I learned to look more upon the bright side of my condition, and less upon the dark side, and to consider what I enjoyed rather than what I wanted; and this gave me sometimes such secret comforts, that I cannot express them; and which I take notice of here, to put those discontented people in mind of it, who cannot enjoy comfortably what God has given them, because they see and covet something that He has not given them.
paragraphs.cn: 我学会了更多地去看我处境中光明的一面,少去看那阴暗的一面,去想我所享有的,而不是我所欠缺的;这有时给了我一种说不出的隐秘慰藉;我在此提到它,是要提醒那些心怀不满的人:他们无法安心享用上帝所赐给他们的,只因为他们看见并贪求某样上帝没有赐给他们的东西。

paragraphs.en: All our discontents about what we want appeared to me to spring from the want of thankfulness for what we have.
paragraphs.cn: 我们对所欠缺之物的一切不满,在我看来,都源于对所拥有之物缺少感恩。

paragraphs.en: Another reflection was of great use to me, and doubtless would be so to any one that should fall into such distress as mine was; and this was, to compare my present condition with what I at first expected it would be; nay, with what it would certainly have been, if the good providence of God had not wonderfully ordered the ship to be cast up nearer to the shore, where I not only could come at her, but could bring what I got out of her to the shore, for my relief and comfort; without which, I had wanted for tools to work, weapons for defence, and gunpowder and shot for getting my food.
paragraphs.cn: 另一番省察对我大有裨益,无疑对任何落入我这般困境的人也会同样有益;那就是:把我目前的境况,同我起初所预料的境况相比较;不,是同它必定会有的样子相比较——倘若上帝美善的眷顾没有奇妙地安排那船被冲到离岸更近的地方,我不但能上到船上,还能把从船上取得的东西搬到岸上来,以救济和安慰我;若没有这一切,我便会短缺干活的工具、防身的武器,以及猎取食物用的火药和弹丸。

paragraphs.en: I spent whole hours, I may say whole days, in representing to myself, in the most lively colours, how I must have acted if I had got nothing out of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我曾花上整整几个钟头,甚至可以说整整几天,用最鲜明的色彩向自己描画:倘若我从船上什么也没弄到,我该怎么办才好。

paragraphs.en: How I could not have so much as got any food, except fish and turtles; and that, as it was long before I found any of them, I must have perished first; that I should have lived, if I had not perished, like a mere savage; that if I had killed a goat or a fowl, by any contrivance, I had no way to flay or open it, or part the flesh from the skin and the bowels, or to cut it up; but must gnaw it with my teeth, and pull it with my claws, like a beast.
paragraphs.cn: 我该会连吃的都弄不到,除了鱼和海龟;而由于我过了很久才找到它们,我恐怕早就先饿死了;就算没饿死,我也该会活得像个十足的野人;就算我用什么巧法子打到一只山羊或一只禽,我也没法给它剥皮开膛,没法把肉从皮和肠子上分下来,或者把它切开;只能像野兽一样,用牙去啃它,用爪去撕它。

paragraphs.en: These reflections made me very sensible of the goodness of Providence to me, and very thankful for my present condition, with all its hardships and misfortunes; and this part also I cannot but recommend to the reflection of those who are apt, in their misery, to say, “Is any affliction like mine?”
paragraphs.cn: 这些省察使我深深体会到天意待我的恩慈,并为我目前的境况——连同它一切的艰辛与不幸——满怀感激;这一层我也不能不推荐给那些人去省察,他们身处苦难时,动辄就说:“有谁的苦难像我这样呢?”

paragraphs.en: Let them consider how much worse the cases of some people are, and their case might have been, if Providence had thought fit.
paragraphs.cn: 让他们想一想,有些人的处境比这要糟得多,而倘若上天觉得该如此,他们自己的处境本也可能糟得多。

paragraphs.en: I had another reflection, which assisted me also to comfort my mind with hopes; and this was comparing my present situation with what I had deserved, and had therefore reason to expect from the hand of Providence.
paragraphs.cn: 我还有另一番省察,也帮着我用希望来宽慰自己的心;那就是:把我目前的处境,同我应得的、因而理当从天意手中所指望的相比较。

paragraphs.en: I had lived a dreadful life, perfectly destitute of the knowledge and fear of God.
paragraphs.cn: 我曾过着一种可怕的生活,全然不知敬畏上帝。

paragraphs.en: I had been well instructed by father and mother; neither had they been wanting to me in their early endeavours to infuse a religious awe of God into my mind, a sense of my duty, and what the nature and end of my being required of me.
paragraphs.cn: 父母都曾好好教导过我;他们在我年幼时也未尝没有尽力,想把对上帝的虔敬、对我本分的意识、以及我这一生的本性与归宿对我的要求,灌注进我的心里。

paragraphs.en: But, alas! falling early into the seafaring life, which of all lives is the most destitute of the fear of God, though His terrors are always before them; I say, falling early into the seafaring life, and into seafaring company, all that little sense of religion which I had entertained was laughed out of me by my messmates; by a hardened despising of dangers, and the views of death, which grew habitual to me by my long absence from all manner of opportunities to converse with anything but what was like myself, or to hear anything that was good or tended towards it.
paragraphs.cn: 可是,唉!我早早堕入了航海的生涯,那在一切生涯中是最不知敬畏上帝的,尽管祂的威严时刻就在他们眼前;我是说,我早早堕入了航海的生涯、混进了航海的人群里,我心中所怀的那一点点宗教意识,全被我的同船伙伴讥笑得荡然无存了;我对危险、对死亡的景象,渐渐练就了一种铁石心肠的蔑视,这成了我的习性,只因我长久以来远离一切机会,身边所能交谈的、所能听闻的,无非就是些跟我一路货色的东西,再没有什么良善的、或趋向良善的话语。

paragraphs.en: So void was I of everything that was good, or the least sense of what I was, or was to be, that, in the greatest deliverances I enjoyed—such as my escape from Sallee; my being taken up by the Portuguese master of the ship; my being planted so well in the Brazils; my receiving the cargo from England, and the like—I never had once the words “Thank God!” so much as on my mind, or in my mouth; nor in the greatest distress had I so much as a thought to pray to Him, or so much as to say, “Lord, have mercy upon me!” no, nor to mention the name of God, unless it was to swear by, and blaspheme it.
paragraphs.cn: 我心中是那样地毫无良善,对自己是什么、将要成为什么毫无一点意识,以至于在我所享有的那些最大的解脱之中——比如从萨累逃脱;被那葡萄牙船长搭救;在巴西安顿得那样好;从英国收到那批货物,诸如此类——我心里或口中竟不曾有过一次“感谢上帝!”这句话;哪怕身处最大的患难,我也不曾动过一个向祂祷告的念头,或哪怕说一句“主啊,可怜我吧!”不,我甚至不曾提起上帝的名,除非是用来赌咒、亵渎。

paragraphs.en: I had terrible reflections upon my mind for many months, as I have already observed, on account of my wicked and hardened life past; and when I looked about me, and considered what particular providences had attended me since my coming into this place, and how God had dealt bountifully with me—had not only punished me less than my iniquity had deserved, but had so plentifully provided for me—this gave me great hopes that my repentance was accepted, and that God had yet mercy in store for me.
paragraphs.cn: 正如我先前所说,好几个月来,我心里为我过去那罪恶而顽梗的生活,怀着可怕的省察;而当我环顾四周,想到自从我来到这地方以来,有过怎样种种特别的眷顾伴随着我,想到上帝待我是何等丰厚——不但惩罚我远轻过我的罪孽所应得的,还这样丰丰富富地供养我——这便给了我极大的盼望:我的悔改已蒙悦纳,上帝仍为我存留着怜悯。

paragraphs.en: With these reflections I worked my mind up, not only to a resignation to the will of God in the present disposition of my circumstances, but even to a sincere thankfulness for my condition; and that I, who was yet a living man, ought not to complain, seeing I had not the due punishment of my sins; that I enjoyed so many mercies which I had no reason to have expected in that place; that I ought never more to repine at my condition, but to rejoice, and to give daily thanks for that daily bread, which nothing but a crowd of wonders could have brought; that I ought to consider I had been fed even by a miracle, even as great as that of feeding Elijah by ravens, nay, by a long series of miracles; and that I could hardly have named a place in the uninhabitable part of the world where I could have been cast more to my advantage; a place where, as I had no society, which was my affliction on one hand, so I found no ravenous beasts, no furious wolves or tigers, to threaten my life; no venomous creatures, or poisons, which I might feed on to my hurt; no savages to murder and devour me.
paragraphs.cn: 怀着这些省察,我把自己的心提振起来,不仅甘心顺服上帝对我目前处境的安排,甚至对我的境况生出一种真诚的感激;我这个如今尚且活着的人,不该抱怨,既然我并没有受到我罪应得的惩罚;我享有着这么多本无理由指望在此地能有的恩典;我再不该为我的境况怨天尤人,而该欢欣,该为那一日的口粮天天献上感谢,那口粮若非一连串的奇迹,是绝无可能得来的;我该想到,我竟是靠着神迹被喂养的,那神迹之大不亚于乌鸦喂养以利亚,不,是靠着一长串接连不断的神迹;而在这世上不宜居住的地方里,我几乎举不出还有哪一处能让我遭难得比这更有利;在这地方,一方面我固然没有伴侣,这是我一重的苦难,可另一方面我又发现,这里没有凶猛的野兽,没有暴烈的狼或虎来威胁我的性命;没有毒虫,没有毒物会让我误食受害;没有野人来杀害我、吞吃我。

paragraphs.en: In a word, as my life was a life of sorrow one way, so it was a life of mercy another; and I wanted nothing to make it a life of comfort but to be able to make my sense of God’s goodness to me, and care over me in this condition, be my daily consolation; and after I did make a just improvement on these things, I went away, and was no more sad.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,我的生活一面固然是充满忧患的生活,另一面却是蒙受怜悯的生活;要把它变成一种安适的生活,我别无所缺,只需能把我对上帝这般待我之美善、以及祂在此境况中对我的看顾的领会,化作我每日的慰藉;而当我确实从这些事上得着了正当的长进之后,我便离开了,不再愁苦。

paragraphs.en: I had now been here so long that many things which I had brought on shore for my help were either quite gone, or very much wasted and near spent.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我在这里已经待了这么久,许多我为帮衬自己搬上岸来的东西,不是已经用光,就是耗损得很厉害、快要用尽了。

paragraphs.en: My ink, as I observed, had been gone some time, all but a very little, which I eked out with water, a little and a little, till it was so pale, it scarce left any appearance of black upon the paper.
paragraphs.cn: 我的墨水,我说过,早已用完了,只剩极少一点,我便一点一点掺水勉强对付着用,直到它淡得几乎在纸上留不下一丝黑迹。

paragraphs.en: As long as it lasted I made use of it to minute down the days of the month on which any remarkable thing happened to me; and first, by casting up times past, I remembered that there was a strange concurrence of days in the various providences which befell me, and which, if I had been superstitiously inclined to observe days as fatal or fortunate, I might have had reason to have looked upon with a great deal of curiosity.
paragraphs.cn: 趁着它还有,我用它把每月里遇到什么值得记的事的日子简略记下来;先是,通过盘点过往的时日,我记起来:在降临于我的种种境遇里,有着一种奇特的日子的巧合,倘若我素来迷信,把某些日子看作凶日或吉日,我本大可以怀着极大的好奇去审视它。

paragraphs.en: First, I had observed that the same day that I broke away from my father and friends and ran away to Hull, in order to go to sea, the same day afterwards I was taken by the Sallee man-of-war, and made a slave; the same day of the year that I escaped out of the wreck of that ship in Yarmouth Roads, that same day-year afterwards I made my escape from Sallee in a boat; the same day of the year I was born on—viz. the 30th of September, that same day I had my life so miraculously saved twenty-six years after, when I was cast on shore in this island; so that my wicked life and my solitary life began both on a day.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我留意到:就在我离弃父亲和亲友、逃到赫尔去打算出海的那同一天,若干年后的同一天,我被那萨累的兵船掳去,做了奴隶;就在我从雅茅斯锚地那条船的失事中逃生的那个年月日,若干年后的同一个年月日,我坐着一条小船从萨累逃了出来;就在我出生的那个年月日——也就是九月三十日,正是这同一天,二十六年之后,我被冲上这座岛的岸,如此奇迹般地保住了性命;所以我那罪恶的生涯和我这孤独的生涯,竟都是在同一天开始的。

paragraphs.en: The next thing to my ink being wasted was that of my bread—I mean the biscuit which I brought out of the ship; this I had husbanded to the last degree, allowing myself but one cake of bread a-day for above a year; and yet I was quite without bread for near a year before I got any corn of my own, and great reason I had to be thankful that I had any at all, the getting it being, as has been already observed, next to miraculous.
paragraphs.cn: 继墨水用尽之后,接着就是我的面包——我是说我从船上带下来的饼干;这个我极其省着吃,一年多来每天只许自己吃一块;可即便如此,在我收到自己种的谷子之前,我还是几乎断了一年的面包,而我实在很有理由感恩,居然还能有一点谷子,因为它的得来,如前所述,简直近乎奇迹。

paragraphs.en: My clothes, too, began to decay; as to linen, I had had none a good while, except some chequered shirts which I found in the chests of the other seamen, and which I carefully preserved; because many times I could bear no other clothes on but a shirt; and it was a very great help to me that I had, among all the men’s clothes of the ship, almost three dozen of shirts.
paragraphs.cn: 我的衣裳也开始破败了;至于亚麻内衣,我早已一件不剩,只有几件格子衬衫,是我在别的水手箱子里找到、又小心保存下来的;因为很多时候,除了一件衬衫,别的衣服我都穿不住;而在船上全部的男人衣物里,我几乎有三打衬衫,这对我是极大的帮助。

paragraphs.en: There were also, indeed, several thick watch-coats of the seamen’s which were left, but they were too hot to wear; and though it is true that the weather was so violently hot that there was no need of clothes, yet I could not go quite naked—no, though I had been inclined to it, which I was not—nor could I abide the thought of it, though I was alone.
paragraphs.cn: 确实也还剩下几件水手们厚厚的值班大衣,可它们穿着太热了;虽说天气热得那样厉害,本用不着穿衣,可我却没法赤条条地一丝不挂——不,哪怕我有那心思也不成,而我并没有——我一想到那样子就受不了,尽管我孑然一身。

paragraphs.en: The reason why I could not go naked was, I could not bear the heat of the sun so well when quite naked as with some clothes on; nay, the very heat frequently blistered my skin: whereas, with a shirt on, the air itself made some motion, and whistling under the shirt, was twofold cooler than without it.
paragraphs.cn: 我没法赤身的缘故是:全身赤裸时,我反倒不如穿点衣服时那样耐得住烈日的暴晒;不,那炎热还常常把我的皮肤晒出泡来:而穿着一件衬衫,空气本身便能有些流动,在衬衫底下飕飕地钻,比不穿要凉快一倍。

paragraphs.en: No more could I ever bring myself to go out in the heat of the sun without a cap or a hat; the heat of the sun, beating with such violence as it does in that place, would give me the headache presently, by darting so directly on my head, without a cap or hat on, so that I could not bear it; whereas, if I put on my hat it would presently go away.
paragraphs.cn: 同样,我也从来没法叫自己在烈日下不戴顶便帽或帽子就出门;那地方的太阳晒得那样猛烈,若不戴帽,阳光直射在我头上,立刻就会让我头痛,叫我受不了;可我只要戴上帽子,头痛马上就消了。

paragraphs.en: Upon these views I began to consider about putting the few rags I had, which I called clothes, into some order; I had worn out all the waistcoats I had, and my business was now to try if I could not make jackets out of the great watch-coats which I had by me, and with such other materials as I had; so I set to work, tailoring, or rather, indeed, botching, for I made most piteous work of it.
paragraphs.cn: 有鉴于这些,我便开始盘算,把我那几件被我称作衣服的破布头整理整理;我那几件背心早已穿破了,如今我的活计便是试试看,能不能用我手头那几件厚厚的值班大衣、连同别的一些材料,做出几件短上衣来;于是我动手当起了裁缝,或者不如说笨手笨脚地胡拼乱凑,因为我把这活儿干得糟糕透顶。

paragraphs.en: However, I made shift to make two or three new waistcoats, which I hoped would serve me a great while: as for breeches or drawers, I made but a very sorry shift indeed till afterwards.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我还是勉强做出了两三件新背心,指望它们能顶用好一阵子:至于裤子或衬裤,我实在只做出了极蹩脚的将就货,直到后来才好些。

paragraphs.en: I have mentioned that I saved the skins of all the creatures that I killed, I mean four-footed ones, and I had them hung up, stretched out with sticks in the sun, by which means some of them were so dry and hard that they were fit for little, but others were very useful.
paragraphs.cn: 我提到过,凡是我打死的野物,我都把它们的皮留了下来,我是指四条腿的;我用木棍把这些皮撑开,挂在太阳底下,这样一来,有些晒得又干又硬,几乎没什么用了,可另一些却很管用。

paragraphs.en: The first thing I made of these was a great cap for my head, with the hair on the outside, to shoot off the rain; and this I performed so well, that after I made me a suit of clothes wholly of these skins—that is to say, a waistcoat, and breeches open at the knees, and both loose, for they were rather wanting to keep me cool than to keep me warm.
paragraphs.cn: 我用这些皮做的头一样东西,是一顶戴头上的大帽子,毛朝外,好把雨水挡开;这个我做得很成功,后来我索性整套衣服全用这些皮来做——也就是说,一件背心和一条膝盖处敞口的裤子,两样都做得宽松,因为它们与其说是要给我保暖,倒不如说是要给我凉快。

paragraphs.en: I must not omit to acknowledge that they were wretchedly made; for if I was a bad carpenter, I was a worse tailor.
paragraphs.cn: 我不能不承认,它们做得糟糕透顶;因为要说我是个蹩脚的木匠,那我更是个不济的裁缝。

paragraphs.en: However, they were such as I made very good shift with, and when I was out, if it happened to rain, the hair of my waistcoat and cap being outermost, I was kept very dry.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,凭着它们我倒也很能将就对付,我出门在外时,若碰上下雨,我背心和帽子上的毛既然朝外,便叫我身上一直干爽。

paragraphs.en: After this, I spent a great deal of time and pains to make an umbrella; I was, indeed, in great want of one, and had a great mind to make one; I had seen them made in the Brazils, where they are very useful in the great heats there, and I felt the heats every jot as great here, and greater too, being nearer the equinox; besides, as I was obliged to be much abroad, it was a most useful thing to me, as well for the rains as the heats.
paragraphs.cn: 在这之后,我又花了大量的时间和力气去做一把伞;我确实极需要一把,也一心想做一把;我在巴西见过人家做伞,那里天气酷热,伞很有用,而我觉得这里的炎热丝毫不逊,甚至更甚,因为离二分点更近;况且,我既不得不常常在外奔走,一把伞对我便是极有用的东西,既挡雨又遮热。

paragraphs.en: I took a world of pains with it, and was a great while before I could make anything likely to hold: nay, after I had thought I had hit the way, I spoiled two or three before I made one to my mind: but at last I made one that answered indifferently well: the main difficulty I found was to make it let down.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这上头下了极大的功夫,过了好久才做出一件像样、撑得住的东西:不,就算我自以为摸着了门道,我还是糟蹋了两三把才做出一把合我心意的:可最后我总算做出了一把,勉强还算管用:我发觉主要的难处是怎样让它收拢下来。

paragraphs.en: I could make it spread, but if it did not let down too, and draw in, it was not portable for me any way but just over my head, which would not do.
paragraphs.cn: 我能让它张开,可它若不能同时收拢、拢进去,那我除了正好顶在头顶上,别的什么姿势都没法把它带着走,那可不行。

paragraphs.en: However, at last, as I said, I made one to answer, and covered it with skins, the hair upwards, so that it cast off the rain like a pent-house, and kept off the sun so effectually, that I could walk out in the hottest of the weather with greater advantage than I could before in the coolest, and when I had no need of it could close it, and carry it under my arm.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,最后,如我所说,我总算做出了一把管用的,还给它蒙上了兽皮,毛朝上,这样它便像披屋顶一样把雨水泻掉,又那样有效地遮住太阳,以至于我在最热的天气里出门,反倒比先前在最凉快的天气里还要舒坦;而当我用不着它时,便可以把它收拢,夹在胳膊底下带着走。

paragraphs.en: Thus I lived mighty comfortably, my mind being entirely composed by resigning myself to the will of God, and throwing myself wholly upon the disposal of His providence.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我过得非常安适,我的心因甘心顺服上帝的旨意、把自己整个儿交托给祂天意的安排,而完全平静了下来。

paragraphs.en: This made my life better than sociable, for when I began to regret the want of conversation I would ask myself, whether thus conversing mutually with my own thoughts, and (as I hope I may say) with even God Himself, by ejaculations, was not better than the utmost enjoyment of human society in the world?
paragraphs.cn: 这使我的生活胜过了有人做伴的生活,因为每当我开始惋惜没有交谈时,我便会问自己:这样彼此和我自己的思想交谈,并且(但愿我可以这样说)靠着一声声的祷告,甚至和上帝本身交谈,难道不胜过享尽这世上人际交往的极致之乐吗?

paragraphs.en: I cannot say that after this, for five years, any extraordinary thing happened to me, but I lived on in the same course, in the same posture and place, as before; the chief things I was employed in, besides my yearly labour of planting my barley and rice, and curing my raisins, of both which I always kept up just enough to have sufficient stock of one year’s provisions beforehand; I say, besides this yearly labour, and my daily pursuit of going out with my gun, I had one labour, to make a canoe, which at last I finished: so that, by digging a canal to it of six feet wide and four feet deep, I brought it into the creek, almost half a mile.
paragraphs.cn: 此后整整五年,我说不出有什么了不得的大事发生在我身上,我依旧过着从前那样的日子,还是同样的处境,同样的地方;除了每年种大麦、种稻子、晒葡萄干这些活计之外——这两样我总留足够一年的存粮备用——我说,除了这些年年要干的活,除了每天扛枪出门打猎,我还干了一桩大活:造一只独木舟,总算让我造成了;我又挖了一条六英尺宽、四英尺深的水沟通到它那里,把它拖进了小河,足足拖了将近半英里。

paragraphs.en: As for the first, which was so vastly big, for I made it without considering beforehand, as I ought to have done, how I should be able to launch it, so, never being able to bring it into the water, or bring the water to it, I was obliged to let it lie where it was as a memorandum to teach me to be wiser the next time: indeed, the next time, though I could not get a tree proper for it, and was in a place where I could not get the water to it at any less distance than, as I have said, near half a mile, yet, as I saw it was practicable at last, I never gave it over; and though I was near two years about it, yet I never grudged my labour, in hopes of having a boat to go off to sea at last.
paragraphs.cn: 至于头一只独木舟,那实在造得太大了,因为我事先没有像本该做的那样,先盘算好自己怎么才能把它下水;结果,我既没法把它弄到水里,也没法把水引到它跟前,只好由它躺在原地,当作一件提醒我下次放聪明些的纪念物;说真的,第二次虽然我找不到合适的树,所在的地方离水也不比头一回近,还是像我说的将近半英里,可我一见这事到底还行得通,就决不肯半途而废;这只船我前前后后忙了将近两年,却从不心疼自己的力气,一心指望终究能有一条船下海去。

paragraphs.en: However, though my little periagua was finished, yet the size of it was not at all answerable to the design which I had in view when I made the first; I mean of venturing over to the _terra firma_, where it was above forty miles broad; accordingly, the smallness of my boat assisted to put an end to that design, and now I thought no more of it.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,尽管我这只小独木舟造成了,它的大小却和我造头一只时心里所打的算盘根本不相称;我是说,我原想冒险渡到对面那片大陆去,那里海面足有四十多英里宽;这么一来,我这船太小,反倒帮着断了我这个念头,如今我再也不去想它了。

paragraphs.en: As I had a boat, my next design was to make a cruise round the island; for as I had been on the other side in one place, crossing, as I have already described it, over the land, so the discoveries I made in that little journey made me very eager to see other parts of the coast; and now I had a boat, I thought of nothing but sailing round the island.
paragraphs.cn: 既然有了船,我下一个打算便是绕岛巡游一圈;因为我从前曾从陆地上横穿过去,到过岛那一头的某个地方——这我前面已经讲过——那次小小的远行让我很想去看看海岸别的地方;如今有了船,我满脑子想的就只是驾船绕岛一周。

paragraphs.en: For this purpose, that I might do everything with discretion and consideration, I fitted up a little mast in my boat, and made a sail too out of some of the pieces of the ship’s sails which lay in store, and of which I had a great stock by me.
paragraphs.cn: 为此,为了事事都办得稳妥周全,我在船上装了一根小桅杆,又拿库存的几块船帆布料做了一面帆,这种布料我手头存得很多。

paragraphs.en: Having fitted my mast and sail, and tried the boat, I found she would sail very well; then I made little lockers or boxes at each end of my boat, to put provisions, necessaries, ammunition, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 装好了桅杆和帆,试了试船,我发现它航行得很好;于是我在船的两头各做了几个小柜子或小箱子,好放粮食、必需品、弹药等等。

paragraphs.en: , into, to be kept dry, either from rain or the spray of the sea; and a little, long, hollow place I cut in the inside of the boat, where I could lay my gun, making a flap to hang down over it to keep it dry.
paragraphs.cn: 把这些东西放进去,好让它们保持干燥,不叫雨水或海上的浪花打湿;我又在船舱内侧挖了一处又长又浅的凹槽,好搁我的枪,还做了一块盖布垂下来罩住它,让它不受潮。

paragraphs.en: I fixed my umbrella also in the step at the stern, like a mast, to stand over my head, and keep the heat of the sun off me, like an awning; and thus I every now and then took a little voyage upon the sea, but never went far out, nor far from the little creek.
paragraphs.cn: 我又把伞插在船尾的座槽里,像根桅杆似的立在我头顶上,替我挡住毒辣的日头,就像一顶天篷;这样我便时不时到海上作一小段航行,不过从不驶得太远,也不离那条小河太远。

paragraphs.en: At last, being eager to view the circumference of my little kingdom, I resolved upon my cruise; and accordingly I victualled my ship for the voyage, putting in two dozen of loaves (cakes I should call them) of barley-bread, an earthen pot full of parched rice (a food I ate a good deal of), a little bottle of rum, half a goat, and powder and shot for killing more, and two large watch-coats, of those which, as I mentioned before, I had saved out of the seamen’s chests; these I took, one to lie upon, and the other to cover me in the night.
paragraphs.cn: 末了,我很想把自己这个小王国的四周好好看个遍,便下决心去巡游一趟;于是我给船备足了这趟航行的口粮:装上两打大麦面包(其实该叫麦饼),一只装满炒米的瓦罐(这种食物我吃得很多),一小瓶朗姆酒,半只山羊,还有火药和铅弹好多打些野味,再加两件厚水手大衣——就是我前面提过、从水手箱子里救出来的那种——我带上它们,一件用来垫着睡,一件夜里用来盖身子。

paragraphs.en: It was the 6th of November, in the sixth year of my reign—or my captivity, which you please—that I set out on this voyage, and I found it much longer than I expected; for though the island itself was not very large, yet when I came to the east side of it, I found a great ledge of rocks lie out about two leagues into the sea, some above water, some under it; and beyond that a shoal of sand, lying dry half a league more, so that I was obliged to go a great way out to sea to double the point.
paragraphs.cn: 那是十一月六日,我登基——或者你爱说被囚也行——第六个年头,我出发去作这趟航行,却发现它比我预料的要漫长得多;因为岛本身虽不很大,可我到了它东边,却发现有一长排礁石伸进海里约莫两里格,有的露在水面上,有的没在水底下;礁石之外又是一片沙滩浅洲,干出来的地方还有半里格多,弄得我不得不驶出老远的海面才能绕过那个岬角。

paragraphs.en: When I first discovered them, I was going to give over my enterprise, and come back again, not knowing how far it might oblige me to go out to sea; and above all, doubting how I should get back again: so I came to an anchor; for I had made a kind of an anchor with a piece of a broken grappling which I got out of the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我头一回发现这些礁石时,本打算就此罢手,掉头回去,因为不知道它会逼我驶出多远的海;尤其拿不准自己怎么才能再回来;于是我抛下了锚;我用从大船上弄来的一截断铁爪做了个像锚的东西。

paragraphs.en: Having secured my boat, I took my gun and went on shore, climbing up a hill, which seemed to overlook that point where I saw the full extent of it, and resolved to venture.
paragraphs.cn: 把船系稳后,我扛起枪上了岸,爬上一座小山,那山似乎正好俯瞰着那个岬角,从山上我能看清它的全貌,便下决心去冒这个险。

paragraphs.en: In my viewing the sea from that hill where I stood, I perceived a strong, and indeed a most furious current, which ran to the east, and even came close to the point; and I took the more notice of it because I saw there might be some danger that when I came into it I might be carried out to sea by the strength of it, and not be able to make the island again; and indeed, had I not got first upon this hill, I believe it would have been so; for there was the same current on the other side the island, only that it set off at a further distance, and I saw there was a strong eddy under the shore; so I had nothing to do but to get out of the first current, and I should presently be in an eddy.
paragraphs.cn: 我站在那山上眺望海面,看出有一股又强又急、真真凶猛无比的水流朝东奔去,一直逼到那岬角跟前;我格外留了心,因为我看出其中或许有些危险——万一我驶进这股水流,可能会被它那股力气冲到大海里去,再也回不了岛;说真的,若不是我先爬上这座山,只怕真会那样了;因为岛的另一边也有同样一股水流,只是它离岸远些冲开去,而我看出近岸处有一股很强的回流;所以我要做的无非是脱出头一股急流,立刻便能进到回流里。

paragraphs.en: I lay here, however, two days, because the wind blowing pretty fresh at ESE.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我却在这儿耽搁了两天,因为风从东南偏东刮得挺猛。

paragraphs.en: , and that being just contrary to the current, made a great breach of the sea upon the point: so that it was not safe for me to keep too close to the shore for the breach, nor to go too far off, because of the stream.
paragraphs.cn: 这风向恰好和水流顶着,在那岬角上激起了滔天大浪:弄得我既不敢太贴近岸边,怕撞上那大浪,又不敢离得太远,怕陷进那股急流。

paragraphs.en: The third day, in the morning, the wind having abated overnight, the sea was calm, and I ventured: but I am a warning to all rash and ignorant pilots; for no sooner was I come to the point, when I was not even my boat’s length from the shore, but I found myself in a great depth of water, and a current like the sluice of a mill; it carried my boat along with it with such violence that all I could do could not keep her so much as on the edge of it; but I found it hurried me farther and farther out from the eddy, which was on my left hand.
paragraphs.cn: 第三天早上,一夜过后风势减了,海面平静,我便冒险动身;可我要给一切鲁莽无知的舵手当个警戒;因为我刚一驶到那岬角,离岸还不到一船身,就发现自己陷进了极深的水里,水流猛得像磨坊的泄水闸;它挟着我的船横冲直撞,我使出浑身解数也没法把它哪怕稳在急流的边上;我只觉得它把我越冲越远,离开了我左手边的那股回流。

paragraphs.en: There was no wind stirring to help me, and all I could do with my paddles signified nothing: and now I began to give myself over for lost; for as the current was on both sides of the island, I knew in a few leagues distance they must join again, and then I was irrecoverably gone; nor did I see any possibility of avoiding it; so that I had no prospect before me but of perishing, not by the sea, for that was calm enough, but of starving from hunger.
paragraphs.cn: 连一丝风也没有帮我,我拿桨拼命划也全然不济事:这下我开始觉得自己完了;因为那水流在岛两边都有,我知道过不了几里格它们必定又会合到一处,那我就无可挽回地送了命;我也看不出有半点躲开的可能;所以摆在我面前的前程只有一死,倒不是死于大海——海面还够平静的——而是活活饿死。

paragraphs.en: I had, indeed, found a tortoise on the shore, as big almost as I could lift, and had tossed it into the boat; and I had a great jar of fresh water, that is to say, one of my earthen pots; but what was all this to being driven into the vast ocean, where, to be sure, there was no shore, no mainland or island, for a thousand leagues at least?
paragraphs.cn: 说真的,我在岸上曾捉到一只海龟,差不多有我抬得动的那么大,已经扔进了船里;我还有一大罐淡水,也就是我的一只瓦罐;可这一切,眼看要被冲进茫茫大洋里去,又算得了什么?那里头,不用说,一千里格之内怕是连一处海岸、一块大陆、一座海岛都没有。

paragraphs.en: And now I saw how easy it was for the providence of God to make even the most miserable condition of mankind worse.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我才看清,上帝的天意要叫人本已最悲惨的境地变得更糟,是何等容易的事。

paragraphs.en: Now I looked back upon my desolate, solitary island as the most pleasant place in the world and all the happiness my heart could wish for was to be but there again.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我回头望着我那座荒凉冷落的孤岛,只觉它是世上最惬意的地方,我心里所能盼望的全部幸福,不过是能再回到那岛上去。

paragraphs.en: I stretched out my hands to it, with eager wishes—“O happy desert!” said I, “I shall never see thee more.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝着它伸出双手,苦苦地祈愿——“啊,幸福的荒岛!”我说,“我再也见不到你了。

paragraphs.en: O miserable creature! whither am I going?”
paragraphs.cn: 啊,可怜的东西!我这是往哪儿去啊?”

paragraphs.en: Then I reproached myself with my unthankful temper, and that I had repined at my solitary condition; and now what would I give to be on shore there again!
paragraphs.cn: 接着我又责备起自己那副不知感恩的性子,怪自己从前竟对孤零零的处境满腹牢骚;如今我情愿拿什么去换,只求能再回到那岸上啊!

paragraphs.en: Thus, we never see the true state of our condition till it is illustrated to us by its contraries, nor know how to value what we enjoy, but by the want of it.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我们非得等到境况被它的反面一映照,才看得清自己真实的处境;非得等到失去了,才懂得该如何珍惜自己所享有的一切。

paragraphs.en: It is scarcely possible to imagine the consternation I was now in, being driven from my beloved island (for so it appeared to me now to be) into the wide ocean, almost two leagues, and in the utmost despair of ever recovering it again.
paragraphs.cn: 我此刻的惶恐几乎无从想象:被冲离了我心爱的海岛(如今它在我眼里成了心爱之地),漂进茫茫大洋将近两里格,却对能否再回去彻底绝了望。

paragraphs.en: However, I worked hard till, indeed, my strength was almost exhausted, and kept my boat as much to the northward, that is, towards the side of the current which the eddy lay on, as possibly I could; when about noon, as the sun passed the meridian, I thought I felt a little breeze of wind in my face, springing up from SSE.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我还是拼命地划,划到力气几乎耗尽,尽量把船稳在偏北的一侧,也就是靠近那股水流里回流所在的一边;约莫到了正午,太阳过了子午线时,我觉得脸上仿佛有一丝微风,从东南偏南方向吹起。

paragraphs.en: This cheered my heart a little, and especially when, in about half-an-hour more, it blew a pretty gentle gale.
paragraphs.cn: 这叫我心里稍稍宽慰,尤其是又过了大约半个钟头，风竟刮成了一阵挺柔和的顺风。

paragraphs.en: By this time I had got at a frightful distance from the island, and had the least cloudy or hazy weather intervened, I had been undone another way, too; for I had no compass on board, and should never have known how to have steered towards the island, if I had but once lost sight of it; but the weather continuing clear, I applied myself to get up my mast again, and spread my sail, standing away to the north as much as possible, to get out of the current.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我已被冲到离岛骇人的远处,倘若再碰上一点点阴云或雾气插进来,我怕是又要从别的路数上完蛋了;因为我船上没有罗盘,一旦让岛离开我的视线，我就再也不知道该怎么朝岛的方向掌舵;好在天气一直晴朗,我便动手重新竖起桅杆、张开帆，尽量朝北驶去,好脱出那股水流。

paragraphs.en: Just as I had set my mast and sail, and the boat began to stretch away, I saw even by the clearness of the water some alteration of the current was near; for where the current was so strong the water was foul; but perceiving the water clear, I found the current abate; and presently I found to the east, at about half a mile, a breach of the sea upon some rocks: these rocks I found caused the current to part again, and as the main stress of it ran away more southerly, leaving the rocks to the north-east, so the other returned by the repulse of the rocks, and made a strong eddy, which ran back again to the north-west, with a very sharp stream.
paragraphs.cn: 我刚把桅杆和帆装好,船开始破浪前进,单凭水色的清浊我就看出水流快要变了;因为水流最猛的地方水是浑的;可我一见水变清了,就知道水流在减弱;不一会儿我便发现东边约莫半英里处,有一处海浪拍在几块礁石上:我发现正是这些礁石又把水流分了开来,主流朝更偏南的方向奔去,把礁石撇在东北面,而另一股水被礁石顶了回来,形成一股很强的回流,又急又快地朝西北倒流回去。

paragraphs.en: They who know what it is to have a reprieve brought to them upon the ladder, or to be rescued from thieves just going to murder them, or who have been in such extremities, may guess what my present surprise of joy was, and how gladly I put my boat into the stream of this eddy; and the wind also freshening, how gladly I spread my sail to it, running cheerfully before the wind, and with a strong tide or eddy underfoot.
paragraphs.cn: 凡是懂得死到临头、脚踏绞架却被人拿来一纸缓刑赦令是什么滋味的人,或是被人从正要下手行凶的强盗手里救出来的人,或是曾陷入这般绝境的人,大概才猜得出我此刻这份又惊又喜是何等心情,才知道我把船驶进这股回流时是何等欢天喜地;风又转顺了,我又是何等欢喜地朝它张开帆,顺着风快活地驶去,脚下还有一股强劲的潮水或回流托着。
