paragraphs.en: This eddy carried me about a league on my way back again, directly towards the island, but about two leagues more to the northward than the current which carried me away at first; so that when I came near the island, I found myself open to the northern shore of it, that is to say, the other end of the island, opposite to that which I went out from.
paragraphs.cn: 这股回流载着我沿归途走了约莫一里格,径直朝岛驶去,不过比起最初把我卷走的那股水流,它偏北了将近两里格;所以我驶近岛时,发现自己正对着岛的北岸,也就是岛的另一头,和我出发的那一头恰好相反。

paragraphs.en: When I had made something more than a league of way by the help of this current or eddy, I found it was spent, and served me no further.
paragraphs.cn: 靠着这股水流或回流的帮助,我行了一里格出头的路，就发现它劲头用尽，再帮不上我什么忙了。

paragraphs.en: However, I found that being between two great currents—viz. that on the south side, which had hurried me away, and that on the north, which lay about a league on the other side; I say, between these two, in the wake of the island, I found the water at least still, and running no way; and having still a breeze of wind fair for me, I kept on steering directly for the island, though not making such fresh way as I did before.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我发现,自己正夹在两股大水流之间——就是南边那股把我卷走的,和北边那股约莫在另一侧一里格处的;我说,夹在这两股之间、在岛的下风处,我发现水至少是静的,哪个方向也不流;我又还有一阵对我正合适的顺风,便一直径直朝岛掌舵,只是不像先前那样飞快地前进了。

paragraphs.en: About four o’clock in the evening, being then within a league of the island, I found the point of the rocks which occasioned this disaster stretching out, as is described before, to the southward, and casting off the current more southerly, had, of course, made another eddy to the north; and this I found very strong, but not directly setting the way my course lay, which was due west, but almost full north.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚约莫四点钟,我这时离岛已在一里格之内,发现那惹出这场大祸的礁石岬角,像前面说过的那样,朝南伸出去,把水流甩向更偏南的方向,自然又在北边搅出了另一股回流;我发现它很强,却不正好朝我所要走的方向,我的航向是正西,而它几乎是正北。

paragraphs.en: However, having a fresh gale, I stretched across this eddy, slanting north-west; and in about an hour came within about a mile of the shore, where, it being smooth water, I soon got to land.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我趁着一阵顺风,斜着西北方向横穿过这股回流;约莫过了一个钟头,便驶到离岸约莫一英里处,那里水面平稳,我很快就上了岸。

paragraphs.en: When I was on shore, I fell on my knees and gave God thanks for my deliverance, resolving to lay aside all thoughts of my deliverance by my boat; and refreshing myself with such things as I had, I brought my boat close to the shore, in a little cove that I had spied under some trees, and laid me down to sleep, being quite spent with the labour and fatigue of the voyage.
paragraphs.cn: 上了岸,我双膝跪下,感谢上帝搭救了我,决意打消一切靠这条船脱险的念头;我拿手头的东西吃了些歇过力来,把船紧靠着岸,停进我在几棵树下瞧见的一个小湾里,便躺下睡觉,这趟航行的劳累和辛苦已把我彻底累垮了。

paragraphs.en: I was now at a great loss which way to get home with my boat!
paragraphs.cn: 如今我大为犯难:该怎么把船弄回家去呢!

paragraphs.en: I had run so much hazard, and knew too much of the case, to think of attempting it by the way I went out; and what might be at the other side (I mean the west side) I knew not, nor had I any mind to run any more ventures; so I resolved on the next morning to make my way westward along the shore, and to see if there was no creek where I might lay up my frigate in safety, so as to have her again if I wanted her.
paragraphs.cn: 我已冒了那么大的险,把这一路的情形也摸得太清楚了,再不敢想着照来时那条路把船弄回去;至于岛那一头(我是说西边)是什么光景,我不得而知,也无心再去冒什么险;于是我决定第二天早上沿海岸往西走,看看有没有一条小河好把我这艘“战舰”稳稳安顿起来,以便日后要用时还能找到它。

paragraphs.en: In about three miles or thereabouts, coasting the shore, I came to a very good inlet or bay, about a mile over, which narrowed till it came to a very little rivulet or brook, where I found a very convenient harbour for my boat, and where she lay as if she had been in a little dock made on purpose for her.
paragraphs.cn: 沿着海岸走了约莫三英里光景,我来到一处很好的水口或海湾,湾口约莫一英里宽,越往里越窄,到末了收成一条极小的溪流;我在那里给船找到一个非常合适的港湾,它停在里头,就像停在一个特地为它造的小船坞里一样。

paragraphs.en: Here I put in, and having stowed my boat very safe, I went on shore to look about me, and see where I was.
paragraphs.cn: 我把船驶了进去,稳稳当当地泊好,便上岸四下张望,看看自己身在何处。

paragraphs.en: I soon found I had but a little passed by the place where I had been before, when I travelled on foot to that shore; so taking nothing out of my boat but my gun and umbrella, for it was exceedingly hot, I began my march.
paragraphs.cn: 我很快发现,自己不过刚刚越过从前步行到那片岸边时到过的地方一点点;于是船上除了枪和伞什么都没带——因为天热得厉害——我便动身赶路。

paragraphs.en: The way was comfortable enough after such a voyage as I had been upon, and I reached my old bower in the evening, where I found everything standing as I left it; for I always kept it in good order, being, as I said before, my country house.
paragraphs.cn: 经历了我方才那样一趟航行之后,这段路走得够舒坦的了,傍晚我到了我那座旧凉棚,只见一切都还照我离开时的样子摆着;因为我总把它收拾得井井有条,前面说过,那是我的乡下别墅。

paragraphs.en: I got over the fence, and laid me down in the shade to rest my limbs, for I was very weary, and fell asleep; but judge you, if you can, that read my story, what a surprise I must be in when I was awaked out of my sleep by a voice calling me by my name several times, “Robin, Robin, Robin Crusoe: poor Robin Crusoe!
paragraphs.cn: 我翻过篱笆,躺到树荫下歇歇腿脚,因为我实在乏极了,便睡着了;可是读我这故事的人哪,你们若能想象,不妨想想:我从睡梦中被一个声音喊醒时是何等吃惊——那声音一遍遍喊着我的名字:“罗宾,罗宾,罗宾·克鲁索:可怜的罗宾·克鲁索!

paragraphs.en: Where are you, Robin Crusoe?
paragraphs.cn: 你在哪儿呀,罗宾·克鲁索?

paragraphs.en: Where are you?
paragraphs.cn: 你在哪儿呀?

paragraphs.en: Where have you been?”
paragraphs.cn: 你上哪儿去了呀?”

paragraphs.en: I was so dead asleep at first, being fatigued with rowing, or paddling, as it is called, the first part of the day, and with walking the latter part, that I did not wake thoroughly; but dozing thought I dreamed that somebody spoke to me; but as the voice continued to repeat, “Robin Crusoe, Robin Crusoe,” at last I began to wake more perfectly, and was at first dreadfully frightened, and started up in the utmost consternation; but no sooner were my eyes open, but I saw my Poll sitting on the top of the hedge; and immediately knew that it was he that spoke to me; for just in such bemoaning language I had used to talk to him and teach him; and he had learned it so perfectly that he would sit upon my finger, and lay his bill close to my face and cry, “Poor Robin Crusoe!
paragraphs.cn: 起先我睡得死沉死沉的,前半天摇橹划桨(人家管这叫划桨)累坏了,后半天又走了路,所以并没有彻底醒过来;只是迷迷糊糊地当是做梦,梦见有人在跟我说话;可那声音一直重复着“罗宾·克鲁索,罗宾·克鲁索”,末了我才渐渐醒得透彻些,起初吓得要命,惊惶万状地一下子跳了起来;可我眼睛刚一睁开,就看见我那只鹦鹉波尔正蹲在篱笆顶上;我立刻明白是它在跟我说话;因为我平日就用这种叹苦的腔调跟它讲话、教它,它学得烂熟,常蹲在我手指上,把嘴凑近我脸叫着:“可怜的罗宾·克鲁索!

paragraphs.en: Where are you?
paragraphs.cn: 你在哪儿呀?

paragraphs.en: Where have you been?
paragraphs.cn: 你上哪儿去了呀?

paragraphs.en: How came you here?” and such things as I had taught him.
paragraphs.cn: 你怎么到这儿来的呀?”还有别的我教它的话。

paragraphs.en: However, even though I knew it was the parrot, and that indeed it could be nobody else, it was a good while before I could compose myself.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,尽管我明知那是鹦鹉,除了它也断不会是别人,可我还是过了好一会儿才定下神来。

paragraphs.en: First, I was amazed how the creature got thither; and then, how he should just keep about the place, and nowhere else; but as I was well satisfied it could be nobody but honest Poll, I got over it; and holding out my hand, and calling him by his name, “Poll,” the sociable creature came to me, and sat upon my thumb, as he used to do, and continued talking to me, “Poor Robin Crusoe! and how did I come here? and where had I been?” just as if he had been overjoyed to see me again; and so I carried him home along with me.
paragraphs.cn: 起先我诧异这小东西是怎么跑到那儿去的;继而又纳闷它怎么偏偏就守在这地方,别处都不去;可我既然确信除了老实的波尔不会是别人,也就想开了;我伸出手,叫着它的名字“波尔”,这爱亲近人的小东西便飞到我跟前,像往常一样蹲在我大拇指上,不停地跟我念叨:“可怜的罗宾·克鲁索!我是怎么到这儿来的呀?我上哪儿去了呀?”那模样简直像重又见到我而欢喜得不得了;于是我便把它一路带回了家。

paragraphs.en: I had now had enough of rambling to sea for some time, and had enough to do for many days to sit still and reflect upon the danger I had been in.
paragraphs.cn: 这一阵子我到海上瞎逛已逛够了,往后好多天里,光是坐着静静回味我方才所历的凶险,就够我忙的了。

paragraphs.en: I would have been very glad to have had my boat again on my side of the island; but I knew not how it was practicable to get it about.
paragraphs.cn: 我倒很想把船弄回到岛我这一边来;可我不知道有什么法子能把它绕回来。

paragraphs.en: As to the east side of the island, which I had gone round, I knew well enough there was no venturing that way; my very heart would shrink, and my very blood run chill, but to think of it; and as to the other side of the island, I did not know how it might be there; but supposing the current ran with the same force against the shore at the east as it passed by it on the other, I might run the same risk of being driven down the stream, and carried by the island, as I had been before of being carried away from it: so with these thoughts, I contented myself to be without any boat, though it had been the product of so many months’ labour to make it, and of so many more to get it into the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我绕过来的岛东边,我心里再清楚不过,那条路是万万冒险不得的;单是想一想,我的心就直往下缩,血都要凉半截;至于岛的另一边是什么光景,我不得而知;但假如那水流在东边冲向岸边的劲头,和它在这一边掠过时一样猛,那我照样有被它冲下急流、被它顺着岛卷走的危险,一如从前被它卷离海岛那样:所以想到这些,我也就甘心没了船,尽管它是我费了那么多个月的功夫才造成、又费了更多个月的功夫才弄下海的。

paragraphs.en: In this government of my temper I remained near a year; and lived a very sedate, retired life, as you may well suppose; and my thoughts being very much composed as to my condition, and fully comforted in resigning myself to the dispositions of Providence, I thought I lived really very happily in all things except that of society.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样管住自己的性子,过了将近一年;日子过得极安详、极清静,这你尽可想见;我对自己的处境想得很开,又甘心把自己交托给天意的安排,得着了十足的宽慰,我觉得自己样样都活得着实很快活,单单缺个人做伴。

paragraphs.en: I improved myself in this time in all the mechanic exercises which my necessities put me upon applying myself to; and I believe I should, upon occasion, have made a very good carpenter, especially considering how few tools I had.
paragraphs.cn: 这段日子里,凡是境遇逼着我不得不动手去干的各样手艺活,我都练得长进了;我相信,若有机会,我准能当个很不错的木匠,尤其想到我手头的工具那么少。

paragraphs.en: Besides this, I arrived at an unexpected perfection in my earthenware, and contrived well enough to make them with a wheel, which I found infinitely easier and better; because I made things round and shaped, which before were filthy things indeed to look on.
paragraphs.cn: 除此之外,我做陶器也到了出乎意料的娴熟地步,还挺巧妙地想出用转轮来做,我发觉这样省事得多、也好得多;因为我做出来的东西又圆又有模样,而先前做的那些实在丑得没法看。

paragraphs.en: But I think I was never more vain of my own performance, or more joyful for anything I found out, than for my being able to make a tobacco-pipe; and though it was a very ugly, clumsy thing when it was done, and only burned red, like other earthenware, yet as it was hard and firm, and would draw the smoke, I was exceedingly comforted with it, for I had been always used to smoke; and there were pipes in the ship, but I forgot them at first, not thinking there was tobacco in the island; and afterwards, when I searched the ship again, I could not come at any pipes.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我想,我平生没有哪回比做成一只烟斗时更为自己的手艺得意,或为自己捣鼓出来的什么东西更欢喜的了;那烟斗做成时虽是个又丑又笨的玩意儿,烧出来也只泛红,跟别的陶器一样,可它既硬实又结实,又抽得动烟,我便拿它得着了极大的安慰,因为我素来抽烟抽惯了;大船上本有烟斗,可我起先忘了,没想到岛上会有烟叶;后来我再去搜那船时,就再也弄不到一只烟斗了。

paragraphs.en: In my wicker-ware also I improved much, and made abundance of necessary baskets, as well as my invention showed me; though not very handsome, yet they were such as were very handy and convenient for laying things up in, or fetching things home.
paragraphs.cn: 我编柳条器物的手艺也大有长进,凭着自己想出的样式,做了好大一批用得着的篮子;虽说不很好看,却都很趁手、很方便,用来收放东西或往家里搬东西。

paragraphs.en: For example, if I killed a goat abroad, I could hang it up in a tree, flay it, dress it, and cut it in pieces, and bring it home in a basket; and the like by a turtle; I could cut it up, take out the eggs and a piece or two of the flesh, which was enough for me, and bring them home in a basket, and leave the rest behind me.
paragraphs.cn: 比方说,我在外头打了只山羊,可以把它挂在树上,剥皮、收拾、切成块,再用篮子提回家;海龟也一样,我可以把它剖开,取出蛋和一两块肉——够我吃就行——用篮子提回家,余下的就撇在那里。

paragraphs.en: Also, large deep baskets were the receivers of my corn, which I always rubbed out as soon as it was dry and cured, and kept it in great baskets.
paragraphs.cn: 还有,又大又深的篮子是我盛谷子的家什,谷子一晒干弄好,我总立刻搓下来,收在大篮子里。

paragraphs.en: I began now to perceive my powder abated considerably; this was a want which it was impossible for me to supply, and I began seriously to consider what I must do when I should have no more powder; that is to say, how I should kill any goats.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我开始察觉自己的火药少得厉害了;这是件我怎么也没法补上的缺欠,我便认真盘算起来:等我再没有火药时该怎么办;这也就是说,我该怎么打山羊。

paragraphs.en: I had, as is observed in the third year of my being here, kept a young kid, and bred her up tame, and I was in hopes of getting a he-goat; but I could not by any means bring it to pass, till my kid grew an old goat; and as I could never find in my heart to kill her, she died at last of mere age.
paragraphs.cn: 前面说过,我到这儿第三年时曾养过一只小母羊,把她驯养大了,一心指望能弄到一只公羊;可我无论如何也办不成,直到我那小母羊长成了老山羊;我又始终狠不下心杀她,末了她纯是老死的。

paragraphs.en: But being now in the eleventh year of my residence, and, as I have said, my ammunition growing low, I set myself to study some art to trap and snare the goats, to see whether I could not catch some of them alive; and particularly I wanted a she-goat great with young.
paragraphs.cn: 可如今我在此栖居已到第十一个年头,又如我说过的,弹药越来越少,便着手琢磨些捕山羊的法子,想看看能不能活捉几只;我尤其想要一只怀着崽的母羊。

paragraphs.en: For this purpose I made snares to hamper them; and I do believe they were more than once taken in them; but my tackle was not good, for I had no wire, and I always found them broken and my bait devoured.
paragraphs.cn: 为此我做了些套子想套住它们;我也确信不止一次真套住过;可我的家什不济事,因为我没有铁丝,总发现套子被挣断了,诱饵也被吃光了。

paragraphs.en: At length I resolved to try a pitfall; so I dug several large pits in the earth, in places where I had observed the goats used to feed, and over those pits I placed hurdles of my own making too, with a great weight upon them; and several times I put ears of barley and dry rice without setting the trap; and I could easily perceive that the goats had gone in and eaten up the corn, for I could see the marks of their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 末了我决意试试挖陷阱;于是我在几处观察到山羊常来吃草的地方挖了几个大坑,又在坑上盖了些自己做的柴排,上头压着很重的东西;有好几次我只放大麦穗和干稻子,不去设机关;我一眼就看得出山羊进去把谷子吃光了,因为我看得见它们的蹄印。

paragraphs.en: At length I set three traps in one night, and going the next morning I found them, all standing, and yet the bait eaten and gone; this was very discouraging.
paragraphs.cn: 末了我一夜里设了三个陷阱,第二天早上去看,发现三个都好端端支着,诱饵却被吃得精光;这真叫人泄气。

paragraphs.en: However, I altered my traps; and not to trouble you with particulars, going one morning to see my traps, I found in one of them a large old he-goat; and in one of the others three kids, a male and two females.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我改动了陷阱;闲话不细说了,一天早上我去看陷阱,发现其中一个里困住了一只又大又老的公羊;另外一个里困着三只小羊,一公两母。

paragraphs.en: As to the old one, I knew not what to do with him; he was so fierce I durst not go into the pit to him; that is to say, to bring him away alive, which was what I wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那只老的,我真不知拿它怎么办才好;它凶得很,我不敢下坑到它跟前去;我是说,不敢去把它活着弄出来,而这正是我想要的。

paragraphs.en: I could have killed him, but that was not my business, nor would it answer my end; so I even let him out, and he ran away as if he had been frightened out of his wits.
paragraphs.cn: 我倒是可以把它杀了,可那不是我要办的事,也成全不了我的目的;于是我索性把它放了出来,它撒腿就跑,像是吓破了胆似的。

paragraphs.en: But I did not then know what I afterwards learned, that hunger will tame a lion.
paragraphs.cn: 可我那时还不懂后来才悟到的道理:饥饿能驯服一头狮子。

paragraphs.en: If I had let him stay three or four days without food, and then have carried him some water to drink and then a little corn, he would have been as tame as one of the kids; for they are mighty sagacious, tractable creatures, where they are well used.
paragraphs.cn: 我若让它饿上三四天不给食,再给它送点水喝、送点谷子,它准会驯得跟那几只小羊一样;因为这种牲口只要待它好,是极机灵、极听话的。

paragraphs.en: However, for the present I let him go, knowing no better at that time: then I went to the three kids, and taking them one by one, I tied them with strings together, and with some difficulty brought them all home.
paragraphs.cn: 不过眼下我还是把它放走了,那时我不懂更好的法子:接着我去看那三只小羊,一只只逮住,用绳子把它们拴在一处,费了些劲总算把它们全带回了家。

paragraphs.en: It was a good while before they would feed; but throwing them some sweet corn, it tempted them, and they began to be tame.
paragraphs.cn: 起先好久它们都不肯吃食;可我扔给它们些甜谷子,勾起了它们的馋,它们便渐渐驯服了。

paragraphs.en: And now I found that if I expected to supply myself with goats’ flesh, when I had no powder or shot left, breeding some up tame was my only way, when, perhaps, I might have them about my house like a flock of sheep.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我明白了,倘若我指望等火药铅弹用尽后还能给自己弄到羊肉吃,唯一的门路就是驯养几只;这么一来,说不定我房子四周就能有它们,像养一群绵羊似的。

paragraphs.en: But then it occurred to me that I must keep the tame from the wild, or else they would always run wild when they grew up; and the only way for this was to have some enclosed piece of ground, well fenced either with hedge or pale, to keep them in so effectually, that those within might not break out, or those without break in.
paragraphs.cn: 可紧接着我又想到,我必须把驯的和野的隔开,不然它们长大了总要跑野的;而唯一的法子,就是有一块围起来的地,拿篱笆或木栅牢牢圈住,把它们关得严严实实,叫里头的出不去,外头的进不来。

paragraphs.en: This was a great undertaking for one pair of hands; yet, as I saw there was an absolute necessity for doing it, my first work was to find out a proper piece of ground, where there was likely to be herbage for them to eat, water for them to drink, and cover to keep them from the sun.
paragraphs.cn: 这在我一双手来说是桩大工程;可我既看出这事非做不可,头一件活便是找出一块合适的地,那里得有草给它们吃、有水给它们喝、有遮荫的地方替它们挡太阳。

paragraphs.en: Those who understand such enclosures will think I had very little contrivance when I pitched upon a place very proper for all these (being a plain, open piece of meadow land, or savannah, as our people call it in the western colonies), which had two or three little drills of fresh water in it, and at one end was very woody—I say, they will smile at my forecast, when I shall tell them I began by enclosing this piece of ground in such a manner that, my hedge or pale must have been at least two miles about.
paragraphs.cn: 懂得这类圈地的人,见我挑中一块对这些条件样样都极合适的地(那是一片平坦开阔的草甸,或者叫热带草原,我们在西边殖民地的人是这么叫它的),里头有两三道小小的淡水沟,一头林木很密——我说,他们准会笑话我这盘算,等我告诉他们:我一开头竟打算把这块地这么圈起来,篱笆或木栅少说也得围上两英里长。

paragraphs.en: Nor was the madness of it so great as to the compass, for if it was ten miles about, I was like to have time enough to do it in; but I did not consider that my goats would be as wild in so much compass as if they had had the whole island, and I should have so much room to chase them in that I should never catch them.
paragraphs.cn: 就周长而论,这倒还不算多么疯:因为哪怕要围十英里,我大概也有的是工夫来干;可我没想到,地方这么大,我那些山羊照样会像占了整座岛一样野,我便有那么大的地方去追它们,结果永远也逮不着。

paragraphs.en: My hedge was begun and carried on, I believe, about fifty yards when this thought occurred to me; so I presently stopped short, and, for the beginning, I resolved to enclose a piece of about one hundred and fifty yards in length, and one hundred yards in breadth, which, as it would maintain as many as I should have in any reasonable time, so, as my stock increased, I could add more ground to my enclosure.
paragraphs.cn: 我记得篱笆动了工、往前修了约莫五十码时,才想到了这一层;于是我立刻停了手,打头一步,决意先圈一块约莫一百五十码长、一百码宽的地,这块地在任何一段合情合理的时间里,足够养活我所能有的那么多羊;日后我的羊群多起来,还可以再往圈里添地。

paragraphs.en: This was acting with some prudence, and I went to work with courage.
paragraphs.cn: 这样做才算有几分精明,我便鼓起勇气动了工。

paragraphs.en: I was about three months hedging in the first piece; and, till I had done it, I tethered the three kids in the best part of it, and used them to feed as near me as possible, to make them familiar; and very often I would go and carry them some ears of barley, or a handful of rice, and feed them out of my hand; so that after my enclosure was finished and I let them loose, they would follow me up and down, bleating after me for a handful of corn.
paragraphs.cn: 头一块地我圈篱笆花了约莫三个月;没圈好之前,我把那三只小羊拴在地里最好的一块,让它们尽量在离我近的地方吃草,好和我混熟;我还常去给它们送些大麦穗或一把稻子,亲手喂它们;这么一来,等我圈好篱笆放它们出来时,它们便前前后后跟着我,咩咩地跟在我后头讨一把谷子吃。

paragraphs.en: This answered my end, and in about a year and a half I had a flock of about twelve goats, kids and all; and in two years more I had three-and-forty, besides several that I took and killed for my food.
paragraphs.cn: 这正遂了我的心愿,约莫一年半光景,我便有了一群约莫十二只的山羊,连小羊算在内;再过两年,我便有了四十三只,还不算我另外逮来杀了吃的好几只。

paragraphs.en: After that, I enclosed five several pieces of ground to feed them in, with little pens to drive them to take them as I wanted, and gates out of one piece of ground into another.
paragraphs.cn: 打那以后,我又圈了五块地来喂它们,每块都带着小栏圈,好把它们赶进去、需要时逮取,还有从这块地通到那块地的栅门。

paragraphs.en: But this was not all; for now I not only had goat’s flesh to feed on when I pleased, but milk too—a thing which, indeed, in the beginning, I did not so much as think of, and which, when it came into my thoughts, was really an agreeable surprise, for now I set up my dairy, and had sometimes a gallon or two of milk in a day.
paragraphs.cn: 可这还不算完;因为如今我不但想吃羊肉就有羊肉吃,还有了奶——这东西说真的我起初压根没想到过,等它闯进我脑子里时,着实是个惬意的意外之喜,因为我这就办起了奶坊,有时一天能挤上一两加仑奶。

paragraphs.en: And as Nature, who gives supplies of food to every creature, dictates even naturally how to make use of it, so I, that had never milked a cow, much less a goat, or seen butter or cheese made only when I was a boy, after a great many essays and miscarriages, made both butter and cheese at last, also salt (though I found it partly made to my hand by the heat of the sun upon some of the rocks of the sea), and never wanted it afterwards.
paragraphs.cn: 大自然既给每样生灵备下食物,也就自然而然地点拨它们如何去享用;我这个从没挤过牛奶、更别提挤羊奶,除了小时候也没见过做黄油、做奶酪的人,经过许许多多回试验和失手,末了竟做成了黄油和奶酪,还做出了盐(虽说我发现日头晒在海边几块礁石上,已替我把盐半做成了),从此再也不缺它了。

paragraphs.en: How mercifully can our Creator treat His creatures, even in those conditions in which they seemed to be overwhelmed in destruction!
paragraphs.cn: 我们的造物主待祂的生灵是何等慈悲啊,哪怕在那些眼看要被毁灭所吞没的境地里也是如此!

paragraphs.en: How can He sweeten the bitterest providences, and give us cause to praise Him for dungeons and prisons!
paragraphs.cn: 祂能把最苦涩的天意变甜,让我们连身陷地牢和监狱也有缘由去赞美祂!

paragraphs.en: What a table was here spread for me in the wilderness, where I saw nothing at first but to perish for hunger!
paragraphs.cn: 在这片荒野里,竟为我摆开了怎样一桌盛筵啊——而我起初在这里看到的,除了活活饿死之外一无所有!

chapters.title_en: Finds Print Of Man’S Foot On The Sand

paragraphs.en: It would have made a Stoic smile to have seen me and my little family sit down to dinner.
paragraphs.cn: 看到我和我的小家庭坐下来吃饭的情景，连斯多葛派的哲人也会忍不住发笑。

paragraphs.en: There was my majesty the prince and lord of the whole island; I had the lives of all my subjects at my absolute command; I could hang, draw, give liberty, and take it away, and no rebels among all my subjects.
paragraphs.cn: 我俨然是全岛的君王和领主；所有臣民的性命都由我绝对支配；我可以处死、可以处置、可以给予自由，也可以收回自由，而我的臣民中没有一个反叛者。

paragraphs.en: Then, to see how like a king I dined, too, all alone, attended by my servants!
paragraphs.cn: 再看看我用膳时那副俨然帝王的派头吧，独自一人，还有仆从伺候着！

paragraphs.en: Poll, as if he had been my favourite, was the only person permitted to talk to me.
paragraphs.cn: 波儿，就像是我的宠臣，是唯一获准跟我说话的。

paragraphs.en: My dog, who was now grown old and crazy, and had found no species to multiply his kind upon, sat always at my right hand; and two cats, one on one side of the table and one on the other, expecting now and then a bit from my hand, as a mark of especial favour.
paragraphs.cn: 我那条狗如今已经又老又糊涂，找不到同类繁衍后代，总是坐在我的右手边；还有两只猫，一只坐桌子这头，一只坐那头，时不时地等着从我手里讨一口吃食，那可是格外的恩宠。

paragraphs.en: But these were not the two cats which I brought on shore at first, for they were both of them dead, and had been interred near my habitation by my own hand; but one of them having multiplied by I know not what kind of creature, these were two which I had preserved tame; whereas the rest ran wild in the woods, and became indeed troublesome to me at last, for they would often come into my house, and plunder me too, till at last I was obliged to shoot them, and did kill a great many; at length they left me.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这两只猫并不是我当初带上岸的那两只，因为那两只都已经死了，还是我亲手把它们埋在住处附近的；其中一只不知跟什么野物交配繁衍，这两只就是我养熟留下来的；其余的都跑进树林里野化了，到最后实在成了我的麻烦，因为它们常跑进我屋里来劫掠，逼得我最终只好开枪打它们，杀了不少；到后来它们才总算离开了我。

paragraphs.en: With this attendance and in this plentiful manner I lived; neither could I be said to want anything but society; and of that, some time after this, I was likely to have too much.
paragraphs.cn: 我就是靠着这样的伺候、过着这般富足的日子；要说我缺什么，也就只缺个伴儿罢了；可就连这个，过不多久，我恐怕反倒要嫌太多了。

paragraphs.en: I was something impatient, as I have observed, to have the use of my boat, though very loath to run any more hazards; and therefore sometimes I sat contriving ways to get her about the island, and at other times I sat myself down contented enough without her.
paragraphs.cn: 如前所述，我心里有些按捺不住，想把我那条船用起来，可又实在不愿再去冒什么险；因此我有时坐着琢磨怎样把船弄到岛的那一边去，有时又干脆没有它也心满意足地坐着。

paragraphs.en: But I had a strange uneasiness in my mind to go down to the point of the island where, as I have said in my last ramble, I went up the hill to see how the shore lay, and how the current set, that I might see what I had to do: this inclination increased upon me every day, and at length I resolved to travel thither by land, following the edge of the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 可我心里总有一种莫名的不安，想到岛的那个岬角去——就是我上回漫游时说过的，我爬上那座山，看海岸的走势、看水流的方向，好弄清自己该怎么办；这念头一天天在我心里增强，最后我下定决心要走陆路过去，沿着海岸边缘走。

paragraphs.en: I did so; but had any one in England met such a man as I was, it must either have frightened him, or raised a great deal of laughter; and as I frequently stood still to look at myself, I could not but smile at the notion of my travelling through Yorkshire with such an equipage, and in such a dress.
paragraphs.cn: 我果然去了；可要是在英格兰有谁碰见我这样一个人，准会被吓一跳，要不就哈哈大笑；我自己也常常停下来端详自己，一想到我竟穿着这样一身行头、这样一副打扮走过约克郡，就忍不住要笑。

paragraphs.en: Be pleased to take a sketch of my figure, as follows.
paragraphs.cn: 那就请看看我这副模样的素描吧，如下。

paragraphs.en: I had a great high shapeless cap, made of a goat’s skin, with a flap hanging down behind, as well to keep the sun from me as to shoot the rain off from running into my neck, nothing being so hurtful in these climates as the rain upon the flesh under the clothes.
paragraphs.cn: 我戴着一顶又高又大、不成形状的帽子，用山羊皮做的，后面还垂着一块帽帘，既能替我遮太阳，也能挡住雨水顺着脖子流进衣领；在这种气候里，最伤身的莫过于雨水淋到衣服底下的皮肉上。

paragraphs.en: I had a short jacket of goat’s skin, the skirts coming down to about the middle of the thighs, and a pair of open-kneed breeches of the same; the breeches were made of the skin of an old he-goat, whose hair hung down such a length on either side that, like pantaloons, it reached to the middle of my legs; stockings and shoes I had none, but had made me a pair of somethings, I scarce knew what to call them, like buskins, to flap over my legs, and lace on either side like spatterdashes, but of a most barbarous shape, as indeed were all the rest of my clothes.
paragraphs.cn: 我穿着一件羊皮短上衣，衣摆垂到大腿中段，还有一条同样质料、膝盖敞口的短裤；短裤是用一只老公羊的皮做的，两侧的毛垂得老长，像马裤一样一直垂到我的小腿中间；袜子和鞋子我都没有，只给自己做了一双不知该叫什么的玩意儿，像是半高筒靴，罩在小腿上，两边系带子，像绑腿一样，样子却野蛮透顶，其实我别的衣物也都是这德性。

paragraphs.en: I had on a broad belt of goat’s skin dried, which I drew together with two thongs of the same instead of buckles, and in a kind of a frog on either side of this, instead of a sword and dagger, hung a little saw and a hatchet, one on one side and one on the other.
paragraphs.cn: 我腰间系着一条晒干的羊皮宽腰带，用两根同样质料的皮条系拢，权当扣子用；腰带两侧各有一个套环似的东西，不挂剑和匕首，却挂着一把小锯子和一把小斧头，一边一个。

paragraphs.en: I had another belt not so broad, and fastened in the same manner, which hung over my shoulder, and at the end of it, under my left arm, hung two pouches, both made of goat’s skin too, in one of which hung my powder, in the other my shot.
paragraphs.cn: 我还有另一条没那么宽的带子，也是同样系法，斜挎在肩上，带子末端、我左臂下面，挂着两个袋子，也都是羊皮做的，一个里面装火药，另一个装弹丸。

paragraphs.en: At my back I carried my basket, and on my shoulder my gun, and over my head a great clumsy, ugly, goat’s-skin umbrella, but which, after all, was the most necessary thing I had about me next to my gun.
paragraphs.cn: 我背上背着筐子，肩上扛着枪，头顶还撑着一把又大又笨、又丑的羊皮伞，可说到底，这伞是我随身除枪之外最不可缺的东西。

paragraphs.en: As for my face, the colour of it was really not so mulatto-like as one might expect from a man not at all careful of it, and living within nine or ten degrees of the equinox.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我这张脸，肤色其实还不像人们料想的那样黑；要知道我是个对自己毫不上心的人，又住在离赤道只有九、十度的地方。

paragraphs.en: My beard I had once suffered to grow till it was about a quarter of a yard long; but as I had both scissors and razors sufficient, I had cut it pretty short, except what grew on my upper lip, which I had trimmed into a large pair of Mahometan whiskers, such as I had seen worn by some Turks at Sallee, for the Moors did not wear such, though the Turks did; of these moustachios, or whiskers, I will not say they were long enough to hang my hat upon them, but they were of a length and shape monstrous enough, and such as in England would have passed for frightful.
paragraphs.cn: 我的胡子曾经任它长到差不多四分之一码长；不过我有足够的剪刀和剃刀，就把它剪得挺短，只留下上唇那撮，修成两大绺穆罕默德式的髭须，就像我在萨累见过一些土耳其人蓄的那样，摩尔人并不留这种，土耳其人却留；这两撇髭须，我不敢说长得够挂帽子，可那长度和样子也着实骇人，搁在英格兰准会被当作吓人的怪物。

paragraphs.en: But all this is by-the-bye; for as to my figure, I had so few to observe me that it was of no manner of consequence, so I say no more of that.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这些都是题外话了；就我这副模样而言，反正也没几个人瞧我，实在无关紧要，所以就不多说了。

paragraphs.en: In this kind of dress I went my new journey, and was out five or six days.
paragraphs.cn: 我就这样一身打扮踏上了新的旅程，在外头待了五六天。

paragraphs.en: I travelled first along the sea-shore, directly to the place where I first brought my boat to an anchor to get upon the rocks; and having no boat now to take care of, I went over the land a nearer way to the same height that I was upon before, when, looking forward to the points of the rocks which lay out, and which I was obliged to double with my boat, as is said above, I was surprised to see the sea all smooth and quiet—no rippling, no motion, no current, any more there than in other places.
paragraphs.cn: 我先沿着海岸走，径直奔向我当初把船抛锚、好爬上礁石的那个地方；如今用不着照看船了，我就抄近路走陆路，来到我从前登上过的那处高地；往前望去，看见那些突出的礁石尖角——就是前面说过、我不得不驾船绕过的那些——我惊讶地发现那儿海面竟一片平静，没有波纹、没有涌动、没有水流，跟别处一模一样。

paragraphs.en: I was at a strange loss to understand this, and resolved to spend some time in the observing it, to see if nothing from the sets of the tide had occasioned it; but I was presently convinced how it was—viz. that the tide of ebb setting from the west, and joining with the current of waters from some great river on the shore, must be the occasion of this current, and that, according as the wind blew more forcibly from the west or from the north, this current came nearer or went farther from the shore; for, waiting thereabouts till evening, I went up to the rock again, and then the tide of ebb being made, I plainly saw the current again as before, only that it ran farther off, being near half a league from the shore, whereas in my case it set close upon the shore, and hurried me and my canoe along with it, which at another time it would not have done.
paragraphs.cn: 我一时怎么也弄不明白这是怎么回事，便决定花些时间观察一番，看看是不是潮汐涨落造成的；可我很快就明白了原委——就是说，退潮的水流从西边下来，跟岸上某条大河的水流汇合，一定就是这股水流的成因；而且随着风从西边或北边吹得更猛，这股水流便离岸更近或更远；因为我在那一带一直等到傍晚，又爬上那礁石，这时退潮起了，我清清楚楚又看见了那股水流，跟先前一样，只是这回离岸更远，约莫离岸半里格，而我上回遇上时它却是紧贴着岸走，把我连人带独木舟一齐卷了去，换个时候它是不会这样的。

paragraphs.en: This observation convinced me that I had nothing to do but to observe the ebbing and the flowing of the tide, and I might very easily bring my boat about the island again; but when I began to think of putting it in practice, I had such terror upon my spirits at the remembrance of the danger I had been in, that I could not think of it again with any patience, but, on the contrary, I took up another resolution, which was more safe, though more laborious—and this was, that I would build, or rather make, me another periagua or canoe, and so have one for one side of the island, and one for the other.
paragraphs.cn: 这番观察使我明白，我只消留意潮水的涨落，就能轻而易举地把船弄到岛的那一边去；可等我一动手要付诸实行，一想起先前遭遇的凶险，心头就涌起那样的恐惧，叫我怎么也没耐心再去想它；恰恰相反，我另拿了个主意，虽然更费力气，却更稳妥——那就是我要再造，或者说再做一条独木舟，这样岛的这一边有一条，那一边也有一条。

paragraphs.en: You are to understand that now I had, as I may call it, two plantations in the island—one my little fortification or tent, with the wall about it, under the rock, with the cave behind me, which by this time I had enlarged into several apartments or caves, one within another.
paragraphs.cn: 你得知道，如今我在岛上可以说有了两处田庄了——一处是我那小小的营垒或者说帐篷，四周围着墙，坐落在岩壁下，背后是山洞，到这时候我已经把它扩成了好几间套间或者说洞室，一间套着一间。

paragraphs.en: One of these, which was the driest and largest, and had a door out beyond my wall or fortification—that is to say, beyond where my wall joined to the rock—was all filled up with the large earthen pots of which I have given an account, and with fourteen or fifteen great baskets, which would hold five or six bushels each, where I laid up my stores of provisions, especially my corn, some in the ear, cut off short from the straw, and the other rubbed out with my hand.
paragraphs.cn: 其中一间最干燥、最宽敞，还有一道门通到我墙外或者说营垒之外——也就是我那墙跟岩壁相接的地方之外——里头全堆满了我前面讲过的那些大陶罐，还有十四五个大筐子，每个能装五六蒲式耳，我把储粮都囤在里头，尤其是我的谷子，有些还带着穗、贴着秸秆割下的，另一些是我用手搓下来的。

paragraphs.en: As for my wall, made, as before, with long stakes or piles, those piles grew all like trees, and were by this time grown so big, and spread so very much, that there was not the least appearance, to any one’s view, of any habitation behind them.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我那道墙，还是像先前一样用长木桩或木柱打成的，那些木桩全都像树一样长起来了，到这时候已经长得那么粗、枝叶铺展得那么开，谁从外头看都瞧不出后面有半点住人的痕迹。

paragraphs.en: Near this dwelling of mine, but a little farther within the land, and upon lower ground, lay my two pieces of corn land, which I kept duly cultivated and sowed, and which duly yielded me their harvest in its season; and whenever I had occasion for more corn, I had more land adjoining as fit as that.
paragraphs.cn: 紧挨着我这住处，不过再往岛内深些、地势较低的地方，是我那两块谷田，我按时耕种播撒，到季节它们也如期给我收成；每当我需要更多谷子时，旁边还有别的地，跟这块一样合用。

paragraphs.en: Besides this, I had my country seat, and I had now a tolerable plantation there also; for, first, I had my little bower, as I called it, which I kept in repair—that is to say, I kept the hedge which encircled it in constantly fitted up to its usual height, the ladder standing always in the inside.
paragraphs.cn: 除此之外，我还有我的乡间别墅，如今那儿也有了一处像样的田庄；因为，首先，我有我那座小凉亭，我称它作凉亭，一直修葺着——就是说，环绕它的篱笆我经常照原来的高度补齐，梯子始终搁在里边。

paragraphs.en: I kept the trees, which at first were no more than stakes, but were now grown very firm and tall, always cut, so that they might spread and grow thick and wild, and make the more agreeable shade, which they did effectually to my mind.
paragraphs.cn: 那些树，起初不过是些木桩，如今已长得又结实又高大，我一直把它们修剪着，好让它们向四面铺展、长得又密又野，撑出更宜人的树荫，这一点它们确实如我所愿地办到了。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of this I had my tent always standing, being a piece of a sail spread over poles, set up for that purpose, and which never wanted any repair or renewing; and under this I had made me a squab or couch with the skins of the creatures I had killed, and with other soft things, and a blanket laid on them, such as belonged to our sea-bedding, which I had saved; and a great watch-coat to cover me.
paragraphs.cn: 在这凉亭正中，我的帐篷一直支着，是用一块帆布张在几根柱子上、为此专门搭起来的，从来不用修补或翻新；帐篷底下我给自己做了张矮榻或者说卧铺，用我打死的野兽皮和别的软和东西铺成，上面铺一条毯子，是从我们船上寝具里抢救下来的；还有一件大厚外套用来盖身。

paragraphs.en: And here, whenever I had occasion to be absent from my chief seat, I took up my country habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 在这里，每当我有事要离开我的主居所，就到这乡间住处来落脚。

paragraphs.en: Adjoining to this I had my enclosures for my cattle, that is to say my goats, and I had taken an inconceivable deal of pains to fence and enclose this ground.
paragraphs.cn: 紧挨着这地方是我给牲口——也就是我的山羊——圈的围栏，为了给这块地围栏设障，我下过难以想象的一番苦功。

paragraphs.en: I was so anxious to see it kept entire, lest the goats should break through, that I never left off till, with infinite labour, I had stuck the outside of the hedge so full of small stakes, and so near to one another, that it was rather a pale than a hedge, and there was scarce room to put a hand through between them; which afterwards, when those stakes grew, as they all did in the next rainy season, made the enclosure strong like a wall, indeed stronger than any wall.
paragraphs.cn: 我一心想让它保持完整，生怕山羊冲破跑出去，于是不停地干，费尽千辛万苦，把篱笆外侧密密地插满小木桩，彼此挨得那么近，与其说是篱笆，不如说是一道栅栏，桩子之间连伸只手进去的空隙都不剩；后来到下一个雨季，那些木桩全长了起来，这围栏便结实得像堵墙，实在比任何墙都还结实。

paragraphs.en: This will testify for me that I was not idle, and that I spared no pains to bring to pass whatever appeared necessary for my comfortable support, for I considered the keeping up a breed of tame creatures thus at my hand would be a living magazine of flesh, milk, butter, and cheese for me as long as I lived in the place, if it were to be forty years; and that keeping them in my reach depended entirely upon my perfecting my enclosures to such a degree that I might be sure of keeping them together; which by this method, indeed, I so effectually secured, that when these little stakes began to grow, I had planted them so very thick that I was forced to pull some of them up again.
paragraphs.cn: 这可以为我作证，我并没有偷懒，凡是为了叫自己过得舒坦、看来必要的事，我都不惜力气去办；因为我盘算着，把一群驯养的牲口这样养在手边，就等于给我备下一座活的肉库，只要我还住在这地方，哪怕是四十年，也不愁没有肉、奶、黄油和奶酪；而要把它们留在手边，全靠我把围栏修到那样牢固的地步，好保证能把它们圈拢在一处；用这个法子，我确实办得极其稳妥，以致这些小木桩一开始长起来，我才发觉自己当初栽得太密，不得不又拔掉了一些。

paragraphs.en: In this place also I had my grapes growing, which I principally depended on for my winter store of raisins, and which I never failed to preserve very carefully, as the best and most agreeable dainty of my whole diet; and indeed they were not only agreeable, but medicinal, wholesome, nourishing, and refreshing to the last degree.
paragraphs.cn: 在这地方我还种着葡萄，我过冬储备的葡萄干主要就指望着它，我从没有一回不小心翼翼地把它们保存好，那可是我全部食物里最好、最合口的珍馐；说真的，它们不光可口，还能入药、有益健康、滋补身子、又格外提神。

paragraphs.en: As this was also about half-way between my other habitation and the place where I had laid up my boat, I generally stayed and lay here in my way thither, for I used frequently to visit my boat; and I kept all things about or belonging to her in very good order.
paragraphs.cn: 由于这地方又正好在我另一处住所和我藏船的地方之间、大约走一半路的位置，我去那边时通常就在这儿歇脚过夜，因为我常去看我的船；凡是船上或跟船有关的一切，我都收拾得井井有条。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes I went out in her to divert myself, but no more hazardous voyages would I go, scarcely ever above a stone’s cast or two from the shore, I was so apprehensive of being hurried out of my knowledge again by the currents or winds, or any other accident.
paragraphs.cn: 有时我也划船出去散散心，可再危险的航程我是不肯去的了，几乎从不敢离岸超过一两石之遥，我实在太害怕再被水流或大风、或别的什么意外把我卷到不知何处去了。

paragraphs.en: But now I come to a new scene of my life.
paragraphs.cn: 可如今我要说到我人生中一个新的场面了。

paragraphs.en: It happened one day, about noon, going towards my boat, I was exceedingly surprised with the print of a man’s naked foot on the shore, which was very plain to be seen on the sand.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，约莫正午时分，我正往船那边走，忽然极其惊骇地看见岸上沙地上有一个赤脚的人的脚印，清清楚楚地印在沙上。

paragraphs.en: I stood like one thunderstruck, or as if I had seen an apparition.
paragraphs.cn: 我像遭了雷击一般站住了，又仿佛见了鬼魂似的。

paragraphs.en: I listened, I looked round me, but I could hear nothing, nor see anything; I went up to a rising ground to look farther; I went up the shore and down the shore, but it was all one; I could see no other impression but that one.
paragraphs.cn: 我侧耳细听，四下张望，可什么也听不见，什么也看不见；我登上一块高地想看得远些；我沿岸往上走、往下走，可都一个样；除了那一个脚印，我再看不到别的印记。

paragraphs.en: I went to it again to see if there were any more, and to observe if it might not be my fancy; but there was no room for that, for there was exactly the print of a foot—toes, heel, and every part of a foot.
paragraphs.cn: 我又回到那儿，看看还有没有别的，也想弄清是不是我的幻觉；可容不得我这么想，因为那分明就是一个脚印——脚趾、脚跟、脚的每一部分都在。

paragraphs.en: How it came thither I knew not, nor could I in the least imagine; but after innumerable fluttering thoughts, like a man perfectly confused and out of myself, I came home to my fortification, not feeling, as we say, the ground I went on, but terrified to the last degree, looking behind me at every two or three steps, mistaking every bush and tree, and fancying every stump at a distance to be a man.
paragraphs.cn: 它是怎么来的，我毫无头绪，连一点也想不出；可在无数纷乱的念头翻腾过后，我像个彻底懵了、魂不附体的人，回到了我的营垒，脚踩在地上，用俗话说，都没了感觉，只是恐惧到了极点，每走两三步就回头望一眼，把每一丛灌木、每一棵树都看错了，远处的每一个树桩都疑心是个人。

paragraphs.en: Nor is it possible to describe how many various shapes my affrighted imagination represented things to me in, how many wild ideas were found every moment in my fancy, and what strange, unaccountable whimsies came into my thoughts by the way.
paragraphs.cn: 我那惊恐的想象把种种东西幻化成多少花样，我脑子里每一刻涌出多少狂乱的念头，一路上又有多少稀奇古怪、莫名其妙的胡思乱想钻进我心里，实在无法形容。

paragraphs.en: When I came to my castle (for so I think I called it ever after this), I fled into it like one pursued.
paragraphs.cn: 等我回到我的城堡（从此以后我想我就一直这么叫它了），我像被人追赶似的逃了进去。

paragraphs.en: Whether I went over by the ladder, as first contrived, or went in at the hole in the rock, which I had called a door, I cannot remember; no, nor could I remember the next morning, for never frightened hare fled to cover, or fox to earth, with more terror of mind than I to this retreat.
paragraphs.cn: 我究竟是照最初那样翻梯子进去的，还是从岩壁上那个我称作门的洞口钻进去的，我已记不清了；不，就连第二天早上也记不起来，因为受惊的野兔逃回窝、狐狸钻回洞，心里的惊恐也不及我逃进这处藏身之所时那样厉害。

paragraphs.en: I slept none that night; the farther I was from the occasion of my fright, the greater my apprehensions were, which is something contrary to the nature of such things, and especially to the usual practice of all creatures in fear; but I was so embarrassed with my own frightful ideas of the thing, that I formed nothing but dismal imaginations to myself, even though I was now a great way off.
paragraphs.cn: 那一夜我根本没合眼；我离受惊的起因越远，心里的忧惧反倒越重，这多少有悖于这类事情的常理，尤其有悖于一切生灵受惊时的惯常表现；可我被自己那些骇人的念头搅得心神大乱，尽管如今离得老远，脑子里却尽是些凄惨的想象。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes I fancied it must be the devil, and reason joined in with me in this supposition, for how should any other thing in human shape come into the place?
paragraphs.cn: 有时我猜想那准是魔鬼，连理智也帮着我这么设想，因为哪还会有别的什么人形之物来到这地方呢？

paragraphs.en: Where was the vessel that brought them?
paragraphs.cn: 把他们带来的船在哪儿？

paragraphs.en: What marks were there of any other footstep?
paragraphs.cn: 哪里还有别的脚印的痕迹？

paragraphs.en: And how was it possible a man should come there?
paragraphs.cn: 一个人又怎么可能来到这儿？

paragraphs.en: But then, to think that Satan should take human shape upon him in such a place, where there could be no manner of occasion for it, but to leave the print of his foot behind him, and that even for no purpose too, for he could not be sure I should see it—this was an amusement the other way.
paragraphs.cn: 可转念一想，撒旦竟会在这样一个地方现出人形，这里根本没有任何理由让他这么做，除了留下一个脚印，而这也毫无目的，因为他没法确定我一定会看见——这么一想，倒又叫我往另一头觉得可笑了。

paragraphs.en: I considered that the devil might have found out abundance of other ways to have terrified me than this of the single print of a foot; that as I lived quite on the other side of the island, he would never have been so simple as to leave a mark in a place where it was ten thousand to one whether I should ever see it or not, and in the sand too, which the first surge of the sea, upon a high wind, would have defaced entirely.
paragraphs.cn: 我琢磨着，魔鬼要吓唬我，尽可以想出无数别的法子，何必单单留下这一个脚印；再说我住在岛的另一头，他绝不会蠢到把印记留在一个万分之一都难保我会看到的地方，而且还留在沙上，只要一起大风，海浪头一涌就会把它冲得一干二净。

paragraphs.en: All this seemed inconsistent with the thing itself and with all the notions we usually entertain of the subtlety of the devil.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切似乎都与这件事本身、与我们通常对魔鬼那份狡诈的看法格格不入。

paragraphs.en: Abundance of such things as these assisted to argue me out of all apprehensions of its being the devil; and I presently concluded then that it must be some more dangerous creature—viz. that it must be some of the savages of the mainland opposite who had wandered out to sea in their canoes, and either driven by the currents or by contrary winds, had made the island, and had been on shore, but were gone away again to sea; being as loath, perhaps, to have stayed in this desolate island as I would have been to have had them.
paragraphs.cn: 诸如此类的种种理由帮着我把它是魔鬼的种种疑惧都辩驳掉了；于是我当下断定，那准是个更危险的东西——就是说，那准是对面大陆上的某些野人，坐着独木舟漂到海上，或被水流、或被逆风推到了这岛上，上过岸，可又已经回海上去了；他们大概跟我一样不情愿待在这荒岛上，就像我不情愿把他们留下一样。

paragraphs.en: While these reflections were rolling in my mind, I was very thankful in my thoughts that I was so happy as not to be thereabouts at that time, or that they did not see my boat, by which they would have concluded that some inhabitants had been in the place, and perhaps have searched farther for me.
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头在我心里翻腾时，我暗自万分庆幸，好在那时候我不在那一带，好在他们没看见我的船，否则他们准会断定这地方有人住过，说不定还会进一步搜寻我。

paragraphs.en: Then terrible thoughts racked my imagination about their having found out my boat, and that there were people here; and that, if so, I should certainly have them come again in greater numbers and devour me; that if it should happen that they should not find me, yet they would find my enclosure, destroy all my corn, and carry away all my flock of tame goats, and I should perish at last for mere want.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，种种可怕的念头折磨着我的想象：他们已经发现了我的船，知道这里有人；果真如此，他们必定会成群结队地再来，把我吞吃掉；就算他们碰巧找不到我，也会找到我的围栏，毁掉我所有的谷子，把我那群驯养的山羊统统赶走，到头来我就只有活活饿死。

paragraphs.en: Thus my fear banished all my religious hope, all that former confidence in God, which was founded upon such wonderful experience as I had had of His goodness; as if He that had fed me by miracle hitherto could not preserve, by His power, the provision which He had made for me by His goodness.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，我的恐惧把我一切虔诚的指望、一切先前对上帝的信心都赶跑了，而那信心本是建立在我亲历过的、祂那奇妙的仁慈之上的；仿佛那位至今用神迹养活我的主，竟不能凭祂的大能保全祂凭仁慈为我预备的食粮似的。

paragraphs.en: I reproached myself with my laziness, that would not sow any more corn one year than would just serve me till the next season, as if no accident could intervene to prevent my enjoying the crop that was upon the ground; and this I thought so just a reproof, that I resolved for the future to have two or three years’ corn beforehand; so that, whatever might come, I might not perish for want of bread.
paragraphs.cn: 我责备自己懒惰，一年里种的谷子只够撑到下一季，仿佛不会有什么意外插进来、妨碍我享用地里的收成似的；我觉得这个责备实在中肯，于是下定决心，往后要预先存下两三年的谷子，这样不管出什么事，我都不至于因缺粮而饿死。

paragraphs.en: How strange a chequer-work of Providence is the life of man! and by what secret different springs are the affections hurried about, as different circumstances present!
paragraphs.cn: 人的一生是天意何等奇妙的一盘错综棋局啊！随着境遇的不同，人的情感又被多少隐秘各异的动力驱来赶去啊！

paragraphs.en: To-day we love what to-morrow we hate; to-day we seek what to-morrow we shun; to-day we desire what to-morrow we fear, nay, even tremble at the apprehensions of.
paragraphs.cn: 今天我们爱的，明天却憎恶；今天我们追求的，明天却躲避；今天我们渴望的，明天却畏惧，不，甚至一想起就发抖。

paragraphs.en: This was exemplified in me, at this time, in the most lively manner imaginable; for I, whose only affliction was that I seemed banished from human society, that I was alone, circumscribed by the boundless ocean, cut off from mankind, and condemned to what I call silent life; that I was as one whom Heaven thought not worthy to be numbered among the living, or to appear among the rest of His creatures; that to have seen one of my own species would have seemed to me a raising me from death to life, and the greatest blessing that Heaven itself, next to the supreme blessing of salvation, could bestow; I say, that I should now tremble at the very apprehensions of seeing a man, and was ready to sink into the ground at but the shadow or silent appearance of a man having set his foot in the island.
paragraphs.cn: 这一点此刻在我身上体现得再鲜明不过了；我，唯一的苦恼本是仿佛被逐出了人类社会，孤身一人，被无边的大洋圈禁，与世人隔绝，注定过着我所谓的无声的生活；我仿佛是个上天认为不配列入生者之数、不配跻身祂其余造物之列的人；对我来说，能见到一个同类，简直就像是把我从死亡里救到生里，是继救赎这至高恩典之后、连上天本身所能赐予的最大福分；我说，如今我一想到会见着一个人，竟浑身发抖，单是一个人的影子、单是他悄无声息地在岛上落过脚，就吓得我几乎瘫倒在地。

paragraphs.en: Such is the uneven state of human life; and it afforded me a great many curious speculations afterwards, when I had a little recovered my first surprise.
paragraphs.cn: 人生的境遇就是这样起伏不定；等我稍稍从最初的惊惧中缓过神来，这事后来给了我许多耐人寻味的思索。

paragraphs.en: I considered that this was the station of life the infinitely wise and good providence of God had determined for me; that as I could not foresee what the ends of Divine wisdom might be in all this, so I was not to dispute His sovereignty; who, as I was His creature, had an undoubted right, by creation, to govern and dispose of me absolutely as He thought fit; and who, as I was a creature that had offended Him, had likewise a judicial right to condemn me to what punishment He thought fit; and that it was my part to submit to bear His indignation, because I had sinned against Him.
paragraphs.cn: 我想，这就是那位无限智慧、无限仁慈的上帝天意为我安排的人生处境；既然我无法预见神的智慧在这一切当中所要达成的结局，我便不该质疑祂的主权；祂既是我的造物主，凭着创造，就有无可置疑的权柄，可以照祂认为合宜的样子绝对地管辖、处置我；而我既是个得罪过祂的造物，祂也有审判的权柄，可以照祂认为合宜的样子定我受什么样的刑罚；我的本分则是俯首承受祂的义怒，因为我曾干犯了祂。

paragraphs.en: I then reflected, that as God, who was not only righteous but omnipotent, had thought fit thus to punish and afflict me, so He was able to deliver me: that if He did not think fit to do so, it was my unquestioned duty to resign myself absolutely and entirely to His will; and, on the other hand, it was my duty also to hope in Him, pray to Him, and quietly to attend to the dictates and directions of His daily providence.
paragraphs.cn: 我接着又想，上帝既不但公义、而且全能，既认为这样惩罚、磨难我是合宜的，那么祂也能拯救我：倘若祂认为不宜这么做，那么我无可置疑的本分就是把自己绝对地、彻底地交托于祂的旨意；而另一方面，我的本分也在于仰望祂、向祂祷告，并安静地留心祂每日天意的指示与引导。

paragraphs.en: These thoughts took me up many hours, days, nay, I may say weeks and months: and one particular effect of my cogitations on this occasion I cannot omit.
paragraphs.cn: 这些思索占去我许多个钟头、许多天，不，我可以说是许多个礼拜、许多个月；这回思索有一个特别的结果，我不能略过不提。

paragraphs.en: One morning early, lying in my bed, and filled with thoughts about my danger from the appearances of savages, I found it discomposed me very much; upon which these words of the Scripture came into my thoughts, “Call upon Me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me.”
paragraphs.cn: 一天清早，我躺在床上，满脑子都是野人出没给我带来的危险，只觉得心里烦乱不堪；正在这时，《圣经》里的这句话涌上了我的心头：“你在患难之日求告我，我必搭救你，你也要荣耀我。”

paragraphs.en: Upon this, rising cheerfully out of my bed, my heart was not only comforted, but I was guided and encouraged to pray earnestly to God for deliverance: when I had done praying I took up my Bible, and opening it to read, the first words that presented to me were, “Wait on the Lord, and be of good cheer, and He shall strengthen thy heart; wait, I say, on the Lord.”
paragraphs.cn: 听了这话，我高高兴兴地从床上起来，心里不但得了安慰，还受了引导和鼓舞，恳切地向上帝祈求拯救；祷告完毕，我拿起《圣经》，翻开来读，头一句映入眼帘的话是：“你要等候耶和华，当壮胆，坚固你的心；我再说，要等候耶和华。”

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to express the comfort this gave me.
paragraphs.cn: 这话给我的安慰，实在无法用言语表达。

paragraphs.en: In answer, I thankfully laid down the book, and was no more sad, at least on that occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 作为回应，我满怀感激地放下书本，从此不再忧愁，至少在那件事上不再忧愁了。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of these cogitations, apprehensions, and reflections, it came into my thoughts one day that all this might be a mere chimera of my own, and that this foot might be the print of my own foot, when I came on shore from my boat: this cheered me up a little, too, and I began to persuade myself it was all a delusion; that it was nothing else but my own foot; and why might I not come that way from the boat, as well as I was going that way to the boat?
paragraphs.cn: 就在这一番思虑、忧惧和反省当中，有一天我心里忽然冒出个念头：这一切说不定纯是我自己的臆想，那脚印说不定就是我自己下船上岸时留下的：这个念头也叫我稍稍宽了心，我开始劝自己说，这全是错觉；那不过就是我自己的脚印罢了；我既能那样去船那边，为什么不能也那样从船那边回来呢？

paragraphs.en: Again, I considered also that I could by no means tell for certain where I had trod, and where I had not; and that if, at last, this was only the print of my own foot, I had played the part of those fools who try to make stories of spectres and apparitions, and then are frightened at them more than anybody.
paragraphs.cn: 再者我也想到，我压根说不准自己究竟踩过哪里、没踩过哪里；倘若到头来这真只是我自己的脚印，那我就活像那班蠢人，编些鬼魂幽灵的故事，回头又被自己吓得比谁都厉害。

paragraphs.en: Now I began to take courage, and to peep abroad again, for I had not stirred out of my castle for three days and nights, so that I began to starve for provisions; for I had little or nothing within doors but some barley-cakes and water; then I knew that my goats wanted to be milked too, which usually was my evening diversion: and the poor creatures were in great pain and inconvenience for want of it; and, indeed, it almost spoiled some of them, and almost dried up their milk.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我开始壮起胆来，又要探头出去了，因为我已经三天三夜没迈出城堡一步，眼看就要断粮了；屋里几乎什么都没有，只剩些大麦饼和水；这时我又想起我的山羊也该挤奶了，挤奶素来是我傍晚的消遣：那些可怜的牲口没人挤奶，正难受得很、别扭得很；说真的，有几只都快给憋坏了，奶差不多都要干了。

paragraphs.en: Encouraging myself, therefore, with the belief that this was nothing but the print of one of my own feet, and that I might be truly said to start at my own shadow, I began to go abroad again, and went to my country house to milk my flock: but to see with what fear I went forward, how often I looked behind me, how I was ready every now and then to lay down my basket and run for my life, it would have made any one have thought I was haunted with an evil conscience, or that I had been lately most terribly frightened; and so, indeed, I had.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，我便用那脚印不过是我自己一只脚印、我实在可以说是被自己的影子吓着了的想法给自己壮胆，重又出门，到我的乡间小屋去给羊群挤奶；可要是有人瞧见我往前走时那副害怕的样子，瞧见我多么频繁地回头望，瞧见我每隔一会儿就要放下筐子、拔腿逃命的模样，准会以为我是让亏心事缠住了，要不就是新近着实吓破过胆；说实在的，我确实是吓破过胆的。

paragraphs.en: However, I went down thus two or three days, and having seen nothing, I began to be a little bolder, and to think there was really nothing in it but my own imagination; but I could not persuade myself fully of this till I should go down to the shore again, and see this print of a foot, and measure it by my own, and see if there was any similitude or fitness, that I might be assured it was my own foot: but when I came to the place, first, it appeared evidently to me, that when I laid up my boat I could not possibly be on shore anywhere thereabouts; secondly, when I came to measure the mark with my own foot, I found my foot not so large by a great deal.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，我就这么下去了两三天，什么也没看见，胆子便渐渐大了些，开始觉得这事其实根本没什么，全是我自己瞎想；可我总没法完全说服自己，除非再下到岸边去，再看看那个脚印，拿我自己的脚去量一量，看看有没有相似、合不合得上，好让自己确信那就是我自己的脚：可等我到了那地方，头一样，我明明白白看出，我藏船的时候根本不可能在那一带上过岸；第二样，等我拿自己的脚去量那印记，却发觉我的脚小了一大截。

paragraphs.en: Both these things filled my head with new imaginations, and gave me the vapours again to the highest degree, so that I shook with cold like one in an ague; and I went home again, filled with the belief that some man or men had been on shore there; or, in short, that the island was inhabited, and I might be surprised before I was aware; and what course to take for my security I knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 这两件事使我脑子里又充满了新的想象，把我重新吓得毛骨悚然到了极点，我冷得直打哆嗦，像个害疟疾的人；我又回到家里，满心相信真有一个人或几个人在那儿上过岸；简而言之，这岛上是有人的，我随时可能在毫无防备时遭到袭击；至于该采取什么办法保全自己，我心里全然没底。

paragraphs.en: Oh, what ridiculous resolutions men take when possessed with fear!
paragraphs.cn: 唉，人一旦被恐惧攫住，会作出多么荒唐的决定啊！

paragraphs.en: It deprives them of the use of those means which reason offers for their relief.
paragraphs.cn: 恐惧夺走了他们运用理智所提供的自救手段的能力。

paragraphs.en: The first thing I proposed to myself was, to throw down my enclosures, and turn all my tame cattle wild into the woods, lest the enemy should find them, and then frequent the island in prospect of the same or the like booty: then the simple thing of digging up my two corn-fields, lest they should find such a grain there, and still be prompted to frequent the island: then to demolish my bower and tent, that they might not see any vestiges of habitation, and be prompted to look farther, in order to find out the persons inhabiting.
paragraphs.cn: 我给自己拿的头一个主意是：拆掉我的围栏，把所有驯养的牲口都赶进树林里放野，免得敌人发现它们，以后老惦记着这岛、盼着来劫同样或类似的战利品；接着那个笨主意是把我那两块谷田刨掉，免得他们在那儿发现这种谷物，越发被勾着常来这岛；再接着是拆毁我的凉亭和帐篷，免得他们看见任何住人的痕迹，被勾着进一步搜寻、好找出住在这里的人来。

paragraphs.en: These were the subject of the first night’s cogitations after I was come home again, while the apprehensions which had so overrun my mind were fresh upon me, and my head was full of vapours.
paragraphs.cn: 这些就是我回来后头一夜思索的内容，那时那曾如此充塞我心头的忧惧还热辣辣地压着我，我满脑子都是惊惶。

paragraphs.en: Thus, fear of danger is ten thousand times more terrifying than danger itself, when apparent to the eyes; and we find the burden of anxiety greater, by much, than the evil which we are anxious about: and what was worse than all this, I had not that relief in this trouble that from the resignation I used to practise I hoped to have.
paragraphs.cn: 由此可见，危险的恐惧比危险本身当真摆在眼前时要可怕上千万倍；我们发觉，焦虑这副担子，远比我们所焦虑的祸患本身沉重得多：而比这一切更糟的是，我原指望凭着素常修习的那份顺服，能在这场苦恼里得些宽慰，如今却偏偏得不到。

paragraphs.en: I looked, I thought, like Saul, who complained not only that the Philistines were upon him, but that God had forsaken him; for I did not now take due ways to compose my mind, by crying to God in my distress, and resting upon His providence, as I had done before, for my defence and deliverance; which, if I had done, I had at least been more cheerfully supported under this new surprise, and perhaps carried through it with more resolution.
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得自己那模样活像扫罗，他不但抱怨非利士人逼近了他，还抱怨上帝离弃了他；因为我这时并没有采取正当的办法来安定自己的心——像我从前那样，在患难中向上帝呼求，安歇在祂的天意里，求祂护佑和拯救；倘若我那样做了，至少在这新的惊惧之下，我会得到更愉快的支撑，说不定还能更有决心地闯过去。

paragraphs.en: This confusion of my thoughts kept me awake all night; but in the morning I fell asleep; and having, by the amusement of my mind, been as it were tired, and my spirits exhausted, I slept very soundly, and waked much better composed than I had ever been before.
paragraphs.cn: 这般思绪的纷乱搅得我整夜没合眼；可到了早上，我却睡着了；由于心思折腾得像是累坏了、精神也耗尽了，我睡得极沉，醒来时心境比先前任何时候都平静得多。

paragraphs.en: And now I began to think sedately; and, upon debate with myself, I concluded that this island (which was so exceedingly pleasant, fruitful, and no farther from the mainland than as I had seen) was not so entirely abandoned as I might imagine; that although there were no stated inhabitants who lived on the spot, yet that there might sometimes come boats off from the shore, who, either with design, or perhaps never but when they were driven by cross winds, might come to this place; that I had lived there fifteen years now and had not met with the least shadow or figure of any people yet; and that, if at any time they should be driven here, it was probable they went away again as soon as ever they could, seeing they had never thought fit to fix here upon any occasion; that the most I could suggest any danger from was from any casual accidental landing of straggling people from the main, who, as it was likely, if they were driven hither, were here against their wills, so they made no stay here, but went off again with all possible speed; seldom staying one night on shore, lest they should not have the help of the tides and daylight back again; and that, therefore, I had nothing to do but to consider of some safe retreat, in case I should see any savages land upon the spot.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我开始能冷静地思量了；跟自己反复掂量之后，我断定，这座岛（它是那样宜人、丰饶，离大陆又不过如我所见的那么远）并不像我想的那样彻底荒无人烟；虽然没有固定居住在这里的人，可有时或许会有船从对岸过来，或是有意而来，或许只在被逆风驱赶时才来，总之可能会到这地方；我在这儿住了十五年了，至今连半点人影儿也没碰上过；就算他们什么时候被驱到这儿，多半也是一有机会就赶紧走了，可见他们从没打算在这儿定居；我能想到的最大危险，也就是有零星游荡的人从大陆偶然意外地登岸，而这种人若被驱赶到这儿来，多半是身不由己，因此不会久留，总是尽快又赶紧离去；难得在岸上过一夜，唯恐赶不上潮水和日光回去；所以，我要做的无非是琢磨出一处安全的退避之所，以防哪天真看见野人在这地方登陆。

paragraphs.en: Now, I began sorely to repent that I had dug my cave so large as to bring a door through again, which door, as I said, came out beyond where my fortification joined to the rock: upon maturely considering this, therefore, I resolved to draw me a second fortification, in the manner of a semicircle, at a distance from my wall, just where I had planted a double row of trees about twelve years before, of which I made mention: these trees having been planted so thick before, they wanted but few piles to be driven between them, that they might be thicker and stronger, and my wall would be soon finished.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我开始痛悔当初把山洞挖得那么大，以致又开出一道门来，这道门，前面说过，是通到我营垒跟岩壁相接处之外的：于是，把这事仔细掂量之后，我决意在离我那道墙有一段距离的地方，照半圆的样子再筑第二道防御工事，就筑在我大约十二年前栽下双排树木的地方，那双排树我前面提过：这些树先前既栽得那么密，只消在它们中间再打进几根木桩，就能长得更密更牢，我这道墙很快就能筑成。

paragraphs.en: So that I had now a double wall; and my outer wall was thickened with pieces of timber, old cables, and everything I could think of, to make it strong; having in it seven little holes, about as big as I might put my arm out at.
paragraphs.cn: 这样我如今就有了双重的墙；我那道外墙又用木料、旧缆绳以及一切我想得到的东西加厚过，好让它结实；墙上留着七个小孔，大约大到能伸出我一条胳膊。

paragraphs.en: In the inside of this I thickened my wall to about ten feet thick with continually bringing earth out of my cave, and laying it at the foot of the wall, and walking upon it; and through the seven holes I contrived to plant the muskets, of which I took notice that I had got seven on shore out of the ship; these I planted like my cannon, and fitted them into frames, that held them like a carriage, so that I could fire all the seven guns in two minutes’ time; this wall I was many a weary month in finishing, and yet never thought myself safe till it was done.
paragraphs.cn: 在这道墙里侧，我不断把土从山洞里挖出来堆到墙脚、再踩实，把墙加厚到约莫十英尺厚；透过那七个孔，我设法架上火枪——我留意到从船上一共弄下来七支火枪；我把它们像架炮一样架好，嵌进框架里，那框架托着它们，像个炮架，这样我两分钟工夫就能把七支枪全放一遍；这道墙我费了好几个把月的辛苦才修成，可直到它完工，我才觉得自己安全。

paragraphs.en: When this was done I stuck all the ground without my wall, for a great length every way, as full with stakes or sticks of the osier-like wood, which I found so apt to grow, as they could well stand; insomuch that I believe I might set in near twenty thousand of them, leaving a pretty large space between them and my wall, that I might have room to see an enemy, and they might have no shelter from the young trees, if they attempted to approach my outer wall.
paragraphs.cn: 这道墙修好后，我又在墙外的地上、朝四面八方老远一片地方，尽量密地插满那种柳条似的木棍或枝条——我发现这种木头极易生长；密到我相信自己大约插了将近两万根，还在它们和我的墙之间留出好大一片空地，好让我有地方望见来敌，而他们若企图逼近我的外墙，也不能靠那些小树得到掩蔽。

paragraphs.en: Thus in two years’ time I had a thick grove; and in five or six years’ time I had a wood before my dwelling, growing so monstrously thick and strong that it was indeed perfectly impassable: and no men, of what kind soever, could ever imagine that there was anything beyond it, much less a habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，两年工夫我就有了一片浓密的树丛；五六年工夫，我住处前面就长起了一片树林，密得、壮得出奇，简直根本无法通行：任凭什么样的人，谁也想象不出那后面还有什么东西，更别说有个住处了。

paragraphs.en: As for the way which I proposed to myself to go in and out (for I left no avenue), it was by setting two ladders, one to a part of the rock which was low, and then broke in, and left room to place another ladder upon that; so when the two ladders were taken down no man living could come down to me without doing himself mischief; and if they had come down, they were still on the outside of my outer wall.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我给自己留的进出通道（因为我没留任何显眼的路口），是靠架两把梯子：一把搭到岩壁一处较低、往里凹进、留出地方能再搭一把梯子的地方；这样，两把梯子一撤，天底下没有一个活人能下来找到我；就算他们下得来，也仍然是在我外墙的外头。

paragraphs.en: Thus I took all the measures human prudence could suggest for my own preservation; and it will be seen at length that they were not altogether without just reason; though I foresaw nothing at that time more than my mere fear suggested to me.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，凡是人的审慎所能想到的保全自己的办法，我都采取了；日后就会看到，这些办法并非全无正当的理由；尽管在当时，除了纯粹的恐惧向我暗示的，我什么也没预料到。

paragraphs.en: While this was doing, I was not altogether careless of my other affairs; for I had a great concern upon me for my little herd of goats: they were not only a ready supply to me on every occasion, and began to be sufficient for me, without the expense of powder and shot, but also without the fatigue of hunting after the wild ones; and I was loath to lose the advantage of them, and to have them all to nurse up over again.
paragraphs.cn: 在忙这件事的时候,我也没有完全不管别的事情;因为我心里一直很挂念我那一小群山羊:它们不但随时都能给我提供食物,而且已经足够我吃,既省下了火药和铅弹,也免去了追猎野羊的辛苦;我实在舍不得失去它们的好处,更不愿一切从头再来、重新把羊养大。

paragraphs.en: For this purpose, after long consideration, I could think of but two ways to preserve them: one was, to find another convenient place to dig a cave underground, and to drive them into it every night; and the other was to enclose two or three little bits of land, remote from one another, and as much concealed as I could, where I might keep about half-a-dozen young goats in each place; so that if any disaster happened to the flock in general, I might be able to raise them again with little trouble and time: and this though it would require a good deal of time and labour, I thought was the most rational design.
paragraphs.cn: 为此,我反复思量,想来想去只有两个办法能保住它们:一是另找一处合适的地方,在地下挖个洞,每晚把羊赶进去;二是圈起两三小块彼此相隔的土地,尽量隐蔽,每处养上六只左右的小羊;这样万一整群羊出了什么意外,我也能省时省力地重新把它们养起来:这法子虽然要花不少时间和力气,我却觉得是最明智的安排。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, I spent some time to find out the most retired parts of the island; and I pitched upon one, which was as private, indeed, as my heart could wish: it was a little damp piece of ground in the middle of the hollow and thick woods, where, as is observed, I almost lost myself once before, endeavouring to come back that way from the eastern part of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我花了些时间去寻找岛上最偏僻的角落;终于选中了一处,那地方真是隐蔽得合我心意:那是一小片潮湿的地,坐落在低洼茂密的树林中央,前面说过,我有一回从岛东边想抄那条路回来,差点在那里迷了路。

paragraphs.en: Here I found a clear piece of land, near three acres, so surrounded with woods that it was almost an enclosure by nature; at least, it did not want near so much labour to make it so as the other piece of ground I had worked so hard at.
paragraphs.cn: 在那里我找到一片开阔的空地,将近三英亩,四周被树林环抱,几乎天然就成了一道围栏;至少比起我先前费尽力气开出的那块地,要把它围起来省事得多。

paragraphs.en: I immediately went to work with this piece of ground; and in less than a month’s time I had so fenced it round that my flock, or herd, call it which you please, which were not so wild now as at first they might be supposed to be, were well enough secured in it: so, without any further delay, I removed ten young she-goats and two he-goats to this piece, and when they were there I continued to perfect the fence till I had made it as secure as the other; which, however, I did at more leisure, and it took me up more time by a great deal.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻着手整治这块地;不到一个月,就把它四周都围好了,我那群羊——你爱叫它群也好、叫它伙也好——如今已不像先前料想的那么野了,养在里面很安全:于是我毫不迟延,把十只小母羊和两只公羊挪到这块地上,等它们进去后,我又继续把围栏加固,直到修得和那一处一样牢靠;不过这次我做得从容些,反倒花了多得多的时间。

paragraphs.en: All this labour I was at the expense of, purely from my apprehensions on account of the print of a man’s foot; for as yet I had never seen any human creature come near the island; and I had now lived two years under this uneasiness, which, indeed, made my life much less comfortable than it was before, as may be well imagined by any who know what it is to live in the constant snare of the fear of man.
paragraphs.cn: 我费这么大的劲,纯粹是因为看见那个人的脚印而心生恐惧;因为到那时为止,我还从没见过有人靠近这座岛;可我已经在这种不安中过了两年,这确实让我的日子比先前难受多了,凡是知道时时活在怕人的圈套里是什么滋味的人,都能想象得到。

paragraphs.en: And this I must observe, with grief, too, that the discomposure of my mind had great impression also upon the religious part of my thoughts; for the dread and terror of falling into the hands of savages and cannibals lay so upon my spirits, that I seldom found myself in a due temper for application to my Maker; at least, not with the sedate calmness and resignation of soul which I was wont to do: I rather prayed to God as under great affliction and pressure of mind, surrounded with danger, and in expectation every night of being murdered and devoured before morning; and I must testify, from my experience, that a temper of peace, thankfulness, love, and affection, is much the more proper frame for prayer than that of terror and discomposure: and that under the dread of mischief impending, a man is no more fit for a comforting performance of the duty of praying to God than he is for a repentance on a sick-bed; for these discomposures affect the mind, as the others do the body; and the discomposure of the mind must necessarily be as great a disability as that of the body, and much greater; praying to God being properly an act of the mind, not of the body.
paragraphs.cn: 还有一点我不得不痛心地指出:我心绪不宁,连信仰上的心思也大受影响;因为害怕落到野人和食人生番手里的恐惧压在我心头,使我很少能有平静的心境去亲近我的造物主;至少做不到从前那种安详、镇定、顺服的心境:我倒像是在极大的苦难和心灵的重压下向上帝祈祷,四面被危险包围,每天夜里都担心天亮前会被杀掉吃掉;我凭切身经验可以作证:平安、感恩、慈爱、深情的心境,远比恐惧和慌乱更适合祷告;人在祸患临头的恐惧之下,就像病榻上的人不宜真心悔改一样,也不宜安然去尽向上帝祷告的本分;因为这种心乱扰的是心灵,正如那些病痛扰的是身体;而心灵的失常,必然和身体的失常一样是极大的妨碍,甚至更甚;因为向上帝祷告本来就是心灵的事,而非身体的事。

paragraphs.en: But to go on.
paragraphs.cn: 不过还是接着说下去吧。

paragraphs.en: After I had thus secured one part of my little living stock, I went about the whole island, searching for another private place to make such another deposit; when, wandering more to the west point of the island than I had ever done yet, and looking out to sea, I thought I saw a boat upon the sea, at a great distance.
paragraphs.cn: 我这样把我那一小群活物的一部分安顿妥当后,便绕着整座岛,想再找一处隐蔽的地方,做同样的储备;这时我比以往任何时候都更往岛的西端游荡,朝海上望去,恍惚看见远远的海面上有一条船。

paragraphs.en: I had found a perspective glass or two in one of the seamen’s chests, which I saved out of our ship, but I had it not about me; and this was so remote that I could not tell what to make of it, though I looked at it till my eyes were not able to hold to look any longer; whether it was a boat or not I do not know, but as I descended from the hill I could see no more of it, so I gave it over; only I resolved to go no more out without a perspective glass in my pocket.
paragraphs.cn: 我从我们船上抢救出来的一只水手箱里找到过一两只望远镜,可当时没带在身上;那船又太远,我看不出个究竟,尽管我一直盯着看,直到眼睛再也支撑不住;那到底是不是一条船我不知道,可等我下了山,就再也看不见它了,于是我只好作罢;只是我下定决心,以后出门口袋里一定要揣着望远镜。

paragraphs.en: When I was come down the hill to the end of the island, where, indeed, I had never been before, I was presently convinced that the seeing the print of a man’s foot was not such a strange thing in the island as I imagined: and but that it was a special providence that I was cast upon the side of the island where the savages never came, I should easily have known that nothing was more frequent than for the canoes from the main, when they happened to be a little too far out at sea, to shoot over to that side of the island for harbour: likewise, as they often met and fought in their canoes, the victors, having taken any prisoners, would bring them over to this shore, where, according to their dreadful customs, being all cannibals, they would kill and eat them; of which hereafter.
paragraphs.cn: 等我下了山,来到岛的这一端——说真的,我以前从没到过这里——我立刻确信,在岛上看见人的脚印,并不像我原先想的那么稀奇:若不是天意特别眷顾,把我抛在了野人从不涉足的岛的那一边,我早该明白:大陆上的独木舟一旦在海上漂得稍远,常会驶到岛的这一边来避风;同样,他们常在独木舟里相遇厮杀,得胜的一方抓了俘虏,就把他们带到这片海岸来,按照他们那可怕的习俗——他们都是食人生番——把俘虏杀掉吃掉;这些以后再说。

paragraphs.en: When I was come down the hill to the shore, as I said above, being the SW. point of the island, I was perfectly confounded and amazed; nor is it possible for me to express the horror of my mind at seeing the shore spread with skulls, hands, feet, and other bones of human bodies; and particularly I observed a place where there had been a fire made, and a circle dug in the earth, like a cockpit, where I supposed the savage wretches had sat down to their human feastings upon the bodies of their fellow-creatures.
paragraphs.cn: 我如前所说下了山来到海边,也就是岛的西南角,顿时惊骇错愕到了极点;我实在无法形容,当我看见海岸上遍布头骨、断手、断脚和人身上其他的骨头时,心里那份恐怖;我尤其注意到有一处生过火,地上挖了个圈,像斗鸡场似的,我猜那些野蛮的恶徒就是坐在那里,拿同类的尸体开人肉宴的。

paragraphs.en: I was so astonished with the sight of these things, that I entertained no notions of any danger to myself from it for a long while: all my apprehensions were buried in the thoughts of such a pitch of inhuman, hellish brutality, and the horror of the degeneracy of human nature, which, though I had heard of it often, yet I never had so near a view of before; in short, I turned away my face from the horrid spectacle; my stomach grew sick, and I was just at the point of fainting, when nature discharged the disorder from my stomach; and having vomited with uncommon violence, I was a little relieved, but could not bear to stay in the place a moment; so I got up the hill again with all the speed I could, and walked on towards my own habitation.
paragraphs.cn: 眼前这些景象把我惊得魂飞魄散,好长一段时间里,我竟没想到这对我自身有什么危险:我满脑子想的都是这种灭绝人性、地狱般的凶残,以及人性堕落到这般地步的恐怖,这种事我虽常听说,却从没这么近地亲眼见过;总之,我扭过脸去,不忍再看那可怕的景象;胃里一阵翻腾,几乎要昏过去,幸好造化把胃里的东西发泄了出来;我猛烈地呕吐了一场,才略觉轻松,却一刻也待不下去;于是我拼尽全力重新爬上山,朝自己的住处走去。

paragraphs.en: When I came a little out of that part of the island I stood still awhile, as amazed, and then, recovering myself, I looked up with the utmost affection of my soul, and, with a flood of tears in my eyes, gave God thanks, that had cast my first lot in a part of the world where I was distinguished from such dreadful creatures as these; and that, though I had esteemed my present condition very miserable, had yet given me so many comforts in it that I had still more to give thanks for than to complain of: and this, above all, that I had, even in this miserable condition, been comforted with the knowledge of Himself, and the hope of His blessing: which was a felicity more than sufficiently equivalent to all the misery which I had suffered, or could suffer.
paragraphs.cn: 等我离开岛的那一带稍远些,便呆呆地站住了,像是惊魂未定,随后回过神来,怀着满心的深情抬起头,眼里噙满泪水,感谢上帝当初把我的命运安排在世上这样一个地方,使我与这些可怕的生灵有别;虽然我曾觉得自己眼下的处境十分悲惨,可上帝仍在其中赐给我这么多安慰,使我该感恩的比该抱怨的还多:尤其可贵的是,即便身处这般苦境,我也蒙他自己的认识和他赐福的盼望所安慰,这份福气足以抵偿我所受过或可能受的一切苦难,还绰绰有余。

paragraphs.en: In this frame of thankfulness I went home to my castle, and began to be much easier now, as to the safety of my circumstances, than ever I was before: for I observed that these wretches never came to this island in search of what they could get; perhaps not seeking, not wanting, or not expecting anything here; and having often, no doubt, been up the covered, woody part of it without finding anything to their purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 怀着这样感恩的心境,我回到我的城堡,如今对自身处境的安全,比以往任何时候都放心多了:因为我看出这些恶徒来这座岛,并不是来搜寻什么东西的;也许他们并不寻找、并不需要、也并不指望在这里得到什么;而且他们无疑常爬上岛上林木掩蔽的地方,却什么合他们意的东西也没找到。

paragraphs.en: I knew I had been here now almost eighteen years, and never saw the least footsteps of human creature there before; and I might be eighteen years more as entirely concealed as I was now, if I did not discover myself to them, which I had no manner of occasion to do; it being my only business to keep myself entirely concealed where I was, unless I found a better sort of creatures than cannibals to make myself known to.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道自己在这里已经待了将近十八年,以前从没在这里见过一丝人的脚印;只要我不向他们暴露自己,我大可再像现在这样隐蔽地过十八年,而我根本没有理由暴露自己;我唯一该做的,就是把自己藏得严严实实,除非我遇到比食人生番更好的生灵,才值得让人知道我在这里。

paragraphs.en: Yet I entertained such an abhorrence of the savage wretches that I have been speaking of, and of the wretched, inhuman custom of their devouring and eating one another up, that I continued pensive and sad, and kept close within my own circle for almost two years after this: when I say my own circle, I mean by it my three plantations—viz. my castle, my country seat (which I called my bower), and my enclosure in the woods: nor did I look after this for any other use than an enclosure for my goats; for the aversion which nature gave me to these hellish wretches was such, that I was as fearful of seeing them as of seeing the devil himself.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,我对前面说的那些野蛮恶徒,以及他们互相吞食这种悲惨、灭绝人性的习俗,厌恶到了极点,以至于此后将近两年,我一直郁郁寡欢,把自己紧紧关在我那一小片天地里:我说我那一小片天地,指的是我的三处产业——也就是我的城堡、我的乡间别墅(我管它叫凉亭),以及我在林中的那片圈地:我照看那片圈地,除了当作羊圈,别无他用;因为造化让我对这些地狱般的恶徒厌恶至极,我怕见他们,就跟怕见魔鬼本身一样。

paragraphs.en: I did not so much as go to look after my boat all this time, but began rather to think of making another; for I could not think of ever making any more attempts to bring the other boat round the island to me, lest I should meet with some of these creatures at sea; in which case, if I had happened to have fallen into their hands, I knew what would have been my lot.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间里,我甚至连去看一眼我那条船都没有,反倒开始盘算再造一条;因为我再也不敢想把那条船绕岛开到我这边来,生怕在海上撞见这些生灵;万一落到他们手里,我知道自己会是什么下场。

paragraphs.en: Time, however, and the satisfaction I had that I was in no danger of being discovered by these people, began to wear off my uneasiness about them; and I began to live just in the same composed manner as before, only with this difference, that I used more caution, and kept my eyes more about me than I did before, lest I should happen to be seen by any of them; and particularly, I was more cautious of firing my gun, lest any of them, being on the island, should happen to hear it.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,时间一久,加上我确信不会被这些人发现,渐渐消磨了我对他们的不安;我又开始像从前那样安稳地过日子,只是有一点不同:我比先前更加小心,眼睛更留意四周,唯恐被他们中的哪个撞见;尤其是开枪时格外谨慎,生怕岛上万一有他们的人听见枪声。

paragraphs.en: It was, therefore, a very good providence to me that I had furnished myself with a tame breed of goats, and that I had no need to hunt any more about the woods, or shoot at them; and if I did catch any of them after this, it was by traps and snares, as I had done before; so that for two years after this I believe I never fired my gun once off, though I never went out without it; and what was more, as I had saved three pistols out of the ship, I always carried them out with me, or at least two of them, sticking them in my goat-skin belt.
paragraphs.cn: 因此,我事先养下一群驯服的山羊,实在是天大的福气,使我再也不必到林子里去打猎射杀;此后即便捉到几只,也是像先前那样用陷阱和套子;所以此后有两年,我想我一枪都没放过,尽管出门从不离枪;更有甚者,我从船上救出三支手枪,出门时总把它们都带上,至少带上两支,插在我的羊皮腰带里。

paragraphs.en: I also furbished up one of the great cutlasses that I had out of the ship, and made me a belt to hang it on also; so that I was now a most formidable fellow to look at when I went abroad, if you add to the former description of myself the particular of two pistols, and a broadsword hanging at my side in a belt, but without a scabbard.
paragraphs.cn: 我还把从船上取来的一把大弯刀磨得锃亮,又做了条腰带把它挂起来;这么一来,我出门时看上去真是个可怕至极的家伙,你只要在先前对我那副模样的描述之外,再添上两支手枪和腰间腰带上挂着的一把没有刀鞘的宽刃大刀就行了。

paragraphs.en: Things going on thus, as I have said, for some time, I seemed, excepting these cautions, to be reduced to my former calm, sedate way of living.
paragraphs.cn: 如我所说,事情这样过了一阵子,除了这些防范之外,我似乎又回到了从前那种平静、安稳的生活。

paragraphs.en: All these things tended to show me more and more how far my condition was from being miserable, compared to some others; nay, to many other particulars of life which it might have pleased God to have made my lot.
paragraphs.cn: 所有这些事都越来越让我明白,与某些人相比,我的处境远算不上悲惨;不,与上帝原可安排给我的许多别种人生境遇相比,更是如此。

paragraphs.en: It put me upon reflecting how little repining there would be among mankind at any condition of life if people would rather compare their condition with those that were worse, in order to be thankful, than be always comparing them with those which are better, to assist their murmurings and complainings.
paragraphs.cn: 这让我不禁反省:倘若人们肯拿自己的处境去和更差的相比,好心存感恩,而不是老拿它去和更好的相比,徒增怨言和牢骚,那么人间对任何境遇的怨天尤人该会少得多。

paragraphs.en: As in my present condition there were not really many things which I wanted, so indeed I thought that the frights I had been in about these savage wretches, and the concern I had been in for my own preservation, had taken off the edge of my invention, for my own conveniences; and I had dropped a good design, which I had once bent my thoughts upon, and that was to try if I could not make some of my barley into malt, and then try to brew myself some beer.
paragraphs.cn: 在我眼下的处境里,其实并没有多少我缺的东西;于是我确实觉得,我为这些野蛮恶徒所受的惊吓,以及为自保而生的忧虑,已经磨掉了我为自己谋便利的那点巧思;我曾经一心想做的一件好事也搁下了,那就是试试能不能把我的一些大麦做成麦芽,然后再试着酿点啤酒。

paragraphs.en: This was really a whimsical thought, and I reproved myself often for the simplicity of it: for I presently saw there would be the want of several things necessary to the making my beer that it would be impossible for me to supply; as, first, casks to preserve it in, which was a thing that, as I have observed already, I could never compass: no, though I spent not only many days, but weeks, nay months, in attempting it, but to no purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 这实在是个异想天开的念头,我常常责怪自己太天真:因为我立刻看出,酿啤酒还缺好几样必需的东西,而这些我根本无从筹办;比如,首先是盛酒的桶,这东西我前面说过,是我怎么也弄不成的:是的,我不但花了许多天,还花了好几个星期、甚至好几个月去试,却全无结果。

paragraphs.en: In the next place, I had no hops to make it keep, no yeast to make it work, no copper or kettle to make it boil; and yet with all these things wanting, I verily believe, had not the frights and terrors I was in about the savages intervened, I had undertaken it, and perhaps brought it to pass too; for I seldom gave anything over without accomplishing it, when once I had it in my head to began it.
paragraphs.cn: 其次,我没有啤酒花使它耐存,没有酵母使它发酵,没有铜锅或水壶使它煮沸;然而,尽管缺这么多东西,我确实相信,若不是对野人的惊惧从中作梗,我准会动手去做,说不定还真能做成;因为一件事只要我起了念头要做,我很少半途而废、不做成功不罢休。

paragraphs.en: But my invention now ran quite another way; for night and day I could think of nothing but how I might destroy some of the monsters in their cruel, bloody entertainment, and if possible save the victim they should bring hither to destroy.
paragraphs.cn: 可如今我的心思完全转到了另一条路上;因为我日思夜想,满脑子只有一件事:怎样才能在那些怪物残忍血腥的宴乐中除掉几个,如果可能的话,还要救下他们带来这里等着杀害的那个牺牲品。

paragraphs.en: It would take up a larger volume than this whole work is intended to be to set down all the contrivances I hatched, or rather brooded upon, in my thoughts, for the destroying these creatures, or at least frightening them so as to prevent their coming hither any more: but all this was abortive; nothing could be possible to take effect, unless I was to be there to do it myself: and what could one man do among them, when perhaps there might be twenty or thirty of them together with their darts, or their bows and arrows, with which they could shoot as true to a mark as I could with my gun?
paragraphs.cn: 要把我心里酝酿出来——不如说反复盘算出来——的种种消灭这些生灵、或至少把他们吓得再也不敢来这里的计谋一一记下来,只怕比这整部书还要厚;可这一切都成了泡影;除非我亲自到场动手,否则没有一样行得通:可我一个人在他们中间又能做什么呢?说不定他们有二三十人聚在一起,带着标枪或弓箭,射起靶来跟我用枪一样准。
