paragraphs.en: Sometimes I thought of digging a hole under the place where they made their fire, and putting in five or six pounds of gunpowder, which, when they kindled their fire, would consequently take fire, and blow up all that was near it: but as, in the first place, I should be unwilling to waste so much powder upon them, my store being now within the quantity of one barrel, so neither could I be sure of its going off at any certain time, when it might surprise them; and, at best, that it would do little more than just blow the fire about their ears and fright them, but not sufficient to make them forsake the place: so I laid it aside; and then proposed that I would place myself in ambush in some convenient place, with my three guns all double-loaded, and in the middle of their bloody ceremony let fly at them, when I should be sure to kill or wound perhaps two or three at every shot; and then falling in upon them with my three pistols and my sword, I made no doubt but that, if there were twenty, I should kill them all.
paragraphs.cn: 有时我想在他们生火的地方底下挖个坑,埋进五六磅火药,等他们点火时,火药自然会引燃,把附近的一切都炸上天:可是,首先,我舍不得在他们身上白费这么多火药,我的存货如今还不到一桶;其次,我也没法保证它会在某个确定的、能出其不意炸到他们的时刻引爆;而且,充其量它也不过是把火在他们耳边炸开、吓他们一跳,还不足以叫他们弃这地方而去:于是我把这念头搁下了;接着我又打算找个合适的地方埋伏起来,把我那三支枪都装上双份弹药,趁他们血腥仪式正酣时朝他们开火,那时我准能每枪打死或打伤两三个;然后再拿着我那三支手枪和刀冲进去,我毫不怀疑,哪怕有二十个,我也能把他们全杀光。

paragraphs.en: This fancy pleased my thoughts for some weeks, and I was so full of it that I often dreamed of it, and, sometimes, that I was just going to let fly at them in my sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 这个念头让我得意了好几个星期,我满脑子都是它,常常梦见它,有时梦里我正要朝他们开火。

paragraphs.en: I went so far with it in my imagination that I employed myself several days to find out proper places to put myself in ambuscade, as I said, to watch for them, and I went frequently to the place itself, which was now grown more familiar to me; but while my mind was thus filled with thoughts of revenge and a bloody putting twenty or thirty of them to the sword, as I may call it, the horror I had at the place, and at the signals of the barbarous wretches devouring one another, abetted my malice.
paragraphs.cn: 我在想象中把这事推演得那么远,还花了好几天工夫,如前所说,去寻找合适的埋伏点等着他们,又常跑到那地方本身去,如今我对那里已经熟悉多了;可正当我满脑子复仇的念头、盘算着怎样一举把二三十人斩于刀下时,我对那地方的恐惧,以及那些野蛮恶徒互相吞食的种种迹象,反倒助长了我的杀心。

paragraphs.en: Well, at length I found a place in the side of the hill where I was satisfied I might securely wait till I saw any of their boats coming; and might then, even before they would be ready to come on shore, convey myself unseen into some thickets of trees, in one of which there was a hollow large enough to conceal me entirely; and there I might sit and observe all their bloody doings, and take my full aim at their heads, when they were so close together as that it would be next to impossible that I should miss my shot, or that I could fail wounding three or four of them at the first shot.
paragraphs.cn: 终于,我在山坡上找到一处地方,我觉得在那里可以安稳地守着,直到看见他们的船开来;那时,甚至在他们还没准备上岸之前,我就能神不知鬼不觉地钻进几丛树林里,其中一丛里有个洞,大得足以把我整个藏起来;我可以坐在那里,观察他们全部血腥的勾当,趁他们挤在一处、我几乎不可能打偏、头一枪就绝不会打不中三四个人的时候,好好瞄准他们的脑袋。

paragraphs.en: In this place, then, I resolved to fulfil my design; and accordingly I prepared two muskets and my ordinary fowling-piece.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我决定就在这地方实施我的计划;我随即备好两支火枪和我那支普通的鸟枪。

paragraphs.en: The two muskets I loaded with a brace of slugs each, and four or five smaller bullets, about the size of pistol bullets; and the fowling-piece I loaded with near a handful of swan-shot of the largest size; I also loaded my pistols with about four bullets each; and, in this posture, well provided with ammunition for a second and third charge, I prepared myself for my expedition.
paragraphs.cn: 两支火枪我各装了两颗大铅弹,外加四五颗手枪弹大小的小弹丸;那支鸟枪我装了近一把最大号的天鹅弹;我的手枪也各装了约四颗子弹;就这样,我备足了第二次和第三次装填的弹药,做好了这次出征的准备。

paragraphs.en: After I had thus laid the scheme of my design, and in my imagination put it in practice, I continually made my tour every morning to the top of the hill, which was from my castle, as I called it, about three miles or more, to see if I could observe any boats upon the sea, coming near the island, or standing over towards it; but I began to tire of this hard duty, after I had for two or three months constantly kept my watch, but came always back without any discovery; there having not, in all that time, been the least appearance, not only on or near the shore, but on the whole ocean, so far as my eye or glass could reach every way.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样定下计划、又在想象中演练了一遍之后,我每天早上都照例爬到山顶去——从我所谓的城堡到那里约有三英里多——看能不能望见有船靠近海岛、或朝岛这边驶来;可我连着两三个月一直坚持守望,每回都空手而归,便渐渐厌倦了这份苦差;因为这段时间里,别说岸上或岸边,就连整片大洋,凡我肉眼或望远镜所及的四面八方,连一点动静都没有。

paragraphs.en: As long as I kept my daily tour to the hill, to look out, so long also I kept up the vigour of my design, and my spirits seemed to be all the while in a suitable frame for so outrageous an execution as the killing twenty or thirty naked savages, for an offence which I had not at all entered into any discussion of in my thoughts, any farther than my passions were at first fired by the horror I conceived at the unnatural custom of the people of that country, who, it seems, had been suffered by Providence, in His wise disposition of the world, to have no other guide than that of their own abominable and vitiated passions; and consequently were left, and perhaps had been so for some ages, to act such horrid things, and receive such dreadful customs, as nothing but nature, entirely abandoned by Heaven, and actuated by some hellish degeneracy, could have run them into.
paragraphs.cn: 只要我每天照旧爬山瞭望,我这计划的劲头就一直没减,精神也似乎始终处在一种适合去做那桩残暴之举的状态里——就是去杀掉二三十个赤身裸体的野人,可他们究竟犯了什么罪,我心里其实从没认真掂量过,不过是当初我一想到那地方的人那不近人情的习俗就满心恐怖,激起了我的义愤罢了;看来上帝在他智慧地安排世界时,任凭这些人除了自己那可憎败坏的情欲之外别无引导,于是他们便被撇下——也许已有好几个世代了——去做这等骇人的事、去遵这等可怕的习俗,这种事唯有全然被上天遗弃、被某种地狱般的堕落所驱使的天性才干得出来。

paragraphs.en: But now, when, as I have said, I began to be weary of the fruitless excursion which I had made so long and so far every morning in vain, so my opinion of the action itself began to alter; and I began, with cooler and calmer thoughts, to consider what I was going to engage in; what authority or call I had to pretend to be judge and executioner upon these men as criminals, whom Heaven had thought fit for so many ages to suffer unpunished to go on, and to be as it were the executioners of His judgments one upon another; how far these people were offenders against me, and what right I had to engage in the quarrel of that blood which they shed promiscuously upon one another.
paragraphs.cn: 可现在,如我所说,我对自己每天早上白跑这么远、这么久的徒劳之行厌倦起来,于是我对这行动本身的看法也开始改变;我开始以更冷静、更平和的心思去掂量自己打算干的事:我有什么权柄、受了什么召唤,竟要充当这些人的法官和刽子手,把他们当作罪犯来惩治?可上天已容忍他们这样过了那么多世代而不加惩罚,任凭他们仿佛互为执行他审判的刽子手;这些人究竟在多大程度上得罪了我?我又有什么权利去插手他们彼此滥杀所流的那些血的纷争?

paragraphs.en: I debated this very often with myself thus: “How do I know what God Himself judges in this particular case?
paragraphs.cn: 我常常这样跟自己辩论:“我怎么知道在这件事上,上帝自己是如何裁断的呢?

paragraphs.en: It is certain these people do not commit this as a crime; it is not against their own consciences reproving, or their light reproaching them; they do not know it to be an offence, and then commit it in defiance of divine justice, as we do in almost all the sins we commit.
paragraphs.cn: 有一点是肯定的:这些人做这事并不当作罪;这既不违背他们自己良心的责备,也不受他们心中亮光的谴责;他们并不知道这是罪过,然后明知故犯、公然违抗神的公义,而我们几乎在所犯的一切罪上都是如此。

paragraphs.en: They think it no more a crime to kill a captive taken in war than we do to kill an ox; or to eat human flesh than we do to eat mutton.”
paragraphs.cn: 在他们看来,杀掉一个战争中抓来的俘虏,并不比我们宰一头牛更算得上是罪;吃人肉,也不比我们吃羊肉更算得上是罪。”

paragraphs.en: When I considered this a little, it followed necessarily that I was certainly in the wrong; that these people were not murderers, in the sense that I had before condemned them in my thoughts, any more than those Christians were murderers who often put to death the prisoners taken in battle; or more frequently, upon many occasions, put whole troops of men to the sword, without giving quarter, though they threw down their arms and submitted.
paragraphs.cn: 我把这事略一细想,便不得不承认自己确实错了;这些人并不是我先前在心里定他们罪时所说的那种杀人凶手,正如那些基督徒也算不上凶手一样——他们常把战争中抓来的俘虏处死;更常见的是,在许多场合把整队整队的人斩尽杀绝、绝不留活口,哪怕对方已经放下武器、俯首投降。

paragraphs.en: In the next place, it occurred to me that although the usage they gave one another was thus brutish and inhuman, yet it was really nothing to me: these people had done me no injury: that if they attempted, or I saw it necessary, for my immediate preservation, to fall upon them, something might be said for it: but that I was yet out of their power, and they really had no knowledge of me, and consequently no design upon me; and therefore it could not be just for me to fall upon them; that this would justify the conduct of the Spaniards in all their barbarities practised in America, where they destroyed millions of these people; who, however they were idolators and barbarians, and had several bloody and barbarous rites in their customs, such as sacrificing human bodies to their idols, were yet, as to the Spaniards, very innocent people; and that the rooting them out of the country is spoken of with the utmost abhorrence and detestation by even the Spaniards themselves at this time, and by all other Christian nations of Europe, as a mere butchery, a bloody and unnatural piece of cruelty, unjustifiable either to God or man; and for which the very name of a Spaniard is reckoned to be frightful and terrible, to all people of humanity or of Christian compassion; as if the kingdom of Spain were particularly eminent for the produce of a race of men who were without principles of tenderness, or the common bowels of pity to the miserable, which is reckoned to be a mark of generous temper in the mind.
paragraphs.cn: 其次,我想到:尽管他们彼此相待的方式如此野蛮、如此灭绝人性,可这其实与我毫不相干:这些人并没有加害于我;倘若他们来犯,或我为了眼前自保而觉得非攻击他们不可,那还能说出点道理来:可我如今还不在他们的势力范围之内,他们对我也确实一无所知,因而对我并无图谋;所以我去攻击他们并不正当;这么做无异于替西班牙人在美洲犯下的一切暴行辩护,他们在那里屠杀了成百上千万这样的人;那些人虽是偶像崇拜者和野蛮人,习俗中有好几样血腥野蛮的仪式,比如用活人祭祀他们的偶像,可就对西班牙人而言,他们却是十分无辜的人;把他们从那片土地上斩尽杀绝,如今连西班牙人自己、以及欧洲所有别的基督教国家,都怀着极度的憎恶和厌恶提起这事,说那纯是一场屠杀,一桩血腥而违反天理的暴行,无论对上帝还是对世人都无法交代;正因如此,“西班牙人”这名字本身,在一切有人性、有基督徒慈悲之心的人听来,都成了可怕可憎的字眼;仿佛西班牙王国格外盛产这样一类人:他们毫无怜悯之心,对苦难者也没有寻常的恻隐之肠,而这恻隐之心本是心地宽厚的标志。

paragraphs.en: These considerations really put me to a pause, and to a kind of a full stop; and I began by little and little to be off my design, and to conclude I had taken wrong measures in my resolution to attack the savages; and that it was not my business to meddle with them, unless they first attacked me; and this it was my business, if possible, to prevent: but that, if I were discovered and attacked by them, I knew my duty.
paragraphs.cn: 这些思量真的让我停顿下来,几乎完全打住了;我一点一点地放弃了原来的打算,断定自己下决心去攻击野人是采取了错误的对策;除非他们先来攻击我,否则跟他们纠缠并不是我该做的事;而我该做的,是尽可能设法防止这种事发生:不过,万一我被他们发现并遭到攻击,我知道自己该尽的本分。

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, I argued with myself that this really was the way not to deliver myself, but entirely to ruin and destroy myself; for unless I was sure to kill every one that not only should be on shore at that time, but that should ever come on shore afterwards, if but one of them escaped to tell their country-people what had happened, they would come over again by thousands to revenge the death of their fellows, and I should only bring upon myself a certain destruction, which, at present, I had no manner of occasion for.
paragraphs.cn: 另一方面,我又跟自己争辩说:这样做其实非但救不了自己,反倒会把自己彻底毁掉;因为除非我有把握把当时在岸上的每一个人、以及日后凡登岸的每一个人全都杀光,否则只要有一个逃回去,把发生的事告诉他的同胞,他们就会成千上万地再度渡海而来,为死去的同伴报仇,而我只会给自己招来必死之祸,这在眼下我根本毫无必要。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, I concluded that I ought, neither in principle nor in policy, one way or other, to concern myself in this affair: that my business was, by all possible means to conceal myself from them, and not to leave the least sign for them to guess by that there were any living creatures upon the island—I mean of human shape.
paragraphs.cn: 总而言之,我断定:无论从道义上还是从策略上,这件事我都不该以任何方式去插手:我该做的,是想尽一切办法把自己藏得让他们看不见,不留下丝毫痕迹让他们猜到岛上有活物——我是说有人形的活物。

paragraphs.en: Religion joined in with this prudential resolution; and I was convinced now, many ways, that I was perfectly out of my duty when I was laying all my bloody schemes for the destruction of innocent creatures—I mean innocent as to me.
paragraphs.cn: 信仰也支持这一明智的决定;如今我从多方面确信,当我筹划种种血腥计谋去毁灭无辜生灵时——我是说对我而言无辜——我完全越出了自己的本分。

paragraphs.en: As to the crimes they were guilty of towards one another, I had nothing to do with them; they were national, and I ought to leave them to the justice of God, who is the Governor of nations, and knows how, by national punishments, to make a just retribution for national offences, and to bring public judgments upon those who offend in a public manner, by such ways as best please Him.
paragraphs.cn: 至于他们彼此之间所犯的罪,那与我无关;那是他们民族内部的事,我应当把它交给上帝的公义去处置,他是万民的主宰,知道如何以民族性的刑罚,为民族性的罪过施行公正的报应,又如何用最合他心意的方式,给那些公然作恶的人降下公开的审判。

paragraphs.en: This appeared so clear to me now, that nothing was a greater satisfaction to me than that I had not been suffered to do a thing which I now saw so much reason to believe would have been no less a sin than that of wilful murder if I had committed it; and I gave most humble thanks on my knees to God, that He had thus delivered me from blood-guiltiness; beseeching Him to grant me the protection of His providence, that I might not fall into the hands of the barbarians, or that I might not lay my hands upon them, unless I had a more clear call from Heaven to do it, in defence of my own life.
paragraphs.cn: 如今这道理在我看来如此清楚,再没有比这更让我欣慰的了:我竟没有被容许去做一件我现在看来大有理由相信、一旦做了便无异于蓄意杀人之罪的事;我跪下向上帝献上最谦卑的感谢,谢他这样救我脱离了流血的罪;并恳求他以他的护佑保守我,使我不致落到那些野蛮人手里,也不致对他们下手,除非我得到上天更明确的召唤,为保全自己的性命而这样做。

paragraphs.en: In this disposition I continued for near a year after this; and so far was I from desiring an occasion for falling upon these wretches, that in all that time I never once went up the hill to see whether there were any of them in sight, or to know whether any of them had been on shore there or not, that I might not be tempted to renew any of my contrivances against them, or be provoked by any advantage that might present itself to fall upon them; only this I did: I went and removed my boat, which I had on the other side of the island, and carried it down to the east end of the whole island, where I ran it into a little cove, which I found under some high rocks, and where I knew, by reason of the currents, the savages durst not, at least would not, come with their boats upon any account whatever.
paragraphs.cn: 怀着这样的心境,此后我又过了将近一年;我非但丝毫不想找机会去袭击这些恶徒,反而在这整段时间里一次也没爬上那座山,去看看有没有他们的人出现,或探明有没有他们的人在那里上过岸,免得我受了诱惑,重新捡起对付他们的种种诡计,或被眼前出现的什么便利所激,去袭击他们;我只做了这一件事:我去把我那条搁在岛另一边的船挪走,一直拖到整座岛的东端,让它驶进我在几块高岩下发现的一个小湾里;我知道,由于那里水流的缘故,野人无论如何都不敢——至少不会——把船开到那儿来。

paragraphs.en: With my boat I carried away everything that I had left there belonging to her, though not necessary for the bare going thither—viz. a mast and sail which I had made for her, and a thing like an anchor, but which, indeed, could not be called either anchor or grapnel; however, it was the best I could make of its kind: all these I removed, that there might not be the least shadow for discovery, or appearance of any boat, or of any human habitation upon the island.
paragraphs.cn: 我把船上凡是属于它的东西也都一并搬走了,尽管单为把船划到那儿去并用不着它们——那就是我给它做的一根桅杆和一张帆,还有一个像锚的东西,其实那既算不上锚也算不上抓钩;不过,那已是我尽力所能做出的同类东西了:这些我全搬走,免得留下丝毫蛛丝马迹,让人发现岛上有船、或有人居住的迹象。

paragraphs.en: Besides this, I kept myself, as I said, more retired than ever, and seldom went from my cell except upon my constant employment, to milk my she-goats, and manage my little flock in the wood, which, as it was quite on the other part of the island, was out of danger; for certain, it is that these savage people, who sometimes haunted this island, never came with any thoughts of finding anything here, and consequently never wandered off from the coast, and I doubt not but they might have been several times on shore after my apprehensions of them had made me cautious, as well as before.
paragraphs.cn: 除此之外,我如前所说,把自己藏得比以往更严,除了照例去挤母羊的奶、照管我在林中那一小群羊之外,很少离开我的洞穴;那林子完全在岛的另一头,没有危险;因为可以肯定,这些偶尔光顾此岛的野人,从没想过要在这里找到什么东西,因而从不离开海岸往里走,而且我毫不怀疑,不论在我因怕他们而变得谨慎之前还是之后,他们都可能已经上过岸好几次了。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, I looked back with some horror upon the thoughts of what my condition would have been if I had chopped upon them and been discovered before that; when, naked and unarmed, except with one gun, and that loaded often only with small shot, I walked everywhere, peeping and peering about the island, to see what I could get; what a surprise should I have been in if, when I discovered the print of a man’s foot, I had, instead of that, seen fifteen or twenty savages, and found them pursuing me, and by the swiftness of their running no possibility of my escaping them!
paragraphs.cn: 说真的,我回想起来还有些不寒而栗:倘若在那之前我撞见了他们、被他们发现,我的处境该会是什么样子?那时我赤手空拳,除了一支枪——而且往往只装了些小弹丸——就到处走动,在岛上东张西望、探头探脑,看能捡点什么;要是当初我发现那人的脚印时,看见的不是脚印,而是十五二十个野人,还发现他们正追赶我,而凭他们奔跑之快我根本无处可逃,那我该会惊骇成什么样子啊!

paragraphs.en: The thoughts of this sometimes sank my very soul within me, and distressed my mind so much that I could not soon recover it, to think what I should have done, and how I should not only have been unable to resist them, but even should not have had presence of mind enough to do what I might have done; much less what now, after so much consideration and preparation, I might be able to do.
paragraphs.cn: 一想到这些,我有时整个心都往下沉,愁得我久久不能平复:我想到自己当时该怎么办,想到我不但根本无力抵抗他们,甚至连做那点本可能做到的事的镇定都不会有;更别提如今经过这么多思量和准备之后,我或许能做到的事了。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, after serious thinking of these things, I would be melancholy, and sometimes it would last a great while; but I resolved it all at last into thankfulness to that Providence which had delivered me from so many unseen dangers, and had kept me from those mischiefs which I could have no way been the agent in delivering myself from, because I had not the least notion of any such thing depending, or the least supposition of its being possible.
paragraphs.cn: 说真的,认真想过这些事之后,我会郁郁不乐,有时一连闷上好长一段时间;可到头来,我把这一切都化作了对天意的感恩——是天意救我脱离了那么多我看不见的危险,使我免遭那些祸患;而对那些祸患,我根本无从靠自己去脱身,因为我压根儿没料到会有这类事临头,连它可能发生也想都没想过。

paragraphs.en: This renewed a contemplation which often had come into my thoughts in former times, when first I began to see the merciful dispositions of Heaven, in the dangers we run through in this life; how wonderfully we are delivered when we know nothing of it; how, when we are in a quandary as we call it, a doubt or hesitation whether to go this way or that way, a secret hint shall direct us this way, when we intended to go that way: nay, when sense, our own inclination, and perhaps business has called us to go the other way, yet a strange impression upon the mind, from we know not what springs, and by we know not what power, shall overrule us to go this way; and it shall afterwards appear that had we gone that way, which we should have gone, and even to our imagination ought to have gone, we should have been ruined and lost.
paragraphs.cn: 这重新勾起了我从前常有的一番沉思——那还是我头一回开始看出上天在我们今生所历的种种危险中那仁慈的安排时候的事:我们在毫不知情之际,竟被奇妙地救护;当我们如俗话所说进退两难、迟疑不定该走这条路还是那条路时,一个隐秘的暗示会指引我们走这条路,而我们本打算走那条路:不,即便理智、我们自己的意愿、也许还有正事都在催我们走那一条,可心头却会莫名地生出一种感触,不知从何而来、凭何种力量,硬是压着我们走这一条;事后便会明白,若当初走了那条我们本该走、连想象中也觉得该走的路,我们准会身败名裂、性命不保。

paragraphs.en: Upon these and many like reflections I afterwards made it a certain rule with me, that whenever I found those secret hints or pressings of mind to doing or not doing anything that presented, or going this way or that way, I never failed to obey the secret dictate; though I knew no other reason for it than such a pressure or such a hint hung upon my mind.
paragraphs.cn: 经过这些以及许多类似的反省,我后来给自己定了一条铁律:每当我心头出现那种隐秘的暗示或催促,叫我去做或不去做眼前的某件事、或走这条路还是那条路时,我从不违背那隐秘的指引;尽管我除了觉得心头有这么一股催促、这么一个暗示之外,说不出别的什么理由。

paragraphs.en: I could give many examples of the success of this conduct in the course of my life, but more especially in the latter part of my inhabiting this unhappy island; besides many occasions which it is very likely I might have taken notice of, if I had seen with the same eyes then that I see with now.
paragraphs.cn: 我这一生中,尤其是在我住在这座苦岛的后期,能举出许多例子来说明这样行事的好处;此外还有许多别的情形,若当年我像如今这样看事情,我很可能早就留意到了。

paragraphs.en: But it is never too late to be wise; and I cannot but advise all considering men, whose lives are attended with such extraordinary incidents as mine, or even though not so extraordinary, not to slight such secret intimations of Providence, let them come from what invisible intelligence they will.
paragraphs.cn: 但为时未晚、悟得再迟也不算晚;我不禁要奉劝一切善于思量、一生际遇像我这般离奇——即便不这么离奇——的人:切莫轻看天意这类隐秘的示意,不论它们出自何种看不见的灵智。

paragraphs.en: That I shall not discuss, and perhaps cannot account for; but certainly they are a proof of the converse of spirits, and a secret communication between those embodied and those unembodied, and such a proof as can never be withstood; of which I shall have occasion to give some remarkable instances in the remainder of my solitary residence in this dismal place.
paragraphs.cn: 那一点我不去讨论,也许我也解释不清;但它们无疑证明了灵界之间的往来,证明了有形之灵与无形之灵之间有一种隐秘的沟通,而且这证明确凿得无可辩驳;关于这一点,在我孤居这凄凉之地的余下日子里,我还会有机会举出几个引人注目的例子来。

paragraphs.en: I believe the reader of this will not think it strange if I confess that these anxieties, these constant dangers I lived in, and the concern that was now upon me, put an end to all invention, and to all the contrivances that I had laid for my future accommodations and conveniences.
paragraphs.cn: 读到这里的读者,想必不会觉得奇怪:我承认,我所过的这种焦虑不安、时时身处险境的日子,以及如今压在我心头的忧虑,叫我一切巧思都断了念头,连我为将来的居住和便利所定的种种打算也全都搁下了。

paragraphs.en: I had the care of my safety more now upon my hands than that of my food.
paragraphs.cn: 如今操心自己的安全,比操心口粮还要占去我更多的心思。

paragraphs.en: I cared not to drive a nail, or chop a stick of wood now, for fear the noise I might make should be heard: much less would I fire a gun for the same reason: and above all I was intolerably uneasy at making any fire, lest the smoke, which is visible at a great distance in the day, should betray me.
paragraphs.cn: 我此刻连钉一枚钉子、劈一根木柴都不敢,生怕弄出的响声被人听见:更别提为同样的缘故去放枪了;尤其是一生火我就坐立不安到无法忍受,唯恐那大白天里老远都看得见的烟把我出卖了。

paragraphs.en: For this reason, I removed that part of my business which required fire, such as burning of pots and pipes, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 为此,我把凡需要用火的那部分活计,比如烧陶罐、烧烟斗之类,

paragraphs.en: , into my new apartment in the woods; where, after I had been some time, I found, to my unspeakable consolation, a mere natural cave in the earth, which went in a vast way, and where, I daresay, no savage, had he been at the mouth of it, would be so hardy as to venture in; nor, indeed, would any man else, but one who, like me, wanted nothing so much as a safe retreat.
paragraphs.cn: 都搬到了我在林中那处新住所去;在那里待了些时候之后,我意外地发现了一处地下天然的洞穴,叫我说不出地宽慰;那洞穴往里延伸得极深,我敢说,哪怕有野人站在洞口,也没胆量冒险钻进去;说真的,除了像我这样别的什么都不缺、单缺一处安全藏身之所的人,别人也不会进去。

paragraphs.en: The mouth of this hollow was at the bottom of a great rock, where, by mere accident (I would say, if I did not see abundant reason to ascribe all such things now to Providence), I was cutting down some thick branches of trees to make charcoal; and before I go on I must observe the reason of my making this charcoal, which was this—I was afraid of making a smoke about my habitation, as I said before; and yet I could not live there without baking my bread, cooking my meat, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 这洞口在一块大岩石的底部,我纯属偶然(我该说“偶然”——若不是我如今有充分理由把这类事全归于天意的话)在那儿砍些粗树枝烧木炭时发现的;在往下说之前,我得先交代一下我烧这木炭的缘由,是这样的:如前所说,我怕在住处附近生烟;可我住在那里,又不能不烤面包、煮肉之类;

paragraphs.en: ; so I contrived to burn some wood here, as I had seen done in England, under turf, till it became chark or dry coal: and then putting the fire out, I preserved the coal to carry home, and perform the other services for which fire was wanting, without danger of smoke.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我想了个法子,像我在英格兰见人做过的那样,在这里把些木头盖上草皮闷烧,烧成焦炭或干煤;然后把火熄灭,把炭存起来带回家,去做那些非用火不可的别的活计,又不必冒生烟的危险。

paragraphs.en: But this is by-the-bye.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这是顺带一提。

paragraphs.en: While I was cutting down some wood here, I perceived that, behind a very thick branch of low brushwood or underwood, there was a kind of hollow place: I was curious to look in it; and getting with difficulty into the mouth of it, I found it was pretty large, that is to say, sufficient for me to stand upright in it, and perhaps another with me: but I must confess to you that I made more haste out than I did in, when looking farther into the place, and which was perfectly dark, I saw two broad shining eyes of some creature, whether devil or man I knew not, which twinkled like two stars; the dim light from the cave’s mouth shining directly in, and making the reflection.
paragraphs.cn: 我正在这里砍些木头时,发现一丛很密的矮树林或灌木后面有个空洞似的地方:我好奇想进去看看;费了好大劲才钻进洞口,发现里面挺大,也就是说,足够我在里面直起身子站着,或许还能再站一个人:可我得向你老实承认,我进去时慢,出来时可快多了;因为当我再往洞里深处望去、那里一片漆黑时,我看见有个什么东西的两只又大又亮的眼睛,是鬼是人我说不清,像两颗星星似的一闪一闪;那是洞口透进的微光直照进去,反射出来的。

paragraphs.en: However, after some pause I recovered myself, and began to call myself a thousand fools, and to think that he that was afraid to see the devil was not fit to live twenty years in an island all alone; and that I might well think there was nothing in this cave that was more frightful than myself.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,愣了一会儿之后,我镇定下来,开始骂自己是天字第一号大傻瓜,心想:一个怕见魔鬼的人,根本不配独自一人在岛上住二十年;我大可认定,这洞里没有什么比我自己更可怕的东西。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, plucking up my courage, I took up a firebrand, and in I rushed again, with the stick flaming in my hand: I had not gone three steps in before I was almost as frightened as before; for I heard a very loud sigh, like that of a man in some pain, and it was followed by a broken noise, as of words half expressed, and then a deep sigh again.
paragraphs.cn: 想到这里,我鼓起勇气,抄起一根火把,举着那燃着火的木棍又冲了进去:才走进三步,我就几乎又像先前那样吓坏了;因为我听见一声很响的叹息,像是个疼痛中的人发出的,接着是一阵含混的声响,仿佛半吐半含的话语,然后又是一声长长的叹息。

paragraphs.en: I stepped back, and was indeed struck with such a surprise that it put me into a cold sweat, and if I had had a hat on my head, I will not answer for it that my hair might not have lifted it off.
paragraphs.cn: 我倒退了一步,确实吓得浑身一激灵,惊出一身冷汗;那时我头上要是戴着帽子,我可不敢担保我的头发不会把它顶起来。

paragraphs.en: But still plucking up my spirits as well as I could, and encouraging myself a little with considering that the power and presence of God was everywhere, and was able to protect me, I stepped forward again, and by the light of the firebrand, holding it up a little over my head, I saw lying on the ground a monstrous, frightful old he-goat, just making his will, as we say, and gasping for life, and, dying, indeed, of mere old age.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我还是尽量给自己壮胆,又想到上帝的能力和同在无处不在、能够保护我,便稍稍宽了心,重新往前迈步;借着火把的光,把它稍稍举过头顶,我看见地上躺着一只怪模怪样、样子吓人的老公羊,正如俗话所说“立遗嘱”呢,喘着最后一口气,确实是纯粹老死的。

paragraphs.en: I stirred him a little to see if I could get him out, and he essayed to get up, but was not able to raise himself; and I thought with myself he might even lie there—for if he had frightened me, so he would certainly fright any of the savages, if any of them should be so hardy as to come in there while he had any life in him.
paragraphs.cn: 我拨弄了它几下,看能不能把它弄出去;它挣扎着想站起来,却支撑不起自己;我心想,干脆让它躺在那儿好了——因为它既然能吓到我,那么只要它还有一口气,万一有野人胆大敢进来,它准也能把野人吓跑。

paragraphs.en: I was now recovered from my surprise, and began to look round me, when I found the cave was but very small—that is to say, it might be about twelve feet over, but in no manner of shape, neither round nor square, no hands having ever been employed in making it but those of mere Nature.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我从惊吓中缓过神来,开始打量四周,发现这洞其实很小——也就是说,大概十二英尺见方,却毫无规整的形状,既不圆也不方,因为除了纯粹的大自然,从没有人的手插手做过它。

paragraphs.en: I observed also that there was a place at the farther side of it that went in further, but was so low that it required me to creep upon my hands and knees to go into it, and whither it went I knew not; so, having no candle, I gave it over for that time, but resolved to go again the next day provided with candles and a tinder-box, which I had made of the lock of one of the muskets, with some wildfire in the pan.
paragraphs.cn: 我还注意到,在它更里边的一头有个地方,再往里延伸,却矮得很,要我手脚并用爬着才能进去,而它通向哪里我不知道;当时手边没有蜡烛,我便暂且作罢,不过打定主意第二天带上蜡烛和一个火绒盒再来;那火绒盒是我用一支火枪的枪机做的,里面撒了些引火药。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, the next day I came provided with six large candles of my own making (for I made very good candles now of goat’s tallow, but was hard set for candle-wick, using sometimes rags or rope-yarn, and sometimes the dried rind of a weed like nettles); and going into this low place I was obliged to creep upon all-fours as I have said, almost ten yards—which, by the way, I thought was a venture bold enough, considering that I knew not how far it might go, nor what was beyond it.
paragraphs.cn: 于是第二天我便带着六支自己做的大蜡烛来了(如今我用羊脂能做出很好的蜡烛了,只是烛芯很难弄,有时用破布或麻绳的纱,有时用一种像荨麻的野草晒干的皮);钻进这处低矮的地方,如前所说,我不得不四肢着地爬行,爬了差不多十码——顺便说一句,我觉得这一钻已经够大胆的了,因为我既不知道它有多深,也不知道那头是什么。

paragraphs.en: When I had got through the strait, I found the roof rose higher up, I believe near twenty feet; but never was such a glorious sight seen in the island, I daresay, as it was to look round the sides and roof of this vault or cave—the wall reflected a hundred thousand lights to me from my two candles.
paragraphs.cn: 钻过这条窄道后,我发现顶部升高了,我估摸着有近二十英尺;可我敢说,岛上从没见过这么壮丽的景象,就像环顾这处地窖或岩洞的四壁和洞顶时所见的那样——洞壁把我两支蜡烛的光反射给我,化作了千千万万点光芒。

paragraphs.en: What it was in the rock—whether diamonds or any other precious stones, or gold which I rather supposed it to be—I knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 岩石里究竟是什么——是钻石还是别的宝石,或是黄金(我倒宁愿认为是黄金)——我不知道。

paragraphs.en: The place I was in was a most delightful cavity, or grotto, though perfectly dark; the floor was dry and level, and had a sort of a small loose gravel upon it, so that there was no nauseous or venomous creature to be seen, neither was there any damp or wet on the sides or roof.
paragraphs.cn: 我所在的地方是个极其宜人的空穴,或者说岩洞,尽管里面漆黑一团;地面又干又平,上面铺着一层松散的细砾石,所以既看不见什么令人作呕或有毒的东西,四壁和洞顶也没有一丝潮气或水渍。

paragraphs.en: The only difficulty in it was the entrance—which, however, as it was a place of security, and such a retreat as I wanted; I thought was a convenience; so that I was really rejoiced at the discovery, and resolved, without any delay, to bring some of those things which I was most anxious about to this place: particularly, I resolved to bring hither my magazine of powder, and all my spare arms—viz. two fowling-pieces—for I had three in all—and three muskets—for of them I had eight in all; so I kept in my castle only five, which stood ready mounted like pieces of cannon on my outmost fence, and were ready also to take out upon any expedition.
paragraphs.cn: 它唯一的难处就在入口——不过,既然这是个安全的地方,正是我想要的那种退身之所,我倒觉得这入口反是一桩便利;所以我真是为这一发现欢喜不已,决心毫不迟延地把我最放心不下的一些东西搬到这里来:我尤其决定把我的火药库和所有备用的武器都搬到这儿——也就是两支鸟枪——我一共有三支——和三支火枪——这类枪我一共有八支;这样我城堡里只留下五支,像大炮似的架在我最外层的围栏上,随时可用,也随时可以取出来带去应付任何行动。

paragraphs.en: Upon this occasion of removing my ammunition I happened to open the barrel of powder which I took up out of the sea, and which had been wet, and I found that the water had penetrated about three or four inches into the powder on every side, which caking and growing hard, had preserved the inside like a kernel in the shell, so that I had near sixty pounds of very good powder in the centre of the cask.
paragraphs.cn: 趁这次搬运弹药,我碰巧打开了那桶我从海里捞上来、曾被水浸过的火药,发现水从四面渗进了火药大约三四英寸深,那部分结成硬块,反倒把里面护住了,就像果壳里的果仁一样,所以桶中央还有近六十磅上好的火药。

paragraphs.en: This was a very agreeable discovery to me at that time; so I carried all away thither, never keeping above two or three pounds of powder with me in my castle, for fear of a surprise of any kind; I also carried thither all the lead I had left for bullets.
paragraphs.cn: 这在当时对我是个十分称心的发现;于是我把这些全搬到那里去了,城堡里再也不留两三磅以上的火药,以防遭到任何意外;我还把剩下用来做子弹的铅也全搬了去。

paragraphs.en: I fancied myself now like one of the ancient giants who were said to live in caves and holes in the rocks, where none could come at them; for I persuaded myself, while I was here, that if five hundred savages were to hunt me, they could never find me out—or if they did, they would not venture to attack me here.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我幻想自己成了古时那些巨人中的一个,据说他们就住在岩石间的洞穴和窟窿里,谁也够不着他们;因为待在这里时,我说服了自己:哪怕有五百个野人来追捕我,他们也永远找不到我——就算找到了,也不敢冒险到这里来攻击我。

paragraphs.en: The old goat whom I found expiring died in the mouth of the cave the next day after I made this discovery; and I found it much easier to dig a great hole there, and throw him in and cover him with earth, than to drag him out; so I interred him there, to prevent offence to my nose.
paragraphs.cn: 我发现那只奄奄一息的老公羊,在我作出这一发现的第二天,就死在了洞口;我觉得在那里挖个大坑,把它扔进去用土盖上,比把它拖出去省事得多;于是我就地把它埋了,免得熏了我的鼻子。

paragraphs.en: I was now in the twenty-third year of my residence in this island, and was so naturalised to the place and the manner of living, that, could I but have enjoyed the certainty that no savages would come to the place to disturb me, I could have been content to have capitulated for spending the rest of my time there, even to the last moment, till I had laid me down and died, like the old goat in the cave.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我在这座岛上已经住到了第二十三个年头,对这里的环境和生活方式早已习以为常。要是我能确信没有野人会闯来打扰我,我倒也心甘情愿在这儿了此余生,一直待到最后一刻,直到我像那只死在山洞里的老山羊一样躺下死去。

paragraphs.en: I had also arrived to some little diversions and amusements, which made the time pass a great deal more pleasantly with me than it did before—first, I had taught my Poll, as I noted before, to speak; and he did it so familiarly, and talked so articulately and plain, that it was very pleasant to me; and he lived with me no less than six-and-twenty years.
paragraphs.cn: 我还给自己找了些小小的消遣和乐趣,日子过得比从前愉快多了。首先,我像前面说过的那样教会了我的鹦鹉说话,它说得那么亲昵,咬字那么清楚流利,让我十分开心;它跟着我一共活了整整二十六年。

paragraphs.en: How long he might have lived afterwards I know not, though I know they have a notion in the Brazils that they live a hundred years.
paragraphs.cn: 至于它后来还能活多久,我就不得而知了,不过我知道巴西人有个说法,说这种鸟能活上一百岁。

paragraphs.en: My dog was a pleasant and loving companion to me for no less than sixteen years of my time, and then died of mere old age.
paragraphs.cn: 我那条狗陪伴了我整整十六年,是我可亲可爱的伙伴,后来纯粹因为年老而死去。

paragraphs.en: As for my cats, they multiplied, as I have observed, to that degree that I was obliged to shoot several of them at first, to keep them from devouring me and all I had; but at length, when the two old ones I brought with me were gone, and after some time continually driving them from me, and letting them have no provision with me, they all ran wild into the woods, except two or three favourites, which I kept tame, and whose young, when they had any, I always drowned; and these were part of my family.
paragraphs.cn: 至于我的那些猫,前面说过,它们繁殖得那么厉害,起初我不得不打死好几只,免得它们把我和我所有的东西都吃个精光;可到后来,我带来的那两只老猫死了,又经过一段时间不断地把它们赶走、不给它们东西吃,它们便全都跑进树林里野化了,只留下两三只我特别喜爱的,养得驯服,它们要是生了小猫,我总是把小猫淹死;这几只算是我家庭的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Besides these I always kept two or three household kids about me, whom I taught to feed out of my hand; and I had two more parrots, which talked pretty well, and would all call “Robin Crusoe,” but none like my first; nor, indeed, did I take the pains with any of them that I had done with him.
paragraphs.cn: 除了这些,我身边还总养着两三只家养的小山羊,教它们从我手里吃食;我另外还有两只鹦鹉,说得也挺不错,都会叫“罗宾·克鲁索”,可没一只比得上我头一只;说实话,我也没像调教头一只那样在它们身上下过工夫。

paragraphs.en: I had also several tame sea-fowls, whose name I knew not, that I caught upon the shore, and cut their wings; and the little stakes which I had planted before my castle-wall being now grown up to a good thick grove, these fowls all lived among these low trees, and bred there, which was very agreeable to me; so that, as I said above, I began to be very well contented with the life I led, if I could have been secured from the dread of the savages.
paragraphs.cn: 我还养了几只叫不出名字的驯服海鸟,是我在海边捉来剪了翅膀的;从前我在城堡墙外插下的那些小木桩,如今已长成一片茂密的小树林,这些海鸟便都栖息在这些矮树间,还在那里繁殖,这让我很是惬意;所以正如前面所说,只要能免去对野人的恐惧,我对自己所过的生活已经相当满足了。

paragraphs.en: But it was otherwise directed; and it may not be amiss for all people who shall meet with my story to make this just observation from it: How frequently, in the course of our lives, the evil which in itself we seek most to shun, and which, when we are fallen into, is the most dreadful to us, is oftentimes the very means or door of our deliverance, by which alone we can be raised again from the affliction we are fallen into.
paragraphs.cn: 可命运偏偏另有安排;凡是读到我这段经历的人,不妨都从中得出这样一个中肯的体会:在我们一生当中,那件我们竭力想躲开、一旦陷进去便觉得最可怕的祸事,却常常正是我们获救的途径或门径,唯有借着它,我们才能从所陷的苦难中重新被拯救出来。

paragraphs.en: I could give many examples of this in the course of my unaccountable life; but in nothing was it more particularly remarkable than in the circumstances of my last years of solitary residence in this island.
paragraphs.cn: 在我这段难以言说的人生里,我可以举出许多这样的例子;而其中最为鲜明的,莫过于我在这座岛上独居的最后几年所遭遇的情形了。

paragraphs.en: It was now the month of December, as I said above, in my twenty-third year; and this, being the southern solstice (for winter I cannot call it), was the particular time of my harvest, and required me to be pretty much abroad in the fields, when, going out early in the morning, even before it was thorough daylight, I was surprised with seeing a light of some fire upon the shore, at a distance from me of about two miles, toward that part of the island where I had observed some savages had been, as before, and not on the other side; but, to my great affliction, it was on my side of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 如前所说,那时正是我住岛第二十三年的十二月;这个季节是南半球的夏至(我实在没法把它叫作冬天),正是我收割庄稼的时候,得常常到田里去。一天清早,天还没大亮我就出了门,却惊愕地看见离我约莫两英里的海边有一堆火光,就在我从前留意到有野人来过的那一带岛上,不在另一边;可让我大为苦恼的是,这回竟在我这一侧的海岛上。

paragraphs.en: I was indeed terribly surprised at the sight, and stopped short within my grove, not daring to go out, lest I might be surprised; and yet I had no more peace within, from the apprehensions I had that if these savages, in rambling over the island, should find my corn standing or cut, or any of my works or improvements, they would immediately conclude that there were people in the place, and would then never rest till they had found me out.
paragraphs.cn: 这景象确实把我吓坏了,我在小树林里停住脚,不敢出去,生怕被人撞见;然而我心里也不得安宁,因为我担心这些野人若在岛上四处游荡,发现我那立着或割下的庄稼,或是我的什么劳作和经营,他们立刻就会断定这地方有人,那就绝不会罢休,非把我找出来不可。

paragraphs.en: In this extremity I went back directly to my castle, pulled up the ladder after me, and made all things without look as wild and natural as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 情急之下,我径直退回城堡,把梯子拉了上来,又把外面一切都尽量弄得像荒野一般自然。

paragraphs.en: Then I prepared myself within, putting myself in a posture of defence.
paragraphs.cn: 随后我在里面做起准备,摆出防御的架势。

paragraphs.en: I loaded all my cannon, as I called them—that is to say, my muskets, which were mounted upon my new fortification—and all my pistols, and resolved to defend myself to the last gasp—not forgetting seriously to commend myself to the Divine protection, and earnestly to pray to God to deliver me out of the hands of the barbarians.
paragraphs.cn: 我把我那些所谓的大炮统统装上弹药——也就是架在新工事上的那几支火枪——还有我所有的手枪,决心拼到最后一口气来保卫自己;同时我也没忘记郑重地把自己托付给上天的护佑,恳切地祈求上帝把我从这些野蛮人手中救出来。

paragraphs.en: I continued in this posture about two hours, and began to be impatient for intelligence abroad, for I had no spies to send out.
paragraphs.cn: 我保持这个架势约莫两个钟头,渐渐按捺不住想探听外面的动静,可我又没有探子可派出去。

paragraphs.en: After sitting a while longer, and musing what I should do in this case, I was not able to bear sitting in ignorance longer; so setting up my ladder to the side of the hill, where there was a flat place, as I observed before, and then pulling the ladder after me, I set it up again and mounted the top of the hill, and pulling out my perspective glass, which I had taken on purpose, I laid me down flat on my belly on the ground, and began to look for the place.
paragraphs.cn: 又坐了一会儿,盘算着这情形下该怎么办,我实在受不了这样一无所知地干坐着;于是我把梯子架到山坡那块我先前说过的平地上,拉上梯子后再架起来,爬上了山顶,取出我特意带来的望远镜,趴在地上,开始朝那地方望去。

paragraphs.en: I presently found there were no less than nine naked savages sitting round a small fire they had made, not to warm them, for they had no need of that, the weather being extremely hot, but, as I supposed, to dress some of their barbarous diet of human flesh which they had brought with them, whether alive or dead I could not tell.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻看清那里坐着不下九个赤身的野人,围着他们生的一小堆火,不是为了取暖——天气热得很,他们用不着取暖——而是照我猜想,是要烹煮他们带来的、那种以人肉为食的野蛮吃食,只是那人是死是活我就说不上来了。

paragraphs.en: They had two canoes with them, which they had hauled up upon the shore; and as it was then ebb of tide, they seemed to me to wait for the return of the flood to go away again.
paragraphs.cn: 他们带着两只独木舟,已经拖上了海滩;当时正值退潮,依我看,他们像是在等涨潮回来好再离去。

paragraphs.en: It is not easy to imagine what confusion this sight put me into, especially seeing them come on my side of the island, and so near to me; but when I considered their coming must be always with the current of the ebb, I began afterwards to be more sedate in my mind, being satisfied that I might go abroad with safety all the time of the flood of tide, if they were not on shore before; and having made this observation, I went abroad about my harvest work with the more composure.
paragraphs.cn: 这景象把我搅得多么惊慌,实在难以想象,尤其见他们竟登上了我这一侧的岛、离我这么近;可当我一想到他们来时准是顺着退潮的水流,心里便渐渐镇定了些,因为我明白只要他们没提早上岸,涨潮那段时间我尽可以安然外出;有了这番观察,我便较为从容地去干我的收割活儿了。

paragraphs.en: As I expected, so it proved; for as soon as the tide made to the westward I saw them all take boat and row (or paddle as we call it) away.
paragraphs.cn: 果然不出我所料;因为潮水一往西退去,我就看见他们全都上了船,划着桨(用我们的话说是荡桨)走了。

paragraphs.en: I should have observed, that for an hour or more before they went off they were dancing, and I could easily discern their postures and gestures by my glass.
paragraphs.cn: 我该提一句,他们动身前有一个多钟头一直在跳舞,我用望远镜能清清楚楚看见他们的姿态和手势。

paragraphs.en: I could not perceive, by my nicest observation, but that they were stark naked, and had not the least covering upon them; but whether they were men or women I could not distinguish.
paragraphs.cn: 任凭我怎样仔细观察,也只看出他们浑身赤裸,身上连一点遮盖都没有;至于是男是女,我却分辨不出。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I saw them shipped and gone, I took two guns upon my shoulders, and two pistols in my girdle, and my great sword by my side without a scabbard, and with all the speed I was able to make went away to the hill where I had discovered the first appearance of all; and as soon as I got thither, which was not in less than two hours (for I could not go quickly, being so loaded with arms as I was), I perceived there had been three canoes more of the savages at that place; and looking out farther, I saw they were all at sea together, making over for the main.
paragraphs.cn: 一见他们上船走了,我便肩上扛了两支枪,腰带里插了两支手枪,身旁挎着我那把没有鞘的大刀,拼命赶往我最初发现火光的那座山;赶到那里少说也花了两个钟头(我身上背着这么多武器,走不快),我看出那地方另外还来过三只野人的独木舟;再往远处望去,只见他们全都一齐出海,朝大陆划去了。

paragraphs.en: This was a dreadful sight to me, especially as, going down to the shore, I could see the marks of horror which the dismal work they had been about had left behind it—viz. the blood, the bones, and part of the flesh of human bodies eaten and devoured by those wretches with merriment and sport.
paragraphs.cn: 这在我看来是个可怕的景象,尤其当我走下海滩,看到他们干下的那桩骇人勾当所留下的种种恐怖痕迹时——就是说,那些被这帮恶徒又吃又啃、还当作取乐消遣的人体,留下的鲜血、骨头和残肉。

paragraphs.en: I was so filled with indignation at the sight, that I now began to premeditate the destruction of the next that I saw there, let them be whom or how many soever.
paragraphs.cn: 眼前这一幕让我满腔义愤,我当下便开始盘算:下次再在那里见到他们,不管是谁、不管有多少,我都要把他们消灭掉。

paragraphs.en: It seemed evident to me that the visits which they made thus to this island were not very frequent, for it was above fifteen months before any more of them came on shore there again—that is to say, I neither saw them nor any footsteps or signals of them in all that time; for as to the rainy seasons, then they are sure not to come abroad, at least not so far.
paragraphs.cn: 在我看来很明显,他们到这岛上来并不太频繁,因为此后过了十五个多月才又有人上岸来——也就是说,这么长时间里我既没见到他们,也没见到他们的任何足迹或踪影;至于雨季,那时候他们准是不出门的,至少不会跑这么远。

paragraphs.en: Yet all this while I lived uncomfortably, by reason of the constant apprehensions of their coming upon me by surprise: from whence I observe, that the expectation of evil is more bitter than the suffering, especially if there is no room to shake off that expectation or those apprehensions.
paragraphs.cn: 然而这段日子我却过得很不安生,因为老是担心他们会冷不防扑到我头上:由此我体会到,对灾祸的预料比灾祸本身更让人难受,尤其是当你无从摆脱那份预料或那份忧惧的时候。

paragraphs.en: During all this time I was in a murdering humour, and spent most of my hours, which should have been better employed, in contriving how to circumvent and fall upon them the very next time I should see them—especially if they should be divided, as they were the last time, into two parties; nor did I consider at all that if I killed one party—suppose ten or a dozen—I was still the next day, or week, or month, to kill another, and so another, even _ad infinitum_, till I should be, at length, no less a murderer than they were in being man-eaters—and perhaps much more so.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间里我一直起着杀人的念头,把本该更好利用的大部分时光,都花在谋划下次一见到他们便如何设伏袭击上——尤其要是他们像上回那样分成两拨;我压根没去想,就算我杀掉一拨——比如说十个或一打——第二天、下一周或下个月,我还得再杀一拨,接着又一拨,如此没完没了,到头来我就跟他们这些吃人者一样,也成了个杀人凶手了——说不定还有过之而无不及。

paragraphs.en: I spent my days now in great perplexity and anxiety of mind, expecting that I should one day or other fall into the hands of these merciless creatures; and if I did at any time venture abroad, it was not without looking around me with the greatest care and caution imaginable.
paragraphs.cn: 这些日子我心绪极度纷乱、焦虑不安,总担心自己迟早会落到这些毫无怜悯之心的家伙手里;我但凡冒险外出,无不万分警觉、小心翼翼地四下张望。

paragraphs.en: And now I found, to my great comfort, how happy it was that I had provided a tame flock or herd of goats, for I durst not upon any account fire my gun, especially near that side of the island where they usually came, lest I should alarm the savages; and if they had fled from me now, I was sure to have them come again with perhaps two or three hundred canoes with them in a few days, and then I knew what to expect.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我大为欣慰地发现,幸好我早备下了一群驯养的山羊,因为无论如何我都不敢再开枪,尤其在他们常来的那一侧海岛附近,唯恐惊动了野人;要是这会儿把他们吓跑了,不出几天,他们准会带着两三百只独木舟卷土重来,那时的下场我就可想而知了。

paragraphs.en: However, I wore out a year and three months more before I ever saw any more of the savages, and then I found them again, as I shall soon observe.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我又熬过了一年零三个月,才再次见到野人,那情形我很快就要讲到。

paragraphs.en: It is true they might have been there once or twice; but either they made no stay, or at least I did not see them; but in the month of May, as near as I could calculate, and in my four-and-twentieth year, I had a very strange encounter with them; of which in its place.
paragraphs.cn: 说实在的,这期间他们兴许来过一两回;只是要么没停留,要么至少我没瞧见;可就在五月里(照我尽量推算的日子),也就是我住岛的第二十四个年头,我跟他们有过一次极其古怪的遭遇;这事容后再讲。

paragraphs.en: The perturbation of my mind during this fifteen or sixteen months’ interval was very great; I slept unquietly, dreamed always frightful dreams, and often started out of my sleep in the night.
paragraphs.cn: 在这十五六个月的间歇里,我心神的不安非常厉害;我睡不安稳,总做可怕的噩梦,夜里常常从睡梦中惊起。

paragraphs.en: In the day great troubles overwhelmed my mind; and in the night I dreamed often of killing the savages and of the reasons why I might justify doing it.
paragraphs.cn: 白天里,重重烦忧压得我心头难安;夜里,我又常梦见自己杀死野人,并梦见为什么杀他们才算正当的种种理由。

paragraphs.en: But to waive all this for a while.
paragraphs.cn: 这些且先撇下不谈。

paragraphs.en: It was in the middle of May, on the sixteenth day, I think, as well as my poor wooden calendar would reckon, for I marked all upon the post still; I say, it was on the sixteenth of May that it blew a very great storm of wind all day, with a great deal of lightning and thunder, and a very foul night it was after it.
paragraphs.cn: 那是五月中旬,我想大概是十六号——照我那可怜的木头日历推算的,因为我仍旧把日子全刻在那根柱子上;我是说,就在五月十六号那天,狂风大作,刮了整整一天,雷电交加,过后又是极其恶劣的一夜。

paragraphs.en: I knew not what was the particular occasion of it, but as I was reading in the Bible, and taken up with very serious thoughts about my present condition, I was surprised with the noise of a gun, as I thought, fired at sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道究竟是什么缘故,不过当我正在读《圣经》、满脑子极其严肃地思量着眼下的处境时,忽然一声枪响把我吓了一跳,我觉得那是从海上打来的。

paragraphs.en: This was, to be sure, a surprise quite of a different nature from any I had met with before; for the notions this put into my thoughts were quite of another kind.
paragraphs.cn: 这一惊可跟我从前遇到过的任何一次全然不同;因为它勾起我心头的联想是另一种性质的。

paragraphs.en: I started up in the greatest haste imaginable; and, in a trice, clapped my ladder to the middle place of the rock, and pulled it after me; and mounting it the second time, got to the top of the hill the very moment that a flash of fire bid me listen for a second gun, which, accordingly, in about half a minute I heard; and by the sound, knew that it was from that part of the sea where I was driven down the current in my boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我尽可能飞快地跳起身来,眨眼间就把梯子架到岩壁中段那块地方,拉上梯子,再第二次爬上去,恰在一道火光让我留神去听第二声炮响的那一刻登上了山顶;果然约莫半分钟后,我就听见了那第二声;听那声音,我知道是从当年我坐船被水流冲下去的那一带海面传来的。

paragraphs.en: I immediately considered that this must be some ship in distress, and that they had some comrade, or some other ship in company, and fired these for signals of distress, and to obtain help.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻想到,这准是哪条船遇了难,他们身边还有个同伴或另一条同行的船,便放炮作为求救的信号,好求人相助。

paragraphs.en: I had the presence of mind at that minute to think, that though I could not help them, it might be that they might help me; so I brought together all the dry wood I could get at hand, and making a good handsome pile, I set it on fire upon the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 那一刻我头脑还算清醒,想到自己虽帮不了他们,可他们说不定倒能帮我;于是我把手边能弄到的干柴统统聚拢起来,堆成一大堆,在山上把它点着了。

paragraphs.en: The wood was dry, and blazed freely; and, though the wind blew very hard, yet it burned fairly out; so that I was certain, if there was any such thing as a ship, they must needs see it.
paragraphs.cn: 柴是干的,烧得很旺;虽说风刮得厉害,火却烧得畅快;这么一来,我断定只要真有那么一条船,他们准能瞧见。

paragraphs.en: And no doubt they did; for as soon as ever my fire blazed up, I heard another gun, and after that several others, all from the same quarter.
paragraphs.cn: 他们无疑是瞧见了;因为我的火一烧旺,我就听见又是一声炮响,随后接连好几声,全都从同一个方向传来。

paragraphs.en: I plied my fire all night long, till daybreak: and when it was broad day, and the air cleared up, I saw something at a great distance at sea, full east of the island, whether a sail or a hull I could not distinguish—no, not with my glass: the distance was so great, and the weather still something hazy also; at least, it was so out at sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我把火添了整整一夜,直到天亮;等到大天亮、空气放晴,我望见远处海面上、正东方向有个东西,是帆是船身我分辨不出——不,连用望远镜也看不清:距离太远,天气也还有些雾蒙蒙的;至少海面上是这样。

paragraphs.en: I looked frequently at it all that day, and soon perceived that it did not move; so I presently concluded that it was a ship at anchor; and being eager, you may be sure, to be satisfied, I took my gun in my hand, and ran towards the south side of the island to the rocks where I had formerly been carried away by the current; and getting up there, the weather by this time being perfectly clear, I could plainly see, to my great sorrow, the wreck of a ship, cast away in the night upon those concealed rocks which I found when I was out in my boat; and which rocks, as they checked the violence of the stream, and made a kind of counter-stream, or eddy, were the occasion of my recovering from the most desperate, hopeless condition that ever I had been in in all my life.
paragraphs.cn: 那一整天我频频望着它,不久便看出它并不移动;于是我立刻断定那是一条抛了锚的船;你尽可以想见,我急于弄个明白,便抄起枪,朝岛的南边、从前被水流卷走的那片礁石跑去;等我爬上那里,这时天已完全放晴,我万分悲痛地清清楚楚看见了一条失事的船,夜里撞毁在那些暗礁上——就是我当年坐船出海时发现的那些暗礁;正是这些礁石挡住了急流的猛势,形成一股回流或漩涡,才让我从这辈子最绝望、最无指望的境地里脱了险。

paragraphs.en: Thus, what is one man’s safety is another man’s destruction; for it seems these men, whoever they were, being out of their knowledge, and the rocks being wholly under water, had been driven upon them in the night, the wind blowing hard at ENE.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,一个人的平安,却是另一个人的毁灭;因为看来这些人,不管他们是谁,由于闯入了他们不熟悉的水域,加上那些礁石又完全没在水下,便在夜里被东北偏东的狂风刮撞了上去。

paragraphs.en: Had they seen the island, as I must necessarily suppose they did not, they must, as I thought, have endeavoured to have saved themselves on shore by the help of their boat; but their firing off guns for help, especially when they saw, as I imagined, my fire, filled me with many thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 倘若他们看见了这座岛——我不得不认定他们没看见——依我想,他们理当会设法借小艇逃到岸上保命;可他们放炮求救,尤其在我猜想他们看见了我的火光之后还放炮,这让我心里生出许多念头。

paragraphs.en: First, I imagined that upon seeing my light they might have put themselves into their boat, and endeavoured to make the shore: but that the sea running very high, they might have been cast away.
paragraphs.cn: 起先,我猜想他们一见我的火光,或许就上了小艇,拼命想划到岸边:可海浪太高,他们说不定翻了船。

paragraphs.en: Other times I imagined that they might have lost their boat before, as might be the case many ways; particularly by the breaking of the sea upon their ship, which many times obliged men to stave, or take in pieces, their boat, and sometimes to throw it overboard with their own hands.
paragraphs.cn: 有时我又猜想,他们说不定早先就把小艇弄丢了,这情形有许多可能;尤其是海浪打在船上,常逼得人不得不把小艇拆散或砸碎,有时甚至亲手把它抛进海里。

paragraphs.en: Other times I imagined they had some other ship or ships in company, who, upon the signals of distress they made, had taken them up, and carried them off.
paragraphs.cn: 还有时我猜想,他们身边或许另有一条或几条同行的船,一见他们发出求救信号,便把他们接了上去、载走了。

paragraphs.en: Other times I fancied they were all gone off to sea in their boat, and being hurried away by the current that I had been formerly in, were carried out into the great ocean, where there was nothing but misery and perishing: and that, perhaps, they might by this time think of starving, and of being in a condition to eat one another.
paragraphs.cn: 又有时我幻想,他们全都坐着小艇出了海,被我当年遭遇过的那股水流一冲,卷进了茫茫大洋,那里除了苦难和灭亡别无他物:说不定这会儿他们正面临饿死,落到要彼此相食的地步。

paragraphs.en: As all these were but conjectures at best, so, in the condition I was in, I could do no more than look on upon the misery of the poor men, and pity them; which had still this good effect upon my side, that it gave me more and more cause to give thanks to God, who had so happily and comfortably provided for me in my desolate condition; and that of two ships’ companies, who were now cast away upon this part of the world, not one life should be spared but mine.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切说到底都只是揣测罢了,所以以我当时的处境,除了旁观这些可怜人的苦难、为他们叹惜之外,我什么也做不了;不过这倒对我起了个好作用,让我越发有理由感谢上帝,是他在我这荒凉的境地里如此幸运、如此安适地眷顾了我;两船的人如今都葬送在世界这一角,却唯独我一人得以保全性命。

paragraphs.en: I learned here again to observe, that it is very rare that the providence of God casts us into any condition so low, or any misery so great, but we may see something or other to be thankful for, and may see others in worse circumstances than our own.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里再一次学会体察到:上帝的安排极少把我们抛入那么低的境地、或那么深的苦难,以致我们竟找不到一点值得感恩的东西,也见不到别人处境比我们更糟。

paragraphs.en: Such certainly was the case of these men, of whom I could not so much as see room to suppose any were saved; nothing could make it rational so much as to wish or expect that they did not all perish there, except the possibility only of their being taken up by another ship in company; and this was but mere possibility indeed, for I saw not the least sign or appearance of any such thing.
paragraphs.cn: 这些人无疑正是如此,我甚至看不出有一丝可能猜想有谁获救;没有什么理由能让人合理地指望或期盼他们不是全数葬身此地,除非仅仅存在他们被同行的另一条船救起的那点可能;可这也不过是纯粹的可能罢了,因为我丝毫看不出有半点这样的迹象或影子。

paragraphs.en: I cannot explain, by any possible energy of words, what a strange longing I felt in my soul upon this sight, breaking out sometimes thus: “Oh that there had been but one or two, nay, or but one soul saved out of this ship, to have escaped to me, that I might but have had one companion, one fellow-creature, to have spoken to me and to have conversed with!”
paragraphs.cn: 我无论用怎样有力的言辞也说不清,眼前这景象在我心底激起了一种何等奇异的渴望,它有时这样迸发出来:“哪怕这船上只救出一两个人,不,哪怕只有一个活人逃到我这儿来,让我有个伴,有个同类能跟我说说话、聊聊天,那该多好啊!”

paragraphs.en: In all the time of my solitary life I never felt so earnest, so strong a desire after the society of my fellow-creatures, or so deep a regret at the want of it.
paragraphs.cn: 在我独居的整段岁月里,我从没像这样热切、这样强烈地渴望有同类做伴,也从没为得不到这样的伴而这般痛惜。

paragraphs.en: There are some secret springs in the affections which, when they are set a-going by some object in view, or, though not in view, yet rendered present to the mind by the power of imagination, that motion carries out the soul, by its impetuosity, to such violent, eager embracings of the object, that the absence of it is insupportable.
paragraphs.cn: 人的情感里藏着某些隐秘的机括,一旦被眼前某个对象触动,或者那对象虽不在眼前、却凭想象之力浮现在心头,那股波动便以其汹涌之势把整个心灵推向对那对象如此强烈、如此急切的拥抱,以致它的不在竟叫人无法忍受。

paragraphs.en: Such were these earnest wishings that but one man had been saved.
paragraphs.cn: 我那份但愿有一个人获救的热切心愿,正是如此。

paragraphs.en: I believe I repeated the words, “Oh that it had been but one!” a thousand times; and my desires were so moved by it, that when I spoke the words my hands would clinch together, and my fingers would press the palms of my hands, so that if I had had any soft thing in my hand I should have crushed it involuntarily; and the teeth in my head would strike together, and set against one another so strong, that for some time I could not part them again.
paragraphs.cn: 我相信我把那句“哪怕只救出一个也好啊!”重复了不下一千遍;这心愿把我搅动得如此厉害,以致我说这话时双手会攥紧,手指会死死压进掌心,要是手里握着什么软东西,我准会不由自主地把它捏碎;我口中的牙齿也会上下相击、咬得那么紧,以致好一阵子都松不开来。

paragraphs.en: Let the naturalists explain these things, and the reason and manner of them.
paragraphs.cn: 这些现象、以及它们产生的缘由和方式,就留给博物学家去解释吧。

paragraphs.en: All I can do is to describe the fact, which was even surprising to me when I found it, though I knew not from whence it proceeded; it was doubtless the effect of ardent wishes, and of strong ideas formed in my mind, realising the comfort which the conversation of one of my fellow-Christians would have been to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我所能做的,只是把这一事实描述出来;当我察觉到它时,连自己都感到惊讶,尽管我不知它究竟从何而来;这无疑是那炽热的心愿、以及我心中所形成的强烈念头所生的效果,我把一位基督徒同胞的交谈会带给我怎样的慰藉活生生地想了出来。

paragraphs.en: But it was not to be; either their fate or mine, or both, forbade it; for, till the last year of my being on this island, I never knew whether any were saved out of that ship or no; and had only the affliction, some days after, to see the corpse of a drowned boy come on shore at the end of the island which was next the shipwreck.
paragraphs.cn: 可这终究没能实现;或是他们的命,或是我的命,或是两者一同,把这事挡住了;因为直到我在这岛上的最后一年,我都不知道那条船上究竟有没有人获救;我只是在几天后受了一场悲痛——看见一个溺死男孩的尸体,被冲上了岛上离那沉船最近的那一头。

paragraphs.en: He had no clothes on but a seaman’s waistcoat, a pair of open-kneed linen drawers, and a blue linen shirt; but nothing to direct me so much as to guess what nation he was of.
paragraphs.cn: 他身上没穿别的衣物,只有一件水手背心、一条膝口敞开的亚麻短裤,还有一件蓝色亚麻衬衫;可没有一样东西能让我哪怕是猜出他是哪国人。

paragraphs.en: He had nothing in his pockets but two pieces of eight and a tobacco pipe—the last was to me of ten times more value than the first.
paragraphs.cn: 他口袋里除了两枚八字银币和一根烟斗外,别无他物——那烟斗对我来说,可比那银币宝贵十倍。

paragraphs.en: It was now calm, and I had a great mind to venture out in my boat to this wreck, not doubting but I might find something on board that might be useful to me.
paragraphs.cn: 这时海面已经平静,我很想冒险划着小艇到这条失事船上去,料想船上准能找到些对我有用的东西。

paragraphs.en: But that did not altogether press me so much as the possibility that there might be yet some living creature on board, whose life I might not only save, but might, by saving that life, comfort my own to the last degree; and this thought clung so to my heart that I could not be quiet night or day, but I must venture out in my boat on board this wreck; and committing the rest to God’s providence, I thought the impression was so strong upon my mind that it could not be resisted—that it must come from some invisible direction, and that I should be wanting to myself if I did not go.
paragraphs.cn: 可真正催逼着我的,倒还不完全是这个,而是船上或许还有活物的那种可能;我不但也许能救它一命,而且救了那条命,还能给我自己带来莫大的慰藉;这念头牢牢揪住我的心,弄得我日夜不得安宁,非划着小艇冒险到这条沉船上去不可;我把其余的事都交托给上帝的安排,只觉得这印象在我心头强烈得无从抗拒——它准是出自某种看不见的指引,我若不去,便是辜负了自己。

paragraphs.en: Under the power of this impression, I hastened back to my castle, prepared everything for my voyage, took a quantity of bread, a great pot of fresh water, a compass to steer by, a bottle of rum (for I had still a great deal of that left), and a basket of raisins; and thus, loading myself with everything necessary.
paragraphs.cn: 在这印象的驱使下,我赶忙回到城堡,把出海的一切都备齐:带上一批面包、一大罐淡水、一只掌舵用的罗盘、一瓶朗姆酒(那玩意儿我还剩下不少),还有一篮葡萄干;就这样,把一切必需之物都装到身上。

paragraphs.en: I went down to my boat, got the water out of her, got her afloat, loaded all my cargo in her, and then went home again for more.
paragraphs.cn: 我下到小艇那儿,把里头的积水舀出来,让它浮起,把我所有的货物都装了进去,然后又回家去取更多的东西。

paragraphs.en: My second cargo was a great bag of rice, the umbrella to set up over my head for a shade, another large pot of water, and about two dozen of small loaves, or barley cakes, more than before, with a bottle of goat’s milk and a cheese; all which with great labour and sweat I carried to my boat; and praying to God to direct my voyage, I put out, and rowing or paddling the canoe along the shore, came at last to the utmost point of the island on the north-east side.
paragraphs.cn: 我第二趟运的是一大袋米、一把用来撑在头顶遮阳的伞、另一大罐水,还有比先前多出约莫两打的小面包或大麦饼,外加一瓶羊奶和一块奶酪;这些东西我费了好大力气、出了一身汗才搬到小艇上;我一面祈求上帝指引我的航程,一面出发,沿着海岸划桨(或者说荡桨),终于来到了岛东北端最尽头的那个岬角。

paragraphs.en: And now I was to launch out into the ocean, and either to venture or not to venture.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我该驶进大海了,是冒险还是不冒险,得拿个主意。

paragraphs.en: I looked on the rapid currents which ran constantly on both sides of the island at a distance, and which were very terrible to me from the remembrance of the hazard I had been in before, and my heart began to fail me; for I foresaw that if I was driven into either of those currents, I should be carried a great way out to sea, and perhaps out of my reach or sight of the island again; and that then, as my boat was but small, if any little gale of wind should rise, I should be inevitably lost.
paragraphs.cn: 我望着那两股湍急的水流,它们不停地在岛的两侧远处奔流,一想起从前身陷其中的凶险,就让我胆战心惊,我的心开始怯了下来;因为我料到,万一被卷进其中一股水流,就会被冲到离岸很远的海上,说不定再也够不着、也望不见这座岛了;到那时,我这小艇又这么小,一旦刮起哪怕一丁点风,我准得没命。

paragraphs.en: These thoughts so oppressed my mind that I began to give over my enterprise; and having hauled my boat into a little creek on the shore, I stepped out, and sat down upon a rising bit of ground, very pensive and anxious, between fear and desire, about my voyage; when, as I was musing, I could perceive that the tide was turned, and the flood come on; upon which my going was impracticable for so many hours.
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头把我的心压得那么沉,我都打算放弃这趟冒险了;我把小艇拖进岸边一条小河汊里,踏上岸,坐在一块隆起的高地上,愁思满怀、忐忑不安,对这趟航行既怕又想;正当我沉吟之际,却察觉潮头已经转了向、涨潮上来了;这么一来,好几个钟头内我都没法动身。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, presently it occurred to me that I should go up to the highest piece of ground I could find, and observe, if I could, how the sets of the tide or currents lay when the flood came in, that I might judge whether, if I was driven one way out, I might not expect to be driven another way home, with the same rapidity of the currents.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我随即想到,我该爬上能找到的最高一块地方,尽量观察一下涨潮时潮流或水流的走向,好判断一下:万一我被冲向一头出海,能不能指望以同样湍急的水流被冲向另一头回家。

paragraphs.en: This thought was no sooner in my head than I cast my eye upon a little hill which sufficiently overlooked the sea both ways, and from whence I had a clear view of the currents or sets of the tide, and which way I was to guide myself in my return.
paragraphs.cn: 这念头刚一冒进脑子,我就一眼瞥见一座小山丘,从那儿两边海面都尽收眼底,水流或潮流的走向、以及我回程该往哪儿把握航向,都看得清清楚楚。

paragraphs.en: Here I found, that as the current of ebb set out close by the south point of the island, so the current of the flood set in close by the shore of the north side; and that I had nothing to do but to keep to the north side of the island in my return, and I should do well enough.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这儿看出:退潮的水流紧贴着岛的南端往外流,而涨潮的水流则紧贴着北岸涌进来;因此我回程时只消一直靠着岛的北侧走,就万无一失了。

paragraphs.en: Encouraged by this observation, I resolved the next morning to set out with the first of the tide; and reposing myself for the night in my canoe, under the watch-coat I mentioned, I launched out.
paragraphs.cn: 这一观察让我大受鼓舞,我便决定第二天一早趁头一拨潮水出发;当夜我裹着前面提过的那件值更大衣,在独木舟里歇了一宿,便出海了。

paragraphs.en: I first made a little out to sea, full north, till I began to feel the benefit of the current, which set eastward, and which carried me at a great rate; and yet did not so hurry me as the current on the south side had done before, so as to take from me all government of the boat; but having a strong steerage with my paddle, I went at a great rate directly for the wreck, and in less than two hours I came up to it.
paragraphs.cn: 我先朝正北方向往海里划出去一小段,直到开始感到那股向东流的水流之助,它以极快的速度把我带走;可它却不像先前南侧那股水流那样把我冲得七荤八素、连船都掌控不住;我用桨牢牢地把着舵,飞快地径直朝那沉船驶去,不到两个钟头就赶到了跟前。

paragraphs.en: It was a dismal sight to look at; the ship, which by its building was Spanish, stuck fast, jammed in between two rocks.
paragraphs.cn: 那船看上去凄惨极了;从造法看,是条西班牙船,牢牢卡死在两块礁石之间。

paragraphs.en: All the stern and quarter of her were beaten to pieces by the sea; and as her forecastle, which stuck in the rocks, had run on with great violence, her mainmast and foremast were brought by the board—that is to say, broken short off; but her bowsprit was sound, and the head and bow appeared firm.
paragraphs.cn: 整个船尾和后半舷都被海浪打得粉碎;由于卡在礁石里的船头前部曾被猛烈地冲撞过,它的主桅和前桅都齐根折断、掀落到船外去了;不过它的船首斜桅还完好,船头和船艏看上去也很结实。

paragraphs.en: When I came close to her, a dog appeared upon her, who, seeing me coming, yelped and cried; and as soon as I called him, jumped into the sea to come to me.
paragraphs.cn: 我划近它时,船上出现了一条狗,它见我过来,便汪汪地哀叫;我一唤它,它就跳进海里向我游来。

paragraphs.en: I took him into the boat, but found him almost dead with hunger and thirst.
paragraphs.cn: 我把它拉进小艇,却发现它已被饥渴折磨得奄奄一息。

paragraphs.en: I gave him a cake of my bread, and he devoured it like a ravenous wolf that had been starving a fortnight in the snow; I then gave the poor creature some fresh water, with which, if I would have let him, he would have burst himself.
paragraphs.cn: 我给了它一块我的面包,它像一头在雪地里饿了半个月的恶狼似的狼吞虎咽;接着我又给这可怜的家伙喝了些淡水,要是我由着它,它准会把自己撑破。

paragraphs.en: After this I went on board; but the first sight I met with was two men drowned in the cook-room, or forecastle of the ship, with their arms fast about one another.
paragraphs.cn: 这之后我上了船;可我头一眼看到的,却是两个淹死在厨舱、也就是船头前舱里的人,他们的胳膊紧紧地抱着彼此。

paragraphs.en: I concluded, as is indeed probable, that when the ship struck, it being in a storm, the sea broke so high and so continually over her, that the men were not able to bear it, and were strangled with the constant rushing in of the water, as much as if they had been under water.
paragraphs.cn: 我断定——这其实也很可能——当这船在风暴中触礁时,海浪打得那么高、那么不停地漫过船身,那些人抵挡不住,被不断灌进来的海水呛得窒息而死,就跟他们淹在水底下没什么两样。

paragraphs.en: Besides the dog, there was nothing left in the ship that had life; nor any goods, that I could see, but what were spoiled by the water.
paragraphs.cn: 除了那条狗,船上再没剩下任何活物;至于货物,凡我能看见的,没有一样不是被水泡坏了的。

paragraphs.en: There were some casks of liquor, whether wine or brandy I knew not, which lay lower in the hold, and which, the water being ebbed out, I could see; but they were too big to meddle with.
paragraphs.cn: 舱底下方躺着几桶酒,是葡萄酒还是白兰地我不清楚,因为水已经退了出去,我才看得见它们;可它们太大,弄不动。

paragraphs.en: I saw several chests, which I believe belonged to some of the seamen; and I got two of them into the boat, without examining what was in them.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见几只箱子,想必是某些水手的;我把其中两只弄进了小艇,也没细看里头装的是什么。

paragraphs.en: Had the stern of the ship been fixed, and the forepart broken off, I am persuaded I might have made a good voyage; for by what I found in those two chests I had room to suppose the ship had a great deal of wealth on board; and, if I may guess from the course she steered, she must have been bound from Buenos Ayres, or the Rio de la Plata, in the south part of America, beyond the Brazils to the Havannah, in the Gulf of Mexico, and so perhaps to Spain.
paragraphs.cn: 倘若这船的船尾还牢固、只是前半截碎了,我敢说这一趟准能满载而归;因为凭我在那两只箱子里所发现的东西,我有理由推想船上载着大批财富;而且,若容我从它所行的航向来猜,它准是从南美洲、巴西以远的布宜诺斯艾利斯或拉普拉塔河出发,开往墨西哥湾里的哈瓦那,或许再驶往西班牙的。

paragraphs.en: She had, no doubt, a great treasure in her, but of no use, at that time, to anybody; and what became of the crew I then knew not.
paragraphs.cn: 船上无疑载着一大笔财宝,可那时对谁都毫无用处;至于船员的下落,我当时也不得而知。

paragraphs.en: I found, besides these chests, a little cask full of liquor, of about twenty gallons, which I got into my boat with much difficulty.
paragraphs.cn: 除了这些箱子,我还发现一只装满酒的小桶,约莫二十加仑,我费了好大劲才把它弄进小艇。

paragraphs.en: There were several muskets in the cabin, and a great powder-horn, with about four pounds of powder in it; as for the muskets, I had no occasion for them, so I left them, but took the powder-horn.
paragraphs.cn: 舱室里有好几支火枪,还有一只大火药筒,里头约莫装着四磅火药;那些火枪我用不着,便留下没拿,可那火药筒我却带走了。

paragraphs.en: I took a fire-shovel and tongs, which I wanted extremely, as also two little brass kettles, a copper pot to make chocolate, and a gridiron; and with this cargo, and the dog, I came away, the tide beginning to make home again—and the same evening, about an hour within night, I reached the island again, weary and fatigued to the last degree.
paragraphs.cn: 我拿了一把火铲和一副火钳,这两样我极想要;还有两只小铜壶、一口煮巧克力用的紫铜锅,以及一个烤架;带着这批货物和那条狗,我便动身返回,这时潮水已开始往回涨——当晚,天黑约莫一个钟头后,我又回到了岛上,累得筋疲力尽到了极点。

paragraphs.en: I reposed that night in the boat and in the morning I resolved to harbour what I had got in my new cave, and not carry it home to my castle.
paragraphs.cn: 那一夜我在小艇里歇了一宿,第二天早上我拿定主意,把弄到的东西都藏进我那新洞里,而不搬回城堡去。

paragraphs.en: After refreshing myself, I got all my cargo on shore, and began to examine the particulars.
paragraphs.cn: 歇过之后,我把所有的货物都搬上了岸,开始一件件查看。

paragraphs.en: The cask of liquor I found to be a kind of rum, but not such as we had at the Brazils; and, in a word, not at all good; but when I came to open the chests, I found several things of great use to me—for example, I found in one a fine case of bottles, of an extraordinary kind, and filled with cordial waters, fine and very good; the bottles held about three pints each, and were tipped with silver.
paragraphs.cn: 那桶酒我发现是一种朗姆酒,可跟我们在巴西喝的不一样;一句话,一点也不好;可等我打开那几只箱子,却发现了好几样对我大有用处的东西——比方说,我在一只箱子里找到一个精致的瓶匣,样式非同寻常,里头装满了甘露酒,又香又好;每只瓶子约莫能装三品脱,瓶口都镶着银。

paragraphs.en: I found two pots of very good succades, or sweetmeats, so fastened also on the top that the salt-water had not hurt them; and two more of the same, which the water had spoiled.
paragraphs.cn: 我又找到两罐极好的蜜饯或果脯,罐口封得严实,咸水都没能坏了它们;另外两罐同样的,却被水泡坏了。

paragraphs.en: I found some very good shirts, which were very welcome to me; and about a dozen and a half of white linen handkerchiefs and coloured neckcloths; the former were also very welcome, being exceedingly refreshing to wipe my face in a hot day.
paragraphs.cn: 我找到几件很好的衬衫,这对我可太合心意了;还有约莫一打半的白亚麻手帕和几条彩色围巾;那些手帕也很中我的意,大热天用来擦脸,别提多爽快了。

paragraphs.en: Besides this, when I came to the till in the chest, I found there three great bags of pieces of eight, which held about eleven hundred pieces in all; and in one of them, wrapped up in a paper, six doubloons of gold, and some small bars or wedges of gold; I suppose they might all weigh near a pound.
paragraphs.cn: 除此之外,我在箱子里的小抽屉里找到三大袋八字银币,总共约莫一千一百枚;其中一袋里,有六枚金达布隆用纸包着,还有几小条或几小锭金子;我估摸它们加起来大概有近一磅重。

paragraphs.en: In the other chest were some clothes, but of little value; but, by the circumstances, it must have belonged to the gunner’s mate; though there was no powder in it, except two pounds of fine glazed powder, in three flasks, kept, I suppose, for charging their fowling-pieces on occasion.
paragraphs.cn: 另一只箱子里装着些衣物,可不值几个钱;不过照种种情形看,它准是属于炮手副手的;箱里没有火药,只有三只小火药瓶里装着两磅上等的光面火药,想必是留着遇上机会给他们的鸟枪装药用的。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, I got very little by this voyage that was of any use to me; for, as to the money, I had no manner of occasion for it; it was to me as the dirt under my feet, and I would have given it all for three or four pair of English shoes and stockings, which were things I greatly wanted, but had had none on my feet for many years.
paragraphs.cn: 总的说来,这一趟我得到的、真正对我有用的东西少得可怜;因为那些钱嘛,我压根用不着;在我眼里,它就跟脚下的泥土一样,我情愿拿它全部去换三四双英国鞋袜,那可是我极想要的东西,这么多年来我脚上一直没得穿。

paragraphs.en: I had, indeed, got two pair of shoes now, which I took off the feet of two drowned men whom I saw in the wreck, and I found two pair more in one of the chests, which were very welcome to me; but they were not like our English shoes, either for ease or service, being rather what we call pumps than shoes.
paragraphs.cn: 说实在的,如今我倒是弄到了两双鞋,是从我在沉船里看见的两个溺死者脚上扒下来的,另外我又在一只箱子里找到两双,这可太合我心意了;只是它们不像我们英国鞋那样,无论穿着舒不舒服还是耐不耐用都比不上,倒更像我们所说的浅口便鞋,算不上正经鞋子。

paragraphs.en: I found in this seaman’s chest about fifty pieces of eight, in rials, but no gold: I supposed this belonged to a poorer man than the other, which seemed to belong to some officer.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这只水手的箱子里找到约莫五十枚里亚尔的八字银币,却没有金子:我猜这箱子的主人比另一个穷些,那另一只箱子看来是属于某位军官的。

paragraphs.en: Well, however, I lugged this money home to my cave, and laid it up, as I had done that before which I had brought from our own ship; but it was a great pity, as I said, that the other part of this ship had not come to my share; for I am satisfied I might have loaded my canoe several times over with money; and, thought I, if I ever escape to England, it might lie here safe enough till I come again and fetch it.
paragraphs.cn: 不管怎样,我还是把这笔钱吃力地拖回我的洞里收好,就像先前收藏我从自己那条船上带回来的钱一样;可正如我说过的,真是天大的可惜,这条船的另外那半截没有落到我手里;因为我确信,那些钱够我把独木舟装满好几趟;我心想,我若有朝一日能逃回英国,这钱在这儿尽可以安然搁着,等我哪天回来再取。

paragraphs.en: Having now brought all my things on shore and secured them, I went back to my boat, and rowed or paddled her along the shore to her old harbour, where I laid her up, and made the best of my way to my old habitation, where I found everything safe and quiet.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我把所有东西都搬上了岸,妥善收好,便回到小船那儿,划着或撑着它沿岸驶回它原来的港湾停泊,然后尽快赶回我的老住处,发现那里一切安然无恙。

paragraphs.en: I began now to repose myself, live after my old fashion, and take care of my family affairs; and for a while I lived easy enough, only that I was more vigilant than I used to be, looked out oftener, and did not go abroad so much; and if at any time I did stir with any freedom, it was always to the east part of the island, where I was pretty well satisfied the savages never came, and where I could go without so many precautions, and such a load of arms and ammunition as I always carried with me if I went the other way.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我开始休养生息,恢复往日的生活方式,料理起自己的家务;有一阵子我过得相当安逸,只是比从前更加警觉,更常出去了望,也不敢常出远门;偶尔想稍稍自由地走动一下,也总是往岛的东边去,因为我十分确信野人从不到那边来,去那儿不必带那么多防备,也不必像去另一边时那样背上一大堆武器弹药。

paragraphs.en: I lived in this condition near two years more; but my unlucky head, that was always to let me know it was born to make my body miserable, was all these two years filled with projects and designs how, if it were possible, I might get away from this island: for sometimes I was for making another voyage to the wreck, though my reason told me that there was nothing left there worth the hazard of my voyage; sometimes for a ramble one way, sometimes another—and I believe verily, if I had had the boat that I went from Sallee in, I should have ventured to sea, bound anywhere, I knew not whither.
paragraphs.cn: 我又这样过了将近两年;可我那颗倒霉的脑袋,似乎生来就要让我的身体受苦,这两年里满脑子都是种种计划和盘算,想着若有可能,该如何逃离这座岛:有时我想再去那残破的船上跑一趟,尽管理智告诉我那儿已没有什么值得我冒险去取的东西了;有时又想往这边漫游,有时想往那边——我确实相信,倘若我手里有当年从萨累逃出来时坐的那条船,我准会冒险出海,不管驶向何方,连自己也不知去往哪里。

paragraphs.en: I have been, in all my circumstances, a memento to those who are touched with the general plague of mankind, whence, for aught I know, one half of their miseries flow: I mean that of not being satisfied with the station wherein God and Nature hath placed them—for, not to look back upon my primitive condition, and the excellent advice of my father, the opposition to which was, as I may call it, my _original sin_, my subsequent mistakes of the same kind had been the means of my coming into this miserable condition; for had that Providence which so happily seated me at the Brazils as a planter blessed me with confined desires, and I could have been contented to have gone on gradually, I might have been by this time—I mean in the time of my being in this island—one of the most considerable planters in the Brazils—nay, I am persuaded, that by the improvements I had made in that little time I lived there, and the increase I should probably have made if I had remained, I might have been worth a hundred thousand moidores—and what business had I to leave a settled fortune, a well-stocked plantation, improving and increasing, to turn supercargo to Guinea to fetch negroes, when patience and time would have so increased our stock at home, that we could have bought them at our own door from those whose business it was to fetch them? and though it had cost us something more, yet the difference of that price was by no means worth saving at so great a hazard.
paragraphs.cn: 就我的种种遭遇而言,我可算是一个警示,警示那些染上了人类通病的人——据我所知,他们的苦难有一半正是由此而来:我指的是不满足于上帝和造物主给他们安排的境遇;因为——且不去回顾我最初的处境和父亲那番极好的劝告(我违逆他的劝告,可以说就是我的原罪)——我后来同类的种种错误,正是把我一步步带进这悲惨境地的祸根;因为倘若那位天意把我幸运地安置在巴西当种植园主时,也赐我以知足的心愿,我能满足于循序渐进地经营下去,那么到如今——我是说到我困在这岛上的这段时候——我或许已成了巴西数一数二的大种植园主了;不,我甚至深信,凭我在那儿短短几年所做的经营,再加上若继续留下去大概还能增添的产业,我说不定已值十万金币了——我究竟为什么要抛下一份稳稳的家业、一座蒸蒸日上不断扩大的富庶种植园,跑去当押货员到几内亚去贩黑奴呢?其实只要有耐心、假以时日,我们家里的资本增长起来,完全可以就在自家门口向那些专做这行的人买到黑奴啊?就算那样多花些钱,可为省下这点差价去冒如此大的风险,实在太不值得了。

paragraphs.en: But as this is usually the fate of young heads, so reflection upon the folly of it is as commonly the exercise of more years, or of the dear-bought experience of time—so it was with me now; and yet so deep had the mistake taken root in my temper, that I could not satisfy myself in my station, but was continually poring upon the means and possibility of my escape from this place; and that I may, with greater pleasure to the reader, bring on the remaining part of my story, it may not be improper to give some account of my first conceptions on the subject of this foolish scheme for my escape, and how, and upon what foundation, I acted.
paragraphs.cn: 但这通常是年轻头脑的命运,而对这份愚蠢的反省,也照例要等到年岁渐长、或用时间换来沉痛教训之后才会有——我如今正是如此;然而这错误在我性情里扎根太深,以致我在自己的处境中总不得安宁,反而没完没了地盘算逃离此地的种种法子和可能;为了让读者读得更有兴味,我不妨先把故事余下的部分讲下去,或许先交代一下我最初对这套逃跑的蠢念头是怎么想的、又是凭着什么、如何着手去做的,倒也不算多余。

paragraphs.en: I am now to be supposed retired into my castle, after my late voyage to the wreck, my frigate laid up and secured under water, as usual, and my condition restored to what it was before: I had more wealth, indeed, than I had before, but was not at all the richer; for I had no more use for it than the Indians of Peru had before the Spaniards came there.
paragraphs.cn: 现在请设想我在那次去残船之后已退回城堡里,我那条小船照旧收在水下藏好,处境又恢复到从前的样子:说起来我如今的财富确实比先前多了,可我并没有因此富裕分毫;因为这些东西于我毫无用处,就像西班牙人到来之前秘鲁的印第安人守着金银一样。

paragraphs.en: It was one of the nights in the rainy season in March, the four-and-twentieth year of my first setting foot in this island of solitude, I was lying in my bed or hammock, awake, very well in health, had no pain, no distemper, no uneasiness of body, nor any uneasiness of mind more than ordinary, but could by no means close my eyes, that is, so as to sleep; no, not a wink all night long, otherwise than as follows:
paragraphs.cn: 那是三月雨季里的一个夜晚,是我头一回踏上这座孤岛后的第二十四个年头,我躺在床上,也就是吊床上,醒着,身体十分健康,没有病痛,没有不适,身上一点不难受,心里也并不比平常更烦乱,却怎么也合不上眼,也就是睡不着;不,整整一夜连一眨眼都没睡,事情是这样的:

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to set down the innumerable crowd of thoughts that whirled through that great thoroughfare of the brain, the memory, in this night’s time.
paragraphs.cn: 要写下这一夜里在头脑那条大通道——记忆里翻腾而过的无数纷乱念头,是根本不可能的。

paragraphs.en: I ran over the whole history of my life in miniature, or by abridgment, as I may call it, to my coming to this island, and also of that part of my life since I came to this island.
paragraphs.cn: 我把自己一生的经历,浓缩地、或者说撮要地,从头到尾在心里过了一遍,直到我来到这座岛上,还有来到岛上之后的那段生活。

paragraphs.en: In my reflections upon the state of my case since I came on shore on this island, I was comparing the happy posture of my affairs in the first years of my habitation here, with the life of anxiety, fear, and care which I had lived in ever since I had seen the print of a foot in the sand.
paragraphs.cn: 在回想自己登上此岛以来的种种境况时,我拿最初住在这里那几年安逸的光景,同自打在沙滩上看到一个脚印以来所过的那种提心吊胆、担惊受怕、忧心忡忡的日子相比。

paragraphs.en: Not that I did not believe the savages had frequented the island even all the while, and might have been several hundreds of them at times on shore there; but I had never known it, and was incapable of any apprehensions about it; my satisfaction was perfect, though my danger was the same, and I was as happy in not knowing my danger as if I had never really been exposed to it.
paragraphs.cn: 倒不是说我不相信那些野人一直常来这岛,而且有时岸上或许一次就有好几百人;只是我从来都不知道,也就无从惊慌;我心里满是知足,尽管危险照旧存在;我因为不知道危险而过得快活,就好像我当真从未身处险境一样。

paragraphs.en: This furnished my thoughts with many very profitable reflections, and particularly this one: How infinitely good that Providence is, which has provided, in its government of mankind, such narrow bounds to his sight and knowledge of things; and though he walks in the midst of so many thousand dangers, the sight of which, if discovered to him, would distract his mind and sink his spirits, he is kept serene and calm, by having the events of things hid from his eyes, and knowing nothing of the dangers which surround him.
paragraphs.cn: 这一想,给了我许多很有益处的感悟,尤其是这一条:天意何等仁慈无比,它在管辖人类时,竟给人的眼界和对事物的认知定下了如此狭窄的界限;人明明行走在成千上万的危险之中,若把这些危险都摆到他眼前,足以搅乱他的心神、消沉他的意志,然而由于事情的结局对他隐而不露、他对周遭的危险一无所知,他反倒得以安然平静。
