paragraphs.en: After these thoughts had for some time entertained me, I came to reflect seriously upon the real danger I had been in for so many years in this very island, and how I had walked about in the greatest security, and with all possible tranquillity, even when perhaps nothing but the brow of a hill, a great tree, or the casual approach of night, had been between me and the worst kind of destruction—viz. that of falling into the hands of cannibals and savages, who would have seized on me with the same view as I would on a goat or turtle; and have thought it no more crime to kill and devour me than I did of a pigeon or a curlew.
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头萦绕了我一阵之后,我便认真反省起自己这么多年在这岛上所处的真实险境,想到我竟一直那样安然自得、无比坦然地四处走动,而其实往往只隔着一道山冈的坡脊、一棵大树,或是黑夜偶然降临,才使我免于最可怕的毁灭——也就是落入那些吃人的野人手里,他们会像我抓一只山羊或海龟那样抓住我,而且觉得杀我、吃我,并不比我杀一只鸽子或麻鹬算更大的罪过。

paragraphs.en: I would unjustly slander myself if I should say I was not sincerely thankful to my great Preserver, to whose singular protection I acknowledged, with great humanity, all these unknown deliverances were due, and without which I must inevitably have fallen into their merciless hands.
paragraphs.cn: 如果我说自己对那位伟大的救主没有由衷的感激,那便是冤枉了我自己;我怀着极深的敬意承认,所有这些不为我所知的解救,都归功于他那奇异的护佑,若没有他,我必定早已落入那些人残忍的魔掌。

paragraphs.en: When these thoughts were over, my head was for some time taken up in considering the nature of these wretched creatures, I mean the savages, and how it came to pass in the world that the wise Governor of all things should give up any of His creatures to such inhumanity—nay, to something so much below even brutality itself—as to devour its own kind: but as this ended in some (at that time) fruitless speculations, it occurred to me to inquire what part of the world these wretches lived in? how far off the coast was from whence they came? what they ventured over so far from home for? what kind of boats they had? and why I might not order myself and my business so that I might be able to go over thither, as they were to come to me?
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头过后,我脑子里有一阵子只盘算着这些可怜生物——我是说那些野人——的本性,想着世上怎么会有这样的事:那位掌管万物的智慧主宰,竟会任凭他所造的一部分生灵如此没有人性——不,竟堕落到连禽兽都不如的地步——去吞食自己的同类;可这番思索(在当时)终归毫无结果,我便转而琢磨起别的问题:这些恶徒究竟住在世上哪一带?他们来时,那海岸离这儿有多远?他们从那么远的家跑来,图的是什么?他们乘的是什么样的船?我又为什么不能安排好自己和我的事,像他们能过到我这儿来一样,过到他们那边去呢?

paragraphs.en: I never so much as troubled myself to consider what I should do with myself when I went thither; what would become of me if I fell into the hands of these savages; or how I should escape them if they attacked me; no, nor so much as how it was possible for me to reach the coast, and not to be attacked by some or other of them, without any possibility of delivering myself; and if I should not fall into their hands, what I should do for provision, or whither I should bend my course; none of these thoughts, I say, so much as came in my way; but my mind was wholly bent upon the notion of my passing over in my boat to the mainland.
paragraphs.cn: 我压根没费心去想:等我到了那边,该拿自己怎么办;万一落到这些野人手里,我会有什么下场;若他们攻击我,我又该如何脱身;不,我甚至没想过:我怎么可能到得了那海岸,而不被这个那个野人袭击,弄得毫无自救之望;就算没落进他们手里,我又靠什么果腹,该朝哪个方向走;我说,这些念头一个都没在我心头掠过;我满心满脑只想着一件事——乘我的小船渡海到大陆去。

paragraphs.en: I looked upon my present condition as the most miserable that could possibly be; that I was not able to throw myself into anything but death, that could be called worse; and if I reached the shore of the main I might perhaps meet with relief, or I might coast along, as I did on the African shore, till I came to some inhabited country, and where I might find some relief; and after all, perhaps I might fall in with some Christian ship that might take me in: and if the worst came to the worst, I could but die, which would put an end to all these miseries at once.
paragraphs.cn: 我把眼下的处境看作天底下最悲惨的境地;除了死亡,我再也跌不进比这更糟的什么了;而若能到达大陆的岸边,我或许能得到接济,或者能像当年在非洲海岸那样沿岸而行,直到来到某个有人烟的国度,在那里找到些许接济;再退一步说,我说不定还能碰上一艘肯收留我的基督徒的船;哪怕最坏也不过一死,而这一死会把这一切苦难一下子全都了结。

paragraphs.en: Pray note, all this was the fruit of a disturbed mind, an impatient temper, made desperate, as it were, by the long continuance of my troubles, and the disappointments I had met in the wreck I had been on board of, and where I had been so near obtaining what I so earnestly longed for—somebody to speak to, and to learn some knowledge from them of the place where I was, and of the probable means of my deliverance.
paragraphs.cn: 请注意,这一切都是一颗躁动的心、一副急不可耐的性子结出的果实,是长期的困顿、以及那次登上残船所遭的失望把我逼到了绝望的地步——就在那船上,我曾那样接近于得到我朝思暮想的东西:一个能与我说话、能让我从他口中打听到我身在何处、又有何脱身之望的人。

paragraphs.en: I was agitated wholly by these thoughts; all my calm of mind, in my resignation to Providence, and waiting the issue of the dispositions of Heaven, seemed to be suspended; and I had as it were no power to turn my thoughts to anything but to the project of a voyage to the main, which came upon me with such force, and such an impetuosity of desire, that it was not to be resisted.
paragraphs.cn: 我完全被这些念头搅得心神不宁;从前我顺服天意、静候上天安排结局所得来的那份心境的宁静,此刻仿佛全都停摆了;我几乎无力把心思转向别的任何事,只想着渡海去大陆这一桩;这念头来势如此之猛,渴望如此之烈,叫人无从抗拒。

paragraphs.en: When this had agitated my thoughts for two hours or more, with such violence that it set my very blood into a ferment, and my pulse beat as if I had been in a fever, merely with the extraordinary fervour of my mind about it, Nature—as if I had been fatigued and exhausted with the very thoughts of it—threw me into a sound sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 这念头把我的思绪搅动了两个多钟头,来势凶猛,竟使我热血翻腾,脉搏跳得像发了高烧一般,而这全然是因为我心里为此激动异常;这时,大自然——仿佛我光是想这件事就已疲惫不堪、精疲力竭似的——把我推入了一场酣睡。

paragraphs.en: One would have thought I should have dreamed of it, but I did not, nor of anything relating to it, but I dreamed that as I was going out in the morning as usual from my castle, I saw upon the shore two canoes and eleven savages coming to land, and that they brought with them another savage whom they were going to kill in order to eat him; when, on a sudden, the savage that they were going to kill jumped away, and ran for his life; and I thought in my sleep that he came running into my little thick grove before my fortification, to hide himself; and that I seeing him alone, and not perceiving that the others sought him that way, showed myself to him, and smiling upon him, encouraged him: that he kneeled down to me, seeming to pray me to assist him; upon which I showed him my ladder, made him go up, and carried him into my cave, and he became my servant; and that as soon as I had got this man, I said to myself, “Now I may certainly venture to the mainland, for this fellow will serve me as a pilot, and will tell me what to do, and whither to go for provisions, and whither not to go for fear of being devoured; what places to venture into, and what to shun.”
paragraphs.cn: 照说我该会梦见这件事,可我并没有,也没梦见任何与它相关的东西,倒是梦见:一天早晨我照例走出城堡,看见岸上有两条独木舟、十一个野人正要上岸,他们还带来了另一个野人,打算杀了吃掉;正在这时,那个要被杀的野人突然跳开,拼命逃命;我在梦里觉得他跑进了我堡垒前那片浓密的小树林里躲藏;我见他孤身一人,又没察觉别人正往那边找他,便现身在他面前,朝他微笑,给他鼓励:他向我跪下,似乎在求我帮他;于是我把梯子指给他看,叫他爬上去,把他带进我的洞里,他就做了我的仆人;我一得到这个人,便自言自语道:“如今我准可以放心渡海去大陆了,因为这家伙可以给我当向导,会告诉我该怎么做、上哪儿去弄食物、哪儿因怕被吃掉而不能去、哪些地方可以冒险闯、哪些地方该避开。”

paragraphs.en: I waked with this thought; and was under such inexpressible impressions of joy at the prospect of my escape in my dream, that the disappointments which I felt upon coming to myself, and finding that it was no more than a dream, were equally extravagant the other way, and threw me into a very great dejection of spirits.
paragraphs.cn: 我带着这念头醒了过来;梦中逃脱有望,我心里涌起说不出的狂喜,以致当我清醒过来、发现那不过是一场梦时,所感到的失望也同样强烈地向反方向袭来,把我抛入了极度的沮丧。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, however, I made this conclusion: that my only way to go about to attempt an escape was, to endeavour to get a savage into my possession: and, if possible, it should be one of their prisoners, whom they had condemned to be eaten, and should bring hither to kill.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,由此我得出了这样一个结论:我要想设法逃脱,唯一的办法就是设法弄到一个野人归我所有;而且若有可能,最好是他们的俘虏之一,那种被他们判定要吃掉、押到这儿来宰杀的人。

paragraphs.en: But these thoughts still were attended with this difficulty: that it was impossible to effect this without attacking a whole caravan of them, and killing them all; and this was not only a very desperate attempt, and might miscarry, but, on the other hand, I had greatly scrupled the lawfulness of it to myself; and my heart trembled at the thoughts of shedding so much blood, though it was for my deliverance.
paragraphs.cn: 可这些念头依旧伴随着一个难题:不攻击他们一整队人、把他们全都杀光,这事就无从办到;而这不仅是一次极其冒险、可能失败的行动,另一方面,我心里也着实对它是否正当大有顾忌;一想到要流这么多血,哪怕是为了自救,我的心也直打颤。

paragraphs.en: I need not repeat the arguments which occurred to me against this, they being the same mentioned before; but though I had other reasons to offer now—viz. that those men were enemies to my life, and would devour me if they could; that it was self-preservation, in the highest degree, to deliver myself from this death of a life, and was acting in my own defence as much as if they were actually assaulting me, and the like; I say though these things argued for it, yet the thoughts of shedding human blood for my deliverance were very terrible to me, and such as I could by no means reconcile myself to for a great while.
paragraphs.cn: 我不必重复那些反对此举、涌上心头的理由,它们和前面提到的一样;不过如今我倒有别的理由可以提出——也就是说:那些人是我性命的仇敌,一有机会就会把我吃掉;把自己从这种活受死的境地里解救出来,是最高程度的自我保全,这跟他们当真在攻击我时我自卫无异,如此等等;我是说,尽管这些道理都支持动手,可为求自救去流人血的念头,于我仍是十分可怕的,叫我好长一段时间怎么也无法说服自己接受。

paragraphs.en: However, at last, after many secret disputes with myself, and after great perplexities about it (for all these arguments, one way and another, struggled in my head a long time), the eager prevailing desire of deliverance at length mastered all the rest; and I resolved, if possible, to get one of these savages into my hands, cost what it would.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,到最后,经过许多回内心的暗自争辩、经过为此的百般困惑(因为这些正反两面的理由在我脑子里争斗了很久),那股急于脱身的强烈渴望终于压倒了其余一切;我下定决心,只要有可能,不惜任何代价也要弄一个这样的野人到手。

paragraphs.en: My next thing was to contrive how to do it, and this, indeed, was very difficult to resolve on; but as I could pitch upon no probable means for it, so I resolved to put myself upon the watch, to see them when they came on shore, and leave the rest to the event; taking such measures as the opportunity should present, let what would be.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来我要盘算怎么去办,这实在很难拿定主意;可我又想不出什么可行的法子,于是便决定亲自守候,等他们上岸时看准了,其余的就听天由命;见机行事,能怎样便怎样。

paragraphs.en: With these resolutions in my thoughts, I set myself upon the scout as often as possible, and indeed so often that I was heartily tired of it; for it was above a year and a half that I waited; and for great part of that time went out to the west end, and to the south-west corner of the island almost every day, to look for canoes, but none appeared.
paragraphs.cn: 心里揣着这些决心,我便尽量常去放哨,而且去得实在太勤,以致我打心底厌烦了;因为我足足等了一年半;其中大半时间几乎天天跑到岛的西端和西南角去张望有没有独木舟,可一条也没出现。

paragraphs.en: This was very discouraging, and began to trouble me much, though I cannot say that it did in this case (as it had done some time before) wear off the edge of my desire to the thing; but the longer it seemed to be delayed, the more eager I was for it: in a word, I was not at first so careful to shun the sight of these savages, and avoid being seen by them, as I was now eager to be upon them.
paragraphs.cn: 这很叫人泄气,开始让我大为烦恼,不过我不能说这一回(像先前某个时候那样)磨钝了我对这件事的渴望;恰恰相反,它越是似乎被拖延,我就越是急切:一句话,起初我还小心翼翼躲着这些野人、生怕被他们瞧见,如今却急不可耐地想扑到他们身上去。

paragraphs.en: Besides, I fancied myself able to manage one, nay, two or three savages, if I had them, so as to make them entirely slaves to me, to do whatever I should direct them, and to prevent their being able at any time to do me any hurt.
paragraphs.cn: 再说,我自忖有本事对付一个、甚至两三个野人——只要我逮住了他们——把他们彻底变成我的奴隶,叫他们唯我之命是从,并防着他们随时有机会加害于我。

paragraphs.en: It was a great while that I pleased myself with this affair; but nothing still presented itself; all my fancies and schemes came to nothing, for no savages came near me for a great while.
paragraphs.cn: 我拿这桩事自娱自乐了好长一阵;可始终不见动静;我所有的空想和盘算都落了空,因为好久好久都没有野人靠近我。

paragraphs.en: About a year and a half after I entertained these notions (and by long musing had, as it were, resolved them all into nothing, for want of an occasion to put them into execution), I was surprised one morning by seeing no less than five canoes all on shore together on my side the island, and the people who belonged to them all landed and out of my sight.
paragraphs.cn: 在我起了这些念头约莫一年半之后(由于迟迟没有机会付诸实行,我反复琢磨,几乎又把它们都想成了空),一天早晨我却大吃一惊,竟看见不下五条独木舟一齐停在我这一侧的岛岸上,而船上的人全都上了岸,不见了踪影。

paragraphs.en: The number of them broke all my measures; for seeing so many, and knowing that they always came four or six, or sometimes more in a boat, I could not tell what to think of it, or how to take my measures to attack twenty or thirty men single-handed; so lay still in my castle, perplexed and discomforted.
paragraphs.cn: 他们人数之多打乱了我全盘的部署;见来了这么多,又知道他们向来一条船只坐四个、六个、有时多几个,我不知该作何想,也不知如何部署去单枪匹马迎战二三十号人;便只好静静躺在城堡里,又慌乱又沮丧。

paragraphs.en: However, I put myself into the same position for an attack that I had formerly provided, and was just ready for action, if anything had presented.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我还是摆出了从前预备好的迎战姿态,只要有什么动静,便随时可以出手。

paragraphs.en: Having waited a good while, listening to hear if they made any noise, at length, being very impatient, I set my guns at the foot of my ladder, and clambered up to the top of the hill, by my two stages, as usual; standing so, however, that my head did not appear above the hill, so that they could not perceive me by any means.
paragraphs.cn: 等了好半天,竖着耳朵听他们有没有弄出什么响动,最后我实在按捺不住,便把枪搁在梯脚下,照旧分两段攀上山顶;不过我站的姿势叫脑袋不露出山冈,好让他们无论如何都发觉不了我。

paragraphs.en: Here I observed, by the help of my perspective glass, that they were no less than thirty in number; that they had a fire kindled, and that they had meat dressed.
paragraphs.cn: 在这儿,借着望远镜,我看清他们人数不下三十;他们生起了一堆火,还烹好了肉。

paragraphs.en: How they had cooked it I knew not, or what it was; but they were all dancing, in I know not how many barbarous gestures and figures, their own way, round the fire.
paragraphs.cn: 他们是怎么把肉煮熟的、那又是什么肉,我不得而知;只见他们全都在跳舞,围着火堆,按他们自己的方式,做出不知多少种野蛮的手势和姿态。

paragraphs.en: While I was thus looking on them, I perceived, by my perspective, two miserable wretches dragged from the boats, where, it seems, they were laid by, and were now brought out for the slaughter.
paragraphs.cn: 我正这样看着他们,透过望远镜瞧见两个可怜的家伙从船上被拖了出来,看来他们先前是被搁在船里的,如今被押出来受戮。

paragraphs.en: I perceived one of them immediately fall; being knocked down, I suppose, with a club or wooden sword, for that was their way; and two or three others were at work immediately, cutting him open for their cookery, while the other victim was left standing by himself, till they should be ready for him.
paragraphs.cn: 我见其中一个立时倒下,想必是被一根棍棒或木刀击倒的,因为那是他们的做法;紧接着两三个人便动起手来,把他剖开料理去烹煮,另一个待宰的却被撇在一旁独自站着,等他们腾出手来收拾他。

paragraphs.en: In that very moment this poor wretch, seeing himself a little at liberty and unbound, Nature inspired him with hopes of life, and he started away from them, and ran with incredible swiftness along the sands, directly towards me; I mean towards that part of the coast where my habitation was.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这当口,这个可怜的家伙见自己稍稍得了自由、又没被绑着,求生的本能给了他一线活命的指望,他猛地从他们中间蹿开,以惊人的速度沿着沙滩狂奔,直朝我这边跑来;我是说,朝着我住处所在的那段海岸跑来。

paragraphs.en: I was dreadfully frightened, I must acknowledge, when I perceived him run my way; and especially when, as I thought, I saw him pursued by the whole body: and now I expected that part of my dream was coming to pass, and that he would certainly take shelter in my grove; but I could not depend, by any means, upon my dream, that the other savages would not pursue him thither and find him there.
paragraphs.cn: 说实话,当我发现他往我这边跑来时,我吓得魂飞魄散;尤其是我以为看见他后头有一大群人在追;这时我料想我梦里的那一段就要应验了,他准会躲进我的树林;可我无论如何也不敢仗着那个梦,就断定别的野人不会追到那儿、把他找出来。

paragraphs.en: However, I kept my station, and my spirits began to recover when I found that there was not above three men that followed him; and still more was I encouraged, when I found that he outstripped them exceedingly in running, and gained ground on them; so that, if he could but hold out for half-an-hour, I saw easily he would fairly get away from them all.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我坚守着原位;当我发现跟在他后面的不过三个人时,心里开始镇定下来;而当我看出他跑得远远把他们甩在后头、越拉越开时,就更受了鼓舞;这样,只要他还能撑上半个钟头,我一眼就看出他准能干干净净地摆脱他们所有人。

paragraphs.en: There was between them and my castle the creek, which I mentioned often in the first part of my story, where I landed my cargoes out of the ship; and this I saw plainly he must necessarily swim over, or the poor wretch would be taken there; but when the savage escaping came thither, he made nothing of it, though the tide was then up; but plunging in, swam through in about thirty strokes, or thereabouts, landed, and ran with exceeding strength and swiftness.
paragraphs.cn: 在他们和我城堡之间隔着一道小河汊,就是我在故事前半段常提到、当年从船上卸货登岸的地方;我看得分明,他非从这儿泅过去不可,否则这可怜人就要在那里被逮住;可那逃命的野人到了跟前,却毫不当回事,尽管当时正涨潮;他一头扎下水,约莫三十来划就泅了过去,上了岸,又使出惊人的力气和速度飞奔起来。

paragraphs.en: When the three persons came to the creek, I found that two of them could swim, but the third could not, and that, standing on the other side, he looked at the others, but went no farther, and soon after went softly back again; which, as it happened, was very well for him in the end.
paragraphs.cn: 那三个人来到河汊时,我发现其中两个会游水,第三个却不会;他站在对岸望着那两人,却没再往前,不一会儿便悄悄退了回去;而结果证明,这对他反倒是件大好事。

paragraphs.en: I observed that the two who swam were yet more than twice as strong swimming over the creek as the fellow was that fled from them.
paragraphs.cn: 我留意到那两个泅水的人,游过河汊的力气还不及那逃命者的一半灵便。

paragraphs.en: It came very warmly upon my thoughts, and indeed irresistibly, that now was the time to get me a servant, and, perhaps, a companion or assistant; and that I was plainly called by Providence to save this poor creature’s life.
paragraphs.cn: 一个念头热切地、简直不可抗拒地涌上我心头:此刻正是我弄个仆人、或许还是个同伴或帮手的时机;而且天意分明是在召唤我去救这可怜生灵的命。

paragraphs.en: I immediately ran down the ladders with all possible expedition, fetched my two guns, for they were both at the foot of the ladders, as I observed before, and getting up again with the same haste to the top of the hill, I crossed towards the sea; and having a very short cut, and all down hill, placed myself in the way between the pursuers and the pursued, hallowing aloud to him that fled, who, looking back, was at first perhaps as much frightened at me as at them; but I beckoned with my hand to him to come back; and, in the meantime, I slowly advanced towards the two that followed; then rushing at once upon the foremost, I knocked him down with the stock of my piece.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻以最快的速度奔下梯子,取来我那两支枪——前面说过,它们都搁在梯脚下——又同样急匆匆地爬回山顶,朝海边横插过去;由于抄了条极近的捷径,又一路下坡,我便挡在了追者与被追者之间,朝那逃命的人高声呼喊;他回头一看,起初对我或许和对他们一样害怕;但我朝他招手叫他回来;与此同时,我慢慢向那两个追来的人逼近;随即猛地一下扑向最前头那个,用枪托把他打翻在地。

paragraphs.en: I was loath to fire, because I would not have the rest hear; though, at that distance, it would not have been easily heard, and being out of sight of the smoke, too, they would not have known what to make of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我不愿开枪,免得让其余的人听见;不过隔那么远,枪声也不容易被听到,又看不见硝烟,他们即便听见也弄不明白是怎么回事。

paragraphs.en: Having knocked this fellow down, the other who pursued him stopped, as if he had been frightened, and I advanced towards him: but as I came nearer, I perceived presently he had a bow and arrow, and was fitting it to shoot at me: so I was then obliged to shoot at him first, which I did, and killed him at the first shot.
paragraphs.cn: 把这家伙打倒后,那个追他的人停住了脚,像是吓着了,我便朝他走去:可越走近,我立刻发觉他手里有弓有箭,正搭箭要射我:于是我不得不抢先向他开枪,一枪就把他打死了。

paragraphs.en: The poor savage who fled, but had stopped, though he saw both his enemies fallen and killed, as he thought, yet was so frightened with the fire and noise of my piece that he stood stock still, and neither came forward nor went backward, though he seemed rather inclined still to fly than to come on.
paragraphs.cn: 那个逃命的可怜野人虽已停下,却因为看见——如他所想——两个仇敌都倒地毙命,又被我枪的火光和响声吓得呆立不动,既不上前也不后退,不过看样子他还是宁可逃跑而不肯走近。

paragraphs.en: I hallooed again to him, and made signs to come forward, which he easily understood, and came a little way; then stopped again, and then a little farther, and stopped again; and I could then perceive that he stood trembling, as if he had been taken prisoner, and had just been to be killed, as his two enemies were.
paragraphs.cn: 我又朝他呼喊,打手势叫他上前,这回他一下就懂了,走近了几步;接着又停下,再往前一点,又停下;这时我看得出他站在那儿浑身发抖,仿佛自己成了俘虏、刚要像他那两个仇敌一样被杀掉似的。

paragraphs.en: I beckoned to him again to come to me, and gave him all the signs of encouragement that I could think of; and he came nearer and nearer, kneeling down every ten or twelve steps, in token of acknowledgment for saving his life.
paragraphs.cn: 我又招手叫他到我跟前来,把我能想到的鼓励手势全都做给他看;他便一步步走近,每走十来步就跪一下,以表示对我救他一命的感激。

paragraphs.en: I smiled at him, and looked pleasantly, and beckoned to him to come still nearer; at length he came close to me; and then he kneeled down again, kissed the ground, and laid his head upon the ground, and taking me by the foot, set my foot upon his head; this, it seems, was in token of swearing to be my slave for ever.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝他微笑,和颜悦色地望着他,招手叫他再走近些;他终于挨到了我身边;随后又跪下去,亲吻地面,把头贴在地上,拉起我的脚放到他头上;看来,这是表示他发誓永远做我的奴隶。

paragraphs.en: I took him up and made much of him, and encouraged him all I could.
paragraphs.cn: 我把他扶起来,好生抚慰他,尽我所能地给他打气。

paragraphs.en: But there was more work to do yet; for I perceived the savage whom I had knocked down was not killed, but stunned with the blow, and began to come to himself: so I pointed to him, and showed him the savage, that he was not dead; upon this he spoke some words to me, and though I could not understand them, yet I thought they were pleasant to hear; for they were the first sound of a man’s voice that I had heard, my own excepted, for above twenty-five years.
paragraphs.cn: 可是还有事要做呢;因为我发觉被我打倒的那个野人并没死,只是被那一击打晕了,这会儿正渐渐苏醒过来:于是我指着他,让那人看那野人还没断气;那人便对我说了几句话,我虽听不懂,却觉得很中听;因为这是二十五年多来,除了我自己的嗓音之外,我头一回听到人的声音。

paragraphs.en: But there was no time for such reflections now; the savage who was knocked down recovered himself so far as to sit up upon the ground, and I perceived that my savage began to be afraid; but when I saw that, I presented my other piece at the man, as if I would shoot him: upon this my savage, for so I call him now, made a motion to me to lend him my sword, which hung naked in a belt by my side, which I did.
paragraphs.cn: 可眼下没工夫作这类感慨了;那被打倒的野人已恢复到能坐起身来,我察觉我那野人开始害怕了;我一见这情形,便端起我另一支枪对准那人,做出要开枪的样子:于是我那野人——我现在就这么叫他了——向我打手势,想借我那把光溜溜挂在身侧腰带里的剑,我便递给了他。

paragraphs.en: He no sooner had it, but he runs to his enemy, and at one blow cut off his head so cleverly, no executioner in Germany could have done it sooner or better; which I thought very strange for one who, I had reason to believe, never saw a sword in his life before, except their own wooden swords: however, it seems, as I learned afterwards, they make their wooden swords so sharp, so heavy, and the wood is so hard, that they will even cut off heads with them, ay, and arms, and that at one blow, too.
paragraphs.cn: 他一拿到剑,就冲向他的仇敌,一刀利落地砍下了那人的脑袋,干净得连德国的刽子手也未必能砍得更快更好;我觉得这真是稀奇,因为我有理由相信他这辈子除了他们自己的木刀之外,从没见过一把真剑:不过,我后来才知道,原来他们把木刀做得那样锋利、那样沉重,木头又那样坚硬,竟真能用它砍下人头,是的,连胳膊也能砍断,而且都是一刀两断。

paragraphs.en: When he had done this, he comes laughing to me in sign of triumph, and brought me the sword again, and with abundance of gestures which I did not understand, laid it down, with the head of the savage that he had killed, just before me.
paragraphs.cn: 砍完之后,他笑呵呵地朝我走来,以示得胜,把剑又还给我,还比了一大堆我看不懂的手势,然后把剑连同他杀掉的那野人的头,一起放在我跟前。

paragraphs.en: But that which astonished him most was to know how I killed the other Indian so far off; so, pointing to him, he made signs to me to let him go to him; and I bade him go, as well as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 可最让他吃惊的,是想弄明白我怎么能从那么远打死了另一个野人;于是他指着那人,打手势要我准他过去看看;我便尽我所能地叫他去。

paragraphs.en: When he came to him, he stood like one amazed, looking at him, turning him first on one side, then on the other; looked at the wound the bullet had made, which it seems was just in his breast, where it had made a hole, and no great quantity of blood had followed; but he had bled inwardly, for he was quite dead.
paragraphs.cn: 他走到那人跟前,像个惊呆了的人似的站着,盯着他看,先把他翻到这一边,又翻到那一边;瞧那子弹打出的伤口,原来正打在他胸口,穿了个洞,却没流出多少血;因为他是内出血,人已经死透了。

paragraphs.en: He took up his bow and arrows, and came back; so I turned to go away, and beckoned him to follow me, making signs to him that more might come after them.
paragraphs.cn: 他捡起那人的弓箭,回到我身边;我便转身要走,招手叫他跟着我,打手势告诉他,后面说不定还会有人追来。

paragraphs.en: Upon this he made signs to me that he should bury them with sand, that they might not be seen by the rest, if they followed; and so I made signs to him again to do so.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他向我打手势,说该用沙把他们埋起来,免得万一有人追来时被其余的人看见;我便又打手势叫他这么办。

paragraphs.en: He fell to work; and in an instant he had scraped a hole in the sand with his hands big enough to bury the first in, and then dragged him into it, and covered him; and did so by the other also; I believe he had buried them both in a quarter of an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 他动起手来;转眼间就用双手在沙里刨出一个足够埋下头一个人的坑,接着把他拖进去盖上;对另一个也照办了;我看他不到一刻钟就把两个都埋好了。

paragraphs.en: Then, calling away, I carried him, not to my castle, but quite away to my cave, on the farther part of the island: so I did not let my dream come to pass in that part, that he came into my grove for shelter.
paragraphs.cn: 随后,我把他叫开,领着他——不是回我的城堡,而是径直去岛另一头我那个山洞;这样一来,我那个梦里说他躲进我树林的那一段,我便没让它应验。

paragraphs.en: Here I gave him bread and a bunch of raisins to eat, and a draught of water, which I found he was indeed in great distress for, from his running: and having refreshed him, I made signs for him to go and lie down to sleep, showing him a place where I had laid some rice-straw, and a blanket upon it, which I used to sleep upon myself sometimes; so the poor creature lay down, and went to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 在这儿我给他面包和一串葡萄干吃,又给他一大口水喝——我看出他跑了这一路,实在渴得厉害;等他缓过劲来,我打手势叫他去躺下睡觉,指给他一处地方,那儿铺着些稻草,上头还盖着一条毯子,是我有时自己睡用的;这可怜的家伙便躺下睡着了。

paragraphs.en: He was a comely, handsome fellow, perfectly well made, with straight, strong limbs, not too large; tall, and well-shaped; and, as I reckon, about twenty-six years of age.
paragraphs.cn: 他是个眉清目秀、相貌堂堂的小伙子,身材长得极匀称,四肢挺直、结实,却不粗大;个子高高的,身形很好看;照我估算,约莫二十六岁上下。

paragraphs.en: He had a very good countenance, not a fierce and surly aspect, but seemed to have something very manly in his face; and yet he had all the sweetness and softness of a European in his countenance, too, especially when he smiled.
paragraphs.cn: 他有一副很好的面容,不凶悍也不阴沉,反倒像是透着几分很有男子气概的神气;可他脸上又带着欧洲人那种全部的甜和柔,尤其是在他微笑的时候。

paragraphs.en: His hair was long and black, not curled like wool; his forehead very high and large; and a great vivacity and sparkling sharpness in his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 他的头发又长又黑,不像羊毛那样卷曲;额头很高很宽;一双眼睛里透着极大的活气和闪亮的机敏。

paragraphs.en: The colour of his skin was not quite black, but very tawny; and yet not an ugly, yellow, nauseous tawny, as the Brazilians and Virginians, and other natives of America are, but of a bright kind of a dun olive-colour, that had in it something very agreeable, though not very easy to describe.
paragraphs.cn: 他的肤色并不全黑,而是很黄褐;可又不是巴西人、弗吉尼亚人以及美洲别的土著那种难看的、发黄的、叫人恶心的黄褐,而是一种明净的浅棕橄榄色,里头透着某种很悦目的东西,只是不太容易形容。

paragraphs.en: His face was round and plump; his nose small, not flat, like the negroes; a very good mouth, thin lips, and his fine teeth well set, and as white as ivory.
paragraphs.cn: 他的脸圆圆的、鼓鼓的;鼻子不大,也不像黑人那样扁平;一张很好看的嘴,嘴唇很薄,一口整齐的好牙,白得像象牙。

paragraphs.en: After he had slumbered, rather than slept, about half-an-hour, he awoke again, and came out of the cave to me, for I had been milking my goats which I had in the enclosure just by: when he espied me he came running to me, laying himself down again upon the ground, with all the possible signs of an humble, thankful disposition, making a great many antic gestures to show it.
paragraphs.cn: 他与其说是睡,不如说是打了个盹,约莫半小时后又醒了,走出山洞来找我,因为我正给我圈养在旁边围栏里的山羊挤奶:他一瞧见我,便朝我跑来,又把自己扑倒在地,做出一切表示谦卑、感恩的姿态,还比划出许多滑稽的手势来表明这心意。

paragraphs.en: At last he lays his head flat upon the ground, close to my foot, and sets my other foot upon his head, as he had done before; and after this made all the signs to me of subjection, servitude, and submission imaginable, to let me know how he would serve me so long as he lived.
paragraphs.cn: 最后他把头平贴在地上,紧挨着我的脚,又像先前那样把我的另一只脚放到他头上;这之后,他向我做出所能想象到的一切表示归顺、臣服、驯从的手势,好让我知道他愿一辈子这样服侍我。

paragraphs.en: I understood him in many things, and let him know I was very well pleased with him.
paragraphs.cn: 他许多意思我都懂了,也让他明白我对他十分满意。

paragraphs.en: In a little time I began to speak to him; and teach him to speak to me; and first, I let him know his name should be Friday, which was the day I saved his life; I called him so for the memory of the time.
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久,我便开始教他说话,教他跟我讲话;首先,我让他知道他的名字该叫“星期五”,因为那是我救他性命的那一天;我这样叫他,是为纪念那个日子。

paragraphs.en: I likewise taught him to say Master; and then let him know that was to be my name; I likewise taught him to say Yes and No and to know the meaning of them.
paragraphs.cn: 我还教他说“主人”,又让他明白那将是我的称呼;我同样教他说“是”和“不是”,并让他懂得这两个词的意思。

paragraphs.en: I gave him some milk in an earthen pot, and let him see me drink it before him, and sop my bread in it; and gave him a cake of bread to do the like, which he quickly complied with, and made signs that it was very good for him.
paragraphs.cn: 我用一个陶罐盛了些羊奶给他,当着他的面先喝给他看,还把面包泡在里头蘸着吃;又给他一块面包让他照样做,他很快就照办了,还打手势表示这东西对他很好。

paragraphs.en: I kept there with him all that night; but as soon as it was day I beckoned to him to come with me, and let him know I would give him some clothes; at which he seemed very glad, for he was stark naked.
paragraphs.cn: 那一整夜我都陪他待在那儿;可天一亮,我便招手叫他跟我走,让他知道我要给他些衣服穿;他听了显得很高兴,因为他浑身赤裸。

paragraphs.en: As we went by the place where he had buried the two men, he pointed exactly to the place, and showed me the marks that he had made to find them again, making signs to me that we should dig them up again and eat them.
paragraphs.cn: 我们经过他埋那两个人的地方时,他准确地指出那处所在,还把他做的记号指给我看,好再找到他们,并打手势说我们该把他们挖出来吃掉。

paragraphs.en: At this I appeared very angry, expressed my abhorrence of it, made as if I would vomit at the thoughts of it, and beckoned with my hand to him to come away, which he did immediately, with great submission.
paragraphs.cn: 对此我装出十分生气的样子,表明我厌恶至极,做出一想到这事就要呕吐的模样,又招手叫他走开,他立刻就走了,十分驯服。

paragraphs.en: I then led him up to the top of the hill, to see if his enemies were gone; and pulling out my glass I looked, and saw plainly the place where they had been, but no appearance of them or their canoes; so that it was plain they were gone, and had left their two comrades behind them, without any search after them.
paragraphs.cn: 随后我领他上到山顶,看看他的仇敌是否已经走了;我掏出望远镜一望,清清楚楚看见他们先前待过的地方,却不见他们的人影或独木舟;可见他们分明已经离去,把两个同伴撇下了,连找都没找。

paragraphs.en: But I was not content with this discovery; but having now more courage, and consequently more curiosity, I took my man Friday with me, giving him the sword in his hand, with the bow and arrows at his back, which I found he could use very dexterously, making him carry one gun for me, and I two for myself; and away we marched to the place where these creatures had been; for I had a mind now to get some further intelligence of them.
paragraphs.cn: 可我并不满足于这点发现;这会儿胆子壮了些,好奇心也随之更盛,我便带上我的仆人星期五,把剑交到他手里,弓箭背在他背上——我发现他用起这些来极其灵巧——又叫他替我扛一支枪,我自己扛两支;我们便动身朝这些家伙待过的地方进发;因为我这会儿存心想再多打探打探他们的底细。

paragraphs.en: When I came to the place my very blood ran chill in my veins, and my heart sunk within me, at the horror of the spectacle; indeed, it was a dreadful sight, at least it was so to me, though Friday made nothing of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我一到那地方,只觉得血液在血管里都凉了,一颗心直往下沉,眼前这景象太骇人了;那的确是可怕的一幕,至少对我是如此,尽管星期五对此毫不在意。

paragraphs.en: The place was covered with human bones, the ground dyed with their blood, and great pieces of flesh left here and there, half-eaten, mangled, and scorched; and, in short, all the tokens of the triumphant feast they had been making there, after a victory over their enemies.
paragraphs.cn: 那地方遍地是人骨,泥土被他们的血染红了,大块大块的人肉这儿那儿地丢着,吃了一半,撕得稀烂,还烧得焦黑;总之,一切迹象都表明,他们战胜仇敌之后,曾在这儿大摆过一场庆功的盛宴。

paragraphs.en: I saw three skulls, five hands, and the bones of three or four legs and feet, and abundance of other parts of the bodies; and Friday, by his signs, made me understand that they brought over four prisoners to feast upon; that three of them were eaten up, and that he, pointing to himself, was the fourth; that there had been a great battle between them and their next king, of whose subjects, it seems, he had been one, and that they had taken a great number of prisoners; all which were carried to several places by those who had taken them in the fight, in order to feast upon them, as was done here by these wretches upon those they brought hither.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见三个头骨、五只手,还有三四条腿脚的骨头,以及许许多多别的肢体残块;星期五打着手势让我明白:他们运过来四个俘虏要开宴吃掉;其中三个已被吃光,他指着自己,说他就是那第四个;还说他们和邻近的一个王之间打过一场大仗,他似乎正是那王的臣民之一,那一仗俘获了大批人;这些俘虏都被擒获他们的人分带到好几处去开宴吃掉,就像这帮恶徒在这儿吃他们押来的人一样。

paragraphs.en: I caused Friday to gather all the skulls, bones, flesh, and whatever remained, and lay them together in a heap, and make a great fire upon it, and burn them all to ashes.
paragraphs.cn: 我叫星期五把所有的头骨、骨头、人肉以及一切剩下的东西都拢到一处,堆成一堆,在上头生起一大堆火,把它们统统烧成灰烬。

paragraphs.en: I found Friday had still a hankering stomach after some of the flesh, and was still a cannibal in his nature; but I showed so much abhorrence at the very thoughts of it, and at the least appearance of it, that he durst not discover it: for I had, by some means, let him know that I would kill him if he offered it.
paragraphs.cn: 我发觉星期五肚里还惦记着几块人肉,骨子里仍是个吃人的野人;可我对这念头本身、以至它稍一露头都表现出极度的厌恶,吓得他再不敢流露出来:因为我用了些法子让他明白,他若敢下手,我就杀了他。

paragraphs.en: When he had done this, we came back to our castle; and there I fell to work for my man Friday; and first of all, I gave him a pair of linen drawers, which I had out of the poor gunner’s chest I mentioned, which I found in the wreck, and which, with a little alteration, fitted him very well; and then I made him a jerkin of goat’s skin, as well as my skill would allow (for I was now grown a tolerably good tailor); and I gave him a cap which I made of hare’s skin, very convenient, and fashionable enough; and thus he was clothed, for the present, tolerably well, and was mighty well pleased to see himself almost as well clothed as his master.
paragraphs.cn: 他把这事办完后,我们便回到城堡;到了那儿我就动手替我的仆人星期五张罗起来;首先,我给了他一条麻布短裤,是从我先前提过、在残船上找到的那可怜炮手的箱子里翻出来的,稍加改动便很合他的身;接着我又尽我的手艺给他做了一件羊皮短上衣(我这会儿已练成了个还算不错的裁缝);又给他一顶我用兔皮做的帽子,很便当,样式也够时兴;这么一来,他眼下也算穿戴得像模像样了,他见自己几乎跟主人穿得一样好,心里得意极了。

paragraphs.en: It is true he went awkwardly in these clothes at first: wearing the drawers was very awkward to him, and the sleeves of the waistcoat galled his shoulders and the inside of his arms; but a little easing them where he complained they hurt him, and using himself to them, he took to them at length very well.
paragraphs.cn: 起初他穿这些衣服的确很别扭:穿短裤对他来说很不自在,上衣的袖子磨得他肩膀和胳膊内侧生疼;不过在他喊疼的地方稍稍放宽些,他也渐渐习惯了,末了便穿得很自在了。

paragraphs.en: The next day, after I came home to my hutch with him, I began to consider where I should lodge him: and that I might do well for him and yet be perfectly easy myself, I made a little tent for him in the vacant place between my two fortifications, in the inside of the last, and in the outside of the first.
paragraphs.cn: 我把他领回窝棚后的第二天,我便开始盘算该把他安顿在哪里:为了既好好待他、又让我自己完全放心,我在我两道防御工事之间那块空地上给他搭了一顶小帐篷,也就是在里面那道墙之内、外面那道墙之外。

paragraphs.en: As there was a door or entrance there into my cave, I made a formal framed door-case, and a door to it, of boards, and set it up in the passage, a little within the entrance; and, causing the door to open in the inside, I barred it up in the night, taking in my ladders, too; so that Friday could no way come at me in the inside of my innermost wall, without making so much noise in getting over that it must needs awaken me; for my first wall had now a complete roof over it of long poles, covering all my tent, and leaning up to the side of the hill; which was again laid across with smaller sticks, instead of laths, and then thatched over a great thickness with the rice-straw, which was strong, like reeds; and at the hole or place which was left to go in or out by the ladder I had placed a kind of trap-door, which, if it had been attempted on the outside, would not have opened at all, but would have fallen down and made a great noise—as to weapons, I took them all into my side every night.
paragraphs.cn: 由于那儿有一道门、也就是通我山洞的入口,我便正正经经用木板做了个门框和一扇门,安在通道里,离入口稍稍靠里些;又让门朝里开,一到夜里就把它闩上,连梯子也一并收进来;这样,星期五无论如何也没法在我最里层的墙内摸到我跟前,不翻过去弄出老大的响动来把我惊醒是办不到的;因为我那第一道墙这会儿已经架上了一整片用长杆搭成的完整屋顶,把我整顶帐篷都盖住,一头斜靠在山坡上;上头又横铺了些较细的枝条充当板条,再厚厚地用稻草苫盖起来——那稻草结实得像芦苇;而在留出供梯子进出的那个洞口处,我又安了个活板门似的装置,若有人从外头去动它,它压根就打不开,反倒会塌下来,弄出好大的响声;至于武器,我每天夜里都把它们全收到我这边来。

paragraphs.en: But I needed none of all this precaution; for never man had a more faithful, loving, sincere servant than Friday was to me: without passions, sullenness, or designs, perfectly obliged and engaged; his very affections were tied to me, like those of a child to a father; and I daresay he would have sacrificed his life to save mine upon any occasion whatsoever—the many testimonies he gave me of this put it out of doubt, and soon convinced me that I needed to use no precautions for my safety on his account.
paragraphs.cn: 可这一切防备我原都用不着;因为从没有哪个人有过比星期五对我更忠诚、更亲爱、更真挚的仆人:他没有邪念,不闹脾气,也无所图谋,一心一意地效命尽忠;他对我的情分,就像孩子对父亲一样紧紧系着;我敢说,无论遇上什么事,他都会舍出性命来救我——他给了我许多这样的凭据,使这一点无可置疑,不久便叫我确信,为着提防他,我根本无需采取任何防范。

paragraphs.en: This frequently gave me occasion to observe, and that with wonder, that however it had pleased God in His providence, and in the government of the works of His hands, to take from so great a part of the world of His creatures the best uses to which their faculties and the powers of their souls are adapted, yet that He has bestowed upon them the same powers, the same reason, the same affections, the same sentiments of kindness and obligation, the same passions and resentments of wrongs, the same sense of gratitude, sincerity, fidelity, and all the capacities of doing good and receiving good that He has given to us; and that when He pleases to offer them occasions of exerting these, they are as ready, nay, more ready, to apply them to the right uses for which they were bestowed than we are.
paragraphs.cn: 这常给我机会去观察,而且是带着惊叹去观察:上帝在他的天意里、在治理他亲手所造的万物时,虽然从世上如此众多的生灵那里,收回了他们的才能和心灵的力量本可派上的最好用处,却仍然赐给了他们同样的能力、同样的理智、同样的情感、同样的仁爱与担当之心、同样面对不义时的激愤与不平、同样的感恩、真诚、忠信之意,以及他赋予我们的一切行善与受善的本领;而当他乐意给他们机会施展这些时,他们运用得同样敏捷,不,比我们更敏捷地把这些用到它们被赋予时的正当用处上去。

paragraphs.en: This made me very melancholy sometimes, in reflecting, as the several occasions presented, how mean a use we make of all these, even though we have these powers enlightened by the great lamp of instruction, the Spirit of God, and by the knowledge of His word added to our understanding; and why it has pleased God to hide the like saving knowledge from so many millions of souls, who, if I might judge by this poor savage, would make a much better use of it than we did.
paragraphs.cn: 这有时叫我十分伤感,因为我一想到:每逢种种机会摆在眼前,我们对这一切的运用竟是何等卑劣——尽管我们这些才能还有那盏伟大的教诲明灯,也就是上帝的圣灵所照亮,还加上对他圣言的认识添进我们的悟性里;而上帝又为何乐意把这同样能拯救人的知识,向那么千百万灵魂隐藏起来——若拿这个可怜的野人来判断,他们运用起来,只怕会比我们强得多。

paragraphs.en: From hence I sometimes was led too far, to invade the sovereignty of Providence, and, as it were, arraign the justice of so arbitrary a disposition of things, that should hide that sight from some, and reveal it to others, and yet expect a like duty from both; but I shut it up, and checked my thoughts with this conclusion: first, that we did not know by what light and law these should be condemned; but that as God was necessarily, and by the nature of His being, infinitely holy and just, so it could not be, but if these creatures were all sentenced to absence from Himself, it was on account of sinning against that light which, as the Scripture says, was a law to themselves, and by such rules as their consciences would acknowledge to be just, though the foundation was not discovered to us; and secondly, that still as we all are the clay in the hand of the potter, no vessel could say to him, “Why hast thou formed me thus?”
paragraphs.cn: 由此我有时被引得走得太远,竟去侵犯天意的主权,可以说去责问:如此专断地安排万事,竟把那洞见向一些人隐藏、又向另一些人显明,却又指望两者尽同样的本分,这究竟公不公道;但我把这心思按下,用这样一个结论来约束自己的念头:其一,我们并不知道这些人该凭着什么光、依着什么律去受审判;而上帝既然按其本性必然是无限圣洁公义的,那么,倘若这些生灵果真都被判定要与他隔绝,那也定是因为他们违背了那道光——正如《圣经》所说,这道光对他们自己就是一条律法——是照着他们良心也会承认为公道的准则,尽管那根基并未向我们显明;其二,既然我们全都是陶匠手中的泥,没有哪个器皿能对他说:“你为什么把我造成这样呢?”

paragraphs.en: But to return to my new companion.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,还是回来说我这位新伙伴吧。

paragraphs.en: I was greatly delighted with him, and made it my business to teach him everything that was proper to make him useful, handy, and helpful; but especially to make him speak, and understand me when I spoke; and he was the aptest scholar that ever was; and particularly was so merry, so constantly diligent, and so pleased when he could but understand me, or make me understand him, that it was very pleasant for me to talk to him.
paragraphs.cn: 我对他喜欢得不得了,把教会他一切能使他变得有用、能干、得力的本事当成我的正事;尤其是要教他说话、教他在我开口时能听懂我;他真是从来没有过的最伶俐的学生;他格外地快活,格外地始终勤勉,一旦能听懂我、或让我听懂他,就格外地欢喜,这使得同他说话对我是一件极愉快的事。

paragraphs.en: Now my life began to be so easy that I began to say to myself that could I but have been safe from more savages, I cared not if I was never to remove from the place where I lived.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我的日子开始变得如此安逸,以致我开始对自己说:只要能不再受更多野人的威胁,我便是永远不搬离我所住的这地方,也毫不在乎。

paragraphs.en: After I had been two or three days returned to my castle, I thought that, in order to bring Friday off from his horrid way of feeding, and from the relish of a cannibal’s stomach, I ought to let him taste other flesh; so I took him out with me one morning to the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 回到我的城堡两三天后，我想着，为了让星期五改掉他那可怕的进食方式，戒掉食人族口味的嗜好，我该让他尝尝别的肉；于是一天早晨，我带他一同去了树林。

paragraphs.en: I went, indeed, intending to kill a kid out of my own flock; and bring it home and dress it; but as I was going I saw a she-goat lying down in the shade, and two young kids sitting by her.
paragraphs.cn: 我原本是打算去打死我自己羊群里的一只小羊，带回家收拾好；可正走着，我看见一只母山羊卧在树荫里，身旁蹲着两只小羊。

paragraphs.en: I catched hold of Friday.
paragraphs.cn: 我一把抓住星期五。

paragraphs.en: “Hold,” said I, “stand still;” and made signs to him not to stir: immediately I presented my piece, shot, and killed one of the kids.
paragraphs.cn: “别动，”我说，“站住；”并打手势叫他不要动弹：随即我举起枪，一枪打死了其中一只小羊。

paragraphs.en: The poor creature, who had at a distance, indeed, seen me kill the savage, his enemy, but did not know, nor could imagine how it was done, was sensibly surprised, trembled, and shook, and looked so amazed that I thought he would have sunk down.
paragraphs.cn: 这可怜的家伙，虽然先前远远地看见我打死过那个野人，也就是他的敌人，却不知道、也想象不出那是怎么做到的，如今大吃一惊，浑身发抖打颤，一脸惊愕，我以为他要瘫倒在地了。

paragraphs.en: He did not see the kid I shot at, or perceive I had killed it, but ripped up his waistcoat to feel whether he was not wounded; and, as I found presently, thought I was resolved to kill him: for he came and kneeled down to me, and embracing my knees, said a great many things I did not understand; but I could easily see the meaning was to pray me not to kill him.
paragraphs.cn: 他没看见我打的那只小羊，也没觉察我把它打死了，只顾撕开自己的背心，摸摸自己有没有中弹；我很快就看出，他以为我是打定主意要杀他：因为他走过来跪在我面前，抱住我的双膝，说了许多我听不懂的话；不过我一眼就看出那意思，是在求我别杀他。

paragraphs.en: I soon found a way to convince him that I would do him no harm; and taking him up by the hand, laughed at him, and pointing to the kid which I had killed, beckoned to him to run and fetch it, which he did: and while he was wondering, and looking to see how the creature was killed, I loaded my gun again.
paragraphs.cn: 我很快找到办法让他相信我不会伤害他；我拉起他的手，冲他笑了笑，指着我打死的那只小羊，招手叫他跑去把它拿来，他照做了：他正纳闷、张望着想看看那牲口是怎么死的时候，我又把枪装上了弹。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by I saw a great fowl, like a hawk, sitting upon a tree within shot; so, to let Friday understand a little what I would do, I called him to me again, pointed at the fowl, which was indeed a parrot, though I thought it had been a hawk; I say, pointing to the parrot, and to my gun, and to the ground under the parrot, to let him see I would make it fall, I made him understand that I would shoot and kill that bird; accordingly, I fired, and bade him look, and immediately he saw the parrot fall.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，我看见一只像鹰一样的大鸟停在射程之内的一棵树上；为了让星期五稍微明白我要做什么，我又把他叫到跟前，指了指那只鸟——它其实是只鹦鹉，虽然我当成了鹰；我是说，我指着那只鹦鹉，又指指我的枪，再指指鹦鹉下面的地，让他看我要让它掉下来，好让他明白我要开枪打死那只鸟；于是我开了火，叫他看，他立刻看见那只鹦鹉掉了下来。

paragraphs.en: He stood like one frightened again, notwithstanding all I had said to him; and I found he was the more amazed, because he did not see me put anything into the gun, but thought that there must be some wonderful fund of death and destruction in that thing, able to kill man, beast, bird, or anything near or far off; and the astonishment this created in him was such as could not wear off for a long time; and I believe, if I would have let him, he would have worshipped me and my gun.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管我对他说了那么多，他还是像又受了惊吓似的站着；我发现他更加惊奇，是因为他没看见我往枪里装任何东西，只当那件东西里必定藏着某种神奇的、置人于死地、能毁灭一切的力量，能杀死远近的人、兽、鸟或任何东西；这在他心里引起的惊骇，久久不能消退；我相信，要是我允许，他会拜我和我的枪当作神明。

paragraphs.en: As for the gun itself, he would not so much as touch it for several days after; but he would speak to it and talk to it, as if it had answered him, when he was by himself; which, as I afterwards learned of him, was to desire it not to kill him.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那杆枪本身，此后好几天他连碰都不敢碰一下；可他独自一人时，会对着它说话，仿佛它会回答他似的；后来我从他那里得知，那是在央求它别杀他。

paragraphs.en: Well, after his astonishment was a little over at this, I pointed to him to run and fetch the bird I had shot, which he did, but stayed some time; for the parrot, not being quite dead, had fluttered away a good distance from the place where she fell: however, he found her, took her up, and brought her to me; and as I had perceived his ignorance about the gun before, I took this advantage to charge the gun again, and not to let him see me do it, that I might be ready for any other mark that might present; but nothing more offered at that time: so I brought home the kid, and the same evening I took the skin off, and cut it out as well as I could; and having a pot fit for that purpose, I boiled or stewed some of the flesh, and made some very good broth.
paragraphs.cn: 等他这阵惊愕稍稍过去，我指着叫他跑去把我打下的那只鸟拿来，他照做了，可去了好一会儿；因为那只鹦鹉没有完全死，扑腾着飞出了落地处相当远的地方：不过他还是找到了它，捡起来带给我；先前我既已看出他对枪一无所知，便趁此机会又把枪装上弹，还不让他看见我怎么做，好让我随时应付可能出现的别的猎物；不过那会儿再没什么可打的了：于是我把小羊带回家，当天傍晚剥了皮，尽力把肉切割好；我有一口正合用的锅，便把一些肉煮了或炖了，做出很不错的肉汤。

paragraphs.en: After I had begun to eat some I gave some to my man, who seemed very glad of it, and liked it very well; but that which was strangest to him was to see me eat salt with it.
paragraphs.cn: 我先吃了些，又分了些给我那仆人，他似乎很高兴，吃得津津有味；可最让他觉得稀奇的，是看我就着盐吃。

paragraphs.en: He made a sign to me that the salt was not good to eat; and putting a little into his own mouth, he seemed to nauseate it, and would spit and sputter at it, washing his mouth with fresh water after it: on the other hand, I took some meat into my mouth without salt, and I pretended to spit and sputter for want of salt, as much as he had done at the salt; but it would not do; he would never care for salt with meat or in his broth; at least, not for a great while, and then but a very little.
paragraphs.cn: 他打手势告诉我盐不好吃；他往自己嘴里放了一点，似乎觉得恶心，又是吐又是啐，之后还用清水漱口：另一方面，我拿了些不加盐的肉放进嘴里，也假装因为没盐而又吐又啐，就像他刚才对着盐那样；可这不管用；他对肉里或汤里加盐始终不感兴趣；至少很长一段时间都是如此，后来也只肯放极少一点。

paragraphs.en: Having thus fed him with boiled meat and broth, I was resolved to feast him the next day by roasting a piece of the kid: this I did by hanging it before the fire on a string, as I had seen many people do in England, setting two poles up, one on each side of the fire, and one across the top, and tying the string to the cross stick, letting the meat turn continually.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样用煮肉和肉汤喂过他之后，我打定主意第二天烤一块小羊肉款待他：我把肉用绳子挂在火前来烤，就像我在英格兰见许多人做的那样，在火的两边各竖一根杆子，顶上横搭一根，把绳子系在那横杆上，让肉不停地转动。

paragraphs.en: This Friday admired very much; but when he came to taste the flesh, he took so many ways to tell me how well he liked it, that I could not but understand him: and at last he told me, as well as he could, he would never eat man’s flesh any more, which I was very glad to hear.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五对这非常佩服；可当他尝到那肉时，他用了那么多法子告诉我他多么喜欢吃，我不能不明白他的意思：末了他尽力对我说，他再也不吃人肉了，我听了非常高兴。

paragraphs.en: The next day I set him to work beating some corn out, and sifting it in the manner I used to do, as I observed before; and he soon understood how to do it as well as I, especially after he had seen what the meaning of it was, and that it was to make bread of; for after that I let him see me make my bread, and bake it too; and in a little time Friday was able to do all the work for me as well as I could do it myself.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天我让他干活，打出些谷子，再按我惯常的方法把它筛干净，前面我说过这些；他很快就学会了做得跟我一样好，尤其是在他看明白这是做什么用、原来是拿来做面包之后；因为在那之后我让他看我做面包、还烤面包；没多久，星期五就能把我所有的活干得跟我自己一样好了。

paragraphs.en: I began now to consider, that having two mouths to feed instead of one, I must provide more ground for my harvest, and plant a larger quantity of corn than I used to do; so I marked out a larger piece of land, and began the fence in the same manner as before, in which Friday worked not only very willingly and very hard, but did it very cheerfully: and I told him what it was for; that it was for corn to make more bread, because he was now with me, and that I might have enough for him and myself too.
paragraphs.cn: 我这时开始盘算，如今要养活两张嘴而不是一张，我必须多开垦些地供收成，比往常多种些谷子；于是我划出一块更大的地，照先前的样子动手围篱笆，星期五干这活不仅十分卖力、十分肯干，而且干得很欢快：我告诉他这是做什么用的；说是为了种谷子好多做些面包，因为如今他跟我在一起了，我得让他和我自己都够吃。

paragraphs.en: He appeared very sensible of that part, and let me know that he thought I had much more labour upon me on his account than I had for myself; and that he would work the harder for me if I would tell him what to do.
paragraphs.cn: 他对这一点显得很懂事，让我知道他觉得我为他所付的辛劳比为我自己的还要多；他还说，只要我肯告诉他该做什么，他愿意为我更卖力地干活。

paragraphs.en: This was the pleasantest year of all the life I led in this place.
paragraphs.cn: 这是我在这地方所过日子中最快活的一年。

paragraphs.en: Friday began to talk pretty well, and understand the names of almost everything I had occasion to call for, and of every place I had to send him to, and talked a great deal to me; so that, in short, I began now to have some use for my tongue again, which, indeed, I had very little occasion for before.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五开始说得相当不错了，几乎能听懂我要用到的一切东西的名称，以及我要派他去的每一个地方的名字，还跟我说了许多话；总之，简而言之，我如今又开始能用上我这条舌头了，其实先前它是很少有机会派上用场的。

paragraphs.en: Besides the pleasure of talking to him, I had a singular satisfaction in the fellow himself: his simple, unfeigned honesty appeared to me more and more every day, and I began really to love the creature; and on his side I believe he loved me more than it was possible for him ever to love anything before.
paragraphs.cn: 除了和他说话的乐趣，这家伙本身也给我一种别样的满足：他那单纯、真挚的老实一天天在我眼前愈发显现，我开始真心喜爱这个人；而在他那一方，我相信他爱我胜过他从前所能爱任何东西的程度。

paragraphs.en: I had a mind once to try if he had any inclination for his own country again; and having taught him English so well that he could answer me almost any question, I asked him whether the nation that he belonged to never conquered in battle?
paragraphs.cn: 有一次我想试试他是否还有回自己故乡的心思；我把英语教得他能几乎回答我任何问题，便问他，他所属的那个部族在打仗时可曾没有打过胜仗？

paragraphs.en: At which he smiled, and said—“Yes, yes, we always fight the better;” that is, he meant always get the better in fight; and so we began the following discourse:—
paragraphs.cn: 他听了微微一笑，说——“会，会，我们打仗总是打得更好；”意思是，他们打仗总是占上风；于是我们就有了下面这番对话：——

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —You always fight the better; how came you to be taken prisoner, then, Friday?
paragraphs.cn: ——你们打仗总占上风；那你怎么会被俘的呢，星期五？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —My nation beat much for all that.
paragraphs.cn: ——尽管那样，我的部族还是打了大胜仗。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —How beat?
paragraphs.cn: ——怎么胜？

paragraphs.en: If your nation beat them, how came you to be taken?
paragraphs.cn: 要是你的部族打赢了他们，你怎么会被抓走？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —They more many than my nation, in the place where me was; they take one, two, three, and me: my nation over-beat them in the yonder place, where me no was; there my nation take one, two, great thousand.
paragraphs.cn: ——在我待的那地方，他们人比我的部族多；他们抓走一个、两个、三个，还有我：我的部族在那边我没去的地方把他们打得大败；那里我的部族抓了一个、两个、好几千个。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —But why did not your side recover you from the hands of your enemies, then?
paragraphs.cn: ——可你们那一方当时为什么没把你从敌人手里救出来呢？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —They run, one, two, three, and me, and make go in the canoe; my nation have no canoe that time.
paragraphs.cn: ——他们把一个、两个、三个，还有我赶跑，逼进独木舟里；那时候我的部族没有独木舟。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —Well, Friday, and what does your nation do with the men they take?
paragraphs.cn: ——好吧，星期五，那你的部族怎么处置他们抓来的人？

paragraphs.en: Do they carry them away and eat them, as these did?
paragraphs.cn: 他们是不是把人带走吃掉，就像这些人干的那样？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —Yes, my nation eat mans too; eat all up.
paragraphs.cn: ——是，我的部族也吃人；全都吃光。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —Where do they carry them?
paragraphs.cn: ——他们把人带到哪里去？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —Go to other place, where they think.
paragraphs.cn: ——去别的地方，他们想去的地方。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —Do they come hither?
paragraphs.cn: ——他们到这里来吗？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —Yes, yes, they come hither; come other else place.
paragraphs.cn: ——来，来，他们到这里来；也到别的地方去。

paragraphs.en: _Master_.
paragraphs.cn: 主人。

paragraphs.en: —Have you been here with them?
paragraphs.cn: ——你跟他们到过这里吗？

paragraphs.en: _Friday_.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五。

paragraphs.en: —Yes, I have been here (points to the NW. side of the island, which, it seems, was their side).
paragraphs.cn: ——到过，我到过这里（他指了指岛的西北面，看来那是他们常来的那一边）。

paragraphs.en: By this I understood that my man Friday had formerly been among the savages who used to come on shore on the farther part of the island, on the same man-eating occasions he was now brought for; and some time after, when I took the courage to carry him to that side, being the same I formerly mentioned, he presently knew the place, and told me he was there once, when they ate up twenty men, two women, and one child; he could not tell twenty in English, but he numbered them by laying so many stones in a row, and pointing to me to tell them over.
paragraphs.cn: 由此我明白，我这仆人星期五从前也在那伙野人当中，那些野人常常上到岛的另一头，为的正是他这次被带来的那种吃人的勾当；后来过了些时候，我鼓起勇气带他到那一边去，也就是我先前提到的那处地方，他立刻认出了那地方，告诉我他曾到过那里一次，那次他们吃了二十个男人、两个女人和一个孩子；他不会用英语数到二十，便把那么多石子摆成一排来计数，再指着叫我替他数一遍。

paragraphs.en: I have told this passage, because it introduces what follows: that after this discourse I had with him, I asked him how far it was from our island to the shore, and whether the canoes were not often lost.
paragraphs.cn: 我把这段经过讲出来，是因为它引出了后面的事：在这番谈话之后，我问他从我们这岛到那岸边有多远，那些独木舟是不是常常出事沉没。

paragraphs.en: He told me there was no danger, no canoes ever lost: but that after a little way out to sea, there was a current and wind, always one way in the morning, the other in the afternoon.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我没有危险，从没有独木舟沉过：不过出海走一小段之后，那里有一股水流和一阵风，早上总是一个方向，下午又是另一个方向。

paragraphs.en: This I understood to be no more than the sets of the tide, as going out or coming in; but I afterwards understood it was occasioned by the great draft and reflux of the mighty river Orinoco, in the mouth or gulf of which river, as I found afterwards, our island lay; and that this land, which I perceived to be W. and NW.
paragraphs.cn: 我起初以为这不过是潮水的涨落罢了；可后来我明白，那是那条浩浩荡荡的奥里诺科大河巨大的排水和回流所致，后来我发现，我们这岛就位于那条河的河口或海湾里；我望见西面和西北面的那片陆地，

paragraphs.en: , was the great island Trinidad, on the north point of the mouth of the river.
paragraphs.cn: 正是那座大岛特立尼达，位于河口北端。

paragraphs.en: I asked Friday a thousand questions about the country, the inhabitants, the sea, the coast, and what nations were near; he told me all he knew with the greatest openness imaginable.
paragraphs.cn: 我向星期五问了一千个关于那地方、居民、大海、海岸以及附近有哪些部族的问题；他把自己所知道的一切都极其坦率地告诉了我。

paragraphs.en: I asked him the names of the several nations of his sort of people, but could get no other name than Caribs; from whence I easily understood that these were the Caribbees, which our maps place on the part of America which reaches from the mouth of the river Orinoco to Guiana, and onwards to St. Martha.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他他们那类人的几个部族叫什么名字，可除了“加勒比人”这个名字外问不出别的来；由此我不难明白，这些就是加勒比人，我们的地图把他们标在美洲那一带，从奥里诺科河口一直延伸到圭亚那，再往前到圣马大。

paragraphs.en: He told me that up a great way beyond the moon, that was beyond the setting of the moon, which must be west from their country, there dwelt white bearded men, like me, and pointed to my great whiskers, which I mentioned before; and that they had killed much mans, that was his word: by all which I understood he meant the Spaniards, whose cruelties in America had been spread over the whole country, and were remembered by all the nations from father to son.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我，在很远很远、月亮那边，也就是月亮落下去的那一头——那必定是在他们国土的西方——住着一些白胡子的人，像我这样，他还指了指我那先前提到的大胡子；他说那些人杀过许多人，“杀人”就是他用的字眼：由这一切我明白他指的是西班牙人，他们在美洲的暴行早已传遍了整个大陆，被各部族一代代父传子地记着。

paragraphs.en: I inquired if he could tell me how I might go from this island, and get among those white men.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他能不能告诉我，我该怎么离开这座岛，去到那些白人当中。

paragraphs.en: He told me, “Yes, yes, you may go in two canoe.”
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我：“能，能，你可以坐两只独木舟去。”

paragraphs.en: I could not understand what he meant, or make him describe to me what he meant by two canoe, till at last, with great difficulty, I found he meant it must be in a large boat, as big as two canoes.
paragraphs.cn: 我起先弄不懂他的意思，也没法让他向我说清“两只独木舟”是什么意思，直到最后费了好大劲，我才弄明白他的意思是，那必须是一条大船，有两只独木舟那么大。

paragraphs.en: This part of Friday’s discourse I began to relish very well; and from this time I entertained some hopes that, one time or other, I might find an opportunity to make my escape from this place, and that this poor savage might be a means to help me.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五这番话我开始很中意了；从这时起，我心里生出几分指望，觉得或许有朝一日我能找到机会从这地方逃出去，而这个可怜的野人或许能成为帮我的一个助力。

paragraphs.en: During the long time that Friday had now been with me, and that he began to speak to me, and understand me, I was not wanting to lay a foundation of religious knowledge in his mind; particularly I asked him one time, who made him.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五跟我在一起已有很长时间，他开始能对我说话、能听懂我的话，我也没有忘了在他心里打下宗教知识的根基；有一次我特意问他，是谁造了他。

paragraphs.en: The creature did not understand me at all, but thought I had asked who was his father—but I took it up by another handle, and asked him who made the sea, the ground we walked on, and the hills and woods.
paragraphs.cn: 这家伙完全没听懂我的意思，只当我问的是谁是他的父亲——可我换了个角度，问他是谁造了大海、我们脚下走着的地面、还有那些山丘和树林。

paragraphs.en: He told me, “It was one Benamuckee, that lived beyond all;” he could describe nothing of this great person, but that he was very old, “much older,” he said, “than the sea or land, than the moon or the stars.”
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我：“是一个叫贝纳姆基的，他住在万物之上；”关于这位伟大的存在他描述不出什么，只说他很老很老，“比大海和陆地还老得多，”他说，“比月亮和星星还老。”

paragraphs.en: I asked him then, if this old person had made all things, why did not all things worship him?
paragraphs.cn: 我于是问他，既然这位老者造了万物，为什么不是万物都敬拜他呢？

paragraphs.en: He looked very grave, and, with a perfect look of innocence, said, “All things say O to him.”
paragraphs.cn: 他神情十分严肃，带着一副全然天真的样子说：“万物都对他说‘噢’。”

paragraphs.en: I asked him if the people who die in his country went away anywhere?
paragraphs.cn: 我问他，他国里死了的人会去往什么地方吗？

paragraphs.en: He said, “Yes; they all went to Benamuckee.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“会；他们都去了贝纳姆基那里。”

paragraphs.en: Then I asked him whether those they eat up went thither too.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我问他，那些被他们吃掉的人是不是也去那里。

paragraphs.en: He said, “Yes.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“是。”

paragraphs.en: From these things, I began to instruct him in the knowledge of the true God; I told him that the great Maker of all things lived up there, pointing up towards heaven; that He governed the world by the same power and providence by which He made it; that He was omnipotent, and could do everything for us, give everything to us, take everything from us; and thus, by degrees, I opened his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 从这些事上，我开始教他认识真神；我告诉他，那位创造万物的伟大主宰住在那上面，一边指着天上；他用创造世界时同样的大能和护佑来治理世界；他是全能的，能为我们做一切、赐我们一切、也能从我们手中取走一切；就这样，我一点一点地开了他的眼。

paragraphs.en: He listened with great attention, and received with pleasure the notion of Jesus Christ being sent to redeem us; and of the manner of making our prayers to God, and His being able to hear us, even in heaven.
paragraphs.cn: 他听得十分专心，欣然接受了耶稣基督被差来救赎我们的道理，以及我们该怎样向神祷告、神即使在天上也能垂听我们的道理。

paragraphs.en: He told me one day, that if our God could hear us, up beyond the sun, he must needs be a greater God than their Benamuckee, who lived but a little way off, and yet could not hear till they went up to the great mountains where he dwelt to speak to them.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天他对我说，如果我们的神能在太阳那头听见我们，那他必定是个比他们那贝纳姆基更伟大的神，因为贝纳姆基住得不过一点点远，却还得等他们上到他所住的大山那里才听得见他们说话。

paragraphs.en: I asked him if ever he went thither to speak to him.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他，他自己可曾到那里去和他说过话。

paragraphs.en: He said, “No; they never went that were young men; none went thither but the old men,” whom he called their Oowokakee; that is, as I made him explain to me, their religious, or clergy; and that they went to say O (so he called saying prayers), and then came back and told them what Benamuckee said.
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“没有；年轻人从不去；除了老人没有人去那里，”他管那些老人叫“乌沃卡基”；照他向我解释的，也就是他们的宗教人士或祭司；那些人去说“噢”（他这么称呼祷告），然后回来告诉他们贝纳姆基说了什么。

paragraphs.en: By this I observed, that there is priestcraft even among the most blinded, ignorant pagans in the world; and the policy of making a secret of religion, in order to preserve the veneration of the people to the clergy, not only to be found in the Roman, but, perhaps, among all religions in the world, even among the most brutish and barbarous savages.
paragraphs.cn: 由此我看出，即便是世上最蒙昧无知的异教徒当中也有僧侣的把戏；把宗教弄得神秘兮兮、好让百姓对祭司保持敬畏的这套手腕，不仅见于罗马教，也许在世上所有宗教里都有，甚至在最粗野最野蛮的野人当中也有。

paragraphs.en: I endeavoured to clear up this fraud to my man Friday; and told him that the pretence of their old men going up to the mountains to say O to their god Benamuckee was a cheat; and their bringing word from thence what he said was much more so; that if they met with any answer, or spake with any one there, it must be with an evil spirit; and then I entered into a long discourse with him about the devil, the origin of him, his rebellion against God, his enmity to man, the reason of it, his setting himself up in the dark parts of the world to be worshipped instead of God, and as God, and the many stratagems he made use of to delude mankind to their ruin; how he had a secret access to our passions and to our affections, and to adapt his snares to our inclinations, so as to cause us even to be our own tempters, and run upon our destruction by our own choice.
paragraphs.cn: 我尽力向我这仆人星期五揭穿这个骗局；告诉他，他们那些老人上山去对他们的神贝纳姆基说“噢”，纯属欺诈；而他们从那里带回话来说他讲了什么，就更是骗人；如果他们真遇到什么回应、或跟那里的什么人说过话，那必定是跟一个恶灵打交道；接着我跟他就魔鬼展开了长长的一番谈论——魔鬼的来历、它对神的反叛、它对人的仇恨及其缘由、它在世上阴暗角落里立自己为神、要人拿它当神来敬拜、以及它诱骗人类走向毁灭所用的种种诡计；它怎样暗中通到我们的情欲和喜好，把陷阱因人所好而设，好使我们竟成了引诱自己的人，凭自己的抉择奔向毁灭。

paragraphs.en: I found it was not so easy to imprint right notions in his mind about the devil as it was about the being of a God.
paragraphs.cn: 我发现，要在他心里刻下关于魔鬼的正确观念，不像刻下关于神存在的观念那么容易。

paragraphs.en: Nature assisted all my arguments to evidence to him even the necessity of a great First Cause, an overruling, governing Power, a secret directing Providence, and of the equity and justice of paying homage to Him that made us, and the like; but there appeared nothing of this kind in the notion of an evil spirit, of his origin, his being, his nature, and above all, of his inclination to do evil, and to draw us in to do so too; and the poor creature puzzled me once in such a manner, by a question merely natural and innocent, that I scarce knew what to say to him.
paragraphs.cn: 大自然帮着我一切的论证，向他证明必有一个伟大的第一因、一个主宰统辖的大能、一位暗中引领的天意，也证明向那创造我们的主献上敬拜是何等合乎公义、合乎正理，如此等等；可关于恶灵——它的来历、它的存在、它的本性，尤其是它作恶、并把我们也拉去作恶的倾向——却没有半点这类现成的印证；这可怜的家伙有一次用一个纯出于天性、天真无邪的问题把我难住了，弄得我几乎不知该怎么回答他。

paragraphs.en: I had been talking a great deal to him of the power of God, His omnipotence, His aversion to sin, His being a consuming fire to the workers of iniquity; how, as He had made us all, He could destroy us and all the world in a moment; and he listened with great seriousness to me all the while.
paragraphs.cn: 我一直在跟他大讲神的大能、神的全能、神对罪的憎恶、神对作孽之人如同烈火焚烧；讲他既造了我们众人，也能一瞬间把我们和整个世界都毁灭；他自始至终都极其认真地听我讲。

paragraphs.en: After this I had been telling him how the devil was God’s enemy in the hearts of men, and used all his malice and skill to defeat the good designs of Providence, and to ruin the kingdom of Christ in the world, and the like.
paragraphs.cn: 在这之后，我一直在对他讲，魔鬼怎样在人心里作神的仇敌，使尽它一切的恶意和伎俩，去挫败天意的美好安排、去毁掉基督在世上的国度，如此等等。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” says Friday, “but you say God is so strong, so great; is He not much strong, much might as the devil?”
paragraphs.cn: “可是，”星期五说，“你说神那么强、那么大；难道他不像魔鬼一样强、一样有本事吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, yes,” says I, “Friday; God is stronger than the devil—God is above the devil, and therefore we pray to God to tread him down under our feet, and enable us to resist his temptations and quench his fiery darts.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，是的，”我说，“星期五；神比魔鬼强——神在魔鬼之上，所以我们祷告神，求他把魔鬼践踏在我们脚下，让我们能抵挡它的引诱、扑灭它那些火箭。”

paragraphs.en: “But,” says he again, “if God much stronger, much might as the wicked devil, why God no kill the devil, so make him no more do wicked?”
paragraphs.cn: “可是，”他又说，“如果神比那邪恶的魔鬼强得多、有本事得多，神为什么不杀了魔鬼，好叫它再也不能作恶呢？”

paragraphs.en: I was strangely surprised at this question; and, after all, though I was now an old man, yet I was but a young doctor, and ill qualified for a casuist or a solver of difficulties; and at first I could not tell what to say; so I pretended not to hear him, and asked him what he said; but he was too earnest for an answer to forget his question, so that he repeated it in the very same broken words as above.
paragraphs.cn: 这个问题把我奇怪地难住了；说到底，我如今虽是个上了年纪的人，在神学上却还是个新手，很不够格当个决疑家或解难人；起先我不知该说什么好；于是我假装没听见，问他说了什么；可他太急于要个答案，忘不了他的问题，便又用上面那番同样蹩脚的话把它重复了一遍。

paragraphs.en: By this time I had recovered myself a little, and I said, “God will at last punish him severely; he is reserved for the judgment, and is to be cast into the bottomless pit, to dwell with everlasting fire.”
paragraphs.cn: 这时我已稍稍定下神来，便说：“神到末了会严厉惩罚它；它被留待审判，将被扔进那无底的深坑，与永火同住。”

paragraphs.en: This did not satisfy Friday; but he returns upon me, repeating my words, “‘_Reserve at last!
paragraphs.cn: 这并没有让星期五满意；他又追问我，重复我的话：“‘留待末了’！

paragraphs.en: _’ me no understand—but why not kill the devil now; not kill great ago?”
paragraphs.cn: 我不懂——可为什么不现在就杀了魔鬼；为什么不老早就杀了它？”

paragraphs.en: “You may as well ask me,” said I, “why God does not kill you or me, when we do wicked things here that offend Him—we are preserved to repent and be pardoned.”
paragraphs.cn: “你也大可以问我，”我说，“神为什么不在我们这里做冒犯他的坏事时把你我杀掉——我们被留下来，是好让我们悔改、得赦免。”

paragraphs.en: He mused some time on this.
paragraphs.cn: 他为这个沉思了好一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “Well, well,” says he, mighty affectionately, “that well—so you, I, devil, all wicked, all preserve, repent, God pardon all.”
paragraphs.cn: “好啦，好啦，”他极其亲切地说，“这就好——那么你、我、魔鬼，全都作恶，全被留下，都悔改，神就赦免所有人。”

paragraphs.en: Here I was run down again by him to the last degree; and it was a testimony to me, how the mere notions of nature, though they will guide reasonable creatures to the knowledge of a God, and of a worship or homage due to the supreme being of God, as the consequence of our nature, yet nothing but divine revelation can form the knowledge of Jesus Christ, and of redemption purchased for us; of a Mediator of the new covenant, and of an Intercessor at the footstool of God’s throne; I say, nothing but a revelation from Heaven can form these in the soul; and that, therefore, the gospel of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, I mean the Word of God, and the Spirit of God, promised for the guide and sanctifier of His people, are the absolutely necessary instructors of the souls of men in the saving knowledge of God and the means of salvation.
paragraphs.cn: 在这里我又被他驳得体无完肤；这对我是一个明证：单凭天性的观念，虽能引导有理性的受造之物去认识有一位神、去认识我们本性所当然向至高的神所献的敬拜或礼敬，可是除了神的启示，什么也不能在人心里形成对耶稣基督、对为我们所成就的救赎的认识；对新约的一位中保、对神宝座脚前的一位代求者的认识；我是说，惟有从天上来的启示才能在灵里形成这些；因此，我们的主和救主耶稣基督的福音，我是指神的道，以及应许作神子民的引导者和成圣者的神的灵，才是引人认识救恩之神、认识得救之法的、对人灵魂绝对不可少的教师。

paragraphs.en: I therefore diverted the present discourse between me and my man, rising up hastily, as upon some sudden occasion of going out; then sending him for something a good way off, I seriously prayed to God that He would enable me to instruct savingly this poor savage; assisting, by His Spirit, the heart of the poor ignorant creature to receive the light of the knowledge of God in Christ, reconciling him to Himself, and would guide me so to speak to him from the Word of God that his conscience might be convinced, his eyes opened, and his soul saved.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我岔开了我和这仆人之间眼下的谈话，急忙站起身来，仿佛忽然有事要出去；接着打发他到老远的地方去取样东西，我恳切地向神祷告，求他使我能把救恩的道确实地教给这可怜的野人；求他借着他的灵，帮助这可怜无知之人的心去领受那认识神在基督里的亮光，使他与神和好，并引导我照着神的道对他说话，好叫他的良心受感、他的眼睛得开、他的灵魂得救。

paragraphs.en: When he came again to me, I entered into a long discourse with him upon the subject of the redemption of man by the Saviour of the world, and of the doctrine of the gospel preached from Heaven, viz. of repentance towards God, and faith in our blessed Lord Jesus.
paragraphs.cn: 他再回到我这里时，我跟他就世界救主救赎人类的题目、以及从天上所传福音的道理，展开了长长的一番谈论，也就是向神悔改、并信靠我们蒙福的主耶稣。

paragraphs.en: I then explained to him as well as I could why our blessed Redeemer took not on Him the nature of angels but the seed of Abraham; and how, for that reason, the fallen angels had no share in the redemption; that He came only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the like.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我尽力向他解释，为什么我们蒙福的救赎主没有取天使的本性，而取了亚伯拉罕的后裔；又为什么因这缘故，那堕落的天使在救赎里没有份；他只为以色列家迷失的羊而来，如此等等。

paragraphs.en: I had, God knows, more sincerity than knowledge in all the methods I took for this poor creature’s instruction, and must acknowledge, what I believe all that act upon the same principle will find, that in laying things open to him, I really informed and instructed myself in many things that either I did not know or had not fully considered before, but which occurred naturally to my mind upon searching into them, for the information of this poor savage; and I had more affection in my inquiry after things upon this occasion than ever I felt before: so that, whether this poor wild wretch was better for me or no, I had great reason to be thankful that ever he came to me; my grief sat lighter upon me; my habitation grew comfortable to me beyond measure: and when I reflected that in this solitary life which I have been confined to, I had not only been moved to look up to heaven myself, and to seek the Hand that had brought me here, but was now to be made an instrument, under Providence, to save the life, and, for aught I knew, the soul of a poor savage, and bring him to the true knowledge of religion and of the Christian doctrine, that he might know Christ Jesus, in whom is life eternal; I say, when I reflected upon all these things, a secret joy ran through every part of my soul, and I frequently rejoiced that ever I was brought to this place, which I had so often thought the most dreadful of all afflictions that could possibly have befallen me.
paragraphs.cn: 神知道，我为教导这可怜家伙所用的一切方法里，诚意多于学识；我必须承认——我相信凡本着同样原则行事的人都会发现——在向他把道理讲开的过程中，我其实使自己在许多事上得了教益、明白了许多先前或者不知道、或者未曾充分想过的事，而这些事，在我为教导这可怜的野人而深入探究它们时，自然而然浮现在我心头；这一回我探究事理时所怀的深情，胜过我以往任何时候所感受到的：所以，不论这可怜的野蛮人对我有没有好处，我都大有理由感恩，感恩他竟到了我这里；我的忧愁在我身上轻了；我的住处对我变得无比舒适：每当我想到，在这被囚禁的孤寂生活里，我不但被感动亲自仰望上天、寻求那把我带到此地的手，如今还要在天意之下被用作一件器皿，去拯救一个可怜野人的性命、就我所知还有他的灵魂，把他领到对宗教和基督教道理的真认识里，好叫他能认识那有永生的基督耶稣；我是说，每当我想到这一切，一种隐秘的喜乐便流遍我灵魂的每一处，我常常庆幸自己竟被带到这地方——这地方，我曾一再以为是可能降在我身上一切苦难中最可怕的。

paragraphs.en: I continued in this thankful frame all the remainder of my time; and the conversation which employed the hours between Friday and me was such as made the three years which we lived there together perfectly and completely happy, if any such thing as complete happiness can be formed in a sublunary state.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这感恩的心境里度过了余下的全部时光；星期五和我之间用来消磨时辰的交谈，使我们一同在那里生活的三年过得十全十美、完完全全地幸福，如果在这日光之下的尘世当中真能有什么完全的幸福可言的话。

paragraphs.en: This savage was now a good Christian, a much better than I; though I have reason to hope, and bless God for it, that we were equally penitent, and comforted, restored penitents.
paragraphs.cn: 这个野人如今成了个好基督徒，比我还好得多；不过我有理由盼望，并为此感谢神，我们二人都同样是悔改的、得着安慰、蒙恩复原的悔罪之人。

paragraphs.en: We had here the Word of God to read, and no farther off from His Spirit to instruct than if we had been in England.
paragraphs.cn: 我们在这里有神的道可读，而离那位用他的灵教导我们的神，并不比我们身在英格兰时更远。

paragraphs.en: I always applied myself, in reading the Scripture, to let him know, as well as I could, the meaning of what I read; and he again, by his serious inquiries and questionings, made me, as I said before, a much better scholar in the Scripture knowledge than I should ever have been by my own mere private reading.
paragraphs.cn: 我读圣经时，总是尽力让他知道我所读之物的意思；而他呢，又借着他那些认真的探问和发问，正如我先前说过的，使我在圣经知识上成了个远比我单靠自己私下阅读所能成为的更好的学生。

paragraphs.en: Another thing I cannot refrain from observing here also, from experience in this retired part of my life, viz. how infinite and inexpressible a blessing it is that the knowledge of God, and of the doctrine of salvation by Christ Jesus, is so plainly laid down in the Word of God, so easy to be received and understood, that, as the bare reading the Scripture made me capable of understanding enough of my duty to carry me directly on to the great work of sincere repentance for my sins, and laying hold of a Saviour for life and salvation, to a stated reformation in practice, and obedience to all God’s commands, and this without any teacher or instructor, I mean human; so the same plain instruction sufficiently served to the enlightening this savage creature, and bringing him to be such a Christian as I have known few equal to him in my life.
paragraphs.cn: 还有一件事，我也忍不住要在这里指出，这是我从退隐生活的这一段里得来的体验，那就是：神的认识、以及借基督耶稣得救的道理，在神的道里说得如此明白、如此容易被领受和明白，实在是无穷无尽、难以言表的大福；单单读圣经就使我能够明白够多的本分，直接把我引向真诚为罪悔改这一大工、引向抓住一位救主以得生命和救恩、引向在行为上确实地改过、并顺服神一切的命令，而这一切用不着任何教师或教导者——我是指世人；同样，这同一份明白的教导，也足以启迪这野蛮的家伙，使他成为这样一个基督徒，我这一生里见过很少几个能与他相比。

paragraphs.en: As to all the disputes, wrangling, strife, and contention which have happened in the world about religion, whether niceties in doctrines or schemes of church government, they were all perfectly useless to us, and, for aught I can yet see, they have been so to the rest of the world.
paragraphs.cn: 至于世上围绕宗教发生的一切争辩、口角、纷争和倾轧，无论是道理上的细枝末节还是教会治理的种种方案，对我们全然无用；而且据我至今所能看出的，它们对世上其余的人也是一样无用。

paragraphs.en: We had the sure guide to heaven, viz. the Word of God; and we had, blessed be God, comfortable views of the Spirit of God teaching and instructing by His word, leading us into all truth, and making us both willing and obedient to the instruction of His word.
paragraphs.cn: 我们有那通往天国的可靠向导，那就是神的道；而且，愿神受赞美，我们对神的灵怀着令人欣慰的看见——他借着他的道教导、训诲，引我们进入一切真理，使我们二人都甘心乐意地顺服他道的教训。

paragraphs.en: And I cannot see the least use that the greatest knowledge of the disputed points of religion, which have made such confusion in the world, would have been to us, if we could have obtained it.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那些在宗教上有争议、在世上闹得如此纷乱的种种问题，就算我们能弄到那最渊博的知识，我也看不出它对我们会有半点用处。

paragraphs.en: But I must go on with the historical part of things, and take every part in its order.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我得接着讲事情按历史顺序的那一部分，一件一件依次道来。

paragraphs.en: After Friday and I became more intimately acquainted, and that he could understand almost all I said to him, and speak pretty fluently, though in broken English, to me, I acquainted him with my own history, or at least so much of it as related to my coming to this place: how I had lived there, and how long; I let him into the mystery, for such it was to him, of gunpowder and bullet, and taught him how to shoot.
paragraphs.cn: 在星期五和我更亲密地相熟之后，他几乎能听懂我对他说的一切，并且能相当流利地——虽然是蹩脚的英语——对我说话，我便把我自己的经历讲给他听，至少讲了其中与我来到这地方有关的那么多：我怎样在这里生活、生活了多久；我把火药和子弹的奥秘——对他来说这的确是奥秘——向他揭开，还教他怎样开枪。

paragraphs.en: I gave him a knife, which he was wonderfully delighted with; and I made him a belt, with a frog hanging to it, such as in England we wear hangers in; and in the frog, instead of a hanger, I gave him a hatchet, which was not only as good a weapon in some cases, but much more useful upon other occasions.
paragraphs.cn: 我给了他一把刀，他喜欢得不得了；我又给他做了一条腰带，带上挂着个刀套，就像英格兰我们佩挂短剑用的那种；套里我没放短剑，而给了他一把小斧头，这斧头在有些情形下不仅是一样同样好用的兵器，在别的场合还更有用处。

paragraphs.en: I described to him the country of Europe, particularly England, which I came from; how we lived, how we worshipped God, how we behaved to one another, and how we traded in ships to all parts of the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我向他描述了欧洲各国，尤其是我出身的英格兰；我们怎样生活、怎样敬拜神、怎样彼此相待、又怎样驾着船同世界各处通商。

paragraphs.en: I gave him an account of the wreck which I had been on board of, and showed him, as near as I could, the place where she lay; but she was all beaten in pieces before, and gone.
paragraphs.cn: 我把我曾经登过的那条失事的船讲给他听，还尽我所能把它所在的地方指给他看；可它先前早已被撞成碎片、荡然无存了。

paragraphs.en: I showed him the ruins of our boat, which we lost when we escaped, and which I could not stir with my whole strength then; but was now fallen almost all to pieces.
paragraphs.cn: 我把我们那条小船的残骸指给他看，就是我们逃命时丢掉、当时我使出浑身力气也挪不动的那条；如今它几乎全都散架了。

paragraphs.en: Upon seeing this boat, Friday stood, musing a great while, and said nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 看到这条船，星期五站着沉思了好久，一言不发。

paragraphs.en: I asked him what it was he studied upon.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他在琢磨什么。

paragraphs.en: At last says he, “Me see such boat like come to place at my nation.”
paragraphs.cn: 末了他说：“我看见这样的船来过我们部族那地方。”

paragraphs.en: I did not understand him a good while; but at last, when I had examined further into it, I understood by him that a boat, such as that had been, came on shore upon the country where he lived: that is, as he explained it, was driven thither by stress of weather.
paragraphs.cn: 我好一阵子没听懂他的意思；可到最后，我进一步问明白后，从他那里弄清了：有一条船，跟这条从前的样子一样，曾漂到他所住的那地方岸上：照他解释的说法，是被风暴逼到那里去的。

paragraphs.en: I presently imagined that some European ship must have been cast away upon their coast, and the boat might get loose and drive ashore; but was so dull that I never once thought of men making their escape from a wreck thither, much less whence they might come: so I only inquired after a description of the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我当即揣想，必是有条欧洲船在他们海岸上失了事，那小船许是挣脱漂到了岸上；可我太迟钝，一时竟没想到会有人从失事船上逃生到那里，更没想过他们可能是从哪儿来的：于是我只问了问那船的模样。

paragraphs.en: Friday described the boat to me well enough; but brought me better to understand him when he added with some warmth, “We save the white mans from drown.”
paragraphs.cn: 星期五把那船向我描述得够清楚了；可当他有些激动地补上一句时，我才更明白他的意思：“我们把那些白人从水里救起来，没让他们淹死。”

paragraphs.en: Then I presently asked if there were any white mans, as he called them, in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我随即问他，那船上是不是有白人——照他的叫法。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” he said; “the boat full of white mans.”
paragraphs.cn: “是，”他说；“船上满是白人。”

paragraphs.en: I asked him how many.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他有多少。

paragraphs.en: He told upon his fingers seventeen.
paragraphs.cn: 他扳着手指头说有十七个。

paragraphs.en: I asked him then what became of them.
paragraphs.cn: 我接着问他，那些人后来怎么样了。

paragraphs.en: He told me, “They live, they dwell at my nation.”
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我：“他们活着，住在我们部族里。”

paragraphs.en: This put new thoughts into my head; for I presently imagined that these might be the men belonging to the ship that was cast away in the sight of my island, as I now called it; and who, after the ship was struck on the rock, and they saw her inevitably lost, had saved themselves in their boat, and were landed upon that wild shore among the savages.
paragraphs.cn: 这让我头脑里生出新的念头；因为我当即揣想，这些人也许就是那条在我岛——我如今这么称呼它——附近失事的船上的人；他们在船撞上礁石、眼看它必定要沉之后，坐着他们的小船逃了命，登上了那野人出没的荒岸。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I inquired of him more critically what was become of them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我更仔细地向他打听他们的下落。

paragraphs.en: He assured me they lived still there; that they had been there about four years; that the savages left them alone, and gave them victuals to live on.
paragraphs.cn: 他向我保证，他们仍旧住在那里；他们在那里已经约有四年；那些野人不去动他们，还给他们食物过活。

paragraphs.en: I asked him how it came to pass they did not kill them and eat them.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他，怎么会没把他们杀掉吃了呢。

paragraphs.en: He said, “No, they make brother with them;” that is, as I understood him, a truce; and then he added, “They no eat mans but when make the war fight;” that is to say, they never eat any men but such as come to fight with them and are taken in battle.
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“不，他们跟他们结为兄弟；”照我理解，就是订了休战之约；接着他又补上一句：“他们只有打仗的时候才吃人；”也就是说，他们从不吃人，除非是那些来跟他们打仗、在战斗中被俘的人。

paragraphs.en: It was after this some considerable time, that being upon the top of the hill at the east side of the island, from whence, as I have said, I had, in a clear day, discovered the main or continent of America, Friday, the weather being very serene, looks very earnestly towards the mainland, and, in a kind of surprise, falls a jumping and dancing, and calls out to me, for I was at some distance from him.
