paragraphs.cn: 又过了相当一段时间，有一天我站在岛东边那山顶上——我说过，天晴的日子从那里我曾望见过美洲的大陆本土——天气十分晴朗，星期五极其热切地朝大陆望去，忽然像是又惊又喜，又蹦又跳地手舞足蹈起来，冲我大声喊叫，因为我离他有些距离。

paragraphs.en: I asked him what was the matter.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他出了什么事。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, joy!” says he; “Oh, glad! there see my country, there my nation!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，高兴啊！”他说；“哦，欢喜！那边看得见我的国土，那边是我的部族！”

paragraphs.en: I observed an extraordinary sense of pleasure appeared in his face, and his eyes sparkled, and his countenance discovered a strange eagerness, as if he had a mind to be in his own country again.
paragraphs.cn: 我注意到他脸上现出一种非同寻常的喜悦，眼睛闪着光，神情里透着一股异样的急切，仿佛他一心想再回到自己的国土去。

paragraphs.en: This observation of mine put a great many thoughts into me, which made me at first not so easy about my new man Friday as I was before; and I made no doubt but that, if Friday could get back to his own nation again, he would not only forget all his religion but all his obligation to me, and would be forward enough to give his countrymen an account of me, and come back, perhaps with a hundred or two of them, and make a feast upon me, at which he might be as merry as he used to be with those of his enemies when they were taken in war.
paragraphs.cn: 我这番观察在我心里勾起了许多念头，起初弄得我对我这新来的仆人星期五不像先前那么放心了；我毫不怀疑，倘若星期五能回到他自己的部族去，他不但会忘掉他所有的宗教，还会忘掉他对我的一切恩义，会巴不得向他的同胞讲说我的事，再回来，也许带上一两百个同胞，拿我摆一场盛宴，在宴上像他从前对付战俘时那样开怀作乐。

paragraphs.en: But I wronged the poor honest creature very much, for which I was very sorry afterwards.
paragraphs.cn: 可我大大冤枉了这可怜老实的家伙，事后我为此很是懊悔。

paragraphs.en: However, as my jealousy increased, and held some weeks, I was a little more circumspect, and not so familiar and kind to him as before: in which I was certainly wrong too; the honest, grateful creature having no thought about it but what consisted with the best principles, both as a religious Christian and as a grateful friend, as appeared afterwards to my full satisfaction.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，随着我的猜疑加深，持续了好几个星期，我变得稍稍谨慎了些，不像先前那样跟他亲昵和气：这我肯定也是错的；这老实、知恩的家伙心里对此毫无别的想头，全是合乎最高尚原则的——无论作为一个虔诚的基督徒，还是作为一个知恩的朋友，这一点后来令我十分满意地显现了出来。

paragraphs.en: While my jealousy of him lasted, you may be sure I was every day pumping him to see if he would discover any of the new thoughts which I suspected were in him; but I found everything he said was so honest and so innocent, that I could find nothing to nourish my suspicion; and in spite of all my uneasiness, he made me at last entirely his own again; nor did he in the least perceive that I was uneasy, and therefore I could not suspect him of deceit.
paragraphs.cn: 在我对他的猜疑持续期间，你尽可以想见，我天天在旁敲侧击地试探他，看他会不会露出我所疑心他心里怀着的那些新念头；可我发现他所说的一切都那么老实、那么天真，我找不出半点足以滋养我疑心的东西；尽管我心里那么不安，他到末了还是让我完全把心又交回给了他；他也丝毫没有觉察到我心里不安，因此我也没法疑心他有诈。

paragraphs.en: One day, walking up the same hill, but the weather being hazy at sea, so that we could not see the continent, I called to him, and said, “Friday, do not you wish yourself in your own country, your own nation?”
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，我们又走上那同一座山，可海上雾蒙蒙的，望不见大陆，我叫住他，说：“星期五，你难道不想回到你自己的国土、你自己的部族去吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” he said, “I be much O glad to be at my own nation.”
paragraphs.cn: “想，”他说，“我要是能回到我自己的部族，会非常非常高兴。”

paragraphs.en: “What would you do there?” said I. “Would you turn wild again, eat men’s flesh again, and be a savage as you were before?”
paragraphs.cn: “你回去要做什么呢？”我说。“你会重新变回野人，重新吃人肉，像从前那样做个野蛮人吗？”

paragraphs.en: He looked full of concern, and shaking his head, said, “No, no, Friday tell them to live good; tell them to pray God; tell them to eat corn-bread, cattle flesh, milk; no eat man again.”
paragraphs.cn: 他满脸忧色，摇着头说：“不，不，星期五要叫他们好好地活；叫他们向神祷告；叫他们吃玉米面包、牛肉、牛奶；再不吃人。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, then,” said I to him, “they will kill you.”
paragraphs.cn: “那么，”我对他说，“他们会杀了你的。”

paragraphs.en: He looked grave at that, and then said, “No, no, they no kill me, they willing love learn.”
paragraphs.cn: 他听了神色一沉，随后说道：“不，不，他们不会杀我，他们乐意爱、乐意学。”

paragraphs.en: He meant by this, they would be willing to learn.
paragraphs.cn: 他这话的意思是，他们会乐意学的。

paragraphs.en: He added, they learned much of the bearded mans that came in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 他还说，他们从坐船来的那些大胡子人那里学到了许多。

paragraphs.en: Then I asked him if he would go back to them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我问他愿不愿意回到他们那里去。

paragraphs.en: He smiled at that, and told me that he could not swim so far.
paragraphs.cn: 他听了微微一笑，告诉我他游不了那么远。

paragraphs.en: I told him I would make a canoe for him.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他，我会给他造一只独木舟。

paragraphs.en: He told me he would go if I would go with him.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我，只要我肯跟他一同去，他就去。

paragraphs.en: “I go!” says I; “why, they will eat me if I come there.”
paragraphs.cn: “我去！”我说；“怎么，我要是去了那里，他们会把我吃掉的。”

paragraphs.en: “No, no,” says he, “me make they no eat you; me make they much love you.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，不，”他说，“我叫他们不吃你；我叫他们非常爱你。”

paragraphs.en: He meant, he would tell them how I had killed his enemies, and saved his life, and so he would make them love me.
paragraphs.cn: 他的意思是，他会告诉他们我怎样杀了他的敌人、救了他的命，这样他就会使他们爱我。

paragraphs.en: Then he told me, as well as he could, how kind they were to seventeen white men, or bearded men, as he called them who came on shore there in distress.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他尽力对我讲，他们对那十七个白人——照他的叫法是大胡子人——曾何等友善，那些人是在遇难时上到那里岸上的。

paragraphs.en: From this time, I confess, I had a mind to venture over, and see if I could possibly join with those bearded men, who I made no doubt were Spaniards and Portuguese; not doubting but, if I could, we might find some method to escape from thence, being upon the continent, and a good company together, better than I could from an island forty miles off the shore, alone and without help.
paragraphs.cn: 从这时起，我承认，我起了心思要冒险渡过去，看看能不能设法跟那些大胡子人会合——我毫不怀疑他们是西班牙人和葡萄牙人；我毫不怀疑，只要能会合，我们或许能想出什么法子从那里逃出去，因为身在大陆上、又是一大帮人在一起，总比我孤身一人、无人相助地从离岸四十英里的一座岛上逃出去要强。

paragraphs.en: So, after some days, I took Friday to work again by way of discourse, and told him I would give him a boat to go back to his own nation; and, accordingly, I carried him to my frigate, which lay on the other side of the island, and having cleared it of water (for I always kept it sunk in water), I brought it out, showed it him, and we both went into it.
paragraphs.cn: 于是过了几天，我又借着聊天让星期五干起活来，告诉他我要给他一条船好回他自己的部族去；随即我领他到我那条小艇跟前，它停在岛的另一侧，我把里面的水清干（因为我一向让它沉在水里），把它拖出来，指给他看，我俩都上了船。

paragraphs.en: I found he was a most dexterous fellow at managing it, and would make it go almost as swift again as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 我发现他是个摆弄船的极其灵巧的好手，能让船跑得几乎比我快上一倍。

paragraphs.en: So when he was in, I said to him, “Well, now, Friday, shall we go to your nation?”
paragraphs.cn: 于是他上船后，我对他说：“好啦，星期五，咱们这就去你的部族好吗？”

paragraphs.en: He looked very dull at my saying so; which it seems was because he thought the boat was too small to go so far.
paragraphs.cn: 我这么一说，他神情变得十分沮丧；看来是因为他觉得这船太小，去不了那么远。

paragraphs.en: I then told him I had a bigger; so the next day I went to the place where the first boat lay which I had made, but which I could not get into the water.
paragraphs.cn: 我于是告诉他我有一条更大的；第二天我便去到我先前造的那第一条船停放的地方，那条船我一直没法弄下水。

paragraphs.en: He said that was big enough; but then, as I had taken no care of it, and it had lain two or three and twenty years there, the sun had so split and dried it, that it was rotten.
paragraphs.cn: 他说那条船够大了；可是，由于我一直没照管它，它在那里搁了二十二三年，太阳把它晒得开裂干枯，早已朽烂了。

paragraphs.en: Friday told me such a boat would do very well, and would carry “much enough vittle, drink, bread;” this was his way of talking.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五告诉我，那样一条船会很合用，能装“很够多的食物、饮水、面包”；这就是他说话的样子。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, I was by this time so fixed upon my design of going over with him to the continent that I told him we would go and make one as big as that, and he should go home in it.
paragraphs.cn: 总而言之,这时我一心想着要跟他一起渡海去大陆,便告诉他,我们要去造一条跟那条一样大的船,让他坐着回家去。

paragraphs.en: He answered not one word, but looked very grave and sad.
paragraphs.cn: 他一句话也没答,只是神色凝重,满脸忧伤。

paragraphs.en: I asked him what was the matter with him.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他到底怎么了。

paragraphs.en: He asked me again, “Why you angry mad with Friday?
paragraphs.cn: 他反问我:“你为什么生星期五的气,发那么大火?

paragraphs.en: —what me done?”
paragraphs.cn: ——我做错了什么?”

paragraphs.en: I asked him what he meant.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他这话什么意思。

paragraphs.en: I told him I was not angry with him at all.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他,我一点也没生他的气。

paragraphs.en: “No angry!” says he, repeating the words several times; “why send Friday home away to my nation?”
paragraphs.cn: “没生气!”他把这几个字重复了好几遍,“那为什么要把星期五送回我的部族去?”

paragraphs.en: “Why,” says I, “Friday, did not you say you wished you were there?”
paragraphs.cn: “怎么啦,”我说,“星期五,你不是说过想回到那儿去吗?”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, yes,” says he, “wish we both there; no wish Friday there, no master there.”
paragraphs.cn: “是啊,是啊,”他说,“我想我们俩都在那儿;不想星期五在那儿,主人不在那儿。”

paragraphs.en: In a word, he would not think of going there without me.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,没有我,他压根不肯考虑回去。

paragraphs.en: “I go there, Friday?” says I; “what shall I do there?”
paragraphs.cn: “我去那儿,星期五?”我说,“我去那儿能做什么?”

paragraphs.en: He turned very quick upon me at this.
paragraphs.cn: 他一听这话,猛地转过身来对着我。

paragraphs.en: “You do great deal much good,” says he; “you teach wild mans be good, sober, tame mans; you tell them know God, pray God, and live new life.”
paragraphs.cn: “你能做许许多多好事,”他说,“你教野人做善良、清醒、驯服的人;你教他们认识上帝,向上帝祷告,过全新的生活。”

paragraphs.en: “Alas, Friday!” says I, “thou knowest not what thou sayest; I am but an ignorant man myself.”
paragraphs.cn: “唉,星期五!”我说,“你不知道你在说什么;我自己也不过是个无知的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, yes,” says he, “you teachee me good, you teachee them good.”
paragraphs.cn: “不,不,”他说,“你教我好,你也能教他们好。”

paragraphs.en: “No, no, Friday,” says I, “you shall go without me; leave me here to live by myself, as I did before.”
paragraphs.cn: “不行,不行,星期五,”我说,“你自己去吧,别管我;把我留在这儿,让我像从前一样独自过活。”

paragraphs.en: He looked confused again at that word; and running to one of the hatchets which he used to wear, he takes it up hastily, and gives it to me.
paragraphs.cn: 听到这话,他又露出迷惑的神情;接着他跑向自己惯常佩带的一把短斧,匆匆抓起来,递给了我。

paragraphs.en: “What must I do with this?” says I to him.
paragraphs.cn: “我拿这个做什么?”我问他。

paragraphs.en: “You take kill Friday,” says he.
paragraphs.cn: “你拿去把星期五杀了吧,”他说。

paragraphs.en: “What must I kill you for?” said I again.
paragraphs.cn: “我为什么要杀你?”我又问。

paragraphs.en: He returns very quick—“What you send Friday away for?
paragraphs.cn: 他很快回道——“那你为什么要把星期五赶走?

paragraphs.en: Take kill Friday, no send Friday away.”
paragraphs.cn: 要杀就杀星期五,别把星期五赶走。”

paragraphs.en: This he spoke so earnestly that I saw tears stand in his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 他说这话时那么恳切,我看见泪水在他眼里打转。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I so plainly discovered the utmost affection in him to me, and a firm resolution in him, that I told him then and often after, that I would never send him away from me if he was willing to stay with me.
paragraphs.cn: 总之,我清清楚楚地看出他对我怀着极深的情谊,心意坚定,于是我当时便告诉他,以后也常对他说:只要他愿意留在我身边,我永远不会把他赶走。

paragraphs.en: Upon the whole, as I found by all his discourse a settled affection to me, and that nothing could part him from me, so I found all the foundation of his desire to go to his own country was laid in his ardent affection to the people, and his hopes of my doing them good; a thing which, as I had no notion of myself, so I had not the least thought or intention, or desire of undertaking it.
paragraphs.cn: 总的来说,我从他的一番话里看出他对我情谊笃厚,什么都无法把他从我身边分开;我也明白,他想回故乡的根由,全在于他对族人满腔的挚爱,以及盼着我能造福他们的心愿——而这件事我自己压根没想过,更没有半分承担它的念头、打算或愿望。

paragraphs.en: But still I found a strong inclination to attempting my escape, founded on the supposition gathered from the discourse, that there were seventeen bearded men there; and therefore, without any more delay, I went to work with Friday to find out a great tree proper to fell, and make a large periagua, or canoe, to undertake the voyage.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我心里仍有一股强烈的冲动,想尝试逃离,这念头是从他的话里得来的一个推想:那里有十七个蓄须的人;于是我不再耽搁,便同星期五动手去物色一棵合适的大树,砍倒它,造一条大独木舟,好去完成这趟航行。

paragraphs.en: There were trees enough in the island to have built a little fleet, not of periaguas or canoes, but even of good, large vessels; but the main thing I looked at was, to get one so near the water that we might launch it when it was made, to avoid the mistake I committed at first.
paragraphs.cn: 岛上的树多得足以造一支小船队,而且不是独木舟或小艇,而是像样的大船;但我最看重的一点,是要选一棵离水足够近的,好让船造好后能顺利下水,免得重蹈我起初犯下的那个错误。

paragraphs.en: At last Friday pitched upon a tree; for I found he knew much better than I what kind of wood was fittest for it; nor can I tell to this day what wood to call the tree we cut down, except that it was very like the tree we call fustic, or between that and the Nicaragua wood, for it was much of the same colour and smell.
paragraphs.cn: 最后星期五挑中了一棵树;因为我发现,论哪种木料最合适,他远比我懂得多;直到今天我也说不出我们砍倒的那棵树叫什么木,只知道它很像我们叫做黄颜木的那种,或介于它和尼加拉瓜木之间,因为颜色和气味都相差无几。

paragraphs.en: Friday wished to burn the hollow or cavity of this tree out, to make it for a boat, but I showed him how to cut it with tools; which, after I had showed him how to use, he did very handily; and in about a month’s hard labour we finished it and made it very handsome; especially when, with our axes, which I showed him how to handle, we cut and hewed the outside into the true shape of a boat.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五本想把这树的树心烧空,做成一条船,但我教他用工具去挖凿;经我一番示范,他做得十分灵巧;大约苦干了一个月,我们才完工,把它造得很漂亮;尤其是我们用斧头——我教过他怎么使——把外面砍削成了真正的船形。

paragraphs.en: After this, however, it cost us near a fortnight’s time to get her along, as it were inch by inch, upon great rollers into the water; but when she was in, she would have carried twenty men with great ease.
paragraphs.cn: 可是在这之后,我们又花了将近半个月的工夫,才把它一寸一寸地架在大滚木上挪进水里;不过它一下水,轻轻松松就能载得下二十个人。

paragraphs.en: When she was in the water, though she was so big, it amazed me to see with what dexterity and how swift my man Friday could manage her, turn her, and paddle her along.
paragraphs.cn: 它虽然那么大,可一下到水里,我那仆人星期五驾驭它、掉转它、划着它前行时那份灵巧和迅捷,着实叫我惊叹。

paragraphs.en: So I asked him if he would, and if we might venture over in her.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我问他,愿不愿意、我们能不能乘它渡海过去。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” he said, “we venture over in her very well, though great blow wind.”
paragraphs.cn: “愿意,”他说,“我们乘它渡海很稳当,就算刮大风也不怕。”

paragraphs.en: However I had a further design that he knew nothing of, and that was, to make a mast and a sail, and to fit her with an anchor and cable.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我还有一个他毫不知情的打算,那就是给船做一根桅杆和一张帆,再配上锚和缆绳。

paragraphs.en: As to a mast, that was easy enough to get; so I pitched upon a straight young cedar-tree, which I found near the place, and which there were great plenty of in the island, and I set Friday to work to cut it down, and gave him directions how to shape and order it.
paragraphs.cn: 至于桅杆,那倒容易得手;于是我在附近选中了一棵笔直的小雪松——这种树岛上多得很——叫星期五去把它砍倒,教他怎么削制、怎么安置。

paragraphs.en: But as to the sail, that was my particular care.
paragraphs.cn: 但说到那张帆,那可是我特别费心的事。

paragraphs.en: I knew I had old sails, or rather pieces of old sails, enough; but as I had had them now six-and-twenty years by me, and had not been very careful to preserve them, not imagining that I should ever have this kind of use for them, I did not doubt but they were all rotten; and, indeed, most of them were so.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道自己有旧帆,或者说旧帆的碎片,数量足够;可这些帆在我手里已放了二十六年,我又没怎么细心保存,压根没料到会派上这种用场,料想它们准都烂了;事实上,大半确实如此。

paragraphs.en: However, I found two pieces which appeared pretty good, and with these I went to work; and with a great deal of pains, and awkward stitching, you may be sure, for want of needles, I at length made a three-cornered ugly thing, like what we call in England a shoulder-of-mutton sail, to go with a boom at bottom, and a little short sprit at the top, such as usually our ships’ long-boats sail with, and such as I best knew how to manage, as it was such a one as I had to the boat in which I made my escape from Barbary, as related in the first part of my story.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我找到了两块看上去还挺好的,便动手做起来;你尽可想见,因为缺针,我费了好大的劲,笨手笨脚地缝了半天,总算做成了一个三角形的丑东西,像我们英国人叫做“羊肩帆”的那种,底下带一根横杆,顶上有一根短短的斜桁,通常是我们船上的大艇挂的那种帆,也是我最会摆弄的一种,因为当年我从巴巴里逃走时所乘的那条船上,用的就是这样一张帆,这在我故事的头一部分里讲过。

paragraphs.en: I was near two months performing this last work, viz. rigging and fitting my masts and sails; for I finished them very complete, making a small stay, and a sail, or foresail, to it, to assist if we should turn to windward; and, what was more than all, I fixed a rudder to the stern of her to steer with.
paragraphs.cn: 我做这最后一项活计——也就是装配桅杆和帆——花了将近两个月;我把它们做得十分完备,又添了一根小小的支索和一张前帆,好在我们需要抢风向时助一臂之力;而尤其难得的是,我还在船尾装了一个舵,好用来掌舵。

paragraphs.en: I was but a bungling shipwright, yet as I knew the usefulness and even necessity of such a thing, I applied myself with so much pains to do it, that at last I brought it to pass; though, considering the many dull contrivances I had for it that failed, I think it cost me almost as much labour as making the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我不过是个蹩脚的造船匠,但我知道这东西何等有用、甚至不可或缺,便下了极大的功夫去做,终于把它弄成了;不过想想我为它捣鼓出那么多笨拙又失败的花样,我觉得它耗去的力气几乎不亚于造那条船。

paragraphs.en: After all this was done, I had my man Friday to teach as to what belonged to the navigation of my boat; though he knew very well how to paddle a canoe, he knew nothing of what belonged to a sail and a rudder; and was the most amazed when he saw me work the boat to and again in the sea by the rudder, and how the sail jibed, and filled this way or that way as the course we sailed changed; I say when he saw this he stood like one astonished and amazed.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切完工之后,我还得教我的仆人星期五驾船的种种门道;他虽然很会划独木舟,却对帆和舵一窍不通;当他看见我用舵操纵船在海上来回行驶,看见帆随着我们航向的改变或这边或那边地转向、鼓满时,他惊愕到了极点;我是说,他看到这情景时,像个惊呆了的人一样呆立着。

paragraphs.en: However, with a little use, I made all these things familiar to him, and he became an expert sailor, except that of the compass I could make him understand very little.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,稍加练习,我便让他对这些都熟悉起来,他成了个熟练的水手,只有罗盘那一样,我怎么也没法叫他弄懂多少。

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, as there was very little cloudy weather, and seldom or never any fogs in those parts, there was the less occasion for a compass, seeing the stars were always to be seen by night, and the shore by day, except in the rainy seasons, and then nobody cared to stir abroad either by land or sea.
paragraphs.cn: 另一方面,由于那一带很少有阴天,几乎从来没有雾,罗盘也就不那么用得着,因为夜里总能看见星星,白天看得见海岸,唯有雨季例外,而那时候谁也不愿在陆上或海上走动。

paragraphs.en: I was now entered on the seven-and-twentieth year of my captivity in this place; though the three last years that I had this creature with me ought rather to be left out of the account, my habitation being quite of another kind than in all the rest of the time.
paragraphs.cn: 我如今已进入被困在这地方的第二十七个年头;不过最后这三年,有了这个人做伴,倒真该从账里除去,因为这段日子里我的生活跟其余时候大不相同。

paragraphs.en: I kept the anniversary of my landing here with the same thankfulness to God for His mercies as at first: and if I had such cause of acknowledgment at first, I had much more so now, having such additional testimonies of the care of Providence over me, and the great hopes I had of being effectually and speedily delivered; for I had an invincible impression upon my thoughts that my deliverance was at hand, and that I should not be another year in this place.
paragraphs.cn: 我像最初一样,怀着对上帝仁慈的同样感激,过着自己登陆这里的周年纪念日:如果说起初我就有理由感恩,那么此刻我更该如此,因为我又多了这些天意眷顾我的凭证,以及我满怀的、即将迅速而切实获救的大希望;因为我心头有一种无法抗拒的感觉,觉得获救就在眼前,我在这地方待不满一年了。

paragraphs.en: I went on, however, with my husbandry; digging, planting, and fencing as usual.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,我照旧忙我的农事:照常挖地、种植、围篱笆。

paragraphs.en: I gathered and cured my grapes, and did every necessary thing as before.
paragraphs.cn: 我采摘葡萄,把它们晾成葡萄干,像从前一样把该做的每一样事都做了。

paragraphs.en: The rainy season was in the meantime upon me, when I kept more within doors than at other times.
paragraphs.cn: 这期间雨季到了,那时候我比平时更多地待在屋里。

paragraphs.en: We had stowed our new vessel as secure as we could, bringing her up into the creek, where, as I said in the beginning, I landed my rafts from the ship; and hauling her up to the shore at high-water mark, I made my man Friday dig a little dock, just big enough to hold her, and just deep enough to give her water enough to float in; and then, when the tide was out, we made a strong dam across the end of it, to keep the water out; and so she lay, dry as to the tide from the sea: and to keep the rain off we laid a great many boughs of trees, so thick that she was as well thatched as a house; and thus we waited for the months of November and December, in which I designed to make my adventure.
paragraphs.cn: 我们把新造的船尽可能稳妥地藏了起来,把它撑进那条小河汊里——就是我一开头说过、我从大船上把木筏运上岸的地方;趁涨潮把它拖到高潮线的岸边,我又叫仆人星期五挖了一个小小的船坞,大小刚够容下它,深浅刚够让它浮起来;然后趁退潮,我们在坞口筑了一道结实的堤坝,把海水挡在外面;这样它就搁在那儿,不受海潮浸泡,干干爽爽的;为了遮雨,我们又铺上许许多多树枝,厚得像给房子盖了顶棚;就这样,我们等着十一月和十二月的到来,我打算在那时候去冒这趟险。

paragraphs.en: When the settled season began to come in, as the thought of my design returned with the fair weather, I was preparing daily for the voyage.
paragraphs.cn: 当稳定的季节开始到来,随着晴好天气我那计划的念头也重新回到心头,我便一天天地为这趟航行做起准备。

paragraphs.en: And the first thing I did was to lay by a certain quantity of provisions, being the stores for our voyage; and intended in a week or a fortnight’s time to open the dock, and launch out our boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我做的头一件事,就是备下一定数量的食物,作为我们这趟航行的储备;打算在一两个星期之内打开船坞,把我们的船放下水去。

paragraphs.en: I was busy one morning upon something of this kind, when I called to Friday, and bid him to go to the sea-shore and see if he could find a turtle or a tortoise, a thing which we generally got once a week, for the sake of the eggs as well as the flesh.
paragraphs.cn: 一天早上我正忙着这类事情,便唤来星期五,叫他到海边去看看能不能找到海龟或乌龟——这东西我们一般每星期都能弄到一只,既为了肉,也为了蛋。

paragraphs.en: Friday had not been long gone when he came running back, and flew over my outer wall or fence, like one that felt not the ground or the steps he set his foot on; and before I had time to speak to him he cries out to me, “O master!
paragraphs.cn: 星期五去了没多久便跑了回来,像脚下感觉不到地面、感觉不到落脚的台阶似的,一下子飞越过我那道外墙或围栏;我还没来得及跟他说话,他就冲我喊道:“哦,主人!

paragraphs.en: O master!
paragraphs.cn: 哦,主人!

paragraphs.en: O sorrow!
paragraphs.cn: 哦,糟啦!

paragraphs.en: O bad!”
paragraphs.cn: 哦,不好啦!”

paragraphs.en: —“What’s the matter, Friday?” says I.
paragraphs.cn: ——“怎么回事,星期五?”我问。

paragraphs.en: “O yonder there,” says he, “one, two, three canoes; one, two, three!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦,那边,”他说,“一、二、三条独木舟;一、二、三!”

paragraphs.en: By this way of speaking I concluded there were six; but on inquiry I found there were but three.
paragraphs.cn: 照他这种说法,我断定来了六条;可一打听才知道只有三条。

paragraphs.en: “Well, Friday,” says I, “do not be frightened.”
paragraphs.cn: “好啦,星期五,”我说,“别害怕。”

paragraphs.en: So I heartened him up as well as I could.
paragraphs.cn: 我便尽力给他鼓劲。

paragraphs.en: However, I saw the poor fellow was most terribly scared, for nothing ran in his head but that they were come to look for him, and would cut him in pieces and eat him; and the poor fellow trembled so that I scarcely knew what to do with him.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我看这可怜的家伙吓得魂飞魄散,因为他脑子里只有一个念头,就是他们是来找他的,要把他碎尸万段吃掉;这可怜人抖得那么厉害,我简直不知该拿他怎么办才好。

paragraphs.en: I comforted him as well as I could, and told him I was in as much danger as he, and that they would eat me as well as him.
paragraphs.cn: 我尽力安慰他,告诉他我和他一样身处险境,他们既会吃他,也一样会吃我。

paragraphs.en: “But,” says I, “Friday, we must resolve to fight them.
paragraphs.cn: “可是,”我说,“星期五,我们必须下定决心跟他们拼。

paragraphs.en: Can you fight, Friday?”
paragraphs.cn: 你能打仗吗,星期五?”

paragraphs.en: “Me shoot,” says he, “but there come many great number.”
paragraphs.cn: “我会放枪,”他说,“可是来了好多好多人。”

paragraphs.en: “No matter for that,” said I again; “our guns will fright them that we do not kill.”
paragraphs.cn: “那没关系,”我又说,“没被打死的,也会被我们的枪吓跑。”

paragraphs.en: So I asked him whether, if I resolved to defend him, he would defend me, and stand by me, and do just as I bid him.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我问他,要是我决意保护他,他肯不肯保护我、守在我身边、一切都听我的吩咐。

paragraphs.en: He said, “Me die when you bid die, master.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“你叫死我就死,主人。”

paragraphs.en: So I went and fetched a good dram of rum and gave him; for I had been so good a husband of my rum that I had a great deal left.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我去取来满满一大杯朗姆酒给他;因为我一向精打细算地用我的朗姆酒,所以还剩下不少。

paragraphs.en: When we had drunk it, I made him take the two fowling-pieces, which we always carried, and loaded them with large swan-shot, as big as small pistol-bullets.
paragraphs.cn: 我们喝完酒,我叫他拿起我们一向随身携带的那两支鸟枪,给它们装上大号的天鹅弹,弹丸有小手枪子弹那么大。

paragraphs.en: Then I took four muskets, and loaded them with two slugs and five small bullets each; and my two pistols I loaded with a brace of bullets each.
paragraphs.cn: 然后我拿起四支火枪,每支装了两颗粗弹和五颗小弹;我那两支手枪则每支装了两颗子弹。

paragraphs.en: I hung my great sword, as usual, naked by my side, and gave Friday his hatchet.
paragraphs.cn: 我照旧把我那把大剑光着挂在腰边,又把短斧交给了星期五。

paragraphs.en: When I had thus prepared myself, I took my perspective glass, and went up to the side of the hill, to see what I could discover; and I found quickly by my glass that there were one-and-twenty savages, three prisoners, and three canoes; and that their whole business seemed to be the triumphant banquet upon these three human bodies: a barbarous feast, indeed! but nothing more than, as I had observed, was usual with them.
paragraphs.cn: 这样武装停当后,我拿起望远镜,登上山坡去看看能瞧见些什么;很快就借着望远镜发现,那里有二十一个野人、三个俘虏、三条独木舟;他们要办的事,似乎全是要拿这三具人的躯体大摆一场得胜的盛宴:真是一场野蛮的筵席!不过,照我所观察到的,这在他们中间也是常事罢了。

paragraphs.en: I observed also that they had landed, not where they had done when Friday made his escape, but nearer to my creek, where the shore was low, and where a thick wood came almost close down to the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我还注意到,他们登陆的地方不是星期五逃走时的那处,而是更靠近我那河汊的地方,那里岸势低平,一片密林几乎一直伸到海边。

paragraphs.en: This, with the abhorrence of the inhuman errand these wretches came about, filled me with such indignation that I came down again to Friday, and told him I was resolved to go down to them and kill them all; and asked him if he would stand by me.
paragraphs.cn: 这一点,加上我对这些恶徒此行那残忍勾当的深恶痛绝,叫我心中充满义愤,便又下山回到星期五那儿,告诉他我决意冲下去把他们统统杀掉;并问他肯不肯助我一臂之力。

paragraphs.en: He had now got over his fright, and his spirits being a little raised with the dram I had given him, he was very cheerful, and told me, as before, he would die when I bid die.
paragraphs.cn: 这会儿他已从惊恐中缓过神来,加上我给他的那杯酒使他精神略振,便十分振奋,像先前一样对我说:你叫死我就死。

paragraphs.en: In this fit of fury I divided the arms which I had charged, as before, between us; I gave Friday one pistol to stick in his girdle, and three guns upon his shoulder, and I took one pistol and the other three guns myself; and in this posture we marched out.
paragraphs.cn: 在这股怒火中,我把先前装好的武器像上次那样在我们俩之间分了分:我给星期五一支手枪插在腰带上,三支枪扛在肩头,我自己拿一支手枪和另外三支枪;就这样一副架势,我们出发了。

paragraphs.en: I took a small bottle of rum in my pocket, and gave Friday a large bag with more powder and bullets; and as to orders, I charged him to keep close behind me, and not to stir, or shoot, or do anything till I bid him, and in the meantime not to speak a word.
paragraphs.cn: 我在口袋里揣了一小瓶朗姆酒,又给了星期五一个大袋子,里面装着更多的火药和子弹;至于命令,我嘱咐他紧跟在我身后,不许乱动、不许放枪、不许做任何事,除非我吩咐,同时一句话也不许说。

paragraphs.en: In this posture I fetched a compass to my right hand of near a mile, as well to get over the creek as to get into the wood, so that I could come within shot of them before I should be discovered, which I had seen by my glass it was easy to do.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我向右手边绕了近一英里的一个大弯,既为了绕过那条河汊,也为了钻进树林,好让我在被发觉之前就能进入射程之内;我借望远镜看过,这样做很容易。

paragraphs.en: While I was making this march, my former thoughts returning, I began to abate my resolution: I do not mean that I entertained any fear of their number, for as they were naked, unarmed wretches, it is certain I was superior to them—nay, though I had been alone.
paragraphs.cn: 就在我这样行进时,先前那些念头又回到心头,我的决心开始动摇:我并不是说我惧怕他们人多,因为他们不过是些赤身裸体、手无寸铁的可怜人,我肯定比他们强——不,就算只有我一个人也一样。

paragraphs.en: But it occurred to my thoughts, what call, what occasion, much less what necessity I was in to go and dip my hands in blood, to attack people who had neither done or intended me any wrong? who, as to me, were innocent, and whose barbarous customs were their own disaster, being in them a token, indeed, of God’s having left them, with the other nations of that part of the world, to such stupidity, and to such inhuman courses, but did not call me to take upon me to be a judge of their actions, much less an executioner of His justice—that whenever He thought fit He would take the cause into His own hands, and by national vengeance punish them as a people for national crimes, but that, in the meantime, it was none of my business—that it was true Friday might justify it, because he was a declared enemy and in a state of war with those very particular people, and it was lawful for him to attack them—but I could not say the same with regard to myself.
paragraphs.cn: 可是我心里转起一个念头:我究竟受了什么召唤、有什么缘由,更谈不上有什么必要,要去把手浸在血里,去攻击这些既没有伤害过我、也无意伤害我的人?他们对我来说是无辜的,他们那野蛮的习俗是他们自己的不幸,那诚然是个记号,表明上帝已抛下他们,连同那一带世上别的部族,任由他们陷入这般愚昧、这般惨无人道的行径,但这并不召唤我去充当审判他们行为的法官,更不是要我做执行上帝公义的刽子手——每当上帝认为合宜,他自会把此事亲手了断,以举国之罚惩治他们这个民族所犯下的举国之罪;可眼下这与我毫不相干——诚然,星期五动手倒说得过去,因为他是这些人公开的仇敌,与他们正处于交战状态,由他去攻击他们是合乎情理的——但换作我自己,却不能这么说。

paragraphs.en: These things were so warmly pressed upon my thoughts all the way as I went, that I resolved I would only go and place myself near them that I might observe their barbarous feast, and that I would act then as God should direct; but that unless something offered that was more a call to me than yet I knew of, I would not meddle with them.
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头一路上那么热切地压在我心头,以致我打定主意,只走过去在他们附近找个地方藏身,好观察他们那野蛮的筵席,然后照上帝的指引行事;除非出现什么比我眼下所知更能召唤我的事,否则我决不去招惹他们。

paragraphs.en: With this resolution I entered the wood, and, with all possible wariness and silence, Friday following close at my heels, I marched till I came to the skirts of the wood on the side which was next to them, only that one corner of the wood lay between me and them.
paragraphs.cn: 抱着这个主意,我钻进树林,尽可能小心翼翼、悄无声息,星期五紧随我脚后,一直走到靠他们那一侧的林边,只剩树林的一个角落横在我和他们之间。

paragraphs.en: Here I called softly to Friday, and showing him a great tree which was just at the corner of the wood, I bade him go to the tree, and bring me word if he could see there plainly what they were doing.
paragraphs.cn: 到了这儿,我轻声唤星期五,指着正在林角上的一棵大树,叫他走到树那儿,若能清楚看见他们在干什么,就回来告诉我。

paragraphs.en: He did so, and came immediately back to me, and told me they might be plainly viewed there—that they were all about their fire, eating the flesh of one of their prisoners, and that another lay bound upon the sand a little from them, whom he said they would kill next; and this fired the very soul within me.
paragraphs.cn: 他照办了,立刻回到我身边,告诉我在那儿能看得清清楚楚——他们全围在火堆旁,吃着一个俘虏的肉,另一个俘虏被绑着躺在离他们不远的沙地上,他说他们接下来就要杀那个人;这话把我心里的一腔怒火点燃了。

paragraphs.en: He told me it was not one of their nation, but one of the bearded men he had told me of, that came to their country in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我,那人不是他们本族的,而是他先前跟我说过的那种蓄须人中的一个,是乘船来到他们国土上的。

paragraphs.en: I was filled with horror at the very naming of the white bearded man; and going to the tree, I saw plainly by my glass a white man, who lay upon the beach of the sea with his hands and his feet tied with flags, or things like rushes, and that he was an European, and had clothes on.
paragraphs.cn: 一听到“白胡子人”这几个字,我心里满是恐惧;走到那棵树那儿,借着望远镜清清楚楚看见一个白人,他躺在海滩上,手脚被草绳或类似灯芯草的东西捆着,而且是个欧洲人,身上穿着衣服。

paragraphs.en: There was another tree and a little thicket beyond it, about fifty yards nearer to them than the place where I was, which, by going a little way about, I saw I might come at undiscovered, and that then I should be within half a shot of them; so I withheld my passion, though I was indeed enraged to the highest degree; and going back about twenty paces, I got behind some bushes, which held all the way till I came to the other tree, and then came to a little rising ground, which gave me a full view of them at the distance of about eighty yards.
paragraphs.cn: 再往前另有一棵树和一小片矮树丛,比我所在的地方离他们近约五十码;我看出只要稍稍绕点路,就能不被发觉地摸到那儿,到那时我便离他们不到半个射程了;于是我按捺住怒火,虽说我确实已被激怒到了极点;我退回约二十步,躲到一些灌木后面,那灌木一路遮掩着,直到我来到那另一棵树跟前,又走到一小块高地上,从这儿在约八十码开外把他们尽收眼底。

paragraphs.en: I had now not a moment to lose, for nineteen of the dreadful wretches sat upon the ground, all close huddled together, and had just sent the other two to butcher the poor Christian, and bring him perhaps limb by limb to their fire, and they were stooping down to untie the bands at his feet.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我一刻也不能耽搁了,因为那十九个可怕的恶徒挤作一堆坐在地上,刚打发另外两个去屠宰那可怜的基督徒,大概要把他一块块肢解了拖到火堆边去,那两人正弯下身去解他脚上的绳索。

paragraphs.en: I turned to Friday.
paragraphs.cn: 我转向星期五。

paragraphs.en: “Now, Friday,” said I, “do as I bid thee.”
paragraphs.cn: “听着,星期五,”我说,“照我吩咐的做。”

paragraphs.en: Friday said he would.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五说他一定照办。

paragraphs.en: “Then, Friday,” says I, “do exactly as you see me do; fail in nothing.”
paragraphs.cn: “那么,星期五,”我说,“你看我怎么做就一模一样地做;一样都不许错。”

paragraphs.en: So I set down one of the muskets and the fowling-piece upon the ground, and Friday did the like by his, and with the other musket I took my aim at the savages, bidding him to do the like; then asking him if he was ready, he said, “Yes.”
paragraphs.cn: 于是我把一支火枪和那支鸟枪放在地上,星期五也照样把他的放下,我用另一支火枪瞄准那些野人,叫他也照样做;然后问他准备好没有,他说:“好了。”

paragraphs.en: “Then fire at them,” said I; and at the same moment I fired also.
paragraphs.cn: “那就朝他们开枪,”我说;与此同时我也开了火。

paragraphs.en: Friday took his aim so much better than I, that on the side that he shot he killed two of them, and wounded three more; and on my side I killed one, and wounded two.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五瞄得比我准多了,他打的那一边,他打死了两个,又打伤了三个;我这一边,我打死一个,打伤两个。

paragraphs.en: They were, you may be sure, in a dreadful consternation: and all of them that were not hurt jumped upon their feet, but did not immediately know which way to run, or which way to look, for they knew not from whence their destruction came.
paragraphs.cn: 你尽可想见,他们惊骇万状:没受伤的全跳起身来,却一时不知该往哪儿逃、往哪儿看,因为他们弄不清这场灭顶之灾是从何而来的。

paragraphs.en: Friday kept his eyes close upon me, that, as I had bid him, he might observe what I did; so, as soon as the first shot was made, I threw down the piece, and took up the fowling-piece, and Friday did the like; he saw me cock and present; he did the same again.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五两眼紧盯着我,好照我吩咐的那样看我怎么做;于是,第一枪一放,我就扔下那支枪,抄起鸟枪,星期五也照样做;他见我扳起击锤、端平枪口,便又同样做了一遍。

paragraphs.en: “Are you ready, Friday?” said I.
paragraphs.cn: “准备好了吗,星期五?”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” says he.
paragraphs.cn: “好了,”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Let fly, then,” says I, “in the name of God!” and with that I fired again among the amazed wretches, and so did Friday; and as our pieces were now loaded with what I call swan-shot, or small pistol-bullets, we found only two drop; but so many were wounded that they ran about yelling and screaming like mad creatures, all bloody, and most of them miserably wounded; whereof three more fell quickly after, though not quite dead.
paragraphs.cn: “那就开火吧,”我说,“奉上帝之名!”说着我又朝那群惊呆的恶徒开了枪,星期五也开了枪;因为我们这会儿装的是我所谓的天鹅弹或小手枪子弹,只见倒下两个;可是许多人都挂了彩,浑身是血,大半伤得很重,一个个像疯了似的乱窜,又叫又嚎;其中又有三个很快倒了下去,不过还没断气。

paragraphs.en: “Now, Friday,” says I, laying down the discharged pieces, and taking up the musket which was yet loaded, “follow me,” which he did with a great deal of courage; upon which I rushed out of the wood and showed myself, and Friday close at my foot.
paragraphs.cn: “听着,星期五,”我说着,放下打空的枪,抄起那支还上着膛的火枪,“跟我来,”他鼓足勇气跟了上来;于是我冲出树林,现出身来,星期五紧跟在我脚边。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I perceived they saw me, I shouted as loud as I could, and bade Friday do so too, and running as fast as I could, which, by the way, was not very fast, being loaded with arms as I was, I made directly towards the poor victim, who was, as I said, lying upon the beach or shore, between the place where they sat and the sea.
paragraphs.cn: 我一发觉他们看见了我,便使出全力大喊,叫星期五也这样喊,然后拼命往前跑——顺带一提,我跑得并不很快,因为身上负着那么多武器——径直朝那可怜的牺牲者冲去,他正如我所说,躺在海滩或岸边,在他们坐的地方和海之间。

paragraphs.en: The two butchers who were just going to work with him had left him at the surprise of our first fire, and fled in a terrible fright to the seaside, and had jumped into a canoe, and three more of the rest made the same way.
paragraphs.cn: 那两个正要动手宰他的屠夫,在我们头一排枪响时大惊之下把他丢下,惊恐万状地逃向海边,跳进了一条独木舟,另外三个也朝同一个方向逃去。

paragraphs.en: I turned to Friday, and bade him step forwards and fire at them; he understood me immediately, and running about forty yards, to be nearer them, he shot at them; and I thought he had killed them all, for I saw them all fall of a heap into the boat, though I saw two of them up again quickly; however, he killed two of them, and wounded the third, so that he lay down in the bottom of the boat as if he had been dead.
paragraphs.cn: 我转向星期五,叫他上前朝他们开枪;他立刻会意,跑出约四十码,好离他们近些,便朝他们开了火;我以为他把他们全打死了,因为我看见他们一齐倒进了船里,不过我很快又看见其中两个爬了起来;总之,他打死了两个,打伤了第三个,那人便躺倒在船底,像是死了一样。

paragraphs.en: While my man Friday fired at them, I pulled out my knife and cut the flags that bound the poor victim; and loosing his hands and feet, I lifted him up, and asked him in the Portuguese tongue what he was.
paragraphs.cn: 我那仆人星期五朝他们开枪时,我抽出小刀割断捆着那可怜牺牲者的草绳;松开他的手脚后,我把他扶起来,用葡萄牙语问他是什么人。

paragraphs.en: He answered in Latin, Christianus; but was so weak and faint that he could scarce stand or speak.
paragraphs.cn: 他用拉丁语答道:Christianus(基督徒);可他虚弱疲乏得几乎站不住、说不出话。

paragraphs.en: I took my bottle out of my pocket and gave it him, making signs that he should drink, which he did; and I gave him a piece of bread, which he ate.
paragraphs.cn: 我从口袋里掏出酒瓶递给他,打手势叫他喝,他喝了;我又给他一块面包,他吃了。

paragraphs.en: Then I asked him what countryman he was: and he said, Espagniole; and being a little recovered, let me know, by all the signs he could possibly make, how much he was in my debt for his deliverance.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我问他是哪国人:他说,Espagniole(西班牙人);略略缓过神后,他用尽一切可能的手势让我明白,他为自己获救而对我感恩不尽。

paragraphs.en: “Seignior,” said I, with as much Spanish as I could make up, “we will talk afterwards, but we must fight now: if you have any strength left, take this pistol and sword, and lay about you.”
paragraphs.cn: “先生,”我用尽我所会的西班牙语说道,“我们回头再谈,可眼下必须打仗:你要是还有一点力气,就拿上这支手枪和这把剑,放手厮杀吧。”

paragraphs.en: He took them very thankfully; and no sooner had he the arms in his hands, but, as if they had put new vigour into him, he flew upon his murderers like a fury, and had cut two of them in pieces in an instant; for the truth is, as the whole was a surprise to them, so the poor creatures were so much frightened with the noise of our pieces that they fell down for mere amazement and fear, and had no more power to attempt their own escape than their flesh had to resist our shot; and that was the case of those five that Friday shot at in the boat; for as three of them fell with the hurt they received, so the other two fell with the fright.
paragraphs.cn: 他万分感激地接了过去;武器一到手,仿佛给他注入了新的活力,他像发狂似的扑向那些杀他的人,顷刻间就把其中两个砍成了几段;因为说实话,这一切对他们来说全是猝不及防,那些可怜虫被我们枪声吓得魂不附体,只因惊骇恐惧就瘫倒在地,再没有力气去谋求自己逃命,正如他们的血肉挡不住我们的子弹一样;星期五在船上打的那五个也是如此:三个是因中弹倒下,另外两个则是因惊吓而倒。

paragraphs.en: I kept my piece in my hand still without firing, being willing to keep my charge ready, because I had given the Spaniard my pistol and sword: so I called to Friday, and bade him run up to the tree from whence we first fired, and fetch the arms which lay there that had been discharged, which he did with great swiftness; and then giving him my musket, I sat down myself to load all the rest again, and bade them come to me when they wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 我仍把枪握在手里没有开火,想留着这一膛弹药备用,因为我已把手枪和剑给了那西班牙人:于是我唤星期五,叫他跑到我们最初开枪的那棵树跟前,把撂在那儿、已经打空的枪都取来,他飞快地照办了;然后我把火枪交给他,自己坐下来重新给其余所有的枪装弹,叫他们需要枪时就来找我。

paragraphs.en: While I was loading these pieces, there happened a fierce engagement between the Spaniard and one of the savages, who made at him with one of their great wooden swords, the weapon that was to have killed him before, if I had not prevented it.
paragraphs.cn: 我正装着这些枪,那西班牙人和一个野人之间爆发了一场恶斗,那野人挥着一把他们的大木刀朝他扑来,先前若不是我阻止,正是这件家伙要了他的命。

paragraphs.en: The Spaniard, who was as bold and brave as could be imagined, though weak, had fought the Indian a good while, and had cut two great wounds on his head; but the savage being a stout, lusty fellow, closing in with him, had thrown him down, being faint, and was wringing my sword out of his hand; when the Spaniard, though undermost, wisely quitting the sword, drew the pistol from his girdle, shot the savage through the body, and killed him upon the spot, before I, who was running to help him, could come near him.
paragraphs.cn: 那西班牙人虽说虚弱,却勇猛无比,与那印第安人搏斗了好一阵,在他头上砍出两道大伤口;可那野人是个粗壮结实的家伙,贴身扑上来,把已经力竭的西班牙人掀翻在地,正要从他手里夺过我那把剑;就在这千钧一发之际,西班牙人虽被压在下面,却机敏地放开剑,从腰带里拔出手枪,一枪穿透了那野人的身子,当场把他打死,我正跑去救他,还没来得及赶到跟前。

paragraphs.en: Friday, being now left to his liberty, pursued the flying wretches, with no weapon in his hand but his hatchet: and with that he despatched those three who as I said before, were wounded at first, and fallen, and all the rest he could come up with: and the Spaniard coming to me for a gun, I gave him one of the fowling-pieces, with which he pursued two of the savages, and wounded them both; but as he was not able to run, they both got from him into the wood, where Friday pursued them, and killed one of them, but the other was too nimble for him; and though he was wounded, yet had plunged himself into the sea, and swam with all his might off to those two who were left in the canoe; which three in the canoe, with one wounded, that we knew not whether he died or no, were all that escaped our hands of one-and-twenty.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五这会儿脱开了身,便去追赶那些逃窜的恶徒,手里除了短斧别无兵器:他就用这斧头结果了先前我说过、起初受伤倒下的那三个,以及一切他追得上的人:那西班牙人跑来向我要枪,我给了他一支鸟枪,他拿着追赶两个野人,把两人都打伤了;但因为他跑不动,那两人都逃进林子躲开了他,星期五便在林中追上去,打死了一个,可另一个太过灵活;那人虽已受伤,却纵身跳进海里,拼命朝独木舟上剩下的那两个人游去;这独木舟里的三个人,连同一个我们不知是死是活的伤者,便是那二十一人中逃出我们手心的全部了。

paragraphs.en: The account of the whole is as follows: Three killed at our first shot from the tree; two killed at the next shot; two killed by Friday in the boat; two killed by Friday of those at first wounded; one killed by Friday in the wood; three killed by the Spaniard; four killed, being found dropped here and there, of the wounds, or killed by Friday in his chase of them; four escaped in the boat, whereof one wounded, if not dead—twenty-one in all.
paragraphs.cn: 整个情形算起来如下:头一枪从树后打死三个;第二枪打死两个;星期五在船上打死两个;星期五又结果了起初受伤的两个;星期五在林中打死一个;西班牙人打死三个;还有四个,是零零落落被发现的,或死于枪伤,或在星期五追击时被他打死;四个乘船逃脱,其中一个受了伤,兴许已死——总共二十一人。

paragraphs.en: Those that were in the canoe worked hard to get out of gun-shot, and though Friday made two or three shots at them, I did not find that he hit any of them.
paragraphs.cn: 独木舟里那几个拼命划桨,想划出枪程之外,尽管星期五朝他们放了两三枪,可我没看出他打中了哪一个。

paragraphs.en: Friday would fain have had me take one of their canoes, and pursue them; and indeed I was very anxious about their escape, lest, carrying the news home to their people, they should come back perhaps with two or three hundred of the canoes and devour us by mere multitude; so I consented to pursue them by sea, and running to one of their canoes, I jumped in and bade Friday follow me: but when I was in the canoe I was surprised to find another poor creature lie there, bound hand and foot, as the Spaniard was, for the slaughter, and almost dead with fear, not knowing what was the matter; for he had not been able to look up over the side of the boat, he was tied so hard neck and heels, and had been tied so long that he had really but little life in him.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五巴不得我乘上他们一条独木舟去追;说实话,他们的逃脱也叫我十分忧心,生怕他们把消息带回族里,兴许会带着两三百条独木舟卷土重来,单凭人多把我们吞掉;于是我答应从海上追击,便跑向他们的一条独木舟,跳了进去,叫星期五跟上我:可是等我上了船,却惊讶地发现里面还躺着一个可怜人,像那西班牙人一样被捆得手脚牢牢的,准备待宰,吓得几乎断了气,还不知道是怎么回事;因为他被绑得脖子和脚跟死死的,根本没法从船舷上探头张望,又被捆了那么久,身上其实已所剩无几生气了。

paragraphs.en: I immediately cut the twisted flags or rushes which they had bound him with, and would have helped him up; but he could not stand or speak, but groaned most piteously, believing, it seems, still, that he was only unbound in order to be killed.
paragraphs.cn: 我立刻割断他们捆他用的那些拧成一股的草绳或灯芯草,想扶他起来;可他既站不住也说不出话,只是最凄惨地呻吟着,看样子他仍以为给他松绑只是为了杀他。

paragraphs.en: When Friday came to him I bade him speak to him, and tell him of his deliverance; and pulling out my bottle, made him give the poor wretch a dram, which, with the news of his being delivered, revived him, and he sat up in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五走到他跟前时,我叫他跟那人说话,告诉他已经获救;又掏出我的酒瓶,让星期五给那可怜人灌了一口酒,这口酒连同获救的消息使他缓过神来,他在船里坐了起来。

paragraphs.en: But when Friday came to hear him speak, and look in his face, it would have moved any one to tears to have seen how Friday kissed him, embraced him, hugged him, cried, laughed, hallooed, jumped about, danced, sang; then cried again, wrung his hands, beat his own face and head; and then sang and jumped about again like a distracted creature.
paragraphs.cn: 可是当星期五走近去听他说话、看清他的脸时,那情景足以叫任何人落泪——只见星期五又亲又抱地搂着他,又哭又笑,又喊又叫,又蹦又跳,又跳舞又唱歌;接着又哭起来,绞着双手,捶自己的脸和头;然后又像个疯癫了的人一样唱起歌、蹦跳起来。

paragraphs.en: It was a good while before I could make him speak to me or tell me what was the matter; but when he came a little to himself he told me that it was his father.
paragraphs.cn: 过了好一阵子,我才让他肯跟我说话、告诉我怎么回事;可等他略略回过神来,他告诉我,那是他的父亲。

paragraphs.en: It is not easy for me to express how it moved me to see what ecstasy and filial affection had worked in this poor savage at the sight of his father, and of his being delivered from death; nor indeed can I describe half the extravagances of his affection after this: for he went into the boat and out of the boat a great many times: when he went in to him he would sit down by him, open his breast, and hold his father’s head close to his bosom for many minutes together, to nourish it; then he took his arms and ankles, which were numbed and stiff with the binding, and chafed and rubbed them with his hands; and I, perceiving what the case was, gave him some rum out of my bottle to rub them with, which did them a great deal of good.
paragraphs.cn: 要我形容这可怜野人一见到他父亲、见到父亲从死里得救时,心中涌起的那种欣喜若狂和孝子之情是怎样地打动了我,实非易事;此后他那份深情种种过分的举动,我更是连一半都描摹不出:他一趟又一趟地上船下船;上去挨着父亲坐下,敞开父亲的胸口,一连好几分钟把父亲的头紧贴在自己怀里暖着;然后又捧起父亲那被绳索勒得又麻又僵的手臂和脚踝,用手又搓又揉;我看出是怎么回事,便从酒瓶里倒了些朗姆酒给他,让他拿去搓揉,大有好处。

paragraphs.en: This affair put an end to our pursuit of the canoe with the other savages, who were now almost out of sight; and it was happy for us that we did not, for it blew so hard within two hours after, and before they could be got a quarter of their way, and continued blowing so hard all night, and that from the north-west, which was against them, that I could not suppose their boat could live, or that they ever reached their own coast.
paragraphs.cn: 这件事使我们放弃了对那条载着别的野人的独木舟的追击,他们这会儿已几乎看不见了;幸好我们没去追,因为不出两小时便刮起大风,他们还没划到四分之一的路程,那风又整夜从西北方向刮个不停,正逆着他们,我料想他们那条船活不成,也到不了自己的海岸。

paragraphs.en: But to return to Friday; he was so busy about his father that I could not find in my heart to take him off for some time; but after I thought he could leave him a little, I called him to me, and he came jumping and laughing, and pleased to the highest extreme: then I asked him if he had given his father any bread.
paragraphs.cn: 再说星期五;他一心扑在父亲身上,我实在不忍心把他拉开一时;可等我觉得他能稍稍离开父亲一会儿了,便唤他到我跟前,他又蹦又笑地跑来,快活到了极点:于是我问他给没给父亲吃点面包。

paragraphs.en: He shook his head, and said, “None; ugly dog eat all up self.”
paragraphs.cn: 他摇摇头,说:“没有;丑狗自己全吃光了。”

paragraphs.en: I then gave him a cake of bread out of a little pouch I carried on purpose; I also gave him a dram for himself; but he would not taste it, but carried it to his father.
paragraphs.cn: 我便从随身专为此带的小口袋里拿出一块面包饼给他;我还给了他一杯酒自己喝;可他不肯尝一口,而是端去给了父亲。

paragraphs.en: I had in my pocket two or three bunches of raisins, so I gave him a handful of them for his father.
paragraphs.cn: 我口袋里还有两三串葡萄干,便抓了一把给他,让他拿去给父亲。

paragraphs.en: He had no sooner given his father these raisins but I saw him come out of the boat, and run away as if he had been bewitched, for he was the swiftest fellow on his feet that ever I saw: I say, he ran at such a rate that he was out of sight, as it were, in an instant; and though I called, and hallooed out too after him, it was all one—away he went; and in a quarter of an hour I saw him come back again, though not so fast as he went; and as he came nearer I found his pace slacker, because he had something in his hand.
paragraphs.cn: 他刚把这些葡萄干给了父亲,我就看见他跳下船,撒腿飞跑,像中了邪一般,因为他是我见过跑得最快的人:我是说,他跑得那么快,几乎一转眼就没了影;我朝他喊、朝他嚷都无济于事——他只管跑;过了一刻钟,我见他又跑了回来,只是没去时那么快;等他走近些,我发现他脚步放慢了,因为手里拿着东西。

paragraphs.en: When he came up to me I found he had been quite home for an earthen jug or pot, to bring his father some fresh water, and that he had got two more cakes or loaves of bread: the bread he gave me, but the water he carried to his father; however, as I was very thirsty too, I took a little of it.
paragraphs.cn: 等他来到我跟前,我才知道他一直跑回家去取一只陶罐,好给父亲带点淡水来,还多带了两块面包饼:面包他给了我,水却端去给父亲;不过因为我也很渴,便喝了一点。

paragraphs.en: The water revived his father more than all the rum or spirits I had given him, for he was fainting with thirst.
paragraphs.cn: 这水比我给他父亲的所有朗姆酒或烈酒都更能使他复元,因为他正渴得发昏。

paragraphs.en: When his father had drunk, I called to him to know if there was any water left.
paragraphs.cn: 他父亲喝完后,我唤星期五过来,问还剩不剩水。

paragraphs.en: He said, “Yes”; and I bade him give it to the poor Spaniard, who was in as much want of it as his father; and I sent one of the cakes that Friday brought to the Spaniard too, who was indeed very weak, and was reposing himself upon a green place under the shade of a tree; and whose limbs were also very stiff, and very much swelled with the rude bandage he had been tied with.
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“还有”;我便叫他拿去给那可怜的西班牙人,他跟星期五父亲一样急需喝水;我又叫人把星期五带来的一块面包饼也送给西班牙人,他确实很虚弱,正在一棵树荫下一块绿草地上歇着;他的四肢也很僵硬,又被那捆过他的粗绳勒得肿胀不堪。

paragraphs.en: When I saw that upon Friday’s coming to him with the water he sat up and drank, and took the bread and began to eat, I went to him and gave him a handful of raisins.
paragraphs.cn: 我见西班牙人一等星期五端水来,便坐起身喝了,接过面包吃了起来,我就走过去,给了他一把葡萄干。

paragraphs.en: He looked up in my face with all the tokens of gratitude and thankfulness that could appear in any countenance; but was so weak, notwithstanding he had so exerted himself in the fight, that he could not stand up upon his feet—he tried to do it two or three times, but was really not able, his ankles were so swelled and so painful to him; so I bade him sit still, and caused Friday to rub his ankles, and bathe them with rum, as he had done his father’s.
paragraphs.cn: 他仰起脸望着我,脸上写满了一切能显露的感激之情;可他实在太虚弱了——尽管方才在打斗中那样奋力过——竟站不起身来;他试着站了两三回,却当真站不起来,他的脚踝肿得那么厉害,痛得那么难受;于是我叫他安坐别动,又让星期五去给他揉脚踝,用朗姆酒擦洗,就像他给父亲揉过的那样。

paragraphs.en: I observed the poor affectionate creature, every two minutes, or perhaps less, all the while he was here, turn his head about to see if his father was in the same place and posture as he left him sitting; and at last he found he was not to be seen; at which he started up, and, without speaking a word, flew with that swiftness to him that one could scarce perceive his feet to touch the ground as he went; but when he came, he only found he had laid himself down to ease his limbs, so Friday came back to me presently; and then I spoke to the Spaniard to let Friday help him up if he could, and lead him to the boat, and then he should carry him to our dwelling, where I would take care of him.
paragraphs.cn: 我注意到,这可怜多情的家伙在这儿的整段时间里,每隔两分钟、也许还不到,就要扭头看看他父亲是不是还在他离开时坐着的老地方、老姿势;末了他发现看不见父亲了,便一跃而起,一句话不说,以那样快的速度朝父亲奔去,快得叫人几乎看不出他的脚沾着地面;可等他跑到,才发现父亲只是躺下歇歇四肢,于是星期五马上又回到我身边;这时我对西班牙人说,让星期五扶他起来,尽力搀他到船上,然后再把他运到我们的住处去,我会照料他。

paragraphs.en: But Friday, a lusty, strong fellow, took the Spaniard upon his back, and carried him away to the boat, and set him down softly upon the side or gunnel of the canoe, with his feet in the inside of it; and then lifting him quite in, he set him close to his father; and presently stepping out again, launched the boat off, and paddled it along the shore faster than I could walk, though the wind blew pretty hard too; so he brought them both safe into our creek, and leaving them in the boat, ran away to fetch the other canoe.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五这个粗壮健硕的家伙,把西班牙人背在背上,一直背到船边,轻轻把他放在独木舟的舷边上,让他的脚在船里头;然后把他整个抱进去,让他挨着他父亲坐下;接着又跨出船外,把船撑离岸边,沿着岸划,划得比我步行还快,尽管那时风也刮得挺猛;就这样他把两人都平安送进了我们的河汊,把他们留在船上,自己又跑去取另一条独木舟。

paragraphs.en: As he passed me I spoke to him, and asked him whither he went.
paragraphs.cn: 他从我身边经过时,我跟他说话,问他去哪儿。

paragraphs.en: He told me, “Go fetch more boat;” so away he went like the wind, for sure never man or horse ran like him; and he had the other canoe in the creek almost as soon as I got to it by land; so he wafted me over, and then went to help our new guests out of the boat, which he did; but they were neither of them able to walk; so that poor Friday knew not what to do.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我:“去多取一条船来;”说罢便像风一样跑了,因为世上准没有哪个人或哪匹马跑得像他那样快;我从陆路刚走到那儿,他几乎同时就把另一条独木舟弄进了河汊;于是他把我摆渡过去,然后又去帮我们两位新客下船,他也办到了;可两人都走不了路,弄得可怜的星期五不知如何是好。

paragraphs.en: To remedy this, I went to work in my thought, and calling to Friday to bid them sit down on the bank while he came to me, I soon made a kind of hand-barrow to lay them on, and Friday and I carried them both up together upon it between us.
paragraphs.cn: 为了补救这一点,我在心里盘算起办法,便叫星期五让他们坐在岸边等他过来找我,我很快做了个像担架似的东西,好把他们放上去,星期五和我便合力把他们俩一同抬了上来。

paragraphs.en: But when we got them to the outside of our wall, or fortification, we were at a worse loss than before, for it was impossible to get them over, and I was resolved not to break it down; so I set to work again, and Friday and I, in about two hours’ time, made a very handsome tent, covered with old sails, and above that with boughs of trees, being in the space without our outward fence and between that and the grove of young wood which I had planted; and here we made them two beds of such things as I had—viz. of good rice-straw, with blankets laid upon it to lie on, and another to cover them, on each bed.
paragraphs.cn: 可是等我们把他们抬到我们围墙或工事的外面,却比先前更犯了难,因为无论如何也没法把他们弄进去,而我又打定主意不去拆墙;于是我重新动手,星期五和我花了大约两小时,搭起一座十分像样的帐篷,顶上盖着旧帆,再上面盖着树枝,搭在我们外围栅栏之外、栅栏和我栽的那片小树林之间的空地上;在这儿,我们用手边现有的东西给他们铺了两张床——也就是用上好的稻草,上面铺着毯子供他们躺卧,每张床上另有一条毯子供他们盖。

paragraphs.en: My island was now peopled, and I thought myself very rich in subjects; and it was a merry reflection, which I frequently made, how like a king I looked.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我这岛上有了臣民,我觉得自己在子民方面很是富有;我常常这样想,自觉活像个国王,想来倒也有趣。

paragraphs.en: First of all, the whole country was my own property, so that I had an undoubted right of dominion.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,整片国土都是我的私产,所以我对它拥有毋庸置疑的统治权。

paragraphs.en: Secondly, my people were perfectly subjected—I was absolutely lord and lawgiver—they all owed their lives to me, and were ready to lay down their lives, if there had been occasion for it, for me.
paragraphs.cn: 其次,我的子民完全归顺于我——我是绝对的君主兼立法者——他们的性命全是我给的,一旦有需要,他们都甘愿为我舍命。

paragraphs.en: It was remarkable, too, I had but three subjects, and they were of three different religions—my man Friday was a Protestant, his father was a Pagan and a cannibal, and the Spaniard was a Papist.
paragraphs.cn: 还有一件也很值得一提,我虽只有三个臣民,他们却分属三种不同的宗教——我的仆人星期五是新教徒,他父亲是异教徒兼食人者,那西班牙人则是天主教徒。

paragraphs.en: However, I allowed liberty of conscience throughout my dominions.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,我在自己的领地里一律准许信仰自由。

paragraphs.en: But this is by the way.
paragraphs.cn: 但这不过是顺带一提罢了。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I had secured my two weak, rescued prisoners, and given them shelter, and a place to rest them upon, I began to think of making some provision for them; and the first thing I did, I ordered Friday to take a yearling goat, betwixt a kid and a goat, out of my particular flock, to be killed; when I cut off the hinder-quarter, and chopping it into small pieces, I set Friday to work to boiling and stewing, and made them a very good dish, I assure you, of flesh and broth; and as I cooked it without doors, for I made no fire within my inner wall, so I carried it all into the new tent, and having set a table there for them, I sat down, and ate my own dinner also with them, and, as well as I could, cheered them and encouraged them.
paragraphs.cn: 我一安顿好这两个虚弱的、被救出来的俘虏,给了他们栖身之所和歇息之处,便开始盘算为他们备些吃食;我做的头一件事,就是吩咐星期五从我那专养的一群羊里牵出一只当年的羊——一只介于羔羊和成羊之间的——宰了;我割下后腿,剁成小块,叫星期五动手煮炖,做了一大盘肉和肉汤,着实鲜美,我向你保证;因为我是在门外做的饭——我内墙里从不生火——便把它全端进新帐篷,给他们摆好一张桌子,我自己也坐下和他们一同用餐,并尽我所能地给他们鼓劲、给他们打气。

paragraphs.en: Friday was my interpreter, especially to his father, and, indeed, to the Spaniard too; for the Spaniard spoke the language of the savages pretty well.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五是我的翻译,尤其是对他父亲,其实对那西班牙人也一样;因为那西班牙人相当通晓野人的语言。

paragraphs.en: After we had dined, or rather supped, I ordered Friday to take one of the canoes, and go and fetch our muskets and other firearms, which, for want of time, we had left upon the place of battle; and the next day I ordered him to go and bury the dead bodies of the savages, which lay open to the sun, and would presently be offensive.
paragraphs.cn: 我们用过正餐、或者说晚餐之后,我吩咐星期五取一条独木舟,去把我们因来不及带走、丢在战场上的火枪和别的火器取回来;第二天我又吩咐他去把那些野人的尸体埋掉,那些尸体正曝晒在太阳底下,眼看就要发臭了。

paragraphs.en: I also ordered him to bury the horrid remains of their barbarous feast, which I could not think of doing myself; nay, I could not bear to see them if I went that way; all which he punctually performed, and effaced the very appearance of the savages being there; so that when I went again, I could scarce know where it was, otherwise than by the corner of the wood pointing to the place.
paragraphs.cn: 我还吩咐他把他们那野蛮筵席留下的可怖残迹埋掉,这活儿我自己想都不敢想去做;不但如此,我若打那儿经过,连看都不忍看;这一切他都一丝不苟地办妥了,把野人到过那里的痕迹抹得干干净净;以致我再去时,几乎认不出那是哪儿,只能靠那林角指认那处地方。

paragraphs.en: I then began to enter into a little conversation with my two new subjects; and, first, I set Friday to inquire of his father what he thought of the escape of the savages in that canoe, and whether we might expect a return of them, with a power too great for us to resist.
paragraphs.cn: 随后我开始跟我这两个新臣民聊上几句;首先,我叫星期五去问他父亲,对那几个乘独木舟逃走的野人怎么看,我们是否该料到他们会带着我们无力抵挡的强大势力卷土重来。

paragraphs.en: His first opinion was, that the savages in the boat never could live out the storm which blew that night they went off, but must of necessity be drowned, or driven south to those other shores, where they were as sure to be devoured as they were to be drowned if they were cast away; but, as to what they would do if they came safe on shore, he said he knew not; but it was his opinion that they were so dreadfully frightened with the manner of their being attacked, the noise, and the fire, that he believed they would tell the people they were all killed by thunder and lightning, not by the hand of man; and that the two which appeared—viz.
paragraphs.cn: 他起初的看法是,船上那些野人绝挨不过他们出发那晚刮起的风暴,必定不是淹死,就是被吹向南边别的海岸,那儿他们即便侥幸不淹死,也一样准会被人吃掉;可他们万一平安上了岸会怎么办,他说他不知道;不过依他看,他们被我们那种攻击方式、那声响和那火光吓得如此魂飞魄散,他相信他们会告诉族人:他们全是被雷电劈死的,不是死在人的手里;而那出现的两个——也就是

paragraphs.en: Friday and I—were two heavenly spirits, or furies, come down to destroy them, and not men with weapons.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五和我——是两个从天而降来毁灭他们的天神或凶神,并非拿着武器的凡人。

paragraphs.en: This, he said, he knew; because he heard them all cry out so, in their language, one to another; for it was impossible for them to conceive that a man could dart fire, and speak thunder, and kill at a distance, without lifting up the hand, as was done now: and this old savage was in the right; for, as I understood since, by other hands, the savages never attempted to go over to the island afterwards, they were so terrified with the accounts given by those four men (for it seems they did escape the sea), that they believed whoever went to that enchanted island would be destroyed with fire from the gods.
paragraphs.cn: 他说这些他是知道的;因为他听见他们全都用他们的语言这样互相嚷嚷;因为他们无论如何也想不通:一个人竟能像方才那样,不抬手就喷出火来、说出雷声、在老远之外把人打死;这老野人说得没错;因为我后来从别的途径得知,那些野人此后再没敢渡海到岛上来,他们被那四个人(看来他们果真逃过了大海)带回的说法吓坏了,深信谁去了那座着魔的岛,就会被神明降下的天火毁灭。

paragraphs.en: This, however, I knew not; and therefore was under continual apprehensions for a good while, and kept always upon my guard, with all my army: for, as there were now four of us, I would have ventured upon a hundred of them, fairly in the open field, at any time.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切我当时却并不知道;因此有好一阵子我始终提心吊胆,时刻带着我全部的兵马严加戒备:因为我们如今有了四个人,无论何时,我都敢在开阔的战场上正大光明地迎战他们一百个人。

paragraphs.en: In a little time, however, no more canoes appearing, the fear of their coming wore off; and I began to take my former thoughts of a voyage to the main into consideration; being likewise assured by Friday’s father that I might depend upon good usage from their nation, on his account, if I would go.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,过了不久,再没有独木舟出现,我对他们来袭的恐惧渐渐消退;我又开始重新考虑先前那个渡海去大陆的念头;星期五的父亲也向我保证,若我肯去,看在他的面子上,尽可放心他们那一族会好好待我。

paragraphs.en: But my thoughts were a little suspended when I had a serious discourse with the Spaniard, and when I understood that there were sixteen more of his countrymen and Portuguese, who having been cast away and made their escape to that side, lived there at peace, indeed, with the savages, but were very sore put to it for necessaries, and, indeed, for life.
paragraphs.cn: 但当我和那西班牙人认真谈过一番,得知还有十六个他的同胞和葡萄牙人,同样遭遇海难逃到了那一带,如今虽与野人相安无事地住在那里,却极缺生活必需品,甚至连活命都很艰难,我的念头便有些踌躇了。

paragraphs.en: I asked him all the particulars of their voyage, and found they were a Spanish ship, bound from the Rio de la Plata to the Havanna, being directed to leave their loading there, which was chiefly hides and silver, and to bring back what European goods they could meet with there; that they had five Portuguese seamen on board, whom they took out of another wreck; that five of their own men were drowned when first the ship was lost, and that these escaped through infinite dangers and hazards, and arrived, almost starved, on the cannibal coast, where they expected to have been devoured every moment.
paragraphs.cn: 我向他详细打听了他们那次航行的经过,得知他们原是一艘西班牙船,从拉普拉塔河驶往哈瓦那,奉命把主要是兽皮和白银的货物卸在那里,再带回他们能弄到的欧洲货;船上有五名葡萄牙水手,是从另一艘失事船上救下来的;船最初失事时,他们自己有五个人淹死了,其余人历尽无数艰险逃生,几乎饿死才到了那片食人族的海岸,时时刻刻都怕被吞掉。

paragraphs.en: He told me they had some arms with them, but they were perfectly useless, for that they had neither powder nor ball, the washing of the sea having spoiled all their powder but a little, which they used at their first landing to provide themselves with some food.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我,他们随身带了些武器,却全然无用,因为既没火药也没子弹,海水把他们的火药几乎全泡坏了,只剩一点点,登陆之初用来打了些食物。

paragraphs.en: I asked him what he thought would become of them there, and if they had formed any design of making their escape.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他,他觉得他们留在那里会有什么下场,是否已定下什么逃走的计划。

paragraphs.en: He said they had many consultations about it; but that having neither vessel nor tools to build one, nor provisions of any kind, their councils always ended in tears and despair.
paragraphs.cn: 他说他们为此商量过许多次;可是既没有船,也没有造船的工具,又没有任何存粮,他们的商议总是以眼泪和绝望收场。

paragraphs.en: I asked him how he thought they would receive a proposal from me, which might tend towards an escape; and whether, if they were all here, it might not be done.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他,他觉得他们会怎样看待我提出的一个也许有助于逃走的建议;若是他们都到这里来,这事能不能办成。

paragraphs.en: I told him with freedom, I feared mostly their treachery and ill-usage of me, if I put my life in their hands; for that gratitude was no inherent virtue in the nature of man, nor did men always square their dealings by the obligations they had received so much as they did by the advantages they expected.
paragraphs.cn: 我坦白告诉他,我最怕的是把性命交到他们手里后,他们背信弃义、恶待于我;因为感恩并非人性中天生的美德,人们行事往往不是照所受的恩情来衡量,而是照他们所指望的好处来衡量。

paragraphs.en: I told him it would be very hard that I should be made the instrument of their deliverance, and that they should afterwards make me their prisoner in New Spain, where an Englishman was certain to be made a sacrifice, what necessity or what accident soever brought him thither; and that I had rather be delivered up to the savages, and be devoured alive, than fall into the merciless claws of the priests, and be carried into the Inquisition.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他,若我成了搭救他们的工具,事后他们却把我带到新西班牙去当囚犯,那可太难堪了;在那里,一个英国人无论出于什么必要、遭遇什么变故被带去,都必定要被拿去献祭;我宁可被交给野人活活吞掉,也不愿落进那些教士毫不留情的爪牙,被押进宗教裁判所。

paragraphs.en: I added that, otherwise, I was persuaded, if they were all here, we might, with so many hands, build a barque large enough to carry us all away, either to the Brazils southward, or to the islands or Spanish coast northward; but that if, in requital, they should, when I had put weapons into their hands, carry me by force among their own people, I might be ill-used for my kindness to them, and make my case worse than it was before.
paragraphs.cn: 我又说,不然的话,我相信,若他们都在这里,凭这么多人手,我们准能造一条大到足以载我们全体离开的船,或往南去巴西,或往北去那些岛屿或西班牙海岸;可要是作为回报,等我把武器交到他们手里后,他们却强行把我押到他们自己人中间,那我倒因好心待他们反受其害,处境比先前更糟。

paragraphs.en: He answered, with a great deal of candour and ingenuousness, that their condition was so miserable, and that they were so sensible of it, that he believed they would abhor the thought of using any man unkindly that should contribute to their deliverance; and that, if I pleased, he would go to them with the old man, and discourse with them about it, and return again and bring me their answer; that he would make conditions with them upon their solemn oath, that they should be absolutely under my direction as their commander and captain; and they should swear upon the holy sacraments and gospel to be true to me, and go to such Christian country as I should agree to, and no other; and to be directed wholly and absolutely by my orders till they were landed safely in such country as I intended, and that he would bring a contract from them, under their hands, for that purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 他十分坦率诚恳地回答说,他们的境况如此凄惨,他们自己也深切体会到这一点,因此他相信,他们对于亏待任何一个搭救他们的人的念头,必定深恶痛绝;他说,若我愿意,他可以同那老人一起去找他们,把这事同他们谈谈,再回来把他们的答复带给我;他要同他们立约,让他们庄严起誓,绝对听从我这位统领和船长的指挥;他们要指着神圣的圣礼和福音书发誓,对我忠诚,只去我所同意的那个基督教国家,别处不去;在安全登上我所指定的那个国家之前,一切都完全绝对听我号令行事;他还要带回一份他们亲笔签字的契约,以此为凭。

paragraphs.en: Then he told me he would first swear to me himself that he would never stir from me as long as he lived till I gave him orders; and that he would take my side to the last drop of his blood, if there should happen the least breach of faith among his countrymen.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他告诉我,他会先亲自向我起誓,只要他活着,不到我下令,他绝不离开我半步;万一他的同胞中有丝毫背信之举,他必站在我这一边,战斗到流尽最后一滴血。

paragraphs.en: He told me they were all of them very civil, honest men, and they were under the greatest distress imaginable, having neither weapons nor clothes, nor any food, but at the mercy and discretion of the savages; out of all hopes of ever returning to their own country; and that he was sure, if I would undertake their relief, they would live and die by me.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我,他们个个都是极其斯文、正直的人,眼下正陷于难以想象的困苦之中,既没武器,也没衣裳,更没食物,全凭野人的恩慈和摆布;回本国的希望已经断绝;他确信,只要我肯出手相救,他们必与我同生共死。

paragraphs.en: Upon these assurances, I resolved to venture to relieve them, if possible, and to send the old savage and this Spaniard over to them to treat.
paragraphs.cn: 有了这些保证,我决意冒险去救他们,若有可能的话,就派这老野人和这西班牙人渡海去同他们商洽。

paragraphs.en: But when we had got all things in readiness to go, the Spaniard himself started an objection, which had so much prudence in it on one hand, and so much sincerity on the other hand, that I could not but be very well satisfied in it; and, by his advice, put off the deliverance of his comrades for at least half a year.
paragraphs.cn: 可当我们把一切都准备停当要动身时,那西班牙人自己却提出一条异议,这异议一方面极有远见,一方面又极其诚恳,叫我不能不十分信服;听了他的劝告,我把搭救他同伴的事至少推迟了半年。

paragraphs.en: The case was thus: he had been with us now about a month, during which time I had let him see in what manner I had provided, with the assistance of Providence, for my support; and he saw evidently what stock of corn and rice I had laid up; which, though it was more than sufficient for myself, yet it was not sufficient, without good husbandry, for my family, now it was increased to four; but much less would it be sufficient if his countrymen, who were, as he said, sixteen, still alive, should come over; and least of all would it be sufficient to victual our vessel, if we should build one, for a voyage to any of the Christian colonies of America; so he told me he thought it would be more advisable to let him and the other two dig and cultivate some more land, as much as I could spare seed to sow, and that we should wait another harvest, that we might have a supply of corn for his countrymen, when they should come; for want might be a temptation to them to disagree, or not to think themselves delivered, otherwise than out of one difficulty into another.
paragraphs.cn: 情形是这样的:他到我们这里已约摸一个月,这期间我让他看了我如何靠着上天的相助为自己张罗生计;他分明看见我囤下了多少谷子和稻米;这些东西对我一个人虽绰绰有余,但如今我这一家已增至四口,若不精打细算便不够用了;倘若他那还活着的、据他说有十六人的同胞都过来,就更远远不够;而要是我们造一条船,航往美洲任何一处基督教殖民地,拿来供给船上口粮,那就最不够用了;所以他对我说,他觉得更稳妥的做法是让他和另外两人多开垦、多耕种一些土地,种子我能匀出多少就种多少,我们再等一次收成,好在他同胞到来时能有一批谷子接济;因为匮乏也许会引诱他们生出嫌隙,或让他们觉得自己不过是脱了一难又入一难,算不得得救。

paragraphs.en: “You know,” says he, “the children of Israel, though they rejoiced at first for their being delivered out of Egypt, yet rebelled even against God Himself, that delivered them, when they came to want bread in the wilderness.”
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“你知道,以色列的子民虽然起初为脱离埃及而欢欣,可等他们在旷野缺了面包,竟连搭救他们的上帝本身也悖逆起来。”

paragraphs.en: His caution was so seasonable, and his advice so good, that I could not but be very well pleased with his proposal, as well as I was satisfied with his fidelity; so we fell to digging, all four of us, as well as the wooden tools we were furnished with permitted; and in about a month’s time, by the end of which it was seed-time, we had got as much land cured and trimmed up as we sowed two-and-twenty bushels of barley on, and sixteen jars of rice, which was, in short, all the seed we had to spare: indeed, we left ourselves barely sufficient, for our own food for the six months that we had to expect our crop; that is to say reckoning from the time we set our seed aside for sowing; for it is not to be supposed it is six months in the ground in that country.
paragraphs.cn: 他这番告诫来得如此合时,他的劝告又如此中肯,我不能不对他的提议深感满意,正如我对他的忠诚也深感放心;于是我们四个人便一齐动手开垦,凭着那几件现有的木头工具尽力而为;约摸一个月工夫,到了播种时节,我们已把一片地整治好,种下了二十二蒲式耳大麦和十六罐稻米,这简而言之就是我们能匀出的全部种子:说实话,我们只给自己留下勉强够吃的口粮,以供收成前那六个月之需;这是从我们把种子留出来播种那时算起的;因为在那个地方,种子入土可想而知用不着六个月。

paragraphs.en: Having now society enough, and our numbers being sufficient to put us out of fear of the savages, if they had come, unless their number had been very great, we went freely all over the island, whenever we found occasion; and as we had our escape or deliverance upon our thoughts, it was impossible, at least for me, to have the means of it out of mine.
paragraphs.cn: 如今有了足够的伙伴,人手也多得足以让我们不再惧怕野人来袭——除非他们人数极多;所以只要有需要,我们便在岛上到处自由走动;而既然逃走或得救的念头萦绕在我们心头,至少对我而言,是断断不可能不把谋划逃走的办法放在心上的。

paragraphs.en: For this purpose I marked out several trees, which I thought fit for our work, and I set Friday and his father to cut them down; and then I caused the Spaniard, to whom I imparted my thoughts on that affair, to oversee and direct their work.
paragraphs.cn: 为此我选定了几棵我觉得合用的树,叫星期五和他父亲去把它们砍倒;然后我把这件事上的心思透露给那西班牙人,叫他去监工指挥他们干活。

paragraphs.en: I showed them with what indefatigable pains I had hewed a large tree into single planks, and I caused them to do the like, till they made about a dozen large planks, of good oak, near two feet broad, thirty-five feet long, and from two inches to four inches thick: what prodigious labour it took up any one may imagine.
paragraphs.cn: 我给他们看,我曾如何不辞辛劳地把一棵大树砍削成一块块木板,又叫他们照样去做,直到他们做出约摸十二块上好的橡木大板,宽近两英尺,长三十五英尺,厚从两英寸到四英寸不等:这要费多么惊人的力气,谁都想象得到。

paragraphs.en: At the same time I contrived to increase my little flock of tame goats as much as I could; and for this purpose I made Friday and the Spaniard go out one day, and myself with Friday the next day (for we took our turns), and by this means we got about twenty young kids to breed up with the rest; for whenever we shot the dam, we saved the kids, and added them to our flock.
paragraphs.cn: 与此同时,我想方设法尽量扩大我那一小群驯养的山羊;为此我让星期五和西班牙人一天出去,我自己和星期五第二天再去(我们轮流着来),用这法子我们逮到了约摸二十只小羊崽和其余的一起养着;因为每回我们打死母羊,就把羊崽留下,添进我们的羊群。

paragraphs.en: But above all, the season for curing the grapes coming on, I caused such a prodigious quantity to be hung up in the sun, that, I believe, had we been at Alicant, where the raisins of the sun are cured, we could have filled sixty or eighty barrels; and these, with our bread, formed a great part of our food—very good living too, I assure you, for they are exceedingly nourishing.
paragraphs.cn: 但最要紧的是,腌制葡萄的季节来临了,我叫人把好大一堆葡萄挂在太阳底下晒;我敢说,若我们是在腌制葡萄干的阿利坎特,准能装满六七十桶;这些葡萄干连同我们的面包,成了我们食物的一大部分——我向你保证,那日子过得也很不错,因为它们极其滋养。

paragraphs.en: It was now harvest, and our crop in good order: it was not the most plentiful increase I had seen in the island, but, however, it was enough to answer our end; for from twenty-two bushels of barley we brought in and thrashed out above two hundred and twenty bushels; and the like in proportion of the rice; which was store enough for our food to the next harvest, though all the sixteen Spaniards had been on shore with me; or, if we had been ready for a voyage, it would very plentifully have victualled our ship to have carried us to any part of the world; that is to say, any part of America.
paragraphs.cn: 如今正是收获时节,我们的庄稼长势喜人:这虽不是我在岛上见过的最丰盛的收成,却也足够我们所需;因为二十二蒲式耳大麦,我们收进打出了两百二十多蒲式耳;稻米也照这个比例增收;这些存粮足够我们吃到下一次收成,哪怕那十六个西班牙人全都上了岸和我在一起;或者说,若我们已备好远航,这也足够丰盛地供给船上口粮,把我们载到世上任何地方——这是说,美洲的任何地方。

paragraphs.en: When we had thus housed and secured our magazine of corn, we fell to work to make more wicker-ware, viz. great baskets, in which we kept it; and the Spaniard was very handy and dexterous at this part, and often blamed me that I did not make some things for defence of this kind of work; but I saw no need of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我们就这样把谷子储藏妥当、库房安顿好后,便着手多编些柳条器具,也就是储粮用的大筐;那西班牙人干这活儿十分灵巧利索,还常怪我不做些这类活儿来加固防御;可我看不出有这个必要。

paragraphs.en: And now, having a full supply of food for all the guests I expected, I gave the Spaniard leave to go over to the main, to see what he could do with those he had left behind him there.
paragraphs.cn: 如今,既已为我所盼的宾客备下了充足的食物,我便准许那西班牙人渡海去大陆,看看他能同他留在那边的人办成些什么。

paragraphs.en: I gave him a strict charge not to bring any man who would not first swear in the presence of himself and the old savage that he would in no way injure, fight with, or attack the person he should find in the island, who was so kind as to send for them in order to their deliverance; but that they would stand by him and defend him against all such attempts, and wherever they went would be entirely under and subjected to his command; and that this should be put in writing, and signed in their hands.
paragraphs.cn: 我严令他:凡不肯当着他和那老野人的面先行起誓的人,一个也不许带来;誓词是:他绝不以任何方式伤害、攻打或袭击岛上那位好心派人去接他们来搭救他们的人;反而要拥护他,抵御一切此类图谋,无论走到哪里都完全归他统辖、听他号令;而且这一切都要写成文字,由他们亲手签字。

paragraphs.en: How they were to have done this, when I knew they had neither pen nor ink, was a question which we never asked.
paragraphs.cn: 至于他们既没笔又没墨,该怎样做到这一点,这个问题我们倒始终没问过。

paragraphs.en: Under these instructions, the Spaniard and the old savage, the father of Friday, went away in one of the canoes which they might be said to have come in, or rather were brought in, when they came as prisoners to be devoured by the savages.
paragraphs.cn: 带着这些嘱托,那西班牙人和那老野人——星期五的父亲——乘上一条独木舟去了;那独木舟可以说就是他们乘来的,或者不如说是当初他们作为俘虏被押来给野人吞食时被带来的。

paragraphs.en: I gave each of them a musket, with a firelock on it, and about eight charges of powder and ball, charging them to be very good husbands of both, and not to use either of them but upon urgent occasions.
paragraphs.cn: 我给了他们每人一支带火枪机的火枪,和约摸八发火药子弹,叮嘱他们对这两样都要极其省着用,非到紧急关头绝不动用。

paragraphs.en: This was a cheerful work, being the first measures used by me in view of my deliverance for now twenty-seven years and some days.
paragraphs.cn: 这是一桩令人欢欣的差事,是我如今被困二十七年零几天以来,为谋求自身得救所采取的头一步。

paragraphs.en: I gave them provisions of bread and of dried grapes, sufficient for themselves for many days, and sufficient for all the Spaniards—for about eight days’ time; and wishing them a good voyage, I saw them go, agreeing with them about a signal they should hang out at their return, by which I should know them again when they came back, at a distance, before they came on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 我给了他们够自己吃许多天、也够所有西班牙人吃约摸八天的面包和葡萄干作为口粮;祝他们一路顺风后,我目送他们离去,并同他们约定好一个信号,待他们回来时挂出,好让我在他们尚未上岸、还离得老远时,便能远远认出他们来。

paragraphs.en: They went away with a fair gale on the day that the moon was at full, by my account in the month of October; but as for an exact reckoning of days, after I had once lost it I could never recover it again; nor had I kept even the number of years so punctually as to be sure I was right; though, as it proved when I afterwards examined my account, I found I had kept a true reckoning of years.
paragraphs.cn: 他们趁着满月那天顺风扬帆而去,依我推算是在十月;可要说准确记日子,我自从有一回记乱了,便再也无法补回来;连年数我也没记得那么精确,拿不准是否没错;不过后来我核对账目时倒发现,我把年数记得分毫不差。

paragraphs.en: It was no less than eight days I had waited for them, when a strange and unforeseen accident intervened, of which the like has not, perhaps, been heard of in history.
paragraphs.cn: 我足足等了他们八天,这时一桩离奇而始料未及的意外插了进来,那样的事在史书上或许都不曾听闻过。

paragraphs.en: I was fast asleep in my hutch one morning, when my man Friday came running in to me, and called aloud, “Master, master, they are come, they are come!”
paragraphs.cn: 一天早晨我正在窝棚里熟睡,我的仆人星期五跑进来找我,大声喊道:“主人,主人,他们来了,他们来了!”

paragraphs.en: I jumped up, and regardless of danger I went, as soon as I could get my clothes on, through my little grove, which, by the way, was by this time grown to be a very thick wood; I say, regardless of danger I went without my arms, which was not my custom to do; but I was surprised when, turning my eyes to the sea, I presently saw a boat at about a league and a half distance, standing in for the shore, with a shoulder-of-mutton sail, as they call it, and the wind blowing pretty fair to bring them in: also I observed, presently, that they did not come from that side which the shore lay on, but from the southernmost end of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 我一跃而起,顾不上危险,一穿好衣裳就穿过我那片小树林——顺便说一句,这树林如今已长成一片极密的树丛;我是说,我顾不上危险,连武器也没带就出去了,这可不是我往常的习惯;可当我把目光转向大海时,不由一惊,只见约摸一里半外有一条小船正朝岸边驶来,挂着一面他们所称的“羊肩帆”,风势相当顺,正把他们送进岸来:我还立时看出,他们并非从海岸所在的那一面来,而是从岛的最南端来的。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I called Friday in, and bade him lie close, for these were not the people we looked for, and that we might not know yet whether they were friends or enemies.
paragraphs.cn: 见此情形,我把星期五叫进来,吩咐他伏低藏好,因为这些不是我们所盼的人,我们也还不知道他们是友是敌。

paragraphs.en: In the next place I went in to fetch my perspective glass to see what I could make of them; and having taken the ladder out, I climbed up to the top of the hill, as I used to do when I was apprehensive of anything, and to take my view the plainer without being discovered.
paragraphs.cn: 接着我进去取我的望远镜,好看清他们究竟是些什么人;把梯子搬出来后,我像每逢心中不安时那样爬上山顶,好把景象看得更真切,又不至于被人发现。

paragraphs.en: I had scarce set my foot upon the hill when my eye plainly discovered a ship lying at anchor, at about two leagues and a half distance from me, SSE.
paragraphs.cn: 我脚才踏上山顶,一眼便清清楚楚望见一艘船抛锚停泊着,在我东南偏南约摸两里半远的地方,

paragraphs.en: , but not above a league and a half from the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 不过离岸不超过一里半。

paragraphs.en: By my observation it appeared plainly to be an English ship, and the boat appeared to be an English long-boat.
paragraphs.cn: 据我观察,那分明是一艘英国船,那小船看来也是一条英国大艇。

paragraphs.en: I cannot express the confusion I was in, though the joy of seeing a ship, and one that I had reason to believe was manned by my own countrymen, and consequently friends, was such as I cannot describe; but yet I had some secret doubts hung about me—I cannot tell from whence they came—bidding me keep upon my guard.
paragraphs.cn: 我说不出自己心里有多慌乱,虽说看见一艘船、而且有理由相信船上是我自己的同胞、因而是朋友,那份喜悦是我无法形容的;可我心头仍萦绕着某种莫名的疑虑——我说不清它从何而来——叫我务必提防。

paragraphs.en: In the first place, it occurred to me to consider what business an English ship could have in that part of the world, since it was not the way to or from any part of the world where the English had any traffic; and I knew there had been no storms to drive them in there in distress; and that if they were really English it was most probable that they were here upon no good design; and that I had better continue as I was than fall into the hands of thieves and murderers.
paragraphs.cn: 首先,我不禁琢磨:一艘英国船跑到世上这一带来能有什么勾当?因为这里既不在往来于英国人有任何贸易的任何地方的航路上;我也知道近来并没有风暴把他们困厄之下逼到这里;而若他们当真是英国人,那多半是来这里没安好心;我最好还是维持现状,免得落进盗贼和凶手手里。

paragraphs.en: Let no man despise the secret hints and notices of danger which sometimes are given him when he may think there is no possibility of its being real.
paragraphs.cn: 但愿没有人小看那些有时向他发出的、关乎危险的暗中提示和示警,哪怕他觉得那危险绝无成真的可能。

paragraphs.en: That such hints and notices are given us I believe few that have made any observation of things can deny; that they are certain discoveries of an invisible world, and a converse of spirits, we cannot doubt; and if the tendency of them seems to be to warn us of danger, why should we not suppose they are from some friendly agent (whether supreme, or inferior and subordinate, is not the question), and that they are given for our good?
paragraphs.cn: 凡对世事稍有留心的人,大概少有能否认我们确会得到这类提示和示警的;它们是那不可见的世界的确凿显现,是与神灵的一种交通,这一点我们不容置疑;而若它们的旨意看来是要警告我们提防危险,那我们为何不该设想它们出自某位善意的使者(至于是至高的,还是次一等、从属的,那不是问题所在),是为我们的好处而赐下的呢?

paragraphs.en: The present question abundantly confirms me in the justice of this reasoning; for had I not been made cautious by this secret admonition, come it from whence it will, I had been done inevitably, and in a far worse condition than before, as you will see presently.
paragraphs.cn: 眼前这件事充分印证了我这番推理的公允;因为若不是这暗中的告诫——无论它从何而来——使我心存戒备,我必定难逃一劫,而且境况比先前糟糕得多,你马上就会看到。
