paragraphs.en: I had not kept myself long in this posture till I saw the boat draw near the shore, as if they looked for a creek to thrust in at, for the convenience of landing; however, as they did not come quite far enough, they did not see the little inlet where I formerly landed my rafts, but ran their boat on shore upon the beach, at about half a mile from me, which was very happy for me; for otherwise they would have landed just at my door, as I may say, and would soon have beaten me out of my castle, and perhaps have plundered me of all I had.
paragraphs.cn: 我保持这姿势没多久,便看见那小船靠近了岸,仿佛在寻一处小河汊好驶进去,便于登陆;然而,由于他们没驶得够远,没看见我先前放木筏上岸的那个小水湾,便把船径直冲上了离我约摸半英里的沙滩;这对我实在万幸,不然他们就会正好登陆在我家门口,可以说,顷刻间便会把我从城堡里赶出来,或许还会把我所有的东西洗劫一空。

paragraphs.en: When they were on shore I was fully satisfied they were Englishmen, at least most of them; one or two I thought were Dutch, but it did not prove so; there were in all eleven men, whereof three of them I found were unarmed and, as I thought, bound; and when the first four or five of them were jumped on shore, they took those three out of the boat as prisoners: one of the three I could perceive using the most passionate gestures of entreaty, affliction, and despair, even to a kind of extravagance; the other two, I could perceive, lifted up their hands sometimes, and appeared concerned indeed, but not to such a degree as the first.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一上岸,我便完全确信他们是英国人,至少大多数是;有一两个我以为是荷兰人,后来证明并非如此;他们一共十一个人,其中三个我发现没带武器,而且照我看是被捆着的;头四五个人一跳上岸,就把那三个人当作俘虏从船里拖了出来:三人中有一个,我瞧得出他做出最痛切的哀求、悲苦和绝望的姿态,甚至到了近乎狂乱的地步;另外两个,我瞧得出偶尔举起手来,显得确实心事重重,却不像头一个那样厉害。

paragraphs.en: I was perfectly confounded at the sight, and knew not what the meaning of it should be.
paragraphs.cn: 我看着这情景,直弄得莫名其妙,不知它究竟是什么意思。

paragraphs.en: Friday called out to me in English, as well as he could, “O master! you see English mans eat prisoner as well as savage mans.”
paragraphs.cn: 星期五用他尽力说出的英语向我喊道:“哦,主人!你瞧,英国人也和野人一样吃俘虏。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, Friday,” says I, “do you think they are going to eat them, then?”
paragraphs.cn: “怎么,星期五,”我说,“你以为他们要吃了他们吗?”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” says Friday, “they will eat them.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的,”星期五说,“他们会吃了他们。”

paragraphs.en: “No no,” says I, “Friday; I am afraid they will murder them, indeed; but you may be sure they will not eat them.”
paragraphs.cn: “不,不,”我说,“星期五;我怕他们真是要谋害他们;可你尽管放心,他们不会吃了他们。”

paragraphs.en: All this while I had no thought of what the matter really was, but stood trembling with the horror of the sight, expecting every moment when the three prisoners should be killed; nay, once I saw one of the villains lift up his arm with a great cutlass, as the seamen call it, or sword, to strike one of the poor men; and I expected to see him fall every moment; at which all the blood in my body seemed to run chill in my veins.
paragraphs.cn: 这整段时间里,我压根没想到事情的真相,只是站在那里,被眼前的惨状吓得直发抖,时时刻刻只等着那三个俘虏被杀掉;不止如此,我还一度看见一个恶徒举起手臂,握着一把水手们所称的大弯刀、或者说剑,朝那可怜人中的一个砍去;我只等着看他随时倒下;那当口,我周身的血在血管里仿佛都凉透了。

paragraphs.en: I wished heartily now for the Spaniard, and the savage that had gone with him, or that I had any way to have come undiscovered within shot of them, that I might have secured the three men, for I saw no firearms they had among them; but it fell out to my mind another way.
paragraphs.cn: 此刻我从心底盼着那西班牙人和随他去的那个野人在场,或者盼我有什么法子能不被察觉地摸到他们射程之内,好把那三个人救下来,因为我看不出他们中间有什么火器;可事情却照另一个样子在我心里成了形。

paragraphs.en: After I had observed the outrageous usage of the three men by the insolent seamen, I observed the fellows run scattering about the island, as if they wanted to see the country.
paragraphs.cn: 在我看了那些蛮横水手对三人的凶暴对待之后,我看见那些家伙四散着在岛上乱跑,仿佛想看看这地方是个什么去处。

paragraphs.en: I observed that the three other men had liberty to go also where they pleased; but they sat down all three upon the ground, very pensive, and looked like men in despair.
paragraphs.cn: 我看见另外那三个人也获准随意走动;可他们三个都坐在地上,神情十分郁郁,看上去像一群陷入绝望的人。

paragraphs.en: This put me in mind of the first time when I came on shore, and began to look about me; how I gave myself over for lost; how wildly I looked round me; what dreadful apprehensions I had; and how I lodged in the tree all night for fear of being devoured by wild beasts.
paragraphs.cn: 这叫我想起自己头一回上岸、开始四下张望时的光景;我如何自认必死无疑;我如何惊惶失措地环顾四周;我心里有过何等可怕的忧惧;又如何整夜栖身树上,唯恐被野兽吞噬。

paragraphs.en: As I knew nothing that night of the supply I was to receive by the providential driving of the ship nearer the land by the storms and tide, by which I have since been so long nourished and supported; so these three poor desolate men knew nothing how certain of deliverance and supply they were, how near it was to them, and how effectually and really they were in a condition of safety, at the same time that they thought themselves lost and their case desperate.
paragraphs.cn: 那一夜我全然不知,凭着上天的安排,风暴和潮水会把船更往岸边推来,让我此后得着接济、被供养扶持了这么久;同样地,这三个凄凉可怜的人也全然不知,他们离得救和接济已如此确定、如此之近,不知在他们自以为已经完了、走投无路的同时,他们其实已实实在在处于安全之境。

paragraphs.en: So little do we see before us in the world, and so much reason have we to depend cheerfully upon the great Maker of the world, that He does not leave His creatures so absolutely destitute, but that in the worst circumstances they have always something to be thankful for, and sometimes are nearer deliverance than they imagine; nay, are even brought to their deliverance by the means by which they seem to be brought to their destruction.
paragraphs.cn: 我们在这世上看得如此浅近,又如此有理由欢欣地仰仗那创造世界的伟大主宰:祂并不把祂造的生灵撇在全然一无所有的境地,反倒使他们即便身处最糟的境况,也总有可感恩之处,有时离得救比他们所想象的还要近;不止如此,他们甚至是被那些看似要把他们引向毁灭的途径带向了得救。

paragraphs.en: It was just at high-water when these people came on shore; and while they rambled about to see what kind of a place they were in, they had carelessly stayed till the tide was spent, and the water was ebbed considerably away, leaving their boat aground.
paragraphs.cn: 这些人上岸时正值高潮;他们四处闲逛、要看看自己置身何处,不留神耽搁到潮水退尽,水已退去老远,把他们的小船搁在了浅滩上。

paragraphs.en: They had left two men in the boat, who, as I found afterwards, having drunk a little too much brandy, fell asleep; however, one of them waking a little sooner than the other and finding the boat too fast aground for him to stir it, hallooed out for the rest, who were straggling about: upon which they all soon came to the boat: but it was past all their strength to launch her, the boat being very heavy, and the shore on that side being a soft oozy sand, almost like a quicksand.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在船上留了两个人,我后来发现,这两人喝了点过量的白兰地睡着了;不过其中一个醒得比另一个稍早些,发觉船搁得太牢,凭他一人挪不动,便高声喊那些四处闲荡的人:他们听见后很快都来到船边:可任凭他们使尽力气也没法把船推下水,那船很沉,而那一边的岸又是软软的、湿黏的沙,几乎像流沙一般。

paragraphs.en: In this condition, like true seamen, who are, perhaps, the least of all mankind given to forethought, they gave it over, and away they strolled about the country again; and I heard one of them say aloud to another, calling them off from the boat, “Why, let her alone, Jack, can’t you? she’ll float next tide;” by which I was fully confirmed in the main inquiry of what countrymen they were.
paragraphs.cn: 在这般境地下,他们像十足的水手——水手大概是天下最不肯预先筹划的一类人——便撂开手不管了,又溜达着往乡野里逛去;我听见他们中一个大声对另一个说,把众人从船边招呼开:“嗨,别管它了,杰克,行不行?下一回潮它自会浮起来;”这一句让我彻底证实了我一直最想弄清的那个问题——他们是哪国人。

paragraphs.en: All this while I kept myself very close, not once daring to stir out of my castle any farther than to my place of observation near the top of the hill: and very glad I was to think how well it was fortified.
paragraphs.cn: 这整段时间里,我把自己藏得极严,一次也不敢从城堡里出去,顶多到山顶附近我那观察点为止:一想到城堡防守得如此稳固,我便十分庆幸。

paragraphs.en: I knew it was no less than ten hours before the boat could float again, and by that time it would be dark, and I might be at more liberty to see their motions, and to hear their discourse, if they had any.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道那船非得再过整整十个钟头才能重新浮起,到那时候天已黑了,我便能更自在地窥看他们的举动,若他们有什么言谈,也好听上一听。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime I fitted myself up for a battle as before, though with more caution, knowing I had to do with another kind of enemy than I had at first.
paragraphs.cn: 这中间我像先前那样整装备战,只是更加谨慎,因为我知道这回要对付的是另一种敌人,不同于我起初遇到的。

paragraphs.en: I ordered Friday also, whom I had made an excellent marksman with his gun, to load himself with arms.
paragraphs.cn: 我也吩咐星期五——我已把他训练成一名出色的枪手——给自己身上装满武器。

paragraphs.en: I took myself two fowling-pieces, and I gave him three muskets.
paragraphs.cn: 我自己拿了两支鸟枪,又给了他三支火枪。

paragraphs.en: My figure, indeed, was very fierce; I had my formidable goat-skin coat on, with the great cap I have mentioned, a naked sword by my side, two pistols in my belt, and a gun upon each shoulder.
paragraphs.cn: 我这副模样着实凶悍:身上穿着那件吓人的羊皮外套,戴着我提过的那顶大帽子,腰边挂一把出鞘的剑,腰带里插两支手枪,两肩上各扛一支枪。

paragraphs.en: It was my design, as I said above, not to have made any attempt till it was dark; but about two o’clock, being the heat of the day, I found that they were all gone straggling into the woods, and, as I thought, laid down to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 如我上文所说,我的打算本是不到天黑不下手;可约摸两点钟、正是一天最热的时候,我发觉他们全都散着走进林子里去了,照我看是躺下睡觉了。

paragraphs.en: The three poor distressed men, too anxious for their condition to get any sleep, had, however, sat down under the shelter of a great tree, at about a quarter of a mile from me, and, as I thought, out of sight of any of the rest.
paragraphs.cn: 那三个可怜的落难人,因为太为自己的处境焦虑而丝毫睡不着,却也在离我约摸四分之一英里的一棵大树荫下坐了下来,照我看是躲开了其余人的视线。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I resolved to discover myself to them, and learn something of their condition; immediately I marched as above, my man Friday at a good distance behind me, as formidable for his arms as I, but not making quite so staring a spectre-like figure as I did.
paragraphs.cn: 见此我便决意在他们面前现身,探听些他们境况的消息;我立刻照上面说的那样进发,我的仆人星期五远远跟在我身后,他武装得和我一样叫人生畏,却不像我这般摆出一副呆愣愣、鬼影似的怪相。

paragraphs.en: I came as near them undiscovered as I could, and then, before any of them saw me, I called aloud to them in Spanish, “What are ye, gentlemen?”
paragraphs.cn: 我尽量不被察觉地走到离他们很近的地方,然后,趁他们谁也没看见我,我用西班牙语高声向他们喊道:“你们是什么人,先生们?”

paragraphs.en: They started up at the noise, but were ten times more confounded when they saw me, and the uncouth figure that I made.
paragraphs.cn: 他们听见声响一下子跳了起来,可等他们看见我、看见我这副古怪的模样,便惊惶了十倍。

paragraphs.en: They made no answer at all, but I thought I perceived them just going to fly from me, when I spoke to them in English.
paragraphs.cn: 他们压根没答话,我倒觉察出他们正要从我面前逃开,这时我改用英语向他们说话。

paragraphs.en: “Gentlemen,” said I, “do not be surprised at me; perhaps you may have a friend near when you did not expect it.”
paragraphs.cn: “先生们,”我说,“不必见我而惊慌;也许你们身边有位朋友,是你们不曾料到的。”

paragraphs.en: “He must be sent directly from heaven then,” said one of them very gravely to me, and pulling off his hat at the same time to me; “for our condition is past the help of man.”
paragraphs.cn: “那他一定是直接从天上派来的了,”他们中一人十分郑重地对我说,同时向我脱下帽子;“因为我们的处境已非人力所能救。”

paragraphs.en: “All help is from heaven, sir,” said I, “but can you put a stranger in the way to help you? for you seem to be in some great distress.
paragraphs.cn: “一切救助都来自上天,先生,”我说,“可你能否指点一个陌生人如何来搭救你们?因为你们看来正陷于极大的困厄之中。

paragraphs.en: I saw you when you landed; and when you seemed to make application to the brutes that came with you, I saw one of them lift up his sword to kill you.”
paragraphs.cn: 你们登陆时我看见了;当你们仿佛在向同来的那些畜生般的家伙哀求时,我看见其中一个举起剑来要杀你。”

paragraphs.en: The poor man, with tears running down his face, and trembling, looking like one astonished, returned, “Am I talking to God or man?
paragraphs.cn: 那可怜人泪流满面,浑身发抖,神情像大受惊愕的人,答道:“我是在同神说话,还是在同人说话?

paragraphs.en: Is it a real man or an angel?”
paragraphs.cn: 这是个真人,还是个天使?”

paragraphs.en: “Be in no fear about that, sir,” said I; “if God had sent an angel to relieve you, he would have come better clothed, and armed after another manner than you see me; pray lay aside your fears; I am a man, an Englishman, and disposed to assist you; you see I have one servant only; we have arms and ammunition; tell us freely, can we serve you?
paragraphs.cn: “这一点你尽管不必害怕,先生,”我说;“若上帝派了个天使来救你,他会穿得比这体面、武装得比你眼下所见的我另有一番气派;请把你的恐惧撇开吧;我是个人,一个英国人,乐意来帮你们;你瞧,我只有一个仆人;我们有武器和弹药;痛痛快快告诉我们,我们能为你们效力吗?

paragraphs.en: What is your case?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们的遭遇是怎么回事?”

paragraphs.en: “Our case, sir,” said he, “is too long to tell you while our murderers are so near us; but, in short, sir, I was commander of that ship—my men have mutinied against me; they have been hardly prevailed on not to murder me, and, at last, have set me on shore in this desolate place, with these two men with me—one my mate, the other a passenger—where we expected to perish, believing the place to be uninhabited, and know not yet what to think of it.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们的遭遇,先生,”他说,“趁那些谋害我们的人离我们这么近,一时说不完;可简而言之,先生,我原是那艘船的船长——我的人叛变了;好不容易才劝住他们没杀我,末了把我撂在这荒凉的地方上了岸,同来的还有这两个人——一个是我的大副,另一个是乘客——我们本以为必死在此地,以为这地方无人居住,至今还不知该怎么看它。”

paragraphs.en: “Where are these brutes, your enemies?” said I; “do you know where they are gone?”
paragraphs.cn: “这些畜生,你的仇敌,眼下在哪里?”我说;“你知道他们去了何处吗?”

paragraphs.en: “There they lie, sir,” said he, pointing to a thicket of trees; “my heart trembles for fear they have seen us and heard you speak; if they have, they will certainly murder us all.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们就躺在那边,先生,”他说,指着一丛树;“我心里直发抖,生怕他们已看见我们、听见你说话;若真如此,他们必定要把我们全都害死。”

paragraphs.en: “Have they any firearms?” said I.
paragraphs.cn: “他们有火器吗?”我说。

paragraphs.en: He answered, “They had only two pieces, one of which they left in the boat.”
paragraphs.cn: 他答道:“他们只有两支枪,其中一支还留在船上。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, then,” said I, “leave the rest to me; I see they are all asleep; it is an easy thing to kill them all; but shall we rather take them prisoners?”
paragraphs.cn: “那好,”我说,“其余的事交给我;我看他们都睡着了;把他们全杀掉是件容易事;不过我们要不要索性把他们捉作俘虏?”

paragraphs.en: He told me there were two desperate villains among them that it was scarce safe to show any mercy to; but if they were secured, he believed all the rest would return to their duty.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我,他们中间有两个亡命的恶棍,几乎不宜对他们施以任何仁慈;但若把这两人制住,他相信其余人都会重归本分。

paragraphs.en: I asked him which they were.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他是哪两个。

paragraphs.en: He told me he could not at that distance distinguish them, but he would obey my orders in anything I would direct.
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉我,隔这么远他分辨不出他们,但无论我如何指派,他都会遵我号令。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” says I, “let us retreat out of their view or hearing, lest they awake, and we will resolve further.”
paragraphs.cn: “好,”我说,“咱们退到他们看不见、听不着的地方去,免得惊醒他们,再作进一步的商量。”

paragraphs.en: So they willingly went back with me, till the woods covered us from them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们心甘情愿地随我退了回去,直到树林把我们同他们遮隔开来。

paragraphs.en: “Look you, sir,” said I, “if I venture upon your deliverance, are you willing to make two conditions with me?”
paragraphs.cn: “你瞧,先生,”我说,“若我冒险来搭救你们,你可愿意同我立下两个条件?”

paragraphs.en: He anticipated my proposals by telling me that both he and the ship, if recovered, should be wholly directed and commanded by me in everything; and if the ship was not recovered, he would live and die with me in what part of the world soever I would send him; and the two other men said the same.
paragraphs.cn: 他抢在我提议之前便说,他本人以及那艘船——若能夺回的话——在一切事情上都完全听凭我指挥调度;若船夺不回来,那么无论我打发他去世上哪一处,他都愿与我同生共死;另外那两个人也说了同样的话。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” says I, “my conditions are but two; first, that while you stay in this island with me, you will not pretend to any authority here; and if I put arms in your hands, you will, upon all occasions, give them up to me, and do no prejudice to me or mine upon this island, and in the meantime be governed by my orders; secondly, that if the ship is or may be recovered, you will carry me and my man to England passage free.”
paragraphs.cn: “好,”我说,“我的条件只有两个;第一,你们和我一同留在这岛上期间,不得在此擅自妄称任何权柄;若我把武器交到你们手里,你们须一有需要便交还给我,不得在这岛上损害我或我的人,这期间一切听我号令;第二,若那船夺回或能夺回,你们须免费送我和我的仆人回英国。”

paragraphs.en: He gave me all the assurances that the invention or faith of man could devise that he would comply with these most reasonable demands, and besides would owe his life to me, and acknowledge it upon all occasions as long as he lived.
paragraphs.cn: 他把人所能想出的、凭机智或凭信义所能立下的一切保证都给了我,说他必依从这几项极其合情合理的要求,此外还说他这条命都欠了我的,只要他活着,便逢人便认这份恩情。

paragraphs.en: “Well, then,” said I, “here are three muskets for you, with powder and ball; tell me next what you think is proper to be done.”
paragraphs.cn: “那好,”我说,“这里有三支火枪给你们,还有火药子弹;接下来告诉我,你觉得该怎么办才妥当。”

paragraphs.en: He showed all the testimonies of his gratitude that he was able, but offered to be wholly guided by me.
paragraphs.cn: 他把他所能表露的一切感激之情都表露了出来,却提出一切都全凭我拿主意。

paragraphs.en: I told him I thought it was very hard venturing anything; but the best method I could think of was to fire on them at once as they lay, and if any were not killed at the first volley, and offered to submit, we might save them, and so put it wholly upon God’s providence to direct the shot.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他,我觉得冒险行事实在艰难;可我所能想到的最好办法,就是趁他们躺着一齐向他们开火,若头一排枪没打死的人愿意投降,我们便可饶他们的命,这样就把弹着一概交托给上帝的安排去指引。

paragraphs.en: He said, very modestly, that he was loath to kill them if he could help it; but that those two were incorrigible villains, and had been the authors of all the mutiny in the ship, and if they escaped, we should be undone still, for they would go on board and bring the whole ship’s company, and destroy us all.
paragraphs.cn: 他十分谦逊地说,若办得到,他不愿杀他们;可那两个人是无可救药的恶棍,是船上那场叛乱的祸首,若让他们逃脱,我们仍要完蛋,因为他们会上船去把全船的人都带来,把我们统统消灭。

paragraphs.en: “Well, then,” says I, “necessity legitimates my advice, for it is the only way to save our lives.”
paragraphs.cn: “那好,”我说,“情势使我这劝告名正言顺,因为这是保住我们性命的唯一办法。”

paragraphs.en: However, seeing him still cautious of shedding blood, I told him they should go themselves, and manage as they found convenient.
paragraphs.cn: 不过,见他仍旧顾虑流血,我便对他说,该由他们自己去动手,怎样方便怎样处置。

paragraphs.en: In the middle of this discourse we heard some of them awake, and soon after we saw two of them on their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 正谈到这话中间,我们听见他们中有几个醒了,不一会儿便见其中两个站起了身。

paragraphs.en: I asked him if either of them were the heads of the mutiny?
paragraphs.cn: 我问他,这两人里有没有叛乱的头目?

paragraphs.en: He said, “No.” “Well, then,” said I, “you may let them escape; and Providence seems to have awakened them on purpose to save themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 他说:“没有。”“那好,”我说,“你可以放他们逃走;上天似乎有意把他们唤醒,好让他们自救。

paragraphs.en: Now,” says I, “if the rest escape you, it is your fault.”
paragraphs.cn: 如今嘛,”我说,“若其余人都从你手里逃脱了,那就是你的过错了。”

paragraphs.en: Animated with this, he took the musket I had given him in his hand, and a pistol in his belt, and his two comrades with him, with each a piece in his hand; the two men who were with him going first made some noise, at which one of the seamen who was awake turned about, and seeing them coming, cried out to the rest; but was too late then, for the moment he cried out they fired—I mean the two men, the captain wisely reserving his own piece.
paragraphs.cn: 受此激励,他把我给他的火枪握在手里,腰带里插了一支手枪,他那两个同伴也跟着他,各人手里拿一支枪;先走的那两个人弄出了些响动,一个醒着的水手闻声转过身来,看见他们过来,便向其余人叫喊;可那时已经太迟,因为他一喊出声,他们便开了火——我是说那两个人开的火,船长很明智地留着自己那支枪没放。

paragraphs.en: They had so well aimed their shot at the men they knew, that one of them was killed on the spot, and the other very much wounded; but not being dead, he started up on his feet, and called eagerly for help to the other; but the captain stepping to him, told him it was too late to cry for help, he should call upon God to forgive his villainy, and with that word knocked him down with the stock of his musket, so that he never spoke more; there were three more in the company, and one of them was slightly wounded.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把枪口对准自己认得的那几个人,瞄得极准,其中一个当场毙命,另一个身受重伤;但没有立时死去,他一跃站起,急切地向另一个人呼救;可船长跨上前去,对他说此刻呼救已太迟,该向上帝祈求宽恕他的罪恶,说着这话便用火枪的枪托把他打倒,叫他再也说不出话来;这一伙里还剩三个人,其中一个受了点轻伤。

paragraphs.en: By this time I was come; and when they saw their danger, and that it was in vain to resist, they begged for mercy.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候我已赶到;他们一见大祸临头、抵抗也是枉然,便求起饶来。

paragraphs.en: The captain told them he would spare their lives if they would give him an assurance of their abhorrence of the treachery they had been guilty of, and would swear to be faithful to him in recovering the ship, and afterwards in carrying her back to Jamaica, from whence they came.
paragraphs.cn: 船长对他们说,若他们能向他保证痛恨自己所犯的背叛之罪,并肯起誓忠于他,协助夺回那船,事后把船开回他们出发地牙买加,他便饶他们性命。

paragraphs.en: They gave him all the protestations of their sincerity that could be desired; and he was willing to believe them, and spare their lives, which I was not against, only that I obliged him to keep them bound hand and foot while they were on the island.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把凡是能求得的、表明自己诚意的种种誓言都向他表白了;他也乐意信他们,饶了他们性命,我对此并不反对,只是要他把这些人留在岛上期间手脚都捆着。

paragraphs.en: While this was doing, I sent Friday with the captain’s mate to the boat with orders to secure her, and bring away the oars and sails, which they did; and by-and-by three straggling men, that were (happily for them) parted from the rest, came back upon hearing the guns fired; and seeing the captain, who was before their prisoner, now their conqueror, they submitted to be bound also; and so our victory was complete.
paragraphs.cn: 趁着办这事的当口,我打发星期五和船长的大副去那小船那里,吩咐他们把船看管住,并把船桨和帆带回来,他们照办了;过了一会儿,有三个四散的人——算他们走运,同其余人分开了——听见枪响便折了回来;他们看见先前身为他们俘虏的船长如今成了他们的征服者,便也甘愿被捆起来;我们的胜利就此圆满。

paragraphs.en: It now remained that the captain and I should inquire into one another’s circumstances.
paragraphs.cn: 如今剩下的,便是船长和我彼此打听一番各自的境遇了。

paragraphs.en: I began first, and told him my whole history, which he heard with an attention even to amazement—and particularly at the wonderful manner of my being furnished with provisions and ammunition; and, indeed, as my story is a whole collection of wonders, it affected him deeply.
paragraphs.cn: 我先开的头,把我的全部经历讲给他听,他听得聚精会神,直到惊叹不已——尤其对我竟能奇妙地备下粮食弹药一事;说实话,我这故事本就是一整部奇迹的汇集,深深打动了他。

paragraphs.en: But when he reflected from thence upon himself, and how I seemed to have been preserved there on purpose to save his life, the tears ran down his face, and he could not speak a word more.
paragraphs.cn: 可当他由此反观自身,想到我仿佛是特意被保全在此以救他性命时,泪水便顺着他的脸淌了下来,他再也说不出一句话来。

paragraphs.en: After this communication was at an end, I carried him and his two men into my apartment, leading them in just where I came out, viz. at the top of the house, where I refreshed them with such provisions as I had, and showed them all the contrivances I had made during my long, long inhabiting that place.
paragraphs.cn: 这番交谈结束后,我把他和他那两个人领进我的居所,就从我出来的那地方——也就是宅子的顶上——领他们进去,在那里用我现有的食物款待了他们,又把我在那地方长年累月栖居期间做出的种种巧妙营造统统指给他们看。

paragraphs.en: All I showed them, all I said to them, was perfectly amazing; but above all, the captain admired my fortification, and how perfectly I had concealed my retreat with a grove of trees, which having been now planted nearly twenty years, and the trees growing much faster than in England, was become a little wood, so thick that it was impassable in any part of it but at that one side where I had reserved my little winding passage into it.
paragraphs.cn: 我指给他们看的一切、对他们说的一切,都叫他们惊奇不已;但最叫船长赞叹的,是我那道工事,以及我如何用一片树林把我的退身之所遮掩得天衣无缝;这片树如今栽下将近二十年,长得比在英国快得多,已成了一小片树丛,密得除了我留着那条弯弯曲曲小径通进去的那一侧,别处都无法穿行。

paragraphs.en: I told him this was my castle and my residence, but that I had a seat in the country, as most princes have, whither I could retreat upon occasion, and I would show him that too another time; but at present our business was to consider how to recover the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他,这是我的城堡、我的居所,不过我也像大多数君王那样在乡下另有一处别墅,遇有需要便可退往那里,改日我也带他去看看;可眼下我们的正事是筹划如何夺回那船。

paragraphs.en: He agreed with me as to that, but told me he was perfectly at a loss what measures to take, for that there were still six-and-twenty hands on board, who, having entered into a cursed conspiracy, by which they had all forfeited their lives to the law, would be hardened in it now by desperation, and would carry it on, knowing that if they were subdued they would be brought to the gallows as soon as they came to England, or to any of the English colonies, and that, therefore, there would be no attacking them with so small a number as we were.
paragraphs.cn: 在这一点上他同我意见一致,却对我说,他实在拿不定该采取什么办法,因为船上还有二十六个人,他们既已结成一桩该死的阴谋,依法个个都已把性命断送掉了,如今更会因绝望而变得死硬,必将一意孤行,因为他们知道,一旦被制服,他们一回到英国或英国任何殖民地便会被送上绞架,所以凭我们这么点人手是无法进攻他们的。

paragraphs.en: I mused for some time on what he had said, and found it was a very rational conclusion, and that therefore something was to be resolved on speedily, as well to draw the men on board into some snare for their surprise as to prevent their landing upon us, and destroying us.
paragraphs.cn: 我把他这番话琢磨了一阵,觉得这是个极合情理的结论,因此必须速速拿定某个主意,既要把船上那些人引进某个圈套好出其不意地拿住他们,又要防他们登岸来把我们消灭。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, it presently occurred to me that in a little while the ship’s crew, wondering what was become of their comrades and of the boat, would certainly come on shore in their other boat to look for them, and that then, perhaps, they might come armed, and be too strong for us: this he allowed to be rational.
paragraphs.cn: 想到这里,我立时想到:再过不多时,船上的人见同伙和小船久去不归,必定纳闷,准会乘他们那另一条小船上岸来找他们,而到那时,他们也许会带着武器,人多势众,叫我们招架不住:这一点他也承认在理。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, I told him the first thing we had to do was to stave the boat which lay upon the beach, so that they might not carry her off, and taking everything out of her, leave her so far useless as not to be fit to swim.
paragraphs.cn: 见此我便对他说,我们头一件要做的,是把搁在沙滩上的那条小船凿穿,免得他们把它开走,又把船里的东西一概取出,叫它彻底失去用处、无法浮水。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, we went on board, took the arms which were left on board out of her, and whatever else we found there—which was a bottle of brandy, and another of rum, a few biscuit-cakes, a horn of powder, and a great lump of sugar in a piece of canvas (the sugar was five or six pounds): all which was very welcome to me, especially the brandy and sugar, of which I had had none left for many years.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我们上了那船,把留在船上的武器取了出来,以及我们在里面找到的一切别的东西——那是一瓶白兰地、另一瓶朗姆酒、几块饼干、一角火药,还有一大块用帆布裹着的糖(那糖有五六磅重):这一切对我都极受用,尤其那白兰地和糖,这两样我已多年一点不剩了。

paragraphs.en: When we had carried all these things on shore (the oars, mast, sail, and rudder of the boat were carried away before), we knocked a great hole in her bottom, that if they had come strong enough to master us, yet they could not carry off the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 等我们把这些东西全搬上岸后(船的桨、桅、帆和舵先前已被搬走),我们在船底凿了个大洞,这样一来,哪怕他们来得人多势众制住了我们,也没法把这条小船开走。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, it was not much in my thoughts that we could be able to recover the ship; but my view was, that if they went away without the boat, I did not much question to make her again fit to carry us to the Leeward Islands, and call upon our friends the Spaniards in my way, for I had them still in my thoughts.
paragraphs.cn: 说实话,我心里并没怎么指望我们真能夺回那艘大船;可我的用意是:若他们撇下这条小船离去,我不大怀疑自己能把它重新修好,载我们去背风群岛,途中还能去拜访我们那些西班牙朋友,因为我心里始终惦记着他们。

paragraphs.en: While we were thus preparing our designs, and had first, by main strength, heaved the boat upon the beach, so high that the tide would not float her off at high-water mark, and besides, had broke a hole in her bottom too big to be quickly stopped, and were set down musing what we should do, we heard the ship fire a gun, and make a waft with her ensign as a signal for the boat to come on board—but no boat stirred; and they fired several times, making other signals for the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 我们正这样筹划着，先是用尽力气把小船拖到沙滩上很高的地方，让涨潮时的水线也漂不走它，还在船底凿了一个大洞，一时半会儿堵不上，然后坐下来盘算该怎么办；就在这时，我们听见大船放了一炮，又挥动旗帜发出信号，叫小船回船上去——可是没有一条小船动弹；他们放了好几炮，又打出别的信号催那小船。

paragraphs.en: At last, when all their signals and firing proved fruitless, and they found the boat did not stir, we saw them, by the help of my glasses, hoist another boat out and row towards the shore; and we found, as they approached, that there were no less than ten men in her, and that they had firearms with them.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他们所有的信号和炮声都白费了，发现那小船毫无动静，我们便借助我的望远镜看见他们放下了另一条小船，朝岸边划来；等他们靠近时，我们发现船上不下十个人，而且都带着火器。

paragraphs.en: As the ship lay almost two leagues from the shore, we had a full view of them as they came, and a plain sight even of their faces; because the tide having set them a little to the east of the other boat, they rowed up under shore, to come to the same place where the other had landed, and where the boat lay; by this means, I say, we had a full view of them, and the captain knew the persons and characters of all the men in the boat, of whom, he said, there were three very honest fellows, who, he was sure, were led into this conspiracy by the rest, being over-powered and frightened; but that as for the boatswain, who it seems was the chief officer among them, and all the rest, they were as outrageous as any of the ship’s crew, and were no doubt made desperate in their new enterprise; and terribly apprehensive he was that they would be too powerful for us.
paragraphs.cn: 大船离岸差不多有两里格远，他们划过来时我们把他们看得一清二楚，连脸都看得分明；因为潮水把他们冲到比先前那条小船略偏东一点的地方，他们便贴着岸边划，想到先前那条船靠岸和停泊的同一地点；就这样，我说，我们把他们看得一清二楚，船长认得船上每个人的相貌和为人，他说其中有三个很老实的家伙，他敢肯定是被其余的人裹挟、又被威逼吓唬着卷进这场阴谋的；但至于那水手长——看来他是他们中间的头目——以及其余所有人，都跟船上那帮暴徒一样凶悍，眼下干这新勾当无疑更是穷凶极恶；他非常担心他们的势力对我们来说太强了。

paragraphs.en: I smiled at him, and told him that men in our circumstances were past the operation of fear; that seeing almost every condition that could be was better than that which we were supposed to be in, we ought to expect that the consequence, whether death or life, would be sure to be a deliverance.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝他笑了笑，对他说，像我们这样处境的人早已不受恐惧的摆布了；眼看几乎任何一种境况都比我们眼下想象的处境要好，我们就该指望不管结局是死是活，都必定是一种解脱。

paragraphs.en: I asked him what he thought of the circumstances of my life, and whether a deliverance were not worth venturing for?
paragraphs.cn: 我问他，他怎么看我这一生的遭遇，难道一场解救不值得去冒一冒险吗？

paragraphs.en: “And where, sir,” said I, “is your belief of my being preserved here on purpose to save your life, which elevated you a little while ago?
paragraphs.cn: “还有，先生，”我说，“你刚才还那么振奋，说我是天意留在这儿专为救你性命的，你那份信念如今哪儿去了？

paragraphs.en: For my part,” said I, “there seems to be but one thing amiss in all the prospect of it.”
paragraphs.cn: 至于我，”我说，“这整桩事的前景里，好像只有一件事不对劲。”

paragraphs.en: “What is that?” say he.
paragraphs.cn: “是什么事？”他问。

paragraphs.en: “Why,” said I, “it is, that as you say there are three or four honest fellows among them which should be spared, had they been all of the wicked part of the crew I should have thought God’s providence had singled them out to deliver them into your hands; for depend upon it, every man that comes ashore is our own, and shall die or live as they behave to us.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，”我说，“就是照你所说，他们中间有三四个老实人应当放过；要是他们全是船上那帮坏蛋，我倒会以为是上帝的旨意把他们挑出来交到你手里；因为你放心好了，凡是上岸来的人都归我们摆布，是死是活全看他们怎么对待我们。”

paragraphs.en: As I spoke this with a raised voice and cheerful countenance, I found it greatly encouraged him; so we set vigorously to our business.
paragraphs.cn: 我提高嗓门、面带喜色说这番话时，发觉这大大鼓舞了他；于是我们精神抖擞地干起自己的活来。

paragraphs.en: We had, upon the first appearance of the boat’s coming from the ship, considered of separating our prisoners; and we had, indeed, secured them effectually.
paragraphs.cn: 小船一从大船那边过来，我们就一见苗头便盘算着把俘虏分开关押；我们也确实把他们看管得妥妥当当。

paragraphs.en: Two of them, of whom the captain was less assured than ordinary, I sent with Friday, and one of the three delivered men, to my cave, where they were remote enough, and out of danger of being heard or discovered, or of finding their way out of the woods if they could have delivered themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 其中有两个，船长对他们比对别人更不放心，我就派星期五和获救的三个人中的一个把他们押到我的山洞里，那儿够偏僻，不会有被听见或被发现的危险，就算他们挣脱了，也找不到走出树林的路。

paragraphs.en: Here they left them bound, but gave them provisions; and promised them, if they continued there quietly, to give them their liberty in a day or two; but that if they attempted their escape they should be put to death without mercy.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把这两人捆着留在那里，可给了他们吃的；还答应他们，只要老老实实待着，过一两天就还他们自由；但要是他们企图逃跑，就毫不留情地处死。

paragraphs.en: They promised faithfully to bear their confinement with patience, and were very thankful that they had such good usage as to have provisions and light left them; for Friday gave them candles (such as we made ourselves) for their comfort; and they did not know but that he stood sentinel over them at the entrance.
paragraphs.cn: 这两人诚心诚意地保证会耐着性子受这份囚禁，还很感激能得到这么好的待遇，有吃的、有灯火；因为星期五给了他们蜡烛（是我们自己做的那种）以求安心；他们还以为星期五在洞口站岗看着他们呢。

paragraphs.en: The other prisoners had better usage; two of them were kept pinioned, indeed, because the captain was not able to trust them; but the other two were taken into my service, upon the captain’s recommendation, and upon their solemnly engaging to live and die with us; so with them and the three honest men we were seven men, well armed; and I made no doubt we should be able to deal well enough with the ten that were coming, considering that the captain had said there were three or four honest men among them also.
paragraphs.cn: 另外几个俘虏待遇要好些；其中两人确实被反绑着，因为船长信不过他们；但另外两人经船长举荐、又庄严起誓要与我们同生共死，便被我收留听我差遣；这样，加上他们和那三个老实人，我们一共有七个全副武装的人；我毫不怀疑，我们完全对付得了正过来的那十个人，何况船长说过他们里头也有三四个老实人。

paragraphs.en: As soon as they got to the place where their other boat lay, they ran their boat into the beach and came all on shore, hauling the boat up after them, which I was glad to see, for I was afraid they would rather have left the boat at an anchor some distance from the shore, with some hands in her to guard her, and so we should not be able to seize the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一到先前那条小船停靠的地方，就把船冲上沙滩，全都上了岸，还把船往上拖，这我看着很高兴，因为我怕他们宁可把船抛锚停在离岸稍远的地方，留几个人守着，那样我们就没法夺船了。

paragraphs.en: Being on shore, the first thing they did, they ran all to their other boat; and it was easy to see they were under a great surprise to find her stripped, as above, of all that was in her, and a great hole in her bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 上岸后，他们头一件事就是全跑到先前那条船那儿；一眼就看得出，他们发现船像前面说的那样被搬空了、船底还有个大洞，都大吃一惊。

paragraphs.en: After they had mused a while upon this, they set up two or three great shouts, hallooing with all their might, to try if they could make their companions hear; but all was to no purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 他们对着这情形琢磨了一会儿，就扯着嗓子大喊了两三声，拼命呼叫，想看看能不能让同伴听见；可全是白费。

paragraphs.en: Then they came all close in a ring, and fired a volley of their small arms, which indeed we heard, and the echoes made the woods ring.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他们凑成一圈，齐放了一排枪，那声音我们的确听见了，回声在树林里嗡嗡作响。

paragraphs.en: But it was all one; those in the cave, we were sure, could not hear; and those in our keeping, though they heard it well enough, yet durst give no answer to them.
paragraphs.cn: 可这也白搭；山洞里那几个，我们敢肯定听不见；而我们看管着的那几个，虽然听得清清楚楚，却不敢应他们一声。

paragraphs.en: They were so astonished at the surprise of this, that, as they told us afterwards, they resolved to go all on board again to their ship, and let them know that the men were all murdered, and the long-boat staved; accordingly, they immediately launched their boat again, and got all of them on board.
paragraphs.cn: 他们对这怪事惊愕万分，后来他们告诉我们，他们决定全都回到大船上去，好让船上的人知道那些人全被杀了、大艇也被凿坏了；于是他们立刻又把小船推下水，全都上了船。

paragraphs.en: The captain was terribly amazed, and even confounded, at this, believing they would go on board the ship again and set sail, giving their comrades over for lost, and so he should still lose the ship, which he was in hopes we should have recovered; but he was quickly as much frightened the other way.
paragraphs.cn: 船长对此大为惊骇，甚至张皇失措，只当他们会回到大船上扬帆而去，把同伙当作已经没命的，那样他还是会失掉这条船——他本指望我们能把船夺回来的；可他很快又被另一头的情形吓着了。

paragraphs.en: They had not been long put off with the boat, when we perceived them all coming on shore again; but with this new measure in their conduct, which it seems they consulted together upon, viz. to leave three men in the boat, and the rest to go on shore, and go up into the country to look for their fellows.
paragraphs.cn: 他们撑着船离岸没多久，我们就看见他们全又朝岸边过来；不过他们的行动里有了个新花样，看来是他们商量好的，就是留三个人在船上，其余的人上岸，进到岛内地去找他们的同伙。

paragraphs.en: This was a great disappointment to us, for now we were at a loss what to do, as our seizing those seven men on shore would be no advantage to us if we let the boat escape; because they would row away to the ship, and then the rest of them would be sure to weigh and set sail, and so our recovering the ship would be lost.
paragraphs.cn: 这对我们是个大扫兴，因为现在我们没了主意，若让那条船跑掉，就算擒住上岸的那七个人也没什么用；因为他们会划回大船去，剩下的人便一定会起锚扬帆，那样我们夺船的指望就落空了。

paragraphs.en: However, we had no remedy but to wait and see what the issue of things might present.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我们别无办法，只能等着看事情会有什么结果。

paragraphs.en: The seven men came on shore, and the three who remained in the boat put her off to a good distance from the shore, and came to an anchor to wait for them; so that it was impossible for us to come at them in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 那七个人上了岸，留在船上的三个人把船撑到离岸挺远的地方抛了锚，等着他们；这样我们就根本没法接近船上的人。

paragraphs.en: Those that came on shore kept close together, marching towards the top of the little hill under which my habitation lay; and we could see them plainly, though they could not perceive us.
paragraphs.cn: 上岸的那几个紧紧挤在一起，朝着我住处底下那座小山的山顶行进；我们把他们看得清清楚楚，他们却察觉不到我们。

paragraphs.en: We should have been very glad if they would have come nearer us, so that we might have fired at them, or that they would have gone farther off, that we might come abroad.
paragraphs.cn: 要是他们肯再走近我们些，让我们好开枪打他们，或者干脆走远些，让我们好出去活动，那我们就再高兴不过了。

paragraphs.en: But when they were come to the brow of the hill where they could see a great way into the valleys and woods, which lay towards the north-east part, and where the island lay lowest, they shouted and hallooed till they were weary; and not caring, it seems, to venture far from the shore, nor far from one another, they sat down together under a tree to consider it.
paragraphs.cn: 可等他们到了山脊上，能望见东北面那片山谷和树林里很远的地方——那也是岛上地势最低的一带——他们喊叫呼唤，一直喊到累了；看来他们既不敢离岸太远，也不敢彼此离得太开，就一起在一棵树下坐下来合计。

paragraphs.en: Had they thought fit to have gone to sleep there, as the other part of them had done, they had done the job for us; but they were too full of apprehensions of danger to venture to go to sleep, though they could not tell what the danger was they had to fear.
paragraphs.cn: 他们要是想在那儿睡上一觉，像先头那伙人那样，那可就替我们把事办成了；可他们满心怕有危险，不敢冒险睡觉，虽说他们也说不清所怕的危险究竟是什么。

paragraphs.en: The captain made a very just proposal to me upon this consultation of theirs, viz. that perhaps they would all fire a volley again, to endeavour to make their fellows hear, and that we should all sally upon them just at the juncture when their pieces were all discharged, and they would certainly yield, and we should have them without bloodshed.
paragraphs.cn: 就着他们这番合计，船长向我提了一个很在理的建议，就是：说不定他们会再齐放一排枪，想让同伙听见，那么就趁他们的枪都放空了的当口，我们全体一齐扑上去，他们准会投降，我们就能兵不血刃地拿下他们。

paragraphs.en: I liked this proposal, provided it was done while we were near enough to come up to them before they could load their pieces again.
paragraphs.cn: 我很赞成这个提议，只要动手时我们离得够近，能在他们重新装弹之前冲到他们跟前。

paragraphs.en: But this event did not happen; and we lay still a long time, very irresolute what course to take.
paragraphs.cn: 可这情形并没发生；我们静静地趴了好久，拿不定该采取什么办法。

paragraphs.en: At length I told them there would be nothing done, in my opinion, till night; and then, if they did not return to the boat, perhaps we might find a way to get between them and the shore, and so might use some stratagem with them in the boat to get them on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 末了我对他们说，依我看天黑之前不会有什么动静；到那时，要是他们不回小船去，我们或许能想法子插到他们和岸边之间，那样就能对船上的人用点计策，把他们诱上岸来。

paragraphs.en: We waited a great while, though very impatient for their removing; and were very uneasy when, after long consultation, we saw them all start up and march down towards the sea; it seems they had such dreadful apprehensions of the danger of the place that they resolved to go on board the ship again, give their companions over for lost, and so go on with their intended voyage with the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 我们等了好长一阵，虽然急切地盼着他们挪窝；等到他们商量了半天，我们看见他们全都站起身来朝海边走去时，我们很不安；看来他们对这地方危险的恐惧太深了，决意再回到大船上去，把同伙当作没命的，就这样驾着船继续他们原定的航程。

paragraphs.en: As soon as I perceived them go towards the shore, I imagined it to be as it really was that they had given over their search, and were going back again; and the captain, as soon as I told him my thoughts, was ready to sink at the apprehensions of it; but I presently thought of a stratagem to fetch them back again, and which answered my end to a tittle.
paragraphs.cn: 我一见他们朝岸边走去，就料到实情正是如此——他们已经放弃搜寻，要往回走了；我把想法一告诉船长，他一听那份忧惧几乎要瘫倒；可我立刻想出一条计策把他们诱回来，这计策把我要的效果办得分毫不差。

paragraphs.en: I ordered Friday and the captain’s mate to go over the little creek westward, towards the place where the savages came on shore, when Friday was rescued, and so soon as they came to a little rising round, at about half a mile distant, I bid them halloo out, as loud as they could, and wait till they found the seamen heard them; that as soon as ever they heard the seamen answer them, they should return it again; and then, keeping out of sight, take a round, always answering when the others hallooed, to draw them as far into the island and among the woods as possible, and then wheel about again to me by such ways as I directed them.
paragraphs.cn: 我吩咐星期五和船长的大副越过西边那条小河汊，朝当初星期五获救时野人上岸的地方走去；等他们到了约莫半英里外一处小高地，我叫他们扯开嗓子拼命呼喊，等到发觉那些水手听见了；那些水手一应声，他们就马上回应；然后躲着别露面，绕着圈子走，那边一喊他们就应，尽量把那些人往岛内和树林深处引，再照我指的路绕回到我这儿来。

paragraphs.en: They were just going into the boat when Friday and the mate hallooed; and they presently heard them, and answering, ran along the shore westward, towards the voice they heard, when they were stopped by the creek, where the water being up, they could not get over, and called for the boat to come up and set them over; as, indeed, I expected.
paragraphs.cn: 那些人正要上船，星期五和大副喊了起来；他们立刻听见了，一边应答一边沿岸往西朝听见的声音跑去，跑到那条河汊被拦住了，河水涨了过不去，便叫小船过来渡他们过河；果然不出我所料。

paragraphs.en: When they had set themselves over, I observed that the boat being gone a good way into the creek, and, as it were, in a harbour within the land, they took one of the three men out of her, to go along with them, and left only two in the boat, having fastened her to the stump of a little tree on the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 等他们渡过河之后，我留意到那条小船已经开进河汊挺深的地方，仿佛进了一处内陆的港湾，他们从那三个人里拉出一个跟着走，只留两个人在船上，还把船拴在岸边一棵小树的树桩上。

paragraphs.en: This was what I wished for; and immediately leaving Friday and the captain’s mate to their business, I took the rest with me; and, crossing the creek out of their sight, we surprised the two men before they were aware—one of them lying on the shore, and the other being in the boat.
paragraphs.cn: 这正是我求之不得的；我立刻把星期五和船长的大副留下办他们的事，自己带上其余的人；趁他们看不见绕过河汊，趁那两个人还没反应过来就把他们逮住了——一个躺在岸上，另一个在船里。

paragraphs.en: The fellow on shore was between sleeping and waking, and going to start up; the captain, who was foremost, ran in upon him, and knocked him down; and then called out to him in the boat to yield, or he was a dead man.
paragraphs.cn: 岸上那家伙半睡半醒，正要跳起来；冲在最前头的船长扑上去把他打倒；接着朝船里那个喊话叫他投降，不然就没命。

paragraphs.en: They needed very few arguments to persuade a single man to yield, when he saw five men upon him and his comrade knocked down: besides, this was, it seems, one of the three who were not so hearty in the mutiny as the rest of the crew, and therefore was easily persuaded not only to yield, but afterwards to join very sincerely with us.
paragraphs.cn: 要劝一个人投降用不着费多少口舌，何况他眼看五个人扑向他、同伙又被打倒；再说，这人看来正是三个在哗变中不像其余船员那么起劲的人之一，所以很容易就被说服，不但投降，后来还诚心诚意地加入了我们。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, Friday and the captain’s mate so well managed their business with the rest that they drew them, by hallooing and answering, from one hill to another, and from one wood to another, till they not only heartily tired them, but left them where they were, very sure they could not reach back to the boat before it was dark; and, indeed, they were heartily tired themselves also, by the time they came back to us.
paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，星期五和船长的大副把差事办得极妙，靠着一喊一应，把那伙人从一座山引到另一座山、从一片林引到另一片林，不但把他们累得够呛，还把他们撂在半路，料定他们天黑之前绝回不到小船那儿；说真的，等他们回到我们这儿时，他们自己也累得筋疲力尽了。

paragraphs.en: We had nothing now to do but to watch for them in the dark, and to fall upon them, so as to make sure work with them.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我们别无他事，只等趁黑守着他们，一举扑上去把他们收拾干净。

paragraphs.en: It was several hours after Friday came back to me before they came back to their boat; and we could hear the foremost of them, long before they came quite up, calling to those behind to come along; and could also hear them answer, and complain how lame and tired they were, and not able to come any faster: which was very welcome news to us.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五回到我这儿好几个钟头之后，那些人才回到他们的小船那边；早在他们完全走近之前，我们就能听见走在最前头的呼唤后头的快跟上；也能听见后头的应声，抱怨自己又瘸又累、没法走快些：这对我们真是再好不过的消息。

paragraphs.en: At length they came up to the boat: but it is impossible to express their confusion when they found the boat fast aground in the creek, the tide ebbed out, and their two men gone.
paragraphs.cn: 末了他们来到小船跟前：可是当他们发现小船牢牢搁浅在河汊里、潮水已经退去、他们的两个人也不见了时，那份慌乱简直没法形容。

paragraphs.en: We could hear them call one to another in a most lamentable manner, telling one another they were got into an enchanted island; that either there were inhabitants in it, and they should all be murdered, or else there were devils and spirits in it, and they should be all carried away and devoured.
paragraphs.cn: 我们能听见他们你一声我一声地凄惶呼喊，彼此说他们落到了一座着了魔的岛上；要么岛上有人，他们全得被杀；要么岛上有妖魔鬼怪，他们全得被掳去吞掉。

paragraphs.en: They hallooed again, and called their two comrades by their names a great many times; but no answer.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又呼喊起来，一遍遍喊着两个同伴的名字；却没有一点回应。

paragraphs.en: After some time we could see them, by the little light there was, run about, wringing their hands like men in despair, and sometimes they would go and sit down in the boat to rest themselves: then come ashore again, and walk about again, and so the same thing over again.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，借着那点微光，我们能看见他们跑来跑去，像绝望的人那样绞着双手，有时又走去坐在船里歇脚：接着再上岸，再来回走，就这样把同一套动作反反复复。

paragraphs.en: My men would fain have had me give them leave to fall upon them at once in the dark; but I was willing to take them at some advantage, so as to spare them, and kill as few of them as I could; and especially I was unwilling to hazard the killing of any of our men, knowing the others were very well armed.
paragraphs.cn: 我的人很想让我准许他们趁黑一下子扑上去；可我情愿在占些便宜时再动手，好放过他们、尽量少杀几个；尤其我不愿冒险伤了我们自己人，因为我知道对方全副武装。

paragraphs.en: I resolved to wait, to see if they did not separate; and therefore, to make sure of them, I drew my ambuscade nearer, and ordered Friday and the captain to creep upon their hands and feet, as close to the ground as they could, that they might not be discovered, and get as near them as they could possibly before they offered to fire.
paragraphs.cn: 我决意等一等，看他们会不会散开；因此为了稳稳拿住他们，我把埋伏往前挪近了些，吩咐星期五和船长手脚并用地贴着地面爬过去，免得被发现，在动手开枪之前尽量爬到离他们最近的地方。

paragraphs.en: They had not been long in that posture when the boatswain, who was the principal ringleader of the mutiny, and had now shown himself the most dejected and dispirited of all the rest, came walking towards them, with two more of the crew; the captain was so eager at having this principal rogue so much in his power, that he could hardly have patience to let him come so near as to be sure of him, for they only heard his tongue before: but when they came nearer, the captain and Friday, starting up on their feet, let fly at them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们那样趴着没多久，那个水手长——他是这场哗变的头号祸首、如今却比谁都显得沮丧颓丧——朝他们走了过来，还带着两个船员；船长一心想拿住这个头号恶棍，几乎沉不住气等他走近到能稳稳打中，因为先前只听见他的说话声：可等他们走近了，船长和星期五一跃而起，朝他们开了火。

paragraphs.en: The boatswain was killed upon the spot: the next man was shot in the body, and fell just by him, though he did not die till an hour or two after; and the third ran for it.
paragraphs.cn: 那水手长当场毙命：第二个人身上中了弹，倒在他身旁，不过过了一两个钟头才断气；第三个撒腿逃了。

paragraphs.en: At the noise of the fire I immediately advanced with my whole army, which was now eight men, viz. myself, generalissimo; Friday, my lieutenant-general; the captain and his two men, and the three prisoners of war whom we had trusted with arms.
paragraphs.cn: 一听枪响，我立刻率领全军挺进，这军队如今有八个人，就是：我本人，大元帅；星期五，我的副帅；船长和他那两个人，还有三个我们信得过、发了武器的战俘。

paragraphs.en: We came upon them, indeed, in the dark, so that they could not see our number; and I made the man they had left in the boat, who was now one of us, to call them by name, to try if I could bring them to a parley, and so perhaps might reduce them to terms; which fell out just as we desired: for indeed it was easy to think, as their condition then was, they would be very willing to capitulate.
paragraphs.cn: 我们的确是趁黑扑向他们的，所以他们看不清我们有多少人；我叫那个原先留在船上、如今归了我们的人喊他们的名字，看能不能引他们来谈判，那样或许能逼他们就范；这一着果然如我们所愿：因为不难想见，凭他们当时的处境，他们一定很乐意投降求和。

paragraphs.en: So he calls out as loud as he could to one of them, “Tom Smith!
paragraphs.cn: 于是他扯开嗓子朝其中一个尽力喊道：“汤姆·史密斯！

paragraphs.en: Tom Smith!”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·史密斯！”

paragraphs.en: Tom Smith answered immediately, “Is that Robinson?” for it seems he knew the voice.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·史密斯立刻应声：“是罗宾逊吗？”看来他听得出这声音。

paragraphs.en: The other answered, “Ay, ay; for God’s sake, Tom Smith, throw down your arms and yield, or you are all dead men this moment.”
paragraphs.cn: 那人答道：“对，对；看在上帝份上，汤姆·史密斯，快扔下武器投降吧，不然你们这会儿就全都没命了。”

paragraphs.en: “Who must we yield to?
paragraphs.cn: “我们得向谁投降？

paragraphs.en: Where are they?” says Smith again.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在哪儿？”史密斯又问。

paragraphs.en: “Here they are,” says he; “here’s our captain and fifty men with him, have been hunting you these two hours; the boatswain is killed; Will Fry is wounded, and I am a prisoner; and if you do not yield you are all lost.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们就在这儿，”他说，“我们的船长带着五十个人在这儿，找了你们两个钟头了；水手长已经死了；威尔·弗莱受了伤，我当了俘虏；你们要是不投降，就全完了。”

paragraphs.en: “Will they give us quarter, then?” says Tom Smith, “and we will yield.”
paragraphs.cn: “那他们肯饶我们的命吗？”汤姆·史密斯说，“我们就投降。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll go and ask, if you promise to yield,” said Robinson: so he asked the captain, and the captain himself then calls out, “You, Smith, you know my voice; if you lay down your arms immediately and submit, you shall have your lives, all but Will Atkins.”
paragraphs.cn: “你要是答应投降，我就去问问，”罗宾逊说：于是他去问船长，船长便亲自喊道：“史密斯，你听得出我的声音；只要你们立刻放下武器归顺，就都能保住性命，只有威尔·阿特金斯除外。”

paragraphs.en: Upon this Will Atkins cried out, “For God’s sake, captain, give me quarter; what have I done?
paragraphs.cn: 威尔·阿特金斯一听这话就叫喊起来：“看在上帝份上，船长，饶了我吧；我做了什么？

paragraphs.en: They have all been as bad as I:” which, by the way, was not true; for it seems this Will Atkins was the first man that laid hold of the captain when they first mutinied, and used him barbarously in tying his hands and giving him injurious language.
paragraphs.cn: 他们全都跟我一样坏：”——顺便一提，这话可不实；因为看来当初哗变时头一个揪住船长的正是这个威尔·阿特金斯，还粗暴地把他的手捆起来、对他破口辱骂。

paragraphs.en: However, the captain told him he must lay down his arms at discretion, and trust to the governor’s mercy: by which he meant me, for they all called me governor.
paragraphs.cn: 不过船长告诉他，他必须无条件放下武器，听凭总督发落：他说的总督就是我，因为他们都管我叫总督。

paragraphs.en: In a word, they all laid down their arms and begged their lives; and I sent the man that had parleyed with them, and two more, who bound them all; and then my great army of fifty men, which, with those three, were in all but eight, came up and seized upon them, and upon their boat; only that I kept myself and one more out of sight for reasons of state.
paragraphs.cn: 总之，他们全都放下武器求饶；我便派那个跟他们谈判过的人再带两个人上去，把他们全都捆了；接着我那支五十人的大军——连同那三人其实一共才八个——上前擒住了他们，连船也一并夺下；只是为了摆摆架子，我留着自己和另外一人没有露面。

paragraphs.en: Our next work was to repair the boat, and think of seizing the ship: and as for the captain, now he had leisure to parley with them, he expostulated with them upon the villainy of their practices with him, and upon the further wickedness of their design, and how certainly it must bring them to misery and distress in the end, and perhaps to the gallows.
paragraphs.cn: 我们下一步的事就是修好小船，再谋划夺取大船：至于船长，如今他有工夫跟他们理论了，便责问他们对他所干的种种恶行，责问他们那更为狠毒的图谋，说这一切到头来必定把他们引向凄惨困厄，说不定还得上绞架。

paragraphs.en: They all appeared very penitent, and begged hard for their lives.
paragraphs.cn: 他们个个显得很悔过，苦苦哀求饶命。

paragraphs.en: As for that, he told them they were not his prisoners, but the commander’s of the island; that they thought they had set him on shore in a barren, uninhabited island; but it had pleased God so to direct them that it was inhabited, and that the governor was an Englishman; that he might hang them all there, if he pleased; but as he had given them all quarter, he supposed he would send them to England, to be dealt with there as justice required, except Atkins, whom he was commanded by the governor to advise to prepare for death, for that he would be hanged in the morning.
paragraphs.cn: 说到这个，他告诉他们，他们不是他的俘虏，而是这岛上主管人的俘虏；他们本以为把他撂在了一座荒凉无人的岛上，可上帝偏偏这样安排，让这岛有人居住，而且那总督还是个英国人；总督高兴的话，尽可以把他们全吊死在这儿；不过既然已经饶了他们的命，他料想总督会把他们送回英国，照法律该怎么办就怎么办，只有阿特金斯除外——总督吩咐他去劝阿特金斯准备受死，因为第二天早上就要把他绞死。

paragraphs.en: Though this was all but a fiction of his own, yet it had its desired effect; Atkins fell upon his knees to beg the captain to intercede with the governor for his life; and all the rest begged of him, for God’s sake, that they might not be sent to England.
paragraphs.cn: 这虽然全是他自己编的一套，却收到了他想要的效果；阿特金斯双膝跪下，求船长替他向总督说情保命；其余人也个个看在上帝份上求他，别把他们送回英国去。

paragraphs.en: It now occurred to me that the time of our deliverance was come, and that it would be a most easy thing to bring these fellows in to be hearty in getting possession of the ship; so I retired in the dark from them, that they might not see what kind of a governor they had, and called the captain to me; when I called, at a good distance, one of the men was ordered to speak again, and say to the captain, “Captain, the commander calls for you;” and presently the captain replied, “Tell his excellency I am just coming.”
paragraphs.cn: 这时我心里想到，我们脱身的时候到了，要把这些家伙拉过来死心塌地帮着夺回大船，简直易如反掌；于是我趁黑从他们跟前退开，免得他们看清他们的总督是个什么样的人，然后把船长叫到跟前；我在挺远的地方一叫，就吩咐一个人再开口，对船长说：“船长，主管人叫你过去；”船长随即应道：“回禀大人，我这就来。”

paragraphs.en: This more perfectly amazed them, and they all believed that the commander was just by, with his fifty men.
paragraphs.cn: 这一下把他们唬得更彻底了，个个都当真那位主管人带着他五十个人就在近旁。

paragraphs.en: Upon the captain coming to me, I told him my project for seizing the ship, which he liked wonderfully well, and resolved to put it in execution the next morning.
paragraphs.cn: 船长来到我跟前，我把夺船的计划告诉了他，他大为称赞，决意第二天一早就付诸行动。

paragraphs.en: But, in order to execute it with more art, and to be secure of success, I told him we must divide the prisoners, and that he should go and take Atkins, and two more of the worst of them, and send them pinioned to the cave where the others lay.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，为了办得更巧妙、更有把握成功，我对他说我们得把俘虏分开，他该去把阿特金斯和另外两个最坏的家伙带走，反绑着押到关着别人的那个山洞里去。

paragraphs.en: This was committed to Friday and the two men who came on shore with the captain.
paragraphs.cn: 这差事交给了星期五和随船长上岸的那两个人。

paragraphs.en: They conveyed them to the cave as to a prison: and it was, indeed, a dismal place, especially to men in their condition.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把这几个人押到山洞里，当作牢房：那地方确实阴森可怕，尤其对处在他们那种境地的人来说。

paragraphs.en: The others I ordered to my bower, as I called it, of which I have given a full description: and as it was fenced in, and they pinioned, the place was secure enough, considering they were upon their behaviour.
paragraphs.cn: 其余的人我吩咐押到我那座凉棚里——就是我先前详细描述过的那个；棚子四周有围栏，人又被反绑着，只要他们规规矩矩，那地方就够稳当了。

paragraphs.en: To these in the morning I sent the captain, who was to enter into a parley with them; in a word, to try them, and tell me whether he thought they might be trusted or not to go on board and surprise the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上我把船长打发去见这几个人，让他跟他们谈一谈；一句话，去试探他们，再告诉我他觉得能不能信得过他们，让他们上船去出其不意夺下大船。

paragraphs.en: He talked to them of the injury done him, of the condition they were brought to, and that though the governor had given them quarter for their lives as to the present action, yet that if they were sent to England they would all be hanged in chains; but that if they would join in so just an attempt as to recover the ship, he would have the governor’s engagement for their pardon.
paragraphs.cn: 他跟他们讲了他所受的伤害，讲了他们如今落到的境地，说总督虽然就眼前这桩事饶了他们的命，可他们要是被送回英国，就都得戴着锁链被绞死；但他们若肯参与夺回大船这样一件正当的事，他愿意去求总督许下赦免他们的诺言。

paragraphs.en: Any one may guess how readily such a proposal would be accepted by men in their condition; they fell down on their knees to the captain, and promised, with the deepest imprecations, that they would be faithful to him to the last drop, and that they should owe their lives to him, and would go with him all over the world; that they would own him as a father to them as long as they lived.
paragraphs.cn: 谁都猜得到，处在他们那种境地的人会多么爽快地接受这样的提议；他们跪倒在船长面前，赌着最重的咒发誓要对他忠心到底、直到流尽最后一滴血，说他们这条命都欠了他的，愿意跟着他走遍天涯海角；说只要活着一天，就把他当作父亲一样敬着。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” says the captain, “I must go and tell the governor what you say, and see what I can do to bring him to consent to it.”
paragraphs.cn: “好，”船长说，“我得去把你们的话回禀总督，看我能不能想法子让他答应。”

paragraphs.en: So he brought me an account of the temper he found them in, and that he verily believed they would be faithful.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他回来向我禀报他所看到的他们那副心境，说他确实相信他们会忠心。

paragraphs.en: However, that we might be very secure, I told him he should go back again and choose out those five, and tell them, that they might see he did not want men, that he would take out those five to be his assistants, and that the governor would keep the other two, and the three that were sent prisoners to the castle (my cave), as hostages for the fidelity of those five; and that if they proved unfaithful in the execution, the five hostages should be hanged in chains alive on the shore.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，为了万无一失，我告诉他，他该再回去挑出那五个人，对他们说——好让他们明白他并不缺人手——他要挑出这五个当他的助手，总督则留下另外两个，连同押到城堡（我的山洞）里的那三个俘虏，一共当作那五个人忠心与否的人质；万一他们在行动中不忠，这五个人质就要活着被戴上锁链吊死在岸边。

paragraphs.en: This looked severe, and convinced them that the governor was in earnest; however, they had no way left them but to accept it; and it was now the business of the prisoners, as much as of the captain, to persuade the other five to do their duty.
paragraphs.cn: 这看着够狠，也叫他们信了总督是当真的；然而他们别无办法，只能接受；如今说服另外那五个人尽本分，成了俘虏们跟船长同样上心的事。

paragraphs.en: Our strength was now thus ordered for the expedition: first, the captain, his mate, and passenger; second, the two prisoners of the first gang, to whom, having their character from the captain, I had given their liberty, and trusted them with arms; third, the other two that I had kept till now in my bower, pinioned, but on the captain’s motion had now released; fourth, these five released at last; so that there were twelve in all, besides five we kept prisoners in the cave for hostages.
paragraphs.cn: 我们这次远征的人手于是这样编排：第一，船长、他的大副和那位乘客；第二，头一伙里的两个俘虏，我从船长那儿听了他们的为人后已还他们自由、并信任地发给了武器；第三，另外两个我一直反绑着留在凉棚里、经船长提议如今已释放的人；第四，最后释放的这五个；这样一共十二个人，此外还有五个当人质关在山洞里。

paragraphs.en: I asked the captain if he was willing to venture with these hands on board the ship; but as for me and my man Friday, I did not think it was proper for us to stir, having seven men left behind; and it was employment enough for us to keep them asunder, and supply them with victuals.
paragraphs.cn: 我问船长是否愿意带着这些人手冒险登船夺舰；至于我和我的仆人星期五，我觉得我们不宜挪动，因为后头还留着七个人；把他们分开看管、供给他们吃食，就够我们忙的了。

paragraphs.en: As to the five in the cave, I resolved to keep them fast, but Friday went in twice a day to them, to supply them with necessaries; and I made the other two carry provisions to a certain distance, where Friday was to take them.
paragraphs.cn: 至于山洞里那五个，我决意把他们看牢，不过星期五每天进去两趟，给他们送必需的东西；我又叫另外那两个人把口粮送到一定的地方，由星期五去取。

paragraphs.en: When I showed myself to the two hostages, it was with the captain, who told them I was the person the governor had ordered to look after them; and that it was the governor’s pleasure they should not stir anywhere but by my direction; that if they did, they would be fetched into the castle, and be laid in irons: so that as we never suffered them to see me as governor, I now appeared as another person, and spoke of the governor, the garrison, the castle, and the like, upon all occasions.
paragraphs.cn: 我在那两个人质面前露面时，是同船长一起去的，船长告诉他们，我就是总督派来看管他们的人；还说这是总督的意思，他们除非得到我的指示，哪儿都不许乱动；要是乱动，就要被抓进城堡、戴上镣铐：这样一来，我们从不让他们看出我就是总督，我如今俨然成了另一个人，逢事总把总督、卫戍队、城堡之类挂在嘴上。

paragraphs.en: The captain now had no difficulty before him, but to furnish his two boats, stop the breach of one, and man them.
paragraphs.cn: 眼下船长面前已没什么难事，只消把两条小船备好，堵上其中一条的破洞，配上人手。

paragraphs.en: He made his passenger captain of one, with four of the men; and himself, his mate, and five more, went in the other; and they contrived their business very well, for they came up to the ship about midnight.
paragraphs.cn: 他让那位乘客当一条船的头，带四个人；他自己带着大副和另外五个人上另一条船；他们把事情安排得很周到，约莫半夜时分便驶到了大船跟前。

paragraphs.en: As soon as they came within call of the ship, he made Robinson hail them, and tell them they had brought off the men and the boat, but that it was a long time before they had found them, and the like, holding them in a chat till they came to the ship’s side; when the captain and the mate entering first with their arms, immediately knocked down the second mate and carpenter with the butt-end of their muskets, being very faithfully seconded by their men; they secured all the rest that were upon the main and quarter decks, and began to fasten the hatches, to keep them down that were below; when the other boat and their men, entering at the forechains, secured the forecastle of the ship, and the scuttle which went down into the cook-room, making three men they found there prisoners.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一进到大船喊得应的距离，他就叫罗宾逊向船上喊话，说他们把人和小船都带回来了，只是找了好久才找着他们，诸如此类，跟他们东拉西扯地搭着话，直搭到船边；这时船长和大副先拿着武器登船，立刻用滑膛枪的枪托把二副和木匠打倒，手下人配合得极其得力；他们制住了主甲板和后甲板上其余所有人，动手钉牢舱盖，把底下的人压在下面；这时另一条船和船上的人从前桅链处登船，制住了船头楼和通往厨房的那道舱口，把发现的三个人全俘虏了。

paragraphs.en: When this was done, and all safe upon deck, the captain ordered the mate, with three men, to break into the round-house, where the new rebel captain lay, who, having taken the alarm, had got up, and with two men and a boy had got firearms in their hands; and when the mate, with a crow, split open the door, the new captain and his men fired boldly among them, and wounded the mate with a musket ball, which broke his arm, and wounded two more of the men, but killed nobody.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切办妥、甲板上全都平安之后，船长吩咐大副带三个人闯进后甲板室——新的叛军头目就睡在那里，他已经听到动静爬了起来，跟两个人、一个小厮抄起了火器；等大副拿撬棍把门劈开，那新头目和他的人朝他们大胆开火，一颗滑膛枪弹打伤了大副、打断了他的胳膊，还打伤了另外两个人，但没打死人。

paragraphs.en: The mate, calling for help, rushed, however, into the round-house, wounded as he was, and, with his pistol, shot the new captain through the head, the bullet entering at his mouth, and came out again behind one of his ears, so that he never spoke a word more: upon which the rest yielded, and the ship was taken effectually, without any more lives lost.
paragraphs.cn: 大副虽然带着伤，仍一面呼救一面冲进后甲板室，用手枪一枪打穿了那新头目的脑袋，子弹从他嘴里进去、又从他一只耳朵后头出来，于是他再也说不出一个字来：见此情形其余人便投降了，大船就此彻底夺下，没再折损一条性命。

paragraphs.en: As soon as the ship was thus secured, the captain ordered seven guns to be fired, which was the signal agreed upon with me to give me notice of his success, which, you may be sure, I was very glad to hear, having sat watching upon the shore for it till near two o’clock in the morning.
paragraphs.cn: 大船一这样拿下，船长便吩咐放了七炮，这是先前跟我约好、通知我他成功的信号；你尽可以想见，我听了有多高兴——为了这信号，我在岸上一直守望到快凌晨两点。

paragraphs.en: Having thus heard the signal plainly, I laid me down; and it having been a day of great fatigue to me, I slept very sound, till I was surprised with the noise of a gun; and presently starting up, I heard a man call me by the name of “Governor!
paragraphs.cn: 这样清清楚楚听见了信号，我便躺了下来；这一天叫我大为劳累，我睡得极沉，直到被一声枪响惊醒；我一骨碌爬起来，听见有人喊我“总督！

paragraphs.en: Governor!” and presently I knew the captain’s voice; when, climbing up to the top of the hill, there he stood, and, pointing to the ship, he embraced me in his arms, “My dear friend and deliverer,” says he, “there’s your ship; for she is all yours, and so are we, and all that belong to her.”
paragraphs.cn: 总督！”，我随即听出是船长的声音；我爬上山顶，他就站在那儿，指着大船把我搂进怀里，“我亲爱的朋友、我的救命恩人，”他说，“你的船在那儿呢；因为她整个都归你，我们和船上所有的人也都归你。”

paragraphs.en: I cast my eyes to the ship, and there she rode, within little more than half a mile of the shore; for they had weighed her anchor as soon as they were masters of her, and, the weather being fair, had brought her to an anchor just against the mouth of the little creek; and the tide being up, the captain had brought the pinnace in near the place where I had first landed my rafts, and so landed just at my door.
paragraphs.cn: 我朝那船望去，只见她就停泊在离岸多半英里的地方；因为他们一夺下船就起了锚，趁天气晴好把她开来，正对着那小河汊口抛了锚；又趁潮水涨着，船长把那小艇撑到我当初头一回卸木筏的地方附近，就在我门口靠了岸。

paragraphs.en: I was at first ready to sink down with the surprise; for I saw my deliverance, indeed, visibly put into my hands, all things easy, and a large ship just ready to carry me away whither I pleased to go.
paragraphs.cn: 起初我惊喜得几乎要瘫倒下去；因为我看见我的解救实实在在地送到了我手上，一切都轻而易举，一条大船就等着把我送往我想去的任何地方。

paragraphs.en: At first, for some time, I was not able to answer him one word; but as he had taken me in his arms I held fast by him, or I should have fallen to the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 起先有好一阵子，我一个字也答不上来；幸亏他把我搂在怀里，我死死抓住他，不然我早就瘫倒在地了。

paragraphs.en: He perceived the surprise, and immediately pulled a bottle out of his pocket and gave me a dram of cordial, which he had brought on purpose for me.
paragraphs.cn: 他察觉了我这惊喜，立刻从口袋里掏出一个瓶子，给我喝了一口提神的甜酒，那是他特意为我带来的。

paragraphs.en: After I had drunk it, I sat down upon the ground; and though it brought me to myself, yet it was a good while before I could speak a word to him.
paragraphs.cn: 喝下之后，我在地上坐了下来；那酒虽让我缓过神来，可过了好一会儿我才能对他说出一句话。

paragraphs.en: All this time the poor man was in as great an ecstasy as I, only not under any surprise as I was; and he said a thousand kind and tender things to me, to compose and bring me to myself; but such was the flood of joy in my breast, that it put all my spirits into confusion: at last it broke out into tears, and in a little while after I recovered my speech; I then took my turn, and embraced him as my deliverer, and we rejoiced together.
paragraphs.cn: 这段时间里，那可怜人跟我一样欣喜若狂，只是不像我那样惊愕；他对我说了千百句体贴温存的话，好让我镇定下来、缓过神来；可我胸中喜潮汹涌，把我一身心神都搅乱了：末了化作泪水涌出，又过了一小会儿我才恢复了说话，于是我这才轮到我，把他当作救命恩人搂在怀里，我俩一同欢欣。

paragraphs.en: I told him I looked upon him as a man sent by Heaven to deliver me, and that the whole transaction seemed to be a chain of wonders; that such things as these were the testimonies we had of a secret hand of Providence governing the world, and an evidence that the eye of an infinite Power could search into the remotest corner of the world, and send help to the miserable whenever He pleased.
paragraphs.cn: 我对他说，我把他看作上天派来搭救我的人，说这整桩事仿佛是一连串奇迹；说这类事情正是我们所得的凭据，证明有一只看不见的天意之手在主宰世界，证明那无限之力的眼睛能洞察世上最偏远的角落，只要祂高兴，便随时向可怜人伸出援手。

paragraphs.en: I forgot not to lift up my heart in thankfulness to Heaven; and what heart could forbear to bless Him, who had not only in a miraculous manner provided for me in such a wilderness, and in such a desolate condition, but from whom every deliverance must always be acknowledged to proceed.
paragraphs.cn: 我没忘记举心向上天感恩；有谁的心能忍住不去颂扬祂呢——祂不但奇迹般地在这样一片荒野、这样一种凄凉的境地里供养了我，而且一切解救都必须承认是出于祂的。

paragraphs.en: When we had talked a while, the captain told me he had brought me some little refreshment, such as the ship afforded, and such as the wretches that had been so long his masters had not plundered him of.
paragraphs.cn: 我们谈了一会儿，船长告诉我，他给我带来了一点小小的吃用，是船上现成能有的，也是那帮长久欺压他的坏蛋没从他手里抢走的。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, he called aloud to the boat, and bade his men bring the things ashore that were for the governor; and, indeed, it was a present as if I had been one that was not to be carried away with them, but as if I had been to dwell upon the island still.
paragraphs.cn: 说着，他朝船上大声喊话，吩咐手下把给总督的东西搬上岸来；说真的，那份礼物简直不像是给一个要跟他们一同离开的人，倒像是给一个还要长住在这岛上的人的。

paragraphs.en: First, he had brought me a case of bottles full of excellent cordial waters, six large bottles of Madeira wine (the bottles held two quarts each), two pounds of excellent good tobacco, twelve good pieces of the ship’s beef, and six pieces of pork, with a bag of peas, and about a hundred-weight of biscuit; he also brought me a box of sugar, a box of flour, a bag full of lemons, and two bottles of lime-juice, and abundance of other things.
paragraphs.cn: 首先，他给我带来一箱上好的提神甜酒，六大瓶马德拉葡萄酒（每瓶装两夸脱），两磅极好的烟草，十二块上好的船上腌牛肉，六块腌猪肉，一袋豌豆，还有约莫一英担饼干；他还给我带来一盒糖、一盒面粉、一满袋柠檬、两瓶青柠汁，以及许许多多别的东西。

paragraphs.en: But besides these, and what was a thousand times more useful to me, he brought me six new clean shirts, six very good neckcloths, two pair of gloves, one pair of shoes, a hat, and one pair of stockings, with a very good suit of clothes of his own, which had been worn but very little: in a word, he clothed me from head to foot.
paragraphs.cn: 可除了这些，还有对我有用千百倍的东西，他给我带来了六件干净的新衬衫、六条很好的领巾、两副手套、一双鞋、一顶帽子、一双长袜，还有一套他自己的很好的、几乎没怎么穿过的衣服：一句话，他把我从头到脚打扮了个齐全。

paragraphs.en: It was a very kind and agreeable present, as any one may imagine, to one in my circumstances, but never was anything in the world of that kind so unpleasant, awkward, and uneasy as it was to me to wear such clothes at first.
paragraphs.cn: 谁都想象得到，对我这样处境的人来说，这是一份多么亲切、多么可喜的礼物，可是世上再没有什么东西像这样叫我别扭、笨拙、浑身不自在了——起初穿上这样的衣服，我实在难受。

paragraphs.en: After these ceremonies were past, and after all his good things were brought into my little apartment, we began to consult what was to be done with the prisoners we had; for it was worth considering whether we might venture to take them with us or no, especially two of them, whom he knew to be incorrigible and refractory to the last degree; and the captain said he knew they were such rogues that there was no obliging them, and if he did carry them away, it must be in irons, as malefactors, to be delivered over to justice at the first English colony he could come to; and I found that the captain himself was very anxious about it.
paragraphs.cn: 这些客套过后，等他那些好东西都搬进了我那间小屋，我们便开始商量该怎么处置手上这些俘虏；因为值得好好考虑一下，我们是否敢把他们带上船去，尤其是其中两个，他知道那两人坏到骨子里、桀骜不驯到极点；船长说他知道那两个是这样的恶棍，怎么也管教不了，要是真把他们带走，就非得像对待重罪犯那样给他们戴上锁链，到他所能到的第一个英国殖民地就交给法律发落；我看得出船长自己也很为这事发愁。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, I told him that, if he desired it, I would undertake to bring the two men he spoke of to make it their own request that he should leave them upon the island.
paragraphs.cn: 听了这话，我对他说，只要他愿意，我可以把他说的那两个人弄得由他们自己开口请求，让他把他们留在岛上。

paragraphs.en: “I should be very glad of that,” says the captain, “with all my heart.”
paragraphs.cn: “那我可就太高兴了，”船长说，“我打心底里赞成。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” says I, “I will send for them up and talk with them for you.”
paragraphs.cn: “好，”我说，“我这就派人把他们叫上来，替你跟他们谈谈。”

paragraphs.en: So I caused Friday and the two hostages, for they were now discharged, their comrades having performed their promise; I say, I caused them to go to the cave, and bring up the five men, pinioned as they were, to the bower, and keep them there till I came.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我叫来星期五和那两个人质——他们如今已经获释，因为他们的同伙履行了诺言；我是说，我叫这几个人到山洞去，把那五个反绑着的人带到凉棚来，看着他们，等我过来。

paragraphs.en: After some time, I came thither dressed in my new habit; and now I was called governor again.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，我换上新装来到那里；如今我又被称作总督了。

paragraphs.en: Being all met, and the captain with me, I caused the men to be brought before me, and I told them I had got a full account of their villainous behaviour to the captain, and how they had run away with the ship, and were preparing to commit further robberies, but that Providence had ensnared them in their own ways, and that they were fallen into the pit which they had dug for others.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都到齐、船长陪着我时，我叫人把那几个人带到我面前，对他们说，他们对船长的种种恶行、他们如何劫走大船、又如何正预备去干更多的抢劫勾当，我已经一清二楚，但天意把他们困在了自己的路数里，让他们掉进了自己给别人挖的坑里。

paragraphs.en: I let them know that by my direction the ship had been seized; that she lay now in the road; and they might see by-and-by that their new captain had received the reward of his villainy, and that they would see him hanging at the yard-arm; that, as to them, I wanted to know what they had to say why I should not execute them as pirates taken in the fact, as by my commission they could not doubt but I had authority so to do.
paragraphs.cn: 我让他们知道，那大船是照我的指示夺下的；如今她就停在锚地；他们过一会儿就能看见，他们那新头目已经得到了作恶的报应，会看见他吊在帆桁上；至于他们，我想听听他们有什么话说，凭什么我不该把他们当作当场拿获的海盗处死——依我所受的委任，他们不必怀疑我有权这么做。

paragraphs.en: One of them answered in the name of the rest, that they had nothing to say but this, that when they were taken the captain promised them their lives, and they humbly implored my mercy.
paragraphs.cn: 其中一人代表大家答道，他们没别的可说，只有一句：他们被擒时船长答应过饶他们的命，他们卑微地恳求我开恩。

paragraphs.en: But I told them I knew not what mercy to show them; for as for myself, I had resolved to quit the island with all my men, and had taken passage with the captain to go to England; and as for the captain, he could not carry them to England other than as prisoners in irons, to be tried for mutiny and running away with the ship; the consequence of which, they must needs know, would be the gallows; so that I could not tell what was best for them, unless they had a mind to take their fate in the island.
paragraphs.cn: 可我告诉他们，我不知该向他们施什么恩；因为就我自己而言，我已决意带着全体手下离开此岛，并已搭船长的船前往英国；至于船长，他要带他们去英国，只能把他们当作戴锁链的囚犯，去受哗变和劫船的审判，其结果他们必定明白，就是绞架；所以我说不准怎样对他们才最好，除非他们情愿留在岛上听天由命。

paragraphs.en: If they desired that, as I had liberty to leave the island, I had some inclination to give them their lives, if they thought they could shift on shore.
paragraphs.cn: 他们若情愿如此，既然我可以自由离岛，我倒有几分意思饶他们的命，只要他们觉得自己能在岸上过活下去。

paragraphs.en: They seemed very thankful for it, and said they would much rather venture to stay there than be carried to England to be hanged.
paragraphs.cn: 他们似乎为此很感激，说他们宁可冒险留在那儿，也不愿被带回英国去绞死。

paragraphs.en: So I left it on that issue.
paragraphs.cn: 于是我就这么定下了这件事。

paragraphs.en: However, the captain seemed to make some difficulty of it, as if he durst not leave them there.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，船长似乎对此有点为难，仿佛不敢把他们留在那儿。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I seemed a little angry with the captain, and told him that they were my prisoners, not his; and that seeing I had offered them so much favour, I would be as good as my word; and that if he did not think fit to consent to it I would set them at liberty, as I found them: and if he did not like it he might take them again if he could catch them.
paragraphs.cn: 见此我便装作对船长有点生气，对他说他们是我的俘虏、不是他的；既然我已经给了他们这么大的恩典，我就要说到做到；他要是觉得不便答应，我就照当初见到他们时那样放他们自由：他若不喜欢，能抓得住就再把他们抓回去好了。

paragraphs.en: Upon this they appeared very thankful, and I accordingly set them at liberty, and bade them retire into the woods, to the place whence they came, and I would leave them some firearms, some ammunition, and some directions how they should live very well if they thought fit.
paragraphs.cn: 听了这话他们显得很感激，我便照此放了他们，叫他们退到树林里、回到他们原先来的地方，还说我会给他们留下一些火器、一些弹药，再指点他们该怎么过日子，只要他们乐意，尽可以过得很好。

paragraphs.en: Upon this I prepared to go on board the ship; but told the captain I would stay that night to prepare my things, and desired him to go on board in the meantime, and keep all right in the ship, and send the boat on shore next day for me; ordering him, at all events, to cause the new captain, who was killed, to be hanged at the yard-arm, that these men might see him.
paragraphs.cn: 这样我就准备上船了；不过我告诉船长，我要留下过这一夜收拾我的东西，请他先上船去，把船上一切照管妥当，第二天再打发小船上岸来接我；还吩咐他无论如何要把那个被打死的新头目吊在帆桁上，好让这些人看见。

paragraphs.en: When the captain was gone I sent for the men up to me to my apartment, and entered seriously into discourse with them on their circumstances.
paragraphs.cn: 船长走后，我把那几个人叫到我屋里，郑重其事地跟他们谈起他们的处境。

paragraphs.en: I told them I thought they had made a right choice; that if the captain had carried them away they would certainly be hanged.
paragraphs.cn: 我对他们说，我认为他们做了个正确的抉择；因为船长若把他们带走，他们必定会被绞死。

paragraphs.en: I showed them the new captain hanging at the yard-arm of the ship, and told them they had nothing less to expect.
paragraphs.cn: 我指给他们看那吊在船的帆桁上的新头目，告诉他们，等着他们的绝不会比这更轻。

paragraphs.en: When they had all declared their willingness to stay, I then told them I would let them into the story of my living there, and put them into the way of making it easy to them.
paragraphs.cn: 等他们都表明了愿意留下，我便对他们说，我要把我在这儿生活的经历讲给他们听，指点他们把日子过得轻松些。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, I gave them the whole history of the place, and of my coming to it; showed them my fortifications, the way I made my bread, planted my corn, cured my grapes; and, in a word, all that was necessary to make them easy.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，我把这地方的来龙去脉、我如何来到这里，都原原本本讲给他们听；给他们看我的防御工事、我做面包的法子、我如何种庄稼、如何晾制葡萄干；一句话，凡是能让他们过得安稳的事，我都一一告诉了他们。

paragraphs.en: I told them the story also of the seventeen Spaniards that were to be expected, for whom I left a letter, and made them promise to treat them in common with themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 我还把预计会来的那十七个西班牙人的事讲给他们听，我为那些人留了一封信，并让这几个人保证要跟自己人一样对待他们。

paragraphs.en: Here it may be noted that the captain, who had ink on board, was greatly surprised that I never hit upon a way of making ink of charcoal and water, or of something else, as I had done things much more difficult.
paragraphs.cn: 这里不妨提一句，船上带着墨水的船长大为惊讶，我竟从没想出个用炭和水、或用别的什么东西制墨的法子，而我做过比这难得多的事呢。

paragraphs.en: I left them my firearms—viz. five muskets, three fowling-pieces, and three swords.
paragraphs.cn: 我把我的火器留给了他们——就是五支滑膛枪、三支鸟枪、三把剑。

paragraphs.en: I had above a barrel and a half of powder left; for after the first year or two I used but little, and wasted none.
paragraphs.cn: 我还剩下一桶半多的火药；因为头一两年过后我就用得很省，一点也没浪费。

paragraphs.en: I gave them a description of the way I managed the goats, and directions to milk and fatten them, and to make both butter and cheese.
paragraphs.cn: 我把自己放牧山羊的法子讲给他们听，指点他们怎样挤奶、怎样把羊养肥，还有怎样做黄油和奶酪。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I gave them every part of my own story; and told them I should prevail with the captain to leave them two barrels of gunpowder more, and some garden-seeds, which I told them I would have been very glad of.
paragraphs.cn: 一句话，我把自己的整个经历原原本本都告诉了他们；还说我会去说动船长再给他们留下两桶火药和一些菜园的种子，我对他们说，那些种子我当初要是有就太好了。

paragraphs.en: Also, I gave them the bag of peas which the captain had brought me to eat, and bade them be sure to sow and increase them.
paragraphs.cn: 我还把船长带给我吃的那袋豌豆给了他们，叮嘱他们一定要播种、把它繁育起来。

paragraphs.en: Having done all this I left them the next day, and went on board the ship.
paragraphs.cn: 做完这一切后，第二天我便告别了他们，登上了那条船。

paragraphs.en: We prepared immediately to sail, but did not weigh that night.
paragraphs.cn: 我们立刻准备起航，但那一夜并没有起锚。

paragraphs.en: The next morning early, two of the five men came swimming to the ship’s side, and making the most lamentable complaint of the other three, begged to be taken into the ship for God’s sake, for they should be murdered, and begged the captain to take them on board, though he hanged them immediately.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天清早，五个人中有两个泅水游到船边，痛哭流涕地控诉另外三个人，苦苦哀求看在上帝份上把他们带上船，说他们再留下就要被杀了，恳求船长收留他们，哪怕上船后立刻把他们绞死也甘心。

paragraphs.en: Upon this the captain pretended to have no power without me; but after some difficulty, and after their solemn promises of amendment, they were taken on board, and were, some time after, soundly whipped and pickled; after which they proved very honest and quiet fellows.
paragraphs.cn: 船长便假装说没有我的同意他做不了主；几经周折，又听他们郑重发誓痛改前非，才把他们带上了船。后来他们被结结实实抽了一顿鞭子，还在伤口上抹了盐水；此后他们倒成了老实安分的人。

paragraphs.en: Some time after this, the boat was ordered on shore, the tide being up, with the things promised to the men; to which the captain, at my intercession, caused their chests and clothes to be added, which they took, and were very thankful for.
paragraphs.cn: 又过了些时候，趁着涨潮，小船奉命划上岸去，把答应给那几个人的东西送去；经我求情，船长还叫人把他们的箱子和衣物一并添上，他们收下后千恩万谢。

paragraphs.en: I also encouraged them, by telling them that if it lay in my power to send any vessel to take them in, I would not forget them.
paragraphs.cn: 我还鼓励他们说，只要我有能力派船来接他们，我绝不会忘了他们。

paragraphs.en: When I took leave of this island, I carried on board, for relics, the great goat-skin cap I had made, my umbrella, and one of my parrots; also, I forgot not to take the money I formerly mentioned, which had lain by me so long useless that it was grown rusty or tarnished, and could hardly pass for silver till it had been a little rubbed and handled, as also the money I found in the wreck of the Spanish ship.
paragraphs.cn: 离开这座岛时，我带上船作为纪念的，有我亲手做的那顶大羊皮帽、我的伞，还有我的一只鹦鹉；我也没忘记带上前面提到过的那些钱——它们在我身边搁置太久，早已锈迹斑斑、失去光泽，不擦拭把玩一番几乎当不成银币了——还有我在那艘西班牙沉船残骸里找到的钱。

paragraphs.en: And thus I left the island, the 19th of December, as I found by the ship’s account, in the year 1686, after I had been upon it eight-and-twenty years, two months, and nineteen days; being delivered from this second captivity the same day of the month that I first made my escape in the long-boat from among the Moors of Sallee.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，据船上的记载，我在1686年12月19日离开了这座岛，此时我已在岛上住了整整二十八年两个月零十九天；而我第二次脱离囚禁的这一天，与我当年乘长舢板从萨累的摩尔人手中逃出来的那一天，恰好是同月同日。

paragraphs.en: In this vessel, after a long voyage, I arrived in England the 11th of June, in the year 1687, having been thirty-five years absent.
paragraphs.cn: 乘着这条船，经过漫长的航行，我于1687年6月11日抵达英格兰，前后离家已有三十五年。

paragraphs.en: When I came to England I was as perfect a stranger to all the world as if I had never been known there.
paragraphs.cn: 我回到英格兰时，对世上所有人都成了个十足的陌生人，仿佛这里从没有人认识过我。

paragraphs.en: My benefactor and faithful steward, whom I had left my money in trust with, was alive, but had had great misfortunes in the world; was become a widow the second time, and very low in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我那位恩人兼忠实的管家——我把钱托付给她保管的那位——还活着，但在世上遭遇了许多不幸；她第二次守了寡，境况十分潦倒。
