paragraphs.en: I made her very easy as to what she owed me, assuring her I would give her no trouble; but, on the contrary, in gratitude for her former care and faithfulness to me, I relieved her as my little stock would afford; which at that time would, indeed, allow me to do but little for her; but I assured her I would never forget her former kindness to me; nor did I forget her when I had sufficient to help her, as shall be observed in its proper place.
paragraphs.cn: 关于她欠我的钱，我让她尽管放宽心，向她保证绝不会为难她；恰恰相反，为报答她从前对我的照料与忠诚，我就凭自己那点微薄的家底接济了她；当时那点钱确实帮不了她多少；但我向她保证，绝不会忘记她昔日待我的恩情；后来等我有了足够的能力，也果然没有忘了帮她，这一点后文自会提到。

paragraphs.en: I went down afterwards into Yorkshire; but my father was dead, and my mother and all the family extinct, except that I found two sisters, and two of the children of one of my brothers; and as I had been long ago given over for dead, there had been no provision made for me; so that, in a word, I found nothing to relieve or assist me; and that the little money I had would not do much for me as to settling in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 随后我南下去了约克郡；可我父亲已经去世，母亲和一家人也都不在了，只剩我找到的两个姐妹，还有我一个哥哥的两个孩子；由于我早就被当作死人，家里没给我留下任何遗产；总之，我发现没有什么能接济或帮助我的；而我手头那点钱也不够我在世上安家立业。

paragraphs.en: I met with one piece of gratitude indeed, which I did not expect; and this was, that the master of the ship, whom I had so happily delivered, and by the same means saved the ship and cargo, having given a very handsome account to the owners of the manner how I had saved the lives of the men and the ship, they invited me to meet them and some other merchants concerned, and all together made me a very handsome compliment upon the subject, and a present of almost £200 sterling.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我倒真遇上了一件出乎意料的报恩事：那位被我幸运搭救、连同船只货物一并保全的船长，向船东们详详细细讲述了我如何救下众人和船只的经过，于是他们邀我去见他们和另外几位有关的商人，众人一齐为此向我郑重道谢，还送了我将近两百英镑的礼金。

paragraphs.en: But after making several reflections upon the circumstances of my life, and how little way this would go towards settling me in the world, I resolved to go to Lisbon, and see if I might not come at some information of the state of my plantation in the Brazils, and of what was become of my partner, who, I had reason to suppose, had some years past given me over for dead.
paragraphs.cn: 但我反复思量自己的境遇，想到这点钱要在世上安家立业实在远远不够，便决意前往里斯本，看看能否打听到我在巴西那片种植园的近况，以及我那位合伙人的下落——我有理由猜想，他这些年多半也早把我当死人了。

paragraphs.en: With this view I took shipping for Lisbon, where I arrived in April following, my man Friday accompanying me very honestly in all these ramblings, and proving a most faithful servant upon all occasions.
paragraphs.cn: 抱着这个念头，我搭船前往里斯本，于次年四月抵达。我那仆人星期五一路上忠心耿耿地陪着我东奔西走，处处证明自己是个最忠实的仆人。

paragraphs.en: When I came to Lisbon, I found out, by inquiry, and to my particular satisfaction, my old friend, the captain of the ship who first took me up at sea off the shore of Africa.
paragraphs.cn: 到了里斯本，我一打听，便格外欣喜地找到了我的老朋友——当年最先在非洲海岸外把我从海上救起的那位船长。

paragraphs.en: He was now grown old, and had left off going to sea, having put his son, who was far from a young man, into his ship, and who still used the Brazil trade.
paragraphs.cn: 他如今已经老了，不再出海，把自己的船交给了儿子——他儿子早已不算年轻——那船至今仍做着巴西的买卖。

paragraphs.en: The old man did not know me, and indeed I hardly knew him.
paragraphs.cn: 老人认不出我了，说实话我也几乎认不出他来。

paragraphs.en: But I soon brought him to my remembrance, and as soon brought myself to his remembrance, when I told him who I was.
paragraphs.cn: 但我一说出自己是谁，很快就唤起了他的记忆，也很快认出了他。

paragraphs.en: After some passionate expressions of the old acquaintance between us, I inquired, you may be sure, after my plantation and my partner.
paragraphs.cn: 叙过一番老相识重逢的动情话语后，你可以想见，我便打听起我的种植园和我的合伙人来。

paragraphs.en: The old man told me he had not been in the Brazils for about nine years; but that he could assure me that when he came away my partner was living, but the trustees whom I had joined with him to take cognisance of my part were both dead: that, however, he believed I would have a very good account of the improvement of the plantation; for that, upon the general belief of my being cast away and drowned, my trustees had given in the account of the produce of my part of the plantation to the procurator-fiscal, who had appropriated it, in case I never came to claim it, one-third to the king, and two-thirds to the monastery of St. Augustine, to be expended for the benefit of the poor, and for the conversion of the Indians to the Catholic faith: but that, if I appeared, or any one for me, to claim the inheritance, it would be restored; only that the improvement, or annual production, being distributed to charitable uses, could not be restored: but he assured me that the steward of the king’s revenue from lands, and the providore, or steward of the monastery, had taken great care all along that the incumbent, that is to say my partner, gave every year a faithful account of the produce, of which they had duly received my moiety.
paragraphs.cn: 老人告诉我，他已有约莫九年没去过巴西了；但他可以向我担保，他离开时我的合伙人还活着，只是我当初委托与他一同料理我那一份产业的两位受托人都已过世；不过他相信，我那种植园经营得极好，我定能得到一笔可观的收益；因为大家普遍认为我遭了海难、淹死了，我的受托人便把我那份种植园的产出账目呈交给了检察官，检察官便将它挪作他用，以防我永不回来认领——三分之一归国王，三分之二拨给圣奥古斯丁修道院，用于救济穷人和劝化印第安人皈依天主教；但只要我本人或代我的人出面认领这份产业，它就会归还，只是那份已用于慈善的收益、即历年产出无法追回；不过他向我保证，国王田产税收的管家和修道院的司库这些年一直尽心尽责，督促现任经营者——也就是我的合伙人——每年如实呈报产出，我那一半份额他们也都按时收下了。

paragraphs.en: I asked him if he knew to what height of improvement he had brought the plantation, and whether he thought it might be worth looking after; or whether, on my going thither, I should meet with any obstruction to my possessing my just right in the moiety.
paragraphs.cn: 我问他，可知那种植园经营到了什么规模，是否值得我去过问；还有，我若亲自前往，占有我那一半应得的产业，会不会遇到什么阻碍。

paragraphs.en: He told me he could not tell exactly to what degree the plantation was improved; but this he knew, that my partner was grown exceeding rich upon the enjoying his part of it; and that, to the best of his remembrance, he had heard that the king’s third of my part, which was, it seems, granted away to some other monastery or religious house, amounted to above two hundred moidores a year: that as to my being restored to a quiet possession of it, there was no question to be made of that, my partner being alive to witness my title, and my name being also enrolled in the register of the country; also he told me that the survivors of my two trustees were very fair, honest people, and very wealthy; and he believed I would not only have their assistance for putting me in possession, but would find a very considerable sum of money in their hands for my account, being the produce of the farm while their fathers held the trust, and before it was given up, as above; which, as he remembered, was for about twelve years.
paragraphs.cn: 他说他没法确切说出那种植园经营到了什么程度；但他只知道，我那合伙人靠着自己那一份已变得极为富有；据他记忆所及，他听说归给我那一份中属于国王的三分之一——似乎已转赠给别的某座修道院或宗教团体——每年就有两百多个葡萄牙金币；至于我能否重新安然占有那份产业，那是毫无疑问的，我的合伙人还活着，可为我的所有权作证，我的名字也登记在当地的册子上；他还告诉我，我那两位受托人的在世遗属都是很正派老实的人，也很富有，他相信我不但能得到他们的协助以占有产业，还能在他们手上找到一大笔属于我账下的钱——那是他们的父辈受托经营、尚未移交国库之前，庄园历年产出所积；据他记得，那大约有十二年之久。

paragraphs.en: I showed myself a little concerned and uneasy at this account, and inquired of the old captain how it came to pass that the trustees should thus dispose of my effects, when he knew that I had made my will, and had made him, the Portuguese captain, my universal heir, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 听了这番话，我显得有些担忧不安，便问老船长：既然他知道我立过遗嘱、指定他这位葡萄牙船长为我的全部遗产继承人，那两位受托人怎么会这样处置我的财产呢？

paragraphs.en: He told me that was true; but that as there was no proof of my being dead, he could not act as executor until some certain account should come of my death; and, besides, he was not willing to intermeddle with a thing so remote: that it was true he had registered my will, and put in his claim; and could he have given any account of my being dead or alive, he would have acted by procuration, and taken possession of the ingenio (so they call the sugar-house), and have given his son, who was now at the Brazils, orders to do it.
paragraphs.cn: 他说这话不假；但因为没有我死亡的证据，在确凿的死讯传来之前，他不能以遗嘱执行人的身份行事；再说，他也不愿去插手这么遥远的一桩事；他确实登记了我的遗嘱，也提出了认领；倘若他能拿出我生死的任何凭据，他早就凭代理权行事，去接管那座“engenio”（他们对制糖作坊的称呼），并吩咐如今正在巴西的儿子去办这件事了。

paragraphs.en: “But,” says the old man, “I have one piece of news to tell you, which perhaps may not be so acceptable to you as the rest; and that is, believing you were lost, and all the world believing so also, your partner and trustees did offer to account with me, in your name, for the first six or eight years’ profits, which I received.
paragraphs.cn: “不过，”老人说道，“我有一条消息要告诉你，也许不像别的那么中听；那就是——当时我以为你已经没了，全世界也都这么以为，你的合伙人和受托人便主动提出，以你的名义把头六到八年的收益结给我，我也收下了。

paragraphs.en: There being at that time great disbursements for increasing the works, building an ingenio, and buying slaves, it did not amount to near so much as afterwards it produced; however,” says the old man, “I shall give you a true account of what I have received in all, and how I have disposed of it.”
paragraphs.cn: 那会儿为扩建作坊、修盖制糖厂、购买奴隶，开销很大，收益远不及后来那么多；不过，”老人接着说，“我会把我总共收了多少、又是怎么处置的，一五一十如实告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: After a few days’ further conference with this ancient friend, he brought me an account of the first six years’ income of my plantation, signed by my partner and the merchant-trustees, being always delivered in goods, viz. tobacco in roll, and sugar in chests, besides rum, molasses, &c.
paragraphs.cn: 和这位故交又商谈了几天之后，他给我拿来了我那种植园头六年的收益账目，上面有我合伙人和几位商人受托人的签字，收益一向以货物交付，即卷装烟草、箱装砂糖，此外还有朗姆酒、糖蜜等等——

paragraphs.en: , which is the consequence of a sugar-work; and I found by this account, that every year the income considerably increased; but, as above, the disbursements being large, the sum at first was small: however, the old man let me see that he was debtor to me four hundred and seventy moidores of gold, besides sixty chests of sugar and fifteen double rolls of tobacco, which were lost in his ship; he having been shipwrecked coming home to Lisbon, about eleven years after my having the place.
paragraphs.cn: 这些都是制糖作坊的产物；我从这份账目看出，收益每年都大幅增长；但如前所说，因开销浩大，起初结余不多；不过老人让我看到，他还欠我四百七十个金币，外加六十箱砂糖和十五大卷烟草，这些都随他的船一起损失了——他在我离开那地方约十一年后返回里斯本途中遭了海难。

paragraphs.en: The good man then began to complain of his misfortunes, and how he had been obliged to make use of my money to recover his losses, and buy him a share in a new ship.
paragraphs.cn: 这位好心人随即诉起自己的种种不幸，说他如何不得不动用我的钱来弥补损失，并入股买了一条新船。

paragraphs.en: “However, my old friend,” says he, “you shall not want a supply in your necessity; and as soon as my son returns you shall be fully satisfied.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过，我的老朋友，”他说，“你急需用钱时绝不会短了供给；等我儿子一回来，你就会得到十足的偿付。”

paragraphs.en: Upon this he pulls out an old pouch, and gives me one hundred and sixty Portugal moidores in gold; and giving the writings of his title to the ship, which his son was gone to the Brazils in, of which he was quarter-part owner, and his son another, he puts them both into my hands for security of the rest.
paragraphs.cn: 说着，他掏出一只旧钱袋，给了我一百六十个葡萄牙金币；又把他那条船的产权文书交给我——那船正是他儿子开去巴西的，他占四分之一股份，他儿子另占一份——他把这两样都交到我手里，作为余款的抵押。

paragraphs.en: I was too much moved with the honesty and kindness of the poor man to be able to bear this; and remembering what he had done for me, how he had taken me up at sea, and how generously he had used me on all occasions, and particularly how sincere a friend he was now to me, I could hardly refrain weeping at what he had said to me; therefore I asked him if his circumstances admitted him to spare so much money at that time, and if it would not straiten him?
paragraphs.cn: 这可怜人的诚实与厚道让我感动得难以自持；想起他为我做过的一切——他如何在海上把我救起，如何处处待我慷慨大方，尤其如今又是这样一位真诚的朋友——他这番话几乎叫我落下泪来；于是我问他，眼下他的境况可容得他拿出这么多钱，这会不会让他手头拮据？

paragraphs.en: He told me he could not say but it might straiten him a little; but, however, it was my money, and I might want it more than he.
paragraphs.cn: 他说，要说不叫他手头有点紧，那也不尽然；但话说回来，这本是我的钱，我兴许比他更用得着。

paragraphs.en: Everything the good man said was full of affection, and I could hardly refrain from tears while he spoke; in short, I took one hundred of the moidores, and called for a pen and ink to give him a receipt for them: then I returned him the rest, and told him if ever I had possession of the plantation I would return the other to him also (as, indeed, I afterwards did); and that as to the bill of sale of his part in his son’s ship, I would not take it by any means; but that if I wanted the money, I found he was honest enough to pay me; and if I did not, but came to receive what he gave me reason to expect, I would never have a penny more from him.
paragraphs.cn: 这好心人说的每一句话都饱含深情，他说话时我几乎忍不住掉泪；总之，我收下了其中一百个金币，叫人拿来笔墨给他写了张收据；然后把其余的还给他，告诉他一旦我占有了那种植园，也会把这些一并还他（后来我确实这么做了）；至于他儿子那条船里他那份股的卖契，我说无论如何都不会收；但假如我需要钱，我看他为人足够诚实，定会还我；假如我不需要，而是如愿收到了他让我指望的那笔款子，那我就再也不会从他手里多拿一个子儿。

paragraphs.en: When this was past, the old man asked me if he should put me into a method to make my claim to my plantation.
paragraphs.cn: 这事过后，老人问我，是否要他替我张罗认领种植园的办法。

paragraphs.en: I told him I thought to go over to it myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉他，我想亲自过去一趟。

paragraphs.en: He said I might do so if I pleased, but that if I did not, there were ways enough to secure my right, and immediately to appropriate the profits to my use: and as there were ships in the river of Lisbon just ready to go away to Brazil, he made me enter my name in a public register, with his affidavit, affirming, upon oath, that I was alive, and that I was the same person who took up the land for the planting the said plantation at first.
paragraphs.cn: 他说我愿意的话尽可以去；但若不去，也有的是办法保住我的权利，并立即把收益划归我用；正巧里斯本河上有几条船就要开往巴西，他便叫我在一份公开的登记簿上写下我的名字，并附上他的宣誓证词，郑重起誓声明我还活着，并且当初开垦土地兴办那座种植园的正是我本人。

paragraphs.en: This being regularly attested by a notary, and a procuration affixed, he directed me to send it, with a letter of his writing, to a merchant of his acquaintance at the place; and then proposed my staying with him till an account came of the return.
paragraphs.cn: 这份文书经公证人正式作证、并附上一纸代理授权后，他叫我连同一封他亲笔写的信，一并寄给他在当地相识的一位商人；随后又提议我暂留他处，等回音传来。

paragraphs.en: Never was anything more honourable than the proceedings upon this procuration; for in less than seven months I received a large packet from the survivors of my trustees, the merchants, for whose account I went to sea, in which were the following, particular letters and papers enclosed:—
paragraphs.cn: 凭这纸代理授权办成的事，再没有比这更体面顺遂的了；不到七个月，我便从受托人的在世遗属——就是我当年为之出海的那几位商人——手里收到了一大包东西，里面附有下列各封信件和文书：

paragraphs.en: First, there was the account-current of the produce of my farm or plantation, from the year when their fathers had balanced with my old Portugal captain, being for six years; the balance appeared to be one thousand one hundred and seventy-four moidores in my favour.
paragraphs.cn: 其一，是我那庄园或种植园产出的往来账目，从他们父辈与我那位葡萄牙老船长结清账目那年起算，共计六年；结余显示，尚有一千一百七十四个金币归我名下。

paragraphs.en: Secondly, there was the account of four years more, while they kept the effects in their hands, before the government claimed the administration, as being the effects of a person not to be found, which they called civil death; and the balance of this, the value of the plantation increasing, amounted to nineteen thousand four hundred and forty-six crusadoes, being about three thousand two hundred and forty moidores.
paragraphs.cn: 其二，是此后又四年的账目，那是在政府以“财产所有人下落不明”（他们称之为“民事死亡”）为由接管之前，他们代为掌管产业的这段时间；这四年因种植园价值不断增长，结余竟达一万九千四百四十六个克鲁扎多，约合三千二百四十个金币。

paragraphs.en: Thirdly, there was the Prior of St. Augustine’s account, who had received the profits for above fourteen years; but not being able to account for what was disposed of by the hospital, very honestly declared he had eight hundred and seventy-two moidores not distributed, which he acknowledged to my account: as to the king’s part, that refunded nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 其三，是圣奥古斯丁修道院院长的账目，他掌管这份收益已有十四年之久；但因无法说清医院那边如何支用，便很诚实地声明，尚有八百七十二个金币未曾拨出，他承认这笔归我名下；至于国王那一份，则分文未退。

paragraphs.en: There was a letter of my partner’s, congratulating me very affectionately upon my being alive, giving me an account how the estate was improved, and what it produced a year; with the particulars of the number of squares, or acres that it contained, how planted, how many slaves there were upon it: and making two-and-twenty crosses for blessings, told me he had said so many _Ave Marias_ to thank the Blessed Virgin that I was alive; inviting me very passionately to come over and take possession of my own, and in the meantime to give him orders to whom he should deliver my effects if I did not come myself; concluding with a hearty tender of his friendship, and that of his family; and sent me as a present seven fine leopards’ skins, which he had, it seems, received from Africa, by some other ship that he had sent thither, and which, it seems, had made a better voyage than I.
paragraphs.cn: 里面还有我合伙人的一封信，情真意切地祝贺我还活着，向我说明产业如何扩展、每年产出多少，并详列它含有多少方地或多少英亩、如何种植、上面有多少奴隶；他还画了二十二个十字表示祝福，说他为我还活着而向圣母诵了这么多遍《圣母经》来谢恩；他极其热切地邀我过去接管我自己的产业，同时叫我留下吩咐——万一我不亲自前来，该把我的财产交给谁；信末诚挚地表达了他及全家对我的友情，并送我一份礼物：七张上好的豹皮，据说是他派往非洲的另一条船给他捎回来的，看来那趟航行比我走运。

paragraphs.en: He sent me also five chests of excellent sweetmeats, and a hundred pieces of gold uncoined, not quite so large as moidores.
paragraphs.cn: 他还送了我五箱上等蜜饯，以及一百枚未经铸造的金块，个头比金币略小些。

paragraphs.en: By the same fleet my two merchant-trustees shipped me one thousand two hundred chests of sugar, eight hundred rolls of tobacco, and the rest of the whole account in gold.
paragraphs.cn: 随同这支船队，我那两位商人受托人给我运来了一千二百箱砂糖、八百卷烟草，其余全部结余则折成黄金。

paragraphs.en: I might well say now, indeed, that the latter end of Job was better than the beginning.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我真可以说，约伯的晚年确实胜过他的起初了。

paragraphs.en: It is impossible to express the flutterings of my very heart when I found all my wealth about me; for as the Brazil ships come all in fleets, the same ships which brought my letters brought my goods: and the effects were safe in the river before the letters came to my hand.
paragraphs.cn: 当我发现所有这些财富都归了我时，心头那阵狂跳简直无法形容；因为巴西的船都是成队而来，捎来我信件的正是那几条船，也运来了我的货物；信还没到我手里，货物就已安然停泊在河上了。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I turned pale, and grew sick; and, had not the old man run and fetched me a cordial, I believe the sudden surprise of joy had overset nature, and I had died upon the spot: nay, after that I continued very ill, and was so some hours, till a physician being sent for, and something of the real cause of my illness being known, he ordered me to be let blood; after which I had relief, and grew well: but I verily believe, if I had not been eased by a vent given in that manner to the spirits, I should have died.
paragraphs.cn: 总之，我脸色煞白，浑身发软；若不是那老人跑去给我取来一剂强心药，我相信那突如其来的狂喜早已把我的心神冲垮，我当场就会送命；不仅如此，此后我还病了好一阵，一连病了好几个钟头，直到请来医生、大致查明我发病的真正缘由，他吩咐给我放血；放过血后我才觉舒缓，渐渐好转；但我确实相信，若不是那样给我的精气开了个泄口，我怕是活不成了。

paragraphs.en: I was now master, all on a sudden, of above five thousand pounds sterling in money, and had an estate, as I might well call it, in the Brazils, of above a thousand pounds a year, as sure as an estate of lands in England: and, in a word, I was in a condition which I scarce knew how to understand, or how to compose myself for the enjoyment of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我如今转眼间成了坐拥五千多英镑现钱的富翁，还在巴西有了一份可称作产业的家当，每年收益一千多英镑，稳当得如同英格兰的一份田产；总之，我一时竟不知该如何理解自己的处境，也不知该如何安下心来享受这一切。

paragraphs.en: The first thing I did was to recompense my original benefactor, my good old captain, who had been first charitable to me in my distress, kind to me in my beginning, and honest to me at the end.
paragraphs.cn: 我做的头一件事，就是报答我最初的恩人——我那位好心的老船长；当年我落难时他最先施以援手，我起步时他待我亲厚，到头来又对我一片诚实。

paragraphs.en: I showed him all that was sent to me; I told him that, next to the providence of Heaven, which disposed all things, it was owing to him; and that it now lay on me to reward him, which I would do a hundred-fold: so I first returned to him the hundred moidores I had received of him; then I sent for a notary, and caused him to draw up a general release or discharge from the four hundred and seventy moidores, which he had acknowledged he owed me, in the fullest and firmest manner possible.
paragraphs.cn: 我把送到我手里的东西全给他看了；我对他说，这一切除了归功于主宰万物的上天护佑，便是全靠了他；如今该轮到我来报答他，我要百倍相报；于是我先把从他那里收下的一百个金币还给他；接着请来一位公证人，叫他以最完备、最牢靠的方式，为他曾承认欠我的那四百七十个金币立了一纸全额免除的字据。

paragraphs.en: After which I caused a procuration to be drawn, empowering him to be the receiver of the annual profits of my plantation: and appointing my partner to account with him, and make the returns, by the usual fleets, to him in my name; and by a clause in the end, made a grant of one hundred moidores a year to him during his life, out of the effects, and fifty moidores a year to his son after him, for his life: and thus I requited my old man.
paragraphs.cn: 随后我又叫人拟了一纸委托授权书，授权他为我种植园历年收益的代收人，并指定我的合伙人向他结账、经由惯常的船队以我的名义把收益转交给他；文末还加了一条，从收益中每年拨给他一百个金币，供他终身享用，他身后再每年拨五十个金币给他儿子，供其一生之用；我就这样报答了我的老人。

paragraphs.en: I had now to consider which way to steer my course next, and what to do with the estate that Providence had thus put into my hands; and, indeed, I had more care upon my head now than I had in my state of life in the island where I wanted nothing but what I had, and had nothing but what I wanted; whereas I had now a great charge upon me, and my business was how to secure it.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我得考虑下一步该往哪儿走，该如何处置上天这样交到我手中的这份产业；说真的，我此刻操的心比在岛上时还要多——在岛上，我除了拥有的别无所求，除了所需的别无所有；而如今我肩上担着一大笔财产，我要操心的正是如何把它保住。

paragraphs.en: I had not a cave now to hide my money in, or a place where it might lie without lock or key, till it grew mouldy and tarnished before anybody would meddle with it; on the contrary, I knew not where to put it, or whom to trust with it.
paragraphs.cn: 如今我没有了那个可以藏钱的山洞，也没有一处能让钱不上锁不加钥匙、一直搁到发霉失色都没人来碰的地方；恰恰相反，我竟不知该把它放到哪儿，也不知该托付给谁。

paragraphs.en: My old patron, the captain, indeed, was honest, and that was the only refuge I had.
paragraphs.cn: 我那位老恩主船长固然诚实可靠，可那也是我唯一的托身之处了。

paragraphs.en: In the next place, my interest in the Brazils seemed to summon me thither; but now I could not tell how to think of going thither till I had settled my affairs, and left my effects in some safe hands behind me.
paragraphs.cn: 其次，我在巴西的产业似乎在召唤我前往；可如今我实在不敢贸然动身，非得先把手头的事料理妥当、把财产留在某个稳妥的人手里不可。

paragraphs.en: At first I thought of my old friend the widow, who I knew was honest, and would be just to me; but then she was in years, and but poor, and, for aught I knew, might be in debt: so that, in a word, I had no way but to go back to England myself and take my effects with me.
paragraphs.cn: 起初我想到了我的老朋友那位寡妇，我知道她诚实，定不会亏待我；可她上了年纪，又很贫寒，而且据我所知，说不定还欠着债；总之，我别无他法，只能亲自回英格兰，把我的财产随身带走。

paragraphs.en: It was some months, however, before I resolved upon this; and, therefore, as I had rewarded the old captain fully, and to his satisfaction, who had been my former benefactor, so I began to think of the poor widow, whose husband had been my first benefactor, and she, while it was in her power, my faithful steward and instructor.
paragraphs.cn: 然而我却过了好几个月才拿定这个主意；因此，既已把那位从前的恩人老船长酬报得十分周全、令他称心，我便开始想到那位可怜的寡妇——她丈夫曾是我最初的恩人，她本人当年也曾尽力做我忠实的管家和引路人。

paragraphs.en: So, the first thing I did, I got a merchant in Lisbon to write to his correspondent in London, not only to pay a bill, but to go find her out, and carry her, in money, a hundred pounds from me, and to talk with her, and comfort her in her poverty, by telling her she should, if I lived, have a further supply: at the same time I sent my two sisters in the country a hundred pounds each, they being, though not in want, yet not in very good circumstances; one having been married and left a widow; and the other having a husband not so kind to her as he should be.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，我做的头一件事，便是托里斯本的一位商人写信给他在伦敦的往来客户，不单是去兑一张汇票，还要去找到她，替我捎去现钱一百英镑，并同她谈谈，用几句话宽慰她的贫困——告诉她只要我还活着，日后还会有进一步的接济；与此同时，我给乡下的两个姐妹各寄去一百英镑，她们虽算不上贫困，境况却也不甚宽裕；一个出嫁后守了寡，另一个的丈夫待她不够体贴。

paragraphs.en: But among all my relations or acquaintances I could not yet pitch upon one to whom I durst commit the gross of my stock, that I might go away to the Brazils, and leave things safe behind me; and this greatly perplexed me.
paragraphs.cn: 可是在我所有的亲戚熟人当中，我却还找不出一个能让我放心托付大宗家产的人，好让我动身去巴西、把财物稳妥地留在身后；这叫我大为犯难。

paragraphs.en: I had once a mind to have gone to the Brazils and have settled myself there, for I was, as it were, naturalised to the place; but I had some little scruple in my mind about religion, which insensibly drew me back.
paragraphs.cn: 我一度动过念头，想干脆去巴西定居，因为我几乎已算入乡随俗、把那里当成了故土；可我心里对宗教有一点小小的顾虑，不知不觉又把我拉了回来。

paragraphs.en: However, it was not religion that kept me from going there for the present; and as I had made no scruple of being openly of the religion of the country all the while I was among them, so neither did I yet; only that, now and then, having of late thought more of it than formerly, when I began to think of living and dying among them, I began to regret having professed myself a Papist, and thought it might not be the best religion to die with.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，眼下让我打消去意的倒并非宗教；因为我身处他们中间时，一向毫不避讳地公开信奉当地的宗教，如今心里也依然如此；只是近来偶尔比从前多想了几分——一想到要在他们中间生老病死，我便开始懊悔自己当初宣称皈依了天主教，觉得带着这个信仰去死未必是最好的。

paragraphs.en: But, as I have said, this was not the main thing that kept me from going to the Brazils, but that really I did not know with whom to leave my effects behind me; so I resolved at last to go to England, where, if I arrived, I concluded that I should make some acquaintance, or find some relations, that would be faithful to me; and, accordingly, I prepared to go to England with all my wealth.
paragraphs.cn: 但如我所说，让我不去巴西的主因并不在此，而实在是我不知道该把财产留给谁；于是我最终决定回英格兰去——只要能平安到达，我料想总能结交些新相识，或找到几门亲戚，会对我忠实可靠；于是我便着手带着全部财富动身回英格兰。

paragraphs.en: In order to prepare things for my going home, I first (the Brazil fleet being just going away) resolved to give answers suitable to the just and faithful account of things I had from thence; and, first, to the Prior of St. Augustine I wrote a letter full of thanks for his just dealings, and the offer of the eight hundred and seventy-two moidores which were undisposed of, which I desired might be given, five hundred to the monastery, and three hundred and seventy-two to the poor, as the prior should direct; desiring the good padre’s prayers for me, and the like.
paragraphs.cn: 为筹备回乡诸事，我首先（趁巴西船队正要开走）决意针对我从那边得来的公正翔实的账目一一作出妥当的回复；先是给圣奥古斯丁修道院院长写了一封信，满纸感谢他办事公道，并处置那尚未拨出的八百七十二个金币——我请他把其中五百个拨给修道院，三百七十二个拨给穷人，具体由院长斟酌；同时恳请这位好神父为我祈祷，如此等等。

paragraphs.en: I wrote next a letter of thanks to my two trustees, with all the acknowledgment that so much justice and honesty called for: as for sending them any present, they were far above having any occasion of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我接着给两位受托人写了一封谢信，把如此这般的公正与诚实所应得的一切谢意都表达了出来；至于给他们送什么礼物，他们的境况远在需要之上了。

paragraphs.en: Lastly, I wrote to my partner, acknowledging his industry in the improving the plantation, and his integrity in increasing the stock of the works; giving him instructions for his future government of my part, according to the powers I had left with my old patron, to whom I desired him to send whatever became due to me, till he should hear from me more particularly; assuring him that it was my intention not only to come to him, but to settle myself there for the remainder of my life.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，我给合伙人写了信，感谢他经营种植园的勤勉，以及他不断增添作坊资产的诚信；我按照留给老恩主的那些授权，就我那一份日后如何打理给了他若干指示，请他把凡到期应归我的都送交老恩主，直到日后再听我更详细的吩咐；并向他保证，我不但打算去他那里，还要在那里安顿下来，度过余生。

paragraphs.en: To this I added a very handsome present of some Italian silks for his wife and two daughters, for such the captain’s son informed me he had; with two pieces of fine English broadcloth, the best I could get in Lisbon, five pieces of black baize, and some Flanders lace of a good value.
paragraphs.cn: 随信我还附上一份很体面的礼物：给他妻子和两个女儿的一些意大利丝绸——船长的儿子告诉我他有这样一妻二女；另外还有两匹上等英格兰细呢，是我在里斯本能买到的最好的，五匹黑色粗呢，以及一些相当值钱的佛兰德斯花边。

paragraphs.en: Having thus settled my affairs, sold my cargo, and turned all my effects into good bills of exchange, my next difficulty was which way to go to England: I had been accustomed enough to the sea, and yet I had a strange aversion to go to England by the sea at that time, and yet I could give no reason for it, yet the difficulty increased upon me so much, that though I had once shipped my baggage in order to go, yet I altered my mind, and that not once but two or three times.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样料理好诸事、卖掉货物、把全部财产都换成可靠的汇票之后，我接下来犯难的便是走哪条路回英格兰：我对海上生活本已十分惯熟，可那时却对走海路回英格兰有一种莫名的抵触，又说不出个所以然来；然而这层顾虑在我心头愈发沉重，以致我虽已把行李搬上船准备启程，却又改了主意，而且不止一次，而是两三次。

paragraphs.en: It is true I had been very unfortunate by sea, and this might be one of the reasons; but let no man slight the strong impulses of his own thoughts in cases of such moment: two of the ships which I had singled out to go in, I mean more particularly singled out than any other, having put my things on board one of them, and in the other having agreed with the captain; I say two of these ships miscarried.
paragraphs.cn: 诚然，我在海上一向很不走运，这或许是原因之一；可是，在这般紧要的关头，谁也别小看自己内心那些强烈的预感：我特意挑出——我是说比挑别的船都更用心挑出——准备搭乘的两条船，一条已把我的东西搬上了船，另一条也已同船长谈妥；我要说，正是这两条船都出了事。

paragraphs.en: One was taken by the Algerines, and the other was lost on the Start, near Torbay, and all the people drowned except three; so that in either of those vessels I had been made miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 一条被阿尔及尔海盗掳去，另一条在托贝附近的斯塔特角触礁沉没，船上的人除三个外全都淹死了；这么说，无论搭上哪一条，我都会落得凄惨下场。

paragraphs.en: Having been thus harassed in my thoughts, my old pilot, to whom I communicated everything, pressed me earnestly not to go by sea, but either to go by land to the Groyne, and cross over the Bay of Biscay to Rochelle, from whence it was but an easy and safe journey by land to Paris, and so to Calais and Dover; or to go up to Madrid, and so all the way by land through France.
paragraphs.cn: 心里这样忐忑不安之际，我那位老领航——凡事我都同他商量——恳切地劝我别走海路，要么从陆路去拉科鲁尼亚，横渡比斯开湾到罗谢尔，再从那里走陆路，一路又轻松又安全地到巴黎，然后经加来去多佛；要么北上马德里，一路全走陆路穿过法国。

paragraphs.en: In a word, I was so prepossessed against my going by sea at all, except from Calais to Dover, that I resolved to travel all the way by land; which, as I was not in haste, and did not value the charge, was by much the pleasanter way: and to make it more so, my old captain brought an English gentleman, the son of a merchant in Lisbon, who was willing to travel with me; after which we picked up two more English merchants also, and two young Portuguese gentlemen, the last going to Paris only; so that in all there were six of us and five servants; the two merchants and the two Portuguese, contenting themselves with one servant between two, to save the charge; and as for me, I got an English sailor to travel with me as a servant, besides my man Friday, who was too much a stranger to be capable of supplying the place of a servant on the road.
paragraphs.cn: 总之，我对走海路已成见极深，除了从加来到多佛那一段，别处一概不肯乘船，便下决心全程走陆路；反正我并不赶时间，也不在乎花销，这样走要惬意得多；为叫这趟旅程更惬意，我那老船长引来一位英格兰绅士——里斯本一位商人的儿子——他愿意与我同行；此后我们又结识了两位英格兰商人和两位年轻的葡萄牙绅士——那两位葡萄牙人只到巴黎为止；这样一来，我们一行共有六人、五个仆人；两位商人和两位葡萄牙人为省开销，每两人合用一个仆人；至于我，除了我那仆人星期五外，还雇了一名英格兰水手随行当仆人——星期五毕竟太生疏，路上还担不起仆人的差事。

paragraphs.en: In this manner I set out from Lisbon; and our company being very well mounted and armed, we made a little troop, whereof they did me the honour to call me captain, as well because I was the oldest man, as because I had two servants, and, indeed, was the origin of the whole journey.
paragraphs.cn: 我便这样从里斯本启程；我们一行人马精良、装备齐整，俨然一支小小的队伍，他们抬举我，推我做队长——一来因为我年纪最长，二来因为我带着两个仆人，再说这整趟旅程本就是由我而起的。

paragraphs.en: As I have troubled you with none of my sea journals, so I shall trouble you now with none of my land journals; but some adventures that happened to us in this tedious and difficult journey I must not omit.
paragraphs.cn: 我既没拿我那些海上日志来烦扰诸位，如今也不会拿我的陆上日志来烦扰你们；不过这趟漫长艰难的旅程中，我们遇上的几桩奇事却不能不提。

paragraphs.en: When we came to Madrid, we, being all of us strangers to Spain, were willing to stay some time to see the court of Spain, and what was worth observing; but it being the latter part of the summer, we hastened away, and set out from Madrid about the middle of October; but when we came to the edge of Navarre, we were alarmed, at several towns on the way, with an account that so much snow was falling on the French side of the mountains, that several travellers were obliged to come back to Pampeluna, after having attempted at an extreme hazard to pass on.
paragraphs.cn: 到了马德里，我们一行都是初到西班牙的生客，都愿意逗留些时日，看看西班牙的宫廷以及值得一观的种种；但那时已是夏末，我们便匆匆动身，约莫十月中旬离开马德里；可等我们走到纳瓦拉边境，一路上好几座城镇都传来消息，叫我们吃了一惊——说山脉法国一侧雪下得极大，好几拨旅人冒着极大风险试图翻越，最终不得不退回潘普洛纳。

paragraphs.en: When we came to Pampeluna itself, we found it so indeed; and to me, that had been always used to a hot climate, and to countries where I could scarce bear any clothes on, the cold was insufferable; nor, indeed, was it more painful than surprising to come but ten days before out of Old Castile, where the weather was not only warm but very hot, and immediately to feel a wind from the Pyrenean Mountains so very keen, so severely cold, as to be intolerable and to endanger benumbing and perishing of our fingers and toes.
paragraphs.cn: 等我们到了潘普洛纳，才发现果真如此；对我这样一向惯于炎热气候、惯于那种几乎穿不住衣裳的地方的人来说，这寒冷实在难以忍受；说真的，仅仅十天前我们还在旧卡斯蒂利亚，那里天气不但暖和还很炎热，转眼却感到从比利牛斯山吹来的风如此凛冽刺骨、如此严寒难当，冻得人手指脚趾几乎要麻木坏死——这与其说痛苦，不如说更叫人惊愕。

paragraphs.en: Poor Friday was really frightened when he saw the mountains all covered with snow, and felt cold weather, which he had never seen or felt before in his life.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的星期五看到群山都覆着白雪、感到这寒冷天气时，着实吓坏了，这是他有生以来从未见过、也从未领受过的。

paragraphs.en: To mend the matter, when we came to Pampeluna it continued snowing with so much violence and so long, that the people said winter was come before its time; and the roads, which were difficult before, were now quite impassable; for, in a word, the snow lay in some places too thick for us to travel, and being not hard frozen, as is the case in the northern countries, there was no going without being in danger of being buried alive every step.
paragraphs.cn: 更糟的是，我们到潘普洛纳后，雪一直下个不停，来势又猛，下得又久，当地人都说冬天没到时候就来了；本就难行的道路如今更是完全无法通行；总之，有些地方积雪太厚，我们无法赶路，而雪又不像北方国家那样冻得结实，一走便有每一步都被活埋的危险。

paragraphs.en: We stayed no less than twenty days at Pampeluna; when (seeing the winter coming on, and no likelihood of its being better, for it was the severest winter all over Europe that had been known in the memory of man) I proposed that we should go away to Fontarabia, and there take shipping for Bordeaux, which was a very little voyage.
paragraphs.cn: 我们在潘普洛纳整整耽搁了二十天；眼见冬天步步逼近，也丝毫没有转好的迹象——那是人们记忆中整个欧洲最严酷的一个冬天——我便提议我们动身去丰塔拉比亚，从那里搭船去波尔多，那可是很短的一段航程。

paragraphs.en: But, while I was considering this, there came in four French gentlemen, who, having been stopped on the French side of the passes, as we were on the Spanish, had found out a guide, who, traversing the country near the head of Languedoc, had brought them over the mountains by such ways that they were not much incommoded with the snow; for where they met with snow in any quantity, they said it was frozen hard enough to bear them and their horses.
paragraphs.cn: 可正当我盘算此事时，来了四位法国绅士；他们和我们被困在西班牙一侧一样，也曾被拦在山口的法国一侧，后来寻得一名向导，那向导取道朗格多克源头附近的地界，带他们翻过山来，一路没怎么受雪的阻碍；因为凡遇上积雪较厚之处，他们说雪都冻得够硬，足以承住他们连人带马。

paragraphs.en: We sent for this guide, who told us he would undertake to carry us the same way, with no hazard from the snow, provided we were armed sufficiently to protect ourselves from wild beasts; for, he said, in these great snows it was frequent for some wolves to show themselves at the foot of the mountains, being made ravenous for want of food, the ground being covered with snow.
paragraphs.cn: 我们派人去请这位向导，他说只要我们武器足够、能自卫防野兽，他就情愿带我们走同一条路，包管没有雪的危险；因为他说，逢这样的大雪天，常有狼群下到山脚来，遍地积雪使它们觅不到食物，饿得凶狠。

paragraphs.en: We told him we were well enough prepared for such creatures as they were, if he would insure us from a kind of two-legged wolves, which we were told we were in most danger from, especially on the French side of the mountains.
paragraphs.cn: 我们告诉他，对付这类畜生我们准备得足够充分，只要他能保我们不遇上一种两条腿的狼——据说那才是我们最该提防的，尤其在山脉的法国一侧。

paragraphs.en: He satisfied us that there was no danger of that kind in the way that we were to go; so we readily agreed to follow him, as did also twelve other gentlemen with their servants, some French, some Spanish, who, as I said, had attempted to go, and were obliged to come back again.
paragraphs.cn: 他叫我们放心，说我们要走的这条路上没有那种危险；于是我们爽快地答应跟他走，另有十二位绅士带着仆人也一同前往，有法国人也有西班牙人，正如我所说，他们都曾试图翻山，却不得不折返回来。

paragraphs.en: Accordingly, we set out from Pampeluna with our guide on the 15th of November; and indeed I was surprised when, instead of going forward, he came directly back with us on the same road that we came from Madrid, about twenty miles; when, having passed two rivers, and come into the plain country, we found ourselves in a warm climate again, where the country was pleasant, and no snow to be seen; but, on a sudden, turning to his left, he approached the mountains another way; and though it is true the hills and precipices looked dreadful, yet he made so many tours, such meanders, and led us by such winding ways, that we insensibly passed the height of the mountains without being much encumbered with the snow; and all on a sudden he showed us the pleasant and fruitful provinces of Languedoc and Gascony, all green and flourishing, though at a great distance, and we had some rough way to pass still.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，我们在11月15日随向导离开潘普洛纳；说真的，我着实吃了一惊——他非但不朝前走，反倒领着我们径直原路折回，沿着我们从马德里来时的那条路走了约莫二十英里；渡过两条河、进入平原地带后，我们又置身于温暖的气候里，那里风景宜人，不见半点积雪；可他冷不丁向左一拐，从另一条路逼近群山；虽说那些山丘和悬崖看着着实骇人，他却绕了那么多弯、走了那么曲折的路、领我们从那么多迂回小径走过，竟叫我们不知不觉翻过了山巅，也没怎么受积雪的拖累；忽然间他便让我们望见了朗格多克和加斯科涅那两片宜人富饶的省份，一派葱绿繁茂，虽说还在很远处，我们也还有些崎岖的路要走。

paragraphs.en: We were a little uneasy, however, when we found it snowed one whole day and a night so fast that we could not travel; but he bid us be easy; we should soon be past it all: we found, indeed, that we began to descend every day, and to come more north than before; and so, depending upon our guide, we went on.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，当我们发现整整一昼一夜大雪纷飞、下得让我们没法赶路时，心里还是有些不安；但他叫我们宽心，说我们很快就能把这一切都抛在身后；果然，我们发觉一天天在往下走，也比先前更往北去了；于是全凭着向导，我们继续前行。

paragraphs.en: It was about two hours before night when, our guide being something before us, and not just in sight, out rushed three monstrous wolves, and after them a bear, from a hollow way adjoining to a thick wood; two of the wolves made at the guide, and had he been far before us, he would have been devoured before we could have helped him; one of them fastened upon his horse, and the other attacked the man with such violence, that he had not time, or presence of mind enough, to draw his pistol, but hallooed and cried out to us most lustily.
paragraphs.cn: 约莫离天黑还有两个钟头，我们的向导走在我们前头一点、恰好不在视线之内时，从一条挨着密林的坳道里，猛地窜出三头巨狼，后面还跟着一只熊；两头狼直扑向导，倘若他离我们太远，不等我们援手他早已被吞食了；一头狼咬住了他的马，另一头如此凶猛地扑向他，弄得他连拔手枪的工夫和镇定都没有，只能扯着嗓子拼命向我们呼救。

paragraphs.en: My man Friday being next me, I bade him ride up and see what was the matter.
paragraphs.cn: 我那仆人星期五就在我身旁，我便叫他骑马上前去看看出了什么事。

paragraphs.en: As soon as Friday came in sight of the man, he hallooed out as loud as the other, “O master!
paragraphs.cn: 星期五一望见那人，就跟对方一样扯着嗓子高喊：“哦，主人！

paragraphs.en: O master!” but like a bold fellow, rode directly up to the poor man, and with his pistol shot the wolf in the head that attacked him.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，主人！”可他到底是个胆大的汉子，径直骑到那可怜人跟前，一枪打中了扑在他身上那头狼的脑袋。

paragraphs.en: It was happy for the poor man that it was my man Friday; for, having been used to such creatures in his country, he had no fear upon him, but went close up to him and shot him; whereas, any other of us would have fired at a farther distance, and have perhaps either missed the wolf or endangered shooting the man.
paragraphs.cn: 多亏来的是我那仆人星期五，才算了那可怜人的运气；因为他在自己家乡见惯了这类畜生，心里毫无惧色，直凑到那狼跟前一枪把它打死；换了我们中的任何别人，都会站得远远地开枪，说不定不是打不中狼，就是有伤着那人的危险。

paragraphs.en: But it was enough to have terrified a bolder man than I; and, indeed, it alarmed all our company, when, with the noise of Friday’s pistol, we heard on both sides the most dismal howling of wolves; and the noise, redoubled by the echo of the mountains, appeared to us as if there had been a prodigious number of them; and perhaps there was not such a few as that we had no cause of apprehension: however, as Friday had killed this wolf, the other that had fastened upon the horse left him immediately, and fled, without doing him any damage, having happily fastened upon his head, where the bosses of the bridle had stuck in his teeth.
paragraphs.cn: 可这场面足以把比我胆大的人都吓住；说真的，当随着星期五的枪声、我们听见两侧传来最凄厉的狼嗥时，全队的人都惊慌起来；那嗥声经群山回响而愈发加倍，听来仿佛有数不清的狼群；而或许它们真的并不像我们所以为的那样少，我们并非没有理由担惊；不过，星期五既已打死了这头狼，那头咬着马的狼便立刻松了口逃走，没给马造成任何伤害——所幸它咬住的是马头，马嚼子的铜饰恰卡在了它的牙缝里。

paragraphs.en: But the man was most hurt; for the raging creature had bit him twice, once in the arm, and the other time a little above his knee; and though he had made some defence, he was just tumbling down by the disorder of his horse, when Friday came up and shot the wolf.
paragraphs.cn: 倒是那人伤得最重；那头狂暴的畜生咬了他两口，一口在手臂上，另一口在膝盖稍上方；他虽也稍作了些抵挡，却因胯下的马受惊乱窜，正要摔下地来，恰在这时星期五赶到，一枪打死了那头狼。

paragraphs.en: It is easy to suppose that at the noise of Friday’s pistol we all mended our pace, and rode up as fast as the way, which was very difficult, would give us leave, to see what was the matter.
paragraphs.cn: 不难想见，一听见星期五的枪声，我们全都加快了脚步，沿着那条极难行的路尽力策马赶上前去，看看究竟出了什么事。

paragraphs.en: As soon as we came clear of the trees, which blinded us before, we saw clearly what had been the case, and how Friday had disengaged the poor guide, though we did not presently discern what kind of creature it was he had killed.
paragraphs.cn: 我们一冲出先前遮住视线的树丛，便看清了原委，也看清了星期五如何解救了那可怜的向导，只是我们一时还辨不出他打死的究竟是什么畜生。

chapters.title_en: Fight Between Friday And A Bear

paragraphs.en: But never was a fight managed so hardily, and in such a surprising manner as that which followed between Friday and the bear, which gave us all, though at first we were surprised and afraid for him, the greatest diversion imaginable.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,接下来星期五与那头熊之间的搏斗,论其大胆和奇特,真是我平生仅见;虽说起初我们都替他捏了一把汗,可这场好戏到头来给了我们谁也想象不到的乐趣。

paragraphs.en: As the bear is a heavy, clumsy creature, and does not gallop as the wolf does, who is swift and light, so he has two particular qualities, which generally are the rule of his actions; first, as to men, who are not his proper prey (he does not usually attempt them, except they first attack him, unless he be excessively hungry, which it is probable might now be the case, the ground being covered with snow), if you do not meddle with him, he will not meddle with you; but then you must take care to be very civil to him, and give him the road, for he is a very nice gentleman; he will not go a step out of his way for a prince; nay, if you are really afraid, your best way is to look another way and keep going on; for sometimes if you stop, and stand still, and look steadfastly at him, he takes it for an affront; but if you throw or toss anything at him, though it were but a bit of stick as big as your finger, he thinks himself abused, and sets all other business aside to pursue his revenge, and will have satisfaction in point of honour—that is his first quality: the next is, if he be once affronted, he will never leave you, night or day, till he has his revenge, but follows at a good round rate till he overtakes you.
paragraphs.cn: 熊是一种笨重迟钝的家伙,不像狼那样轻捷善跑,它有两个特别的脾性,行事大抵照此而来:头一样是对人——人本不是它的猎物(它一般不会主动招惹人,除非你先动手,或者它饿极了,如今地上盖着雪,想必正是这种情形)——你若不惹它,它便不惹你;可你得留神对它客气些,给它让路,因为它是位极讲究的绅士,哪怕是王子挡了道,它也不肯让开一步;真要害怕了,你最好的法子是望着别处只管往前走,因为你若停下站定、盯着它瞧,它会当作是冒犯;可你若朝它扔点什么,哪怕只是根手指粗细的小棍,它便觉得受了侮辱,撇下一切别的事只顾报仇,非得挣回这口气不可——这是它头一样脾性;再一样是,它一旦被惹恼了,便昼夜不离地追着你,不报此仇决不罢休,以极快的步子紧追,直到把你赶上。

paragraphs.en: My man Friday had delivered our guide, and when we came up to him he was helping him off his horse, for the man was both hurt and frightened, when on a sudden we espied the bear come out of the wood; and a monstrous one it was, the biggest by far that ever I saw.
paragraphs.cn: 我的仆人星期五救下了我们的向导;我们赶到时,他正扶那人下马,因为那人又是受伤又是受惊;忽然间,我们瞧见那头熊从林子里走了出来,那是头庞然大物,是我生平所见最大的一头。

paragraphs.en: We were all a little surprised when we saw him; but when Friday saw him, it was easy to see joy and courage in the fellow’s countenance.
paragraphs.cn: 见到它,我们都吃了一惊;可星期五一见到它,那家伙脸上分明露出了欢喜和勇气。

paragraphs.en: O!
paragraphs.cn: 噢!

paragraphs.en: O!” says Friday, three times, pointing to him; “O master, you give me te leave, me shakee te hand with him; me makee you good laugh.”
paragraphs.cn: 噢!”星期五连叫三声,指着那熊说,“噢,主人,你让我去,我跟它握握手;我逗你们好好乐一场。”

paragraphs.en: I was surprised to see the fellow so well pleased.
paragraphs.cn: 见这家伙这般高兴,我倒吃了一惊。

paragraphs.en: “You fool,” says I, “he will eat you up.”
paragraphs.cn: “你这傻瓜,”我说,“它会把你吃掉。”

paragraphs.en: —“Eatee me up! eatee me up!” says Friday, twice over again; “me eatee him up; me makee you good laugh; you all stay here, me show you good laugh.”
paragraphs.cn: “吃掉我!吃掉我!”星期五又连说两遍,“我把它吃掉;我逗你们好好乐;你们都待在这儿,我给你们看场好乐子。”

paragraphs.en: So down he sits, and gets off his boots in a moment, and puts on a pair of pumps (as we call the flat shoes they wear, and which he had in his pocket), gives my other servant his horse, and with his gun away he flew, swift like the wind.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他坐下来,一转眼脱掉靴子,换上一双平底软鞋(就是他们穿的那种平底鞋,他口袋里正装着一双),把马交给我另一个仆人,提起枪像风一样飞奔而去。

paragraphs.en: The bear was walking softly on, and offered to meddle with nobody, till Friday coming pretty near, calls to him, as if the bear could understand him.
paragraphs.cn: 那熊正不慌不忙地走着,谁也不去招惹,直到星期五走得相当近了,才朝它喊话,仿佛那熊听得懂似的。

paragraphs.en: “Hark ye, hark ye,” says Friday, “me speakee with you.”
paragraphs.cn: “听着,听着,”星期五说,“我跟你说话呢。”

paragraphs.en: We followed at a distance, for now being down on the Gascony side of the mountains, we were entered a vast forest, where the country was plain and pretty open, though it had many trees in it scattered here and there.
paragraphs.cn: 我们远远跟在后头;这时我们已下到山的加斯科尼那一侧,进了一片大森林,地势平坦,颇为开阔,只是零零散散长着不少树。

paragraphs.en: Friday, who had, as we say, the heels of the bear, came up with him quickly, and took up a great stone, and threw it at him, and hit him just on the head, but did him no more harm than if he had thrown it against a wall; but it answered Friday’s end, for the rogue was so void of fear that he did it purely to make the bear follow him, and show us some laugh as he called it.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五脚程比那熊快(照我们的说法),很快就赶上了它,捡起一块大石头朝它掷去,正打在它头上,可那对它的伤害,不比朝墙上扔一块石头更甚;不过这倒合了星期五的心意,因为这胆大包天的家伙这么做,纯粹是要引那熊来追他,好照他说的给我们看场笑话。

paragraphs.en: As soon as the bear felt the blow, and saw him, he turns about and comes after him, taking very long strides, and shuffling on at a strange rate, so as would have put a horse to a middling gallop; away runs Friday, and takes his course as if he ran towards us for help; so we all resolved to fire at once upon the bear, and deliver my man; though I was angry at him for bringing the bear back upon us, when he was going about his own business another way; and especially I was angry that he had turned the bear upon us, and then ran away; and I called out, “You dog! is this your making us laugh?
paragraphs.cn: 那熊一挨这一下,又见了他,便掉过身来追他,迈着极长的大步,以一种古怪的姿势蹒跚疾走,那速度足以叫一匹马跑成个不快不慢的奔跑;星期五撒腿就跑,那路数像是朝我们这边跑来求救;于是我们都打定主意一齐向那熊开枪,救下我的仆人;虽说我很生他的气,怪他把熊引回来冲着我们,而它本来正朝另一个方向办自己的事;尤其气他把熊招到我们头上,自己却跑开了;我便喊道:“你这狗东西!这就是你逗我们发笑的法子?

paragraphs.en: Come away, and take your horse, that we may shoot the creature.”
paragraphs.cn: 快过来,牵上你的马,好让我们打死这畜生。”

paragraphs.en: He heard me, and cried out, “No shoot, no shoot; stand still, and you get much laugh:” and as the nimble creature ran two feet for the bear’s one, he turned on a sudden on one side of us, and seeing a great oak-tree fit for his purpose, he beckoned to us to follow; and doubling his pace, he got nimbly up the tree, laying his gun down upon the ground, at about five or six yards from the bottom of the tree.
paragraphs.cn: 他听见了,喊道:“别开枪,别开枪;站着别动,你们有好多乐子看:”那敏捷的家伙他跑两步、熊才跑一步,他忽然转到我们的一侧,瞧见一棵合他心意的大橡树,便招手叫我们跟上;他加快脚步,身手利落地爬上那树,把枪撂在离树根约莫五六码远的地上。

paragraphs.en: The bear soon came to the tree, and we followed at a distance: the first thing he did he stopped at the gun, smelt at it, but let it lie, and up he scrambles into the tree, climbing like a cat, though so monstrous heavy.
paragraphs.cn: 那熊很快到了树下,我们远远跟着:它头一件事是在枪旁停住,嗅了嗅,却由它撂着,便手脚并用往树上爬,虽说那样笨重庞大,竟像猫一样往上攀。

paragraphs.en: I was amazed at the folly, as I thought it, of my man, and could not for my life see anything to laugh at, till seeing the bear get up the tree, we all rode near to him.
paragraphs.cn: 我看着我这仆人的傻劲(我当时是这么想的),暗自吃惊,怎么也瞧不出有什么好笑的,直到见那熊爬上了树,我们才都策马靠近他。

paragraphs.en: When we came to the tree, there was Friday got out to the small end of a large branch, and the bear got about half-way to him.
paragraphs.cn: 我们到树下时,只见星期五已经爬到一根大树枝的细梢上,那熊爬到了离他约莫一半的地方。

paragraphs.en: As soon as the bear got out to that part where the limb of the tree was weaker, “Ha!” says he to us, “now you see me teachee the bear dance:” so he began jumping and shaking the bough, at which the bear began to totter, but stood still, and began to look behind him, to see how he should get back; then, indeed, we did laugh heartily.
paragraphs.cn: 熊一爬到那树枝较弱的部位,他便冲我们喊:“哈!这下你们看我教这熊跳舞:”于是他开始又蹦又摇那枝子,弄得熊直打晃,却站住不动,回头张望,想瞧瞧怎么退回去;这一下,我们可真是开怀大笑了。

paragraphs.en: But Friday had not done with him by a great deal; when seeing him stand still, he called out to him again, as if he had supposed the bear could speak English, “What, you come no farther? pray you come farther;” so he left jumping and shaking the tree; and the bear, just as if he understood what he said, did come a little farther; then he began jumping again, and the bear stopped again.
paragraphs.cn: 可星期五远没跟它了结呢;见它站住不动,他又冲它喊起来,仿佛当那熊听得懂英语似的:“怎么,你不往前来了?求你再往前来些;”于是他停了跳、停了摇树;那熊竟像听懂了他的话,果真又往前挪了一点;他便又跳起来,那熊又停住了。

paragraphs.en: We thought now was a good time to knock him in the head, and called to Friday to stand still and we should shoot the bear: but he cried out earnestly, “Oh, pray!
paragraphs.cn: 我们心想这会儿正是敲碎它脑袋的好时机,便喊星期五站着别动,好让我们打那熊:可他急切地喊道:“噢,求你们!

paragraphs.en: Oh, pray! no shoot, me shoot by and then:” he would have said by-and-by.
paragraphs.cn: 噢,求你们!别开枪,我一会儿开枪:”他是想说“待一会儿”。

paragraphs.en: However, to shorten the story, Friday danced so much, and the bear stood so ticklish, that we had laughing enough, but still could not imagine what the fellow would do: for first we thought he depended upon shaking the bear off; and we found the bear was too cunning for that too; for he would not go out far enough to be thrown down, but clung fast with his great broad claws and feet, so that we could not imagine what would be the end of it, and what the jest would be at last.
paragraphs.cn: 然而,长话短说,星期五跳个不停,那熊站得战战兢兢,把我们逗得够乐,却仍猜不透这家伙究竟要干什么:起先我们以为他指望把熊摇下来;可我们发现那熊也太狡猾,不上这个当,它不肯往外爬到会被摔下去的地方,只用它那对又宽又大的爪子和脚死死攀住,弄得我们猜不出这事的结局,也猜不出末了会是怎样一场笑话。

paragraphs.en: But Friday put us out of doubt quickly: for seeing the bear cling fast to the bough, and that he would not be persuaded to come any farther, “Well, well,” says Friday, “you no come farther, me go; you no come to me, me come to you;” and upon this he went out to the smaller end, where it would bend with his weight, and gently let himself down by it, sliding down the bough till he came near enough to jump down on his feet, and away he ran to his gun, took it up, and stood still.
paragraphs.cn: 可星期五很快替我们解了疑:他见那熊死死攀住枝子,怎么劝也不肯再往前来,便说:“好吧,好吧,你不来,我去;你不来找我,我来找你;”说着他往那更细的一头爬去,那里在他体重下会弯下来,他便顺着枝子轻轻往下溜,一直溜到离地够近、能跳下落地时,便一跃而下,跑向他的枪,拿起枪站定了。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said I to him, “Friday, what will you do now?
paragraphs.cn: “好啊,”我对他说,“星期五,你这下打算怎么办?

paragraphs.en: Why don’t you shoot him?”
paragraphs.cn: 你怎么不开枪打它?”

paragraphs.en: “No shoot,” says Friday, “no yet; me shoot now, me no kill; me stay, give you one more laugh:” and, indeed, so he did; for when the bear saw his enemy gone, he came back from the bough, where he stood, but did it very cautiously, looking behind him every step, and coming backward till he got into the body of the tree, then, with the same hinder end foremost, he came down the tree, grasping it with his claws, and moving one foot at a time, very leisurely.
paragraphs.cn: “别开枪,”星期五说,“还不到时候;我现在开枪,打不死它;我等等,再给你们看一场乐子:”果然,他真这么做了;因为那熊见敌人走了,便从它站着的枝子上往回退,退得却极小心,每退一步都回头张望,倒退着一直退到树身,然后照样后半身在前,从树上爬下来,用爪子攀着,一次挪一只脚,慢条斯理。

paragraphs.en: At this juncture, and just before he could set his hind foot on the ground, Friday stepped up close to him, clapped the muzzle of his piece into his ear, and shot him dead.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这当口,正当它后脚将要触地之际,星期五一步抢上前去,把枪口抵进它耳朵里,一枪把它打死了。

paragraphs.en: Then the rogue turned about to see if we did not laugh; and when he saw we were pleased by our looks, he began to laugh very loud.
paragraphs.cn: 随后这机灵鬼转过身来,看我们笑没笑;一见我们神色欢喜,便放声大笑起来。

paragraphs.en: “So we kill bear in my country,” says Friday.
paragraphs.cn: “在我的家乡,我们就是这样打熊的,”星期五说。

paragraphs.en: “So you kill them?” says I; “why, you have no guns.”
paragraphs.cn: “你们就这么打熊?”我说;“可是,你们又没有枪。”

paragraphs.en: —“No,” says he, “no gun, but shoot great much long arrow.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有,”他说,“没枪,可是射又长又多的箭。”

paragraphs.en: This was a good diversion to us; but we were still in a wild place, and our guide very much hurt, and what to do we hardly knew; the howling of wolves ran much in my head; and, indeed, except the noise I once heard on the shore of Africa, of which I have said something already, I never heard anything that filled me with so much horror.
paragraphs.cn: 这给了我们一场好乐子;可我们仍身处荒野,向导又伤得不轻,该怎么办我们几乎没了主意;狼的嗥叫一直在我脑子里回响;老实说,除了从前在非洲海岸上听过的那一次(那事我先前已略提过),我从没听过什么声音叫我这般毛骨悚然。

paragraphs.en: These things, and the approach of night, called us off, or else, as Friday would have had us, we should certainly have taken the skin of this monstrous creature off, which was worth saving; but we had near three leagues to go, and our guide hastened us; so we left him, and went forward on our journey.
paragraphs.cn: 这些事,加上夜色将临,催着我们上路;不然的话,照星期五的意思,我们准定会剥下这庞然大物的皮,那皮是值得留下的;可我们还有近三里格的路要走,向导又催得急;于是我们撇下它,继续赶路。

paragraphs.en: The ground was still covered with snow, though not so deep and dangerous as on the mountains; and the ravenous creatures, as we heard afterwards, were come down into the forest and plain country, pressed by hunger, to seek for food, and had done a great deal of mischief in the villages, where they surprised the country people, killed a great many of their sheep and horses, and some people too.
paragraphs.cn: 地上依旧盖着雪,只是不像山上那么深、那么危险;那些饿极了的畜生,我们后来听说,被饥饿逼着下到了森林和平原地带觅食,在村庄里闯了不少祸,惊扰了乡下人,咬死了他们许多羊和马,也咬死了几个人。

paragraphs.en: We had one dangerous place to pass, and our guide told us if there were more wolves in the country we should find them there; and this was a small plain, surrounded with woods on every side, and a long, narrow defile, or lane, which we were to pass to get through the wood, and then we should come to the village where we were to lodge.
paragraphs.cn: 我们有一处险地要过,向导告诉我们,这一带若还有狼,准会在那儿碰上;那是一片小平原,四面环林,还有一条又长又窄的隘口(或者说小径),我们得穿过它才能出林,然后便到我们要投宿的村子了。

paragraphs.en: It was within half-an-hour of sunset when we entered the wood, and a little after sunset when we came into the plain: we met with nothing in the first wood, except that in a little plain within the wood, which was not above two furlongs over, we saw five great wolves cross the road, full speed, one after another, as if they had been in chase of some prey, and had it in view; they took no notice of us, and were gone out of sight in a few moments.
paragraphs.cn: 我们进林时离日落还有半个钟头,出到平原上时已是日落之后不久:头一片林子里我们什么也没遇上,只是在林中一小片不过两浪远的空地上,看见五头大狼一头接一头飞速横穿过路,像是在追赶什么猎物、且已望见了它;它们没理会我们,不一会儿便没了踪影。

paragraphs.en: Upon this, our guide, who, by the way, was but a fainthearted fellow, bid us keep in a ready posture, for he believed there were more wolves a-coming.
paragraphs.cn: 见此情形,我们那位——顺便说一句——胆子很小的向导,叫我们做好戒备,因为他相信还有更多的狼要来。

paragraphs.en: We kept our arms ready, and our eyes about us; but we saw no more wolves till we came through that wood, which was near half a league, and entered the plain.
paragraphs.cn: 我们把武器备好,四下留神;可直到穿过那片近半里格的林子、进到平原上,我们再没见到别的狼。

paragraphs.en: As soon as we came into the plain, we had occasion enough to look about us.
paragraphs.cn: 一进到平原上,我们就有的是理由四下张望了。

paragraphs.en: The first object we met with was a dead horse; that is to say, a poor horse which the wolves had killed, and at least a dozen of them at work, we could not say eating him, but picking his bones rather; for they had eaten up all the flesh before.
paragraphs.cn: 我们碰上的头一样东西是一匹死马;说白了,是匹被狼咬死的可怜的马,至少有一打狼正围着它忙活,与其说是在吃它,不如说是在啃它的骨头,因为肉早被它们吃光了。

paragraphs.en: We did not think fit to disturb them at their feast, neither did they take much notice of us.
paragraphs.cn: 我们觉得不便去搅扰它们的这顿盛宴,它们也没怎么理会我们。

paragraphs.en: Friday would have let fly at them, but I would not suffer him by any means; for I found we were like to have more business upon our hands than we were aware of.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五本想朝它们放枪,可我无论如何不许他这么做;因为我看出,我们要应付的麻烦,怕比自己料想的还多。

paragraphs.en: We had not gone half over the plain when we began to hear the wolves howl in the wood on our left in a frightful manner, and presently after we saw about a hundred coming on directly towards us, all in a body, and most of them in a line, as regularly as an army drawn up by experienced officers.
paragraphs.cn: 我们过平原还没到一半,就开始听见左边林子里传来狼群骇人的嗥叫,紧接着便看见约莫一百头狼径直朝我们涌来,拧成一团,大多排成一线,整齐得像一支由老练军官布好阵的军队。

paragraphs.en: I scarce knew in what manner to receive them, but found to draw ourselves in a close line was the only way; so we formed in a moment; but that we might not have too much interval, I ordered that only every other man should fire, and that the others, who had not fired, should stand ready to give them a second volley immediately, if they continued to advance upon us; and then that those that had fired at first should not pretend to load their fusees again, but stand ready, every one with a pistol, for we were all armed with a fusee and a pair of pistols each man; so we were, by this method, able to fire six volleys, half of us at a time; however, at present we had no necessity; for upon firing the first volley, the enemy made a full stop, being terrified as well with the noise as with the fire.
paragraphs.cn: 我几乎不知该怎样应付它们,可发现把我们自己收拢成密集的一列是唯一的法子;于是我们转眼间摆好了阵;为免间隔太大,我下令每隔一人才开一枪,没开枪的那些人则备好,一旦它们继续向我们逼近,便立刻给它们第二轮齐射;头一批开过枪的人不必再去装弹,而是各持一把手枪备着,因为我们每人都配了一支火枪和一对手枪;这样一来,靠这法子我们能打六轮齐射,每次半数人开枪;不过眼下还用不着;因为头一轮齐射一放,敌人便完全停住了,枪声和火光把它们都吓住了。

paragraphs.en: Four of them being shot in the head, dropped; several others were wounded, and went bleeding off, as we could see by the snow.
paragraphs.cn: 其中四头被打中脑袋倒下;另有几头受了伤,淌着血跑开了,这我们从雪地上看得出来。

paragraphs.en: I found they stopped, but did not immediately retreat; whereupon, remembering that I had been told that the fiercest creatures were terrified at the voice of a man, I caused all the company to halloo as loud as they could; and I found the notion not altogether mistaken; for upon our shout they began to retire and turn about.
paragraphs.cn: 我发觉它们停住了,却没有立刻退走;于是我想起曾听人说过,最凶猛的野兽也怕人的呼喝声,便叫全队人放开嗓子大喊;我发现这说法并非全然无稽,因为一听我们喊,它们便开始后退、掉头。

paragraphs.en: I then ordered a second volley to be fired in their rear, which put them to the gallop, and away they went to the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 我随即下令朝它们后队再放一轮齐射,这一下把它们赶得撒蹄狂奔,一齐逃回林子里去了。

paragraphs.en: This gave us leisure to charge our pieces again; and that we might lose no time, we kept going; but we had but little more than loaded our fusees, and put ourselves in readiness, when we heard a terrible noise in the same wood on our left, only that it was farther onward, the same way we were to go.
paragraphs.cn: 这让我们得空重新装弹;为不耽误工夫,我们边走边装;可我们刚给火枪装好弹、备停当,就听见左边那同一片林子里传来一阵可怕的响动,只是更靠前些,正是我们要去的方向。

paragraphs.en: The night was coming on, and the light began to be dusky, which made it worse on our side; but the noise increasing, we could easily perceive that it was the howling and yelling of those hellish creatures; and on a sudden we perceived three troops of wolves, one on our left, one behind us, and one in our front, so that we seemed to be surrounded with them: however, as they did not fall upon us, we kept our way forward, as fast as we could make our horses go, which, the way being very rough, was only a good hard trot.
paragraphs.cn: 夜色渐渐逼近,天光开始昏暗,这对我们这边更为不利;可那响动越来越大,我们轻易便听出,那是这些恶魔般的畜生在嗥叫嘶吼;忽然间我们发觉三队狼——一队在左,一队在后,一队在前——仿佛把我们团团围住了:好在它们并未扑上来,我们便只管往前走,尽量让马快跑,只是道路极其崎岖,顶多不过是稳稳的一路快步小跑。

paragraphs.en: In this manner, we came in view of the entrance of a wood, through which we were to pass, at the farther side of the plain; but we were greatly surprised, when coming nearer the lane or pass, we saw a confused number of wolves standing just at the entrance.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样,我们望见了平原那一头一片林子的入口,我们正要从那里穿过去;可当我们走近那小径或隘口时,却大吃一惊,只见入口处密密麻麻站着一大群狼。

paragraphs.en: On a sudden, at another opening of the wood, we heard the noise of a gun, and looking that way, out rushed a horse, with a saddle and a bridle on him, flying like the wind, and sixteen or seventeen wolves after him, full speed: the horse had the advantage of them; but as we supposed that he could not hold it at that rate, we doubted not but they would get up with him at last: no question but they did.
paragraphs.cn: 忽然间,在林子另一处豁口,我们听见一声枪响,朝那边望去,只见一匹马冲了出来,身上还配着鞍辔,像风一样飞奔,后面十六七头狼全速紧追:那马虽占了上风,可我们料想它这速度撑不了多久,毫不怀疑它终会被追上:它准是被追上了。

paragraphs.en: But here we had a most horrible sight; for riding up to the entrance where the horse came out, we found the carcasses of another horse and of two men, devoured by the ravenous creatures; and one of the men was no doubt the same whom we heard fire the gun, for there lay a gun just by him fired off; but as to the man, his head and the upper part of his body was eaten up.
paragraphs.cn: 可这里我们撞见了极其恐怖的一幕;因为策马来到那马冲出来的入口处,我们发现另一匹马和两个人的尸首,已被那些贪婪的畜生吞噬;那两人中有一个,无疑就是我们听见放枪的那个,因为他身边正躺着一支放过的枪;可那人呢,他的头和上半身都被吃光了。

paragraphs.en: This filled us with horror, and we knew not what course to take; but the creatures resolved us soon, for they gathered about us presently, in hopes of prey; and I verily believe there were three hundred of them.
paragraphs.cn: 这一幕叫我们毛骨悚然,不知该走哪条路;可那些畜生很快替我们下了决心,因为它们眼下就围拢过来,指望着捕食;我确信它们足有三百头。

paragraphs.en: It happened, very much to our advantage, that at the entrance into the wood, but a little way from it, there lay some large timber-trees, which had been cut down the summer before, and I suppose lay there for carriage.
paragraphs.cn: 对我们大为有利的是,恰好在进林的入口处、离它不远的地方,横着几根大木料,是头年夏天砍倒的,我想是留在那儿等着运走的。

paragraphs.en: I drew my little troop in among those trees, and placing ourselves in a line behind one long tree, I advised them all to alight, and keeping that tree before us for a breastwork, to stand in a triangle, or three fronts, enclosing our horses in the centre.
paragraphs.cn: 我把我这小队人马带进那些木料之间,让大家排成一列,躲在一根长木料后面,劝他们全都下马,把那根木料当作胸墙挡在身前,摆成一个三角、也就是三面朝外的阵势,把我们的马圈在当中。

paragraphs.en: We did so, and it was well we did; for never was a more furious charge than the creatures made upon us in this place.
paragraphs.cn: 我们照办了,幸亏我们这么做了;因为这些畜生在此处向我们发起的猛攻,凶得前所未有。

paragraphs.en: They came on with a growling kind of noise, and mounted the piece of timber, which, as I said, was our breastwork, as if they were only rushing upon their prey; and this fury of theirs, it seems, was principally occasioned by their seeing our horses behind us.
paragraphs.cn: 它们发出一种低吼似的响声扑上来,爬上那根木料——我方才说过,那是我们的胸墙——仿佛只顾着扑向猎物;它们这般凶狂,看来主要是因为望见了我们身后的马。

paragraphs.en: I ordered our men to fire as before, every other man; and they took their aim so sure that they killed several of the wolves at the first volley; but there was a necessity to keep a continual firing, for they came on like devils, those behind pushing on those before.
paragraphs.cn: 我命令我们的人照先前那样,每隔一人开枪;他们瞄得极准,头一轮齐射就打死了好几头狼;可我们必须连着不停地开火,因为它们像恶魔一样涌上来,后面的推着前面的。

paragraphs.en: When we had fired a second volley of our fusees, we thought they stopped a little, and I hoped they would have gone off, but it was but a moment, for others came forward again; so we fired two volleys of our pistols; and I believe in these four firings we had killed seventeen or eighteen of them, and lamed twice as many, yet they came on again.
paragraphs.cn: 我们放过第二轮火枪齐射后,只觉它们稍稍停了停,我盼着它们会退走,可那不过是一瞬,别的狼又扑上前来;于是我们放了两轮手枪;我相信这四轮开火下来,我们打死了十七八头,打瘸了加倍那么多,可它们仍旧扑上来。

paragraphs.en: I was loth to spend our shot too hastily; so I called my servant, not my man Friday, for he was better employed, for, with the greatest dexterity imaginable, he had charged my fusee and his own while we were engaged—but, as I said, I called my other man, and giving him a horn of powder, I had him lay a train all along the piece of timber, and let it be a large train.
paragraphs.cn: 我不愿把弹药耗得太急;便叫我的仆人——不是我那仆人星期五,他另有更好的用处,因为他手脚极其麻利,趁我们酣战时已把我的火枪和他自己的都装好了弹——而是,我方才说了,叫我另一个仆人,给了他一角火药,让他沿着那根木料铺一道药线,而且要铺得又粗又长。

paragraphs.en: He did so, and had but just time to get away, when the wolves came up to it, and some got upon it, when I, snapping an uncharged pistol close to the powder, set it on fire; those that were upon the timber were scorched with it, and six or seven of them fell; or rather jumped in among us with the force and fright of the fire; we despatched these in an instant, and the rest were so frightened with the light, which the night—for it was now very near dark—made more terrible that they drew back a little; upon which I ordered our last pistols to be fired off in one volley, and after that we gave a shout; upon this the wolves turned tail, and we sallied immediately upon near twenty lame ones that we found struggling on the ground, and fell to cutting them with our swords, which answered our expectation, for the crying and howling they made was better understood by their fellows; so that they all fled and left us.
paragraphs.cn: 他照办了,刚够时间撤开身,那些狼便涌到了木料前,有几头爬了上去,这时我把一支没装弹的手枪凑近火药一扳,便把药线点着了;爬在木料上的那几头被烧得焦头烂额,六七头栽了下来,或者说是被火的冲力和惊吓吓得跳进了我们中间;我们一转眼就把这几头结果了,其余的被那火光吓得不轻——如今天已近乎全黑,火光越发显得可怕——它们便稍稍退了些;我趁势下令把最后几支手枪一齐放掉,放完我们又齐声大喊;这一下狼群掉头就逃,我们立时扑向近二十头在地上挣扎的瘸狼,挥剑砍杀它们,这一招正合我们所愿,因为它们发出的哀号嗥叫,同伴们比什么都听得明白;于是它们全都逃窜,把我们撇下了。

paragraphs.en: We had, first and last, killed about threescore of them, and had it been daylight we had killed many more.
paragraphs.cn: 前前后后,我们大约打死了六十头,若是白天,还能打死更多。

paragraphs.en: The field of battle being thus cleared, we made forward again, for we had still near a league to go.
paragraphs.cn: 战场就这样清了出来,我们又继续前行,因为还有近一里格的路要走。

paragraphs.en: We heard the ravenous creatures howl and yell in the woods as we went several times, and sometimes we fancied we saw some of them; but the snow dazzling our eyes, we were not certain.
paragraphs.cn: 一路上,我们好几次听见那些贪婪的畜生在林中嗥叫嘶吼,有时还恍惚觉得瞧见了几头;可白雪晃花了我们的眼,拿不准是不是真的。

paragraphs.en: In about an hour more we came to the town where we were to lodge, which we found in a terrible fright and all in arms; for, it seems, the night before the wolves and some bears had broken into the village, and put them in such terror that they were obliged to keep guard night and day, but especially in the night, to preserve their cattle, and indeed their people.
paragraphs.cn: 又走了约莫一个钟头,我们来到要投宿的那座镇子,只见镇上人心惶惶、全都拿起了武器;原来,头天夜里狼和几头熊闯进了村子,把他们吓得不轻,逼得他们不得不昼夜守卫,尤其是夜里,好保住他们的牲口,其实也是保住他们的人。

paragraphs.en: The next morning our guide was so ill, and his limbs swelled so much with the rankling of his two wounds, that he could go no farther; so we were obliged to take a new guide here, and go to Toulouse, where we found a warm climate, a fruitful, pleasant country, and no snow, no wolves, nor anything like them; but when we told our story at Toulouse, they told us it was nothing but what was ordinary in the great forest at the foot of the mountains, especially when the snow lay on the ground; but they inquired much what kind of guide we had got who would venture to bring us that way in such a severe season, and told us it was surprising we were not all devoured.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上,我们的向导病得很重,那两处伤口发了炎,腿肿得厉害,他再也走不动了;于是我们只好在这儿另换一名向导,前往图卢兹,到了那里,我们发现气候温暖,乡野肥沃宜人,没有雪,没有狼,也没有任何类似的东西;可当我们在图卢兹讲起我们的经历,他们却说这在山脚下那片大森林里不过是寻常事,尤其是地上有雪的时候;不过他们再三追问,我们究竟找了个什么样的向导,竟敢在这般严酷的时节领我们走那条路,还说我们没被全数吃掉,真是稀奇。

paragraphs.en: When we told them how we placed ourselves and the horses in the middle, they blamed us exceedingly, and told us it was fifty to one but we had been all destroyed, for it was the sight of the horses which made the wolves so furious, seeing their prey, and that at other times they are really afraid of a gun; but being excessively hungry, and raging on that account, the eagerness to come at the horses had made them senseless of danger, and that if we had not by the continual fire, and at last by the stratagem of the train of powder, mastered them, it had been great odds but that we had been torn to pieces; whereas, had we been content to have sat still on horseback, and fired as horsemen, they would not have taken the horses so much for their own, when men were on their backs, as otherwise; and withal, they told us that at last, if we had stood altogether, and left our horses, they would have been so eager to have devoured them, that we might have come off safe, especially having our firearms in our hands, being so many in number.
paragraphs.cn: 当我们讲到自己和马是怎样围在当中时,他们大加责备,说我们能不全军覆没,那是五十分之一的侥幸,因为正是望见了马,狼群才那样凶狂——它们瞧见了猎物;平时它们其实是怕枪的,可饿得太狠、为此发了狂,一心要扑到马跟前,便对危险浑然不觉了;若不是我们靠不停开火、最后又靠那道火药线的计策制住了它们,我们十有八九早被撕成碎片了;反倒是,倘若我们甘心稳坐马背、像骑手那样开枪,狼群就不会那么把马当作自家的猎物,因为马背上有人骑着,便不同了;此外他们还说,到末了,倘若我们全都站到一处、撇下马匹,狼群会急着去吞那些马,我们说不定就能安然脱身,何况我们手里有火器,人数又这么多。

paragraphs.en: For my part, I was never so sensible of danger in my life; for, seeing above three hundred devils come roaring and open-mouthed to devour us, and having nothing to shelter us or retreat to, I gave myself over for lost; and, as it was, I believe I shall never care to cross those mountains again: I think I would much rather go a thousand leagues by sea, though I was sure to meet with a storm once a-week.
paragraphs.cn: 就我而言,我平生从未这样真切地感到过危险;因为眼看三百多个魔鬼张着大口、吼叫着扑来要吞掉我们,又无处遮蔽、无处可退,我只当自己没命了;照这情形,我想我这辈子再不愿翻越那些山了:我情愿走一千里格的海路,哪怕明知一星期要遇上一回风暴。

paragraphs.en: I have nothing uncommon to take notice of in my passage through France—nothing but what other travellers have given an account of with much more advantage than I can.
paragraphs.cn: 我穿越法国的这段路程,没什么稀奇的可记——无非是别的旅人早已记述过的,而且比我记得精彩得多。

paragraphs.en: I travelled from Toulouse to Paris, and without any considerable stay came to Calais, and landed safe at Dover the 14th of January, after having had a severe cold season to travel in.
paragraphs.cn: 我从图卢兹赶到巴黎,没怎么停留便到了加来,一月十四日平安在多佛尔登陆,这一路上正赶上严寒的时节。

paragraphs.en: I was now come to the centre of my travels, and had in a little time all my new-discovered estate safe about me, the bills of exchange which I brought with me having been currently paid.
paragraphs.cn: 这时我已到了旅程的中心,不多久,我那些新到手的产业便安然归我所有,我随身带来的那些汇票也都如期兑付了。

paragraphs.en: My principal guide and privy-counsellor was my good ancient widow, who, in gratitude for the money I had sent her, thought no pains too much nor care too great to employ for me; and I trusted her so entirely that I was perfectly easy as to the security of my effects; and, indeed, I was very happy from the beginning, and now to the end, in the unspotted integrity of this good gentlewoman.
paragraphs.cn: 我的主要顾问和心腹是那位善良的老寡妇;她感念我先前寄给她的钱,为我办事从不嫌辛苦、不嫌操心过甚;我对她全然信赖,以致对自己财物的安稳完全放了心;说实话,从头到尾,这位善良女子那毫无瑕疵的正直,都叫我十分欣幸。

paragraphs.en: And now, having resolved to dispose of my plantation in the Brazils, I wrote to my old friend at Lisbon, who, having offered it to the two merchants, the survivors of my trustees, who lived in the Brazils, they accepted the offer, and remitted thirty-three thousand pieces of eight to a correspondent of theirs at Lisbon to pay for it.
paragraphs.cn: 如今,我已决意脱手在巴西的种植园,便写信给我里斯本的老朋友;他把园子转让给那两位商人——我那几位受托人中活下来的两位,他们就住在巴西——他们接了这桩买卖,汇了三万三千枚八字银元给他们在里斯本的一位代办人,用来付款。

paragraphs.en: In return, I signed the instrument of sale in the form which they sent from Lisbon, and sent it to my old man, who sent me the bills of exchange for thirty-two thousand eight hundred pieces of eight for the estate, reserving the payment of one hundred moidores a year to him (the old man) during his life, and fifty moidores afterwards to his son for his life, which I had promised them, and which the plantation was to make good as a rent-charge.
paragraphs.cn: 作为回报,我按他们从里斯本寄来的格式签了卖契,寄给我那位老友;他又把三万二千八百枚八字银元的汇票寄给我,作为那产业的价款,只留下每年一百枚莫伊多金币付给他(那老人)终身,他死后再每年付五十枚给他儿子终身——这是我答应过他们的,由那种植园作为地租来担保。

paragraphs.en: And thus I have given the first part of a life of fortune and adventure—a life of Providence’s chequer-work, and of a variety which the world will seldom be able to show the like of; beginning foolishly, but closing much more happily than any part of it ever gave me leave so much as to hope for.
paragraphs.cn: 至此,我讲完了这一段充满际遇与冒险的人生的前半部——一段天意织就的斑斓人生,其变幻之多,世上罕有其匹;开头愚蠢糊涂,结尾却比其中任何一段所曾容我指望的都要幸福得多。

paragraphs.en: Any one would think that in this state of complicated good fortune I was past running any more hazards—and so, indeed, I had been, if other circumstances had concurred; but I was inured to a wandering life, had no family, nor many relations; nor, however rich, had I contracted fresh acquaintance; and though I had sold my estate in the Brazils, yet I could not keep that country out of my head, and had a great mind to be upon the wing again; especially I could not resist the strong inclination I had to see my island, and to know if the poor Spaniards were in being there.
paragraphs.cn: 谁都会以为,处在这般层层叠叠的好运里,我该不会再去冒什么险了——说真的,倘若别的情形也凑在一起,我本也不会再冒险的;可我早已惯了漂泊的生活,没有家室,亲戚也不多;纵然富有,也没结下什么新交;虽说我卖掉了在巴西的产业,却仍把那地方放不下,一心又想振翅远行;尤其我按捺不住那股强烈的念头,想去看看我那座岛,想知道那几个可怜的西班牙人是否还在那里。

paragraphs.en: My true friend, the widow, earnestly dissuaded me from it, and so far prevailed with me, that for almost seven years she prevented my running abroad, during which time I took my two nephews, the children of one of my brothers, into my care; the eldest, having something of his own, I bred up as a gentleman, and gave him a settlement of some addition to his estate after my decease.
paragraphs.cn: 我那位真诚的朋友——那寡妇——极力劝阻我,竟也奏了效,足足有近七年光景,她拦住我没让我远游;这期间我把我的两个侄儿(我一个兄弟的孩子)接来照料;老大自己略有些家产,我把他当作绅士来培养,并在我身后另给他添了一份产业。

paragraphs.en: The other I placed with the captain of a ship; and after five years, finding him a sensible, bold, enterprising young fellow, I put him into a good ship, and sent him to sea; and this young fellow afterwards drew me in, as old as I was, to further adventures myself.
paragraphs.cn: 老二我托付给一位船长;五年之后,见他是个明理、勇敢、有闯劲的年轻人,我便让他上了一条好船,送他出海;这个年轻人后来又把我这把年纪的人牵进了新的冒险。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, I in part settled myself here; for, first of all, I married, and that not either to my disadvantage or dissatisfaction, and had three children, two sons and one daughter; but my wife dying, and my nephew coming home with good success from a voyage to Spain, my inclination to go abroad, and his importunity, prevailed, and engaged me to go in his ship as a private trader to the East Indies; this was in the year 1694.
paragraphs.cn: 在这期间,我也在此地大致安顿了下来;因为首先,我结了婚,这门亲事无论于我的利益还是心意都无所亏损,还生了三个孩子,两男一女;可后来我妻子去世,我那侄儿从西班牙的航行中满载而归,我想出海的心思加上他的一再怂恿,终于占了上风,促使我以私商的身份搭他的船前往东印度群岛;这是在一六九四年。

paragraphs.en: In this voyage I visited my new colony in the island, saw my successors the Spaniards, had the old story of their lives and of the villains I left there; how at first they insulted the poor Spaniards, how they afterwards agreed, disagreed, united, separated, and how at last the Spaniards were obliged to use violence with them; how they were subjected to the Spaniards, how honestly the Spaniards used them—a history, if it were entered into, as full of variety and wonderful accidents as my own part—particularly, also, as to their battles with the Caribbeans, who landed several times upon the island, and as to the improvement they made upon the island itself, and how five of them made an attempt upon the mainland, and brought away eleven men and five women prisoners, by which, at my coming, I found about twenty young children on the island.
paragraphs.cn: 在这次航行中,我探访了我在那岛上的新殖民地,见到了我的继任者——那几个西班牙人,听了他们生活的老故事,以及我留在那里的那几个恶棍的往事:起先他们如何欺侮那几个可怜的西班牙人,后来又如何时而和睦、时而反目、时而联合、时而分裂,末了西班牙人如何不得不对他们动武,他们如何被西班牙人制服,西班牙人又如何厚道地待他们——这段历史,若细细道来,其变幻曲折、奇遇之多,不亚于我自己那一段——尤其是他们和加勒比人的几番厮杀(那些人曾几次登上岛来),以及他们在岛上所做的种种经营,还有他们五个人如何进袭大陆,掳回十一个男人、五个女人作俘虏,以至我这次来时,发现岛上已有约莫二十个幼小的孩子。

paragraphs.en: Here I stayed about twenty days, left them supplies of all necessary things, and particularly of arms, powder, shot, clothes, tools, and two workmen, which I had brought from England with me, viz. a carpenter and a smith.
paragraphs.cn: 我在这里逗留了约莫二十天,给他们留下了一切必需的物品,尤其是武器、火药、弹丸、衣服、工具,还有两名我从英国带来的工匠,即一名木匠和一名铁匠。

paragraphs.en: Besides this, I shared the lands into parts with them, reserved to myself the property of the whole, but gave them such parts respectively as they agreed on; and having settled all things with them, and engaged them not to leave the place, I left them there.
paragraphs.cn: 除此之外,我把土地分给了他们,把整块地的产权保留在自己名下,却按他们各自商定的份额分给他们相应的部分;把一切都同他们安排妥当、并要他们答应不离开此地之后,我便把他们留在了那里。

paragraphs.en: From thence I touched at the Brazils, from whence I sent a bark, which I bought there, with more people to the island; and in it, besides other supplies, I sent seven women, being such as I found proper for service, or for wives to such as would take them.
paragraphs.cn: 从那里我又到了巴西,从巴西打发了一条我在当地买下的小船,载着更多的人前往那岛;船上除了别的补给,我还送去了七个女人,都是我看着合用来做工、或给愿意娶她们的人做妻子的。

paragraphs.en: As to the Englishmen, I promised to send them some women from England, with a good cargo of necessaries, if they would apply themselves to planting—which I afterwards could not perform.
paragraphs.cn: 至于那几个英国人,我答应从英国给他们送些女人来,再带一大批必需的货物,只要他们肯用心种地——这事我后来却没能办到。

paragraphs.en: The fellows proved very honest and diligent after they were mastered and had their properties set apart for them.
paragraphs.cn: 那几个家伙被制服、又各自分得了产业之后,倒证明是十分老实勤快的。

paragraphs.en: I sent them, also, from the Brazils, five cows, three of them being big with calf, some sheep, and some hogs, which when I came again were considerably increased.
paragraphs.cn: 我还从巴西给他们送去了五头母牛,其中三头怀着牛犊,又送了些羊和些猪,等我再来时,已增添了不少。

paragraphs.en: But all these things, with an account how three hundred Caribbees came and invaded them, and ruined their plantations, and how they fought with that whole number twice, and were at first defeated, and one of them killed; but at last, a storm destroying their enemies’ canoes, they famished or destroyed almost all the rest, and renewed and recovered the possession of their plantation, and still lived upon the island.
paragraphs.cn: 可这一切,连同三百个加勒比人如何前来进犯、毁了他们的种植园,他们又如何两次同那整整一群人交战、起先落败、还折了一人;末了却因一场风暴毁掉了敌人的独木舟,他们便饿死或杀死了其余几乎所有的敌人,重新夺回并恢复了对种植园的占有,仍旧在那岛上生活——凡此种种,

paragraphs.en: All these things, with some very surprising incidents in some new adventures of my own, for ten years more, I shall give a farther account of in the Second Part of my Story.
paragraphs.cn: 这一切,连同我自己在此后十年间一些新冒险里几桩极其惊人的遭遇,我都将在我故事的第二部里,再作进一步的叙述。

translate_target: Simplified Chinese for teen readers (12+) of a classic adventure novel: faithful and natural, clear and readable, good for reading aloud; not childish, not stiffly literary. Keep sentences reasonably short.
